conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ is integral (for example finite).
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_{small, *}$ transforms surjections into surjections (on sheaves
of sets and on abelian sheaves),
\item $f_{small}^{-1}f_{small, *}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$
is surjective for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$,
\item
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
is faithful and reflects injections and surjections, and
\item
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}
Keep the distinction between *sheaves of sets* and *abelian sheaves*. Exactness is an **abelian-category** assertion, while direct image preservation of surjective maps also holds for set-valued sheaves.

Let $X_{\acute et}$ and $Y_{\acute et}$ denote the **small étale sites** of schemes $X$ and $Y$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})$ be the corresponding topoi of sheaves of sets, with structure sheaves of local rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ on these sites. A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, define the following exact **three source properties** of its small étale-site pullback functor $V/Y\mapsto X\times_YV$: **(A)** for each étale $U\to X$ and $u\in U$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV=W\amalg W'$ and an $X$-morphism $W\to U$ whose image contains $u$; **(B)** for each étale $V\to Y$ and étale cover $\{U_i\to X\times_YV\}$, some étale cover $\{V_j\to V\}$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV_j=\coprod_i W_{ij}$ for every $j$, with each $W_{ij}\to X\times_YV$ factoring through the relevant $U_i$; **(C)** for every étale $U\to X$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a *surjective $X$-morphism* $X\times_YV\to U$. These are properties of the morphism, **not** generic properties of all scheme maps. In the topos notation $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\dashv f_{\mathrm{small},*}$, the map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}f_{\mathrm{small},*}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is the **counit**. A functor *reflects* monomorphisms/epimorphisms if whenever the image map is mono/epi, so was the original.

formulation.statement:
Let $X_{\acute et}$ and $Y_{\acute et}$ denote the **small étale sites** of schemes $X$ and $Y$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})$ be the corresponding topoi of sheaves of sets, with structure sheaves of local rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ on these sites. A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, define the following exact **three source properties** of its small étale-site pullback functor $V/Y\mapsto X\times_YV$: **(A)** for each étale $U\to X$ and $u\in U$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV=W\amalg W'$ and an $X$-morphism $W\to U$ whose image contains $u$; **(B)** for each étale $V\to Y$ and étale cover $\{U_i\to X\times_YV\}$, some étale cover $\{V_j\to V\}$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV_j=\coprod_i W_{ij}$ for every $j$, with each $W_{ij}\to X\times_YV$ factoring through the relevant $U_i$; **(C)** for every étale $U\to X$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a *surjective $X$-morphism* $X\times_YV\to U$. These are properties of the morphism, **not** generic properties of all scheme maps. In the topos notation $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\dashv f_{\mathrm{small},*}$, the map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}f_{\mathrm{small},*}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is the **counit**. A functor *reflects* monomorphisms/epimorphisms if whenever the image map is mono/epi, so was the original.

**Statement (with original hypotheses):**
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ is integral (for example finite).
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_{small, *}$ transforms surjections into surjections (on sheaves
of sets and on abelian sheaves),
\item $f_{small}^{-1}f_{small, *}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$
is surjective for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$,
\item
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
is faithful and reflects injections and surjections, and
\item
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}

**Scope of conclusion:** Keep the distinction between *sheaves of sets* and *abelian sheaves*. Exactness is an **abelian-category** assertion, while direct image preservation of surjective maps also holds for set-valued sheaves.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For an integral f, the four numbered assertions concern preservation of surjections on set and abelian sheaves, surjectivity of the abelian counit, faithfulness and reflection of monos/epis, and exactness of abelian direct image. All four are included with correct site variance.

phase3.reason: The full proof derives each numbered consequence of integrality from cited integral/property-B lemmas and an exactness criterion in Modules on Sites.

\label{lemma-same-image}
Let $k$ be a field, and let $R$, $S$ be $k$-algebras.
Let $S' \subset S$ be a sub $k$-algebra, and let $f \in S' \otimes_k R$.
In the commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec((S \otimes_k R)_f) \ar[rd] \ar[rr] & &
\Spec((S' \otimes_k R)_f) \ar[ld] \\
& \Spec(R) &
}
$$
the images of the diagonal arrows are the same.

\label{lemma-make-injective}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $\alpha : K \to L$ be a homomorphism of differential graded
$A$-modules. There exists a factorization
$$
\xymatrix{
K \ar[r]^{\tilde \alpha} \ar@/_1pc/[rr]_\alpha &
\tilde L \ar[r]^\pi & L
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\tilde \alpha$ is an admissible monomorphism (see
Definition \ref{definition-admissible-ses}),
\item there is a morphism $s : L \to \tilde L$
such that $\pi \circ s = \text{id}_L$ and such that
$s \circ \pi$ is homotopic to $\text{id}_{\tilde L}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-third-map-idempotent}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a pre-triangulated category.
Let $(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)$ be a distinguished triangle.
If
$$
\xymatrix{
Z \ar[r]_h \ar[d]_c & X[1] \ar[d]^{a[1]} \\
Z \ar[r]^h & X[1]
}
$$
is commutative and $a^2 = a$, $c^2 = c$, then there exists a
morphism $b : Y \to Y$ with $b^2 = b$ such that
$(a, b, c)$ is an endomorphism of the triangle $(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)$.

Let
$$
0 \to M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3 \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules.

$R$-module.
\item If $M_1$ and $M_3$ are finitely presented $R$-modules, then $M_2$
is a finitely presented $R$-module.
\item If $M_2$ is a finite $R$-module, then $M_3$ is a finite $R$-module.
\item If $M_2$ is a finitely presented $R$-module and $M_1$ is a
finite $R$-module, then $M_3$ is a finitely presented $R$-module.
\item If $M_3$ is a finitely presented $R$-module and $M_2$ is a finite
$R$-module, then $M_1$ is a finite $R$-module.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $X$ be a spectral topological space; let $X_0\subseteq X$ be its closed points and let $\pi_0(X)$ denote the connected-component space. The following are equivalent:
(1) Every open cover of $X$ admits a refinement by a **finite partition** of $X$ into pairwise disjoint clopen subsets.
(2) The canonical map $X_0\to\pi_0(X)$ is bijective.
Furthermore, if $X_0$ is a closed subset of $X$ and every point of $X$ specializes to a unique point of $X_0$, then conditions (1) and (2) hold.

source.label: lemma-spectral-split
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spectral-split}
Let $X$ be a spectral space. Let $X_0 \subset X$ be the set of closed points.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every open covering of $X$ can be refined by a finite
disjoint union decomposition $X = \coprod U_i$ with $U_i$
open and closed in $X$.
\item The composition $X_0 \to X \to \pi_0(X)$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X_0$ is closed in $X$ and every point of $X$ specializes
to a unique point of $X_0$, then these conditions are satisfied.

source.label: lemma-lift-covering-of-quasi-compact-hausdorff-subset
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-covering-of-quasi-compact-hausdorff-subset}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $Z \subset X$ be a quasi-compact subset
such that any two points of $Z$ have disjoint open neighbourhoods in $X$.
Suppose given an integer $p \geq 0$, a set $I$, for every $i \in I$
an open $U_i \subset X$, and for every $(p + 1)$-tuple
$i_0, \ldots, i_p$ of $I$ an open
$W_{i_0 \ldots i_p} \subset U_{i_0} \cap \ldots \cap U_{i_p}$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z \subset \bigcup U_i$, and
\item for every $i_0, \ldots, i_p$ we have
$W_{i_0 \ldots i_p} \cap Z = U_{i_0} \cap \ldots \cap U_{i_p} \cap Z$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exist opens $V_i$ of $X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z \subset \bigcup V_i$,
\item $V_i \subset U_i$ for all $i$,
\item $\overline{V_i} \cap Z \subset U_i$ for all $i$, and
\item $V_{i_0} \cap \ldots \cap V_{i_p} \subset W_{i_0 \ldots i_p}$
for all $(p + 1)$-tuples $i_0, \ldots, i_p$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $S = \lim_{i \in I} S_i$ be a limit of a directed system of schemes
with affine transition morphisms $g_{i'i} : S_{i'} \to S_i$.
We assume that $S_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated for all $i \in I$.
Let $0 \in I$. Let $X_0 \to S_0$ and $Y_0 \to S_0$ be smooth proper morphisms.
We set $X_i = S_i \times_{S_0} X_0$ for $i \geq 0$
and $X = S \times_{S_0} X_0$ and similarly for $Y_0$. If $K$ is the
Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from $X$ to $Y$ over $S$
then for some $i \geq 0$ there exists a
Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from $X_i$ to $Y_i$ over $S_i$.
The inverse system of qcqs S_i has affine transitions; at a sufficiently large index i one finds a perfect kernel *with inverse* satisfying both relative convolution identities; not merely a descended perfect complex.

formulation.statement:
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ a Koszul-regular closed immersion, i.e. its ideal sheaf is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. Let $\mathcal C_{X/Y}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf, $\mathcal N=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal C_{X/Y},\mathcal O_X)$ its normal vector bundle of locally constant rank $r$, and $a_i$ the right adjoint to $Ri_*$ on unbounded derived categories of quasi-coherent cohomology. Then the right-adjoint value on the structure sheaf admits an isomorphism
\[
\bigwedge^r_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal N[-r]\xrightarrow{\sim}a_i(\mathcal O_Y).
\]
If the rank varies between connected components the shift is understood componentwise.

source.label: lemma-regular-immersion
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular-immersion}
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $i : X \to Y$ be a Koszul-regular closed immersion.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint of
$Ri_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}. Then there is an isomorphism
$$
\wedge^r\mathcal{N}[-r] \longrightarrow a(\mathcal{O}_Y)
$$
where
$\mathcal{N} = \SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{C}_{X/Y}, \mathcal{O}_X)$
is the normal sheaf of $i$
(Morphisms, Section \ref{morphisms-section-conormal-sheaf})
and $r$ is its rank viewed as a locally constant
function on $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-weakly-ass-pullback}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module. Let $x \in X$ with $s = f(x)$.
If $f$ is flat at $x$, the point $x$ is a generic point of the fibre $X_s$, and
$s \in \text{WeakAss}_S(\mathcal{G})$, then
$x \in \text{WeakAss}(f^*\mathcal{G})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-invertible-sheaf-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $D_1$, $D_2$ be effective Cartier divisors on $S$.
Let $D = D_1 + D_2$.
Then there is a unique isomorphism
$$
\mathcal{O}_S(D_1) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathcal{O}_S(D_2)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{O}_S(D)
$$
which maps $1_{D_1} \otimes 1_{D_2}$ to $1_D$.

\label{lemma-colimit-complexes}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X = \lim_{i \in I} X_i$ be a limit of a
directed system of schemes over $S$ with affine transition morphisms
$f_{i'i} : X_{i'} \to X_i$. We assume that $X_i$ is quasi-compact and

$$
\colim_{i \in I} H_\etale^p(X_i, K|_{X_i}) = H_\etale^p(X, K|_X).
$$
for all $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ where $K|_{X_i}$ and $K|_X$
are the pullbacks of $K$ to $X_i$ and $X$.

conclusions: $f^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_!$.
formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ be two sites.
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $E \subset \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ be a subset such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $V \in E$ there exists a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$
on $\mathcal{C}$ such that $f^{-1}\mathcal{F}(V) = 
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})$ functorially
for $\mathcal{F}$ in $\Sh(\mathcal{C})$,
\item every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by objects of $E$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_!$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For topoi morphism f:Sh(D)→Sh(C), if each evaluation (f^{-1}F)(V) for V in a covering-generating set E is represented by a sheaf G on C, and every object of D admits an E-cover, then f^{-1} has a left adjoint f_!. Both representability and covering conditions are preserved.

phase3.reason: Representability of f^{-1}F(V) for the covering-generating set E defines f_! on the sheafified representable generators and their maps, then on their coproducts. Express any sheaf as a coequalizer of such coproducts and define f_! using the same coequalizer; the displayed equalizers of Hom sets verify f_!⊣f^{-1}.

\label{lemma-add-summand-strict-monomorphism}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a strict monomorphism of filtered objects.
Let $g : A \to C$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
Then $f \oplus g : A \to B \oplus C$ is a strict monomorphism.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universally-injective-to-completion-flat}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map, and $N$ an $S$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a Noetherian ring,
\item $S$ is a Noetherian ring,
\item $N$ is a finite $S$-module,
\item $N$ is flat over $R$, and
\item for any prime $\mathfrak q \subset S$ which is an associated prime of
$N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ where $\mathfrak p = R \cap \mathfrak q$
we have $IS + \mathfrak q \not = S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map $N \to N^\wedge$ of $N$ into the $I$-adic completion of $N$
is universally injective as a map of $R$-modules.

\label{lemma-compare-derived}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The essential image of the fully faithful functor
$\epsilon^{-1} : \textit{Mod}(X_\etale, \Lambda) \to
\textit{Mod}(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$

\label{lemma-localize-cartesian-square}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^{-1} \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^{-1}$
as functors $D(\mathcal{C}/X) \to D(\mathcal{C}/Y')$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dim-1-projective-completion}
Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$.
If $\dim(X) \leq 1$, then there exists an open immersion
$j : X \to \overline{X}$ with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\overline{X}$ is H-projective over $k$, i.e., $\overline{X}$
is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf{P}^d_k$ for some $d$,
\item $j(X) \subset \overline{X}$ is dense and scheme
theoretically dense,
\item $\overline{X} \setminus X = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$
for some closed points $x_i \in \overline{X}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowup-fitting-ideal-locally-free}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module.
Let $k \geq 0$ and $I = \text{Fit}_k(M)$. Assume that
$M_\mathfrak p$ is free of rank $k$ for every
$\mathfrak p \not \in V(I)$. Then for every $a \in I$
with $R' = R[\frac{I}{a}]$ the strict transform
$$
M' = (M \otimes_R R')/a\text{-power torsion}
$$
is locally free of rank $k$.

formulation.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. If $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ and each $X_i\to S_i$ is an affine morphism, then the datum is effective: there is an $S$-scheme $X$ and compatible isomorphisms $X\times_SS_i\simeq X_i$. In fact one may construct $X$ by faithfully flat descent of the quasi-coherent algebras defining the affine morphisms.

The proposal restores the family and cocycle definitions, concludes effectiveness by an S-scheme X with compatible identifications, and does not impose an affine base S or finite index family.

phase3.reason: The proof first reduces affine descent by a τ-cover to one faithfully-flat affine map, converts the affine scheme datum into a descent datum on its coordinate algebra, applies faithfully-flat module descent, then proves the descended module is a ring and takes Spec.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is affine, then the descent datum is
effective.

formulation.statement:
Let $f$ be a morphism of ringed sites, with continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. On **unbounded** derived module categories $Rf_*$ is total derived direct image; $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ and $R\Gamma(\mathcal D,-)$ are right derived global-sections functors. To compare both sides as $\Gamma(\mathcal D,\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$-module complexes, the source ring's action is restricted along the natural map on global rings. No bounded-below condition is imposed.

Let $f : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed sites
corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
Then $R\Gamma(\mathcal{D}, -) \circ Rf_* = R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, -)$ as
functors $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to D(\Gamma(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}))$.
More generally, for $V \in \mathcal{D}$ with $U = u(V)$
we have $R\Gamma(U, -) = R\Gamma(V, -) \circ Rf_*$.

Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme. Let $Z_1, \ldots, Z_n$ be pairwise
distinct irreducible components of $X$. Let $\eta_i \in Z_i$ be their
generic points. Let $x \in X$ be arbitrary.

$x$ and all the $\eta_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-induced}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be a set and let
$f : Y \to X$ be an injective map of sets. The induced
topology on $Y$ is the topology characterized by
each of the following statements:
\begin{enumerate}
\item it is the weakest topology on $Y$ such that $f$ is continuous,
\item the open subsets of $Y$ are $f^{-1}(U)$ for $U \subset X$ open,
\item the closed subsets of $Y$ are the sets $f^{-1}(Z)$ for $Z \subset X$
closed.
\end{enumerate}

An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

Given a covering $\{T_i\to T\}$, an *effective descent datum* for quasi-coherent sheaves is a family of quasi-coherent $\mathcal F_i$ on $T_i$ with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:\mathrm{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $T_i\times_TT_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triples, and an isomorphism of this datum with the pullbacks of a single quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$. For a ring map $A\to B$, its *Amitsur cochain complex* $(B/A)_\bullet$ has degree $q$ term $B^{\otimes_A(q+1)}$ and alternating coface differential inserting $1$ in every position.

If $\mathcal{V} = \{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is an fpqc covering, then all
descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves with respect to $\mathcal{V}$
are effective.

**Scope and interpretation:** Effective descent includes the isomorphisms on pairwise fibre products and the **triple-overlap cocycle**. The descended sheaf exists on the base T, rather than merely a compatible family of local sections.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-finite-type}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $k$ be a field.
Let $f : \Spec(k) \to S$ be a morphism.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is of finite type.
\item The morphism $f$ is locally of finite type.
\item There exists an affine open $U = \Spec(R)$ of $S$
such that $f$ corresponds to a finite ring map $R \to k$.
\item There exists an affine open $U = \Spec(R)$ of $S$
such that the image of $f$ consists of a closed point $u$ in $U$
and the field extension $k/\kappa(u)$ is finite.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-etale-local
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is \'etale,
\item for every $x \in |X|$ the morphism $f$ is \'etale at $x$,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is \'etale,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is \'etale,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is an \'etale morphism,
\item there exists a scheme $U$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$\varphi : U \to X$ such that the composition $f \circ \varphi$
is \'etale,
\item for every commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d] \ar[r] & V \ar[d] \\
X \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
where $U$, $V$ are schemes and the vertical arrows are \'etale
the top horizontal arrow is \'etale,
\item there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d] \ar[r] & V \ar[d] \\
X \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
where $U$, $V$ are schemes, the vertical arrows are \'etale, and
$U \to X$ surjective such that the top horizontal arrow is \'etale, and
\item there exist Zariski coverings $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ and
$f^{-1}(Y_i) = \bigcup X_{ij}$ such that each morphism
$X_{ij} \to Y_i$ is \'etale.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.hold_reason: The source's meaning is that for every quasi-coherent O_Y-module G, its pullback f*G remains quasi-coherent. The structured hypotheses quantify only the morphism f; G and its quasi-coherence are embedded wholly in the conclusion, so the proposed hypothesis-result split omits the essential sheaf premise.
phase2.proposed_correction: Add 'Let G be a quasi-coherent O_Y-module' to hypotheses and assert f*G is quasi-coherent. Seek independent review.

phase3.reason: A global direct-sum presentation of the original module sheaf and right exactness of pullback give the required local presentation.

source.label: lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
The pullback $f^*\mathcal{G}$ of a quasi-coherent

formulation.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Let $(K_n\to L_n\to M_n\to K_n[1])_n$ be an inverse system of distinguished triangles in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ whose transition morphisms are morphisms of triangles. If the pro-objects $(K_n)$ and $(M_n)$ are each isomorphic in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X))$ to a Deligne system for $U\subseteq X$, then $(L_n)$ is also pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for this same open immersion.

The final 2-of-3 assertion correctly concludes that the MIDDLE system also is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system; it does not assume levelwise Deligne presentation.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Let $\overline{x}$ be a geometric point of $X$ and let
$\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$ be the image in $Y$.
Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
(f^*\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} =
\mathcal{G}_{\overline{y}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y, \overline{y}}}
\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}
$$
of the stalk of the pullback with the tensor product of the stalk
with the local ring of $X$ at $\overline{x}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-pullback-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Let $\overline{x}$ be a geometric point of $X$ and let
$\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$ be the image in $Y$.
Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
(f^*\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} =
\mathcal{G}_{\overline{y}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y, \overline{y}}}
\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}
$$
of the stalk of the pullback with the tensor product of the stalk
with the local ring of $X$ at $\overline{x}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coherent-on-proj}
Let $A$ be a graded ring such that $A_0$ is Noetherian and
$A$ is generated by finitely many elements of $A_1$ over $A_0$.
Set $X = \text{Proj}(A)$. Then $X$ is a Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists an $r \geq 0$ and
$d_1, \ldots, d_r \in \mathbf{Z}$ and a surjection
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, r} \mathcal{O}_X(d_j)
\longrightarrow \mathcal{F}.
$$
\item For any $p$ the cohomology group $H^p(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a finite
$A_0$-module.
\item If $p > 0$, then $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}(d)) = 0$ for all $d$ large enough.
\item For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}$ the graded $A$-module
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq k} H^0(X, \mathcal{F}(d))
$$
is a finite $A$-module.
\end{enumerate}

For a ringed site (C,O), RSheafHom(L,M) is the internal derived Hom in D(O), contravariant in the first variable and covariant in the second. It may be represented by SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet,I^bullet) for any representative L^bullet of L and a **K-injective** representative I^bullet of M; equivalently it is right adjoint to −⊗^L_O L (source lines 8839–8869). $$
K \longrightarrow R\SheafHom(L, K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} L)
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O})$ functorial in both $K$ and $L$.

\label{lemma-internal-hom-diagonal}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Given $K, L$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ there is a canonical morphism
$$
K \longrightarrow R\SheafHom(L, K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} L)
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O})$ functorial in both $K$ and $L$.

\label{lemma-adjoint-exact}
Let $u$ be a left adjoint to $v$ as in Definition \ref{definition-adjoint}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that $M : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{C}$ is a diagram,
and suppose that $\colim_\mathcal{I} M$ exists in
$\mathcal{C}$. Then $u(\colim_\mathcal{I} M) =
\colim_\mathcal{I} u \circ M$. In other words,
$u$ commutes with (representable) colimits.
\item Suppose that $M : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{D}$ is a diagram,
and suppose that $\lim_\mathcal{I} M$ exists in
$\mathcal{D}$. Then $v(\lim_\mathcal{I} M) =
\lim_\mathcal{I} v \circ M$. In other words $v$ commutes
with representable limits.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kunneth}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes over $k$ and
let $\mathcal{F}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module, resp.\ $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Then we have a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^n(X \times_{\Spec(k)} Y, \text{pr}_1^*\mathcal{F}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X \times_{\Spec(k)} Y}} \text{pr}_2^*\mathcal{G}) =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{p + q = n}
H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) \otimes_k H^q(Y, \mathcal{G})
$$
provided $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-compact and have affine
diagonal\footnote{The case where $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-separated
will be discussed in Lemma \ref{lemma-kunneth-general} below.}
(for example if $X$ and $Y$ are separated).

formulation.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map is **ind-Zariski** when its target is a filtered colimit of local-isomorphism algebras over the source.

Let $A$ be a ring such that $X = \Spec(A)$ is w-local. Let $I \subset A$
be the radical ideal cutting out the set $X_0$ of closed points in $X$.
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map inducing algebraic extensions on residue
fields at primes. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item every point of $Z = V(IB)$ is a closed point of $\Spec(B)$,
\item there exists an ind-Zariski ring map $B \to C$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B/IB \to C/IC$ is an isomorphism,
\item the space $Y = \Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item the induced map $p : Y \to X$ is w-local, and
\item $p^{-1}(X_0)$ is the set of closed points of $Y$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

There exists IND-ZARISKI B→C preserving B/IB≅C/IC, making Spec(C) and its map to Spec(A) W-LOCAL with closed-point preimage exactly closed points.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homotopy-s-N}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an additive category. Let $a, b : U \to V$ be morphisms
of simplicial objects of $\mathcal{A}$. If $a$, $b$ are homotopic,
then $s(a), s(b) : s(U) \to s(V)$ are homotopic maps of chain complexes.
If $\mathcal{A}$ is abelian, then also $N(a), N(b) : N(U) \to N(V)$ are
homotopic maps of chain complexes.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-local-X}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism which is locally of finite type.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$. If $f$ is flat at $x$ over $S$, then
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is essentially of finite presentation over
$\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$.

Let $R \to S$ be a flat local homomorphism of local Noetherian rings
such that $R/\mathfrak m_R \cong S/\mathfrak m_R S$.

of $R$ is the injective hull of the residue field of $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-determinant}
Let $X$ be a locally ringed space. Let
$$
\mathcal{E}_1 \xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal{E}_0 \to \mathcal{F} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Assume $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_0$ are locally
free of ranks $r_1, r_0$. Then there is a canonical map
$$
\wedge^{r_0 - r_1}\mathcal{F}
\longrightarrow
\wedge^{r_1}(\mathcal{E}_1^\vee) \otimes \wedge^{r_0}\mathcal{E}_0
$$
which is an isomorphism on the stalk at $x \in X$
if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ is locally free of rank $r_0 - r_1$
in an open neighbourhood of $x$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Then $X$ is Jacobson if and only if $|X|$ is Jacobson.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L5334–5338 asserts X DECENT and equates the algebraic-space Jacobson property with |X| being JACOBSON as a topological space (closed points dense in each closed subset). The proposed iff retains decency as an essential hypothesis, and the two distinct uses of Jacobson.

phase3.reason: Use density of finite-type points for one direction; conversely an étale affine chart of a decent algebraic space is Jacobson by contradiction from a nonclosed locally closed point and groupoid invariance.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-space-presentation}
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $f : U \to F$ be a
surjective \'etale morphism from a scheme to $F$. Set $R = U \times_F U$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $j : R \to U \times_S U$ defines an equivalence relation on
$U$ over $S$ (see
Groupoids, Definition \ref{groupoids-definition-equivalence-relation}).
\item the morphisms $s, t : R \to U$ are \'etale, and
\item the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
R \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &
U \ar[r] &
F
}
$$
is a coequalizer diagram in $\Sh((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-morphism-of-sites-almost-cocontinuous}
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites
associated to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
If $u$ is almost cocontinuous then $f_*$ commutes with
pushouts and coequalizers (and more generally finite connected colimits).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $s \in S$.
Assume that $f$ is proper and $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set.
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $V \subset S$ of $s$
such that $f|_{f^{-1}(V)} : f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

formulation.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, an object $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is a *dualizing complex* if on every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ it is the sheafification of a ring-theoretic dualizing complex: a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D_A,D_A)$. Write $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^\pm,D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ for derived complexes with coherent bounded-below, bounded-above and bounded cohomology respectively. If $f:X\to Y$ lies in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, then its upper-shriek functor maps bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology to bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology:
\[
f^!:D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_X).
\]
The assertion does not extend automatically to the unbounded-right-adjoint $a_f$ without a proper compactification.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L4468 says for an arbitrary S-morphism f:X→Y in FTS_S over NOETHERIAN S, f^! preserves BOUNDED-BELOW coherent-derived categories D_Coh^+(Y)→D_Coh^+(X). The final preserves f's separated finite-type context and does NOT claim unrestricted a_f or unbounded D_Coh is coherent-preserving.

phase3.reason: Locally factor the finite-type morphism into a closed immersion and affine-line projections, applying the cited dualizing and shriek lemmas inductively.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be proper over $k$. Let $\alpha = \sum n_i[Z_i]$
be in $Z_0(X)$. Then
$$
\deg(\alpha) = \sum n_i\deg(Z_i)
$$
where $\deg(Z_i)$ is the degree of $Z_i \to \Spec(k)$, i.e.,
$\deg(Z_i) = \dim_k \Gamma(Z_i, \mathcal{O}_{Z_i})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spell-out-degree-zero-cycle}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be proper over $k$. Let $\alpha = \sum n_i[Z_i]$
be in $Z_0(X)$. Then
$$
\deg(\alpha) = \sum n_i\deg(Z_i)
$$
where $\deg(Z_i)$ is the degree of $Z_i \to \Spec(k)$, i.e.,
$\deg(Z_i) = \dim_k \Gamma(Z_i, \mathcal{O}_{Z_i})$.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), a complex E^bullet is **perfect** when after a covering of every site object it has a quasi-isomorphism from a **strictly perfect** complex (bounded, termwise direct summand of finite free O-modules); a derived object is perfect if represented by such a complex (source Definition perfect at 12734–12746). A perfect object is **not assumed globally bounded** unless the topos is quasi-compact. Its relation to pseudo-coherence and local finite Tor dimension is an equivalence only where stated, not an inherited hypothesis. The first clause assumes a **final object X**, while the second is independent of any such object.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and there exist a
covering $\{U_i \to X\}$, strictly perfect complexes $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$
of $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules, and isomorphisms
 $\alpha_i : \mathcal{E}_i^\bullet \to E|_{U_i}$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$, then $E$ is perfect.
\item If $E$ is perfect, then any complex representing $E$ is perfect.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: If a site has final X and E admits a strictly perfect derived-isomorphic local representative over a cover of X, E is perfect; separately perfect E implies every representing complex is perfect. The two clauses remain independently scoped.

phase3.reason: The proof explicitly reduces to the previously proven independence-of-representative argument for pseudo-coherence, now with local quasi-isomorphisms.

\label{lemma-perfect-independent-representative}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and there exist a
covering $\{U_i \to X\}$, strictly perfect complexes $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$
of $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules, and isomorphisms
 $\alpha_i : \mathcal{E}_i^\bullet \to E|_{U_i}$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$, then $E$ is perfect.
\item If $E$ is perfect, then any complex representing $E$ is perfect.
\end{enumerate}

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

Under the above base hypotheses, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
with dual $\mathcal{E}^\vee$. Then
$ch_i(\mathcal{E}^\vee) = (-1)^i ch_i(\mathcal{E})$ in
$A^i(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q}$.

hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.
formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

Let $A \to B$ be a surjective ring map whose kernel $I$ is generated
by a Koszul-regular sequence (for example a regular sequence).
Then $L_{B/A}$ is quasi-isomorphic to $I/I^2[1]$.

The proposed expansion explains positive Koszul homology vanishing and does not substitute an arbitrary nonregular ideal.

\label{lemma-closed-immersion}
Let $i : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a closed immersion of
topoi. Then $i_*$ is fully faithful, transforms surjections into surjections,
commutes with coequalizers, commutes with pushouts, reflects injections,
reflects surjections, and reflects bijections.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fitting-ideals-and-pd1}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $R$-module. Let $k \geq 0$.
Assume that $\text{Fit}_k(M) = (f)$ for some nonzerodivisor $f \in R$
and $\text{Fit}_{k - 1}(M) = 0$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M$ has projective dimension $\leq 1$,
\item $M' = \Ker(f : M \to M)$ is the $f$-power torsion submodule of $M$,
\item $M'$ has projective dimension $\leq 1$,
\item $M/M'$ is finite locally free of rank $k$, and
\item $M \cong M/M' \oplus M'$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-pre-prepare-adjoint-dual}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \mathcal{D}$
be a full subcategory invariant under all shifts.
Consider a distinguished triangle
$$
X \to Y \to Z \to X[1]
$$
of $\mathcal{D}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is in ${}^\perp\mathcal{B}$, and
\item $\Hom(Y, B) = \Hom(Z, B)$ for all $B \in \Ob(\mathcal{B})$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{proposition-coherator}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is a Grothendieck
abelian category. Consequently, $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has enough injectives and all limits.
\item The inclusion functor
$\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has a right adjoint\footnote{This functor is sometimes called
the {\it coherator}.}
$$
Q : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \longrightarrow \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
such that for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction mapping
$Q(\mathcal{F}) \to \mathcal{F}$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X_1 \to X_2$ be a flat morphism of schemes. Let $Z_2 \subset X_2$ be a
closed subscheme. Let $Z_1$ be the inverse image of $Z_2$ in $X_1$.
Let $X'_i$ be the blowup of $Z_i$ in $X_i$. Then there exists a cartesian
diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1' \ar[r] \ar[d] & X_2' \ar[d] \\
X_1 \ar[r] & X_2
}
$$
of schemes.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $K$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal{C}$.
Consider the morphism of topoi
$j : \Sh(\mathcal{C}/K) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$, see

$H^p(K, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(\mathcal{C}/K, j^{-1}\mathcal{F})$
for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.

\label{lemma-flat-going-down}
Let $R \to S$ be flat. Let $\mathfrak p \subset \mathfrak p'$
be primes of $R$. Let $\mathfrak q' \subset S$ be a prime of $S$

$\mathfrak q \subset \mathfrak q'$ mapping to $\mathfrak p$.

formulation.statement:
An S-rational map is an equivalence class of S-morphisms on dense open subsets, equivalent when equal on a dense open in their overlap; take the given representative on U. The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$.
Assume $X$ is Noetherian and $Y$ is proper over $S$.
Given an $S$-rational map $f : U \to Y$ from $X$ to $Y$
there exists a morphism $p : X' \to X$ and an
$S$-morphism $f' : X' \to Y$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p$ is proper and $p^{-1}(U) \to U$ is an isomorphism,
\item $f'|_{p^{-1}(U)}$ is equal to $f \circ p|_{p^{-1}(U)}$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement: For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for the unbounded derived category of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology on $T$, and let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$. Its unit and counit are $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_fRf_*$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper between Noetherian schemes. Suppose $V\subseteq Y$ is open and the restricted morphism $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. Then for each bounded-below $K\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the canonical comparison $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ becomes an isomorphism after restriction to $f^{-1}(V)$. No global isomorphism outside this open is asserted.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes. Let $V \subset Y$

Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M$ is reflexive,
\item $M_\mathfrak p$ is a reflexive $R_\mathfrak p$-module
for all primes $\mathfrak p \subset R$, and
\item $M_\mathfrak m$ is a reflexive $R_\mathfrak m$-module
for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $R$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-torsion-tensor-product}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
For $K, L \in D(A)$ we have
$$
R\Gamma_Z(K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} L) =
K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} R\Gamma_Z(L) =
R\Gamma_Z(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} L =
R\Gamma_Z(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} R\Gamma_Z(L)
$$
If $K$ or $L$ is in $D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A)$ then so is
$K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} L$.

\label{lemma-augmentation-howto}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $U$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{C}$.
To give an augmentation of $U$ towards $X$ is
the same as giving a morphism $\epsilon_0 : U_0 \to X$
such that $\epsilon_0 \circ d^1_0 = \epsilon_0 \circ d^1_1$.

\label{lemma-going-down-flat-module}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $N$ be a finite $S$-module flat over $R$.
Endow $\text{Supp}(N) \subset \Spec(S)$ with the induced topology.
Then generalizations lift along $\text{Supp}(N) \to \Spec(R)$.

source.label: proposition-finite-presentation-flat-pure-is-projective
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-finite-presentation-flat-pure-is-projective}
Let $f : X \to S$ be an affine, finitely presented morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of
finite presentation, flat over $S$. Then the following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_*\mathcal{F}$ is locally projective on $S$, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is pure relative to $S$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, given a ring map $A \to B$ of finite presentation and
a finitely presented $B$-module $N$ flat over $A$ we have:
$N$ is projective as an $A$-module if and only if $\widetilde{N}$
on $\Spec(B)$ is pure relative to $\Spec(A)$.

\label{lemma-smooth-standard-smooth}
Let $R \to A$ be a smooth ring map. Then there exists a smooth $R$-algebra
map $A \to B$ with a retraction such that $B$ is standard smooth over
$R$, i.e.,
$$
B \cong R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)
$$
and $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i, j = 1, \ldots, c}$
is invertible in $B$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-Jacobson-permanence}
Let $R$ be a Jacobson ring. Let $R \to S$ be a
ring map of finite type. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item The ring $S$ is Jacobson.
\item The map $\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$ transforms
closed points to closed points.
\item For $\mathfrak m' \subset S$ maximal lying over $\mathfrak m \subset R$
the field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak m')/\kappa(\mathfrak m)$
is finite.
\end{enumerate}

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is integral,
\item $f$ is of finite type, and

$X_U \to U$ is flat and of finite presentation and such that
$\mathcal{F}|_{X_U}$ is flat over $U$ and of finite presentation
over $\mathcal{O}_{X_U}$.

\label{lemma-adjoint-ext}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $T \subset \Spec(A)$
be a subset stable under specialization.
For any object $K$ of $D(A)$ we have
$$
H^i(RH^0_T(K)) = \colim_{Z \subset T\text{ closed}} H^i_Z(K)
$$

formulation.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a **proper** morphism between finite-type $S$-schemes, and let $D_X,D_Y$ be their dualizing complexes normalized relative to the same $D_S$. Let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*$ (both schemes Noetherian and qcqs, but not necessarily separated over $S$). Then there is a canonical isomorphism $a_f(D_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X$, compatible with the normalization on separated open pieces.

The final retains properness and normalization, including the possibility that X,Y are not separated over S themselves.

\label{lemma-proper-map-good-dualizing-complex}
Let $(S, \omega_S^\bullet)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-dualizing}.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over $S$.
Let $\omega_X^\bullet$ and $\omega_Y^\bullet$ be dualizing complexes
normalized relative to $\omega_S^\bullet$. Let $a$ be the
right adjoint of Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image} for
$f$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$a(\omega_Y^\bullet) = \omega_X^\bullet$.

**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A ring map $A\to B$ is a **local isomorphism** when near every prime of $B$ it induces an open immersion after inverting an element of $B$; it **identifies local rings** when $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism for every prime $q$ of $B$. A ring map is **ind-Zariski** when its target is a filtered colimit of local-isomorphism algebras over the source.

\label{proposition-maps-wich-identify-local-rings}
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map which identifies local rings.
Then there exists a faithfully flat, ind-Zariski ring map
$B \to B'$ such that $A \to B'$ is ind-Zariski.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $c_1(\mathcal{L}) \in A^1(X)$ is in the center of $A^*(X)$ and
\item if $f : X' \to X$ is locally of finite type and $c \in A^*(X' \to X)$,
then $c \circ c_1(\mathcal{L}) = c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \circ c$.
\end{enumerate}

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$, let $\omega_X^\bullet=f^!k\in D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the normalized relative dualizing complex of the structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$, and put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(\omega_X^\bullet)$. Its Grothendieck duality property is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^i(K,\omega_X^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,K),k)$ functorially for $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional then $\omega_X^\bullet\simeq\omega_X[1]$, so Serre duality is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^{i+1}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,\mathcal F),k)$. If $X$ is a smooth curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

Let $X$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$
with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Then
$$
\dim_k H^0(X, \Omega_{X/k}) = g
\quad\text{and}\quad
\deg(\Omega_{X/k}) = 2g - 2
$$

\label{lemma-genus-smooth}
Let $X$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$
with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Then

$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $E$ be an object of
$D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $a \in \mathbf{Z}$. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ has tor-amplitude in $[a, \infty]$.
\item $E$ can be represented by a K-flat complex $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$
of flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules with $\mathcal{E}^i = 0$ for
$i \not \in [a, \infty]$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we can choose $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ such that any pullback
by a morphism of ringed sites is a K-flat complex with flat terms.

Let
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{T}_2 \ar[r] \ar[d] & \mathcal{T}_1 \ar[d]^G \\
\mathcal{S}_2 \ar[r]^F & \mathcal{S}_1
}
$$
be a $2$-cartesian diagram of stacks in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$.
If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F : \mathcal{S}_2 \to \mathcal{S}_1$ is fully faithful,
\item for every $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and
$x \in \Ob((\mathcal{S}_1)_U)$ there exists a covering
$\{U_i \to U\}$ such that $x|_{U_i}$ is in the essential
image of $F : (\mathcal{S}_2)_{U_i} \to (\mathcal{S}_1)_{U_i}$, and
\item $\mathcal{T}_2$ is a stack in setoids.
\end{enumerate}
then $\mathcal{T}_1$ is a stack in setoids.

formulation.statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a surjective flat morphism over $S$. Then the pullback functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ is faithful: two morphisms of descent data that become equal after pullback were already equal.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension}
Let $R \to S$ be a finite and finitely presented ring map.
Let $M$ be an $S$-module.
Then $M$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module if and only if
$M$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chi-tensor-finite}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be a coherent sheaf with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})) \leq 0$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is generated by global sections,
\item $H^0(X, \mathcal{F}) =
\bigoplus_{x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})} \mathcal{F}_x$,
\item $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > 0$,
\item $\chi(X, \mathcal{F}) = \dim_k H^0(X, \mathcal{F})$, and
\item
$\chi(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{E}) = n\chi(X, \mathcal{F})$
for every locally free module $\mathcal{E}$ of rank $n$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-projective-module}
Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal.
Let $\overline{P}$ be a finite projective $A/I$-module.
Then there exists an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ which induces
an isomorphism $A/I \to A'/IA'$ and a finite projective
$A'$-module $P'$ lifting $\overline{P}$.

\label{lemma-have-one-root}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $P(T)$ be a monic polynomial with coefficients
in $R$. Let $\alpha \in R$ be such that $P(\alpha) = 0$. Then
$P(T) = (T - \alpha)Q(T)$ for some monic polynomial $Q(T) \in R[T]$.

source.label: lemma-stalk-internal-hom
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-internal-hom}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type then the canonical map
$$
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})_x
\to
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}}(\mathcal{F}_x, \mathcal{G}_x)
$$
is injective.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finitely presented,
this canonical morphism is an isomorphism.

source.label: lemma-stalk-R-f-shriek
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-R-f-shriek}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite type separated morphism of schemes
with $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $K$ be an object of
$D^+_{tors}(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ or of $D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ in case
$\Lambda$ is torsion. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
(Rf_!K)_{\overline{y}}
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c(X_{\overline{y}}, K|_{X_{\overline{y}}})
$$
in $D(\Lambda)$ for any geometric point $\overline{y} : \Spec(k) \to Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-points-complement}
Let $A$ be a local ring. Let $I, J \subset A$ be ideals.
If $J$ is finitely generated and $I \subset J^n$ for all $n \geq 1$,
then $V(I)$ contains the closed points of $\Spec(A) \setminus V(J)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exactness-stalks}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site and let $\{p_i\}_{i\in I}$ be a conservative
family of points. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item Given any map of sheaves $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$
we have $\forall i, \varphi_{p_i}$ injective implies $\varphi$ injective.
\item Given any map of sheaves $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$
we have $\forall i, \varphi_{p_i}$ surjective implies $\varphi$ surjective.
\item Given any pair of maps of sheaves
$\varphi_1, \varphi_2 : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$
we have $\forall i, \varphi_{1, p_i} = \varphi_{2, p_i}$
implies $\varphi_1 = \varphi_2$.
\item Given a finite diagram $\mathcal{G} : \mathcal{J}
\to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$, a sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ and morphisms
$q_j : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}_j$ then $(\mathcal{F}, q_j)$
is a limit of the diagram if and only if for each $i$ the stalk
$(\mathcal{F}_{p_i}, (q_j)_{p_i})$ is one.
\item Given a finite diagram $\mathcal{F} : \mathcal{J}
\to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$, a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ and morphisms
$e_j : \mathcal{F}_j \to \mathcal{G}$ then $(\mathcal{G}, e_j)$
is a colimit of the diagram if and only if for each $i$ the stalk

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf,
\item there exists an algebraic space $X$ and a map $X \to F$
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Delta_F$ is representable (by schemes).

\label{lemma-bootstrap-diagonal}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf,
\item there exists an algebraic space $X$ and a map $X \to F$
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Delta_F$ is representable (by schemes).

\label{lemma-delta-invariant-and-change-of-fields-better}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
Let $K/k$ be a field extension and set $Y = X_K$.
Let $y \in Y$ with image $x \in X$.
Assume assumptions (a), (b), (c) of
Lemma \ref{lemma-geometrically-normal-in-codim-1}
hold for $x \in X$ and that $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}) = 1$.
Then the $\delta$-invariant
of $X$ at $x$ is $\delta$-invariant of $Y$ at $y$.

\label{lemma-blow-up-reduced-scheme}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. If $X$ is reduced, then the
blowup $X'$ of $X$ in $\mathcal{I}$ is reduced.
