hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

Let $i : X \to Y$ and $j : Y \to Z$ be regular immersions
of schemes locally of finite type over $S$. Then
$j \circ i$ is a regular immersion and
$(j \circ i)^! = i^! \circ j^!$.

conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Ab}(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$
is exact.
\item The functor
$f^{-1} : \Sh(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \Sh(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$
is exact, i.e., it commutes with finite limits and colimits, see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-exact}.
\item Let $\overline{x} \to X$ be a geometric point.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf on $Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
Then there is a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} = \mathcal{G}_{\overline{y}}.
$$
where $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\item For any $V \to Y$ \'etale we have $f^{-1}h_V = h_{X \times_Y V}$.
\end{enumerate}
The inverse-image functor is exact on **abelian sheaves** and finite-limit/colimit exact on **set-valued sheaves**. Pullback of geometric stalks is to $ ar y=f ar x$, and inverse image of representable h_V is h_{X×_Y V}. These statements are about f_small^{-1}, not tensor pullback of modules.

Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the induced **morphism of small étale topoi** $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute etale})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute etale})$ has inverse image $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$); it sends **sheaves of sets** on $Y_{\acute etale}$ to sheaves on $X_{\acute etale}$, and also induces inverse image of abelian sheaves. It is different from the **ringed-site module pullback** $f^*$, which additionally tensors by the target structure sheaf. For an étale $V\to Y$, let $h_V$ be its representable sheaf and $X\times_Y V$ the fibre product, an object of $X_{\acute etale}$. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

$f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Ab}(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$

$f^{-1} : \Sh(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \Sh(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$

$$

where $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\item For any $V \to Y$ \'etale we have $f^{-1}h_V = h_{X \times_Y V}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K^\bullet$ represents a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$, and
\item $E = \Hom_{\text{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal{O})}(K^\bullet, K^\bullet)$
computes the ext groups of $K^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet :
D(E, \text{d})
\longrightarrow
D(\mathcal{O})
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-tensor-with-complex-derived} is fully faithful.

Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site and $K^\bullet$ a complex of $\mathcal O$-modules. Here $(E,\mathrm d)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal O)}(K^\bullet,K^\bullet)$ is the differential graded endomorphism algebra of $K^\bullet$.

The functor $K(\text{Mod}_{(E, \text{d})}) \to K(\mathcal{O})$
induced by the dg tensor functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_E K^\bullet$ has a left derived
version defined on all of $D(E, \text{d})$. We denote it
$- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet : D(E, \text{d}) \to D(\mathcal{O})$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The homotopy-level tensor functor -⊗_E K with E the dg endomorphism algebra of K admits a left derived version on ALL D(E), with codomain D(O). The candidate explicitly restores the earlier-defined functor and source/codomain.

phase3.reason: The class of property-(P) dg E-modules provides quasi-isomorphic resolutions of every object, and quasi-isomorphisms between these are homotopy equivalences. These conditions satisfy the cited derived-functor existence/computation criterion, yielding the left derived tensor on all of D(E).

over a field $k$ for which $k(X)/k(Y)$ is a finite separable extension, equivalently $f$ is generically étale. If
$k = H^0(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$
and $X$ and $Y$ have genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, then

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rh}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of smooth proper curves
over a field $k$ which satisfies the equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{lemma-generically-etale}. If
$k = H^0(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$
and $X$ and $Y$ have genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, then
$$
2g_X - 2 = (2g_Y - 2) \deg(f) + \deg(R)
$$
where $R \subset X$ is the effective Cartier divisor cut out by
the different of $f$.

\label{lemma-quotient-by-closed}
Let $R$ be a topological ring. Let $M$ be a complete, linearly topologized
$R$-module. Let $N \subset M$ be a closed submodule. If $M$ has a
countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of $0$, then
$M/N$ is complete and the map $M \to M/N$ is open.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-flat-finite-over-dense-open}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is flat and proper.
Let $U \subset S$ be a dense open such that $X_U \to U$ is finite.
If also either $f$ is locally of finite presentation or
$U \subset S$ is retrocompact, then $f$ is finite.

formulation.statement:
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$I \subset J \subset A$ be proper ideals. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A/J$ has finite tor dimension over $A/I$, and
\item $J$ is generated by a regular sequence.
\end{enumerate}
Then $I$ is generated by a regular sequence and $J/I$
is generated by a regular sequence.

phase3.reason: The conormal injection extends generators of I to minimal generators of J, whose regularity transfers to the original sequence.

formulation.statement:
A one-dimensional equidimensional closed subscheme $Z\subset\mathbf P_k^2$ without embedded associated points is Cohen–Macaulay, and its saturated homogeneous defining ideal $I(Z)\subset k[T_0,T_1,T_2]$ is generated by a single nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$. Such a $Z$ is an integral curve exactly when $F$ is irreducible. Its arithmetic genus, when $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=k$, is $g(Z)=\dim_kH^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

Let $Z \subset \mathbf{P}^2_k$ be a one-dimensional equidimensional closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^2_k$ without embedded points, with principal saturated homogeneous ideal as above
and let $I(Z) = (F)$ for some $F \in k[T_0, T_1, T_2]$.
If $Z \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth in at least one point and $k$ is infinite, then
there exists a closed point $z \in Z$ contained in the smooth
locus such that $\kappa(z)/k$ is finite separable of degree
at most $d$.

phase3.reason: At a smooth point, a nonzero partial derivative makes a coordinate projection étale over a nonempty open. Its fibres have degree at most the polynomial degree d; infinitude of k provides a rational parameter value, yielding a smooth closed point with separable residue degree at most d.

Let $Z \subset \mathbf{P}^2_k$ be as in Lemma \ref{lemma-equation-plane-curve}

If $Z \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth in at least one point and $k$ is infinite, then

locus such that $\kappa(z)/k$ is finite separable of degree
at most $d$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let ${\mathcal L}_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of rank $r$ endowed with a filtration
$$
0 = \mathcal{E}_0 \subset \mathcal{E}_1 \subset \mathcal{E}_2
\subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{E}_r = \mathcal{E}
$$
such that $\mathcal{E}_i/\mathcal{E}_{i - 1} \cong \mathcal{L}_i$.
Set $c_1({\mathcal L}_i) = x_i$. Then
$$
c(\mathcal{E})
=
\prod\nolimits_{i = 1}^r (1 + x_i)
$$
in $A^*(X)$.

\label{lemma-chern-filter-by-linebundles}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let ${\mathcal L}_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally free rank
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module endowed with a filtration
$$
0 = \mathcal{E}_0 \subset \mathcal{E}_1 \subset \mathcal{E}_2
\subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{E}_r = \mathcal{E}
$$
such that $\mathcal{E}_i/\mathcal{E}_{i - 1} \cong \mathcal{L}_i$.
Set $c_1({\mathcal L}_i) = x_i$. Then
$$
c(\mathcal{E})
=
\prod\nolimits_{i = 1}^r (1 + x_i)
$$
in $A^*(X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-orthogonal-triangulated}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category. Let
$\mathcal{A} \subset \mathcal{D}$ be a full subcategory invariant
under all shifts. Then both the right orthogonal $\mathcal{A}^\perp$ and
the left orthogonal ${}^\perp\mathcal{A}$ of $\mathcal{A}$
are strictly full, saturated\footnote{Definition \ref{definition-saturated}.},
triangulated subcagories of $\mathcal{D}$.

A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a nonsingular proper curve over $k$.
Let $(\mathcal{L}, V)$ be a $\mathfrak g^1_d$ on $X$. Then the morphism
$\varphi : X \to \mathbf{P}^1_k$ associated to the pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ by the projective-space construction above
either
\begin{enumerate}
\item is nonconstant and has degree $\leq d$, or
\item factors through a closed point of $\mathbf{P}^1_k$ and in this
case $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \not = k$.
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: Pulls back O(1) from the induced map to the projective line, bounds its degree via a nonzero map to the linear-series bundle, and separates constant from finite-degree cases.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-karoubian}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ is Karoubian,
\item every idempotent endomorphism of an object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a
cokernel, and
\item given an idempotent endomorphism $p : z \to z$ of $\mathcal{C}$
there exists a direct sum decomposition $z = x \oplus y$ such
that $p$ corresponds to the projection onto $y$.
\end{enumerate}

\item $\mathcal{F}$ coherent on $X$

\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the ideal of
denominators of $s$. Let $T \subset X$ be the union
of the supports of $\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}$ and
$\mathcal{L}/s(\mathcal{I})$ which is a nowhere dense closed
subset $T \subset X$ according to

1 : \mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}, \quad

\label{lemma-make-maps-regular-section}
Suppose given
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ a locally Noetherian scheme,
\item $\mathcal{L}$ an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
\item $s$ a regular meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ coherent on $X$
without embedded associated points and $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) = X$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the ideal of
denominators of $s$. Let $T \subset X$ be the union
of the supports of $\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}$ and
$\mathcal{L}/s(\mathcal{I})$ which is a nowhere dense closed
subset $T \subset X$ according to
Lemma \ref{lemma-regular-meromorphic-ideal-denominators}.
Then there are canonical injective maps
$$
1 : \mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}, \quad
s : \mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}\mathcal{L}
$$
whose cokernels are supported on $T$.

formulation.statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *étale-local on the source* if $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ exactly when all composites $X_i\to X\to Y$ have it, for any étale covering $\{X_i\to X\}$. It is *étale-local on the target* if the corresponding equivalence holds after étale base change on $Y$. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and every étale covering $\{a_i:X_i\to X\}$, the morphism $f$ is étale if and only if each composite $f\circ a_i:X_i\to Y$ is étale.

A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-representable-by-spaces}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a map of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Suppose $a : F \to G$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
If $X$ is an algebraic space over $S$, and $X \to G$ is a map of presheaves
then $X \times_G F$ is an algebraic space.

source.label: lemma-etale-image-open
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-image-open}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $U$ be a scheme and let $f : U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism.
Let $X' \subset X$ be the open subspace corresponding to
the open $|f|(|U|) \subset |X|$ via
Lemma \ref{lemma-open-subspaces}.
Then $f$ factors through a surjective \'etale morphism $f' : U \to X'$.
Moreover, if $R = U \times_X U$, then $R = U \times_{X'} U$ and $X'$ has
the presentation $X' = U/R$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian. Then
$i$ is regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

\label{lemma-regular-immersion-noetherian}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian. Then
$i$ is regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

generating the unit ideal. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
formulation.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ be elements of $R$
generating the unit ideal. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
The sequence
$$
0 \to
M \xrightarrow{\alpha}
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1}^n M_{f_i} \xrightarrow{\beta}
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i, j = 1}^n M_{f_i f_j}
$$
is exact, where $\alpha(m) = (m/1, \ldots, m/1)$
and $\beta(m_1/f_1^{e_1}, \ldots, m_n/f_n^{e_n})
= (m_i/f_i^{e_i} - m_j/f_j^{e_j})_{(i, j)}$.

If the underlying topological space of $X$ is Noetherian and
$\dim(X) \leq 1$, then $\Pic(X) \to \Pic(Z)$ is surjective.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-diagonal-morphism-finite-type}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with diagonal
$\Delta : X \to X \times_Y X$. If $f$ is locally of finite type
then $\Delta$ is locally of finite presentation. If $f$ is quasi-separated
and locally of finite type, then $\Delta$ is of finite presentation.

hypotheses: For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$, let $\omega_X^\bullet=f^!k\in D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the normalized relative dualizing complex of the structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$, and put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(\omega_X^\bullet)$. Its Grothendieck duality property is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^i(K,\omega_X^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,K),k)$ functorially for $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional then $\omega_X^\bullet\simeq\omega_X[1]$, so Serre duality is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^{i+1}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,\mathcal F),k)$. If $X$ is a smooth curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

A one-dimensional equidimensional closed subscheme $Z\subset\mathbf P_k^2$ without embedded associated points is Cohen–Macaulay, and its saturated homogeneous defining ideal $I(Z)\subset k[T_0,T_1,T_2]$ is generated by a single nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$. For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$, let $\omega_X^\bullet=f^!k\in D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the normalized relative dualizing complex of the structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$, and put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(\omega_X^\bullet)$. Its Grothendieck duality property is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^i(K,\omega_X^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,K),k)$ functorially for $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional then $\omega_X^\bullet\simeq\omega_X[1]$, so Serre duality is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^{i+1}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,\mathcal F),k)$. If $X$ is a smooth curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

A one-dimensional equidimensional closed subscheme $Z\subset\mathbf P_k^2$ without embedded associated points is Cohen–Macaulay, and its saturated homogeneous defining ideal $I(Z)\subset k[T_0,T_1,T_2]$ is generated by a single nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$. Such a $Z$ is an integral curve exactly when $F$ is irreducible. Its arithmetic genus, when $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=k$, is $g(Z)=\dim_kH^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

Let $X$ be a proper curve over a field $k$ with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$.
If $X$ is Gorenstein and has genus $0$, then $X$
is isomorphic to a plane curve of degree $2$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $\Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra.
Let $\pi \in R$ and assume that $\text{Ann}_R(\pi) = \text{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and
$\text{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi) = \text{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$.
Let $A \to \Lambda$ and $D \to \Lambda$ be $R$-algebra maps with
$A$ and $D$ of finite presentation. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$, and
\item there exists an $R$-algebra map $A/\pi^4 A \to D/\pi^4 D$ compatible
with the maps to $\Lambda/\pi^4 \Lambda$.
\end{enumerate}
Then we can find an $R$-algebra map $B \to \Lambda$ with $B$ of finite
presentation and $R$-algebra maps $A \to B$ and $D \to B$
compatible with the maps to $\Lambda$ such that $H_{D/R}B \subset H_{B/D}$
and $H_{D/R}B \subset H_{B/R}$.

source.label: lemma-smoothness-dimension
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-smoothness-dimension}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a smooth morphism of locally Noetherian schemes.
For every point $x$ in $X$ with image $y$ in $Y$,
$$
\dim_x(X) = \dim_y(Y) + \dim_x(X_y),
$$
where $X_y$ denotes the fiber over $y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-product-representable-transformations}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F_i, G_i : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$, $i = 1, 2$.
Let $a_i : F_i \to G_i$, $i = 1, 2$
be representable transformations of functors.
Then
$$
a_1 \times a_2 : F_1 \times F_2 \longrightarrow G_1 \times G_2
$$
is a representable transformation of functors.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-generic-flatness-reduced-quasi-separated}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is reduced,
\item $f$ is quasi-separated,
\item $f$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open dense subspace $W \subset Y$ such that
the base change $X_W \to W$ of $f$ is flat and of finite presentation
and such that $\mathcal{F}|_{X_W}$ is flat over $W$ and of
finite presentation over $\mathcal{O}_{X_W}$.

conclusions: The property "normal" holds on S exactly when it holds on all covering schemes S_i.
hypotheses: S is a scheme; k is fixed when relevant; {S_i→S} is a smooth covering.
formulation.statement: Fix a nonnegative integer $k$ when the named property involves $(S_k)$ or $(R_k)$. Let $S$ be a scheme. The property "normal" (meaning each local ring is an integrally closed domain (using the usual normal-scheme convention)) is local for the smooth topology: for every smooth covering $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, the scheme $S$ has this property if and only if every member $S_i$ has it.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pin L4973: normality is smooth-local, not merely Zariski-local. The formulation uses normal local rings (integrally closed domains), retains arbitrary smooth ascent and surjective smooth descent, and neither assumes geometric normality nor drops one direction.

phase3.reason: The full proof checks Zariski locality, smooth ascent of normality via the cited algebra lemma, and normality descent under faithfully flat surjective smooth affine maps; it then applies the local-property criterion.

formulation.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $f, g \in R(X)^*$. Then
$$
\text{div}_X(fg) = \text{div}_X(f) + \text{div}_X(g)
$$
as Weil divisors on $X$.

\label{lemma-div-additive}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $f, g \in R(X)^*$. Then
$$
\text{div}_X(fg) = \text{div}_X(f) + \text{div}_X(g)
$$
as Weil divisors on $X$.

\label{lemma-stackify-groupoids-universal-property}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category fibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$. Let $p' : \mathcal{S}' \to \mathcal{C}$ and
$G : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{S}'$
the stack in groupoids and $1$-morphism constructed in
Lemma \ref{lemma-stackify-groupoids}.
This construction has the following universal property: Given a stack
in groupoids $q : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{C}$ and a $1$-morphism
$F : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{X}$ of categories over $\mathcal{C}$
there exists a $1$-morphism $H : \mathcal{S}' \to \mathcal{X}$
such that the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{S} \ar[rr]_F \ar[rd]_G & & \mathcal{X} \\
& \mathcal{S}' \ar[ru]_H
}
$$
is $2$-commutative.

formulation.statement:
In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

An open (respectively closed, locally closed) immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism which, after every base change by a scheme, is an open (respectively closed, locally closed) immersion of schemes.

Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.
A composition of (closed, resp.\ open) immersions of
algebraic spaces over $S$ is a (closed, resp.\ open)
immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.

Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.

algebraic spaces over $S$ is a (closed, resp.\ open)
immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-upstairs-finite-type-injective-into-flat-mod-m}
Let $A \to B$ be a local ring homomorphism of local rings which is
essentially of finite type. Let $u : N \to M$ be a $B$-module map.
If $N$ is a finite $B$-module, $M$ is flat over $A$, and
$\overline{u} : N/\mathfrak m_A N \to M/\mathfrak m_A M$ is injective,
then $u$ is $A$-universally injective, $N$ is of finite presentation over
$B$, and $N$ is flat over $A$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $p : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism.
Suppose $\alpha, \beta \in Z_k(X)$ are rationally equivalent.
Then $p_*\alpha$ is rationally equivalent to $p_*\beta$.

The exact Stage B implication keeps both properness and the equivalence conclusion for p_*alpha,p_*beta; no generically-finite hypothesis has been inserted.

\label{lemma-proper-pushforward-rational-equivalence}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $p : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism.
Suppose $\alpha, \beta \in Z_k(X)$ are rationally equivalent.
Then $p_*\alpha$ is rationally equivalent to $p_*\beta$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $N$ be an $S$-module.
If $N$ is $I$-adically complete, then for any $R$-module $M$ and
for any prime $\mathfrak q \subset S$ which is an associated prime of
$N \otimes_R M$ we have $\mathfrak q + I S \not = S$.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F_i, G_i : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$, $i = 1, 2$.

Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal of $R$
and let $J \subset S$ be an ideal of $S$. If the closure of the image
of $V(J)$ in $\Spec(R)$ is disjoint from $V(I)$, then there exists
an element $f \in R$ which maps to $1$ in $R/I$ and to an element
of $J$ in $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-create-map-from-subcollection}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a collection
of opens of $X$. Assume $X = \bigcup_{U \in \mathcal{B}} U$ and
for $U, V \in \mathcal{B}$ we have
$U \cap V = \bigcup_{W \in \mathcal{B}, W \subset U \cap V} W$.
Then there is a continuous map $f : X \to Y$ of topological spaces
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the image $f(U)$ is open,
\item for $U \in \mathcal{B}$ we have $f^{-1}(f(U)) = U$, and
\item the opens $f(U)$, $U \in \mathcal{B}$
form a basis for the topology on $Y$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-proj-finite-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra. Let
$p : X = \underline{\text{Proj}}_S(\mathcal{A}) \to S$ be the relative
Proj of $\mathcal{A}$. If $\mathcal{A}$ is a finitely presented
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra, then $p$ is of finite presentation
and $\mathcal{O}_X(d)$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation.

formulation.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $X = U \cup V$ be
the union of two open subspaces of $X$. Suppose given
\begin{enumerate}
\item an object $A$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$,
\item an object $B$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_V)$, and
\item an isomorphism $c : A|_{U \cap V} \to B|_{U \cap V}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an object $F$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
and isomorphisms $f : F|_U \to A$, $g : F|_V \to B$ such
that $c = g|_{U \cap V} \circ f^{-1}|_{U \cap V}$.
Moreover, given
\begin{enumerate}
\item an object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item a morphism $a : A \to E|_U$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$,
\item a morphism $b : B \to E|_V$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_V)$, 
\end{enumerate}
such that
$$
a|_{U \cap V}  = b|_{U \cap V} \circ c.
$$
Then there exists a morphism $F \to E$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
whose restriction to $U$ is $a \circ f$
and whose restriction to $V$ is $b \circ g$.

source.label: lemma-glue
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glue}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $X = U \cup V$ be
the union of two open subspaces of $X$. Suppose given
\begin{enumerate}
\item an object $A$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$,
\item an object $B$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_V)$, and
\item an isomorphism $c : A|_{U \cap V} \to B|_{U \cap V}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an object $F$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
and isomorphisms $f : F|_U \to A$, $g : F|_V \to B$ such
that $c = g|_{U \cap V} \circ f^{-1}|_{U \cap V}$.
Moreover, given
\begin{enumerate}
\item an object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item a morphism $a : A \to E|_U$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$,
\item a morphism $b : B \to E|_V$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_V)$, 
\end{enumerate}
such that
$$
a|_{U \cap V}  = b|_{U \cap V} \circ c.
$$
Then there exists a morphism $F \to E$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
whose restriction to $U$ is $a \circ f$
and whose restriction to $V$ is $b \circ g$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universally-injective-to-completion}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map, and $N$ an $S$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a Noetherian ring,
\item $S$ is a Noetherian ring,
\item $N$ is a finite $S$-module, and
\item for any finite $R$-module $Q$, any
$\mathfrak q \in \text{Ass}_S(Q \otimes_R N)$
satisfies $IS + \mathfrak q \not = S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map $N \to N^\wedge$ of $N$ into the $I$-adic completion of $N$
is universally injective as a map of $R$-modules.

formulation.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $X$ be an affine integral normal scheme with separably closed
function field. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme. Let
$V \to Z$ be an \'etale morphism with $V$ affine. Then $V$ is a finite
disjoint union of open subschemes of $Z$. If $V \to Z$ is
surjective and finite \'etale, then $V \to Z$ has a section.

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\varphi$ is regular,
\item $S$ is Noetherian, and
\item $R$ is Noetherian and reduced.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-zero-scheme}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Consider closed immersions $i : Z \to X$ such that
$i^*s \in \Gamma(Z, i^*\mathcal{L})$ is zero
ordered by inclusion. The zero scheme $Z(s)$ is the
maximal element of this ordered set.
\item For any morphism of schemes $f : Y \to X$ we have
$f^*s = 0$ in $\Gamma(Y, f^*\mathcal{L})$ if and only if
$f$ factors through $Z(s)$.
\item The zero scheme $Z(s)$ is a locally principal closed subscheme.
\item The zero scheme $Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor
if and only if $s$ is a regular section of $\mathcal{L}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-derived-adjoint-functors}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and $G : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$
be functors of abelian categories such that $F$ is a right adjoint to $G$.
If the derived functors $RF : D(\mathcal{A}) \to D(\mathcal{B})$ and
$LG : D(\mathcal{B}) \to D(\mathcal{A})$ exist, then
$RF$ is a right adjoint to $LG$.

source.label: lemma-descent-quasi-compact
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descent-quasi-compact}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $g : Y' \to Y$ be a universally open and surjective morphism of
algebraic spaces such that the base change $f' : X' \to Y'$ is quasi-compact.
Then $f$ is quasi-compact.

\label{lemma-triangle-sections-with-support}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $i : Z \to X$ be the
inclusion of a closed subset. Let $U = X \setminus Z$.
There is a distinguished triangle
$$
R\Gamma_Z(X, K) \to R\Gamma(X, K) \to R\Gamma(U, K) \to
R\Gamma_Z(X, K)[1]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_X(X))$ functorial for $K$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category, and let $J$ and $J'$ be topologies on $\mathcal{C}$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For Grothendieck topologies J,J' on the same category C, J⊆J' iff every J'-sheaf is a J-sheaf. The source merely refers back to the prior theorem for C,J,J'; the candidate explicitly supplies those binders and preserves the biconditional and its direction.

phase3.reason: If every J'-sheaf is a J-sheaf, the J'-sheafification factors through J-sheafification. Applying this to a sieve S→h_U, any J-cover gives an isomorphism after J-sheafification and therefore after J'-sheafification, so it is a J'-cover by the preceding sieve characterization.

Let $k$ be a field. Set $S = \Spec(k[[t]])$ and
$S_n = \Spec(k[t]/(t^n))$. Let $Y \to S$ be a proper, flat morphism
of schemes whose special fibre $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay and
equidimensional of dimension $d$. Denote $X_n = Y \times_S S_n$.

contains $t^{n - 1}$, then the generic fibre of $Y \to S$ is smooth.

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a presheaf on $\Sch/S$. Then
$\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology
if and only if
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the sheaf property with respect to the
Zariski topology, and
\item for every faithfully flat morphism $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$
of affine schemes over $S$, the sheaf axiom holds for the covering
$\{\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)\}$. Namely, this means that
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(A)) \ar[r] &
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B)) \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B \otimes_A B))
}
$$
is an equalizer diagram.
\end{enumerate}
The affine test uses B⊗_A B and the two restriction maps. The Zariski sheaf axiom must be checked on all S-schemes; the affine faithfully flat test is sufficient *together* with it.
hypotheses:
A *site* $\mathcal C$ is a small category endowed with covering families $\{U_i\to U\}$ satisfying the isomorphism, composition/refinement, and base-change axioms. A *presheaf* of sets (or abelian groups) is a contravariant functor. For a covering, a *matching family* consists of sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose restrictions to every fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ coincide (including $i=j$). A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

For a base scheme $S$, let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ denote **all schemes over $S$** (using the source's size conventions). An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a presheaf on $\Sch/S$. Then
$\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology
if and only if
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the sheaf property with respect to the
Zariski topology, and
\item for every faithfully flat morphism $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$
of affine schemes over $S$, the sheaf axiom holds for the covering
$\{\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)\}$. Namely, this means that
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(A)) \ar[r] &
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B)) \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B \otimes_A B))
}
$$
is an equalizer diagram.
\end{enumerate}

**Scope and interpretation:** The affine test uses B⊗_A B and the two restriction maps. The Zariski sheaf axiom must be checked on all S-schemes; the affine faithfully flat test is sufficient *together* with it.

\label{lemma-proper-h-descent}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Let $\{g_i : S_i \to S\}$
be a h covering. Then $\alpha$ is proper
if and only if each base change $g_i^*\alpha$ is proper.

\label{lemma-closed-fp}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $R$.
Let $S = R/I$.
Then the image of a constructible subset of $\Spec(S)$
is constructible in $\Spec(R)$.

\label{lemma-homology-complex}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms
with fixed target such that all fibre products
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}$ exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
The chain complex $\mathbf{Z}_{\mathcal{U}, \bullet}$ of presheaves
of Lemma \ref{lemma-cech-map-into} above is exact in positive
degrees, i.e., the homology presheaves
$H_i(\mathbf{Z}_{\mathcal{U}, \bullet})$ are zero for $i > 0$.

Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf
of $A$-algebras. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Then we have
$$
R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})^\wedge =
R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\wedge)
$$
in $D(A)$ where $\mathcal{F}^\wedge$ is the derived
completion of $\mathcal{F}$ with respect to $I\mathcal{O}$ and on the
left hand wide we have the derived completion with respect to $I$.
This produces two spectral sequences
$$
E_2^{i, j} = H^i(H^j(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})^\wedge)
\quad\text{and}\quad
E_2^{p, q} = H^p(\mathcal{C}, H^q(\mathcal{F}^\wedge))
$$
both converging to
$H^*(R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})^\wedge) =
H^*(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\wedge)$

source.label: lemma-formal-functions-general
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-formal-functions-general}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf
of $A$-algebras. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Then we have
$$
R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})^\wedge =
R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\wedge)
$$
in $D(A)$ where $\mathcal{F}^\wedge$ is the derived
completion of $\mathcal{F}$ with respect to $I\mathcal{O}$ and on the
left hand wide we have the derived completion with respect to $I$.
This produces two spectral sequences
$$
E_2^{i, j} = H^i(H^j(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})^\wedge)
\quad\text{and}\quad
E_2^{p, q} = H^p(\mathcal{C}, H^q(\mathcal{F}^\wedge))
$$
both converging to
$H^*(R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})^\wedge) =
H^*(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\wedge)$

\label{lemma-projection-formula-perfect}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and $K \in D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $K$ is perfect, then
$$
Rf_*E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_Y} K =
Rf_*(E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} Lf^*K)

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stack-in-groupoids-equivalent}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{S}_1$, $\mathcal{S}_2$ be categories over $\mathcal{C}$.
Suppose that $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are equivalent
as categories over $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $\mathcal{S}_1$ is a stack in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if
$\mathcal{S}_2$ is a stack in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$.

of $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$, and $\mathcal{H}$ is $\leq k$.
Then $[\mathcal{G}]_k = [\mathcal{F}]_k + [\mathcal{H}]_k$.

\label{lemma-isom-depth-2-torsion-free}
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme. Let
$\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Assume $\mathcal{F}$ is coherent,
$\mathcal{G}$ is torsion free, and that for every $x \in X$ one of the
following happens
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}_x \to \mathcal{G}_x$ is an isomorphism, or
\item $\text{depth}(\mathcal{F}_x) \geq 2$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-fibres-nr-geometrically-connected-components}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let
$$
n_{X/Y} : Y \to \{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, \infty\}
$$
be the function which associates to $y \in Y$ the number of connected
components of $(X_y)_K$ where $K$ is a separably closed extension
of $\kappa(y)$. This is well defined and if $g : Y' \to Y$ is a morphism
then
$$
n_{X'/Y'} = n_{X/Y} \circ g
$$
where $X' \to Y'$ is the base change of $f$.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of
schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $c \in A^p(X \to Z)$ and assume $f$ is proper.
Then the rule that to $Z' \to Z$ assigns
$\alpha \longmapsto f'_*(c \cap \alpha)$
is a bivariant class denoted $f_* \circ c \in A^p(Y \to Z)$.

Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of

source.label: lemma-classifying-stacks
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-classifying-stacks}
\begin{slogan}
The classifying stack of a group scheme or group algebraic space.
\end{slogan}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $B$. Then the stacks
in groupoids
$$
[B/G],\quad
[[B/G]],\quad
G\textit{-Torsors},\quad
\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}\textit{-Torsors}
$$
are all canonically equivalent.
If $G \to B$ is flat and locally
of finite presentation, then these are also equivalent to
$G\textit{-Principal}$.

\label{lemma-composition-representable-transformations}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$, $b : G \to H$ be representable transformations of functors.
Then
$$
b \circ a : F \longrightarrow H
$$
is a representable transformation of functors.

\label{lemma-base-change-dimension-fibres}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of finite type. Let
$$
n_{X/Y} : Y \to \{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, \infty\}
$$
be the function which associates to $y \in Y$ the dimension of $X_y$.
If $g : Y' \to Y$ is a morphism then
$$
n_{X'/Y'} = n_{X/Y} \circ g
$$
where $X' \to Y'$ is the base change of $f$.

Let $X$ be a topological space.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $U \subset S$ an open. If

\item $U \subset S$ is retrocompact and scheme theoretically dense,
\end{enumerate}
then $f$ is an open immersion.

conclusions: $i$ is a regular immersion.
hypotheses:
Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. If $Z$ and $X$ are
regular schemes,
formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. If $Z$ and $X$ are
regular schemes, then $i$ is a regular immersion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-shriek-lqf-and-proper}
Consider a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[r]_f \ar[rd]_g & Y \ar[d]^h \\
& Z
}
$$
with $f$ and $g$ locally quasi-finite and $h$ proper. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
Funtorially in $K \in D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ there is a canonical map
$$
g_!K \longrightarrow Rh_*(f_!K)
$$
in $D(Z_\etale, \Lambda)$. This map is an isomorphism if
(a) $K$ is bounded below and has torsion cohomology sheaves, or
(b) $\Lambda$ is a torsion ring.

hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

If $R$ is henselian and $A$ is a finite $R$-algebra, then $A$ is a finite
product of henselian local rings.

**Precise scope:** Every finite R-algebra A is a *finite product* of henselian local rings, not simply a ring with henselian maximal-ideal localizations in an uncontrolled infinite family.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module. The closed subschemes
$$
S = Z_{-1} \supset Z_0 \supset Z_1 \supset Z_2 \ldots
$$
defined by the Fitting ideals of $\mathcal{F}$ have the following
properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item The intersection $\bigcap Z_r$ is empty.
\item The functor $(\Sch/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ defined by the rule
$$
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ is locally generated by }
\leq r\text{ sections} \\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
is representable by the open subscheme $S \setminus Z_r$.
\item The functor $F_r : (\Sch/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ defined by the rule
$$
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ locally free rank }r\\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
is representable by the locally closed subscheme $Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r$
of $S$.
\end{enumerate}
If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, then
$Z_r \to S$, $S \setminus Z_r \to S$, and $Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r \to S$
are of finite presentation.
Here $\mathcal F_T$ denotes pullback along $T\to S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-dualizing-flat-vanishing}
Let $R \to A$ be a flat finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\mathfrak q \subset A$ be a prime ideal lying over
$\mathfrak p \subset R$. Then
$$
H^i(\omega_{A/R}^\bullet)_\mathfrak q \not = 0
\Rightarrow - d \leq i \leq 0
$$
where $d$ is the dimension of the fibre of $\Spec(A) \to \Spec(R)$
over $\mathfrak p$ at the point $\mathfrak q$. If all fibres of
$\Spec(A) \to \Spec(R)$ have dimension $\leq d$, then
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ has tor amplitude in $[-d, 0]$
as a complex of $R$-modules.

\label{lemma-codimension-local-ring}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Y \subset X$ be an irreducible closed
subset. Let $\xi \in Y$ be the generic point. Then
$$
\text{codim}(Y, X) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi})
$$
where the codimension is as defined in
Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-codimension}.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is a Grothendieck

has enough injectives and all limits.

$\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has a right adjoint\footnote{This functor is sometimes called

Q : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \longrightarrow \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
such that for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction mapping

\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-coherator}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is a Grothendieck
abelian category. Consequently, $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has enough injectives and all limits.
\item The inclusion functor
$\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has a right adjoint\footnote{This functor is sometimes called
the {\it coherator}.}
$$
Q : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \longrightarrow \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
such that for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction mapping
$Q(\mathcal{F}) \to \mathcal{F}$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

Let $A,B$ be graded rings, $\psi:A\to B$ a graded ring map, $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. Put $U(\psi)=\bigcup_{f\in A_+\text{ homogeneous}}D_+(\psi(f))\subset Y$ and let $r_\psi:U(\psi)\to X$ and $\theta_\psi$ be the canonical morphism and graded-sheaf map of the source lemma. 
Assume $A_d \to B_d$ is surjective for all $d \gg 0$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U(\psi) = Y$,
\item $r_\psi : Y \to X$ is a closed immersion, and
\item the maps $\theta : r_\psi^*\mathcal{O}_X(n) \to \mathcal{O}_Y(n)$
are surjective but not isomorphisms in general (even if $A \to B$ is
surjective).
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: Eventually surjective homogeneous graded components yield global coverage, a closed immersion and surjective twist maps; the source tests the claims on standard opens and gives an illustrative counterexample to stronger claims.

\label{lemma-extension-torsion-free}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let
$0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{F}'' \to 0$

is torsion free.

source.label: lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
Let $X_s$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$.
\item The point $x$ is isolated in $X_s$.
\item The point $x$ is closed in $X_s$
and there is no point $x' \in X_s$, $x' \not = x$
which specializes to $x$.
\item For any pair of affine opens
$\Spec(A) = U \subset X$, $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with
$f(U) \subset V$ and $x \in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q \subset A$
the ring map $R \to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-lift-idempotent}
Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal, let $\overline{e} \in A/I$
be an idempotent. There exists an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ which
induces an isomorphism $A/I \to A'/IA'$ and an idempotent $e' \in A'$
lifting $\overline{e}$.

\label{lemma-standard-open-proj}
Let $S$ be a graded ring. Let $f \in S$ be homogeneous of positive degree.
Suppose that $D(g) \subset \Spec(S_{(f)})$ is a standard open.
Then there exists an $h \in S$ homogeneous of positive degree such that
$D(g)$ corresponds to $D_{+}(h) \subset D_{+}(f)$ via the homeomorphism
of Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-topology-proj}. In fact we can
take $h$ such that $g = h/f^n$ for some $n$.

\label{lemma-pro-isomorphism}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category. Let
$$
A_n \to B_n \to C_n \to A_n[1]
$$
be an inverse system of distinguished triangles. If the system $C_n$
is pro-zero (essentially constant with value $0$), then the maps
$A_n \to B_n$ determine a pro-isomorphism between the pro-object $(A_n)$
and the pro-object $(B_n)$.

\label{lemma-write-as-colimit}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category with direct sums.
Let $E_i$, $i \in I$ be a family of compact objects of $\mathcal{D}$
such that $\bigoplus E_i$ generates $\mathcal{D}$.
Then every object $X$ of $\mathcal{D}$ can be written as
$$
X = \text{hocolim} X_n
$$
where $X_1$ is a direct sum of shifts of the $E_i$ and each transition
morphism fits into a distinguished triangle
$Y_n \to X_n \to X_{n + 1} \to Y_n[1]$
where $Y_n$ is a direct sum of shifts of the $E_i$.

\label{lemma-covering}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Let $k \geq 0$ be an integer.
Let $u : Z \to K_k$ be a covering
in $\text{SR}(\mathcal{C}, X)$.
Then there exists a morphism of hypercoverings
$f: L \to K$ such that $L_k \to K_k$
factors through $u$.

conclusions: The Gysin morphisms form a chain map with respect to the de Rham differential.
hypotheses: $Z$ is cut out by the given functions on $X/S$, and $\gamma^p$ is the indicated local-cohomology Gysin map.
formulation.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, let $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ be global functions on $X$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be their common vanishing subscheme. For each $p\geq0$, define the local Gysin morphism
$$\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$$
by the local cohomology/Čech class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$, for a lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$. Then the Gysin maps commute with the de Rham differentials:
$$d\circ\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}=\gamma^{p+1}_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}\circ d.$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original pinned derham.tex L5183–5217 defines LOCAL GYSIN maps for Z cut out by f1,…,fc on X using the Čech/local-cohomology class of lifted forms wedged with df1⋯dfc. Lemma L5214–5218 asserts they COMMUTE WITH de Rham differentials. The proposal reproduces the correct shift of form degree p→p+c, local cohomology index c, and differential identity.

phase3.reason: The exterior differential is a morphism of abelian sheaves, inducing maps on local cohomology compatible with the extended Čech complex. Differentiating the local Gysin fraction introduces only d(omega), since d(df_i)=0 and repeated df_i terms vanish; this gives the chain-map compatibility.

source.label: lemma-glue-maps
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glue-maps}
\begin{slogan}
Maps of sheaves glue.
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\{U_i \to U\}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$.
Given a collection
$$
\varphi_i :
\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i}
$$
of maps of sheaves such that for all $i, j \in I$ the maps
$\varphi_i, \varphi_j$ restrict to the same map
$\varphi_{ij} : \mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j} \to
\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U_i \times_U U_j}$
then there exists a unique map of sheaves
$$
\varphi :
\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U}
$$
whose restriction to each $\mathcal{C}/U_i$ agrees with $\varphi_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unramified-G-unramified}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $f$ is G-unramified if and only if $f$ is unramified and
locally of finite presentation.

of schemes locally of finite type over $S$ whose horizontal arrows
are closed immersions. Let $\mathcal{N}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{N}'$
be a virtual normal sheaf for $Z \subset X$, resp.\ $Z' \to X'$.
Assume given a short exact sequence
$0 \to \mathcal{N}' \to g^*\mathcal{N} \to \mathcal{E} \to 0$
of finite locally free modules on $Z'$ such that the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
g^*\mathcal{N}^\vee \ar[r] \ar[d] &
(\mathcal{N}')^\vee \ar[d] \\
g^*\mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \ar[r] &
\mathcal{C}_{Z'/X'}
}
$$
commutes. Then we have
$$
res(c(Z \to X, \mathcal{N})) =
c_{top}(\mathcal{E}) \circ c(Z' \to X', \mathcal{N}')
$$
in $A^*(Z' \to X')^\wedge$.

For a unital map of commutative rings $u:R\to S$, going down means: for every chain $\mathfrak p\subset\mathfrak p^\prime$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$, there exists $\mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p$. If the induced map
$\varphi : \Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$ is open, then
$R \to S$ satisfies going down.

\label{lemma-flat-finite-type-affine-neighbourhood-projective}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism which is locally of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module which is
of finite type. Let $x \in X$ with $s = f(x) \in S$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$ there exists an affine
elementary \'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$ and
an affine open $U' \subset X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$
which contains $x' = (x, s')$ such that
$\Gamma(U', \mathcal{F}|_{U'})$ is a free
$\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$-module.

formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

A simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ consists of $A$-algebras $P_n$ and simplicial face and degeneracy maps. An augmentation $P_\bullet\to B$ views $B$ as a constant simplicial algebra. A trivial Kan fibration on underlying simplicial sets has the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$. The $n$-skeleton $\operatorname{sk}_n(P_\bullet)$ retains degrees through $n$; the $n$-coskeleton $\operatorname{cosk}_n$ freely reconstructs compatible higher simplices by a right Kan extension. The condition $P_\bullet=\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nP_\bullet$ says it is $n$-coskeletal.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map.
Then $H^n(L_{B/A})$ is a finite $B$-module for all $n \in \mathbf{Z}$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L655–659 assumes A Noetherian and A→B finite type; it concludes for EVERY integer n that H^n(L_{B/A}) is a finite B-module. The proposal keeps all integer quantifiers, finite generation, and ring map assumptions, and does not replace the cohomology conclusion by a boundedness assertion.

For a ringed site (C,O), a complex E^bullet is **perfect** when after a covering of every site object it has a quasi-isomorphism from a **strictly perfect** complex (bounded, termwise direct summand of finite free O-modules); a derived object is perfect if represented by such a complex (source Definition perfect at 12734–12746). A perfect object is **not assumed globally bounded** unless the topos is quasi-compact. Its relation to pseudo-coherence and local finite Tor dimension is an equivalence only where stated, not an inherited hypothesis. The input E is on the **target** ringed site (D,O_D), and the derived pullback goes to the source site (C,O_C). No flatness of f is required.

Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
be a morphism of ringed sites.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$.
If $E$ is perfect in $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$,
then $Lf^*E$ is perfect in $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-finite-type-quasi-finite-part}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Then there exists a canonical open subspace $X' \subset X$ such that
$f|_{X'} : X' \to Y$ is locally quasi-finite, and such that the
relative dimension of $f$ at any $x \in |X|$, $x \not \in |X'|$ is
$\geq 1$. Formation of $X'$ commutes with arbitrary base change.

formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be Noetherian with a dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$. At each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ let $\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)$ be the unique integer such that the stalk-localization $\omega_{A,\mathfrak p}^\bullet[-\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)]$ is normalized over $A_{\mathfrak p}$, meaning its derived Hom from $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[0]$. This is a *dimension function*: across an immediate specialization $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ of height-one difference, $\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)=\delta_\omega(\mathfrak q)+1$. Suppose $\varphi:A\twoheadrightarrow B=A/I$ is a surjective homomorphism of Noetherian rings, and choose $\omega_B^\bullet=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,\omega_A^\bullet)$ as the induced dualizing complex over $B$. Then the induced dimension functions satisfy
\[
\delta_{\omega_B^\bullet}(\mathfrak q)=\delta_{\omega_A^\bullet}(\varphi^{-1}\mathfrak q)
\qquad(\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B).
\]
The isomorphism is the restriction of the numerical function under the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quotient-function}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing
complex. Let $A \to B$ be a surjective ring map and let
$\omega_B^\bullet = R\Hom(B, \omega_A^\bullet)$ be the dualizing
complex for $B$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-dualizing-quotient}. Then we have
$$
\delta_{\omega_B^\bullet} = \delta_{\omega_A^\bullet}|_{\Spec(B)}
$$
