\label{lemma-characterize-integral}
A scheme $X$ is integral if and only if it is reduced and irreducible.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

Let $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(Y, \mathcal{L})$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_\delta(Y) \leq k + 1$,
\item $\dim_\delta(Z(s)) \leq k$, and
\item for every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of
$Z(s)$ of $\delta$-dimension $k$ the multiplication by $s$
induces an injection $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi} \to \mathcal{L}_\xi$.
\end{enumerate}
Write $[Y]_{k + 1} = \sum n_i[Y_i]$ where $Y_i \subset Y$ are the
irreducible components of $Y$ of $\delta$-dimension $k + 1$.
Set $s_i = s|_{Y_i} \in \Gamma(Y_i, \mathcal{L}|_{Y_i})$. Then
\begin{equation}
\label{equation-equal-as-cycles}
[Z(s)]_k =  \sum n_i[Z(s_i)]_k
\end{equation}
as $k$-cycles on $Y$.

\label{lemma-degree-pullback-map-proper-curves}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a nonconstant morphism of
proper curves over $k$. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally free
$\mathcal{O}_Y$-module. Then
$$
\deg(f^*\mathcal{E}) = \deg(X/Y) \deg(\mathcal{E})
$$

\label{lemma-direct-sum-triangles}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a pre-triangulated category.
Let $(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)$ and $(X', Y', Z', f', g', h')$ be triangles.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(X \oplus X', Y \oplus Y', Z \oplus Z',
f \oplus f', g \oplus g', h \oplus h')$
is a distinguished triangle,
\item both $(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)$ and $(X', Y', Z', f', g', h')$ are
distinguished triangles.
\end{enumerate}

$Q : \mathcal{C} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$ is additive.

\label{lemma-d-fitting-ideal-omega-smooth}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $d \geq 0$ be an integer.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat,
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation, and
\item every nonempty fibre of $f$ is equidimensional of dimension $d$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $Z \subset X$ be the closed subscheme cut out by the $d$th fitting
ideal of $\Omega_{X/S}$. Then $Z$ is exactly the set of points
where $f$ is not smooth.

conclusions:
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes.
Let $U, U'$ be schemes \'etale over $X$. Let $h : U_Z \to U'_Z$
be a morphism over $Z$. Then there exists a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U & W \ar[l]_a \ar[r]^b & U'
}
$$
in $X_\etale$ such that $a_Z : W_Z \to U_Z$
is an isomorphism and $h = b_Z \circ (a_Z)^{-1}$.
With $U_Z=U\times_XZ$ and $U'_Z$ defined likewise, $W\to U,W\to U'$ lie in the **small étale site of X**. The base-changed $W_Z\to U_Z$ is an isomorphism; the prescribed $h$ factors through the resulting inverse. A literal global lift $U\to U'$ is not claimed.
hypotheses:
Let $X_{\acute et}$ and $Y_{\acute et}$ denote the **small étale sites** of schemes $X$ and $Y$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})$ be the corresponding topoi of sheaves of sets, with structure sheaves of local rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ on these sites. A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$, $(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_\tau$ and $(\mathrm{Sch}/Y)_\tau$ denote the **big** $\tau$-sites (small-universe selections of schemes over the bases). A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces $f_{\mathrm{big}}:\operatorname{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/X)_\tau)\to\operatorname{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/Y)_\tau)$ with inverse image and direct image adjoints. A *monomorphism of schemes* is a morphism $f$ with injective functor-of-points maps $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)$ for every scheme $T$. A *closed immersion* realizes $X$ as a closed subscheme of $Y$; its étale base changes remain closed immersions. A site functor is **almost cocontinuous** when pullbacks of covering families are locally refinable by covering families whose pieces either map into a source cover member or map to the empty scheme; this is the weaker lifting criterion used for big-site direct image exactness.

Let $X_{\acute et}$ and $Y_{\acute et}$ denote the **small étale sites** of schemes $X$ and $Y$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})$ be the corresponding topoi of sheaves of sets, with structure sheaves of local rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ on these sites. A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$, $(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_\tau$ and $(\mathrm{Sch}/Y)_\tau$ denote the **big** $\tau$-sites (small-universe selections of schemes over the bases). A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces $f_{\mathrm{big}}:\operatorname{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/X)_\tau)\to\operatorname{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/Y)_\tau)$ with inverse image and direct image adjoints. A *monomorphism of schemes* is a morphism $f$ with injective functor-of-points maps $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)$ for every scheme $T$. A *closed immersion* realizes $X$ as a closed subscheme of $Y$; its étale base changes remain closed immersions. A site functor is **almost cocontinuous** when pullbacks of covering families are locally refinable by covering families whose pieces either map into a source cover member or map to the empty scheme; this is the weaker lifting criterion used for big-site direct image exactness.

**Statement (with original hypotheses):**
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes.
Let $U, U'$ be schemes \'etale over $X$. Let $h : U_Z \to U'_Z$
be a morphism over $Z$. Then there exists a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U & W \ar[l]_a \ar[r]^b & U'
}
$$
in $X_\etale$ such that $a_Z : W_Z \to U_Z$
is an isomorphism and $h = b_Z \circ (a_Z)^{-1}$.

**Scope of conclusion:** With $U_Z=U\times_XZ$ and $U'_Z$ defined likewise, $W\to U,W\to U'$ lie in the **small étale site of X**. The base-changed $W_Z\to U_Z$ is an isomorphism; the prescribed $h$ factors through the resulting inverse. A literal global lift $U\to U'$ is not claimed.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-immersion-almost-full}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes.
Let $U, U'$ be schemes \'etale over $X$. Let $h : U_Z \to U'_Z$
be a morphism over $Z$. Then there exists a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U & W \ar[l]_a \ar[r]^b & U'
}
$$
in $X_\etale$ such that $a_Z : W_Z \to U_Z$
is an isomorphism and $h = b_Z \circ (a_Z)^{-1}$.

phase2.hold_reason: The original theorem cites 'More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-K-flat}'. Although the preface paraphrases K-flatness for sheaves and points, it does not inline the ordinary-complex K-flat definition and the final statement retains the unresolved cross-chapter reference. Both directions have different hypotheses (only the converse requires enough points), so the corrected theorem must retain this asymmetry.
phase2.proposed_correction: Explicitly define ordinary stalk K-flatness as acyclicity of tensor with every acyclic O_p-complex, remove the More on Algebra LaTeX reference, and encode the two implication directions with the enough-points premise only in the converse; seek new independent approval.

phase3.reason: The proof checks the converse via stalkwise detection of acyclicity and proves forward direction through flat K-flat resolution, acyclic cones, neighbourhood filtered colimits and finitely presented stalk modules.

formulation.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. Suppose $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering and every morphism $X_i\to S_i$ is a closed immersion. Then $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is effective: it comes from a scheme over $S$, because each closed immersion is affine and fpqc descent data for affine morphisms are effective.

\label{lemma-closed-immersion}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is a closed immersion, then the descent datum is
effective.

formulation.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. The functor
$\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})} \to D(A, \text{d})$
has a natural structure of a $\delta$-functor, with
$$
\delta_{K \to L \to M} = - p \circ q^{-1}
$$
For a short exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow{a}L\xrightarrow{b}M\to0$, $q:C(a)\to M$ is the quasi-isomorphism induced by the projection of the cone onto $L$ followed by $b$, while $p:C(a)\to K[1]$ is the cone projection; $q^{-1}$ is taken in $D(A,\mathrm d)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For an exact sequence 0→K→L→M→0 of dg modules, the canonical δ-functor boundary is minus the cone projection p followed by inverse of q:C(a)→M in the derived category. The reconstructed definitions preserve that q is invertible only after localization and the negative sign from the pinned context.

phase3.reason: The cone projection construction yields a distinguished triangle for every short exact sequence, and the functoriality of cones makes the connecting morphism −p q^−1 natural. The proof cites the corresponding standard derived canonical delta-functor argument.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. The functor
$\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})} \to D(A, \text{d})$
defined has the natural structure of a $\delta$-functor, with
$$
\delta_{K \to L \to M} = - p \circ q^{-1}
$$
with $p$ and $q$ as explained above.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-torsion-in-pic}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let $f \in \mathfrak m$
be a nonzerodivisor and assume that $\text{depth}(A/fA) \geq 2$, or equivalently
$\text{depth}(A) \geq 3$. Let $U$, resp.\ $U_0$ be the punctured
spectrum of $A$, resp.\ $A/fA$. The map
$$
\Pic(U) \to \Pic(U_0)
$$
is injective on torsion.

\label{lemma-morphism-ringed-sites-almost-cocontinuous}
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites
associated to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
Assume $u$ is almost cocontinuous. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_* : \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{D}) \to \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$ is exact.
\item if $f^\sharp : f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$
is given so that $f$ becomes a morphism of ringed sites, then
$f_* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \to
\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})$ is exact.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-normalize-projective}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ be the normalization morphism, see
Morphisms, Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-normalization}.
Then $X^\nu$ is proper over $k$. If $X$ is projective over $k$,
then $X^\nu$ is projective over $k$.

hypotheses:
Let $A$ be Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a projective morphism. Let
$\mathcal{I} = I\mathcal{O}_X$.

Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
formulation.statement:
Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
Let $A$ be Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a projective morphism. Let
$\mathcal{I} = I\mathcal{O}_X$.
Then the functor $\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_X)\longrightarrow\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal{I}),\quad \mathcal{G}\longmapsto (\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{G})_{n\geq 1}$ is an equivalence.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For projective X over I-complete Noetherian A, the same completion functor is an equivalence, not merely fully faithful. The projective hypothesis is preserved and not weakened to proper in this source lemma.

phase3.reason: After full faithfulness, ample twisting lifts compatible global generators and presents each formal system as a cokernel of completed coherent sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-of-sites-covering}
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites given by the
functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$. Given any object $V$ of
$\mathcal{D}$ there exists a covering $\{V_j \to V\}$ such that for every
$j$ there exists a morphism $V_j \to u(U_j)$ for some object $U_j$
of $\mathcal{C}$.

is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-degree-finite-morphism-in-terms-degrees}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a finite
dominant morphism of proper varieties over $k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$
be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
$$
\deg_{f^*\mathcal{L}}(Y) = \deg(f) \deg_\mathcal{L}(X)
$$
where $\deg(f)$ is as in
Morphisms, Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-degree}.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-along-fibre-free-variant}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at all points of $X_s$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an elementary \'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
and a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d] & X' \ar[l]^g \ar[d] \\
S & \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}) \ar[l]
}
$$
such that $X' \to X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$
is \'etale, $X_s = g((X')_{s'})$, the scheme $X'$ is affine,
and such that $\Gamma(X', g^*\mathcal{F})$ is a free
$\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$-module.

A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

For a divided power ideal $(I,\gamma)$, $I^{[n]}$ is the ideal generated by products $\prod_j\gamma_{e_j}(x_j)$ with $x_j\in I$ and $\sum e_j\ge n$, with $I^{[0]}=A$ and $I^{[1]}=I$. The ideal $I^{[2]}$ consists of terms of divided-power order at least two.

Given a ring map $A\to B$ and a divided power ideal $(J,\delta)$ on $B$, a divided power $A$-derivation $d:B\to M$ into a $B$-module is additive, vanishes on $A$, satisfies $d(bb')=b\,d(b')+b'\,d(b)$, and $d(\delta_n(x))=\delta_{n-1}(x)d(x)$ for $x\in J$. The universal module representing such derivations is $\Omega_{B/A,\delta}$ with universal map $d_{B/A,\delta}$. The ordinary Kähler differential module $\Omega_{B/A}$ represents all $A$-derivations. For a divided power scheme $(T,\mathcal J,\delta)\to S$, the sheaf $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ represents divided power derivations and is the quotient of $\Omega_{T/S}$ by the divided-power derivative relations.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above,
Let $(U, T, \delta)$ be an object of $\text{Cris}(X/S)$.
Let
$$
(U(1), T(1), \delta(1)) = (U, T, \delta) \times (U, T, \delta)
$$
in $\text{Cris}(X/S)$. Let $\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{O}_{T(1)}$
be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals corresponding to the closed
immersion $\Delta : T \to T(1)$. Then
$\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{J}_{T(1)}$ is preserved by the
divided structure on $\mathcal{J}_{T(1)}$ and we have
$$
(\Omega_{X/S})_T = \mathcal{K}/\mathcal K^{[2]}
$$

Y \ar[r]^{F_Y} & Y
}
$$
commutes.

source.label: lemma-cofinal-essentially-constant
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cofinal-essentially-constant}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $H : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{J}$
be a functor of filtered index categories. If $H$ is cofinal, then
any diagram $M : \mathcal{J} \to \mathcal{C}$ is essentially constant
if and only if $M \circ H$ is essentially constant.

Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

U \ar[d]_p \ar[r]_g & V \ar[d]^q \\

source.label: lemma-properties-diagonal
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-properties-diagonal}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\Delta : F \to F \times F$ be the diagonal morphism.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta$ is locally of finite type,
\item $\Delta$ is a monomorphism,
\item $\Delta$ is separated, and
\item $\Delta$ is locally quasi-finite.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $U, V \subset X$ be quasi-compact open subschemes.
Let $b : V' \to V$ be a $U \cap V$-admissible blowup.
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $X' \to X$
whose restriction to $V$ is $V'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-admissible-blowups}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $U, V \subset X$ be quasi-compact open subschemes.
Let $b : V' \to V$ be a $U \cap V$-admissible blowup.
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $X' \to X$
whose restriction to $V$ is $V'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functorial-injective}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a Grothendieck abelian category.
There exists a functor $M^\bullet \mapsto \mathbf{N}^\bullet(M^\bullet)$
and a natural transformation
$j_{M^\bullet} : M^\bullet \to \mathbf{N}^\bullet(M^\bullet)$
such
\begin{enumerate}
\item $j_{M^\bullet}$ is a (termwise) injective quasi-isomorphism, and
\item for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ the map $M^n \to \mathbf{N}^n(M^\bullet)$
factors through a subobject $I^n \subset \mathbf{N}^n(M^\bullet)$ where $I^n$
is an injective object of $\mathcal{A}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-separated}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
If there exists a quasi-separated scheme $U$ and a surjective
\'etale morphism $U \to X$ such that either of the projections
$U \times_X U \to U$ is quasi-compact, then $X$ is quasi-separated.

\label{lemma-Noetherian-scheme-regular-ideal}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $x$ be a point of the support of
$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by a regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by an $H_1$-regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by a quasi-regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item there exists an affine neighbourhood $U = \Spec(A)$ of $x$ such
that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by a
regular sequence in $A$, and
\item there exists an affine neighbourhood $U = \Spec(A)$ of $x$ such
that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by a
Koszul-regular sequence in $A$, and
\item there exists an affine neighbourhood $U = \Spec(A)$ of $x$ such
that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by an
$H_1$-regular sequence in $A$, and
\item there exists an affine neighbourhood $U = \Spec(A)$ of $x$ such
that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by a
quasi-regular sequence in $A$,
\item there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\mathcal{J}|_U$
is regular, and
\item there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\mathcal{J}|_U$
is Koszul-regular, and
\item there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\mathcal{J}|_U$
is $H_1$-regular, and
\item there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\mathcal{J}|_U$
is quasi-regular.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, on a locally Noetherian scheme the notions of
regular, Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, or quasi-regular ideal sheaf all agree.

\label{lemma-weak-relative-noether-normalization}
Let $R \to S$ be a finite type ring map. Let $d$ be the maximum
of the dimensions of fibres of $\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$.
Then there exists a quasi-finite ring map
$R[t_1, \ldots, t_d] \to S$.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme of finite presentation.
Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up with center $Z$. Let $Z' \subset X'$ be
a closed subscheme of finite presentation.
Let $X'' \to X'$ be the blowing up with center $Z'$.
There exists a closed subscheme $Y \subset X$ of finite presentation,
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y = Z \cup b(Z')$ set theoretically, and
\item the composition $X'' \to X$ is isomorphic to the blowing up
of $X$ in $Y$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $Y \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $s \in \Gamma(Y, \mathcal{L}|_Y)$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_\delta(Y) \leq k + 1$,
\item $\dim_\delta(Z(s)) \leq k$, and
\item for every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of
$Z(s)$ of $\delta$-dimension $k$ the multiplication by $s$
induces an injection
$\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi} \to (\mathcal{L}|_Y)_\xi$\footnote{For example,
this holds if $s$ is a regular section of $\mathcal{L}|_Y$.}.
\end{enumerate}
Then
$$
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [Y]_{k + 1} = [Z(s)]_k
$$
in $\mathrm{CH}_k(X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometric-cap}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $Y \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $s \in \Gamma(Y, \mathcal{L}|_Y)$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_\delta(Y) \leq k + 1$,
\item $\dim_\delta(Z(s)) \leq k$, and
\item for every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of
$Z(s)$ of $\delta$-dimension $k$ the multiplication by $s$
induces an injection
$\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi} \to (\mathcal{L}|_Y)_\xi$\footnote{For example,
this holds if $s$ is a regular section of $\mathcal{L}|_Y$.}.
\end{enumerate}
Then
$$
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [Y]_{k + 1} = [Z(s)]_k
$$
in $\CH_k(X)$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a differential graded category over $R$ satisfying the following axioms. Axiom (A) requires a zero object and binary differential graded direct sums. Axiom (B) requires dg shift functors $[n]$, with $[0]=\mathrm{id}$ and $[n+m]=[n]\circ[m]$, and composition-compatible identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(x,y[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(x,y)[n]$ of dg modules. Axiom (C) requires, for every closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$, an admissible short exact sequence $y\to c(f)\to x[1]$ in $\operatorname{Comp}(\mathcal A)$ whose connecting morphism $x[1]\to y[1]$ agrees with $f[1]$.

\label{lemma-cohomological-descent-finite}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a surjective finite morphism of schemes.
Set $f_n : X_n \to Y$ equal to the $(n + 1)$-fold fibre product
of $X$ over $Y$. For $\mathcal{F} \in \textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$ set
$\mathcal{F}_n = f_{n, *}f_n^{-1}\mathcal{F}$. There is an exact
sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}_0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to
\mathcal{F}_2 \to \ldots
$$
on $Y_\etale$. Moreover, there is a spectral sequence
$$
E_1^{p, q} = H^q_\etale(X_p, f_p^{-1}\mathcal{F})
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(Y_\etale, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

source.label: lemma-map-stalks-local-map
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-stalks-local-map}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $x \in X$.
Suppose $\psi : \mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{F}_x$ is a map of
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules.
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$ and a map
$\varphi : \mathcal{G}|_U \to \mathcal{F}|_U$ such that
$\varphi_x = \psi$.

Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The kernel of $R \to S$ consists of nilpotent elements.
\item The minimal primes of $R$ are in the image of
$\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$.
\item The image of $\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$ is dense
in $\Spec(R)$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Kernel nil, minimal primes hit, and dense spectrum image are equivalent.

\label{lemma-projective-into-acyclic-is-zero}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $K^\bullet$ be an acyclic complex.
Let $P^\bullet$ be bounded above and consisting of projective objects.
Any morphism $P^\bullet \to K^\bullet$ is homotopic to zero.

\label{lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\overline{x}$ be a geometric point of $X$.
Let $(U, \overline{u})$ an \'etale neighborhood of $\overline{x}$.
Let $\{\varphi_i : U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be an \'etale covering in
$X_{spaces, \etale}$.
Then there exist $i \in I$ and $\overline{u}_i : \overline{x} \to U_i$
such that $\varphi_i : (U_i, \overline{u}_i) \to (U, \overline{u})$
is a morphism of \'etale neighborhoods.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The category of
constructible abelian sheaves is exactly the category of abelian
sheaves of the form
$$
\Coker\left(
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, m}
j_{V_j!}\underline{\mathbf{Z}/m_j\mathbf{Z}}_{V_j}
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n}
j_{U_i!}\underline{\mathbf{Z}/n_i\mathbf{Z}}_{U_i}
\right)

with $V_j$ and $U_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects of
$X_\etale$ and $m_j$, $n_i$ positive integers.
In fact, we can even assume $U_i$ and $V_j$ affine.
The finite presentation is a **cokernel of a map between finite direct sums of $j_!$ of constant finite abelian sheaves**; it is not a presentation by arbitrary sheaf coproducts.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-constructible}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
A subset $E$ of $X$ is locally constructible in $X$ if and only if
$E \cap U$ is constructible in $U$ for every affine open $U$ of $X$.

corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of
abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$.
Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Denote $\mathcal{B}$ the set of
$V \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ such that
$H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$.
If every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
then $R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compact-set-in-affine}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $G$ be a group scheme over $k$.
Assume that $G$ is Jacobson and that all closed points are $k$-rational.
Let $T = \Spec(A)$ where $A$ is a directed colimit of algebras which
are finite products of copies of $k$. For any morphism $f : T \to G$
there exists an affine open $U \subset G$ containing $f(T)$.

formulation.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The site hypotheses are exactly (i) quasi-compact **final object X**, (ii) finite cofinal coverings of every quasi-compact object by quasi-compact objects, (iii) quasi-compact pairwise fibre products inside such finite covers. These imply **bounded-below** compactness for perfect K; an **additional** finite cohomological dimension of the final object X is required for compactness in the full unbounded category.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Assume
$\mathcal{C}$ has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ has a quasi-compact final object $X$,
\item every quasi-compact object of $\mathcal{C}$
has a cofinal system of coverings which are finite
and consist of quasi-compact objects,
\item for a finite covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
with $U$, $U_i$ quasi-compact the fibre products $U_i \times_U U_j$ are
quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $K$ is a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$
in the following sense: if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(K, M) = \bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(K, M_i)$.
\item[(b)] If $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$
has finite cohomological dimension, i.e., if there exists
a $d$ such that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > d$ for
any $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{F}$, then
$K$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}

The extra condition is correctly restricted to the second conditional assertion.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Assume
$\mathcal{C}$ has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}

\item every quasi-compact object of $\mathcal{C}$

and consist of quasi-compact objects,
\item for a finite covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
with $U$, $U_i$ quasi-compact the fibre products $U_i \times_U U_j$ are
quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $K$ is a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$
in the following sense: if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(K, M) = \bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(K, M_i)$.
\item[(b)] If $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$

a $d$ such that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > d$ for

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-basis-hypercovering}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology of $X$.
There exists a hypercovering $(I, \{U_i\})$ of $X$
such that each $U_i$ is an element of $\mathcal{B}$.

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat and quasi-compact, and
\item the geometric fibres of $f$ are connected.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
Then $\Gamma(S, \mathcal{F}) = \Gamma(T, f^{-1}_{small}\mathcal{F})$.
The canonical pullback map on global sections is an isomorphism when f is **flat quasi-compact** with *geometrically connected fibres*. The target sheaf is the small étale inverse image on T; connectedness is of every geometric fibre, not merely the ordinary fibres.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the induced **morphism of small étale topoi** $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute etale})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute etale})$ has inverse image $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$); it sends **sheaves of sets** on $Y_{\acute etale}$ to sheaves on $X_{\acute etale}$, and also induces inverse image of abelian sheaves. It is different from the **ringed-site module pullback** $f^*$, which additionally tensors by the target structure sheaf. For an étale $V\to Y$, let $h_V$ be its representable sheaf and $X\times_Y V$ the fibre product, an object of $X_{\acute etale}$. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale\}$ let $\pi_S:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau\to S_\tau$ be the canonical morphism of the **big** to the **small** site; its inverse image $\pi_S^{-1}$ takes small-site sheaves to big-site sheaves. For $f:T\to S$, $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on the *small* $\tau$-site $T_\tau$, and $\Gamma(T_\tau,-)$ denotes global sections over its final object $T$. An **fpqc cover** means a flat jointly surjective family with the finite affine-source cover condition over each affine open.

The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the induced **morphism of small étale topoi** $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute etale})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute etale})$ has inverse image $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$); it sends **sheaves of sets** on $Y_{\acute etale}$ to sheaves on $X_{\acute etale}$, and also induces inverse image of abelian sheaves. It is different from the **ringed-site module pullback** $f^*$, which additionally tensors by the target structure sheaf. For an étale $V\to Y$, let $h_V$ be its representable sheaf and $X\times_Y V$ the fibre product, an object of $X_{\acute etale}$. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale\}$ let $\pi_S:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau\to S_\tau$ be the canonical morphism of the **big** to the **small** site; its inverse image $\pi_S^{-1}$ takes small-site sheaves to big-site sheaves. For $f:T\to S$, $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on the *small* $\tau$-site $T_\tau$, and $\Gamma(T_\tau,-)$ denotes global sections over its final object $T$. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat and quasi-compact, and
\item the geometric fibres of $f$ are connected.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
Then $\Gamma(S, \mathcal{F}) = \Gamma(T, f^{-1}_{small}\mathcal{F})$.

**Precise scope:** The canonical pullback map on global sections is an isomorphism when f is **flat quasi-compact** with *geometrically connected fibres*. The target sheaf is the small étale inverse image on T; connectedness is of every geometric fibre, not merely the ordinary fibres.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A flat quasi-compact f:T→S with geometrically connected fibres induces equality of global sections of any small étale sheaf before and after small-site inverse image. Both flatness and quasi-compactness remain.

phase3.reason: The proof invokes fpqc descent and shows fibrewise agreement of pullbacks because a constant sheaf over each connected geometric fibre has constant sections.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let
$$
\ldots \to I_3^\bullet \to I_2^\bullet \to I_1^\bullet
$$
be an inverse system of complexes. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item each $I_n^\bullet$ is $K$-injective,
\item each map $I_{n + 1}^m \to I_n^m$ is a split surjection,
\item the limits $I^m = \lim I_n^m$ exist.
\end{enumerate}
Then the complex $I^\bullet$ is K-injective.

\label{lemma-invertible}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{L}$
be an $\mathcal{O}$-module. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is invertible, and
\item there exists an $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{N}$
such that
$\mathcal{L} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{N} \cong \mathcal{O}$.
\end{enumerate}
In this case we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\mathcal{L}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module of finite presentation,
\item[(b)] for every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ there exists a
covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that $\mathcal{L}|_{U_i}$
is a direct summand of a finite free module, and
\item[(c)] the module $\mathcal{N}$ in (2) is isomorphic to
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd]_j \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume $X \to S$ smooth, and $i$, $j$ immersions.
If $j$ is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular)
immersion, then so is $i$.

\label{lemma-affine-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable and affine,
\item $f$ is affine,
\item for every affine scheme $V$ and \'etale morphism $V \to Y$
the scheme $X \times_Y V$ is affine,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is affine, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is affine.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
be a functor. Suppose that for every covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ of $\mathcal{C}$
\begin{enumerate}
\item the map $\coprod u(U_i) \to u(U)$ is surjective, and
\item the maps
$u(U_i \times_U U_j) \to u(U_i) \times_{u(U)} u(U_j)$ are surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $u^pE$ is a sheaf for all sets $E$, denote it $u^sE$,
\item the stalk functor $\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$
and the functor $u^s: \textit{Sets} \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ are
adjoint, and
\item we have $\mathcal{F}_p = \mathcal{F}^\#_p$
for every presheaf of sets $\mathcal{F}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. If $f$ is locally of finite type, $Y$ is Jacobson
(Properties of Spaces, Remark
\ref{spaces-properties-remark-list-properties-local-etale-topology}),
and $x \in |X|$ is a finite type point of $X$,
then the transcendence degree of $x/f(x)$ is $0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-degree-birational-pullback}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X' \to X$ be a birational morphism of
proper schemes of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$. Then
$$
\deg(f^*\mathcal{E}) = \deg(\mathcal{E})
$$
for every finite locally free sheaf of constant rank. More generally
it suffices if $f$ induces a bijection between irreducible components
of dimension $1$ and isomorphisms of local rings at the corresponding
generic points.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functorial-homotopies}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a Grothendieck abelian category.
Let $(K_i^\bullet)_{i \in I}$ be a set of acyclic complexes.
There exists a functor $M^\bullet \mapsto \mathbf{M}^\bullet(M^\bullet)$
and a natural transformation
$j_{M^\bullet} : M^\bullet \to \mathbf{M}^\bullet(M^\bullet)$
such
\begin{enumerate}
\item $j_{M^\bullet}$ is a (termwise) injective quasi-isomorphism, and
\item for every $i \in I$ and $w : K_i^\bullet \to M^\bullet$
the morphism $j_{M^\bullet} \circ w$ is homotopic to zero.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-change-fields-flat
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-change-fields-flat}
Let $K/k$ be an extension of fields. Let $X$ be scheme over $k$
and set $Y = X_K$. If $y \in Y$ with image $x \in X$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is a
faithfully flat local ring homomorphism,
\item with $\mathfrak p_0 = \Ker(\kappa(x) \otimes_k K \to \kappa(y))$
we have $\kappa(y) = \kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$,
\item $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y} = (\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \otimes_k K)_\mathfrak p$
where $\mathfrak p \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \otimes_k K$ is the inverse
image of $\mathfrak p_0$.
\item we have
$\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}/\mathfrak m_x\mathcal{O}_{Y, y} =
(\kappa(x) \otimes_k K)_{\mathfrak p_0}$
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-pushout-filtered
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pushout-filtered}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : A \to B$ and $g : A \to C$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a pushout
$$
\xymatrix{
A \ar[r]_f \ar[d]_g & B \ar[d]^{g'} \\
C \ar[r]^{f'} & C \amalg_A B
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colim-works-over-collection}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$ be the set
of coverings of $\mathcal{C}$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-site}). Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ with $I$ finite,
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map
$$
\colim_i H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
H^p(U, \colim_i \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $p \geq 0$, every $U \in \mathcal{B}$, and
every filtered diagram $\mathcal{I} \to \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.

conclusions: The contravariant character-dual functor is exact and detects injections/surjections by reversing them.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring and $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$.
formulation.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, define the contravariant $R$-module functor $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $R$-action $(r\cdot\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$. Then $C$ is an exact contravariant functor: for each short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ the sequence
$$0\to C(M'')\to C(M)\to C(M')\to0$$
is exact. Furthermore, it reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms: an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ is injective if and only if $C(u):C(N)\to C(M)$ is surjective, and $u$ is surjective if and only if $C(u)$ is injective.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L947–964 defines CONTRAVARIANT C(M)=Hom_Ab(M,Q/Z) with R-action (rλ)(m)=λ(rm), then asserts C is EXACT and REFLECTS injections and surjections. The reconstruction correctly reverses arrow directions: injective u iff surjective C(u) and vice versa.

phase3.reason: Exactness of the character-dual functor is established by the cited module lemma, and the remaining properties follow.

source.label: lemma-limit-purity
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-limit-purity}
Let $I$ be a directed set.
Let $(S_i, g_{ii'})$ be an inverse system of affine schemes over $I$.
Set $S = \lim_i S_i$ and $s \in S$.
Denote $g_i : S \to S_i$ the projections and set $s_i = g_i(s)$.
Suppose that $f : X \to S$ is a morphism of finite presentation,
$\mathcal{F}$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation
which is pure along $X_s$ and flat over $S$ at all points of $X_s$.
Then there exists an $i \in I$, a morphism of finite presentation
$X_i \to S_i$, a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X_i}$-module $\mathcal{F}_i$
of finite presentation which is pure along $(X_i)_{s_i}$ and flat over $S_i$
at all points of $(X_i)_{s_i}$ such that $X \cong X_i \times_{S_i} S$
and such that the pullback of $\mathcal{F}_i$ to $X$ is isomorphic
to $\mathcal{F}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a normal variety over $k$.
Let $U \subset \mathbf{A}^n_k$ be an open subscheme with
$k$-rational points $p, q \in U(k)$. For every invertible
module $\mathcal{L}$ on $X \times_{\Spec(k)} U$ the restrictions
$\mathcal{L}|_{X \times p}$ and $\mathcal{L}|_{X \times q}$
are isomorphic.

\label{lemma-filtered-injective-right-resolution-single-object}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with enough injectives.
For any object $A$ of $\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$ there exists
a filtered quasi-isomorphism $A[0] \to I^\bullet$
where $I^\bullet$ is a complex of filtered injective objects
with $I^n = 0$ for $n < 0$.

\label{lemma-qis-equivalence}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
If $\varphi : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ is a homomorphism of
differential graded $\mathcal{O}$-algebras which induces an
isomorphism on cohomology sheaves, then
$$
D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(\mathcal{B}, \text{d}), \quad
\mathcal{M}
\longmapsto
\mathcal{M} \otimes_\mathcal{A}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{B}
$$
is an equivalence of categories.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves}
Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Let $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$.
Given a set $I$ and sheaves $F_i$ on $\Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$,
if $U \cong \coprod_{i\in I} F_i$
as sheaves, then each $F_i$ is representable by an open and closed
subscheme $U_i$ and $U \cong \coprod U_i$ as schemes.

Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{N}$ are invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, then so is

$\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{O}_X) \to \mathcal{O}_X$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

be pairwise distinct maximal ideals of $A$. For $i = 1, \ldots, r$ let
$\varphi_i : A_{\mathfrak m_i} \to B_i$ be a ring map whose
kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power
of $\mathfrak m_i$. Then there exists a ring map $\varphi : A \to B$ such
that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the localization of $\varphi$ at $\mathfrak m_i$ is
isomorphic to $\varphi_i$, and
\item $\Ker(\varphi)$ and $\Coker(\varphi)$ are annihilated
by a power of $\mathfrak m_1 \cap \ldots \cap \mathfrak m_r$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if each $\varphi_i$ is finite, injective, or
surjective then so is $\varphi$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glue-at-max}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $\mathfrak m_1, \ldots, \mathfrak m_r$
be pairwise distinct maximal ideals of $A$. For $i = 1, \ldots, r$ let
$\varphi_i : A_{\mathfrak m_i} \to B_i$ be a ring map whose
kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power
of $\mathfrak m_i$. Then there exists a ring map $\varphi : A \to B$ such
that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the localization of $\varphi$ at $\mathfrak m_i$ is
isomorphic to $\varphi_i$, and
\item $\Ker(\varphi)$ and $\Coker(\varphi)$ are annihilated
by a power of $\mathfrak m_1 \cap \ldots \cap \mathfrak m_r$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if each $\varphi_i$ is finite, injective, or
surjective then so is $\varphi$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ML-local}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(M_n)$ be an inverse system of finite $A$-modules. Then the
inverse system $H^i_\mathfrak m(M_n)$ satisfies the Mittag-Leffler
condition for any $i$.
\item Let $U = \Spec(A) \setminus \{\mathfrak m\}$ be the
punctured spectrum of $A$.
Let $\mathcal{F}_n$ be an inverse system of
coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules.
Then the inverse system $H^i(U, \mathcal{F}_n)$

formulation.statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes (no quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or Noetherian assumption). Choose an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X\times_SX$ of the diagonal for which $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$ is a closed immersion, and let $p_1:W\to X$ be the first projection. A *relative dualizing complex* is a **pair** $(K,\xi)$ consisting of an $S$-perfect complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ (pseudo-coherent with locally finite relative Tor amplitude) and a *rigidifying map* $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*K$ in $D(\mathcal O_W)$ which induces an isomorphism $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_W}(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,Lp_1^*K)$. The condition is independent of the choice of $W$ and uses the diagonal and derived internal Hom, not only self-duality of $K$. Now assume additionally $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to S$ *proper, flat and finitely presented*. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories and put $\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_S)$. Let $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X\times_SX$ be the (closed) diagonal, $p_1$ the first projection, and $c_\Delta$ the right adjoint of $R\Delta_*$. The *pre-rigidity* isomorphism $\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c_\Delta(Lp_1^*\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet})$ from relative duality determines, by diagonal adjunction, a rigidifying map $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}$. Then $(\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet},\xi)$ is a relative dualizing pair as above.

\label{lemma-compose-delta-functor-homological}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $G : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a $\delta$-functor.
Let $H : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homological functor.
Assume that $H^{-1}(G(A)) = 0$ for all $A$ in $\mathcal{A}$.
Then the collection
$$
\{H^n \circ G, H^n(\delta_{A \to B \to C})\}_{n \geq 0}
$$
is a $\delta$-functor from $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$, see
Homology, Definition \ref{homology-definition-cohomological-delta-functor}.

hypotheses: For a **connected** scheme $X$ with geometric basepoint $\bar x$, its étale fundamental group $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ is the profinite automorphism group of the fibre functor of finite étale covers of $X$. A *finite continuous $\pi_1$-set* is a finite set with continuous action; a *finite continuous $\pi_1$-module* is a finite abelian group with compatible continuous action. A scheme is *geometrically unibranch* if every strictly henselian local ring has a unique minimal prime (equivalently the local geometric branches are unique); this is a hypothesis of the extension of the finite-type module correspondence to possibly infinite underlying fibre modules.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For connected X with geometric base point, finite locally constant sets and abelian sheaves correspond to finite continuous π1-actions; for finite Λ, finite-type locally constant Λ-modules correspond to finite π1-modules with commuting Λ-action. All three equivalences and the finite coefficient ring clause survive.

phase3.reason: The proof uses the fundamental-group equivalence for finite étale covers and transfers abelian and module structures through product-preserving equivalences.

\label{lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Assume $f$ is finite and of finite presentation.
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation
if and only if $f_*\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module of finite
presentation.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-of-partial-section}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $V \subset Y$ be an open subspace such that $V \to Y$ is quasi-compact.
Let $s : V \to X$ be a morphism such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_V$.
Let $Y'$ be the scheme theoretic image of $s$.
Then $Y' \to Y$ is an isomorphism over $V$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-abelian}
Let $(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed topos.
The category $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$ is an abelian category.
The forgetful functor
$\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}) \to \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$
is exact, hence kernels, cokernels and exactness of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules, correspond to the corresponding notions
for abelian sheaves.

For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_T W]_{q+r}$ with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. It also induces a map on Chow groups.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_T W]_{q+r}$ with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. It also induces a map on Chow groups.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Let $\alpha$ be a $k$-cycle on $Y$.
Then
$$
f^*(c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap \alpha) = c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \cap f^*\alpha
$$
in $\mathrm{CH}_{k + r - 1}(X)$.

source.label: lemma-flat-pullback-cap-c1
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-pullback-cap-c1}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Let $\alpha$ be a $k$-cycle on $Y$.
Then
$$
f^*(c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap \alpha) = c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \cap f^*\alpha
$$
in $\CH_{k + r - 1}(X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-subbase-theorem}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a subbase for $X$.
If every covering of $X$ by elements of $\mathcal{B}$ has a finite

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-torsors}
Let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $G$ be a group algebraic
space over $B$. Denote $\mathcal{G}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{B}$ the algebraic
space $G$, resp.\ $B$ seen as a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The functor
$$
G\textit{-Torsors} \longrightarrow \mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}\textit{-Torsors}
$$
which associates to a triple $(U, b, X)$ the triple
$(U, b, \mathcal{X})$ where $\mathcal{X}$ is $X$ viewed as a sheaf
is an equivalence of stacks in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.

formulation.statement:
Let $A' \to B'$ be a ring map. Let $I \subset A'$ be an ideal.
Set $A = A'/I$ and $B = B'/IB'$. Let $f'_1, \ldots, f'_r \in B'$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A' \to B'$ is flat and of finite presentation,
\item $I$ is locally nilpotent,
\item the images $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in B$ form a quasi-regular sequence,
\item $B/(f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ is flat over $A$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $B'/(f'_1, \ldots, f'_r)$ is flat over $A'$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For A'→B' flat finitely presented, I⊂A' locally nilpotent and reduced f_i quasi-regular, flatness of B/(f_i) over A'/I implies flatness of B'/(f'_i) over A'. All four conditions survive.

phase3.reason: Local flatness reduces to regular sequences in fiber rings, where the relative quasi-regularity lemma and Noetherian equivalence apply.

\label{lemma-is-limit-per-point}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Assume that for every $x \in X$ there exist
a function $p(x, -) : \mathbf{Z} \to \mathbf{Z}$ and
a fundamental system $\mathfrak{U}_x$ of open neighbourhoods of $x$
such that
$$
H^p(U, H^{m - p}(E)) = 0 \text{ for }
U \in \mathfrak{U}_x \text{ and } p > p(x, m)
$$
Then the map $E \to R\lim \tau_{\geq -n} E$ of
Derived Categories, Remark
\ref{derived-remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations}
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-periodic-lengths}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $f : (M, \varphi, \psi) \to (M', \varphi', \psi')$
be a map of $(2, 1)$-periodic complexes whose cohomology modules
have finite length. If $\Ker(f)$ and $\Coker(f)$ have finite length,
then $e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) = e_R(M', \varphi', \psi')$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.

\label{lemma-no-sections-dual-nef}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$
which is reduced, connected, and equidimensional of dimension $1$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
If $\deg(\mathcal{L}|_C) \leq 0$ for all irreducible components $C$
of $X$, then either $H^0(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$ or
$\mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{O}_X$.

formulation.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $X$ be a normal integral affine scheme with separably closed
function field. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
For any finite abelian group $M$ we have
$H^q_\etale(Z, \underline{M}) = 0$ for $q \geq 1$.

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

\label{lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed}
Let $X$ be a normal integral affine scheme with separably closed
function field. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
For any finite abelian group $M$ we have
$H^q_\etale(Z, \underline{M}) = 0$ for $q \geq 1$.

Koszul-regular sequence. Then the extended alternating
{\v C}ech complex $R \to \bigoplus\nolimits_{i_0} R_{f_{i_0}} \to

\ldots \to R_{f_1\ldots f_r}$ from Section \ref{section-alternating-cech}
only has cohomology in degree $r$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-cohomology-ext}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
For any object $K$ of $D(A)$ we have
$$
R\Gamma_I(K) = \text{hocolim}\ R\Hom_A(A/I^n, K)
$$
in $D(A)$ and
$$
R^q\Gamma_I(K) = \colim_n \Ext_A^q(A/I^n, K)
$$
as modules for all $q \in \mathbf{Z}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-permanence}
Let $h : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $Y$.
Let $x \in X$ with $y = h(x) \in Y$. If $h$ is flat at $x$, then
$$
\mathcal{G}\text{ flat over }S\text{ at }y
\Leftrightarrow
h^*\mathcal{G}\text{ flat over }S\text{ at }x.
$$
In particular: If $h$ is surjective and flat, then
$\mathcal{G}$ is flat over $S$, if and only if
$h^*\mathcal{G}$ is flat over $S$. If $h$ is surjective and
flat, and $X$ is flat over $S$, then $Y$ is flat over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-exact-modules}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $p$ be a point of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_p)$,
$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}_p$ is exact.
\item The stalk functor
$\textit{PMod}(\mathcal{O}) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_p)$,
$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}_p$
is exact.
\item For $\mathcal{F} \in \Ob(\textit{PMod}(\mathcal{O}))$
we have $\mathcal{F}_p = \mathcal{F}^\#_p$.
\end{enumerate}

For a base scheme $S$, let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ denote **all schemes over $S$** (using the source's size conventions). An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

Given a covering $\{T_i\to T\}$, an *effective descent datum* for quasi-coherent sheaves is a family of quasi-coherent $\mathcal F_i$ on $T_i$ with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:\mathrm{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $T_i\times_TT_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triples, and an isomorphism of this datum with the pullbacks of a single quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$. For a ring map $A\to B$, its *Amitsur cochain complex* $(B/A)_\bullet$ has degree $q$ term $B^{\otimes_A(q+1)}$ and alternating coface differential inserting $1$ in every position.

If $A \to B$ is faithfully flat, then the complex $(B/A)_\bullet$ is exact in
positive degrees, and $H^0((B/A)_\bullet) = A$.

**Scope and interpretation:** The complex is the **unaugmented Amitsur complex**, B in degree 0 and B⊗_A B in degree 1, with alternating unit-insertion differential. The H^0 identification is the canonical inclusion A→B and H^q vanishes for every q>0.

\label{proposition-going-down-normal-integral}
Let $R \subset S$ be an inclusion of domains.
Assume $R$ is normal and $S$ integral over $R$.
Let $\mathfrak p \subset \mathfrak p' \subset R$
be primes. Let $\mathfrak q'$ be a prime of $S$
with $\mathfrak p' = R \cap \mathfrak q'$.
Then there exists a prime $\mathfrak q$
with $\mathfrak q \subset \mathfrak q'$
such that $\mathfrak p = R \cap \mathfrak q$. In other words:
the going down property holds for $R \to S$, see
Definition \ref{definition-going-up-down}.

\label{lemma-equivalence-finite-length}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local
ring. Let $F$ be an $A$-linear self-equivalence of the category of
finite length $A$-modules. Then $F$ is isomorphic to the identity functor.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of the scheme $X$ along a closed
subscheme $Z$. Let $U = \Spec(A)$ be an affine open of $X$ and let
$I \subset A$ be the ideal corresponding to $Z \cap U$.
Let $a \in I$ and let $x' \in X'$ be a point mapping to a point of $U$.
Then $x'$ is a point of the affine open $U' = \Spec(A[\frac{I}{a}])$
if and only if the image of $a$ in $\mathcal{O}_{X', x'}$ cuts
out the exceptional divisor.

source.label: lemma-characterize-affine-blowup
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-affine-blowup}
Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of the scheme $X$ along a closed
subscheme $Z$. Let $U = \Spec(A)$ be an affine open of $X$ and let
$I \subset A$ be the ideal corresponding to $Z \cap U$.
Let $a \in I$ and let $x' \in X'$ be a point mapping to a point of $U$.
Then $x'$ is a point of the affine open $U' = \Spec(A[\frac{I}{a}])$
if and only if the image of $a$ in $\mathcal{O}_{X', x'}$ cuts
out the exceptional divisor.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphisms-left-localization}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category and let $S$ be a left multiplicative
system of morphisms of $\mathcal{C}$. Given any finite collection
$g_i : X_i \to Y$ of morphisms of $S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$
(indexed by $i$),
we can find an element $s : Y \to Y'$ of $S$ and
a family of morphisms $f_i : X_i \to Y'$ of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
each $g_i$ is the equivalence class of the pair
$(f_i : X_i \to Y', s : Y \to Y')$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-bounded-derived}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. The subcategories
$\text{FAc}^{+}(\mathcal{A})$, $\text{FAc}^{-}(\mathcal{A})$,
resp.\ $\text{FAc}^b(\mathcal{A})$
are strictly full saturated triangulated subcategories
of $K^{+}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})$, $K^{-}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})$,
resp.\ $K^b(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})$.
The corresponding saturated multiplicative systems (see
Lemma \ref{lemma-operations})
are the sets $\text{FQis}^{+}(\mathcal{A})$, $\text{FQis}^{-}(\mathcal{A})$,
resp.\ $\text{FQis}^b(\mathcal{A})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The kernel of the functor
$K^{+}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A}) \to DF^{+}(\mathcal{A})$
is $\text{FAc}^{+}(\mathcal{A})$ and this induces an equivalence
of triangulated categories
$$
K^{+}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})/\text{FAc}^{+}(\mathcal{A}) =
\text{FQis}^{+}(\mathcal{A})^{-1}K^{+}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})
\longrightarrow
DF^{+}(\mathcal{A})
$$
\item The kernel of the functor
$K^{-}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A}) \to DF^{-}(\mathcal{A})$
is $\text{FAc}^{-}(\mathcal{A})$ and this induces an equivalence
of triangulated categories
$$
K^{-}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})/\text{FAc}^{-}(\mathcal{A}) =
\text{FQis}^{-}(\mathcal{A})^{-1}K^{-}(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})
\longrightarrow
DF^{-}(\mathcal{A})
$$
\item The kernel of the functor
$K^b(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A}) \to DF^b(\mathcal{A})$
is $\text{FAc}^b(\mathcal{A})$ and this induces an equivalence
of triangulated categories
$$
K^b(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})/\text{FAc}^b(\mathcal{A}) =
\text{FQis}^b(\mathcal{A})^{-1}K^b(\text{Fil}^f\mathcal{A})
\longrightarrow
DF^b(\mathcal{A})
$$
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-total-ring-fractions}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $S \subset R$ be a multiplicative subset consisting of nonzerodivisors.
Then $Q(R) \cong Q(S^{-1}R)$.
In particular $Q(R) \cong Q(Q(R))$.

source.label: lemma-pullback
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Consider a morphism
$f : (U, R, s, t, c) \to (U', R', s', t', c')$
of groupoid schemes over $S$. Then pullback $f^*$ given by
$$
(\mathcal{F}, \alpha) \mapsto (f^*\mathcal{F}, f^*\alpha)
$$
defines a functor from the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on
$(U', R', s', t', c')$ to the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on
$(U, R, s, t, c)$.

\label{lemma-f-map}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map.
There are bijections between the following four sets
\begin{enumerate}
\item the set of maps $\mathcal{G} \to f_*\mathcal{F}$,
\item the set of maps $f^{-1}\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$,
\item the set of $f$-maps $\xi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$, and
\item the set of all collections of maps
$\xi_{U, V} : \mathcal{G}(V) \to \mathcal{F}(U)$ for all
$U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$ open such that $f(U) \subset V$
compatible with all restriction maps,
\end{enumerate}
functorially in $\mathcal{F} \in \Sh(X)$ and $\mathcal{G} \in \Sh(Y)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kahler-different-complete-intersection}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $n \geq 1$ and
$f_1, \ldots, f_n \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Set $B = A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_n)$.
The K\"ahler different of $B$ over $A$ is the ideal
of $B$ generated by $\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$.
