\label{lemma-induction-step}
Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a local ring. Let $R \to S$ be a finitely presented
flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres. Write
$\mathfrak p = \mathfrak mS$. Let $\mathfrak q \subset S$ be a prime ideal
lying over $\mathfrak m$. Let $N$ be a finite $S$-module.
There exist $r \geq 0$ and an $S$-module map
$$
\alpha : S^{\oplus r} \longrightarrow N
$$
such that
$\alpha : \kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\oplus r} \to N \otimes_S \kappa(\mathfrak p)$
is an isomorphism. For any such $\alpha$ the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat,
\item $\alpha$ is $R$-universally injective and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat,
\item $\alpha$ is injective and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat,
\item $\alpha_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat, and
\item $\alpha_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-ringed-stalk}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Consider the following conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and $f \in \mathcal{O}(U)$
there exists a covering $\{U_j \to U\}$ such that for each $j$
either $f|_{U_j}$ is invertible or $(1 - f)|_{U_j}$ is invertible.
\item For every point $p$ of $\mathcal{C}$ the stalk $\mathcal{O}_p$
is either the zero ring or a local ring.
\end{enumerate}
We always have (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2). If $\mathcal{C}$ has enough points
then (1) and (2) are equivalent.

\label{lemma-integral-closure-transitive}
Let $A \to B \to C$ be ring maps.
Let $B'$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$,
let $C'$ be the integral closure of $B'$ in $C$. Then
$C'$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $C$.

\label{lemma-pullback-ses}
Let
$f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}') \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. Let
$0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H} \to 0$
be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}$-modules with $\mathcal{H}$
a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module. Then the sequence
$0 \to f^*\mathcal{F} \to f^*\mathcal{G} \to f^*\mathcal{H} \to 0$
is exact as well.

source.label: lemma-almost-cocontinuous-sheafification
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-almost-cocontinuous-sheafification}
Let $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ be sites.
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor.
Assume that $u$ is continuous and almost cocontinuous.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal{D}$ such that $\mathcal{G}(V)$ is
a singleton whenever $V$ is sheaf theoretically empty.
Then $(u^p\mathcal{G})^\# = u^p(\mathcal{G}^\#)$.

conclusions: The two degree-zero direct-image comparisons and the positive-degree derived direct-image comparison for relative differential forms are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: $L$ is the blow-up of the specified affine space $X=\mathbf A^{m+n}_S$ along its standard coordinate subspace $Z=\mathbf A^m_S$, with $n\geq1$.
formulation.statement:
Fix a ring $R$, integers $m\geq0$ and $n\geq1$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n]=\mathbf A^{m+n}_S$, and let $i:Z=\mathbf A^m_S\hookrightarrow X$ be defined by $(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$. Let $b:L=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(X)\to X$ be the blow-up, $P=Z\times_S\mathbf P^{n-1}_S$, and $p:P\to Z$ the projection. Identify the exceptional divisor $E\subset L$ with $P$ via its zero-section embedding into the natural line bundle $L\to P$.

For every $a\geq0$:
(1) the natural map $\Omega^a_{X/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_*\Omega^a_{L/S}$ is an isomorphism;
(2) the natural map $\Omega^a_{Z/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*\Omega^a_{P/S}$ is an isomorphism; and
(3) the map $Rb_*\Omega^a_{L/S}\to i_*Rp_*\Omega^a_{P/S}$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^j$ for every $j\geq1$.

Original L2637–2647 gives three distinct comparison results: b_*Ω^a≅Ω^a_X, p_*Ω^a≅Ω^a_Z and positive-degree cohomology of Rb_*Ω_L^a→i_*Rp_*Ω_P^a isomorphism, for all a≥0. All three and the standing geometric setup remain.

phase3.reason: The proof splits relative forms on the projective bundle to identify degree-zero pushforward, then applies the graded description of forms on the line bundle and vanishing of higher cohomology for positive projective twists to compare R^j for j>=1. For b_* forms, codimension at least two gives extension across the center and torsion-freeness away from the exceptional zero section; n=1 is trivial. Some local calculations are omitted.

Let $H : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{A}$ be a homological functor between a

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

If $A \to B$ is a smooth ring map, then $L_{B/A} = \Omega_{B/A}[0]$.

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F, G, H$ are sheaves,
\item $a : F \to G$ is representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Then $b$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L1847–1859 assumes F,G,H fppf sheaves; a:F→G representable, surjective, flat, lfp; and b∘a:F→H representable. It descends representability to b:G→H. All three sheaf premises and the composite orientation are retained.

phase3.reason: Every scheme-valued test pullback of G receives a representable fppf surjection from the corresponding algebraic-space pullback of F, so bootstrap applies.

source.label: lemma-representable-by-spaces-cover
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-representable-by-spaces-cover}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F, G, H$ are sheaves,
\item $a : F \to G$ is representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Then $b$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

\label{lemma-dense-image}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces. Assume that
$f(X)$ is dense in $Y$ and that $Y$ is Hausdorff. Then the cardinality
of $Y$ is at most the cardinality of $P(P(X))$ where $P$ is the power
set operation.

source.label: lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals}
\begin{slogan}
Trivial duality for systems of perfect objects.
\end{slogan}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(K_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ be a system of perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $K = \text{hocolim} K_n$ be the derived colimit
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-derived-colimit}).
Then for any object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O})$ we have
$$
R\SheafHom(K, E) = R\lim E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K_n^\vee
$$
where $(K_n^\vee)$ is the inverse system of dual perfect complexes.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ if and only if
$f_*\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$.

\label{lemma-nonempty-limit}
If $S : \mathcal{I} \to \textit{Sets}$ is a cofiltered diagram of sets
and all the $S_i$ are finite nonempty, then $\lim_i S_i$ is nonempty.
In other words, the limit of a directed inverse system of finite nonempty sets
is nonempty.

**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction. A **pro-étale covering** of $T$ is a family of weakly étale maps whose images admit finite affine-open refinements covering every affine open of $T$. The small pro-étale site $S_{\proetale}$ uses weakly étale $S$-schemes from a chosen big pro-étale universe; $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{\proetale}$ is its big slice site.

Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-proetale-site}.
Let $T = \Spec(A)$ be an affine object of $\Sch_\proetale$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible,
\item $T$ is a weakly contractible
(Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-w-contractible})
object of $\Sch_\proetale$, and
\item every pro-\'etale covering of $T$ can be refined by
a Zariski covering of the form $T = \coprod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} U_i$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible}
Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-proetale-site}.
Let $T = \Spec(A)$ be an affine object of $\Sch_\proetale$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible,
\item $T$ is a weakly contractible
(Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-w-contractible})
object of $\Sch_\proetale$, and
\item every pro-\'etale covering of $T$ can be refined by
a Zariski covering of the form $T = \coprod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} U_i$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-locally-projective}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item for some scheme $U$ and surjective \'etale morphism
$U \to X$ the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is locally projective
on $U$, and
\item for any scheme $U$ and any \'etale morphism
$U \to X$ the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is locally projective
on $U$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-base-change-fs}
Let $R$, $S$ be rings. Let $\mathfrak n \subset S$ be an ideal.
Let $R \to S$ be formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.
Let $R \to R'$ be any ring map. Then $R' \to S' = S \otimes_R R'$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-projective-space}
Let $S = \mathbf{Z}[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$ with $\deg(T_i) = 1$.
The scheme
$$
\mathbf{P}^n_{\mathbf{Z}} = \text{Proj}(S)
$$
represents the functor which associates to a scheme $Y$ the pairs
$(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots, s_n))$ where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is an invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module, and
\item $s_0, \ldots, s_n$ are global sections of $\mathcal{L}$
which generate $\mathcal{L}$
\end{enumerate}
up to the following equivalence:
$(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots, s_n)) \sim
(\mathcal{N}, (t_0, \ldots, t_n))$ $\Leftrightarrow$ there exists
an isomorphism $\beta : \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{N}$
with $\beta(s_i) = t_i$ for $i = 0, \ldots, n$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coherent-over-first-order-thickening}
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d] \ar[r]_i & X' \ar[d] \\
T \ar[r] & T'
}
$$
be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces where $T \to T'$ is a first
order thickening. Let $\mathcal{F}'$ be an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module
flat over $T'$. Set $\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}'$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module
of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}'$ is an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation,
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-essentially-surjective-when-ff}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{S}_1$, $\mathcal{S}_2$ be stacks over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $F : \mathcal{S}_1 \to \mathcal{S}_2$ be a $1$-morphism which is
fully faithful. Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is an equivalence,
\item for every $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and for every
$x \in \Ob(\mathcal{S}_{2, U})$ there exists a covering
$\{f_i : U_i \to U\}$ such that $f_i^*x$ is in the essential image
of the functor $F : \mathcal{S}_{1, U_i} \to \mathcal{S}_{2, U_i}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-lift-factorization-easy
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-factorization-easy}
Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Let $f \in A[x]$ be a
monic polynomial. Let $\overline{f} = \overline{g} \overline{h}$ be a
factorization of $f$ in $A/I[x]$ and assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the leading coefficient of $\overline{g}$ is an invertible element
of $A/I$, and
\item $\overline{g}$, $\overline{h}$ generate the unit ideal in $A/I[x]$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ which induces an
isomorphism $A/I \to A'/IA'$ and a factorization $f = g' h'$ in $A'[x]$
lifting the given factorization over $A/I$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sum-is-ok}
Let $R \to S$ be a finite type ring map. Let $d \geq 0$. Let $a, b \in S$.
Assume that the fibres of
$$
f_a : \Spec(S) \longrightarrow \mathbf{A}^1_R
$$
given by the $R$-algebra map $R[x] \to S$ sending $x$ to $a$
have dimension $\leq d$. Then there exists an $n_0$ such that for
$n \geq n_0$ the fibres of
$$
f_{a^n + b} : \Spec(S) \longrightarrow \mathbf{A}^1_R
$$
given by the $R$-algebra map $R[x] \to S$ sending $x$ to $a^n + b$
have dimension $\leq d$.

phase3.reason: Divisibility of coefficients in a valuation ring reduces arbitrary relations to trivial ones by the equational criterion of flatness.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-big-site-Zariski}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski
site containing $S$.
The functor $(\textit{Aff}/S)_{Zar} \to (\Sch/S)_{Zar}$
is a special cocontinuous functor. Hence it induces an equivalence
of topoi from $\Sh((\textit{Aff}/S)_{Zar})$ to
$\Sh((\Sch/S)_{Zar})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-tangent-spaces}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $y = f(x)$. If $\kappa(y) = \kappa(x)$,
then $f$ induces a natural linear map
$$
\text{d}f : T_{X/S, x} \longrightarrow T_{Y/S, y}
$$
which is dual to the linear map
$\Omega_{Y/S, y} \otimes \kappa(y) \to \Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes \kappa(x)$
via the identifications of Lemma \ref{lemma-tangent-space-cotangent-space}.

formulation.statement:
A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $\leq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of constant
rank. Then
$$
\deg(\mathcal{E}) = \deg(c_1(\mathcal{E}) \cap [X]_1)
$$
where $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(X,\mathcal E)-\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal E)\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$.

\label{lemma-degree-vector-bundle}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $\leq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of constant

\deg(\mathcal{E}) = \deg(c_1(\mathcal{E}) \cap [X]_1)
$$
where the left hand side is defined in
Varieties, Definition \ref{varieties-definition-degree-invertible-sheaf}.

\label{lemma-diagram-localize}
Suppose given a cartesian diagram of rings
$$
\xymatrix{
R &
R' \ar[l]^t \\
B \ar[u]_s &
B'\ar[u] \ar[l]
}
$$
i.e., $B' = B \times_R R'$. If $h \in B'$ corresponds to $g \in B$
and $f \in R'$ such that $s(g) = t(f)$, then the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
R_{s(g)} = R_{t(f)} &
(R')_f \ar[l]^-t \\
B_g \ar[u]_s &
(B')_h \ar[u] \ar[l]
}
$$
is cartesian too.

\label{lemma-trivial-filter-finite-module}
\begin{slogan}
Finite modules have filtrations such that successive quotients are
cyclic modules.
\end{slogan}
Let $R$ be a ring, and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module.
There exists a filtration by finite $R$-submodules
$$
0 = M_0 \subset M_1 \subset \ldots \subset M_n = M
$$
such that each quotient $M_i/M_{i - 1}$ is isomorphic
to $R/I_i$ for some ideal $I_i$ of $R$.

\label{lemma-quasi-compact-local}
\begin{slogan}
Quasi-compact morphisms of algebraic spaces are preserved under pullback
and local on the target.
\end{slogan}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is quasi-compact,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism of
algebraic spaces $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is quasi-compact,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the algebraic space $Z \times_Y X$ is quasi-compact,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a quasi-compact morphism
of algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists a surjective \'etale morphism
$Y' \to Y$ of algebraic spaces such that $Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$
is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-section-smooth-morphism}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\sigma : S \to X$ be a section of $f$.
Let $s \in S$ be a point such that $f$ is smooth at $x = \sigma(s)$.
Then there exist affine open neighbourhoods
$\Spec(A) = U \subset S$ of $s$ and $\Spec(B) = V \subset X$
of $x$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f(V) \subset U$ and $\sigma(U) \subset V$,
\item with $I = \Ker(\sigma^\# : B \to A)$ the module $I/I^2$
is a free $A$-module, and
\item $B^\wedge \cong A[[x_1, \ldots, x_d]]$ as $A$-algebras where
$B^\wedge$ denotes the completion of $B$ with respect to $I$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-cycle-smooth}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $r \geq 0$. Assume $S$
locally Noetherian and $f$ smooth of relative dimension $r$. Let
$\alpha \in z(X/S, r)$. Then the support of $\alpha$ is open and closed in $X$
(see proof for a more precise result).

\label{lemma-affine-diagonal-universal-delta-functor}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal
(for example if $X$ is separated). Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item given a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$
there exists an embedding $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}'$ of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
such that $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}') = 0$ for all $p \geq 1$, and
\item $\{H^n(X, -)\}_{n \geq 0}$
is a universal $\delta$-functor from $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ to
$\textit{Ab}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$, $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be complexes
of $\mathcal{O}$-modules with
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}^n = 0$ for $n \ll 0$,
\item $\mathcal{E}^n = 0$ for $n \gg 0$, and
\item $\mathcal{E}^n$ isomorphic to a direct summand of a finite
free $\mathcal{O}$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Then the internal hom $R\SheafHom(\mathcal{E}^\bullet, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$
is represented by the complex $\mathcal{H}^\bullet$ with terms
$$
\mathcal{H}^n =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n = p + q}
\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{E}^{-q}, \mathcal{F}^p)
$$
and differential as described in Section \ref{section-internal-hom}.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-skolem-noether}
Let $A$ be a finite central simple $k$-algebra. Let $B$ be a simple
$k$-algebra. Let $f, g : B \to A$ be two $k$-algebra homomorphisms.
Then there exists an invertible element $x \in A$ such that
$f(b) = xg(b)x^{-1}$ for all $b \in B$.

formulation.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $j : U \to X$ be an
open subspace. Let $T \subset X$ be a closed subset contained in $U$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $E$ is an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose cohomology sheaves
are supported on $T$, then $E \to Rj_*(E|_U)$ is an isomorphism.
\item If $F$ is an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$ whose cohomology sheaves
are supported on $T$, then $j_!F \to Rj_*F$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For an open immersion j:U→X and closed T⊂U, derived objects supported cohomologically on T satisfy two claims: E→Rj_*(E|U) is an isomorphism for E over X, and j_!F→Rj_*F is an isomorphism for F over U. Both support hypotheses and the separate objects are preserved.

phase3.reason: Checks both asserted derived comparisons on the supported open and its complementary open using vanishing of restriction outside support.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a Nagata scheme (and in particular locally Noetherian).
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes locally
of finite type over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ proper,
\item for any commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^f \\
C \ar[r] \ar@{..>}[ru] & Y
}
$$
of schemes over $S$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $C$ is a normal integral scheme of finite type over $S$,
\item $U = C \setminus \{c\}$ for some closed point $c \in C$,
\item $A = \mathcal{O}_{C, c}$ has dimension $1$\footnote{It follows
that $A$ is a discrete valuation ring, see
Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-characterize-dvr}.
Moreover, $c$ maps to a finite type point $s \in S$ and
$A$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$.}
\end{enumerate}
then in the commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^f \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & Y
}
$$
where $K = \text{Frac}(A)$ there exists exactly one dotted arrow\footnote{By
Lemma \ref{lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point} this is
equivalent to asking for the existence and uniqueness of the dotted arrow
making the first commutative diagram commute.}
making the diagram commute.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned limits.tex L4443 (lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-proper): Pinned source assumes S NAGATA and f:X→Y QUASI-COMPACT and LOCALLY FINITE TYPE OVER S. Properness is equivalent to EXACTLY ONE lift for each diagram with C NORMAL INTEGRAL finite type over S, U punctured at a closed codimension-one c with local DVR. The quasi-compactness distinction from the separatedness criterion is retained. The reviewed mathematical formulation matches the pinned original and all required quantifiers.

phase3.reason: The essentially finite-type proper criterion is exactly conjunction of the previously proven universally-closed and separated criteria.

$(g, g^\sharp) : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')
\to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}''), \mathcal{O}'')$

D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}) \to D(\mathcal{A}'', \text{d})$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the morphism $f$ is quasi-separated, and
\item the morphism $f$ satisfies the uniqueness
part of the valuative criterion.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is separated.

phase3.reason: Valuative uniqueness implies that Δ_{X/Y} satisfies the existence criterion: any pair of lifts over Spec A agree. Quasi-separatedness makes the diagonal quasi-compact; the previously proved criterion yields its universal closedness, and its locally finite-type separated monomorphism structure then makes it finite and hence a closed immersion.

\label{lemma-geometrically-normal-at-point}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Let $x \in X$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically normal at $x$,
\item for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'$ of $k$
and $x' \in X_{k'}$ lying over $x$ the local ring
$\mathcal{O}_{X_{k'}, x'}$ is normal, and
\item the ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is geometrically
normal over $k$ (see
Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-geometrically-normal}).
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-canonical-morphism}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of schemes. By Schemes, Lemma \ref{schemes-lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent}
the sheaf $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebras. There is a canonical morphism
$$
can : X \longrightarrow \underline{\Spec}_S(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
of schemes over $S$.
For any affine open $U \subset S$ the restriction $can|_{f^{-1}(U)}$
is identified with the canonical morphism
$$
f^{-1}(U) \longrightarrow \Spec(\Gamma(f^{-1}(U), \mathcal{O}_X))
$$
coming from Schemes, Lemma \ref{schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine}.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-union-Noetherian}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $X_i \subset X$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$ be a finite collection of subsets.
If each $X_i$ is Noetherian (with the induced topology), then
$\bigcup_{i = 1, \ldots, n}  X_i$ is Noetherian (with the induced topology).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-projective-in-category-hausdorff-qc}
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff, quasi-compact topological space.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is extremally disconnected,
\item for any surjective continuous map $f : Y \to X$ with $Y$ Hausdorff
quasi-compact there exists a continuous section, and
\item for any solid commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
& Y \ar[d] \\
X \ar@{..>}[ru] \ar[r] & Z
}
$$
of continuous maps of quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces with $Y \to Z$
surjective, there is a dotted arrow
in the category of topological spaces making the diagram commute.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
For a scheme $X$, $X_{\acute et}$ denotes its **small étale site**. $H^q_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)$ is the $q$th right-derived global-sections functor of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$. Open subschemes $U,V$ inherit the restricted sheaf. Given a scheme map $f:X\to Y$, the direct image $f_*$ of abelian étale sheaves is the right adjoint to $f^{-1}$ and has right-derived functors $R^qf_*$, which are **abelian sheaves on $Y_{\acute et}$**. The two-cover Mayer–Vietoris map to $U\cap V$ is the difference of the two restrictions.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-remove-irreducible-connected}
Let $X$ be a connected topological space with a finite number of
irreducible components $X_1, \ldots, X_n$. If $n > 1$ there is an
$1 \leq j \leq n$ such that $X' = \bigcup_{i \not = j} X_i$ is connected.

\label{lemma-torsion-free-finite-noetherian-domain}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme with generic point $\eta$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonzero coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is torsion free,
\item $\eta$ is the only associated prime of $\mathcal{F}$,
\item $\eta$ is in the support of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}$
has property $(S_1)$, and
\item $\eta$ is in the support of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}$
has no embedded associated prime.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-2-fibre-product}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$ be algebraic stacks over $S$.
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$, $g : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of algebraic stacks. Then the $2$-fibre product
$\mathcal{X} \times_{f, \mathcal{Z}, g} \mathcal{Y}$ is an algebraic stack.
It is also the $2$-fibre product in the $2$-category of algebraic stacks
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Let $X^0 \subset |X|$, resp.\ $Y^0 \subset |Y|$ denote the set of
codimension $0$ points of $X$, resp.\ $Y$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is decent,
\item $X^0$ and $Y^0$ are finite and $f^{-1}(Y^0) = X^0$,
\item either $f$ is quasi-compact or $f$ is separated.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a dense open $V \subset Y$
such that $f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

\label{lemma-finite-over-dense-open}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Let $X^0 \subset |X|$, resp.\ $Y^0 \subset |Y|$ denote the set of
codimension $0$ points of $X$, resp.\ $Y$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is decent,
\item $X^0$ and $Y^0$ are finite and $f^{-1}(Y^0) = X^0$,
\item either $f$ is quasi-compact or $f$ is separated.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a dense open $V \subset Y$
such that $f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjective-Pic-first}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and $f \in \mathfrak m$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $f$-adically complete,
\item $f$ is a nonzerodivisor,
\item $H^1_\mathfrak m(A/fA)$ and $H^2_\mathfrak m(A/fA)$
are finite $A$-modules, and
\item $H^3_\mathfrak m(A/fA) = 0$\footnote{Observe that (3) and (4) hold
if $\text{depth}(A/fA) \geq 4$, or equivalently $\text{depth}(A) \geq 5$.}.
\end{enumerate}
Let $U$, resp.\ $U_0$ be the punctured spectrum of $A$, resp.\ $A/fA$.
Then
$$
\colim_{U_0 \subset U' \subset U\text{ open}} \Pic(U')
\longrightarrow
\Pic(U_0)
$$
is surjective.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-with-support-sheaf-on-support}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $i : Z \to X$ be the
inclusion of a closed subset.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R\mathcal{H}_Z : D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_X|_Z)$
is right adjoint to $i_* : D(\mathcal{O}_X|_Z) \to D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\item For $K$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X|_Z)$ we have $R\mathcal{H}_Z(i_*K) = K$.
\item Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X|_Z$-modules on $Z$. Then
$\mathcal{H}^p_Z(i_*\mathcal{G}) = 0$ for $p > 0$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. The full subcategory
$\text{FAc}(\mathcal{A})$ of $K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$
consisting of filtered acyclic complexes is a strictly full saturated
triangulated subcategory of $K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$.
The corresponding saturated multiplicative system (see
Lemma \ref{lemma-operations})
of $K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$ is the set
$\text{FQis}(\mathcal{A})$ of filtered quasi-isomorphisms.
In particular, the kernel of the localization
functor
$$
Q :
K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))
\longrightarrow
\text{FQis}(\mathcal{A})^{-1}K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))
$$
is $\text{FAc}(\mathcal{A})$ and the functor $H^0 \circ \text{gr}$
factors through $Q$.

\item if $Y \to T$ is separated, then $i$ is a closed immersion, and

\end{enumerate}

then $R \cong R_1 \times R_2$ with $U \cong \Spec(R_1)$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-disjoint-implies-product}
Let $R$ be a ring.
If $\Spec(R) = U \amalg V$ with both $U$ and $V$ open
then $R \cong R_1 \times R_2$ with $U \cong \Spec(R_1)$
and $V \cong \Spec(R_2)$ via the maps in Lemma \ref{lemma-spec-product}.
Moreover, both $R_1$ and $R_2$ are localizations as well as quotients
of the ring $R$.

\label{lemma-ext-2-zero-pre}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $K$ be an object of
$D^b(\mathcal{A})$ such that $\Ext^p_\mathcal{A}(H^i(K), H^j(K)) = 0$

sum of its cohomologies: $K \cong \bigoplus H^i(K)[-i]$.

\label{lemma-pullback-tensor-flat-module}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module flat over $Y$. Then the functor
$$
\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X),\quad
\mathcal{G} \longmapsto f^*\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{F}
$$
is exact.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$.
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, K)$ be a Noetherian local
$k$-algebra. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$,
\item for all $k \subset k' \subset k^{1/p}$
finite over $k$ the ring $A \otimes_k k'$ is regular,
\item $A$ is regular and the canonical map
$H_1(L_{K/k}) \to \mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is injective, and
\item $A$ is regular and the map
$\Omega_{k/\mathbf{F}_p} \otimes_k K \to \Omega_{A/\mathbf{F}_p} \otimes_A K$
is injective.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-get-many-weakly-contractible}
Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-proetale-site}.
For every object $T$ of $\Sch_\proetale$ there exists
a covering $\{T_i \to T\}$ in $\Sch_\proetale$
with each $T_i$ affine and the spectrum of a w-contractible
ring. In particular, $T_i$ is weakly contractible in $\Sch_\proetale$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-algebra}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map of finite presentation.
Let $M$ be a finite $S$-module. Assume $\text{WeakAss}_R(R)$ is finite.
Then
$$
U = \{\mathfrak q \subset S \mid M_{\mathfrak q}\text{ flat over }R\}
$$
is open in $\Spec(S)$ and for every $g \in S$ such that
$D(g) \subset U$ the localization $M_g$ is a finitely presented
$S_g$-module flat over $R$.

\label{lemma-affine-s-opens-cover-quasi-separated}
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Assume for every point $x$ of $X$ there exists $n \geq 1$ and

$x \in X_s$ and $X_s$ is affine. Then $X$ is separated.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-irreducible-components-in-neighbourhood}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $Y$ irreducible with
generic point $\eta$ and $f$ of finite type. If $X_\eta$ has $n$
irreducible components, then there exists a nonempty open $V \subset Y$
such that for all $y \in V$ the fibre $X_y$ has at least $n$
irreducible components.

\label{lemma-delta-invariant-and-change-of-fields}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
Let $K/k$ be a field extension and set $Y = X_K$.
Let $y \in Y$ with image $x \in X$.
Assume $X$ is geometrically reduced at $x$ and
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}) = 1$.
Then
$$
\delta\text{-invariant of }X\text{ at }x \leq
\delta\text{-invariant of }Y\text{ at }y
$$

formulation.statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a proper finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension $d$. Let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $a_p$ be the right adjoint to $Rp_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, where $Rp_*$ identifies with derived global sections $R\Gamma(X,-)$. Define the *canonical normalized dualizing complex* $D_X=a_p(k[0])$; it is the compactification-based $p^!k$. Put $\omega_X=H^{-d}(D_X)$ and let $t:H^0(X,D_X)\to k$ be the cohomological trace induced by the adjunction counit $R\Gamma(X,D_X)\to k$. Suppose $X$ is additionally Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension $d$, and set $\omega_X=H^{-d}(D_X)$. Then $D_X\simeq\omega_X[d]$, and (1) $\omega_X$ is a dualizing module on $X$ (the lowest cohomology of its dualizing complex); (2) $\omega_X$ is coherent and Cohen–Macaulay as a module, supported on all of $X$; (3) for any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and integer $i$, $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(K,\omega_X[d])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,K),k)$ naturally and compatibly with shifts and distinguished triangles; (4) for any quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{d-i}_X(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^i(X,\mathcal F),k)$ naturally. All Ext groups are *global derived Ext*, not sheaf Ext.

source.label: lemma-duality-proper-over-field-CM
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-duality-proper-over-field-CM}
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$ which is Cohen-Macaulay
and equidimensional of dimension $d$. The module $\omega_X$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-duality-proper-over-field} has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_X$ is a dualizing module on $X$
(Section \ref{section-dualizing-module}),
\item $\omega_X$ is a coherent Cohen-Macaulay module whose support is $X$,
\item there are functorial isomorphisms
$\Ext^i_X(K, \omega_X[d]) = \Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)$
compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles for $K \in D_\QCoh(X)$,
\item there are functorial isomorphisms
$\Ext^{d - i}(\mathcal{F}, \omega_X) = \Hom_k(H^i(X, \mathcal{F}), k)$
for $\mathcal{F}$ quasi-coherent on $X$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-spectral-sequence}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ be an open covering.
For any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ there
is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(U, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

source.label: lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $K$ be a simplicial presheaf.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf.
Let $K \to \mathcal{G}$ be an augmentation of $K$
towards $\mathcal{G}$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism of presheaves $K_0 \to \mathcal{G}$ becomes
a surjection after sheafification.
\item The morphism
$$
(d^1_0, d^1_1) :
K_1
\longrightarrow
K_0 \times_\mathcal{G} K_0
$$
becomes a surjection after sheafification.
\item For every $n \geq 1$ the morphism
$$
K_{n + 1} \longrightarrow (\text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n K)_{n + 1}
$$
turns into a surjection after sheafification.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H_i(K) = 0$ for $i > 0$ and
$H_0(K) = \mathbf{Z}_\mathcal{G}^\#$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-product-degenerate}
Let $U$, $V$ be simplicial sets.
Let $a, b \geq 0$ be integers.
Assume every $n$-simplex of $U$ is degenerate if $n > a$.
Assume every $n$-simplex of $V$ is degenerate if $n > b$.
Then every $n$-simplex of $U \times V$ is degenerate
if $n > a + b$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rr]_f \ar[rd]_p & & Y \ar[ld]^q \\
& Z
}
$$
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume that $X \to Z$ is locally of

such that $|U(f)| \subset |X|$ is the set of points where $f$ is unramified.

$U(f')$ is the inverse image of $U(f)$ under the projection $X' \to X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-where-unramified}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rr]_f \ar[rd]_p & & Y \ar[ld]^q \\
& Z
}
$$
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume that $X \to Z$ is locally of
finite type. Then there exists an open subspace $U(f) \subset X$
such that $|U(f)| \subset |X|$ is the set of points where $f$ is unramified.
Moreover, for any morphism of algebraic spaces $Z' \to Z$, if
$f' : X' \to Y'$ is the base change of $f$ by $Z' \to Z$, then
$U(f')$ is the inverse image of $U(f)$ under the projection $X' \to X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-reflexive-S2-extend}
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme. Let $j : U \to X$
be an open subscheme with complement $Z$. Assume $\mathcal{O}_{X, z}$
has depth $\geq 2$ for all $z \in Z$. Then $j^*$ and $j_*$ define
an equivalence of categories between the category of coherent reflexive
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and the category of coherent reflexive
$\mathcal{O}_U$-modules.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism.
Assume $\{Z_i\}_{i \in I}$ is a locally
finite collection of closed subsets of $Y$.
Then $\{f^{-1}(Z_i)\}_{i \in I}$ is a locally finite
collection of closed subsets of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-image-locally-finite}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism.
Assume $\{Z_i\}_{i \in I}$ is a locally
finite collection of closed subsets of $Y$.
Then $\{f^{-1}(Z_i)\}_{i \in I}$ is a locally finite
collection of closed subsets of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tor-injective-hull}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local Gorenstein ring
of dimension $d$. Let $E$ be the injective hull of $\kappa$. Then
$\text{Tor}_i^A(E, \kappa)$ is zero for $i \not = d$
and $\text{Tor}_d^A(E, \kappa) = \kappa$.

formulation.statement:
Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Given *any* morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, form $X'=X\times_YY'$ with $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. Write $a'=a_{f'}$. As $f$ is flat the square is Tor-independent, and the canonical duality base-change map
\[
L(g')^*a_f(K)\longrightarrow a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\]
is an isomorphism for all $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. No Tor-dimension assumption is needed on $g$ beyond qcqs.

The proposed claim preserves arbitrary g (not necessarily flat) and distinguishes g from proper flat f.

\label{lemma-proper-flat-base-change}
Let $g : Y' \to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation.
Then the base change map (\ref{equation-base-change-map}) is an isomorphism
for all $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-goes-up}
Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a flat homorphism of Noetherian rings such
that for all primes $\mathfrak q \subset B$ we have
$\mathfrak p B_\mathfrak q = \mathfrak qB_\mathfrak q$
where $\mathfrak p = \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, for example
if $\varphi$ is \'etale.
If $I$ is an injective $A$-module, then $I \otimes_A B$ is
an injective $B$-module.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For proper, not necessarily projective X/k and K in unbounded D_QCoh, bounded coherent K is equivalent to finite total Ext against every perfect E. Both quantified directions and properness remain.

phase3.reason: One implication follows from the prior finiteness lemma; the converse follows from relative perfectness, with the projective case checked by embedding in projective space.

conclusions: Family descent data and descent data along the coproduct map are equivalent categories.
hypotheses: A family of schemes over S and its coproduct X.
formulation.statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Let $X=\coprod_{i\in I}X_i$ for a family $\{X_i\to S\}$. Then the category of descent data for schemes relative to the family is canonically equivalent to $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$, by taking $V=\coprod_iV_i$ and identifying the descent isomorphism over $X\times_SX=\coprod_{i,j}(X_i\times_SX_j)$ with the disjoint union of the maps $\varphi_{ij}$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L8249 states an equivalence between scheme descent data for a FAMILY {X_i→S} and the one-map coproduct X=⨿X_i→S. The final formulation gives the correct scheme-valued cocycle isomorphisms on pair overlaps, constructs V=⨿V_i and φ=⨿φ_ij using X×_S X=⨿_(i,j)(X_i×_S X_j), and retains a categorical equivalence rather than asserting all descent data effective.

phase3.reason: The proof explicitly identifies the fibre products of the disjoint union X=⨿Xi as disjoint unions of pairwise overlaps, so a descent datum and its cocycle/morphisms correspond componentwise in both categories.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For complexes $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ of modules, $\mathrm{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}B^\bullet)$ denotes the ordinary total tensor-product complex with the standard signed differential; $K(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ is the homotopy category of complexes. Tensoring with a quasi-isomorphism between **two K-flat complexes** on the other side is the precise asserted invariance, even when the first factor is an arbitrary complex.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$\alpha : \mathcal{P}^\bullet \to \mathcal{Q}^\bullet$ be a
quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
For every complex $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
the induced map
$$
\text{Tot}(\text{id}_{\mathcal{F}^\bullet} \otimes \alpha) :
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{P}^\bullet)
\longrightarrow
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{Q}^\bullet)
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A quasi-isomorphism between two K-flat complexes remains a quasi-isomorphism after total tensor with any fixed F• on the other side; neither F• boundedness nor K-flatness is needed.

phase3.reason: The proof replaces the arbitrary first tensor factor with a K-flat resolution and applies the earlier K-flat quasi-isomorphism lemma to three sides of a commuting square.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-X}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite
type. Assume the set of weakly associated points of $S$ is locally finite
in $S$. Then the set of points $x \in X$ where $f$ is flat is an open
subscheme $U \subset X$ and $U \to S$ is flat and locally of finite
presentation.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, smooth morphism all of whose fibres are nonempty and equidimensional of the same dimension $n\geq0$.
Then $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a finite étale $\mathcal O_S$-algebra. Zariski-locally on $S$ there exists a perfect complex $P$ of Tor amplitude contained in $[1,\infty)$ with

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-dualizing-composition}
Let $f : Y \to X$ and $X \to S$ be morphisms of schemes
which are flat and of finite presentation.
Let $(K, \xi)$ and $(M, \eta)$
be a relative dualizing complex for $X \to S$ and $Y \to X$.
Set $E = M \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} Lf^*K$.
Then $(E, \zeta)$ is a relative dualizing complex for $Y \to S$ for
a suitable $\zeta$.

conclusions: Upper-shriek structure complex invertible and f^! preserves perfect complexes.
hypotheses: f local complete intersection in FTS_S.
formulation.statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ is a *local complete intersection morphism*: locally on its source it factors as a regular (Koszul-regular) closed immersion into a smooth $Y$-scheme. Then (1) $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is *derived-invertible*: locally on $X$ it is a shift of an invertible sheaf and admits a two-sided inverse for derived tensor product; and (2) the upper-shriek functor $f^!$ takes perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ to perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, interpreted on the bounded-below subcategory where $f^!$ is defined.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L4691 assumes an LCI S-morphism f in FTS_S. It yields TWO claims: f^!O_Y is INVERTIBLE IN D(O_X), locally a shifted line bundle, AND f^! sends perfect complexes on Y to perfect complexes on X. The proposed statement restores the local Koszul-regular closed immersion plus smooth factorization, and retains both properties.

phase3.reason: Factor a local complete intersection into a smooth affine projection and Koszul-regular immersion, then into effective Cartier divisors; each shriek dualizing object is invertible.

Let $x \in |X|$ be a point. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is regular at $x$, and
\item the \'etale local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}$ is
regular for any (equivalently some) geometric point $\overline{x}$
lying over $x$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-torsion-flat-change-rings}
Let $A \to B$ be a flat ring map and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely
generated ideal such that $A/I = B/IB$. Then base change and
restriction induce quasi-inverse equivalences
$D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A) = D_{(IB)^\infty\text{-torsion}}(B)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-projection-formula}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Assume $\mathcal{E}$ is finite locally free on $Y$, see
Modules, Definition \ref{modules-definition-locally-free}.
Then there exist isomorphisms
$$
\mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} R^qf_*\mathcal{F}
\longrightarrow
R^qf_*(f^*\mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{F})
$$
for all $q \geq 0$. In fact there exists an isomorphism
$$
\mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} Rf_*\mathcal{F}
\longrightarrow
Rf_*(f^*\mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{F})
$$
in $D^{+}(Y)$ functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

\label{lemma-pullback-etale-equivalence-relation}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
Then $\Delta_{F/G} : F \to F \times_G F$ is representable by
algebraic spaces.

phase3.reason: The diagonal of the fibre square is identified with a fibre product of the algebraic-space diagonal, proving representability.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

Let $c : X \to Y$ be the contraction of a rational bridge
(with rational bridge as explicitly defined above).
Then $c^*\omega_Y \cong \omega_X$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For the contraction c:X→Y of a rational bridge, c*ω_Y≅ω_X. The proposal includes the pushout contraction model and preserves equality of these two dualizing sheaves.

phase3.reason: The contraction pullback equivalence on invertible sheaves trivial along the bridge follows from the Picard-contraction result and projection formula. The restricted dualizing sheaf has degree zero and is trivial by the genus-zero criterion. Using R^1c_*O_X=0, Leray, and the representing property of the dualizing sheaf gives the asserted crepant identification; a small degree detail is omitted.

**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map is **ind-Zariski** when its target is a filtered colimit of local-isomorphism algebras over the source.

Let $A$ be a ring. Let $V(I) \subset \Spec(A)$ be a closed subset
which is a profinite topological space. Then there exists an
ind-Zariski ring map $A \to B$ such that $\Spec(B)$ is w-local,
the set of closed points is $V(IB)$, and $A/I \cong B/IB$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localize-along-closed-profinite}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $V(I) \subset \Spec(A)$ be a closed subset
which is a profinite topological space. Then there exists an
ind-Zariski ring map $A \to B$ such that $\Spec(B)$ is w-local,
the set of closed points is $V(IB)$, and $A/I \cong B/IB$.

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A *Serre functor* on a Hom-finite $k$-linear triangulated category $\mathcal T$ is a $k$-linear self-equivalence $S$ equipped with bifunctorial isomorphisms $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(Y,S(X))^\vee$. The specified bifunctorial isomorphisms are part of the Serre data. A covariant functor is *representable* if isomorphic to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(Q,-)$ for some $Q$ and *corepresentable* if of the opposite Hom variance.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a $k$-linear
triangulated category such that $\dim_k \Hom_\mathcal{T}(X, Y) < \infty$
for all $X, Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{T})$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a $k$-linear equivalence
$S : \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{T}$ and $k$-linear isomorphisms
$c_{X, Y} : \Hom_\mathcal{T}(X, Y) \to \Hom_\mathcal{T}(Y, S(X))^\vee$
functorial in $X, Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{T})$,
\item for every $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{T})$
the functor $Y \mapsto \Hom_\mathcal{T}(X, Y)^\vee$
is representable and the functor $Y \mapsto \Hom_\mathcal{T}(Y, X)^\vee$
is corepresentable.
\end{enumerate}

**Scope and interpretation:** Representability and corepresentability must use the appropriate covariant or contravariant Hom variance. Finite-dimensional Hom spaces allow bidual identification and construction of a quasi-inverse.

formulation.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Here $M$ is any differential graded right $B$-module, viewed as an object of $D(B,\mathrm d)$ as appropriate.

Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras
over a ring $R$. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ there are isomorphisms
$$
H^n(R\Hom(N, M)) = \Ext^n_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, M)
$$
of $R$-modules functorial in $M$. It is also functorial in $N$
contravariantly under homomorphisms of differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodules (by precomposition on derived Hom).

phase2.semantic_review_note: For every integer n, the n-th cohomology of RHom_B(N,M) computes Ext^n in D(B) from N to M, as R-modules. The proposed formulation retains covariant naturality in M and the source's contravariant naturality in bimodule N.

phase3.reason: Computes RHom(N,M) as Hom_B(N,I) for a property-(I) replacement M→I. The cited derived-Hom comparison identifies its cohomology with Ext^n_{D(B)}(N,M). Contravariance in N follows by precomposition using the earlier functoriality lemma; the source omits details of the latter.

source.label: lemma-derived-restriction-exts
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-derived-restriction-exts}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras
over a ring $R$. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ there are isomorphisms
$$
H^n(R\Hom(N, M)) = \Ext^n_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, M)
$$
of $R$-modules functorial in $M$. It is also functorial in $N$
with respect to the operation described in
Lemma \ref{lemma-functoriality-derived-restriction}.

\label{lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing}
Consider a cartesian square
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_{g'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
of schemes. Assume $X \to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.
Let $(K, \xi)$ be a relative dualizing complex for $f$.
Set $K' = L(g')^*K$. Let $\xi'$ be the derived base change of $\xi$
(see proof). Then $(K', \xi')$ is a relative dualizing complex for $f'$.

source.label: lemma-relocalize
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relocalize}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $f : V \to U$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{C}/V \ar[rd]_{j_V} \ar[rr]_j & &
\mathcal{C}/U \ar[ld]^{j_U} \\
& \mathcal{C} &
}
$$
of continuous and cocontinuous functors.
The functor $j : \mathcal{C}/V \to \mathcal{C}/U$,
$(a : W \to V) \mapsto (f \circ a : W \to U)$
is identified with the functor
$j_{V/U} : (\mathcal{C}/U)/(V/U) \to \mathcal{C}/U$
via the identification $(\mathcal{C}/U)/(V/U) = \mathcal{C}/V$.
Moreover we have $j_{V!} = j_{U!} \circ j_!$,
$j_V^{-1} = j^{-1} \circ j_U^{-1}$, and
$j_{V*} = j_{U*} \circ j_*$.

source.label: lemma-permanence-finite-type
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-permanence-finite-type}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of
formal algebraic spaces over $S$. If $g \circ f : X \to Z$ is locally of
finite type, then $f : X \to Y$ is locally of finite type.

phase2.proposed_correction: Introduce j_U:C/U→C and the associated direct-image functor j_{U*}, then state the internal Hom identification with the full target sheaf formula; independently re-review.

phase3.reason: Yoneda applied to a chain of adjunctions gives Hom(G,j_*F|_{C/U})=Hom(G|_{C/U},F|_{C/U})=Hom(G×h_U#,F)=Hom(G,SheafHom(h_U#,F)); hence the claimed internal-Hom sheaf identification.

formulation.statement:
The relative dimension and transcendence degree of an algebraic-space morphism at a point are defined in §33 via suitable étale presentations and geometric fibres.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X \to Y \to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$ and let $y \in |Y|$, $z \in |Z|$
be the images. Assume $X \to Y$ is locally quasi-finite and $Y \to Z$
locally of finite type. Then the transcendence degree of $x/z$
is equal to the transcendence degree of $y/z$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For X→Y locally quasi-finite and Y→Z locally finite type, transcendence degrees of x/z and y/z agree. Every map and local finiteness condition is retained.

phase3.reason: At compatible étale scheme charts, local quasi-finiteness of X→Y forces the residue-field extension κ(u)/κ(v) finite. The transcendence degree of x/z is therefore that of y/z by the tower formula and invariance under étale field extensions.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-tr-deg}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X \to Y \to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$ and let $y \in |Y|$, $z \in |Z|$
be the images. Assume $X \to Y$ is locally quasi-finite and $Y \to Z$
locally of finite type. Then the transcendence degree of $x/z$
is equal to the transcendence degree of $y/z$.

A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.
formulation.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to
\mathcal{X} \times_{\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every $1$-morphism $\mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
with $\mathcal{V}$ representable (by a scheme) the fibre product
$\mathcal{Y} =
\mathcal{X} \times_{\Delta, \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{V}$
has diagonal representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-charpoly}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be an $n \times n$
matrix with coefficients in $R$. Let $P(x) \in R[x]$
be the characteristic polynomial of $A$ (defined
as $\det(x\text{id}_{n \times n} - A)$).
Then $P(A) = 0$ in $\text{Mat}(n \times n, R)$.

source.label: lemma-pre-symbol
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pre-symbol}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module of dimension $1$.
Assume $\varphi, \psi : M \to M$ are two injective
$A$-module maps, and assume $\varphi(\psi(M)) = \psi(\varphi(M))$,
for example if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ commute.
Then $\text{length}_A(M/\varphi\psi M) < \infty$
and $(M/\varphi\psi M, \varphi, \psi)$ is an exact
$(2, 1)$-periodic complex.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators}
Let $R \to A$ be a standard smooth ring map.
Let $E \subset A$ be a finite subset of order $|E| = n$.
Then there exists a presentation
$A = R[x_1, \ldots, x_{n + m}]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$ with $c \geq n$,
with $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i, j = 1, \ldots, c}$
invertible in $A$, and such that $E$ is the set of congruence classes of
$x_1, \ldots, x_n$.

Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Let $\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\to H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ be the Gysin map constructed from $\gamma^p$ and the map from cohomology with support to ordinary cohomology. Then for $\alpha\in H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/S})$,
$$\gamma^{p,q}(i^*\alpha)=\alpha\cup\gamma^{0,0}(1)\quad\text{in }H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}),$$
where $1\in H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

\label{lemma-left-localization-diagram}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $S$ be a left multiplicative
system. If $f : X \to Y$, $f' : X' \to Y'$ are two morphisms of
$\mathcal{C}$ and if
$$
\xymatrix{
Q(X) \ar[d]_{Q(f)} \ar[r]_a & Q(X') \ar[d]^{Q(f')} \\
Q(Y) \ar[r]^b & Q(Y')
}
$$
is a commutative diagram in $S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$, then there exist
a morphism $f'' : X'' \to Y''$ in $\mathcal{C}$ and a commutative
diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d]_f \ar[r]_g & X'' \ar[d]^{f''} & X' \ar[d]^{f'} \ar[l]^s \\
Y \ar[r]^h & Y'' & Y' \ar[l]_t
}
$$
in $\mathcal{C}$ with $s, t \in S$ and $a = s^{-1}g$, $b = t^{-1}h$.

source.label: lemma-blowup
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowup}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes
smooth over $S$. Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of $Z$ with
exceptional divisor $E \subset X'$. Then $X'$ and $E$ are smooth
over $S$. The morphism $p : E \to Z$ is canonically isomorphic
to the projective space bundle
$$
\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}^2) \longrightarrow Z
$$
where $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ is the ideal sheaf
of $Z$. The relative $\mathcal{O}_E(1)$ coming from the projective
space bundle structure is isomorphic to the restriction of
$\mathcal{O}_{X'}(-E)$ to $E$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-affine-cohomology}
Let $f : X \to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = H^i(S, f_*\mathcal{F})$ for all $i \geq 0$.

$\mathcal{F}$ coherent and the map on stalks
$\varphi_x : \mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{F}_x$ injective.

$x \in U \subset X$ such that $\varphi|_U$ is injective.

\label{lemma-effective-support-closed}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$ be integers.
Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$.
If $\alpha$ is effective, then $\text{Supp}(\alpha)$ is
closed in $X$.

Pinned-source conventions: a short exact sequence of $A$-modules is universally exact (pure exact) when it remains exact after tensoring with any $A$-module. An $A$-module $P$ is pure projective if $\Hom_A(P,-)$ takes every universally exact short exact sequence to a short exact sequence. An $A$-module $I$ is pure injective if $\Hom_A(-,I)$ takes every universally exact short exact sequence to a short exact sequence (with arrows reversed).

Let $A$ be a ring. For any $A$-module $M$ set
$M^\vee = \Hom_\mathbf{Z}(M, \mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $A$-module $M$ the $A$-module $M^\vee$ is pure injective.
\item An $A$-module $I$ is pure injective if and only if the map
$I \to (I^\vee)^\vee$ splits.
\item For any module $M$ there exists a universally exact sequence
$0 \to M \to I \to N \to 0$ with $I$ pure injective.
\end{enumerate}
