source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-cohomology}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$ we have
$$
H^i(X_\etale, \mathcal{F}) =
H^i(X_\proetale, \epsilon^{-1}\mathcal{F})
$$
for all $i$.
\item For $K \in D^+(X_\etale)$ we have
$$
R\Gamma(X_\etale, K) = R\Gamma(X_\proetale, \epsilon^{-1}K)
$$
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
In the category of abelian sheaves on a site, $\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$ denotes the sheaf product. For an object $U$, the projections induce a canonical comparison from the cohomology of this product to the product of the individual cohomology groups.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$ let 
$\mathcal{F}_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$. Let
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. The canonical map
$$
H^p(U, \prod\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \in I} H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for $p = 0$ and injective for $p = 1$.

\label{lemma-cohomology-products}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$ let 
$\mathcal{F}_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$. Let
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. The canonical map
$$
H^p(U, \prod\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \in I} H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for $p = 0$ and injective for $p = 1$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-between-flat}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is locally of finite presentation over $S$,
\item $X$ is flat over $S$,
\item for every $s \in S$ the morphism
$f_s : X_s \to Y_s$ is flat, and
\item $Y$ is locally of finite type over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is flat. If $f$ is also surjective, then $Y$ is flat over $S$.

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-covering-quotient}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Consider an algebraic space $F$ of the form $F = U/R$
where $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is a groupoid in algebraic spaces
over $S$ such that $s, t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, and
$j = (t, s) : R \to U \times_S U$ is an equivalence relation.
Then $U \to F$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation.

Flatness of a quasi-coherent module at x over Y can be tested on an étale scheme diagram or on the strict-henselian étale local rings.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in |X|$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item for some commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d]_a \ar[r]_h & V \ar[d]^b \\
X \ar[r]^f & Y
}
$$
where $U$ and $V$ are schemes, $a, b$ are \'etale, and
$u \in U$ mapping to $x$ the module $a^*\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $u$ over $V$,
\item the stalk $\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}}$ is flat over
the \'etale local ring $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \overline{y}}$
where $\overline{x}$ is any geometric point lying over
$x$ and $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\end{enumerate}

The base-change stalk formula, faithfully flat descent, and the flatness-up-and-down henselization lemma show equivalence of both flatness tests.

\label{lemma-flat-at-point}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in |X|$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item for some commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d]_a \ar[r]_h & V \ar[d]^b \\
X \ar[r]^f & Y
}
$$
where $U$ and $V$ are schemes, $a, b$ are \'etale, and
$u \in U$ mapping to $x$ the module $a^*\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $u$ over $V$,
\item the stalk $\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}}$ is flat over
the \'etale local ring $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \overline{y}}$
where $\overline{x}$ is any geometric point lying over
$x$ and $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $(\mathcal F_n^\bullet)$ be an inverse system of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules on a ringed site, and let $\mathcal F^\bullet=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n^\bullet$ be their **termwise** inverse limit. For a site object $U$, $H^m(\mathcal F_n^\bullet(U))$ is cohomology of the complex of **sections** over $U$, while $H^m(\mathcal F_n^\bullet)$ is the **cohomology sheaf**. The $R^1\varprojlim$ conditions below concern inverse systems of groups of sections; the final map is an isomorphism of sheaves. This is a technical lemma about an ordinary limit, not an assumption that ordinary and derived limits coincide automatically.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet)$ be an inverse system of complexes of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules. Let $m \in \mathbf{Z}$. Suppose given
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and an integer
$n_0$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item for every $U \in \mathcal{B}$
\begin{enumerate}
\item the systems of abelian groups
$\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 2}(U)$ and $\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 1}(U)$
have vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example these have the Mittag-Leffler property),
\item the system of abelian groups $H^{m - 1}(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U))$
has vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example it has the Mittag-Leffler property), and
\item we have
$H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U)) = H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet(U))$
for all $n \geq n_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then the maps $H^m(\mathcal{F}^\bullet) \to \lim H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet)
\to H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet)$ are isomorphisms of sheaves where
$\mathcal{F}^\bullet = \lim \mathcal{F}_n^\bullet$ is the termwise
inverse limit.

Distinction from sections retained.

\begin{enumerate}

$\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 2}(U)$ and $\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 1}(U)$

\item the system of abelian groups $H^{m - 1}(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U))$
has vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example it has the Mittag-Leffler property), and
\item we have
$H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U)) = H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet(U))$

\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-projective-after-field-extension}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$. If $X_K$ is projective
over $K$ for some field extension $K/k$, then $X$ is projective
over $k$.

\item $\mathcal{J}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}$-module, and
\item the canonical maps
$$
\text{Sym}^n_{\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}}(\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2)

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-regular-ideal}
Let $X$ be a locally ringed space. Let $\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a sheaf of ideals. Then $\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-regular if and
only if the following conditions are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{J}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}$-module, and
\item the canonical maps
$$
\text{Sym}^n_{\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}}(\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{J}^n/\mathcal{J}^{n + 1}
$$
are isomorphisms for all $n \geq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-directed-colimit-exact}
\begin{slogan}
Filtered colimits are exact. Directed colimits are exact.
\end{slogan}
Let $I$ be a directed set.
Let $(L_i, \lambda_{ij})$, $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$, and
$(N_i, \nu_{ij})$ be systems of $R$-modules over $I$.
Let $\varphi_i : L_i \to M_i$ and $\psi_i : M_i \to N_i$ be
morphisms of systems over $I$. Assume that for all $i \in I$ the
sequence of $R$-modules
$$
\xymatrix{
L_i \ar[r]^{\varphi_i} &
M_i \ar[r]^{\psi_i} &
N_i
}
$$
is a complex with homology $H_i$.
Then the $R$-modules $H_i$ form a system over $I$,
the sequence of $R$-modules
$$
\xymatrix{
\colim_i L_i \ar[r]^\varphi &
\colim_i M_i \ar[r]^\psi &
\colim_i N_i
}
$$
is a complex as well, and denoting $H$ its homology we have
$$
H = \colim_i H_i.
$$

formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

Let $A \to A' \to B$ be ring maps such that $B = B \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A'$.
Then $L_{B/A} = L_{B/A'}$ in $D(B)$.

source.label: lemma-integral-normal
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-normal}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme.
Then $X$ is normal if and only if for every nonempty affine open
$U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is a normal domain.

formulation.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A ring map is **ind-étale** when its target is a filtered colimit of étale algebras over the source.

Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. The base change functor
$$
\text{ind-\'etale }A\text{-algebras}
\longrightarrow
\text{ind-\'etale }A/I\text{-algebras},\quad
C \longmapsto C/IC
$$
has a fully faithful right adjoint $v$. In particular, given
an ind-\'etale $A/I$-algebra $\overline{C}$ there exists
an ind-\'etale $A$-algebra $C = v(\overline{C})$ such that
$\overline{C} = C/IC$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned proetale.tex L1220 (lemma-lift-ind-etale): For any ideal I⊂A, base change from IND-ÉTALE A-algebras to IND-ÉTALE A/I-algebras has a FULLY FAITHFUL RIGHT ADJOINT v. Every ind-étale quotient algebra thus lifts to C=v(Cbar) with C/IC=Cbar. Both the adjunction and existence consequence are retained.

phase3.reason: Constructs the directed category of étale A-algebras mapping to an ind-étale A/I-algebra; filtered colimit C is ind-étale and reduces modulo I to the target. The universal property of the category produces Hom_A(D,C)=Hom_{A/I}(D/ID,Cbar), hence a fully faithful right adjoint. Routine set-theoretic details are flagged in the original.

source.label: lemma-lift-ind-etale
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-ind-etale}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. The base change functor
$$
\text{ind-\'etale }A\text{-algebras}
\longrightarrow
\text{ind-\'etale }A/I\text{-algebras},\quad
C \longmapsto C/IC
$$
has a fully faithful right adjoint $v$. In particular, given
an ind-\'etale $A/I$-algebra $\overline{C}$ there exists
an ind-\'etale $A$-algebra $C = v(\overline{C})$ such that
$\overline{C} = C/IC$.

source.label: lemma-colimits-abelian-as-sets
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colimits-abelian-as-sets}
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an index category, i.e., a category. Assume
that for every pair of objects $x, y$ of $\mathcal{I}$
there exist an object $z$ and morphisms $x \to z$ and $y \to z$.
Let $M : \mathcal{I} \to \textit{Ab}$ be a diagram of abelian
groups over $\mathcal{I}$. Then the colimit of $M$ in the category
of sets surjects onto the colimit of $M$ in the category of
abelian groups.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exact-sequence-induction}
Let $k$ be an infinite field. Let $n \geq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent module on $\mathbf{P}^n_k$.
Then there exist a nonzero section
$s \in \Gamma(\mathbf{P}^n_k, \mathcal{O}(1))$
and a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F}(-1) \to \mathcal{F} \to i_*\mathcal{G} \to 0
$$
where $i : H \to \mathbf{P}^n_k$ is the hyperplane $H$ associated to $s$
and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{F}$.

Conversely, if C has enough points and every stalk E_p has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then E has Tor-amplitude [a,b].
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, E∈D(O) and a≤b integers.
formulation.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). An O-module F has Tor dimension ≤d when F[0] has Tor-amplitude in [−d,0] (source Definition tor-amplitude lines 12376–12394). Stalkwise Tor-amplitude uses derived stalks E_p over the local stalk ring O_p. The **converse** requires the site to have **enough points** and is not asserted for arbitrary sites.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$, then for every point $p$
of the site $\mathcal{C}$ the object $E_p$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_p)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$.
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has enough points, then the converse is true.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Tor-amplitude [a,b] passes to all derived stalks at any site point, while reflection from all stalks to E requires C to have enough points; the extra hypothesis is scoped exclusively to the converse.

phase3.reason: The forward direction applies the Tor-amplitude pullback lemma to each point and the converse uses enough points to detect cohomology vanishing of all derived tensors.

\label{lemma-functor-equivalence}
Let $A$ and $B$ be rings. If
$$
F : \text{Mod}_A \longrightarrow \text{Mod}_B
$$
is an equivalence of categories, then there exists an isomorphism
$A \to B$ of rings and an invertible $B$-module $L$ such that
$F$ is isomorphic to the functor $M \mapsto (M \otimes_A B) \otimes_B L$.

Let $K$ be a field with separable closure $K^{sep}$ and absolute Galois group $G_K$. For a maximal pro-$\ell$ subgroup $H\subseteq G_K$, its fixed field is $L=(K^{sep})^H$, so $\operatorname{Gal}(K^{sep}/L)=H$; $\ell$-*primary torsion étale sheaves* on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ are discrete continuous $G_K$-modules killed elementwise by some power of $\ell$. Their cohomology agrees with continuous Galois cohomology. The *Brauer group* $\operatorname{Br}(K)$ consists of Morita classes of finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebras. A field $K$ is **$C_r$** if, for every positive integer degree $d$ and number of variables $n>d^r$, every homogeneous degree-$d$ polynomial over $K$ in $n$ variables has a **nonzero common solution** (for one polynomial). A *variety over $k$* in this source means a **separated integral scheme of finite type** over $k$, and its function field is the local ring at the generic point.

The function field of a variety of dimension $r$ over an algebraically closed
field $k$ is $C_r$.

formulation.statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *local on the target for the $\tau$-topology* if for every $\tau$-covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ if and only if each base-changed morphism $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ has $\mathcal P$. Let $\tau$ be one of fpqc, fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale, or Zariski, and let $\mathcal P$ be $\tau$-local on the target. If $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$, then its base change along any $g:Y'\to Y$ belonging to the corresponding class of maps—flat for fpqc; flat locally finitely presented for fppf; syntomic for syntomic; smooth for smooth; étale for étale; and an open immersion for Zariski—also has $\mathcal P$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-property-local-target}
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, syntomic, smooth, \etale, Zariski\}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms which is $\tau$ local
on the target. Let $f : X \to Y$ have property $\mathcal{P}$.
For any morphism $Y' \to Y$ which is
flat, resp.\ flat and locally of finite presentation, resp.\ syntomic,
resp.\ \'etale, resp.\ an open immersion, the base change
$f' : Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$ of $f$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

cartesian diagram
$$

P \ar[u] \ar[l]
}

with $\psi_i$ and $\varphi_i$ surjective, and $Q$, $A_i$, $B_i$ of
finite type over $R$. Then $P$ is of finite type over $R$.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. For an immersion $i:Z\to X$, choose an open $V\subset X$ where it is closed, with ideal $\mathcal I$; the conormal algebra $\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ has degree $n$ piece corresponding to $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ on $Z$, and $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal C_{Z/X,1}$. Its canonical map from $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})$ is induced by multiplication of ideals. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes. Then $i$ is a quasi-regular
immersion if and only if the following conditions are satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item the conormal sheaf $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ is finite locally free, and
\item the map (\ref{equation-conormal-algebra-quotient}) is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-maximal-points-affine}
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme.
Let $Z_1, \ldots, Z_n$ be pairwise distinct irreducible components of $X$,
see Topology, Section \ref{topology-section-irreducible-components}.
Let $\eta_i \in Z_i$ be their generic points, see
Schemes, Lemma \ref{schemes-lemma-scheme-sober}.
There exist affine open neighbourhoods $\eta_i \in U_i$
such that $U_i \cap U_j = \emptyset$ for all $i \not = j$.
In particular, $U = U_1 \cup \ldots \cup U_n$ is an affine
open containing all of the points $\eta_1, \ldots, \eta_n$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume either
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is quasi-affine.
\item The scheme $X$ is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme
of an affine scheme.
\item There exists an ample invertible sheaf on $X$.
\item The scheme $X$ is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme
of $\text{Proj}(S)$ for some graded ring $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for any finite subset $E \subset X$ there exists an
affine open $U \subset X$ with $E \subset U$.

\label{lemma-cute-groupoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
If $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ is a category fibred in groupoids
and $p$ factors through $p' : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}/U$
then $p' : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}/U$ is fibred in groupoids.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-morphism-sites}
\begin{slogan}
A map of sites defines a map on points, and pullback respects stalks.
\end{slogan}
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites
given by a continuous functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
Let $q$ be a point of $\mathcal{D}$ given by the functor
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$, see
Definition \ref{definition-point}.
Then the functor $v \circ u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
defines a point $p$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and moreover there is
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, say *at worst nodal of relative dimension one* if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and each nonempty geometric fibre is an equidimensional one-dimensional scheme with at-worst-nodal singularities. Equivalently $f$ is syntomic of relative dimension one and $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, defined by the first Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/S}$, is unramified over $S$. Here syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres. This property is stable under base change and local for the étale topology on the source and fpqc topology on the target.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, say *at worst nodal of relative dimension one* if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and each nonempty geometric fibre is an equidimensional one-dimensional scheme with at-worst-nodal singularities. Equivalently $f$ is syntomic of relative dimension one and $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, defined by the first Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/S}$, is unramified over $S$. Here syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres. This property is stable under base change and local for the étale topology on the source and fpqc topology on the target.

Let $S' \to S$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
Let $f : X \to S'$ be at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.
Then the composition $g : X \to S$
is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.

\label{lemma-nodal-family-postcompose-etale}
Let $S' \to S$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
Let $f : X \to S'$ be at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.
Then the composition $g : X \to S$
is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.

phase3.reason: Splitting every sheafified cover epi lifts local sections of a sheaf epi globally, proving (1)⇒(2). Conversely apply (2) to the covering epi ⨿h_{U_i}#→h_U#, lift id_U and use Yoneda to obtain its right inverse.

For a property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms preserved under arbitrary base change and fppf-local on the base, $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ precisely if all resulting scheme maps $V_\xi\to U$ have $\mathcal P$. \label{lemma-descent-representable-transformations-property}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Let $b : H \to G$ be any transformation of functors.
Consider the fibre product diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
H \times_{b, G, a} F \ar[r]_-{b'} \ar[d]_{a'} & F \ar[d]^a \\
H \ar[r]^b & G
}
$$
Assume that $b$ induces a surjective map of fppf sheaves $H^\# \to G^\#$.
In this case, if $a'$ has property $\mathcal{P}$, then also $a$
has property $\mathcal{P}$.

hypotheses: f in FTS_S, K bounded coherent on X, L bounded below coherent on Y, compactification-based upper/lower shriek.
formulation.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$; let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of separated schemes of finite type over $S$. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, the *upper shriek* $f^!$ sends $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ and is built from proper compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$ by $j^*a_{\bar f}$, where $a_{\bar f}$ is right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$. The corresponding *lower shriek* $Rf_!:D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_Y))$ is $R\bar f_*Rj_!$ for any compactification; proper pushforward is applied termwise to the pro-system. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ and every *bounded-below coherent* $L\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a bifunctorial isomorphism of Hom sets
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(K,f^!L)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y))}(Rf_!K,L).
\]
The right side regards $L$ as a **constant** pro-object; this is the coherent pro-category analogue of an adjunction, not an ordinary adjunction between $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)$ and $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(Y)$ alone.

The final retains the pro-object lower-shriek Rf_! built by compactification and pro-extension, treats L as constant, and does not mistake this for ordinary Hom adjunction on two ordinary categories.

\label{proposition-duality-compactly-supported}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Then the functors $Rf_!$ and $f^!$ are adjoint in
the following sense: for all $K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
and $L \in D^+_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ we have
$$
\Hom_X(K, f^!L) =
\Hom_{\text{Pro-}D^+_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_Y)}(Rf_!K, L)
$$
bifunctorially in $K$ and $L$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $x \in X$. Set $y = f(x)$ and $s \in S$ the image of $x$ in $S$.
Assume $S$, $X$, $Y$ locally Noetherian,
$\mathcal{F}$ coherent, and $\mathcal{F}_x \not = 0$.
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at $x$, and
$\mathcal{F}_s$ is flat over $Y_s$ at $x$, and
\item $Y$ is flat over $S$ at $y$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is
flat over $Y$ at $x$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $S$ be a scheme all of whose local rings are strictly henselian.
Then for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $S_\etale$ we have
$H^i(S_\etale, \mathcal{F}) = H^i(S_{Zar}, \mathcal{F})$.

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

phase3.reason: The proof compares étale and Zariski higher direct-image stalks through local limits and applies strictly Henselian local acyclicity and Leray.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-rings-strictly-henselian}
Let $S$ be a scheme all of whose local rings are strictly henselian.
Then for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $S_\etale$ we have
$H^i(S_\etale, \mathcal{F}) = H^i(S_{Zar}, \mathcal{F})$.

Let $R \to R'$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $R \to A$ be of finite type. Set $A' = A \otimes_R R'$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to R'$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is perfect
and $R'$ and $A$ are tor independent over $R$,
\end{enumerate}
then there is an isomorphism
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' \to \omega^\bullet_{A'/R'}$
in $D(A')$.
The conclusion is existence of a base-change isomorphism in D(A'), not a canonical choice; under the third alternative the explicit condition is Tor_i^R(A,R')=0 for i>0.

formulation.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

Let $R \to R'$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $R \to A$ be of finite type. Set $A' = A \otimes_R R'$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to R'$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is perfect
and $R'$ and $A$ are tor independent over $R$,
\end{enumerate}
then there is an isomorphism
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' \to \omega^\bullet_{A'/R'}$
in $D(A')$.

**Scope and interpretation:** The conclusion is existence of a base-change isomorphism in D(A'), not a canonical choice; under the third alternative the explicit condition is Tor_i^R(A,R')=0 for i>0.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-relative-algebraic}
Let $R \to R'$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $R \to A$ be of finite type. Set $A' = A \otimes_R R'$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to R'$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is perfect
and $R'$ and $A$ are tor independent over $R$,
\end{enumerate}
then there is an isomorphism
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' \to \omega^\bullet_{A'/R'}$
in $D(A')$.

phase2.proposed_correction: Use equivalence logical form and expand finite locally free for a representable morphism to a standalone condition, then obtain a fresh independent source-first review.

phase3.reason: If f is finite locally free, its structure-sheaf pushforward becomes finite locally free after a surjective étale chart; descent makes the pushforward finite locally free. Conversely an affine map with finite locally free pushforward is locally finite locally free on charts, and the descent theorem recovers f finite locally free.

source.label: lemma-finite-locally-free-representable
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-locally-free-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then $f$ is finite locally free
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if $f$ is affine and the sheaf $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is
a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.

\label{lemma-locally-P}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $P$ be a property of ring maps.
Let $U$ be an affine open of $X$,
and $V$ an affine open of $S$ such that
$f(U) \subset V$.
If $f$ is locally of type $P$ and $P$ is local,
then $P(\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U))$ holds.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-degree-on-proper-curve}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper curve over $k$ with generic point
$\xi$. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of rank $n$
and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
$$
\chi(X, \mathcal{E} \otimes \mathcal{F}) =
r \deg(\mathcal{E}) + n \chi(X, \mathcal{F})
$$
where $r = \dim_{\kappa(\xi)} \mathcal{F}_\xi$ is the rank of $\mathcal{F}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-isomorphic-finite-projective-lifts}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal. Assume that
every element of $1 + I$ is a unit (in other words $I$ is contained
in the Jacobson radical of $R$). If $P$ and $P'$ are finite
projective $R$-modules, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $\varphi : P \to P'$ is an $R$-module map inducing an
isomorphism $\overline{\varphi} : P/IP \to P'/IP'$, then $\varphi$
is an isomorphism,
\item if $P/IP \cong P'/IP'$, then $P \cong P'$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes. Let
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
cutting out $Z$. The functor
$$
i_* :
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those quasi-coherent

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale}
Let $T$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $T' \to T$ is an isomorphism then $\{T' \to T\}$
is an \'etale covering of $T$.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is an \'etale covering and for each
$i$ we have an \'etale covering $\{T_{ij} \to T_i\}_{j\in J_i}$, then
$\{T_{ij} \to T\}_{i \in I, j\in J_i}$ is an \'etale covering.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is an \'etale covering
and $T' \to T$ is a morphism of schemes then
$\{T' \times_T T_i \to T'\}_{i\in I}$ is an \'etale covering.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian separated scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be
a dense affine open. If $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all
$x \in X \setminus U$, then there exists an effective Cartier
divisor $D \subset X$ with $U = X \setminus D$.

For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme
equidimensional of dimension $1$ whose singularities are at-worst-nodal.
Then $X$ is Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

formulation.statement:
An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme with ideal locally generated by one nonzerodivisor. A relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ is such a divisor $D\subset X$ with $D\to S$ flat; this does not assume $X\to S$ flat. Sums are defined by products of ideal sheaves. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor, and
\item $D \to S$ is a flat morphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then for every morphism of schemes $g : S' \to S$ the pullback
$(g')^{-1}D$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X' = S' \times_S X$
where $g' : X' \to X$ is the projection.

source.label: lemma-relative-Cartier
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-Cartier}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor, and
\item $D \to S$ is a flat morphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then for every morphism of schemes $g : S' \to S$ the pullback
$(g')^{-1}D$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X' = S' \times_S X$
where $g' : X' \to X$ is the projection.

formulation.statement:
For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$f^{-1}L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} = L_{f^{-1}\mathcal{B}/f^{-1}\mathcal{A}}$.

\label{lemma-pullback-cotangent-morphism-topoi}
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$f^{-1}L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} = L_{f^{-1}\mathcal{B}/f^{-1}\mathcal{A}}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-through-quasi-isomorphism}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Given a solid diagram of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{E}^\bullet \ar@{..>}[dr] \ar[r]_\alpha & \mathcal{F}^\bullet \\
& \mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[u]_f
}
$$
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect, $\mathcal{E}^j = 0$ for
$j < a$ and $H^j(f)$ an isomorphism for $j > a$ and surjective for $j = a$,
then a dotted arrow making the diagram commute up to homotopy
exists locally on $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is a finite dimensional $k$-algebra,
\item $A = \prod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} A_i$ is a product of Artinian
local $k$-algebras, one factor for each connected component of $X$,
\item if $X$ is reduced, then $A = \prod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} k_i$
is a product of fields, each a finite extension of $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically reduced, then $k_i$ is finite separable
over $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically connected, then $A$ is geometrically
irreducible over $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically irreducible, then $A$ is geometrically
irreducible over $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected, then
$A = k$, and
\item if $X$ is geometrically integral, then $A = k$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
x \ar[r]^f \ar[d]^\alpha &

sequence $\Ker(\alpha) \to \Ker(\beta) \to \Ker(\gamma)$ 
is exact.
\item If the second row is exact and $g$ is an epimorphism, then the induced 
sequence
$\Coker(\alpha) \to \Coker(\beta) \to \Coker(\gamma)$ 
is exact.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibred-groupoids-fibre-product-goes-up}
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category fibred in groupoids.
Let $x \to y$ and $z \to y$ be morphisms of $\mathcal{S}$.
If $p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$ exists, then
$x \times_y z$ exists and $p(x \times_y z) = p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$.

conclusions: Scalar extension of ω_A is dualizing over A[x].
hypotheses: A Noetherian, dualizing ω_A, B=A[x].
formulation.statement: For a Noetherian ring $A$, let $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full derived category of complexes with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. A *dualizing complex* $\omega_A^\bullet\in D(A)$ means a bounded complex with finite injective dimension and finitely generated cohomology such that the homothety map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. The functor $\mathbb D_A(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is contravariant. If $\omega_A^\bullet$ is dualizing, then the flat scalar extension $\omega_A^\bullet\otimes_A A[x]$ is a dualizing complex over the polynomial ring $A[x]$. No cohomological shift is needed merely to obtain *a* dualizing complex; normalization in a local sense is a separate question.

phase2.semantic_review_note: If ω_A is dualizing over Noetherian A, then flat extension ω_A⊗_A A[x] is dualizing for A[x]. The proposal preserves the unnormalized claim and introduces no spurious shift.

phase3.reason: Finite injective dimension and coherent cohomology survive flat polynomial extension, while the canonical dualizing evaluation isomorphism follows from the cited flat base-change formula for derived Hom.

source.label: lemma-explain-why-pure
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-explain-why-pure}
Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $N$ be an $S$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N$ is projective as an $R$-module, and
\item $S/\mathfrak mS$ is Noetherian and $N/\mathfrak mN$ is a finite
$S/\mathfrak mS$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Then for any prime $\mathfrak q \subset S$ which is an associated prime of
$N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ where $\mathfrak p = R \cap \mathfrak q$
we have $\mathfrak q + \mathfrak m S \not = S$.

\label{lemma-compare-cohomology-point}
Notation and assumptions as in
Lemma \ref{lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point}.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\Spec(K)_\etale$
which corresponds to the $G$-module $M$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item in $D(\textit{Ab})$ we have a canonical isomorphism
$R\Gamma(S, \mathcal{F}) = R\Gamma_G(M)$,
\item $H_\etale^0(S, \mathcal{F}) = M^G$, and
\item $H_\etale^q(S, \mathcal{F}) = H^q(G, M)$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Let $f:X\to S$ be of finite type, and $D_X$ normalized relative to $D_S$. For every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, one has
\[
\delta_X(x)-\delta_S(s)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x).
\]
Here $\delta_X,\delta_S$ are normalized dualizing dimension functions, and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is the induced residue-field extension.

The proposal defines the associated dualizing dimension functions and preserves the sign, residue-field base and universal x scope.

source.label: lemma-good-dualizing-dimension-function
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-dualizing-dimension-function}
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $\omega_S^\bullet$ be a
dualizing complex. Let $f : X \to S$ be of finite type
and let $\omega_X^\bullet$ be the dualizing complex
normalized relative to $\omega_S^\bullet$. For all $x \in X$ we have
$$
\delta_X(x) - \delta_S(f(x)) = \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}(\kappa(x))
$$
where $\delta_S$, resp.\ $\delta_X$
is the dimension function of
$\omega_S^\bullet$, resp.\ $\omega_X^\bullet$, see
Lemma \ref{lemma-dimension-function-scheme}.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ and $q : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
If $p$ and $q$ are limit preserving on objects, then so is the composition
$q \circ p$.

\label{lemma-cech-vanish-collection}
(Variant of Cohomology, Lemma \ref{cohomology-lemma-cech-vanish}.)
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$ be the set
of coverings of $\mathcal{C}$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-site}). Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$,
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ we have
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$ and any $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed on a site. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_r$
be global sections of $\mathcal{O}$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$ be
the ideal sheaf generated by $f_1, \ldots, f_r$.
Then the inclusion functor $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O}) \to D(\mathcal{O})$
has a left adjoint, i.e., given any object $K$ of $D(\mathcal{O})$
there exists a map $K \to K^\wedge$ with $K^\wedge$ in $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O})$
such that the map
$$
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K^\wedge, E) \longrightarrow \Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K, E)
$$
is bijective whenever $E$ is in $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O})$. In fact
we have
$$
K^\wedge =
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}
(\mathcal{O} \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} \mathcal{O}_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} \mathcal{O}_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to
\ldots \to \mathcal{O}_{f_1\ldots f_r}, K)
$$
functorially in $K$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-derived-completion}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed on a site. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_r$
be global sections of $\mathcal{O}$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$ be
the ideal sheaf generated by $f_1, \ldots, f_r$.
Then the inclusion functor $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O}) \to D(\mathcal{O})$
has a left adjoint, i.e., given any object $K$ of $D(\mathcal{O})$
there exists a map $K \to K^\wedge$ with $K^\wedge$ in $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O})$
such that the map
$$
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K^\wedge, E) \longrightarrow \Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K, E)
$$
is bijective whenever $E$ is in $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O})$. In fact
we have
$$
K^\wedge =
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}
(\mathcal{O} \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} \mathcal{O}_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} \mathcal{O}_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to
\ldots \to \mathcal{O}_{f_1\ldots f_r}, K)
$$
functorially in $K$.

\label{lemma-proetale-affine}
Let $T$ be an affine scheme. Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be a pro-\'etale
covering of $T$. Then there exists a pro-\'etale covering
$\{U_j \to T\}_{j = 1, \ldots, n}$ which is a refinement
of $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ such that each $U_j$ is an affine
scheme. Moreover, we may choose each $U_j$ to be open affine
in one of the $T_i$.

\label{lemma-section-closed}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $s : Y \to X$ be a continuous map such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_Y$.
If $X$ is Hausdorff, then $s(Y)$ is closed.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $1$.
Let $L = \prod A_\mathfrak p$ where the product is over

which map to the same element of $L$ such that $\mathfrak m_A = \sqrt{(a)}$.

\label{lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Assume that $R$ has finitely many minimal primes
$\mathfrak q_1, \ldots, \mathfrak q_t$, and that
$\mathfrak q_1 \cup \ldots \cup \mathfrak q_t$ is the set
of zerodivisors of $R$.
Then the total ring of fractions $Q(R)$ is equal to
$R_{\mathfrak q_1} \times \ldots \times R_{\mathfrak q_t}$.

Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
In each of the following cases pullbacks of meromorphic
functions are defined.
\begin{enumerate}
\item every weakly associated point of $X$ maps to
a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral and $f$ is dominant,
\item $X$ is integral and the generic point of $X$ maps
to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$ is reduced and every generic point of every irreducible
component of $X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component
of $Y$,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian, and any associated point of
$X$ maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian, has no embedded points and
any generic point of an irreducible component of
$X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, and
\item $f$ is flat.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-pullback-meromorphic-sections-defined}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
In each of the following cases pullbacks of meromorphic
functions are defined.
\begin{enumerate}
\item every weakly associated point of $X$ maps to
a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral and $f$ is dominant,
\item $X$ is integral and the generic point of $X$ maps
to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$ is reduced and every generic point of every irreducible
component of $X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component
of $Y$,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian, and any associated point of
$X$ maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian, has no embedded points and
any generic point of an irreducible component of
$X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, and
\item $f$ is flat.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-property-initial}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of coherent sheaves on $X$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any short exact sequence of coherent sheaves
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to 0
$$
if $\mathcal{F}_i$, $i = 1, 2$ have property $\mathcal{P}$
then so does $\mathcal{F}$.
\item For every integral closed subscheme $Z \subset X$
and every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_Z$ we have
$\mathcal{P}$ for $i_*\mathcal{I}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for every coherent sheaf
on $X$.

A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth curves over $k$, the following are equivalent: the function-field extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable, the map of invertible differential sheaves $df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$ is generically nonzero, and $f$ is étale on a dense open subscheme of $X$. Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

For an extension of discrete valuation rings $A\subset B$ with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$, the ramification index $e(B/A)$ is defined by $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B^e$. For a finite extension of fields $L/k$, the inseparable degree $[L:k]_i$ is $[L:k]/[L:k]_s$.\n\nLet $X$ be a smooth curve over a field $k$. Let
$\overline{x} \in X_{\overline{k}}$ be a closed
point with image $x \in X$. The ramification index of
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \subset \mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{k}}, \overline{x}}$
is the inseparable degree of $\kappa(x)/k$.

phase3.reason: Reduces by an étale local coordinate to affine line, where a closed point has irreducible polynomial P(t)=Q(t^q), with Q separable and inseparable degree q; over an algebraic closure P has roots of multiplicity q, giving ramification index q.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ramification-to-algebraic-closure}
Let $X$ be a smooth curve over a field $k$. Let
$\overline{x} \in X_{\overline{k}}$ be a closed
point with image $x \in X$. The ramification index of
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \subset \mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{k}}, \overline{x}}$
is the inseparable degree of $\kappa(x)/k$.

\label{lemma-support-in-subset}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E \subset X$ be a subset closed
under specialization.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$
whose support is contained in $E$. Then $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$
is a filtered colimit of constructible abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}_i$
such that for each $i$ the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained in
a closed subset contained in $E$.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathcal{F}$ a sheaf
of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$ whose support is contained in $E$.
Then $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$
is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained in a closed subset
contained in $E$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colimit-cohomology}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$ be a filtered colimit
of abelian sheaves on $X$. Then for any $p \geq 0$ we have
$$
R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i.
$$

\begin{reference}
Variant of \cite[Lemma 2.15]{Orlov-K3}
\end{reference}
Let $F : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}'$ be an exact functor of
triangulated categories. Let $S \subset \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ be
a set of objects. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ has both right and left adjoints,
\item for $K \in \mathcal{D}$ if $\Hom(E, K[i]) = 0$ for all
$E \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K = 0$,
\item for $K \in \mathcal{D}$ if $\Hom(K, E[i]) = 0$ for all
$E \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K = 0$,
\item the map $\Hom(E, E'[i]) \to \Hom(F(E), F(E')[i])$ induced by $F$
is bijective for all $E, E' \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is fully faithful.
S is a set of left- and right-spanning objects: vanishing of all shifted Hom from S and to S separately detects zero. Both adjoints to F are assumed, and the Hom comparison for all E,E' in S and all shifts is bijective.
hypotheses: Over a field $k$, let $\mathcal O_x=i_{x*}\kappa(x)$ denote the skyscraper sheaf at a **closed point** $x$ of a $k$-scheme. For a regular scheme, such skyscrapers are perfect. The derived dual of a perfect object is $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,\mathcal O_X)$, and $\operatorname{Ext}_X^i(E,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,F[i])$. A sheaf has *zero-dimensional support* if its support consists of finitely many closed points.

Over a field $k$, let $\mathcal O_x=i_{x*}\kappa(x)$ denote the skyscraper sheaf at a **closed point** $x$ of a $k$-scheme. For a regular scheme, such skyscrapers are perfect. The derived dual of a perfect object is $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,\mathcal O_X)$, and $\operatorname{Ext}_X^i(E,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,F[i])$. A sheaf has *zero-dimensional support* if its support consists of finitely many closed points.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension
$\leq 1$ over $k$. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a finite morphism
such that there exists a dense open $U \subset X$ over
which $f$ is a closed immersion. Then
$$
\dim_k H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \geq \dim_k H^1(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)
$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: For finite Y→X that is a closed immersion over a dense open of proper one-dimensional X, h¹(O_X)≥h¹(O_Y). The proposal retains the dense-open closed-immersion condition, not merely finiteness.

phase3.reason: The kernel/cokernel sequence O_X→f_*O_Y has zero-dimensional cokernel with H^1=0, and the kernel has H^2=0 on dimension-one X. The cohomology sequence forces H^1(O_X)→H^1(f_*O_Y) surjective, with finite-map cohomology identifying the latter as H^1(O_Y).

Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.

Let $X$ be a scheme proper over a field $k$. Let
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and let $E$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be perfect. Then
$\sum_{i \in \mathbf{Z}} \dim_k \Ext^i_X(E, K) < \infty$.

**Scope and interpretation:** The conclusion is finiteness of the **total sum** of dimensions over all Ext degrees, not merely pointwise finite-dimensionality.

\label{lemma-finiteness}
Let $X$ be a scheme proper over a field $k$. Let
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and let $E$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be perfect. Then
$\sum_{i \in \mathbf{Z}} \dim_k \Ext^i_X(E, K) < \infty$.

\label{lemma-base-change-fibres-nr-geometrically-irreducible-components}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let
$$
n_{X/Y} : Y \to \{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, \infty\}
$$
be the function which associates to $y \in Y$ the number of irreducible
components of $(X_y)_K$ where $K$ is a separably closed extension
of $\kappa(y)$. This is well defined and if $g : Y' \to Y$ is a morphism
then
$$
n_{X'/Y'} = n_{X/Y} \circ g
$$
where $X' \to Y'$ is the base change of $f$.

\label{lemma-preserve-injective-maps}
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an index category, i.e., a category. Assume
that for every solid diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
x \ar[d] \ar[r] & y \ar@{..>}[d] \\
z \ar@{..>}[r] & w
}
$$
in $\mathcal{I}$ there exist an object $w$ and dotted arrows
making the diagram commute. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item an injective morphism $M \to N$ of diagrams of sets over
$\mathcal{I}$ gives rise to an injective map $\colim M_i \to \colim N_i$
of sets,
\item in general the same is not the case for diagrams of abelian
groups and their colimits.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions:
Then the map $E \to R\lim \tau_{\geq -n} E$ of
Derived Categories, Remark
\ref{derived-remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations}
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

phase3.reason: Specializes the preceding criterion to the local cohomological-dimension bound p(x,m)=d_x+max(0,m).

\label{theorem-chevalley}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation.
Then the image of every \'etale locally constructible subset of $|X|$ is
an \'etale locally constructible subset of $|Y|$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-with-derived-completion}
Let $U$ be the punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring $A$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Then
$$
H^i(R\Gamma(U, \mathcal{F})^\wedge) =
\lim H^i(U, \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F})
$$
for all $i$ where $R\Gamma(U, \mathcal{F})^\wedge$ denotes
the derived $I$-adic completion.

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

Let $k'/k$ be a finite separable field extension.
Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k'$-scheme of dimension $1$.
Let $x \in X$ be a closed point. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is a node, and
\item $x$ is a node when $X$ viewed as a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: A finite separable extension k′/k preserves and reflects the nodal status of a closed point of a one-dimensional k′-scheme when viewed as a k-scheme. Both sides of the equivalence survive.

phase3.reason: The proof cites the preceding intrinsic characterization of nodes. A finite separable extension of the base field does not alter the separability and completed-local nodal criteria used there.

source.label: lemma-affine-diagonal
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-diagonal}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ has affine diagonal $\Delta : X \to X \times X$,
\item for $U, V \subset X$ affine open, the intersection
$U \cap V$ is affine, and
\item there exists an open covering $\mathcal{U} : X = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$
such that $U_{i_0 \ldots i_p}$ is affine open for all $p \ge 0$ and all
$i_0, \ldots, i_p \in I$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular this holds if $X$ is separated.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tricky}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $\overline{k}/k$ be a (possibly infinite)
Galois extension. Let $f : T \to X$ be a morphism of schemes over $k$.
Assume $T_{\overline{k}}$ connected and $X_{\overline{k}}$
disconnected. Then $X$ is disconnected.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-cohomology-and-restriction}
Let $A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism and let $I \subset A$
be a finitely generated ideal. Set $J = IB$. Set $Z = V(I)$
and $Y = V(J)$. Then
$$
R\Gamma_Z(M_A) = R\Gamma_Y(M)_A
$$
functorially in $M \in D(B)$. Here $(-)_A$ denotes the restriction
functors $D(B) \to D(A)$ and
$D_{J^\infty\text{-torsion}}(B) \to D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A)$.

formulation.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The selected covers Cov form a **finite cofinal system** for every U∈B, with all finite iterated fibre products remaining in B; this condition, not mere quasi-compactness of U, is the source hypothesis.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site
with set of coverings $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ with $I$ finite,
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the object $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$ is
a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$ in the following sense:
if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M) =
\bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M_i)$.

\label{lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant}
Let $X$ be a connected scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $K \in D_{ctf}(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ have locally constant cohomology sheaves.
Then there exists a finite complex of finite projective $\Lambda$-modules
$M^\bullet$ and an \'etale covering $\{U_i \to X\}$ such that
$K|_{U_i} \cong \underline{M^\bullet}|_{U_i}$ in $D(U_{i, \etale}, \Lambda)$.

\label{lemma-characterize-right-exact}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
Suppose all finite colimits exist in $\mathcal{A}$,
see Lemma \ref{lemma-colimits-exist}.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is right exact,
\item $F$ commutes with finite coproducts and coequalizers, and
\item $F$ transforms an initial object of $\mathcal{A}$
into an initial object of $\mathcal{B}$, and commutes with pushouts.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Write $S = \Spec(A)$ and $S_n = \Spec(A/I^n)$.
Let $X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type.
For $n \geq 1$ we set $X_n = X \times_S S_n$.
Suppose given a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Y_1 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Y_2 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Y_3 \ar[r] \ar[d] & \ldots \\
X_1 \ar[r]^{i_1} & X_2 \ar[r]^{i_2} & X_3 \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
of schemes with cartesian squares. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y_n \to X_n$ is a finite morphism, and
\item $Y_1 \to S_1$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a finite morphism of schemes $Y \to X$ such that
$Y_n = Y \times_S S_n$. Moreover, $Y$ is proper over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-has-dualizing-module-CM-scheme}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. If there exists a coherent sheaf
$\omega_X$ such that $\omega_X[0]$ is a dualizing complex on $X$, then
$X$ is a Cohen-Macaulay scheme.

with fibre products and equalizers.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-put-in-T-etale}
Let $\Sch_\etale$ be a big \'etale site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_\etale$.
The functor $T_\etale \to (\Sch/S)_\etale$
is cocontinuous and induces a morphism of topoi
$$
i_f :
\Sh(T_\etale)
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_\etale)
$$
For a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $(\Sch/S)_\etale$
we have the formula $(i_f^{-1}\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
The functor $i_f^{-1}$ also has a left adjoint $i_{f, !}$ which commutes
with fibre products and equalizers.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-semi-local-dimension-one-conductor}
Let $B$ be a semi-local Noetherian domain of dimension $1$.
Let $B'$ be the integral closure of $B$ in its fraction field.
Then $B'$ is a semi-local Dedekind domain.
Let $x$ be a nonzero element of the Jacobson radical of $B'$.
Then for every $y \in B'$ there exists an $n$ such that
$x^n y \in B$.

formulation.statement:
A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$(M, \varphi, \psi)$ be a $(2, 1)$-periodic complex over $R$
with $M$ finite and with cohomology groups of finite length over $R$.
Let $x \in R$ be such that $\dim(\text{Supp}(M/xM)) \leq 0$. Then
$$
e_R(M, x\varphi, \psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) - e_R(\Im(\varphi), 0, x)
$$
and
$$
e_R(M, \varphi, x\psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) + e_R(\Im(\psi), 0, x)
$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: The Chow multiplicity transformation lemma at 463–477 assumes Noetherian local R, finite M, (2,1)-periodic complex with finite-length cohomology, and dim Supp(M/xM)≤0. It gives TWO distinct equalities: scaling φ by x SUBTRACTS e_R(Im φ,0,x), while scaling ψ by x ADDS e_R(Im ψ,0,x). The reviewed split faithfully retains both signs and image modules.

phase3.reason: Removes x-power torsion by additivity and computes the multiplicity difference from the stated exact sequence when x is injective; the second formula is analogous.

source.label: lemma-multiply-period-length
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-multiply-period-length}
Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$(M, \varphi, \psi)$ be a $(2, 1)$-periodic complex over $R$
with $M$ finite and with cohomology groups of finite length over $R$.
Let $x \in R$ be such that $\dim(\text{Supp}(M/xM)) \leq 0$. Then
$$
e_R(M, x\varphi, \psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) - e_R(\Im(\varphi), 0, x)
$$
and
$$
e_R(M, \varphi, x\psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) + e_R(\Im(\psi), 0, x)
$$

\label{lemma-representable-by-algebraic-spaces}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Y$ be a formal algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a map of sheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which is
representable by algebraic spaces. Then $X$ is a formal
algebraic space.

\label{lemma-flat-proper-family-cannot-collapse-fibre}
Consider a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rr]_h \ar[rd]_f & & Y \ar[ld]^g \\
& S
}
$$
Let $s \in S$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to S$ is a proper morphism,
\item $Y \to S$ is separated and locally of finite type, and
\item the image of $X_s \to Y_s$ is finite.
\end{enumerate}
Then there is an open
subspace $U \subset S$ containing $s$ such that $X_U \to Y_U$
factors through a closed subscheme $Z \subset Y_U$ finite over $U$.
