source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-describe-etale-local-ring}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\overline{x}$ be a geometric point of $X$.
Let $(U, \overline{u})$ be an \'etale neighbourhood of $\overline{x}$
where $U$ is a scheme. Then we have
$$
\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}} =
\mathcal{O}_{U, \overline{u}} =
\mathcal{O}_{U, u}^{sh}
$$
where the left hand side is the stalk of the structure sheaf of $X$,
and the right hand side is the strict henselization of the local ring
of $U$ at the point $u$ at which $\overline{u}$ is centered.

formulation.statement:
Pinned-source scope: work over a fixed big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Categories fibred in groupoids over this site are considered up to equivalence of fibred categories. A stack in setoids is a stack in groupoids whose fibre-groupoid objects have no nontrivial automorphisms. The inertia stack $\mathcal I_\mathcal X$ has over $T$ pairs $(x,\gamma)$ with $x\in\mathcal X_T$ and $\gamma\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$; $\mathcal I_\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ forgets $\gamma$. A Deligne--Mumford stack is an algebraic stack admitting a surjective étale atlas by a scheme; an algebraic stack admits a surjective smooth atlas by a scheme. A morphism is representable by algebraic spaces when its 2-base change against every map from a scheme is equivalent to the stack associated with an algebraic space.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is a stack in setoids,
\item the canonical $1$-morphism $\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$
is an equivalence, and
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is representable by an algebraic space.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: The source does not require a DM hypothesis for this separate characterization: an algebraic stack is representable by an algebraic space exactly when it is a stack in setoids or has trivial inertia. The proposal retains the three equivalent alternatives without inserting DM.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kill-by-twisting}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is Noetherian,
\item $f$ is proper,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is coherent, and
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is relatively ample on $X/S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an $n_0$ such that for all $n \geq n_0$
we have
$$
R^pf_*\left(\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}\right)
=
0
$$
for all $p > 0$.

Let $X$ be a scheme. Let
$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$.
Let $\mathcal{C}_1 \subset \mathcal{C}_2 \subset (\Sch/X)_\tau$ be full
subcategories with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For an object $U/X$ of $\mathcal{C}_t$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $\{U_i \to U\}$ is a covering of $(\Sch/X)_\tau$, then
$U_i/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$,
\item $U \times \mathbf{A}^1/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$.
\end{enumerate}
\item $X/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$.
\end{enumerate}
We endow $\mathcal{C}_t$ with the structure of a site whose coverings are
exactly those coverings $\{U_i \to U\}$ of $(\Sch/X)_\tau$ with
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C}_t)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] The functor $\mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_2$
is fully faithful, continuous, and cocontinuous.
\end{enumerate}
Denote $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}_1) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C}_2)$ the corresponding
morphism of topoi. Denote $\mathcal{O}_t$ the restriction of $\mathcal{O}$
to $\mathcal{C}_t$. Denote $g_!$ the functor of
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-g-shriek}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(b)] The canonical map $g_!\mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
The sites are **full subcategories** of the selected big-$\tau$ site, closed under base-site covering members and $U\times_X\mathbf A^1_X$, containing $X/X$. The left adjoint $g_!$ here is the **module lower-shriek** functor from the included site, and the comparison is specifically $g_!\mathcal O_1\simeq\mathcal O_2$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spell-out-representable-map-stack-in-groupoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ be categories fibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism.
If $F$ is representable then every one of the functors
$$
F_U : \mathcal{X}_U \longrightarrow \mathcal{Y}_U
$$
between fibre categories is faithful.

The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

\label{lemma-section-smooth}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $p : P \to X$ be a smooth morphism of schemes locally of finite type
over $S$ and let $s : X \to P$ be a section. Then $s$ is a
regular immersion and $1 = s^! \circ p^*$ in $A^*(X)^\wedge$
where $p^* \in A^*(P \to X)^\wedge$ is the bivariant class
of Lemma \ref{lemma-flat-pullback-bivariant}.

\label{lemma-compactifyable}
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$
be a morphism of schemes over $S$ with $Y$ separated and of finite type
over $S$ and $X$ compactifyable over $S$. Then $X$ has a compactification
over $Y$.

source.label: lemma-finite-type-flat-along-fibre
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-along-fibre}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at every point of the fibre $X_s$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an elementary \'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
and an open subscheme
$$
V \subset X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})
$$
which contains the fibre $X_s = X \times_S s'$ such that the pullback
of $\mathcal{F}$ to $V$ is an $\mathcal{O}_V$-module
of finite presentation and flat over $\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$.

$$

$$
is open in $X$. The map $s : \mathcal{O}_{X_s} \to \mathcal{L}|_{X_s}$
is an isomorphism, and there exists a section $s'$
of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes -1}$ over $X_s$ such that $s' (s|_{X_s}) = 1$.

source.label: lemma-s-open
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-s-open}
\begin{slogan}
A (local) trivialisation of a linebundle
is the same as a (local) nonvanishing section.
\end{slogan}
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Assume that each stalk $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
For any section $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$ the set
$$
X_s = \{x \in X \mid \text{image }s \not\in \mathfrak m_x\mathcal{L}_x\}
$$
is open in $X$. The map $s : \mathcal{O}_{X_s} \to \mathcal{L}|_{X_s}$
is an isomorphism, and there exists a section $s'$
of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes -1}$ over $X_s$ such that $s' (s|_{X_s}) = 1$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be continuous maps
of topological spaces. The functors $(g \circ f)^{-1}$

presheaves.

source.label: lemma-pullback-composition
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-composition}
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be continuous maps
of topological spaces. The functors $(g \circ f)^{-1}$
and $f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}$ are canonically isomorphic.
Similarly $(g \circ f)_p \cong f_p \circ g_p$ on
presheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exactness}
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$ be
a morphism of topoi. Assume at least one of the following properties
holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_*$ transforms surjections of sheaves of sets into surjections,
\item $f_*$ transforms surjections of abelian sheaves into surjections,
\item $f_*$ commutes with coequalizers on sheaves of sets,
\item $f_*$ commutes with pushouts on sheaves of sets,
\end{enumerate}
Then $f_* : \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{D})$
is exact.

source.label: lemma-locally-quasi-finite-characterize
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-quasi-finite-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is locally quasi-finite.
\item For every pair of affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is quasi-finite.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is locally quasi-finite.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
quasi-finite, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is locally quasi-finite then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally quasi-finite.

\label{lemma-pre-equivalence-equivalence-relation-points}
Let $j : R \to U \times_S U$ be a pre-relation.
Consider the relation on points of the scheme $U$ defined by
the rule
$$
x \sim y
\Leftrightarrow
\exists\ r \in R :
t(r) = x,
s(r) = y.
$$
If $j$ is a pre-equivalence relation then this is an
equivalence relation.

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
schemes over $k$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is separated over $k$,
\item $X$ is proper of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$,
\item $f(Z)$ has at least two points for every irreducible
component $Z \subset X$ of dimension $1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is finite.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The finiteness criterion requires Y separated, X proper of dimension ≤1, and every one-dimensional component to have image containing at least two points. The draft keeps all three premises and concludes f finite.

phase3.reason: Establishes properness and finite fibres over closed images, then applies the local finite-neighbourhood theorem to cover the target.

On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$ of a scheme $X$, a *constant sheaf* $\underline E$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value a set $E$ (similarly an abelian group or $\Lambda$-module). A sheaf $\mathcal F$ is *locally constant* if there is an étale cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ on which it becomes isomorphic to a constant sheaf; it is *finite locally constant* for set-valued sheaves if its constant fibre sets are finite, and *finite type locally constant* for $\Lambda$-modules if its local fibre modules are finitely generated. For an étale map $U\to X$, its representable sheaf is $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$. In an abelian category a *weak Serre subcategory* is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions (without necessarily all subobjects).

**Statement (source hypotheses preserved):**
Let $X$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of sets on $X_\etale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finite locally constant, there exists an
\'etale covering $\{U_i \to X\}$ such that
$\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of constant sheaves associated to
a map of sets.
\item Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of abelian groups on $X_\etale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finite locally constant, there exists an \'etale
covering $\{U_i \to X\}$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of
constant abelian sheaves associated to a map of abelian groups.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, then there exists an \'etale covering
$\{U_i \to X\}$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of constant
sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules associated to a map of $\Lambda$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

**Typed interpretation:** The set/abelian sheaf hypothesis asks *finite* locally constant **domain**, whereas the module version requires only *finite type*, with codomain locally constant. The conclusion is **local constant-coordinate description of the map**, not global.

\label{lemma-morphism-locally-constant}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of sets on $X_\etale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finite locally constant, there exists an
\'etale covering $\{U_i \to X\}$ such that
$\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of constant sheaves associated to
a map of sets.
\item Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of abelian groups on $X_\etale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finite locally constant, there exists an \'etale
covering $\{U_i \to X\}$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of
constant abelian sheaves associated to a map of abelian groups.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, then there exists an \'etale covering
$\{U_i \to X\}$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of constant
sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules associated to a map of $\Lambda$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

$$
\delta\text{-invariant of }A \geq \text{number of geometric branches of }A - 1

For a reduced Nagata local ring $A$ of dimension1, $\delta(A)=\operatorname{length}_A(A^\nu/A)$, where $A^\nu$ is its integral closure in its total ring of fractions.
Branch number is the number of minimal primes of the henselization of the local ring; geometric branch number uses its strict henselization (infinity if not finite). Geometrically unibranch means one geometric branch.

Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a $1$-dimensional reduced Nagata local ring. Then
$$
\delta\text{-invariant of }A \geq \text{number of geometric branches of }A - 1
$$

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

all $p > 0$.

\label{lemma-integral-closure-reflexive}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$.
Let $L$ be a finite extension of $K$. If the integral closure
$B$ of $A$ in $L$ is finite over $A$, then $B$ is reflexive as an $A$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-criterion-map-representable-spaces-fibred-in-groupoids}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism
of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are necessary and sufficient conditions for
$f$ to be representable by algebraic spaces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each scheme $U/S$ the
functor $f_U : \mathcal{X}_U \longrightarrow \mathcal{Y}_U$
between fibre categories is faithful, and
\item for each $U$ and each $y \in \Ob(\mathcal{Y}_U)$ the presheaf
$$
(h : V \to U)
\longmapsto
\{(x, \phi) \mid x \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_V), \phi : h^*y \to f(x)\}/\cong
$$
is an algebraic space over $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Here we have made a choice of pullbacks for $\mathcal{Y}$.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1

Let $p \geq 0$. Assume
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} H^{p + 1}(X, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})

satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded

Mittag-Leffler condition\footnote{In fact, there exists

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ML-general}
Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules on $X$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Assume
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} H^{p + 1}(X, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
$$
satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module.
Then the inverse system $M_n = H^p(X, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image
for all $n \geq c$.}.

\label{lemma-coherent-finite-presentation}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.

and hence quasi-coherent.

formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s$ be a regular meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
Let us denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ the
sheaf of ideals defined by the rule
$$
\mathcal{I}(V)
=
\{f \in \mathcal{O}_X(V) \mid fs \in \mathcal{L}(V)\}.
$$
The formula makes sense since
$\mathcal{L}(V) \subset \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})(V)$.
Then $\mathcal{I}$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and
we have injective maps
$$
1 : \mathcal{I} \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_X,
\quad
s : \mathcal{I} \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}
$$
whose cokernels are supported on closed nowhere dense subsets of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular-meromorphic-ideal-denominators}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s$ be a regular meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
Let us denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ the
sheaf of ideals defined by the rule
$$
\mathcal{I}(V)
=
\{f \in \mathcal{O}_X(V) \mid fs \in \mathcal{L}(V)\}.
$$
The formula makes sense since
$\mathcal{L}(V) \subset \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})(V)$.
Then $\mathcal{I}$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and
we have injective maps
$$
1 : \mathcal{I} \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_X,
\quad
s : \mathcal{I} \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}
$$
whose cokernels are supported on closed nowhere dense subsets of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-after-blowing-up}
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $U \subset S$ be a quasi-compact open.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to S$ is proper, and
\item $X_U \to U$ is finite locally free.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $S' \to S$ such that
the strict transform of $X$ is finite locally free over $S'$.

\label{lemma-galois-action-connected-components}
Let $k$ be a field, with separable algebraic closure $\overline{k}$.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
There is an action
$$
\text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)^{opp} \times \pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})
\longrightarrow
\pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})
$$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item An element $\overline{T} \in \pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})$
is fixed by the action if and only if there exists a connected component
$T \subset X$, which is geometrically connected over $k$,
such that $T_{\overline{k}} = \overline{T}$.
\item For any field extension $k'/k$ with separable
algebraic closure $\overline{k}'$ the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\text{Gal}(\overline{k}'/k') \times \pi_0(X_{\overline{k}'})
\ar[r] \ar[d] &
\pi_0(X_{\overline{k}'}) \ar[d] \\
\text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k) \times \pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})
\ar[r] &
\pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})
}
$$
is commutative (where the right vertical arrow is a bijection
according to Lemma \ref{lemma-separably-closed-field-connected-components}).
\end{enumerate}

conclusions:
The scheme $\Spec(\mathbf{Z})$ is not quasi-compact
in the canonical topology on the category of schemes.

phase3.reason: The constructed canonical-topology cover of Spec Z is a universal effective epimorphism. No finite subfamily admits an effective epimorphic refinement because each factors through Spec Z[1/p], so Spec Z is not quasi-compact in this site.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extension}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$ and
let $k$ be an integer $\geq 0$. Consider the
simplicial object $E$ defined by the following rules
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E_n = \bigoplus_\alpha A$, where the
sum is over $\alpha : [n] \to [k + 1]$ whose
image is either $[k]$ or $[k + 1]$.
\item Given $\varphi : [m] \to [n]$ the map
$E_n \to E_m$ maps the summand corresponding
to $\alpha$ via $\text{id}_A$ to the summand
corresponding to $\alpha \circ \varphi$,
provided $\Im(\alpha \circ \varphi)$
is equal to $[k]$ or $[k + 1]$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to K(A, k) \to E \to K(A, k + 1) \to 0
$$
which is term by term split exact.

be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf

\mathcal{F}(U)

is an isomorphism.

source.label: lemma-chaotic-quasi-coherent
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chaotic-quasi-coherent}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category viewed as a site with the chaotic
topology, see Sites, Example \ref{sites-example-indiscrete}. Let $\mathcal{O}$
be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf
of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent if
and only if for all $U \to V$ in $\mathcal{C}$ the canonical map
$$
\mathcal{F}(V) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}(V)} \mathcal{O}(U)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{F}(U)
$$
is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-first-quadrant-ss}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $K^{\bullet, \bullet}$
be a double complex. Assume that for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ there are
only finitely many nonzero $K^{p, q}$ with $p + q = n$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the two spectral sequences associated to $K^{\bullet, \bullet}$
are bounded,
\item the filtrations $F_I$, $F_{II}$ on each
$H^n(\text{Tot}(K^{\bullet, \bullet}))$ are finite,
\item the spectral sequences $({}'E_r, {}'d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ and
$({}''E_r, {}''d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ converge to
$H^*(\text{Tot}(K^{\bullet, \bullet}))$,
\item if $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ is a weak Serre subcategory
and for some $r$ we have ${}'E_r^{p, q} \in \mathcal{C}$ for all
$p, q \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $H^n(\text{Tot}(K^{\bullet, \bullet}))$
is in $\mathcal{C}$. Similarly for $({}''E_r, {}''d_r)_{r \geq 0}$.
\end{enumerate}

Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $T$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$, and
\item $S = \Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(T, B)$
represents $R\Hom(T, B)$ in $D(A, \text{d})$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $S$ has a structure of a differential graded $(B, A)$-bimodule
and there is an isomorphism
$$
N \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} S \longrightarrow R\Hom(T, N)
$$
functorial in $N$ in $D(B, \text{d})$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The bimodule T must be compact in D(B) and its actual dg Hom_B(T,B)=S must represent RHom(T,B). The result is a (B,A)-bimodule structure on S and a natural derived tensor-to-RHom isomorphism N⊗_B^L S→RHom(T,N), preserving all claims and algebra order.

phase3.reason: The composition pairing constructs the dg (B,A)-bimodule S=Hom_B(T,B) and natural evaluation c_N:N⊗_B S→Hom_B(T,N). Property-(P) and property-(I) replacements make this a natural derived transformation. Exactness and compactness reduce the isomorphism test to N=B[k], where the assumed computation of RHom(T,B) applies.

source.label: lemma-RHom-is-tensor
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-RHom-is-tensor}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $T$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$, and
\item $S = \Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(T, B)$
represents $R\Hom(T, B)$ in $D(A, \text{d})$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $S$ has a structure of a differential graded $(B, A)$-bimodule
and there is an isomorphism
$$
N \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} S \longrightarrow R\Hom(T, N)
$$
functorial in $N$ in $D(B, \text{d})$.

For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.
formulation.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

stacks in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If

\item $\mathcal{U}$ is representable by an algebraic space, and
\item $u$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation,
\end{enumerate}
then

\label{lemma-flat-finite-presentation-surjective-diagonal}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $u : \mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ be a $1$-morphism of
stacks in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{U}$ is representable by an algebraic space, and
\item $u$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation,
\end{enumerate}
then
$\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
representable by algebraic spaces.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compose-homotopy}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $f, g : L \to M$ be homomorphisms of differential graded $A$-modules.
Suppose given further homomorphisms $a : K \to L$, and $c : M \to N$.
If $h : L \to M$ is an $A$-module map which defines a homotopy between
$f$ and $g$, then $c \circ h \circ a$ defines a homotopy between
$c \circ f \circ a$ and $c \circ g \circ a$.

\label{lemma-immersion-when-closed}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Then $|i| : |Z| \to |X|$ is a homeomorphism onto a
locally closed subset, and $i$ is a closed immersion if and only if
the image $|i|(|Z|) \subset |X|$ is a closed subset.

\label{lemma-ses-cech-h1}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset.
If there exists a cofinal system of open coverings $\mathcal{U}$
of $U$ such that $\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$,
then the map $\mathcal{G}(U) \to \mathcal{H}(U)$ is
surjective.

formulation.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Consider any cartesian square $X'=X\times_YY'$ with maps $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$. Suppose $f$ is flat and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ is such that $Lg^*E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. For each affine open $U'\subseteq X'$ whose images are contained in affine opens of $X,Y,Y'$, the two derived complexes $L(g')^*(f^!E)|_{U'}$ and $(f')^!(Lg^*E)|_{U'}$ are isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_{U'})$. This is an assertion of existence of local isomorphisms and does not claim they glue to a canonical global base-change transformation.

\label{lemma-base-change-locally}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\textit{FTS}_S$.
Let $E \in D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ be an object
such that $Lg^*E$ is in $D^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $f$ is flat, then $L(g')^*f^!E$ and $(f')^!Lg^*E$
restrict to isomorphic objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_{U'})$
for $U' \subset X'$ affine open mapping into affine opens of $Y$, $Y'$, and $X$.

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
If $G$ is a sheaf, then so is $F$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L110–115 states that if a:F→G is representable by algebraic spaces and G is an fppf sheaf, F is an fppf sheaf. The proposed implication preserves exactly the direction, site and premises.

phase3.reason: The proof establishes sheaf gluing and uniqueness by reducing to a representable fibre product, then descending local sections.

\label{lemma-representable-by-spaces-transformation-to-sheaf}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
If $G$ is a sheaf, then so is $F$.

formulation.statement:
For any map of sets \(f:A\to B\), let \(U\) be its Čech nerve, with \(U_n=A\times_B\cdots\times_B A\) (\(n+1\) copies), faces dropping and degeneracies repeating factors.
Let $A$, $B$ be sets, and that $f : A \to B$ is a map. Consider the simplicial
set $U$ with $n$-simplices
$$
A \times_B A \times_B \ldots \times_B A\ (n + 1 \text{ factors)}.
$$
with faces induced by projections and degeneracies by diagonals.
If $f$ is surjective, the morphism $U \to B$
where $B$ indicates the constant simplicial set with value $B$
is a trivial Kan fibration.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The source's Čech nerve of a surjective map A→B has n-simplices (n+1)-fold B-fiber products with face projections and degeneracy diagonals. Its map to constant B is a trivial Kan fibration; expansion in the proposal is equivalent.

phase3.reason: The proof identifies the Čech nerve with the base change of the 0-coskeleton of A→B; surjectivity makes that comparison a trivial Kan fibration, and base-change stability gives the claim.

\label{lemma-cosk-minus-one-equivalence}
Let $A$, $B$ be sets, and that $f : A \to B$ is a map. Consider the simplicial
set $U$ with $n$-simplices
$$
A \times_B A \times_B \ldots \times_B A\ (n + 1 \text{ factors)}.
$$
see Example \ref{example-fibre-products-simplicial-object}.
If $f$ is surjective, the morphism $U \to B$
where $B$ indicates the constant simplicial set with value $B$
is a trivial Kan fibration.

formulation.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Assume $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and the composite $p:X\to S$ is syntomic (flat, locally finitely presented, with local complete intersection fibres). Then both $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ are syntomic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flasque-acyclic}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Any flasque $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
is acyclic for $R\Gamma(X, -)$ as well as $R\Gamma(U, -)$ for any
open $U$ of $X$.

formulation.statement:
Suppose that $f: K^\bullet \to L^\bullet$ and $g : L^\bullet \to M^\bullet$
are morphisms of complexes such that $g \circ f$ is homotopic to zero.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g$ factors through a morphism $C(f)^\bullet \to M^\bullet$, and
\item $f$ factors through a morphism $K^\bullet \to C(g)^\bullet[-1]$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: With composable chain maps f and g whose composite is null-homotopic, both factorisations through the respective mapping cones are asserted. The statement keeps the null-homotopy condition and both separate outcomes, including the [-1] shift.

phase3.reason: The functorial cone lemma supplies maps to and from cones of a commutative square; shifting gives the required morphism.

formulation.statement:
A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$, an $A$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $J\subset B$ containing $IB$, the divided power envelope $D_{B,\gamma}(J)=(D,\bar J,\bar\gamma)$ is the universal divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra equipped with a ring map $B\to D$ carrying $J$ into $\bar J$: maps $D\to(C,K,\delta)$ of divided power $A$-algebras correspond naturally to $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ carrying $J$ into $K$. The canonical map $D\to B/J$ has kernel $\bar J$. For a divided power ring $(B,I,\gamma)$, $B\langle x_t\rangle$ denotes the divided power polynomial algebra, the free divided power $B$-algebra on elements $x_t$ of the divided power ideal $IB\langle x_t\rangle+B\langle x_t\rangle_+$, with $x_t^{[n]}=\gamma_n(x_t)$.

Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring.
Let $\varphi : B' \to B$ be a surjection of $A$-algebras with kernel $K$.
Let $IB \subset J \subset B$ be an ideal. Let $J' \subset B'$
be the inverse image of $J$. Write
$D_{B', \gamma}(J') = (D', \bar J', \bar\gamma)$.
Then $D_{B, \gamma}(J) = (D'/K', \bar J'/K', \bar\gamma)$
where $K'$ is the ideal generated by the elements $\bar\gamma_n(k)$
for $n \geq 1$ and $k \in K$.

phase3.reason: Uses universal properties of both divided-power envelopes to construct inverse maps after quotienting by the compatible divided-power ideal.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-divided-power-envelop-quotient}
Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring.
Let $\varphi : B' \to B$ be a surjection of $A$-algebras with kernel $K$.
Let $IB \subset J \subset B$ be an ideal. Let $J' \subset B'$
be the inverse image of $J$. Write
$D_{B', \gamma}(J') = (D', \bar J', \bar\gamma)$.
Then $D_{B, \gamma}(J) = (D'/K', \bar J'/K', \bar\gamma)$
where $K'$ is the ideal generated by the elements $\bar\gamma_n(k)$
for $n \geq 1$ and $k \in K$.

\label{lemma-closed}
Let $R$ be a topological ring. Let $M$ be a linearly topologized
$R$-module and let $M_\lambda$, $\lambda \in \Lambda$ be a fundamental
system of open submodules. Let $N \subset M$ be a submodule.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-generate-two-sided-ideal}
Let $A$ be a $k$-algebra. Let $K$ be a central $k$-algebra
which is a skew field. Then any two-sided ideal $I \subset A \otimes_k K$
is of the form $J \otimes_k K$ for some two-sided ideal $J \subset A$.
In particular, if $A$ is simple, then so is $A \otimes_k K$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-picard-stack-open-in-coh}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to B$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$ which is flat, of finite presentation, and proper.
The natural map
$$
\Picardstack_{X/B} \longrightarrow \Cohstack_{X/B}
$$
is representable by open immersions.

\label{lemma-when-point-maps-to-pair}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes over a base scheme $S$. Given points $x \in X$ and
$y \in Y$, there is a point of $X \times_S Y$ mapping to $x$ and $y$ under the
projections if and only if $x$ and $y$ lie above the same point of $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-numerical-intersection-effective-Cartier-divisor}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be proper over $k$. Let $Z \subset X$ be
a closed subscheme of dimension $d$. Let $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_d$
be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Assume there exists an
effective Cartier divisor $D \subset Z$ such that
$\mathcal{L}_1|_Z \cong \mathcal{O}_Z(D)$. Then
$$
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) =
(\mathcal{L}_2 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot D)
$$

A property $\mathcal P$ of morphisms of schemes is *$\tau$-local on the source* if for every $f:X\to Y$ and every $\tau$-covering $\{a_i:X_i\to X\}$ one has $\mathcal P(f)$ if and only if $\mathcal P(f\circ a_i)$ for every $i$. If $\mathcal P$ is $\tau$-local on the source and $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$, then for any $a:X'\to X$ in the class corresponding to $\tau$—flat for fpqc; flat locally finitely presented for fppf; syntomic for syntomic; smooth for smooth; étale for étale; open immersion for Zariski—the composite $f\circ a:X'\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-precompose-property-local-source}
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, syntomic, smooth, \etale, Zariski\}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms which is $\tau$ local
on the source. Let $f : X \to Y$ have property $\mathcal{P}$.
For any morphism $a : X' \to X$ which is
flat, resp.\ flat and locally of finite presentation, resp.\ syntomic,
resp.\ \'etale, resp.\ an open immersion, the composition
$f \circ a : X' \to Y$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

On the small étale site $X_{\acute et}$ of a **qcqs scheme**, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* when its restriction to a finite constructible partition is **finite locally constant**; for modules over a **Noetherian** ring $\Lambda$, constructible means *finite type* locally constant on every stratum. For an étale object $j_U:U\to X$, $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$ is the representable sheaf, and $j_{U!}\underline M$ is **extension by zero** of the constant abelian or $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U$, left adjoint to $j_U^{-1}$. A *torsion abelian sheaf* has torsion stalks at every geometric point. A *filtered colimit* of sheaves is taken in the sheaf category (sheafification of the sectionwise colimit). A constructible sheaf is *finitely presented/compact for filtered colimits* if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\operatorname*{colim}_i\mathcal G_i)\cong\operatorname*{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ for every filtered system. *Essentially constant* for an ind-object means isomorphic in its ind-category to a constant ind-object. For a directed inverse system with affine transitions, its category-colimit means objects and morphisms descend from sufficiently large finite stages, **up to category equivalence**.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-bootstrap}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf,
\item the diagonal morphism $F  \to F \times F$ is representable by
algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists an algebraic space $X$
and a map $X \to F$ which is surjective, and \'etale.
\end{enumerate}
or assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf, and
\item[(b)] there exists an algebraic space $X$ and a map $X \to F$
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, and \'etale.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$.
Let $(\Lambda, \mathfrak m, K)$ be an Artinian local $k$-algebra.

$A$ essentially of finite type over $k$.

hypotheses: A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$, an $A$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $J\subset B$ containing $IB$, the divided power envelope $D_{B,\gamma}(J)=(D,\bar J,\bar\gamma)$ is the universal divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra equipped with a ring map $B\to D$ carrying $J$ into $\bar J$: maps $D\to(C,K,\delta)$ of divided power $A$-algebras correspond naturally to $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ carrying $J$ into $K$. The canonical map $D\to B/J$ has kernel $\bar J$. For a divided power ring $(B,I,\gamma)$, $B\langle x_t\rangle$ denotes the divided power polynomial algebra, the free divided power $B$-algebra on elements $x_t$ of the divided power ideal $IB\langle x_t\rangle+B\langle x_t\rangle_+$, with $x_t^{[n]}=\gamma_n(x_t)$.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ with $A$ a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-algebra, together with an $A$-algebra $C$ such that $IC=0$ and $p$ is nilpotent in $C$. An object of $\mathrm{CRIS}(C/A)$ is a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $(B,J_B,\delta)$ with $p$ nilpotent in $B$ and a compatible $A$-algebra map $C\to B/J_B$; morphisms preserve the divided powers and this map from $C$. The full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ consists of objects with $C\cong B/J_B$. The completed category $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ has analogously compatible objects complete for the $p$-adic topology, with divided powers extended to the completion; for sufficiently large $e$, reductions $B/p^eB$ lie in $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$.

For a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $D$ with distinguished ideal $\bar J$, write $D^\wedge=\varprojlim_eD/p^eD$ for its $p$-adic completion. For $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $J$, put $P_e=P/p^eP$, $J_e=(J+p^eP)/p^eP$, $D_e=D_{P_e,\gamma}(J_e)$ (for all sufficiently large $e$), and let $J^\wedge$ be the completed distinguished ideal. A divided power structure on $\bar J$ extends uniquely to $J^\wedge$ when $p$ is nilpotent in $D/\bar J$.
formulation.statement:
A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$, an $A$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $J\subset B$ containing $IB$, the divided power envelope $D_{B,\gamma}(J)=(D,\bar J,\bar\gamma)$ is the universal divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra equipped with a ring map $B\to D$ carrying $J$ into $\bar J$: maps $D\to(C,K,\delta)$ of divided power $A$-algebras correspond naturally to $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ carrying $J$ into $K$. The canonical map $D\to B/J$ has kernel $\bar J$. For a divided power ring $(B,I,\gamma)$, $B\langle x_t\rangle$ denotes the divided power polynomial algebra, the free divided power $B$-algebra on elements $x_t$ of the divided power ideal $IB\langle x_t\rangle+B\langle x_t\rangle_+$, with $x_t^{[n]}=\gamma_n(x_t)$.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ with $A$ a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-algebra, together with an $A$-algebra $C$ such that $IC=0$ and $p$ is nilpotent in $C$. An object of $\mathrm{CRIS}(C/A)$ is a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $(B,J_B,\delta)$ with $p$ nilpotent in $B$ and a compatible $A$-algebra map $C\to B/J_B$; morphisms preserve the divided powers and this map from $C$. The full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ consists of objects with $C\cong B/J_B$. The completed category $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ has analogously compatible objects complete for the $p$-adic topology, with divided powers extended to the completion; for sufficiently large $e$, reductions $B/p^eB$ lie in $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$.

For a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $D$ with distinguished ideal $\bar J$, write $D^\wedge=\varprojlim_eD/p^eD$ for its $p$-adic completion. For $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $J$, put $P_e=P/p^eP$, $J_e=(J+p^eP)/p^eP$, $D_e=D_{P_e,\gamma}(J_e)$ (for all sufficiently large $e$), and let $J^\wedge$ be the completed distinguished ideal. A divided power structure on $\bar J$ extends uniquely to $J^\wedge$ when $p$ is nilpotent in $D/\bar J$.

Under the affine crystalline setup stated above,
Let $P$ be a polynomial algebra over $A$ and let
$P \to C$ be a surjection of $A$-algebras with kernel $J$.
For $D_e=D_{P_e,\gamma}(J_e)$, where $P_e=P/p^eP$, $J_e=(J+p^eP)/p^eP$ and $e$ is large enough:
for every object $(B, J_B, \delta)$ of $\text{CRIS}(C/A)$ there
exists an $e$ and a morphism $D_e \to B$ of $\text{CRIS}(C/A)$.

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a curve and let $Y$ be the nonsingular
projective model of $X$. If $k$ is perfect, then $Y$ is a smooth
projective curve.

phase2.semantic_review_note: When k is perfect the nonsingular projective model of any curve over k is smooth. The proposal retains the perfect-field hypothesis and both nonsingularity and projectivity.

phase3.reason: Invokes the cited result identifying regular points on curves with smooth points over the field under the stated hypotheses.

\label{lemma-nonsingular-model-smooth}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a curve and let $Y$ be the nonsingular
projective model of $X$. If $k$ is perfect, then $Y$ is a smooth
projective curve.

\label{lemma-make-base}
Let $X$ be a set and let $\mathcal{B}$ be a collection of subsets.
Assume that $X = \bigcup_{B \in \mathcal{B}} B$ and that given
$x \in B_1 \cap B_2$ with $B_1, B_2 \in \mathcal{B}$ there is a
$B_3 \in \mathcal{B}$ with $x \in B_3 \subset B_1 \cap B_2$.
Then there is a unique topology on $X$ such that $\mathcal{B}$
is a basis for this topology.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an additive category. Let $S$ be a multiplicative
system. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$, and $Q:\mathcal C\to S^{-1}\mathcal C$ the localization functor. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Q(X) = 0$ in $S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$,
\item there exists $Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that
$0 : X \to Y$ is an element of $S$, and
\item there exists $Z \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that
$0 : Z \to X$ is an element of $S$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-kernel-localization
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kernel-localization}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an additive category. Let $S$ be a multiplicative
system. Let $X$ be an object
of $\mathcal{C}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Q(X) = 0$ in $S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$,
\item there exists $Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that
$0 : X \to Y$ is an element of $S$, and
\item there exists $Z \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that
$0 : Z \to X$ is an element of $S$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-abelian-variety-multiplication-by-p}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $A$ be an abelian variety
of dimension $g$
over $k$. The fibre of $[p] : A \to A$ over $0$ has at most
$p^g$ distinct points.

For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be composable qcqs scheme maps, $h=g\circ f$, and write $a=a_f$, $b=a_g$, $c=a_h\simeq a\circ b$. For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ there are two natural maps from
\[
Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes_Y^{\mathbf L}b(\mathcal O_Z))\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}a(\mathcal O_Y)
\]
to $c(K)$: (i) apply $\mu_{f,Lg^*K\otimes b(\mathcal O_Z)}$ and then $a(\mu_{g,K})$, or (ii) first apply the base-change associativity and the comparison at the structure sheaf to identify the source with $Lh^*K\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}c(\mathcal O_Z)$, then apply $\mu_{h,K}$. These two maps agree, with the canonical identifications of pullbacks and right adjoints.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback}
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be composable morphisms of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated schemes and set $h = g \circ f$. Let $a, b, c$ be the
adjoints of Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image} for $f, g, h$.
For any $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)$ the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Lf^*(Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L}
b(\mathcal{O}_Z)) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} a(\mathcal{O}_Y)
\ar@{=}[d] \ar[r] &
a(Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} b(\mathcal{O}_Z)) \ar[r] &
a(b(K)) \ar@{=}[d] \\
Lh^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} Lf^*b(\mathcal{O}_Z)
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} a(\mathcal{O}_Y) \ar[r] &
Lh^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} c(\mathcal{O}_Z) \ar[r] &
c(K)
}
$$
is commutative where the arrows are (\ref{equation-compare-with-pullback})
and we have used $Lh^* = Lf^* \circ Lg^*$ and $c = a \circ b$.

\label{lemma-thickening-quasi-affine}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes
inducing a homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces.
Then $X$ is quasi-affine if and only if $Z$ is quasi-affine.

conclusions: Any algebraic space locally of finite type over $X$ is Jacobson.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a Jacobson algebraic space over $S$.
Any algebraic space locally of finite type over $X$ is Jacobson.

The proposal keeps locally finite type (rather than finite type) and does not require X decent; the chapter's Jacobson property is étale-local as described in L5238–5243.

phase3.reason: Apply the scheme result that locally finite type morphisms preserve Jacobson schemes after an étale scheme chart of X; conclude the resulting algebraic space is Jacobson by chartwise definition.

\label{lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $E \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a
subset such that every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by
elements of $E$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets. There exists a
diagram of sheaves of sets
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}_1 \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &

The proposed hypotheses incorrectly include all five equivalence clauses as premises, distorting scope and reducing the equivalence to a tautological conditional.
phase2.proposed_correction: Remove all five alternatives from hypotheses, express them as five-way equivalence with a separate subsequent implication for U'→U, retaining both pieces and independent review.

phase3.reason: Representability of sections F(U)=Hom(h_U#,F) identifies sheaf-theoretic emptiness with universal singleton sections. source.label: lemma-characterize-empty
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-empty}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U$ is sheaf theoretically empty,
\item $\mathcal{F}(U)$ is a singleton for each sheaf $\mathcal{F}$,
\item $\emptyset^\#(U)$ is a singleton,
\item $\emptyset^\#(U)$ is nonempty, and
\item the empty family is a covering of $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $U$ is sheaf theoretically empty, then for any morphism
$U' \to U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ the object $U'$ is sheaf theoretically empty.

\label{lemma-derived-complete-limit}
Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a derived complete sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules

Then there exists an integer $t$ and a surjective map
$$
(\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge)^{\oplus t} \to \mathcal{F}
$$

hypotheses: $f$ is a **flat** morphism of ringed topoi.
$K\in D^+(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is bounded below.
For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the unit $H^q(K)\to Rf_*f^*H^q(K)$ is an isomorphism.
formulation.statement:
Let $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O')$ be a morphism of ringed topoi, with adjoint derived functors $Lf^*:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$ and $Rf_*:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$. A weak Serre subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions arising from its morphisms; $D_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal O)$ consists of derived objects whose cohomology modules lie in $\mathcal A$. With $f$ flat and $K$ bounded below **downstairs**, the source assumes each cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ satisfies the derived adjunction **unit** $H^q(K)\to Rf_*f^*H^q(K)$. The conclusion is the unit on the **whole** complex.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat,
\item $K$ is bounded below,
\item $H^q(K) \to Rf_*f^*H^q(K)$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $K \to Rf_*f^*K$ is an isomorphism.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For flat f and bounded-below K DOWNSTAIRS D(O_D), isomorphism of derived unit H^q(K)→Rf_*f*H^q(K) for all q implies K→Rf_*f*K is isomorphism. Clearly distinct from prior counit claim.

phase3.reason: The proof similarly reduces unit isomorphism to cohomology sheaves under derived pushforward and invokes the downstairs thick triangulated subcategory.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

decent and locally Noetherian algebraic spaces. Let
$\delta : |X| \to \mathbf{Z}$ be a function. If $\delta \circ |f|$ is a
dimension function, then $\delta$ is a dimension function.

If δ∘|f| is a dimension function on |Y|, δ is a dimension function on |X|. The draft preserves surjectivity, finiteness, and BOTH spaces' hypotheses; it asserts descent, not an unconditional converse.

phase3.reason: Finite surjectivity and closedness lift every specialization of X to Y; finite fibres prohibit intermediate specialization jumps, so immediate specializations have the same dimension-function increment.

\label{lemma-check-dimension-function-finite-cover}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a surjective finite morphism of
decent and locally Noetherian algebraic spaces. Let
$\delta : |X| \to \mathbf{Z}$ be a function. If $\delta \circ |f|$ is a
dimension function, then $\delta$ is a dimension function.

source.label: lemma-smooth-characterize
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-smooth-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is smooth.
\item For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is smooth.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is smooth.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
smooth, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is smooth then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is smooth.

\label{lemma-globally-generated-omega-twist-1}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf
and let $s_0, \ldots, s_n$ be global sections of $\mathcal{L}$
which generate it. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the kernel of the induced
map $\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus n + 1} \to \mathcal{L}$.
Then $\mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}$ is globally generated.

phase3.reason: Hom(Delta[n],K)_0=K_n, and each face map is induced by an inclusion Delta[n-1]→Delta[n], which is covering by the add-simplices lemma. Composing face coverings with K_0→X yields every K_n→X a covering.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-globally-generated-base-change}
Let $X \to \Spec(A)$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $A \subset A'$
be a faithfully flat ring map. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is globally generated
if and only if the base change $\mathcal{F}_{A'}$ is globally generated.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-big-site-smooth}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_{smooth}$ be a big smooth
site containing $S$.
The functor
$(\textit{Aff}/S)_{smooth} \to (\Sch/S)_{smooth}$
is special cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from
$\Sh((\textit{Aff}/S)_{smooth})$ to
$\Sh((\Sch/S)_{smooth})$.

conclusions: For each $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map of sheaves $H^q(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_n H^q(K_n)$ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site and $(K_n)$ is an inverse system in $D(\mathcal O)$.
$\mathcal B\subseteq\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ covers every site object.
For all $U\in\mathcal B$ and all $q\in\mathbf Z$, $H^p(U,H^q(K_n))=0$ for all $p>0$ and every $n$, and $R^1\varprojlim_n H^0(U,H^q(K_n))=0$.
formulation.statement:
For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. The canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\ge -n}E$ uses good truncations. Here $H^q(K_n)$ denotes cohomology **sheaves**, and $H^0(U,H^q(K_n))$ denotes their section groups. The $R^1\varprojlim$ hypothesis is imposed on these degree-zero section groups for each site object in a covering set and each cohomology degree.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $(K_n)$
be an inverse system of objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a subset. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item for all $U \in \mathcal{B}$ and all $q \in \mathbf{Z}$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, H^q(K_n)) = 0$ for $p > 0$,
\item the inverse system $H^0(U, H^q(K_n))$ has vanishing $R^1\lim$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^q(R\lim K_n) = \lim H^q(K_n)$ for $q \in \mathbf{Z}$.

\label{lemma-embedded}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the generic points of irreducible components of
$\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ are associated points of $\mathcal{F}$, and
\item an associated point of $\mathcal{F}$ is embedded if and only
if it is not a generic point of an irreducible component
of $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular an embedded point of $X$ is an associated point of $X$
which is not a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-seminormalize-base}
Let $g : S' \to S$ be a universal homeomorphism of locally Noetherian schemes
which induces isomorphisms of residue fields. Let $f : X \to S$ be locally of
finite type. Set $X' = S' \times_S X$. Let $r \geq 0$. Then base change by $g$
determines a bijection $z(X/S, r) \to z(X'/S', r)$.

hypotheses: Normalized local dualizing ω_A, injective hull E, finite-length N.
formulation.statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring, with a *normalized* dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$: this is a dualizing complex satisfying $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\kappa[0]$. For an $A$-module $M$ put $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,\omega_A^\bullet)=H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\omega_A^\bullet))$. Let $E$ be an injective hull of the residue field $\kappa$, i.e. an injective $A$-module in which $\kappa$ is an essential submodule. For every finite-length $A$-module $N$, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,E)[0].
\]
The right-hand side is the ordinary Matlis dual viewed in degree $0$; its derived higher cohomology vanishes on finite-length $N$. The isomorphism is functorial in $N$, not merely one selected for each module.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A normalized dualizing complex over Noetherian local A computes the Matlis dual Hom_A(N,E)[0] of every finite-length N, naturally in N. The injective hull E and normalization hypothesis are included.

phase3.reason: Induction on length yields degree-zero Matlis duality of finite-length modules; combining the two anti-equivalences and Matlis biduality identifies them functorially.

source.label: lemma-dualizing-finite-length
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dualizing-finite-length}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local
ring with normalized dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$.
Let $E$ be an injective hull of $\kappa$. Then there exists
a functorial isomorphism
$$
R\Hom_A(N, \omega_A^\bullet) = \Hom_A(N, E)[0]
$$
for $N$ running through the finite length $A$-modules.

\label{lemma-product-hypercoverings}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
If $K, L$ are hypercoverings of $X$, then
$K \times L$ is a hypercovering of $X$.

\label{lemma-injective-dimension-over-polynomial-ring}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $E$ be an injective $A$-module.
Then $E \otimes_A A[x]$ has injective-amplitude $[0, 1]$
as an object of $D(A[x])$. In particular, $E \otimes_A A[x]$
has finite injective dimension as an $A[x]$-module.

\label{lemma-localizing}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{C}$
be a category fibred in groupoids. Let $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{X})$
lying over $U = p(x)$. The functor $p$ induces an equivalence of sites
$\mathcal{X}/x \to \mathcal{C}/U$ where $\mathcal{X}$ is endowed with
the topology inherited from $\mathcal{C}$.

\label{lemma-stalk-module-differentials}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $X$. Let $x \in X$. Then we have

\Omega_{\mathcal{O}_{2, x}/\mathcal{O}_{1, x}}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cd-top-vanishing}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring of dimension $d$. Let $I \subset I' \subset A$
be ideals. If $I'$ is contained in the Jacobson radical
of $A$ and $\text{cd}(A, I') < d$, then $\text{cd}(A, I) < d$.
