source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-finiteness}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $M$ be an $S$-module.
Let $R \to R'$ be a ring map and let $S' = S \otimes_R R'$ and
$M' = M \otimes_R R'$ be the base changes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ is a finite $S$-module, then the base change
$M'$ is a finite $S'$-module.
\item If $M$ is an $S$-module of finite presentation, then
the base change $M'$ is an $S'$-module of finite presentation.
\item If $R \to S$ is of finite type, then the base change
$R' \to S'$ is of finite type.
\item If $R \to S$ is of finite presentation, then
the base change $R' \to S'$ is of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-intersection-not-zero}
Let $A \subset B$ be an inclusion of domains inducing an algebraic extension
of fraction fields. If $J \subset B$ is a nonzero ideal, then $A \cap J$
is nonzero too. Thus the image of a proper closed subset of $\Spec(B)$
is not dense in $\Spec(A)$.

$(X, Y, Z \oplus Z', f, g, h)$ such that $f \in S$.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(5)] the morphism $0 \to Z$ is an element of $S$,
\item[(6)] the morphism $Z \to 0$ is an element of $S$,
\item[(7)] there exists a distinguished triangle $(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)$
such that $f \in S$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-connected-components-in-neighbourhood}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $Y$ irreducible with
generic point $\eta$ and $f$ of finite type. If $X_\eta$ has $n$
connected components, then there exists a nonempty open $V \subset Y$
such that for all $y \in V$ the fibre $X_y$ has at least $n$
connected components.

formulation.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $S$ be an affine scheme such that
(1) all points are closed, and (2) all residue fields are separably
algebraically closed. Then
for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $S_\etale$ we have
$H^i(S_\etale, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > 0$.

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

source.label: lemma-flat-under-geometrically-regular
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-under-geometrically-regular}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes over $k$.
Let $x \in X$ be a point and set $y = f(x)$.
If $X$ is geometrically regular at $x$ and
$f$ is flat at $x$ then $Y$ is geometrically regular at $y$.
In particular, if $X$ is geometrically regular over $k$ and
$f$ is flat and surjective, then $Y$ is geometrically regular over $k$.

The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

Let $A \to B \to C$ be ring maps such that $L_{C/B} = 0$.
Then $L_{C/A} = L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} C$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Noetherian-goes-to-spectral}
Let $X$ be a topological space and let $c : X \to X'$ be the universal
map from $X$ to a sober topological space, see
Lemma \ref{lemma-make-sober}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $X$ is quasi-compact, so is $X'$.
\item If $X$ is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens,
and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, then
$X'$ is spectral.
\item If $X$ is Noetherian, then $X'$ is a Noetherian spectral space.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-check-immersion}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. If for all $y \in Y$
there is an open subscheme $f(y) \in U \subset X$ such that
$f|_{f^{-1}(U)} : f^{-1}(U) \to U$ is an immersion, then $f$ is
an immersion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unbounded-relative-mayer-vietoris}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Suppose that $X = U \cup V$ is a union of two open subsets.
Denote $a = f|_U : U \to Y$, $b = f|_V : V \to Y$, and
$c = f|_{U \cap V} : U \cap V \to Y$.
For every object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ there exists a
distinguished triangle
$$
Rf_*E \to
Ra_*(E|_U) \oplus Rb_*(E|_V) \to
Rc_*(E|_{U \cap V}) \to
Rf_*E[1]
$$
This triangle is functorial in $E$.

\label{lemma-base-change-and-fitting-ideal-omega}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $X = Z_{-1} \supset Z_0 \supset Z_1 \supset \ldots$
be the closed subschemes defined by the fitting ideals
of $\Omega_{X/S}$. Then the formation of $Z_i$ commutes
with arbitrary base change.

Let $\Phi:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal A)$ denote the affine-morphism equivalence under which $Rf_*$ becomes restriction of scalars along $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal A$. Denote the right derived $\mathcal A$-module-valued internal Hom functor by $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A,-)$, viewed as an object of $D(\mathcal A)$. Assume $f:Y\to X$ is finite and pseudo-coherent. Then $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A,-)$ maps $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ to $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal A)$. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-twisted}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a finite pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes
(a finite morphism of Noetherian schemes is pseudo-coherent).
The functor $R\SheafHom(f_*\mathcal{O}_Y, -)$ maps
$D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_X)$ into $D_\QCoh^+(f_*\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_X) \ar[rr]_a \ar[rd]_{R\SheafHom(f_*\mathcal{O}_Y, -)}
& & D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y) \ar[ld]^\Phi \\
& D_\QCoh^+(f_*\mathcal{O}_Y)
}
$$
is commutative, where $a$ is the right adjoint of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image} for $f$ and $\Phi$ is the equivalence
of Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma
\ref{perfect-lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence}.

\label{lemma-prepare-representable-map-stack-in-groupoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ be categories fibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism.
Let $G : \mathcal{C}/U \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism.
Then
$$
(\mathcal{C}/U) \times_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{C}/U
$$
is a category fibred in groupoids.

Let $R$ be a ring, and let $f_1, f_2, \ldots f_n\in R$ generate

\left(\frac{x_i}{f_i^{r_i}}-\frac{x_j}{f_j^{r_j}}~\text{in}~R_{f_if_j}\right).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-precise-vanishing}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $P^\bullet$, $K^\bullet$ be complexes.
Let $n \in \mathbf{Z}$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P^\bullet$ is a bounded complex consisting of projective
objects,
\item $P^i = 0$ for $i < n$, and
\item $H^i(K^\bullet) = 0$ for $i \geq n$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
$\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(P^\bullet, K^\bullet) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{A})}(P^\bullet, K^\bullet) = 0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-artinian-finite-type}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $A$ be an Artinian local ring with residue field $\kappa$.
Let $f : \Spec(A) \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Then $f$ is of finite type if and only if the composition
$\Spec(\kappa) \to \Spec(A) \to S$ is of finite type.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-explain-why-pure-ML}
Let $R$ be a henselian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $N$ be an $S$-module.
Assume $N$ is countably generated and Mittag-Leffler as an $R$-module.
Then for any $R$-module $M$ and for any prime $\mathfrak q \subset S$
which is an associated prime of $N \otimes_R M$ we have
$\mathfrak q + \mathfrak m S \not = S$.

formulation.statement:
Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. For every (possibly unbounded) $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical morphism
\[
Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\mu_{f,K}}a_f(K)
\]
is an isomorphism. In particular, the functor $a_f$ is obtained by derived pullback followed by tensoring with the relative dualizing complex, functorially on the full unbounded quasi-coherent derived category.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L2674 asserts that μ_{f,K}:Lf^*K⊗^L a_f(O_Y)→a_f(K) is an isomorphism for EVERY K∈D_QCoh(Y) assuming f proper flat finitely presented and Y qcqs. The proposal restores the definition of relative dualizing complex ω=a_f(O_Y) and maintains the unbounded comparison, without restricting K to perfect objects.

phase3.reason: The class of objects where the comparison is an isomorphism is localizing; perfect generation reduces the result to the already proved perfect-object case.

source.label: lemma-covering-sheaf
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-covering-sheaf}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
Let $u : \mathcal{F} \to F(K_n)$ be a morphism
of presheaves which becomes surjective
on sheafification.
Then there exists a morphism of hypercoverings
$f: L \to K$ such that $F(f_n) : F(L_n) \to F(K_n)$
factors through $u$.

For $X$ irreducible we have $\dim(X) = \dim(U)$ for any
nonempty open $U \subset X$ and $\dim(X) = \dim_x(X)$
for any $x \in X$.
\item
For $X$ irreducible any chain of irreducible closed subsets can be
extended to a maximal chain and all maximal chains of irreducible
closed subsets have length equal to $\dim(X)$.
\item
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \max \dim(Z) = \min \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$
where the maximum is over irreducible components
$Z \subset X$ containing $x$ and the minimum is over
specializations $x \leadsto x'$ with $x'$ closed in $X$.
\item
If $X$ is irreducible with generic point $x$, then
$\dim(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization

$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x')) + 1$.
\item
The dimension of $X$ is the supremum of the numbers
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$ where $x$ runs over the
generic points of the irreducible components of $X$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is a nontrivial specialization of points of $X$, then
\begin{enumerate}

\end{enumerate}
\item
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) + \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$ and $X$ is irreducible or equidimensional, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + 1$.

\label{lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
\label{item-catenary}

(Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-catenary}).
\item
\label{item-dimension-at-closed-point}

\item
\label{item-dimension-irreducible}
For $X$ irreducible we have $\dim(X) = \dim(U)$ for any
nonempty open $U \subset X$ and $\dim(X) = \dim_x(X)$
for any $x \in X$.
\item
\label{item-irreducible-maximal-chains}
For $X$ irreducible any chain of irreducible closed subsets can be
extended to a maximal chain and all maximal chains of irreducible
closed subsets have length equal to $\dim(X)$.
\item
\label{item-dimension-irreducibles-passing-through}
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \max \dim(Z) = \min \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$
where the maximum is over irreducible components
$Z \subset X$ containing $x$ and the minimum is over
specializations $x \leadsto x'$ with $x'$ closed in $X$.
\item
\label{item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg}
If $X$ is irreducible with generic point $x$, then
$\dim(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$.
\item
\label{item-immediate-specialization}
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$, then we have
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x')) + 1$.
\item
\label{item-dimension-sup-trdeg}
The dimension of $X$ is the supremum of the numbers
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$ where $x$ runs over the
generic points of the irreducible components of $X$.
\item
\label{item-specialization}
If $x \leadsto x'$ is a nontrivial specialization of points of $X$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_x(X) \leq \dim_{x'}(X)$,
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) < \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$,
\item $\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) > \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x'))$, and
\item any maximal chain of nontrivial specializations
$x = x_0 \leadsto x_1 \leadsto \ldots \leadsto x_n = x'$ has
length $n = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) - \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x'))$.
\end{enumerate}
\item
\label{item-dimension-formula}
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) + \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item
\label{item-immediate-specialization-local-ring}
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$ and $X$ is irreducible or equidimensional, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + 1$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-2-fibre-product-general}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{Z}$ be a stack in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$
whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces.
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ be algebraic stacks over $S$.
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$, $g : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of stacks in groupoids. Then the $2$-fibre product
$\mathcal{X} \times_{f, \mathcal{Z}, g} \mathcal{Y}$ is an algebraic stack.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universally-separating}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $g : X' \to X$ be a flat morphism of schemes over $S$
with $X$ locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
which is flat over $S$. If $\text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F}) \subset g(X')$
then the canonical map
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow g_*g^*\mathcal{F}
$$
is injective, and remains injective after any base change.

Let $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ be a functor. For presheaves let $u^p\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{G}\circ u$. For $V\in\Ob(\mathcal{D})$ let $\mathcal{I}^u_V$ have objects $(U,\phi:V\to u(U))$ and arrows $\alpha:(U,\phi)\to(U',\phi')$ with $u(\alpha)\circ\phi=\phi'$. Let $u_p\mathcal{F}(V)=\colim_{(\mathcal{I}^u_V)^{opp}}\mathcal{F}(U)$ with the induced restriction maps (source §5, L383–409, 495–539).
The functor $u_p$ is a left adjoint to the functor $u^p$.
In other words the formula
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F}, u^p\mathcal{G})
=
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{D})}(u_p\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})
$$
holds bifunctorially in $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.

\label{lemma-adjoints-u}
The functor $u_p$ is a left adjoint to the functor $u^p$.
In other words the formula
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F}, u^p\mathcal{G})
=
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{D})}(u_p\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})
$$
holds bifunctorially in $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.

Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ has finite rank $r \geq 0$, and
\item there exists a nonempty open $U \subset X$
such that $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is free of rank $r$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-extra-silly}
Let $A$ be a ring, $I \subset A$ an ideal,
$\mathfrak p_1, \ldots, \mathfrak p_r$ primes of $A$, and
$\overline{f} \in A/I$ an element. If $I \not \subset \mathfrak p_i$
for all $i$, then there exists an $f \in A$, $f \not \in \mathfrak p_i$
which maps to $\overline{f}$ in $A/I$.

source.label: lemma-dominate-modification-by-blowup
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dominate-modification-by-blowup}
Let $\varphi : X \to S$ be a proper morphism with
$S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $U \subset S$ be a
quasi-compact open such that $\varphi^{-1}U \to U$ is an isomorphism.
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $S' \to S$
which dominates $X$, i.e., such that there exists a factorization
$S' \to X \to S$ of the blowup morphism.

Then $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

source.label: proposition-generic-flatness-reduced
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-generic-flatness-reduced}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is reduced,
\item $f$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open dense subspace $W \subset Y$ such that
the base change $X_W \to W$ of $f$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and
quasi-compact and such that $\mathcal{F}|_{X_W}$ is flat over $W$ and of
finite presentation over $\mathcal{O}_{X_W}$.

phase2.hold_reason: The source gives parallel conditional claims for specialization and generalization lifting. The Stage B hypotheses contain only specialization-lifting premises while the conclusions also assert generalization lifting.
phase2.proposed_correction: State two independent implications: lifting along f and g for each relation implies lifting along g∘f for that relation.

phase3.reason: Specializations and generalizations lift successively along each map, giving the corresponding lifting property for the composite.

source.label: lemma-lift-specialization-composition
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-specialization-composition}
Suppose $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ are continuous maps
of topological spaces. If specializations lift along both $f$ and $g$
then specializations lift along $g \circ f$. Similarly for
``generalizations lift along''.

formulation.statement:
The slice site $\mathcal C/U$ has objects morphisms $V\to U$ of $\mathcal C$, with induced coverings. Denote by $\mathcal O_U$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ the respective restrictions of $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal F$ to this slice. The groups $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ and $H^p(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal F|_U)$ are the respective right-derived section functors (with $p\ge0$).

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{I}$ is an injective $\mathcal{O}$-module
then $\mathcal{I}|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
\item For any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ we have
$H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(\mathcal{C}/U, \mathcal{F}|_U)$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-smoothness-dimension-spaces}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be locally Noetherian algebraic spaces over a scheme
$S$, and let $f : X \to Y$ be a smooth morphism.
For every point $x \in |X|$ with image $y \in |Y|$,
$$
\dim_x(X) = \dim_y(Y) + \dim_x(X_y)
$$
where $\dim_x(X_y)$ is the relative dimension of $f$ at $x$ as
in Definition \ref{definition-dimension-fibre}.

\label{lemma-associated-point-specializes}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $y \in \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$ with image $t \in S$.
Denote $Y \subset X$ the closure of $\{y\}$ in $X$ viewed
as an integral closed subscheme. Let $s \in S$
and let $x \in Y_s$ be a generic point of an irreducible component
of $Y_s$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at $x$, then
$x \in \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$ and
$\dim_x(Y_s) = \dim(Y_t)$.

formulation.statement:
For a morphism $X\to Y$ in a site $\mathcal C$, write $j_{X/Y}:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/Y)$ for the localization morphism of topoi; on a ringed site it induces the corresponding morphism of ringed topoi. The restriction functors $j^{-1}$ (abelian sheaves) and $j^*$ (ringed-module sheaves) are exact. For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ and cartesian square of objects, the slice sites inherit ring sheaves $\mathcal O_X$ etc. The isomorphism concerns the ordinary exact restriction $j^*$ on **module derived categories**, not the inverse-image $j^{-1}$ used for abelian sheaves.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^* \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^*$
as functors
$D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_{Y'})$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a cartesian object square in a RINGED site, the module-derived pushforward base-change isomorphism uses j^* instead of j^{-1} and correctly lands in D(O_{Y'}), with all slice rings retained.

phase3.reason: The proof identifies localization pullback with exact inverse image for the localized structure sheaves and reduces the module square to the abelian-sheaf square via the earlier unbounded comparison lemma.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localize-cartesian-square-modules}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^* \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^*$
as functors
$D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_{Y'})$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly. This operator also descends to Chow groups.

For a pair $(\mathcal M,u)$ with $\mathcal M$ invertible on $T$, $u\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal M)$, and $j:E=Z(u)\hookrightarrow T$, define the Gysin map $j^*:Z_{q+1}(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_q(E)$ on integral closed $W\subset T$ by $j^*[W]=[E\cap W]_q$ if $W\not\subset E$, and $j^*[W]=(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. When $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor, write $E\cdot\alpha=j_*j^*\alpha$ for the resulting intersection class. The Gysin map also descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pushforward of an integral $[W]\in Z_q(T')$ is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if $\dim_\delta h(W)=q$, and $0$ if that dimension is smaller. This extends linearly and induces a map on Chow groups.

For a pair $(\mathcal M,u)$ with $\mathcal M$ invertible on $T$, $u\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal M)$, and $j:E=Z(u)\hookrightarrow T$, define the Gysin map $j^*:Z_{q+1}(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_q(E)$ on integral closed $W\subset T$ by $j^*[W]=[E\cap W]_q$ if $W\not\subset E$, and $j^*[W]=(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Let $X$ be locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$, let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and let $D=Z(s)$ with closed immersion $i:D\hookrightarrow X$. Then
$i^*i_* : \mathrm{CH}_k(D) \to \mathrm{CH}_{k - 1}(D)$ sends $\alpha$ to
$c_1(\mathcal{L}|_D) \cap \alpha$.

Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}. Let $X$ be locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $(\mathcal{L}, s, i : D \to X)$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-gysin-homomorphism}. Then
$i^*i_* : \CH_k(D) \to \CH_{k - 1}(D)$ sends $\alpha$ to
$c_1(\mathcal{L}|_D) \cap \alpha$.

Let $X$ be a scheme over the field $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a field extension.
Then $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ if and only if
$X_{k'}$ is geometrically irreducible over $k'$.

formulation.statement:
Work over the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. A category fibred in groupoids is represented by an algebraic space when it is equivalent to the fibred category of points of an algebraic space over $S$. A 1-morphism of fibred categories is representable by algebraic spaces if every 2-base change by a morphism from a scheme is represented by an algebraic space. A representable morphism $j:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is a monomorphism when each induced morphism $F_y\to U$ of algebraic spaces is a monomorphism, i.e., its diagonal is an isomorphism. For any $U/S$ and objects $x,y\in\mathcal X_U$, $\mathit{Isom}(x,y)$ denotes the functor on schemes $V\to U$ of isomorphisms between pullbacks of $x$ and $y$. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{(\Sch/S)_{fppf}}\mathcal X$ sends each object to the pair $(x,x)$. A representable category fibred in groupoids means one equivalent to $(\Sch/U)_{fppf}$ for a scheme $U/S$; representable by an algebraic space is a broader condition. All products of fibred categories are 2-products.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred in groupoids over
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the diagonal $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every scheme $U$ over $S$, and any
$x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_U)$ the sheaf
$\mathit{Isom}(x, y)$ is an algebraic space over $U$,
\item for every scheme $U$ over $S$, and any $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_U)$
the associated $1$-morphism $x : (\Sch/U)_{fppf} \to \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every pair of schemes $T_1, T_2$ over $S$, and any
$x_i \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_{T_i})$, $i = 1, 2$ the $2$-fibre product
$(\Sch/T_1)_{fppf} \times_{x_1, \mathcal{X}, x_2}
(\Sch/T_2)_{fppf}$
is representable by an algebraic space,
\item for every representable category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal{U}$
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ every $1$-morphism
$\mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every pair $\mathcal{T}_1, \mathcal{T}_2$ of representable
categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ and any
$1$-morphisms $x_i : \mathcal{T}_i \to \mathcal{X}$, $i = 1, 2$ the
$2$-fibre product $\mathcal{T}_1 \times_{x_1, \mathcal{X}, x_2} \mathcal{T}_2$
is representable by an algebraic space,
\item for every category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal{U}$
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which is
representable by an algebraic space every $1$-morphism
$\mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every pair $\mathcal{T}_1, \mathcal{T}_2$ of categories fibred
in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which are representable
by algebraic spaces, and any $1$-morphisms
$x_i : \mathcal{T}_i \to \mathcal{X}$ the
$2$-fibre product $\mathcal{T}_1 \times_{x_1, \mathcal{X}, x_2} \mathcal{T}_2$
is representable by an algebraic space.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-relative-affine-vanishing}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.

\label{lemma-constructible-partition-refined-by-stratification}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Suppose $X = T_1 \cup \ldots \cup T_n$
is written as a union of constructible subsets. There exists a finite
stratification $X = \coprod X_i$ with each $X_i$ constructible
such that each $T_k$ is a union of strata.

Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let
$(K_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ be a system of perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $K = \text{hocolim} K_n$ be the derived colimit
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-derived-colimit}).
Then for any object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have
$$
R\SheafHom(K, E) = R\lim E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} K_n^\vee
$$
where $(K_n^\vee)$ is the inverse system of dual perfect complexes.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let
$(K_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ be a system of perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $K = \text{hocolim} K_n$ be the derived colimit
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-derived-colimit}).
Then for any object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have
$$
R\SheafHom(K, E) = R\lim E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} K_n^\vee
$$
where $(K_n^\vee)$ is the inverse system of dual perfect complexes.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed subset inclusion, and let $D_Z(\mathcal O_X)\subseteq D(\mathcal O_X)$ denote the strictly full triangulated subcategory consisting of objects with cohomology sheaves supported on $Z$. Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $i : Z \to X$ be the
inclusion of a closed subset.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $K$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X|_Z)$ we have $i_*K$ in $D_Z(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\item The functor $i_* : D(\mathcal{O}_X|_Z) \to D_Z(\mathcal{O}_X)$
is an equivalence with quasi-inverse
$i^{-1}|_{D_Z(\mathcal{O}_X)} = R\mathcal{H}_Z|_{D_Z(\mathcal{O}_X)}$.
\item The functor
$i_* \circ R\mathcal{H}_Z : D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_Z(\mathcal{O}_X)$
is right adjoint to the inclusion functor
$D_Z(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a closed subset Z⊂X, i_* takes D(O_X|Z) equivalently to the derived category D_Z(O_X) of complexes with cohomology on Z; both i^{-1} and RH_Z are given as quasi-inverses on this subcategory. The composite i_*RH_Z is right adjoint to the inclusion D_Z→D. All three source parts survive.

phase3.reason: Proves essential surjectivity and full faithfulness of closed pushforward via exact inverse image and the support condition on cohomology sheaves.

source.label: lemma-j-shriek-flat
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-j-shriek-flat}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Consider the functor $j_U : \mathcal{C}/U \to \mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The presheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$ (see
Remark \ref{remark-localize-presheaves})
is flat.
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ is a site, $\mathcal{O}$ is a sheaf of rings,
$j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$ is a flat sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bijection-irreducible-components}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $k$.
Assume $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$.
Then the projection morphism
$$
p : X \times_k Y \longrightarrow Y
$$
induces a bijection between irreducible components.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-resolution-of-flat}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings.
Let
$$
\ldots \to
\mathcal{F}_2 \to
\mathcal{F}_1 \to
\mathcal{F}_0 \to
\mathcal{Q} \to 0
$$
be an exact complex of presheaves of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
If $\mathcal{Q}$ and all $\mathcal{F}_i$ are flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules,
then for any presheaf $\mathcal{G}$ of $\mathcal{O}$-modules the
complex
$$
\ldots \to
\mathcal{F}_2 \otimes_{p, \mathcal{O}} \mathcal{G} \to
\mathcal{F}_1 \otimes_{p, \mathcal{O}} \mathcal{G} \to
\mathcal{F}_0 \otimes_{p, \mathcal{O}} \mathcal{G} \to
\mathcal{Q} \otimes_{p, \mathcal{O}} \mathcal{G} \to 0
$$
is exact also. If $\mathcal{C}$ is a site and $\mathcal{O}$ is a
sheaf of rings then the same result holds $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.

In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, a morphism of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** when every Yoneda test $h_U\to G$ has scheme-representable fibre product $h_U\times_GF$. For a property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms preserved under arbitrary base change and fppf-local on the base, $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ precisely if all resulting scheme maps $V_\xi\to U$ have $\mathcal P$. A surjective representable morphism means surjective on such scheme tests; this is distinguished from surjectivity as a presheaf map.

\label{lemma-surjective-flat-locally-finite-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be sheaves.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective.
Then $a : F \to G$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $Y$ irreducible with
generic point $\eta$ and $f$ of finite type. If $X_\eta$ is nonreduced,
then there exists a nonempty open $V \subset Y$
such that for all $y \in V$ the fibre $X_y$ is nonreduced.

\label{lemma-gorenstein-divide-by-nonzerodivisor}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$
be a Noetherian local ring. Let $f \in \mathfrak m$ be a
nonzerodivisor. Set $B = A/(f)$. Then $A$ is Gorenstein if and
only if $B$ is Gorenstein.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
If $\dim_\delta(Z) \leq k$, then $[Z]_k = [{\mathcal O}_Z]_k$.

The expanded standalone dimension-function and generic-length notation agrees with source, without assuming Z reduced.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-complement-affine-open}
Let $X$ be a separated locally Noetherian scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be an
affine open. For every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of
$X \setminus U$ the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}$
has dimension $\leq 1$. If $U$ is dense or if $\xi$ is in the closure
of $U$, then $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}) = 1$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is irreducible with generic point $\eta$,
\item $X_\eta$ is geometrically reduced, and

such that $X_V \to V$ has geometrically reduced fibres.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-de-rham-affine}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of affine schemes given by the ring map
$R \to A$. Then $R\Gamma(X, \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}) = \Omega^\bullet_{A/R}$
in $D(R)$ and $H^i_{dR}(X/S) = H^i(\Omega^\bullet_{A/R})$.

Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Define its *algebraic upper-shriek functor* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ by choosing a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and putting
\[
\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n].
\]
For surjective $\varphi$, one may use $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$ with its natural $A$-action. Different polynomial presentations give isomorphic functors, but the isomorphisms are *not canonical*. Here $D^\pm$ means bounded below/above cohomology, $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}$ means coherent cohomology, and a *perfect* ring map is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension (equivalently $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex after a suitable finite polynomial presentation).

Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing complex for $A$. Set
$\omega_B^\bullet = \varphi^!(\omega_A^\bullet)$. Denote
$D_A(K) = R\Hom_A(K, \omega_A^\bullet)$ for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
and
$D_B(L) = R\Hom_B(L, \omega_B^\bullet)$ for $L \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(B)$.
Then there is a functorial isomorphism
$$
\varphi^!(K) = D_B(D_A(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B)
$$
for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$.

D_A and D_B are two different ring-specific duality functors: D_A(K)=RHom_A(K,ω_A) and D_B(L)=RHom_B(L,ω_B), ω_B=φ^!(ω_A).

source.label: lemma-relative-dualizing-if-have-omega
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-dualizing-if-have-omega}
Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing complex for $A$. Set
$\omega_B^\bullet = \varphi^!(\omega_A^\bullet)$. Denote
$D_A(K) = R\Hom_A(K, \omega_A^\bullet)$ for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
and
$D_B(L) = R\Hom_B(L, \omega_B^\bullet)$ for $L \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(B)$.
Then there is a functorial isomorphism
$$
\varphi^!(K) = D_B(D_A(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B)
$$
for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z$ is reduced, locally Noetherian, and $|Z|$
is a singleton, and
\item there exists a locally finitely presented, surjective, flat morphism
$\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to Z$ where $k$ is a field.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-finite-presentation}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
The pullback $f^*\mathcal{G}$ of a module of finite presentation
is of finite presentation.

conclusions: The local rings have equal Krull dimension.
hypotheses: f is étale and v=f(u).
formulation.statement:
Let $f:U\to V$ be an étale morphism of schemes and $u\in U$, $v=f(u)$. Then the induced étale homomorphism of local rings $\mathcal O_{V,v}\to\mathcal O_{U,u}$ preserves Krull dimension:
$$\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}=\dim\mathcal O_{V,v}.$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L5236 states equality of Krull dimensions of the LOCAL RINGS at u and its étale image v. The reconstruction explicitly asserts that local-ring equality and the étale condition; it does not mistake this for the germ dimension result immediately preceding it.

phase3.reason: The complete pinned proof explicitly reduces equality of étale local-ring dimensions to the cited More on Algebra dimension-of-étale-extension lemma, with matching localization at corresponding primes.

source.label: lemma-dimension-local-ring-local
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dimension-local-ring-local}
Let $f : U \to V$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
Let $u \in U$ and $v = f(u)$. Then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{U, u}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{V, v})$.

\label{lemma-base-change-flat}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces. If $\mathcal{G}$ is a flat
$\mathcal{O}_Y$-module, then $f^*\mathcal{G}$ is a flat
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

\label{lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite}
Let $S = \Spec(A)$ with $A$ a Noetherian ring.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper morphism.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then $H^i(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a finite $A$-module for all $i \geq 0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-support-stalk}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally quasi-finite.
Let $\overline{y} : \Spec(k) \to Y$ be a geometric point.
Functorially in $\mathcal{F}$ in $\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)$ we have
$$
(f_{p!}\mathcal{F})_{\overline{y}} =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{f(\overline{x}) = \overline{y}} \mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}}
$$

\label{lemma-extend-off-basis}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal{B}$.
There exists a unique sheaf of sets $\mathcal{F}^{ext}$
on $X$ such that $\mathcal{F}^{ext}(U) = \mathcal{F}(U)$
for all $U \in \mathcal{B}$ compatibly with the restriction
mappings.

Let $R \to A \to B$ be ring maps.

The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.
formulation.statement:
Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel $I$; let $A\to B$ be an $A$-algebra, $N$ a $B$-module, and $c:I\to N$ an $A$-linear map. A solution of the lifting problem is a commutative diagram of ring homomorphisms with exact rows $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ and $0\to N\to B'\to B\to0$ in which $N\subset B'$ is square-zero, $B'$ is an $A'$-algebra and the induced map $I\to N$ equals $c$. Isomorphisms of solutions commute with the maps from $A'$ and to $B$ and are the identity on the identified $N$.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.

If there exists a solution to the square-zero ring-algebra lifting problem specified above, then the set of
isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}, N)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The square-zero algebra lifting problem includes A'→A, A→B, c:I→N and a compatible square-zero extension B'; the isomorphism classes are an Ext^1_B(NL_{B/A},N)-torsor conditional on one solution existing, retaining this essential nonemptiness premise.

phase3.reason: The obstruction class separates square-zero extension isomorphism classes; every Ext¹ class is realized by modifying a chosen polynomial-presentation pushout.

formulation.statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be affine, and let $\mathcal U=\{f_i:U_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ be a finite standard fpqc covering: each $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ is affine, and the map $\coprod_{i=1}^nU_i\to S$ is faithfully flat (equivalently, $R\to\prod_{i=1}^nA_i$ is faithfully flat). Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such datum is effective and the canonical functor $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal U}(\operatorname{QCoh})$ is fully faithful; in fact it is an equivalence.

The draft's faithfully flat finite product ∏A_i retains finiteness, affine objects and both categorical properties.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-fpqc-covering}
Let $S$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to S\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
be a standard fpqc covering of $S$, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-standard-fpqc}.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.

Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item every finite flat quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module is
finite locally free, and
\item every closed subset $Z \subset X$ which is closed under generalizations
is open.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-irreducible-fibres-irreducible-components}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated finite type morphism of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes. Let $\Lambda$ be a torsion ring.

$$
is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case}
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Rf_*$ sends $D_{comp}(\mathcal{D}, \Lambda)$
into $D_{comp}(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$,
\item the map $Rf_* : D_{comp}(\mathcal{D}, \Lambda) \to
D_{comp}(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$ has a left adjoint
$Lf_{comp}^* : D_{comp}(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda) \to
D_{comp}(\mathcal{D}, \Lambda)$ which is $Lf^*$ followed by
derived completion,
\item $Rf_*$ commutes with derived completion,
\item for $K$ in $D_{comp}(\mathcal{D}, \Lambda)$ we have
$Rf_*K = R\lim Rf_*(K \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\Lambda \underline{\Lambda/I^n})$.
\item for $M$ in $D_{comp}(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$ we have
$Lf^*_{comp}M =
R\lim Lf^*(M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\Lambda \underline{\Lambda/I^n})$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex-d1}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$.
Assume $\mathcal{A}$ has countable direct sums.
Let $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ be the spectral sequence
associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map
$$
d_1^{p, q} :
E_1^{p, q} = H^{p + q}(\text{gr}^p(K^\bullet))
\longrightarrow
E_1^{p + 1, q} = H^{p + q + 1}(\text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet))
$$
is equal to the boundary map in cohomology associated to the short
exact sequence of complexes
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet) \to
F^pK^\bullet/F^{p + 2}K^\bullet \to \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet) \to 0.
$$
\item Assume that $d(F^pK) \subset F^{p + 1}K$ for all $p \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Then $d$ induces the zero differential on $\text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)$
and hence
$E_1^{p, q} = \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)^{p + q}$.
Furthermore, in this case
$$
d_1^{p, q} :
E_1^{p, q} = \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)^{p + q}
\longrightarrow
E_1^{p + 1, q} = \text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet)^{p + q + 1}
$$
is the morphism induced by $d$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors}
Let $f : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D$ be an effective Cartier divisor on $S$.
If the pullback of $D$ is defined then
$f^*\mathcal{O}_S(D) = \mathcal{O}_{S'}(f^*D)$
and the canonical section $1_D$ pulls back to

source.label: lemma-homothety-spectrum
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homothety-spectrum}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $N$ be a $S$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$,
\item $\overline{S} = S/\mathfrak m S$ is Noetherian, and
\item $\overline{N} = N/\mathfrak m_R N$ is a finite $\overline{S}$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\Sigma \subset S$ be the multiplicative subset of elements which are not
a zerodivisor on $\overline{N}$. Then $\Sigma^{-1}S$ is a semi-local ring
whose spectrum consists of primes $\mathfrak q \subset S$ contained in an
element of $\text{Ass}_S(\overline{N})$. Moreover, any maximal
ideal of $\Sigma^{-1}S$ corresponds to an associated prime of
$\overline{N}$ over $\overline{S}$.

formulation.statement: Let $A$ be Noetherian, and let $F:D^b_{\rm Coh}(A)\to D^b_{\rm Coh}(A)$ be an **$A$-linear exact equivalence** of triangulated categories, meaning scalar multiplication by every $a\in A$ on morphisms is preserved. Then $F(A[0])$ is *derived-invertible*: it has a two-sided tensor inverse in $(D(A),\otimes_A^{\mathbf L})$; equivalently, $\operatorname{Spec}A$ admits an open cover on each member of which $F(A)$ is isomorphic to a shift of an invertible $A$-module. The local shifts may vary between connected components.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable and quasi-affine,
\item $f$ is quasi-affine,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is quasi-affine, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is quasi-affine.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-ogoma}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $M$ be a finite $A$-module.
Let $S \subset A$ be a multiplicative set. If $\pi \in A$ and
$\Ker(\pi : S^{-1}M \to S^{-1}M) =
\Ker(\pi^2 : S^{-1}M \to S^{-1}M)$
then there exists an $s \in S$ such that for any $n > 0$ we have
$\Ker(s^n\pi : M \to M) = \Ker((s^n\pi)^2 : M \to M)$.

\label{lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Then we have
$$
\begin{matrix}
\text{relative dimension of }f\text{ at }x \\
= \\
\text{dimension of local ring of the fibre of }f\text{ at }x \\
+ \\
\text{transcendence degree of }x/f(x)
\end{matrix}
$$
where the notation is as in
Definition \ref{definition-dimension-fibre}.

hypotheses: C is a site and U∈C is weakly contractible in the sheaf-epimorphism sense.
formulation.statement:
On a site C, an object U is **weakly contractible** if every epimorphism of sheaves of sets F→G induces a surjection on sections F(U)→G(U). This is stronger than topological weak contractibility of a space. For a ringed site (C,O), extension by zero j_{U!}O_U is the left adjoint to localization/restriction at U.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $U$ be a weakly contractible
object of $\mathcal{C}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the functor $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}(U)$ is an exact
functor $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Ab}$,
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$
for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ and all $p \geq 1$, and
\item for any sheaf of groups $\mathcal{G}$ any $\mathcal{G}$-torsor
has a section over $U$.
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: The source deduces exactness of evaluation at weakly contractible objects from the defining lifting property, applies vanishing of right-derived functors of an exact functor, and obtains torsor sections from surjectivity.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. The full subcategory
$\text{Ac}(\mathcal{A})$ of $K(\mathcal{A})$ consisting of acyclic complexes
is a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory of $K(\mathcal{A})$.
The corresponding saturated multiplicative system (see
Lemma \ref{lemma-operations})
of $K(\mathcal{A})$ is the set $\text{Qis}(\mathcal{A})$
of quasi-isomorphisms. In particular, the kernel of the localization
functor $Q : K(\mathcal{A}) \to \text{Qis}(\mathcal{A})^{-1}K(\mathcal{A})$
is $\text{Ac}(\mathcal{A})$ and the functor $H^0$ factors through $Q$.

**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A ring map is **ind-étale** when its target is a filtered colimit of étale algebras over the source.

Let $A \to B$ and $A \to A'$ be ring maps. Let $B' = B \otimes_A A'$
be the base change of $B$.
If $A \to B$ is ind-\'etale, then $A' \to B'$ is ind-\'etale.

\label{lemma-base-change-ind-etale}
Let $A \to B$ and $A \to A'$ be ring maps. Let $B' = B \otimes_A A'$
be the base change of $B$.
If $A \to B$ is ind-\'etale, then $A' \to B'$ is ind-\'etale.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometric-lift-to-usual}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\overline{x} : \Spec(k) \to X$ be a geometric point of $X$
lying over $x \in |X|$. Let $\varphi : U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism
of algebraic spaces and let $u \in |U|$ with $\varphi(u) = x$.
Then there exists a geometric point
$\overline{u} : \Spec(k) \to U$ lying over $u$ with
$\overline{x} = \varphi \circ \overline{u}$.

conclusions: The category of O-modules which are direct summands of finite free O-modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective R-modules.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site and R=Γ(C,O).
formulation.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), the monoidal category (D(O),⊗^L_O,O) contains an **invertible** object M when some N satisfies M⊗^L_O N≅O (and equivalently N⊗^L_O M≅O). An invertible O_n-module is an O_n-module locally free of rank 1. A family (O_n) of ring sheaves giving O≅∏_nO_n is *locally finite* when after a covering of each site object only finitely many component rings remain nonzero; shifts H^n[-n] are in the cohomological convention. A direct summand of a finite free O-module need not be globally free. Put R=Γ(C,O) the global section ring, and let global sections act on O-summands.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Set $R = \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. The category of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules which are summands of finite free
$\mathcal{O}$-modules is equivalent to the category of
finite projective $R$-modules.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For R=Γ(C,O), modules which are direct summands of finite free O-modules are categorically equivalent to finite projective R-modules, via global sections and extension of scalars. No assertion that all locally free finite sheaves are globally summands is introduced.

phase3.reason: The proof identifies finite projective modules with finite-free summands and constructs inverse equivalences via global sections and the ringed-topos pullback from the punctual topos.

\label{lemma-category-summands-finite-free}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Set $R = \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. The category of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules which are summands of finite free
$\mathcal{O}$-modules is equivalent to the category of
finite projective $R$-modules.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-presentation-flat-along-fibre}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at every point of the fibre $X_s$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an elementary \'etale neighbourhood
$(S', s') \to (S, s)$ and a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d] & X' \ar[l]^g \ar[d] \\
S & S' \ar[l]
}
$$
such that $g$ is \'etale, $X_s \subset g(X')$, the schemes
$X'$, $S'$ are affine, and such that
$\Gamma(X', g^*\mathcal{F})$ is a projective
$\Gamma(S', \mathcal{O}_{S'})$-module.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of ringed spaces.
If $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$ is a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules,

$\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.

In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms has **effective fppf descent** when objects of that type with suitable descent data descend effectively, in addition to being stable under arbitrary base change and fppf-local on the base. The five listed conditions are simultaneous, not alternatives.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $G \to F$ be a transformation of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is preserved under any base change, fppf local on the
base, and morphisms of type $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy descent for fppf coverings,
see Descent, Definition \ref{descent-definition-descending-types-morphisms},
\item $G$ is a sheaf,
\item $F$ is an algebraic space,
\item there exists a $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a surjective \'etale morphism $U \to F$ such that
$V = G \times_F U$ is representable, and
\item $V \to U$ has $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $G$ is an algebraic space, $G \to F$ is representable and has property
$\mathcal{P}$.

source.label: lemma-morphism-sheaves-with-P-effective-descent-etale
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-sheaves-with-P-effective-descent-etale}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $G \to F$ be a transformation of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is preserved under any base change, fppf local on the
base, and morphisms of type $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy descent for fppf coverings,
see Descent, Definition \ref{descent-definition-descending-types-morphisms},
\item $G$ is a sheaf,
\item $F$ is an algebraic space,
\item there exists a $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a surjective \'etale morphism $U \to F$ such that
$V = G \times_F U$ is representable, and
\item $V \to U$ has $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $G$ is an algebraic space, $G \to F$ is representable and has property
$\mathcal{P}$.

formulation.statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. (1) For every eligible $\tau$, passing from quasi-coherent sheaves to the associated big-site sheaves commutes with pullback, and the same holds on the small Zariski and étale sites: $f_{\mathrm{site}}^*(\mathcal G^a)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^a$. (2) The analogous big-site pushforward compatibility is false in general (and $f_*$ need not preserve quasi-coherence). (3) If $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale}\}$ both $f_*$ on schemes and $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on small sites preserve quasi-coherent sheaves, and $f_{\mathrm{small},*}(\mathcal F^a)\cong(f_*\mathcal F)^a$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$.

source.label: proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial}
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The equivalences of categories of
Proposition \ref{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent}
are compatible with pullback.
More precisely, we have $f^*(\mathcal{G}^a) = (f^*\mathcal{G})^a$
for any quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $S$.
\item The equivalences of categories of
Proposition \ref{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent} part (1)
are {\bf not} compatible with pushforward in general.
\item If $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and
$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale\}$ then $f_*$ and $f_{small, *}$
preserve quasi-coherent sheaves and the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_T)
\ar[rr]_{f_*} \ar[d]_{\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}^a} & &
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)
\ar[d]^{\mathcal{G} \mapsto \mathcal{G}^a} \\
\QCoh(T_\tau, \mathcal{O}) \ar[rr]^{f_{small, *}} & &
\QCoh(S_\tau, \mathcal{O})
}
$$
is commutative, i.e., $f_{small, *}(\mathcal{F}^a) = (f_*\mathcal{F})^a$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain}
\begin{slogan}
Short exact sequences of complexes give rise to long exact sequences
of (co)homology.
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Suppose that
$$
0 \to
A^\bullet \to
B^\bullet \to
C^\bullet \to
0
$$
is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then there is a long exact cohomology sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \ar[lld] \\
H^i(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
H^{i + 1}(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\
}
$$
The construction produces long exact cohomology sequences
which are functorial in the short exact
sequence and compatible with shifts as in
Definition \ref{definition-cohomology-shift}.

The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. For finite-length $R$-module $M$ and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:M\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=\psi\varphi=0$ and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, call $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex. Define the determinant symbol $d_M(a,b)=\det_\kappa(M/abM,a,b)\in\kappa^\times$. Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

For finite-length $R$-module $M$ and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:M\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=\psi\varphi=0$ and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, call $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex. With $I_\varphi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, $I_\psi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, put $K_\varphi=\ker\varphi=I_\psi$, $K_\psi=\ker\psi=I_\varphi$. Let $\gamma_\varphi:\det K_\varphi\otimes\det I_\varphi\to\det M$, $\gamma_\psi:\det K_\psi\otimes\det I_\psi\to\det M$ be the determinant isomorphisms and $\sigma$ swap the tensor factors. Define $\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)\in\kappa^\times$ as the unique scalar such that $\gamma_\psi\circ\sigma\circ\gamma_\varphi^{-1}$ acts on $\det M$ by $(-1)^{\ell(I_\varphi)\ell(I_\psi)}\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)$.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $\kappa$. If $M$ is a finite $A$-module whose support has Krull dimension one and $a,b\in A$ are nonzerodivisors on $M$, the quotient $M/abM$ has finite length and multiplication by $a,b$ defines an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex on it. Define the determinant symbol $d_M(a,b)=\det_\kappa(M/abM,a,b)\in\kappa^\times$. For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $A$, use $d_A(a,b)$ for the special case $M=A$, and write $\operatorname{ord}_A(b)=\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$ for a nonzero nonunit $b$ (extended with value zero for units).

Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $a, b, c \in A$. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module
with $\dim(\text{Supp}(M)) = 1$. Assume $a, b, c$ are nonzerodivisors on $M$.
Then
$$
d_M(a, bc) = d_M(a, b) d_M(a, c)
$$
and $d_M(a, b)d_M(b, a) = 1$.

\label{lemma-multiplicativity-symbol}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $a, b, c \in A$. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module
with $\dim(\text{Supp}(M)) = 1$. Assume $a, b, c$ are nonzerodivisors on $M$.
Then
$$
d_M(a, bc) = d_M(a, b) d_M(a, c)
$$
and $d_M(a, b)d_M(b, a) = 1$.

formulation.statement:
**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A **w-local** spectral space has closed closed-point set and unique closed specialization of each point; a w-local map is spectral and maps closed points to closed points. An **ind-étale** map is a filtered colimit of étale algebras. A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction.

Let $A$ be a ring. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible,
\item every faithfully flat, ind-\'etale ring map $A \to B$ has
a retraction, and
\item $A$ satisfies
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Spec(A)$ is w-local,
\item $\pi_0(\Spec(A))$ is extremally disconnected, and
\item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m \subset A$ the
local ring $A_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.
formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

Let $A \to B$ be a local complete intersection map.
Then $L_{B/A}$ is a perfect complex with tor amplitude in $[-1, 0]$.

The proposed definitions of perfect and Tor-amplitude describe exactly the source target properties, without weakening to ordinary cohomological bounds alone.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
The blowing up $b : X' \to X$ of $Z$ in $X$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $b|_{b^{-1}(X \setminus Z)} : b^{-1}(X \setminus Z) \to X \setminus Z$
is an isomorphism,
\item the exceptional divisor $E = b^{-1}(Z)$ is an effective Cartier divisor
on $X'$,
\item there is a canonical isomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_{X'}(-1) = \mathcal{O}_{X'}(E)$
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: A generator supplies one map escaping each proper subobject of M; their direct sum surjects onto M with the required size bound, yielding a set of bounded-size isomorphism classes.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-alteration-dimension-general}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume
$Y$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ is locally of finite type.
Then
$$
\dim(X) \leq \dim(Y) + E
$$
where $E$ is the supremum of the transcendence degrees of
$\xi/f(\xi)$ where $\xi$ runs through the points at
which the local ring of $X$ has dimension $0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dimension}
Suppose that $k$ is a field and suppose that $V$ is a nonzero vector
space over $k$. Assume the dimension of $V$ (which is a cardinal number)
is smaller than the cardinality of $k$. Then for any linear operator
$T : V \to V$ there exists some monic polynomial $P(t) \in k[t]$ such that
$P(T)$ is not invertible.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-separated-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be any of the separation
axioms of Definition \ref{definition-separated}.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is $\mathcal{P}$,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and morphism $Z \to Y$ the
base change $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ of $f$ is $\mathcal{P}$,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$ the
base change $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ of $f$ is $\mathcal{P}$,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$ the
algebraic space $Z \times_Y X$ is $\mathcal{P}$ (see
Properties of Spaces, Definition \ref{spaces-properties-definition-separated}),
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that the base change $V \times_Y X \to V$ has
$\mathcal{P}$, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that each
of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ has $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}
