Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Assume we have disjoint union decompositions
$X = \coprod_{i \in I} X_i$ and $Y = \coprod_{j \in J} Y_j$
by open and closed subschemes
and a map $a : I \to J$ of sets such that $f(X_i) \subset Y_{a(i)}$.

$$

Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.

$$

Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski site. Consider a cartesian diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
T' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & T \ar[d]^f \\

and $g_{big}^{-1} \circ f_{big, *} = f'_{big, *} \circ (g'_{big})^{-1}$.

formulation.statement:
For an $\mathcal O_X$-module F, $F^*=\mathcal Hom(F,\mathcal O_X)$ and reflexive means the evaluation map $F\to F^{**}$ is an isomorphism. The rank-one reflexive group law is $[F][G]=[(F\otimes G)^{**}]$. Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a rank 1 coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$. Let
$$
U = \{x \in X \mid s : \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{F}_x
\text{ is an isomorphism}\}
$$
Then $j : U \to X$ is an open subscheme of $X$ and
$$
j_*\mathcal{O}_U =
\colim (\mathcal{O}_X \xrightarrow{s} \mathcal{F}
\xrightarrow{s} \mathcal{F}^{[2]}
\xrightarrow{s} \mathcal{F}^{[3]}
\xrightarrow{s} \ldots)
$$
where $\mathcal{F}^{[1]} = \mathcal{F}$ and
inductively $\mathcal{F}^{[n + 1]} =
(\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{F}^{[n]})^{**}$.

source.label: lemma-structure-sheaf-Xs
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-structure-sheaf-Xs}
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a rank 1 coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$. Let
$$
U = \{x \in X \mid s : \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{F}_x
\text{ is an isomorphism}\}
$$
Then $j : U \to X$ is an open subscheme of $X$ and
$$
j_*\mathcal{O}_U =
\colim (\mathcal{O}_X \xrightarrow{s} \mathcal{F}
\xrightarrow{s} \mathcal{F}^{[2]}
\xrightarrow{s} \mathcal{F}^{[3]}
\xrightarrow{s} \ldots)
$$
where $\mathcal{F}^{[1]} = \mathcal{F}$ and
inductively $\mathcal{F}^{[n + 1]} =
(\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{F}^{[n]})^{**}$.

\label{lemma-check-after-closed}
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $i : X \to Y$ be a closed immersion
of schemes locally of finite type over $S$. Let $r \geq 0$.
Let $\alpha$ be a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$.
Then $\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$ if and only if
$i_*\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle on $Y/S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-frobenius}
Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $S$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$.
Then the relative frobenius $F_{X/S} : X \to X^{(p)}$
is a universal homeomorphism, is integral, and
induces purely inseparable residue field extensions.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-algebraization}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Set $S = \Spec(A)$ and $S_n = \Spec(A/I^n)$. Consider a commutative
diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1 \ar[r]_{i_1} \ar[d] & X_2 \ar[r]_{i_2} \ar[d] & X_3 \ar[r] \ar[d] &
\ldots \\
S_1 \ar[r] & S_2 \ar[r] & S_3 \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
of schemes with cartesian squares. Suppose given $(\mathcal{L}_n, \varphi_n)$
where each $\mathcal{L}_n$ is an invertible sheaf on $X_n$ and
$\varphi_n : i_n^*\mathcal{L}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{L}_n$
is an isomorphism. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X_1 \to S_1$ is proper, and
\item $\mathcal{L}_1$ is ample on $X_1$
\end{enumerate}
then there exists a proper morphism of schemes $X \to S$
and an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{L}$
and isomorphisms $X_n \cong X \times_S S_n$ and
$\mathcal{L}_n \cong \mathcal{L}|_{X_n}$ compatible with
the morphisms $i_n$ and $\varphi_n$.

\label{lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation}
Let $(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let
$\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. If $\mathcal{G}$ is finite type, then
$\Coker(\varphi)$ is finitely presented.

\label{lemma-sheafify-abelian-presheaf}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian presheaf on $X$.
Then there exists a unique structure of
abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{F}^\#$ such that
$\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}^\#$ is a morphism
of abelian presheaves. Moreover, the following adjointness
property holds
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PAb}(X)}(\mathcal{F}, i(\mathcal{G}))
=
\Mor_{\textit{Ab}(X)}(\mathcal{F}^\#, \mathcal{G}).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors-union}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $D, D' \subset X$ be effective Cartier divisors
such that the scheme theoretic intersection $D \cap D'$ is an effective
Cartier divisor on $D'$. Then $D + D'$ is the scheme theoretic
union of $D$ and $D'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-closed-proper-over-base}
Consider a cartesian diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_{g'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
with $f$ locally of finite type.
If $Z$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$, then
$(g')^{-1}(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X'$ proper over $S'$.

formulation.statement:
A norm of degree $d$ for a finite morphism $\pi:X\to Y$ means $d\geq1$ and a multiplicative sheaf map $N:\pi_*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ with $N(\pi^\sharp g)=g^d$, and such that for every open $V\subset Y$ and $a\in\Gamma(\pi^{-1}V,\mathcal O_X)$ vanishing at $x$, $N(a)$ vanishes at $\pi(x)$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $p$ be a prime number such that
$p\mathcal{O}_X = 0$. Then for some $e > 0$ there exists a norm
of degree $p^e$ for $X_{red} \to X$ where $X_{red}$ is the reduction
of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Frobenius-gives-norm-for-reduction}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $p$ be a prime number such that
$p\mathcal{O}_X = 0$. Then for some $e > 0$ there exists a norm
of degree $p^e$ for $X_{red} \to X$ where $X_{red}$ is the reduction
of $X$.

conclusions: K^vee:=RSheafHom(K,O) is perfect and the double dual (K^vee)^vee≅K.
For every M there is a natural isomorphism M⊗^L_O K^vee≅RSheafHom(K,M).
The associated map H^0(C,M⊗^L_O K^vee)≅Hom_{D(O)}(K,M) is an isomorphism of groups.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, K∈D(O) is perfect and M∈D(O).
formulation.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), the monoidal category of complexes uses total tensor with signed differential, and the symmetric monoidal category D(O) uses derived tensor ⊗^L with Koszul signs. A *left dual* of K is an object K^vee with coevaluation η:O→K⊗K^vee and evaluation ε:K^vee⊗K→O satisfying both triangular identities (using the relevant underived or derived tensor). For perfect K, K^vee=RSheafHom(K,O), and for a chain complex locally strictly perfect the ordinary Hom complex supplies its candidate dual. For any **perfect derived** K, the derived dual K^vee:=RSheafHom(K,O) is again perfect; the formulas are functorial in every M∈D(O), and the H^0 equality is a group-level global-section equality.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Then $K^\vee = R\SheafHom(K, \mathcal{O})$ is a
perfect object too and $(K^\vee)^\vee \cong K$. There are
functorial isomorphisms
$$
M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee = R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(K, M)
$$
and
$$
H^0(\mathcal{C}, M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K, M)
$$
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For perfect K, derived dual K^vee=RSheafHom(K,O) is perfect with canonical double-dual identification; for all derived M, M⊗^L K^vee≅RSheafHom(K,M), inducing degree-zero global Hom isomorphism. All separate source statements retained.

phase3.reason: The proof reduces locally to strictly perfect representatives, dualizes finite locally projective terms, identifies bidual evaluation termwise and proves the tensor–internal-Hom comparison through finite-free direct summands.

\label{lemma-dual-perfect-complex}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Then $K^\vee = R\SheafHom(K, \mathcal{O})$ is a
perfect object too and $(K^\vee)^\vee \cong K$. There are
functorial isomorphisms
$$
M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee = R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(K, M)
$$
and
$$
H^0(\mathcal{C}, M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K, M)
$$
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$.

source.label: lemma-pre-delta-invariant
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pre-delta-invariant}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a reduced Nagata $1$-dimensional local ring.
Let $A'$ be the integral closure of $A$ in the total ring of fractions
of $A$. Then $A'$ is a normal Nagata ring, $A \to A'$ is finite, and
$A'/A$ has finite length as an $A$-module.

source.label: lemma-isomorphism
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-isomorphism}
Let $S$ be a scheme, let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$.
If $(\mathcal{F}, \alpha)$ is a quasi-coherent module on $(U, R, s, t, c)$
then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism.

\item $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'} = g_*\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$
and $g^\sharp$ is the obvious map,

\label{lemma-morphism-ringed-topoi-comes-from-morphism-ringed-sites}

be a morphism of ringed topoi. There exists a factorization
$$
\xymatrix{

\ar[rr]_{(f, f^\sharp)}
\ar[d]_{(g, g^\sharp)}
& &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \ar[d]^{(e, e^\sharp)}
\\
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'})
\ar[rr]^{(h, h^\sharp)} & &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
}
$$
where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C}')$
is an equivalence of topoi induced by a special cocontinuous functor
$\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{C}'$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-special-cocontinuous-functor}),
\item $e : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D}')$
is an equivalence of topoi induced by a special cocontinuous functor
$\mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}'$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-special-cocontinuous-functor}),
\item $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'} = g_*\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$
and $g^\sharp$ is the obvious map,
\item $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'} = e_*\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$
and $e^\sharp$ is the obvious map,
\item the sites $\mathcal{C}'$ and $\mathcal{D}'$ have final objects
and fibre products (i.e., all finite limits),
\item $h$ is a morphism of sites induced by a continuous functor
$u : \mathcal{D}' \to \mathcal{C}'$ which commutes with all finite limits
(i.e., it satisfies the assumptions of
Sites, Proposition \ref{sites-proposition-get-morphism}), and
\item given any set of sheaves $\mathcal{F}_i$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{G}_j$)
on $\mathcal{C}$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{D}$) we may assume each of these is
a representable sheaf on $\mathcal{C}'$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{D}'$).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $(f, f^\sharp)$ is an equivalence of ringed topoi,
then we can choose the diagram such that
$\mathcal{C}' = \mathcal{D}'$,
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'} = \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'}$
and $(h, h^\sharp)$ is the identity.

\label{lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r] \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}

\item if $\mathcal{F}$ is an abelian sheaf, then
$R^if'_{small, *}(\mathcal{F}|_{X'}) = (R^if_{small, *}\mathcal{F})|_{Y'}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $K$ be a field and $A,B\subset K$ subrings with fraction field $K$; put $R=A\cap B$. The map $A\otimes B\to K$ means multiplication (tensor over $\mathbf Z$ when no base subscript is supplied). In this setup assume that $B$ is a valuation ring.
Then for every unit $u$ of $A$ either $u \in R$ or $u^{-1} \in R$.

formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of varieties
with $Y$ proper and $X$ a curve.
There exists a factorization $X \to \overline{X} \to Y$
where $X \to \overline{X}$ is an open immersion
and $\overline{X}$ is a projective curve.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Every morphism from a curve to a proper variety factors through an open immersion of X into a projective curve over the same target. The proposal preserves properness and projective completion.

and $\overline{X}$ is a projective curve.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-serre-subcategory-is-kernel}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory.
There exists an abelian category $\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}$
and an exact functor
$$
F : \mathcal{A} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}
$$
which is essentially surjective and whose kernel is $\mathcal{C}$.
The category $\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}$ and the functor $F$ are
characterized by the following universal property: For any exact
functor $G : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ such that
$\mathcal{C} \subset \Ker(G)$ there exists a factorization
$G = H \circ F$ for a unique exact functor
$H : \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{B}$.

\label{lemma-quasi-affine-permanence}
Suppose $g : X \to Y$ is a morphism of schemes over $S$.
If $X$ is quasi-affine over $S$ and $Y$ is quasi-separated over $S$,
then $g$ is quasi-affine. In particular, any morphism from a
quasi-affine scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-affine.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-put-in-T}
Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_{Zar}$.
The functor $T_{Zar} \to (\Sch/S)_{Zar}$
is cocontinuous and induces a morphism of topoi
$$
i_f :
\Sh(T_{Zar})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_{Zar})
$$
For a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $(\Sch/S)_{Zar}$
we have the formula $(i_f^{-1}\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
The functor $i_f^{-1}$ also has a left adjoint $i_{f, !}$ which commutes
with fibre products and equalizers.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes. Assume
$Y$ irreducible with generic point $\eta$. If $X_\eta = \emptyset$
then there exists a nonempty open $V \subset Y$ such that
$X_V = V \times_Y X = \emptyset$.

formulation.statement:
For a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$, the Čech cohomology $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ is cohomology of the complex of compatible products of sections on iterated fibre products. The word injective refers to injectivity in the **sheaf** category $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective abelian sheaf, i.e., an injective
object of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.
Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: The Čech cohomology of an injective abelian SHEAF on a covering of U has degree-zero group I(U) and vanishing positive degrees; no assumption of presheaf injectivity substituted.

phase3.reason: The proof uses injectivity of the sheaf as a presheaf and the previously established derived Čech vanishing for injective presheaves, with H⁰ from the sheaf condition.

Let $\pi : X \to Y$ be a nonconstant morphism of smooth projective curves

\pi^* : H^2_\etale(Y, \mu_n) \longrightarrow H^2_\etale(X, \mu_n)

is given by multiplication by the degree of $\pi$.

Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. Assume $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering and each $X_i\to S_i$ is quasi-affine, meaning that locally on the base the source is quasi-compact and an open subscheme of an affine scheme over that base. Then the descent datum $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is effective. In particular, the relative affine hulls $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_i}((p_i)_*\mathcal O_{X_i})$ descend by affine descent, and the compatible quasi-compact open subschemes $X_i$ descend to an open subscheme of the resulting affine hull over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is quasi-affine, then the descent datum is
effective.

formulation.statement:
A field extension K/k is separably generated if some transcendence basis B makes K/k(B) separable algebraic. It is separable in the source sense if every finitely generated intermediate extension over k is separably generated. Let $K/k$ be a separably generated, and finitely generated
field extension.
Set $r = \text{trdeg}_k(K)$. Then there exist elements
$x_1, \ldots, x_{r + 1}$ of $K$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x_1, \ldots, x_r$ is a transcendence basis of $K$ over $k$,
\item $K = k(x_1, \ldots, x_{r + 1})$, and
\item $x_{r + 1}$ is separable over $k(x_1, \ldots, x_r)$.
\end{enumerate}

of divided power rings. Let $(B(1), J(1), \delta(1))$ be the coproduct
of $(B, J, \delta)$ with itself over $(A, I, \gamma)$, i.e.,
such that
$$
\xymatrix{
(B, J, \delta) \ar[r] & (B(1), J(1), \delta(1)) \\

$$
\Omega_{B/A, \delta} = K/ \left(K^2 + (K \cap J(1))^{[2]}\right)

canonically.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-ringed}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and $f \in \mathcal{O}(U)$
there exists a covering $\{U_j \to U\}$ such that for each $j$
either $f|_{U_j}$ is invertible or $(1 - f)|_{U_j}$ is invertible.
\item For $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, $n \geq 1$, and
$f_1, \ldots, f_n \in \mathcal{O}(U)$ which generate the unit ideal
in $\mathcal{O}(U)$ there exists a covering $\{U_j \to U\}$
such that for each $j$ there exists an $i$ such that $f_i|_{U_j}$
is invertible.
\item The map of sheaves of sets
$$
(\mathcal{O} \times \mathcal{O})
\amalg
(\mathcal{O} \times \mathcal{O})
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{O} \times \mathcal{O}
$$
which maps $(f, a)$ in the first component to $(f, af)$ and
$(f, b)$ in the second component to $(f, b(1 - f))$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-residue-field-quasi-finite}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
If $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then the residue field
extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

Under the stated base assumptions, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ be a perfect object whose Chern classes are
defined. Then $c_i(E^\vee) = (-1)^i c_i(E)$, $P_i(E^\vee) = (-1)^iP_i(E)$,

\label{lemma-surjective-pic-birational-finite}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes. Assume there
exists an open $V \subset Y$ such that $f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is an
isomorphism and $Y \setminus V$ is a discrete space. Then every
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module is the pullback of an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.

hypotheses: For algebraic spaces $Z\to B$ and $X\to B$ over $S$, the relative morphism functor $\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,X)$ sends a scheme $T$ over $S$ to pairs $(a:T\to B,\ b:Z_T:=T\times_BZ\to X_T:=T\times_BX\text{ over }T)$. It is an fppf sheaf. For a base change $B'\to B$, write $Z'=B'\times_BZ$, $X'=B'\times_BX$; then the analogous relative functor $\operatorname{Mor}_{B'}(Z',X')$ is the pullback over $B'$.

For a finite locally free morphism $Z\to U$ and an étale algebraic-space morphism $W\to Z$, the functor of sections $F(T)=\{\sigma:Z\times_UT\to W\times_UT\mid\sigma\text{ is a section over }Z\times_UT\}$ on $U$-schemes is an fppf sheaf. formulation.statement:
For algebraic spaces $Z\to B$ and $X\to B$ over $S$, the relative morphism functor $\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,X)$ sends a scheme $T$ over $S$ to pairs $(a:T\to B,\ b:Z_T:=T\times_BZ\to X_T:=T\times_BX\text{ over }T)$. It is an fppf sheaf. For a base change $B'\to B$, write $Z'=B'\times_BZ$, $X'=B'\times_BX$; then the analogous relative functor $\operatorname{Mor}_{B'}(Z',X')$ is the pullback over $B'$.

For a finite locally free morphism $Z\to U$ and an étale algebraic-space morphism $W\to Z$, the functor of sections $F(T)=\{\sigma:Z\times_UT\to W\times_UT\mid\sigma\text{ is a section over }Z\times_UT\}$ on $U$-schemes is an fppf sheaf. If $W\to Z$ is surjective, sections exist étale-locally on $U$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \to B$ and $X' \to X \to B$ be morphisms of
algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X' \to X$ is \'etale, and
\item $Z \to B$ is finite locally free.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathit{Mor}_B(Z, X') \to \mathit{Mor}_B(Z, X)$ is representable
by algebraic spaces and \'etale. If $X' \to X$ is also surjective,
then $\mathit{Mor}_B(Z, X') \to \mathit{Mor}_B(Z, X)$ is surjective.

phase3.reason: A pullback of the relative Hom map is identified with the étale section functor for W→Z_U; its representability and conditional surjectivity follow from the earlier two lemmas.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bounded}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
is bounded above, then
$K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
is uniformly bounded above for all $n$.
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I})$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$ for all $n$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-make-spectral-space-minus}
Let $X$ be a spectral space. Let $E \subset X$ be a constructible subset.
Let $W \subset X$ be the set of points of $X$ which specialize
to a point of $E$. Then $W \setminus E$ is a spectral space.
If $W = \bigcap U_i$ with $U_i$ as in
Lemma \ref{lemma-make-spectral-space}
(\ref{item-intersection-quasi-compact-open})
then $W \setminus E = \lim (U_i \setminus E)$.

For an unbounded derived object $K\in D(\mathcal O)$, $H^q(K)$ is its cohomology sheaf, whereas $H^q(U,K)$ is cohomology of derived sections over $U$. The assertion compares them under vanishing of **higher sheaf cohomology of every cohomology sheaf** over a covering family of objects.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $K$
be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a subset. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item $H^p(U, H^q(K)) = 0$ for all $p > 0$, $q \in \mathbf{Z}$, and
$U \in \mathcal{B}$.

Then $H^q(U, K) = H^0(U, H^q(K))$ for $q \in \mathbf{Z}$
and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-over-U-trivial}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $K$
be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a subset. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item $H^p(U, H^q(K)) = 0$ for all $p > 0$, $q \in \mathbf{Z}$, and
$U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^q(U, K) = H^0(U, H^q(K))$ for $q \in \mathbf{Z}$
and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.

conclusions: $Y$ is w-local: it is spectral, its closed-point subset is closed, and each point specializes to exactly one closed point.
hypotheses: $X$ is spectral, its closed points $X_0$ form a closed subset, and every point of $X$ specializes to a unique closed point.
$Y\subseteq X$ is a closed subspace.
formulation.statement:
For a topological space $Z$, $\pi_0(Z)$ is its space of connected components. A spectral space is **w-local** when its closed-point subset $Z_0$ is closed and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a continuous map between w-local spaces is **w-local** if it is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. This is terminology, not an additional ambient hypothesis.

Let $X$ be a spectral space such that its set of closed points $X_0$ is closed and each $x\in X$ specializes to a unique closed point. If $Y$ is a closed subspace of $X$, then $Y$ is spectral, its set of closed points is closed in $Y$, and every point of $Y$ specializes to a unique closed point; equivalently, $Y$ is w-local.

phase3.reason: For closed Y⊂X, the closed-point set is Y∩X_0, hence closed. Every y∈Y specializes in X to its unique closed point, which remains in Y since Y is closed; this point is closed in Y.

\label{lemma-reduced-finite-irreducible}
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme such that any quasi-compact open
has a finite number of irreducible components. Let $X^0$ be the set
of generic points of irreducible components of $X$. Then we have
$$
\mathcal{K}_X =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\kappa(\eta) =
\prod\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\kappa(\eta)
$$
where $j_\eta : \Spec(\kappa(\eta)) \to X$ is the canonical map
of Schemes, Section \ref{schemes-section-points}. Moreover
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{K}_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-algebras,
\item for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the sheaf
$$
\mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{F}) =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{F}_\eta =
\prod\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{F}_\eta
$$
of meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{F}$
is quasi-coherent,
\item $\mathcal{S}_x \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is the set of nonzerodivisors for any $x \in X$,
\item $\mathcal{K}_{X, x}$ is the total quotient ring of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
for any $x \in X$,
\item $\mathcal{K}_X(U)$ equals the total quotient ring of $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
for any affine open $U \subset X$,
\item the ring of rational functions of $X$ is the ring of meromorphic
functions on $X$, in a formula: $R(X) = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{K}_X)$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$, then it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes. Equivalently, for every base change $T'\to T$ and every test scheme $Z$, every family of maps $h_i:T_i\times_TT'\to Z$ whose restrictions agree on all pairwise fibre products $(T_i\times_TT')\times_{T'}(T_j\times_TT')$ comes from a unique map $h:T'\to Z$. Thus every representable presheaf $\operatorname{Hom}(-,Z)$ on schemes satisfies fpqc descent.

The proposal correctly expresses the equalizer/gluing property for all base changes and all TEST SCHEMES.

\label{lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms}
Let $\{T_i \to T\}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Then $\{T_i \to T\}$ is a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-universal-effective-epimorphisms}.
In other words, every representable functor on the category of schemes
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-sheaf-property-fpqc}.

A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. Then
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A N$ defines a functor
$$
- \otimes_A N :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})})
$$ by passing to closed degree-zero maps and homotopy classes.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tensor}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. Then
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A N$ defines a functor
$$
- \otimes_A N :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})})
$$
by an application of Lemma \ref{lemma-functorial}.

\label{lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1}
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian affine scheme of finite dimension.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring which is torsion.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, locally constant sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on an open subscheme $U \subset \mathbf{A}^1_Y$.
Then $Rf_!\mathcal{F}$ has constructible cohomology sheaves where
$f : U \to Y$ is the structure morphism.

\label{lemma-integral-going-up}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map such that
$S$ is integral over $R$.
Let $\mathfrak p \subset \mathfrak p' \subset R$
be primes. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime of $S$ mapping
to $\mathfrak p$. Then there exists a prime $\mathfrak q'$
with $\mathfrak q \subset \mathfrak q'$
mapping to $\mathfrak p'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-jacobson-equivalent-constructible}
Suppose $X$ is a Jacobson topological space.
Let $X_0$ be the set of closed points of $X$.
There is a bijective, inclusion preserving correspondence
$$
\{\text{constructible subsets of } X\}
\leftrightarrow
\{\text{constructible subsets of } X_0\}
$$
given by $E \mapsto E \cap X_0$. This correspondence preserves
the subset of retrocompact open subsets, as well as complements
of these.

Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$
be a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let

is a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
Let $U$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : \mathcal{S}_U \to \mathcal{X}$ be a surjective smooth morphism.
Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be the groupoid in algebraic spaces
and $f_{can} : [U/R] \to \mathcal{X}$ be the result of applying

\begin{enumerate}
\item the morphisms $s$, $t$ are smooth, and
\item the $1$-morphism $f_{can} : [U/R] \to \mathcal{X}$
is an equivalence.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-homotopy
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homotopy}
Let $f^0, f^1 : V \to U$ be maps of simplicial sets.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item The maps $f^j_i : V_i \to U_i$, $j = 0, 1$ are equal for $i < n$.
\item The canonical morphism $U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n U$
is an isomorphism.
\item The canonical morphism $V \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n V$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f^0$ is homotopic to $f^1$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, smooth morphism all of whose fibres are nonempty and equidimensional of the same dimension $n\geq0$.
There exists a trace morphism in $D(\mathcal O_S)$
$$t:Rf_*\Omega^n_{X/S}[n]\longrightarrow\mathcal O_S,$$
unique up to precomposition with multiplication by a unit of $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For every $p$ with $0\leq p\leq n$, composing the relative cup product with $t$ gives a perfect pairing of perfect complexes on $S$:
$$Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}^{\mathbf L}Rf_*\Omega^{n-p}_{X/S}[n]\longrightarrow\mathcal O_S.$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L5659–5677 in the SAME relative-duality situation establishes trace t:Rf_*Ω^n[n]→O_S UNIQUE up to precomposition by unit of H^0(X,O_X), such that for all meaningful 0≤p≤n the induced CUP PRODUCT pairing Rf_*Ω^p⊗^L Rf_*Ω^{n−p}[n]→O_S is PERFECT. The proposal correctly reconstructs the inherited situation and uniqueness group; it does not claim a uniquely normalized canonical trace.

phase3.reason: Over a Noetherian base, relative Grothendieck duality identifies the smooth relative dualizing complex with Omega^n[n], and wedge-duality of differential bundles yields perfect relative Hodge cup pairings. Noetherian approximation plus proper smooth derived base change extends existence to qcqs S. The trace is unique up to a global unit via the finite étale f_*O_X and its perfect dual pairing with R^n f_*Omega^n; the source has minor internal Hom notation slips.

\label{lemma-relative-duality-hodge}
In Situation \ref{situation-relative-duality} there exists an
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module map
$$
t : Rf_*\Omega^n_{X/S}[n] \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_S
$$
unique up to precomposing by multiplication by a unit of
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ with the following property: for all $p$ the pairing
$$
Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S}^\mathbf{L}
Rf_*\Omega^{n - p}_{X/S}[n]
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{O}_S
$$
given by the relative cup product composed with $t$
is a perfect pairing of perfect complexes on $S$.

A constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf is the $I$-adic inverse limit of its constructible reductions; lisse means reductions locally constant; adic lisse means locally completed constant finite-type reduction.

Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$.
Then there exists a finite partition $X = \coprod X_i$ by
locally closed subschemes such that the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_{X_i}$
is lisse.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Noetherian-constructible}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$.
Then there exists a finite partition $X = \coprod X_i$ by
locally closed subschemes such that the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_{X_i}$
is lisse.

Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$.
Let $f, g : X \to Y$ be morphisms over $S$. Let $x \in X$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the structure morphism $Y \to S$ is unramified,
\item $f(x) = g(x)$ in $Y$, say $y = f(x) = g(x)$, and
\item the induced maps $f^\sharp, g^\sharp : \kappa(y) \to \kappa(x)$
are equal.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$ on which
$f$ and $g$ are equal.

source.label: lemma-value-at-one-point
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-value-at-one-point}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$.
Let $f, g : X \to Y$ be morphisms over $S$. Let $x \in X$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the structure morphism $Y \to S$ is unramified,
\item $f(x) = g(x)$ in $Y$, say $y = f(x) = g(x)$, and
\item the induced maps $f^\sharp, g^\sharp : \kappa(y) \to \kappa(x)$
are equal.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$ on which
$f$ and $g$ are equal.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-covering-by-formal-algebraic-spaces}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\{X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of maps
of sheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Assume (a) $X_i$ is a
formal algebraic space over $S$, (b) $X_i \to X$ is representable
by algebraic spaces and \'etale, and (c) $\coprod X_i \to X$
is a surjection of sheaves. Then $X$ is a formal algebraic space
over $S$.

A complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of modules is K-injective if $\mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet[n])=0$ for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ and every integer $n$; such complexes compute unbounded right derived functors. conclusions:
any decent algebraic
space locally of finite type over $X$ is universally catenary.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent, locally Noetherian, and
universally catenary algebraic space over $S$. Then any decent algebraic
space locally of finite type over $X$ is universally catenary.

formulation.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $S$ a scheme of characteristic $p$, and $X\to S$ a smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Let $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$ and let $F_{X/S}:X\to X^{(p)}$ denote relative Frobenius. Then $F_{X/S}$ is finite syntomic. Let
$$\Theta_{X/X^{(p)}}:F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X^{(p)}/S}$$
be its relative de Rham trace map. All graded components of this map vanish except in degree $d$; in degree $d$ the map $F_{X/S,*}\Omega^d_{X/S}\to\Omega^d_{X^{(p)}/S}$ is surjective.

Relative Frobenius X→X^(p) is finite SYNTOMIC; its Garel de Rham trace vanishes in all form degrees ≠d and is SURJECTIVE in form degree d. The reconstruction retains surjectivity only in the top degree and does not mistake Frobenius for an étale morphism.

phase3.reason: Establishes relative Frobenius finite syntomic by fibrewise flatness and lci permanence, then reduces étale locally to coordinatewise p-th powers on affine space. A characteristic-zero universal trace computation shows degree-i trace values are multiples of p^(d−i), vanishing modulo p for i<d; in top degree the surviving monomial traces span all top forms. Exterior degrees >d are zero.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Garel-map-frobenius-smooth-char-p}
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $X \to S$ be a smooth morphism
of relative dimension $d$ of schemes in characteristic $p$.
The relative Frobenius $F_{X/S} : X \to X^{(p)}$ of $X/S$
(Varieties, Definition \ref{varieties-definition-relative-frobenius})
is finite syntomic and the corresponding map
$$
\Theta_{X/X^{(p)}} :
F_{X/S, *}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{X^{(p)}/S}
$$
is zero in all degrees except in degree $d$ where it defines a
surjection.

conclusions: Dualizing complex condition ascends and descends under these covers.
hypotheses: f surjective locally Noetherian, syntomic or flat lci or finite-type Gorenstein; K in D_QCoh(Y).
formulation.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism of locally Noetherian schemes satisfying at least one of: (i) $f$ syntomic (flat lfp lci); (ii) $f$ flat and a local complete intersection; (iii) $f$ a finite-type Gorenstein morphism (flat with Gorenstein fibres). For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the complex $K$ is dualizing on $Y$ iff its derived pullback $Lf^*K$ is dualizing on $X$. The assertion includes both ascent and descent; no properness of $f$ is imposed.

It asserts a genuine BIDIRECTIONAL dualizing-complex test K dualizing on Y iff Lf^*K dualizing on X for all K in D_QCoh(Y). The final correctly preserves the three alternative sufficiency guards and does not require properness.

formulation.statement:
Let $R \to S$ be a flat ring map.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to S$ is faithfully flat,
\item the induced map on $\Spec$ is surjective, and
\item any closed point $x \in \Spec(R)$ is
in the image of the map $\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-CM}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. If $A$ has a dualizing complex
$\omega_A^\bullet$, then
$\{\mathfrak p \in \Spec(A) \mid A_\mathfrak p\text{ is Cohen-Macaulay}\}$
is a dense open subset of $\Spec(A)$.

\label{lemma-rank-additive}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme.
Let $0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{F}'' \to 0$
be a short  exact sequence of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Then the rank of $\mathcal{F}'$ is the sum of the ranks of
$\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}''$.

\label{lemma-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension}
Let $X$ be a scheme over the field $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a field extension.
Then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ if and only if
$X_{k'}$ is geometrically connected over $k'$.

Proper means universally closed, separated, and of finite type, jointly.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rr]_h \ar[rd]_f & & Y \ar[ld]^g \\
& B
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to B$ is a proper morphism,
\item $Y \to B$ is separated and locally of finite type,
\end{enumerate}
Then the scheme theoretic image $Z \subset Y$ of $h$
is proper over $B$ and $X \to Z$ is surjective.

phase3.reason: Proper X→B and separated locally finite-type Y→B make h:X→Y quasi-compact. Its scheme-theoretic image Z receives a dense image of X, which is also closed by universal closedness of h, hence X→Z is surjective. The preceding proper-image lemma yields Z proper over B.

\label{lemma-find-strictly-standard}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_m)$.
Let $\mathfrak q \subset A$ be a prime ideal. Assume $R \to A$ is smooth
at $\mathfrak q$. Then there exists an $a \in A$, $a \not \in \mathfrak q$,
an integer $c$, $0 \leq c \leq \min(n, m)$, subsets
$U \subset \{1, \ldots, n\}$, $V \subset \{1, \ldots, m\}$
of cardinality $c$ such that
$$
a = a' \det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j \in V, i \in U}
$$
for some $a' \in A$ and
$$
a f_\ell \in (f_j, j \in V) + (f_1, \ldots, f_m)^2
$$
for all $\ell \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$.

conclusions: Two pre-rigidity identities and a quadratic rigidity isomorphism for omega.
hypotheses: f proper flat finite presentation over qcqs Y; omega=a_f(O_Y), c right adjoint of diagonal pushforward.
formulation.statement:
Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Write $X\times_YX$ for the fibre square, $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2:X\times_YX\to X$ for its two projections, and $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$ for the diagonal. Let $c:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X\times_YX})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $R\Delta_*$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_X)$:
\[
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet})
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(L\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}),
\]
and
\[
\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}
c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X\times_YX}}^{\mathbf L}L\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}).
\]
The statement uses the right adjoint for the *diagonal*, not for $f$ itself, and the two projections are taken on the fibre product.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L2941 (Rigidity) assumes f proper flat finite-presentation over qcqs Y, ω=a_f(O_Y), and c RIGHT ADJOINT to RΔ_* for Δ:X→X×_Y X. The final statement reproduces BOTH pre-rigid identities O_X≅c(Lpr_1^*ω)≅c(Lpr_2^*ω) AND the quadratic rigid ω≅c(Lpr_1^*ω⊗^L Lpr_2^*ω). It uses c for the diagonal, not for f.

phase3.reason: Writes the rigid dualizing comparison as four successive functorial equalities under diagonal and base change; each equality is supplied by the identified adjunction/base-change lemma.

formulation.statement:
A module $M$ over $R$ is flat if and only if
every relation in $M$ is trivial.
Every relation is trivial means: for every $n\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in M$ with $\sum_i f_i x_i=0$, there exist $m\geq0$, $y_1,\ldots,y_m\in M$ and $a_{ij}\in R$ such that $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ for every $i$ and $\sum_i f_i a_{ij}=0$ for every $j$.

A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
If $X$ is smooth and $k(Y) \subset k(X)$ is purely inseparable,
then there is a unique $n \geq 0$ and a unique isomorphism $Y = X^{(p^n)}$
such that $f$ is the $n$-fold relative Frobenius of $X/k$.

\label{lemma-purely-inseparable-smooth}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
If $X$ is smooth and $k(Y) \subset k(X)$ is purely inseparable,
then there is a unique $n \geq 0$ and a unique isomorphism $Y = X^{(p^n)}$
such that $f$ is the $n$-fold relative Frobenius of $X/k$.

\label{lemma-fibre-product-spaces}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F \to H$, $G \to H$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.

in the category of algebraic spaces over $S$.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.

$\Lambda$-modules (with $\Lambda$ Noetherian) on $X_\etale$.
If there exist constructible locally closed subschemes $T_i \subset X$

hypotheses: A *constructible locally closed subscheme* $T\subset X$ is a locally closed subscheme whose underlying subset is **constructible** (a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact opens). On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* if on **every affine open** it admits a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata $T_i$ on which the sheaf is **finite locally constant**. If $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules is *constructible* if the restrictions on those strata are **finite type locally constant** (finitely generated $\Lambda$-fibres), possibly of infinite cardinality. A *weak Serre* subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions, whereas the stronger Serre condition also includes **arbitrary subobjects and quotients** of its objects.

\label{lemma-separated-over-separated}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Y$ is separated and $f$ is separated, then $X$ is separated.
\item If $Y$ is quasi-separated and $f$ is quasi-separated, then
$X$ is quasi-separated.
\item If $Y$ is locally separated and $f$ is locally separated, then
$X$ is locally separated.
\item If $Y$ is separated over $S$ and $f$ is separated, then
$X$ is separated over $S$.
\item If $Y$ is quasi-separated over $S$ and $f$ is quasi-separated, then
$X$ is quasi-separated over $S$.
\item If $Y$ is locally separated over $S$ and $f$ is locally separated, then
$X$ is locally separated over $S$.
\end{enumerate}

on a scheme $X$. Then
\begin{enumerate}

\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_x \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) \not = 0.
$$

$\text{Supp}(f^*\mathcal{F}) = f^{-1}(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The support of $\mathcal{F}$ is closed.
\item For $x \in X$ we have
$$
x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_x \not = 0
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_x \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) \not = 0.
$$
\item For any morphism of schemes $f : Y \to X$ the pullback
$f^*\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type as well and we have
$\text{Supp}(f^*\mathcal{F}) = f^{-1}(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-surjective}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : T \to X$ be a morphism from a scheme to $X$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f : T \to X$ is surjective (according to
Spaces, Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}),
and
\item $|f| : |T| \to |X|$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.

For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

For a proper $d$-dimensional $k$-scheme $Z$ and invertible $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_d$, the numerical intersection $(\mathcal L_1\cdots\mathcal L_d\cdot Z)$ is the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_d$ in the degree-$d$ polynomial $\chi(Z,\mathcal L_1^{\otimes n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_d^{\otimes n_d})$. For an ample $\mathcal L$, $\deg_{\mathcal L}(Z)$ is $d!$ times the leading coefficient of $\chi(Z,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$.
formulation.statement:
A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

For a proper $d$-dimensional $k$-scheme $Z$ and invertible $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_d$, the numerical intersection $(\mathcal L_1\cdots\mathcal L_d\cdot Z)$ is the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_d$ in the degree-$d$ polynomial $\chi(Z,\mathcal L_1^{\otimes n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_d^{\otimes n_d})$. For an ample $\mathcal L$, $\deg_{\mathcal L}(Z)$ is $d!$ times the leading coefficient of $\chi(Z,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme of dimension $d$.
Let $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_d$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Then
$$
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) =
\deg(
c_1(\mathcal{L}_1) \cap \ldots \cap c_1(\mathcal{L}_d) \cap [Z]_d)
$$
where the left side is the mixed intersection number given by the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_d$ in the degree-$d$ Euler-characteristic polynomial.
In particular,
$$
\deg_\mathcal{L}(Z) = \deg(c_1(\mathcal{L})^d \cap [Z]_d)
$$
if $\mathcal{L}$ is an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset S$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $D \subset S$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
Let $Z' \subset S$ be the closed subscheme cut out by the product
of the ideal sheaves of $Z$ and $D$.
Let $S' \to S$ be the blowup of $S$ in $Z$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The blowup of $S$ in $Z'$ is isomorphic to $S' \to S$.
\item Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $\mathcal{F}$
be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. If $\mathcal{F}$ has
no nonzero local sections supported in $f^{-1}D$, then the
strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$ relative to the blowing up
in $Z$ agrees with the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$ relative
to the blowing up of $S$ in $Z'$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-strict-transform-different-centers
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-strict-transform-different-centers}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset S$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $D \subset S$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
Let $Z' \subset S$ be the closed subscheme cut out by the product
of the ideal sheaves of $Z$ and $D$.
Let $S' \to S$ be the blowup of $S$ in $Z$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The blowup of $S$ in $Z'$ is isomorphic to $S' \to S$.
\item Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $\mathcal{F}$
be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. If $\mathcal{F}$ has
no nonzero local sections supported in $f^{-1}D$, then the
strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$ relative to the blowing up
in $Z$ agrees with the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$ relative
to the blowing up of $S$ in $Z'$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
If the extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ of function fields
is purely inseparable, then there exists a factorization
$$
X = X_0 \to X_1 \to \ldots \to X_n = Y
$$
such that each $X_i$ is a proper nonsingular curve
and $X_i \to X_{i + 1}$ is a degree $p$
morphism with $k(X_{i + 1}) \subset k(X_i)$
inseparable.

\label{lemma-slice-smooth-given-element}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point with image $s \in S$.
Let $h \in \mathfrak m_x \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is smooth at $x$, and
\item the image $\text{d}\overline{h}$ of $\text{d}h$ in
$$
\Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) =
\Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x)
$$
is nonzero.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an affine open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
such that $h$ comes from $h \in \Gamma(U, \mathcal{O}_U)$ and such
that $D = V(h)$ is an effective Cartier divisor in $U$ with $x \in D$ and
$D \to S$ smooth.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibred-gives-fibred-groupoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a fibred category.
Let $\mathcal{S}'$ be the subcategory of $\mathcal{S}$ defined
as follows
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Ob(\mathcal{S}') = \Ob(\mathcal{S})$, and
\item for $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{S}')$ the set of morphisms between $x$
and $y$ in $\mathcal{S}'$ is the set of strongly cartesian morphisms between
$x$ and $y$ in $\mathcal{S}$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $p' : \mathcal{S}' \to \mathcal{C}$ be the restriction of $p$
to $\mathcal{S}'$. Then $p' : \mathcal{S}' \to \mathcal{C}$ is fibred
in groupoids.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $p : \Spec(K) \to X$ and $q : \Spec(L) \to X$

phase2.hold_reason: The original assertion is an unconditional biconditional: an open U⊂X is scheme-theoretically dense iff O_X→j_*O_U is injective. The Stage B logical_form labels it single_implication, distorting the two-way result in searchable structure.
phase2.proposed_correction: Set logical_form=equivalence (or explicit equivalence_sides), keep the iff and direct-image injection criteria, and independently review the corrected structured content.

phase3.reason: Injectivity of O_X→j_*O_U is checked on each étale affine chart; it forces the kernel of the chart's restriction to vanish, making U dense scheme-theoretically. Conversely a nonzero local kernel section on an affine chart cuts out a proper closed subscheme containing the image, contradicting density.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $U$ is scheme theoretically dense in $X$ if and only if
$\mathcal{O}_X \to j_*\mathcal{O}_U$ is injective.

Let $V$ be a $k$ vector space. Let $K$ be a central $k$-algebra

$K$-sub vector space. Then $W$ is generated as a left $K$-vector
space by $W \cap (V \otimes 1)$.

source.label: lemma-morphisms-representable-fibred-categories
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphisms-representable-fibred-categories}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ be categories fibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$. Assume that $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$
are representable by objects $X$, $Y$ of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then
$$
\Mor_{\textit{Cat}/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})
\Big/
2\text{-isomorphism}
=
\Mor_\mathcal{C}(X, Y)
$$
More precisely, given $\phi : X \to Y$ there exists a
$1$-morphism $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ which induces
$\phi$ on isomorphism classes of objects and
which is unique up to unique $2$-isomorphism.

\label{lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module of finite presentation. Let
$\mathcal{G} = \colim_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \mathcal{G}_\lambda$
be a filtered colimit of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Then the canonical map
$$
\colim_\lambda \SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_\lambda)
\longrightarrow
\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})
$$
is an isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-compact-generic-point-not-in-image}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes.
Let $\eta \in S$ be a generic point of an irreducible
component of $S$. If $\eta \not \in f(X)$ then there
exists an open neighbourhood $V \subset S$ of $\eta$
such that $f^{-1}(V) = \emptyset$.

\label{lemma-homotopy-colimit}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let
$M_n$ be a system of differential graded modules. Then the derived
colimit $\text{hocolim} M_n$ in $D(A, \text{d})$ is represented
by the differential graded module $\colim M_n$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homological-functor-kernel}
Let $H : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{A}$ be a homological functor of
a pre-triangulated category into an abelian category.
Let $\mathcal{D}'$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$ with objects
$$
\Ob(\mathcal{D}') =
\{X \in \Ob(\mathcal{D}) \mid
H(X[n]) = 0\text{ for all }n \in \mathbf{Z}\}
$$
Then $\mathcal{D}'$ is a strictly full saturated pre-triangulated subcategory
of $\mathcal{D}$. If $\mathcal{D}$ is a triangulated category, then
$\mathcal{D}'$ is a triangulated subcategory.
