\label{proposition-topological-invariance}
Let $X_0 \to X$ be a universal homeomorphism of schemes
(for example the closed immersion defined by a nilpotent sheaf of ideals).
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the \'etale sites $X_\etale$ and $(X_0)_\etale$ are isomorphic,
\item the \'etale topoi $\Sh(X_\etale)$ and $\Sh((X_0)_\etale)$
are equivalent, and
\item $H^q_\etale(X, \mathcal{F}) = H^q_\etale(X_0, \mathcal{F}|_{X_0})$
for all $q$ and
for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be
an open and let $D \subset U$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
If $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all $x \in X \setminus U$,
then there exists an effective Cartier divisor $D' \subset X$
with $D = U \cap D'$.

\label{lemma-two-compactifications}
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme of finite type
and separated over $S$. Let $U = U_1 \cup U_2$ be opens such that
$U_1$ and $U_2$ have compactifications over $S$ and such that
$U_1 \cap U_2$ is dense in $U$. Then $U$ has a compactification over $S$.

\label{lemma-irreducible-polynomial-over-domain}
Let $A$ be a domain with fraction field $K$.
Let $P \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Denote $\overline{K}$ the algebraic closure of $K$.
Assume $P$ is irreducible in $\overline{K}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Then there exists a $f \in A$ such that
$P^\varphi \in \kappa[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ is irreducible for all
homomorphisms $\varphi : A_f \to \kappa$ into fields.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$

\item $\mathcal{F}' \to Rf_*f^*\mathcal{F}'$ is an isomorphism
for $\mathcal{F}' \in \Ob(\mathcal{A}')$.
\end{enumerate}

$f^* : D_{\mathcal{A}'}^+(\mathcal{O}') \to D_\mathcal{A}^+(\mathcal{O})$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-pullback}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f_{small}^{-1} :
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)$
is exact.
\item The functor
$f_{small}^{-1} :
\Sh(Y_\etale)
\to
\Sh(X_\etale)$
is exact, i.e., it commutes with finite limits and colimits, see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-exact}.
\item For any \'etale morphism $V \to Y$ of algebraic spaces
we have $f_{small}^{-1}h_V = h_{X \times_Y V}$.
\item Let $\overline{x} \to X$ be a geometric point.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf on $Y_\etale$.
Then there is a canonical identification
$$
(f_{small}^{-1}\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} = \mathcal{G}_{\overline{y}}.
$$
where $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometrically-normal-in-codim-1}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ be the normalization of $X$.
Let $x \in X$ be a point such that (a) $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is reduced, (b) $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) = 1$, and (c)
for every $x' \in X^\nu$ with $\nu(x') = x$ the extension
$\kappa(x')/k$ is separable. Then $X$ is geometrically reduced at $x$
and $X^\nu$ is geometrically regular at $x'$ with $\nu(x') = x$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-normalization-smooth-localization}
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y_2 \ar[r] \ar[d]_{f_2} & Y_1 \ar[d]^{f_1} \\
X_2 \ar[r]^\varphi & X_1
}
$$
be a fibre square in the category of schemes. Assume $f_1$ is quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and $\varphi$ is smooth.
Let $Y_i \to X_i' \to X_i$ be the normalization of $X_i$ in $Y_i$.
Then $X_2' \cong X_2 \times_{X_1} X_1'$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free sheaf of rank $r$ on $X$.
If $\alpha \sim_{rat} \beta$ are rationally equivalent $k$-cycles
on $X$ then $c_j(\mathcal{E}) \cap \alpha = c_j(\mathcal{E}) \cap \beta$
in $\mathrm{CH}_{k - j}(X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cap-chern-class-factors-rational-equivalence}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free sheaf of rank $r$ on $X$.
If $\alpha \sim_{rat} \beta$ are rationally equivalent $k$-cycles
on $X$ then $c_j(\mathcal{E}) \cap \alpha = c_j(\mathcal{E}) \cap \beta$
in $\CH_{k - j}(X)$.

formulation.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be composable morphisms of ringed topoi, and let $R^q f_*$ and $R^p g_*$ denote their higher direct images. The spectral sequence computes the higher direct images of the composite $g\circ f$, not merely global cohomology. The same construction is asserted for bounded-below complexes in place of a single module.

Let
$f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
and
$g : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{E}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{E})$
be morphisms of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module.
There is a spectral sequence with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal{F})

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\xi \in Y$ be a point.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral,
\item $Y$ is locally Noetherian
\item $f$ is proper, dominant and $R(Y) \subset R(X)$ is finite, and
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}) = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $V \subset Y$ of $\xi$
such that $f|_{f^{-1}(V)} : f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

source.label: lemma-finite-in-codimension-one
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-in-codimension-one}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\xi \in Y$ be a point.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral,
\item $Y$ is locally Noetherian
\item $f$ is proper, dominant and $R(Y) \subset R(X)$ is finite, and
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}) = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $V \subset Y$ of $\xi$
such that $f|_{f^{-1}(V)} : f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper smooth curves over $k$.
Then we can factor $f$ as
$$
X \longrightarrow X^{(p^n)} \longrightarrow Y
$$
where $X^{(p^n)} \to Y$ is a nonconstant morphism of proper smooth curves
inducing a separable field extension $k(X^{(p^n)})/k(Y)$, we have
$$
X^{(p^n)} = X \times_{\Spec(k), F_{\Spec(k)}^n} \Spec(k),
$$
and $X \to X^{(p^n)}$ is the $n$-fold relative frobenius of $X$.

phase3.reason: Chooses the maximal separable intermediate field, realizes it as a nonsingular proper curve by the function-field/model correspondence, and applies the relative-Frobenius factorization lemma to the initial purely inseparable map.

source.label: lemma-characterize-jacobson
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-jacobson}
Let $R$ be a ring. If $R$ is not Jacobson there exist
a prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$, an element $f \in R$
such that the following hold
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathfrak p$ is not a maximal ideal,
\item $f \not \in \mathfrak p$,
\item $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f) = \{\mathfrak p\}$, and
\item $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.
\end{enumerate}
On the other hand, if $R$ is Jacobson, then for any pair $(\mathfrak p, f)$
such that (1) and (2) hold the set $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f)$ is
infinite.

\label{lemma-adjoint-lower-shriek-restrict}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $U \subset X$ be an
open subset. Denote $j : (U, \mathcal{O}_U) \to (X, \mathcal{O}_X)$
the corresponding open immersion. The restriction functor
$D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_U)$ is a right adjoint to
extension by zero $j_! : D(\mathcal{O}_U) \to D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$,
\item if $N' \in D(B, \text{d})$ and
$\Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N'[n]) = 0$ for $n \in \mathbf{Z}$,
then $N' = 0$, and
\item the map $H^k(A) \to \Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N[k])$ is an
isomorphism for all $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tilting-equivalence}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be 
differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$,
\item if $N' \in D(B, \text{d})$ and
$\Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N'[n]) = 0$ for $n \in \mathbf{Z}$,
then $N' = 0$, and
\item the map $H^k(A) \to \Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N[k])$ is an
isomorphism for all $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
$$
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N : D(A, \text{d}) \to D(B, \text{d})
$$
gives an $R$-linear equivalence of triangulated categories.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. Let $U, V$ be quasi-compact disjoint open subschemes of $X$.
Then there exist a $U \cup V$-admissible blowup $b : X' \to X$
such that $X'$ is a disjoint union of open subschemes
$X' = X'_1 \amalg X'_2$ with $b^{-1}(U) \subset X'_1$ and
$b^{-1}(V) \subset X'_2$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rank}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Suppose that the support of $\mathcal{O}_X$ is $X$,
i.e., all stalks of $\mathcal{O}_X$ are nonzero rings.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a locally free sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
There exists a locally constant function
$$
\text{rank}_\mathcal{F} :
X \longrightarrow \{0, 1, 2, \ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}
$$
such that for any point $x \in X$ the cardinality of any
set $I$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to
$\bigoplus_{i\in I} \mathcal{O}_X$ in a neighbourhood
of $x$ is $\text{rank}_\mathcal{F}(x)$.

\label{lemma-affine-map-quasi-compact}
Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map.
The induced continuous map $f : \Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$
is quasi-compact. For any constructible set $E \subset \Spec(R)$
the inverse image $f^{-1}(E)$ is constructible in $\Spec(S)$.

Taking suitable inverse-image open subspaces in the respective irreducible spaces gives mutually inverse morphisms, hence isomorphic nonempty open subspaces; the converse is immediate.

source.label: lemma-birational
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-birational}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic
space over $S$ with $|X|$ and $|Y|$ irreducible.
Then $X$ and $Y$ are birational if and only if
there are nonempty open subspaces $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$
which are isomorphic as algebraic spaces over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-existence-tricky}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let
$\mathcal{I}, \mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals.
Let $X_e \subset X$ be the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal{K}^e$.
Let $\mathcal{I}_e = \mathcal{I}\mathcal{O}_{X_e}$.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ be an object of $\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the functor
$\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_{X_e}) \to \textit{Coh}(X_e, \mathcal{I}_e)$
is an equivalence for all $e \geq 1$, and
\item there exists a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{H}$ on $X$ and a map
$\alpha : (\mathcal{F}_n) \to \mathcal{H}^\wedge$ whose
kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of $\mathcal{K}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ is in the essential image of
(\ref{equation-completion-functor}).

\label{lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs}
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $A = K[[x_1, \ldots, x_n]]$.
Let $L$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$ and $B = L[[x_1, \ldots, x_n]]$.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Cohen ring. Let $C = \Lambda[[x_1, \ldots, x_n]]$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbf{Q} \to A$ is formally smooth in the 
$\mathfrak m_A$-adic topology.
\item $\mathbf{F}_p \to B$ is formally smooth in the 
$\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology.
\item $\mathbf{Z} \to C$ is formally smooth in the
$\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: If $X$ is quasi-compact and the connected components of $X_{\overline k}$ are open, then their set is finite and the Galois action on this discrete set is continuous.
If $X$ is finite type over $k$, then both preceding hypotheses hold.
hypotheses: $k$ is a field, $\overline k$ a separable algebraic closure, and $X$ a $k$-scheme.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, with separable algebraic closure $\overline{k}$.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is quasi-compact, and
\item the connected components of $X_{\overline{k}}$ are open.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})$ is finite, and
\item[(b)] the action of $\text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)$ on
$\pi_0(X_{\overline{k}})$ is continuous.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, assumptions (1) and (2) are satisfied when $X$ is
of finite type over $k$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-directed-colimits-sections}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $I$ be a directed set.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of sheaves of sets
over $I$, see
Categories, Section \ref{categories-section-posets-limits}.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset.
Consider the canonical map
$$
\Psi :
\colim_i \mathcal{F}_i(U)
\longrightarrow
\left(\colim_i \mathcal{F}_i\right)(U)
$$
\begin{enumerate}
\item If all the transition maps are injective then
$\Psi$ is injective for any open $U$.
\item If $U$ is quasi-compact, then $\Psi$ is injective.
\item If $U$ is quasi-compact and all the transition maps are injective
then $\Psi$ is an isomorphism.
\item If $U$ has a cofinal system of open coverings
$\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{j\in J} U_j$ with
$J$ finite and $U_j \cap U_{j'}$ quasi-compact
for all $j, j' \in J$, then $\Psi$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}

X_{k'} \ar[r] \ar[d] &

\Spec(k') \ar[r] &
\Spec(k)
}

\item $k'/k$ is a finite purely inseparable extension of fields,

\item $k'_i/k'$ is a finite separable extension for $i = 1, \ldots, n$,

dimension $\leq 1$ over $k'_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-generically-finite}
Let $f: X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is quasi-compact,
quasi-separated, and locally of finite type. If $\eta$ is a generic point
of an irreducible component of $Y$ such that $f^{-1}(\eta)$ is finite, then
there exists an open $V \subset Y$ containing $\eta$ such that
$f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an index category, i.e., a category. Assume
that for every pair of objects $x, y$ of $\mathcal{I}$
there exist an object $z$ and morphisms $x \to z$ and $y \to z$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ and $N$ are diagrams of sets over $\mathcal{I}$,
then $\colim (M_i \times N_i) \to \colim M_i \times \colim N_i$
is surjective,
\item in general colimits of diagrams of sets over $\mathcal{I}$
do not commute with finite nonempty products.
\end{enumerate}

It concludes (i) the natural map colim(M_i×N_i)→colim M_i×colim N_i of SETS is surjective for two diagrams, and (ii) in general such colimits FAIL to commute with finite nonempty products. source.label: lemma-preserve-products
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-preserve-products}
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an index category, i.e., a category. Assume
that for every pair of objects $x, y$ of $\mathcal{I}$
there exist an object $z$ and morphisms $x \to z$ and $y \to z$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ and $N$ are diagrams of sets over $\mathcal{I}$,
then $\colim (M_i \times N_i) \to \colim M_i \times \colim N_i$
is surjective,
\item in general colimits of diagrams of sets over $\mathcal{I}$
do not commute with finite nonempty products.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functoriality-differentials}
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r]_f & X \ar[d] \\
S' \ar[r] & S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of schemes. The canonical map
$\mathcal{O}_X \to f_*\mathcal{O}_{X'}$ composed with the map
$f_*\text{d}_{X'/S'} : f_*\mathcal{O}_{X'} \to f_*\Omega_{X'/S'}$ is a
$S$-derivation. Hence we obtain a canonical map of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\Omega_{X/S} \to f_*\Omega_{X'/S'}$, and by
adjointness of $f_*$ and $f^*$ a
canonical $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module homomorphism
$$
c_f : f^*\Omega_{X/S} \longrightarrow \Omega_{X'/S'}.
$$
It is uniquely characterized by the property that
$f^*\text{d}_{X/S}(h)$ maps to $\text{d}_{X'/S'}(f^* h)$
for any local section $h$ of $\mathcal{O}_X$.

\label{lemma-hypercovering-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.

$0$ in degrees $> 0$ and equal to $\mathbf{Z}_X^\#$
in degree $0$.

hypotheses: A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology}
Let $X$ be an affine scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists an integral surjective morphism $X' \to X$ such that for
every closed subscheme $Z' \subset X'$, every finite abelian group $M$, and
every $q \geq 1$ we have $H^q_\etale(Z', \underline{M}) = 0$.
\item For any closed subscheme $Z \subset X$, finite abelian group $M$,
$q \geq 1$, and $\xi \in H^q_\etale(Z, \underline{M})$ there exists a
finite surjective morphism $X' \to X$ of finite presentation such that
$\xi$ pulls back to zero in $H^q_\etale(X' \times_X Z, \underline{M})$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-morphism-quotient-topology}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be surjective, closed, continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $T \subset Y$ be a subset. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\overline{T} = f(\overline{f^{-1}(T)})$,
\item $T \subset Y$ is closed if and only if $f^{-1}(T)$ is closed,
\item $T \subset Y$ is open if and only if $f^{-1}(T)$ is open, and
\item $T \subset Y$ is locally closed if and only if
$f^{-1}(T)$ is locally closed.
\end{enumerate}
In particular we see that $f$ is submersive.

\label{lemma-dimension-decent-invariant-under-etale}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be an \'etale morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Let $x \in X$. Then
(1) $\dim_x(X) = \dim_{f(x)}(Y)$ and (2) the dimension of
the local ring of $X$ at $x$ equals the dimension of
the local ring of $Y$ at $f(x)$. If $f$ is surjective, then
(3) $\dim(X) = \dim(Y)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-trivial}
Let $j : U \to X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any quasi-coherent sheaf on $U$ extends to a quasi-coherent
sheaf on $X$.
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{F}|_U$ be a quasi-coherent
subsheaf. There exists a quasi-coherent subsheaf $\mathcal{H}$ of
$\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{H}|_U = \mathcal{G}$
as subsheaves of $\mathcal{F}|_U$.
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $U$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}|_U$ be a morphism
of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules. There exists a quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{H}$
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and a map $\psi : \mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{F}$
such that $\mathcal{H}|_U = \mathcal{G}$ and that
$\psi|_U = \varphi$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
Let $(f_N,f_{M'}):(N_1,M'_1,\varphi_1)\to(N_2,M'_2,\varphi_2)$ be a morphism of compatible triples, so the two component maps commute with the isomorphisms after extension of scalars to $A$. If $f_N:N_1\to N_2$ and $f_{M'}:M'_1\to M'_2$ are surjective, then the induced $B'$-linear map $N_1\times_{\varphi_1,M_1}M'_1\to N_2\times_{\varphi_2,M_2}M'_2$, where $M_i=M'_i/IM'_i$, is surjective.

\label{lemma-cartier-equality}
Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension.
Then $\Omega_{K/k}$ and $H_1(L_{K/k})$ are finite dimensional and
$\text{trdeg}_k(K) = \dim_K \Omega_{K/k} - \dim_K H_1(L_{K/k})$.

hypotheses: Fix $d\ge1$. For a morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids, the relative finite Hilbert stack $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ has over a scheme $U$ objects $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, where $Z\to U$ is finite locally free of constant rank $d$, $y\in\mathcal Y(U)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$, and $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$ is an isomorphism. Morphisms consist of compatible base changes and isomorphisms of the displayed data. The absolute $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X)$ forgets the target $\mathcal Y$, and $\mathcal H_d$ is the finite Hilbert stack of degree-$d$ finite locally free schemes. Natural forgetful maps send $(Z,y,x,\alpha)$ to $y$ and to the underlying $(Z,x)$ respectively.

For $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ representable by algebraic spaces, flat and locally of finite presentation and a relative Hilbert object $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, let $X_y=U\times_\mathcal Y\mathcal X$ be the algebraic space representing the corresponding base change and let $x_\alpha:Z\to X_y$ be the induced map over $U$. The full substack $\mathcal H_{d,\mathrm{lci}}(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ consists of objects for which $x_\alpha$ is both unramified and a local complete intersection morphism (locally it factors as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism).
formulation.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$. For a morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids, the relative finite Hilbert stack $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ has over a scheme $U$ objects $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, where $Z\to U$ is finite locally free of constant rank $d$, $y\in\mathcal Y(U)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$, and $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$ is an isomorphism. Morphisms consist of compatible base changes and isomorphisms of the displayed data. The absolute $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X)$ forgets the target $\mathcal Y$, and $\mathcal H_d$ is the finite Hilbert stack of degree-$d$ finite locally free schemes. Natural forgetful maps send $(Z,y,x,\alpha)$ to $y$ and to the underlying $(Z,x)$ respectively.

For $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ representable by algebraic spaces, flat and locally of finite presentation and a relative Hilbert object $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, let $X_y=U\times_\mathcal Y\mathcal X$ be the algebraic space representing the corresponding base change and let $x_\alpha:Z\to X_y$ be the induced map over $U$. The full substack $\mathcal H_{d,\mathrm{lci}}(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ consists of objects for which $x_\alpha$ is both unramified and a local complete intersection morphism (locally it factors as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism).

Let $U \subset U'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes.
Let $X'$ be an algebraic space flat over $U'$. Set $X = U \times_{U'} X'$.
Let $Z \to U$ be finite locally free of degree $d$. Finally, let
$f : Z \to X$ be unramified and a local complete intersection morphism.
Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
(Z \subset Z') \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_{(f, f')} & & (X \subset X') \ar[ld] \\
& (U \subset U')
}
$$
of algebraic spaces over $U'$ such that $Z' \to U'$ is finite locally free
of degree $d$ and $Z = U \times_{U'} Z'$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The first-order lifting statement assumes an affine first-order thickening U⊂U′, flat X′/U′, a degree-d finite locally free Z/U and an unramified local complete intersection f:Z→X. The proposed diagram preserves existence of Z′ and f′, degree d, commutation, and equality Z=U×_{U′}Z′.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lci-unobstructed}
Let $U \subset U'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes.
Let $X'$ be an algebraic space flat over $U'$. Set $X = U \times_{U'} X'$.
Let $Z \to U$ be finite locally free of degree $d$. Finally, let
$f : Z \to X$ be unramified and a local complete intersection morphism.
Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
(Z \subset Z') \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_{(f, f')} & & (X \subset X') \ar[ld] \\
& (U \subset U')
}
$$
of algebraic spaces over $U'$ such that $Z' \to U'$ is finite locally free
of degree $d$ and $Z = U \times_{U'} Z'$.

\label{lemma-affineline-special}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $f, g \in R[x]$ be polynomials.
Assume the leading coefficient of $g$ is a unit of $R$.
There exists elements $r_i\in R$, $i = 1\ldots, n$ such that
the image of $D(f) \cap V(g)$ in $\Spec(R)$ is
$\bigcup_{i = 1, \ldots, n} D(r_i)$.

conclusions: Gorenstein iff dualizing complex invertible, with local and open-locus claims and O_X normalization.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian; dualizing D_X for part 1, X Gorenstein for part 2.
formulation.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. (1) If $D_X$ is any dualizing complex on $X$, then (a) $X$ is Gorenstein iff $D_X$ is derived-invertible on $X$; (b) for every $x\in X$, the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Gorenstein iff its derived stalk $(D_X)_x$ is an invertible object of $D(\mathcal O_{X,x})$; and (c) the locus of Gorenstein points is an open Gorenstein subscheme. (2) If $X$ is Gorenstein, then the existence of *some* dualizing complex on $X$ is equivalent to the structure complex $\mathcal O_X[0]$ itself being dualizing. The equivalences refer to derived-invertibility, not mere invertibility of a chosen cohomology sheaf unless the complex is concentrated in one degree.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L6182 assumes X LOCALLY NOETHERIAN. Under the EXTRA condition X has dualizing D_X, it states (a) Gorenstein X iff D_X derived-invertible, (b) Gorenstein stalk iff D_X stalk invertible, and (c) Gorenstein locus open. Separately if X Gorenstein, existence of dualizing iff O_X[0] is dualizing. The final preserves the distinct guards and every subclaim, without claiming bare O_X always dualizing.

phase3.reason: Affine local duality reduces the result to the established algebraic Gorenstein criterion.

conclusions: There exists i\ge 0 such that f_i:X_i\to Y_i is syntomic.
hypotheses: I is a directed indexing set, 0\in I, and (S_i)_{i\in I} is an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms.
S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_i.
f_0:X_0\to Y_0 is a morphism of schemes over S_0.
S_0, X_0, Y_0 are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
For every i\ge 0, f_i:X_i\to Y_i is obtained from f_0 by base change along S_i\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is the corresponding base change of f_0 along S\to S_0.
f_0:X_0\to Y_0 is locally of finite presentation.
f:X\to Y is syntomic.
formulation.statement: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). Fix \(0\in I\) and a morphism of \(S_0\)-schemes \(f_0:X_0\to Y_0\) with \(S_0,X_0,Y_0\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each \(i\ge 0\), let \(f_i:X_i\to Y_i\) be the base change of \(f_0\) to \(S_i\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be its base change to \(S\). Suppose \(f_0\) is locally of finite presentation. If \(f\) is syntomic, then there exists \(i\ge 0\) such that \(f_i\) is syntomic.

The reviewed statement correctly imports Situation-descent-property and preserves its existential finite-stage quantifier.

phase3.reason: Syntomicity is affine-local and the local complete intersection algebra criterion descends through finitely presented filtered limits.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A \to B$ and $C \to B$ be $R$-algebra maps.

\begin{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-Noetherian-base-change}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a finitely generated field extension.
Then $X$ is locally Noetherian if and only if $X_{k'}$ is locally
Noetherian.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_T W]_{q+r}$ with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. It also induces a map on Chow groups.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Assume $Y$ is integral and $n = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
Let $s$ be a nonzero meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
Then we have
$$
f^*\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) = \sum n_i\text{div}_{f^*\mathcal{L}|_{X_i}}(s_i)
$$
in $Z_{n + r - 1}(X)$. Here the sum is over the irreducible
components $X_i \subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n + r$,
the section $s_i = f|_{X_i}^*(s)$ is the pullback of $s$, and
$n_i = m_{X_i, X}$ is the multiplicity of $X_i$ in $X$.

\label{lemma-prepare-flat-pullback-cap-c1}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Assume $Y$ is integral and $n = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
Let $s$ be a nonzero meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
Then we have
$$
f^*\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) = \sum n_i\text{div}_{f^*\mathcal{L}|_{X_i}}(s_i)
$$
in $Z_{n + r - 1}(X)$. Here the sum is over the irreducible
components $X_i \subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n + r$,
the section $s_i = f|_{X_i}^*(s)$ is the pullback of $s$, and
$n_i = m_{X_i, X}$ is the multiplicity of $X_i$ in $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dimension-fibre-in-codim-1}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be locally of finite type. Let $x \in X$ be a point
with image $y \in Y$ such that $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is Noetherian of
dimension $\leq 1$. Let $d \geq 0$ be an integer such that for every
generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $X$ which contains
$x$, we have $\dim_\eta(X_{f(\eta)}) = d$. Then $\dim_x(X_y) = d$.

formulation.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. Now full compactness in unbounded D(O) follows because there is **one uniform finite cohomological-dimension bound d for the object U**, in addition to preservation of sums.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object of
$\mathcal{C}$. The $\mathcal{O}$-module $j_!\mathcal{O}_U$ is a
compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$ if there exists an integer $d$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > d$, and
\item the functors $\mathcal{F} \mapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$
commute with direct sums.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: The j_{U!}O_U object is compact in full D(O) if higher H^p(U,F) vanish above one uniform d for all F and each H^p(U,-) commutes with direct sums. Both hypotheses and unbounded conclusion preserved.

phase3.reason: The proof uses finite cohomological dimension and acyclicity of sums of injectives to compute unbounded derived sections termwise on direct sums of K-injective resolutions.

\label{lemma-sum-closed-subschemes-effective-Cartier}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z, Y$ be two closed subschemes of $X$
with ideal sheaves $\mathcal{I}$ and $\mathcal{J}$. If $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{J}$
defines an effective Cartier divisor $D \subset X$, then $Z$ and $Y$
are effective Cartier divisors and $D = Z + Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-locally-quasi-separated-open-dense-scheme}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$. If $X$ is
Zariski locally quasi-separated (for example if $X$ is quasi-separated), then
there exists a dense open subspace $X'$ of $X$ which is a scheme.
More precisely, every point $x \in |X|$ of codimension $0$ on $X$
is contained in $X'$.

formulation.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms such that *all* fibres of $f,g,g\circ f$ are locally Noetherian. Then (1) if $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$, $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (2) if $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein everywhere, then $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein; (3) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$; (4) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $f$ flat everywhere, then $f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $g$ is Gorenstein **at points in the image of $f$**, not necessarily outside that image.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L6358 requires the fibres of f:X→Y, g:Y→Z and gf to be locally Noetherian, and gives FOUR implications. The proposal retains pointwise/local and global composition, the converses subject to f FLAT at x or globally, and correctly restricts the global conclusion for g to the IMAGE of f, not all Y.

source.label: lemma-composition-gorenstein
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-composition-gorenstein}
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms. Assume that the
fibres $X_y$, $Y_z$ and $X_z$ of $f$, $g$, and $g \circ f$ are
locally Noetherian.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ is Gorenstein
at $f(x)$, then $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$.
\item If $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein, then $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein.
\item If $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$,
then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ is Gorenstein at $f(x)$.
\item If $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein and $f$ is flat, then
$f$ is Gorenstein and $g$ is Gorenstein at every point in
the image of $f$.
\end{enumerate}

$$
U = \{x \in X \mid \mathcal{F} \text{ flat at }x \text{ over }Y\}.

is flat over $Y' = Y \times_S S'$, then $U' = U \times_S S'$.

\label{lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I = (f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ be an ideal
of $A$. Set $Z = V(I) \subset \Spec(A)$. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$
R\Gamma_I(A) \to
(A \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} A_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} A_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to
\ldots \to A_{f_1\ldots f_r}) \to R\Gamma_Z(A)
$$
in $D(A)$. If $M$ is an $A$-module, then we have similarly
$$
R\Gamma_I(M) \cong
(M \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} M_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} M_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to
\ldots \to M_{f_1\ldots f_r}) \cong R\Gamma_Z(M)
$$
in $D(A)$.

hypotheses: $R\to A$ is a commutative-ring map and $(N,\varphi)$ a module descent datum satisfying the cocycle identity.
formulation.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. An $A$-module descent datum is an $A$-module $N$ together with an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R A$-modules $\varphi:N\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes_R N$ such that the two induced ways of transporting $N$ across three $A$-factors agree (the usual cocycle identity on $A\otimes_R A\otimes_R A$). Set $B_n=A^{\otimes_R(n+1)}$ for $n\geq0$. For $0\leq i\leq n$, define the $B_n$-module $N_{n,i}=A^{\otimes_R i}\otimes_R N\otimes_R A^{\otimes_R(n-i)}$ with $N$ in tensor position $i$. The descent isomorphism supplies compatible $B_n$-linear identifications $\varphi^n_{ij}:N_{n,i}\to N_{n,j}$ for $i\leq j$, and for an order-preserving map $\beta:[n]\to[m]$ there is a canonical $B_n\to B_m$-semilinear map $N_{\beta,n}:N_{n,n}\to N_{m,\beta(n)}$ sending $1\otimes\cdots\otimes n$ to the corresponding tensor in position $\beta(n)$. Define $N_n=N_{n,n}$ and
$$N_\bullet(\beta)=\varphi^m_{\beta(n),m}\circ N_{\beta,n}:N_n\to N_m.$$
Then $(N_n,N_\bullet(\beta))$ is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial $R$-algebra $B_\bullet$, and the construction is functorial in $(N,\varphi)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L373–384 constructs a cosimplicial (A/R)_•-MODULE from each A/R-module descent datum (N,φ), with N_n=N_{n,n} and maps φ^m_{β(n),m}∘N_{β,n} for EVERY monotone β:[n]→[m]. The proposal preserves the detailed indices and functoriality and does not assume A/R faithfully flat.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descent-datum-cosimplicial}
Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Given a descent datum $(N, \varphi)$ we can associate to it a
cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module $N_\bullet$\footnote{We should really
write $(N, \varphi)_\bullet$.} by the
rules $N_n = N_{n, n}$ and given $\beta : [n] \to [m]$
setting we define
$$
N_\bullet(\beta) = (\varphi^m_{\beta(n)m}) \circ N_{\beta, n} :
N_{n, n} \longrightarrow N_{m, m}.
$$
This procedure is functorial in the descent datum.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-free-open}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is
locally of finite presentation.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
flat over $S$. Then the set
$$
\{x \in X : \mathcal{F}\text{ free in a neighbourhood of }x\}
$$
is open in $X$ and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change
$S' \to S$.

formulation.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, let $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full derived category of complexes with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. A *dualizing complex* $\omega_A^\bullet\in D(A)$ means a bounded complex with finite injective dimension and finitely generated cohomology such that the homothety map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. The functor $\mathbb D_A(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is contravariant. If $\omega_A^\bullet$ is dualizing, then $\mathbb D_A$ defines an exact anti-equivalence $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\to D_{\rm Coh}(A)$, interchanging the bounded-below and bounded-above subcategories and restricting to an anti-equivalence of the bounded coherent subcategory. The evaluation map
\[
K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet),\omega_A^\bullet)
\]
is an isomorphism, natural in every $K\in D_{\rm Coh}(A)$, so $\mathbb D_A^2\simeq\mathrm{id}$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A dualizing complex induces the contravariant RHom anti-equivalence on coherent-derived objects, interchanges bounded-above and bounded-below, restricts to bounded coherent complexes and satisfies biduality. Every conclusion is preserved.

phase3.reason: The preceding finite-Ext lemma makes duality land in coherent derived complexes, and the dualizing evaluation map exhibits D² as the identity, giving the stated anti-equivalences.

source.label: lemma-dualizing
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dualizing}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. If $\omega_A^\bullet$ is a dualizing
complex, then the functor
$$
D : K \longmapsto R\Hom_A(K, \omega_A^\bullet)
$$
is an anti-equivalence $D_{\textit{Coh}}(A) \to D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
which exchanges $D^+_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$ and $D^-_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
and induces an anti-equivalence
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(A) \to D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$.
Moreover $D \circ D$ is isomorphic to the identity functor.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-iff-weakly-adic}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of affine
formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces,
surjective, and flat. Then $X$ is weakly adic
if and only if $Y$ is weakly adic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-closure}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-algebras.
There exists a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-algebras
$\mathcal{A}' \subset \mathcal{A}$ such that
for any affine object $U$ of $X_\etale$ the ring
$\mathcal{A}'(U) \subset \mathcal{A}(U)$ is
the integral closure of $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ in $\mathcal{A}(U)$.

formulation.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $F : D(A, \text{d}) \to D(B, \text{d})$
be an $R$-linear equivalence of triangulated categories. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A = H^0(A)$, and
\item $B$ is K-flat as a complex of $R$-modules.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an $(A, B)$-bimodule $N$ which is compact in $D(B,\mathrm d)$, generates $D(B,\mathrm d)$ in the sense that $\operatorname{Hom}(N,N'[n])=0$ for all $n$ implies $N'=0$, and induces isomorphisms $H^k(A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,\mathrm d)}(N,N[k])$ for every integer $k$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The Rickard-style existence conclusion is under a given R-linear triangulated equivalence F, ordinary dg algebra A concentrated in degree 0 (A=H^0(A)), and B K-flat over R. The proposed N expands 'as in tilting lemma' to compact generator plus all graded self-Ext isomorphisms; it does not claim N represents the original F.

phase3.reason: Taking N=F(A) gives a compact generator with endomorphism dg algebra E whose cohomology is concentrated in degree zero and equals A. Its nonpositive smart truncation E' is quasi-isomorphic both to E and ordinary A; the induced derived equivalences and the composition-of-tensor-functors result strictify a suitable (A,B)-bimodule.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restrict-stabilizer}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$.
Let $g : U' \to U$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $(U', R', s', t', c')$ be the restriction of $(U, R, s, t, c)$ via $g$.
Let $G$ be the stabilizer of $(U, R, s, t, c)$ and let
$G'$ be the stabilizer of $(U', R', s', t', c')$.
Then $G'$ is the base change of $G$ by $g$, i.e.,
there is a canonical identification $G' = U' \times_{g, U} G$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-catenary-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is catenary,
\item there exists an open covering of $S$ all of whose members are
catenary schemes,
\item for every affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset S$ the ring
$R$ is catenary, and
\item there exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup U_i$ such
that each $U_i$ is the spectrum of a catenary ring.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in this case any locally closed subscheme of $S$ is catenary
as well.

\label{lemma-locally-generated-by-r-sections-descends}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be an fpqc covering such that
each $f_i^*\mathcal{F}$ is locally generated by $r$ sections as an
$\mathcal{O}_{X_i}$-module. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is locally generated by
$r$ sections as an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

Definition \ref{definition-weaker-than-canonical},

\coprod\nolimits_{\varphi \in \Mor_\mathcal{C}(V, U)}
\mathcal{G}(V \xrightarrow{\varphi} U),
$$
in other words sheafification is not necessary in
Lemma \ref{lemma-describe-j-shriek}.

\label{lemma-local-finiteness-for-finite-locally-free}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Set $Z = V(I)$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer. If $H^i_Z(A)$ is finite for $0 \leq i \leq n$,
then the same is true for $H^i_Z(M)$, $0 \leq i \leq n$ for
any finite $A$-module $M$ such that $M_f$ is a finite locally free
$A_f$-module for all $f \in I$.

\label{lemma-locally-nilpotent-unit}
Let $R$ be a ring and let $I \subset R$ be a locally nilpotent
ideal.
An element $x$ of $R$ is a unit if and only if the image of $x$
in $R/I$ is a unit.

The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of $X$
in the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}$. If $\mathcal{I}$ is of finite type, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $b : X' \to X$ is a projective morphism, and
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X'}(1)$ is a $b$-relatively ample invertible sheaf.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $Z' \to Z$ be a monomorphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume there exists a field $k$ and a locally finitely presented, surjective,
flat morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to Z$. Then either $Z'$
is empty or $Z' = Z$.

\label{lemma-monomorphism-into-point}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $Z' \to Z$ be a monomorphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume there exists a field $k$ and a locally finitely presented, surjective,
flat morphism $\Spec(k) \to Z$. Then either $Z'$
is empty or $Z' = Z$.

source.label: lemma-partially-defined-adjoint
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-partially-defined-adjoint}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $u : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
If there exists a subset $\mathcal{P} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{B})$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{B}$ is a quotient of an element
of $\mathcal{P}$, and
\item for every $P \in \mathcal{P}$ there exists an object
$Q$ of $\mathcal{A}$ such that
$\Hom_\mathcal{A}(Q, A) = \Hom_\mathcal{B}(P, u(A))$ functorially
in $A$,
\end{enumerate}
then there exists a left adjoint $v$ of $u$.

formulation.statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-finite morphism of Noetherian schemes. For an affine map of Noetherian rings $A\to B$ arising locally from $f$, define $\omega_{B/A}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,A)\otimes_EB$ using a finite $A$-algebra $E$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is an open immersion, and let $\omega_{Y/X}$ be the coherent sheaf formed by gluing these modules. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is a Gorenstein morphism; (2) $f$ is flat and every scheme-theoretic fibre is Gorenstein (equivalently, its local rings are Gorenstein); (3) $f$ is flat and $\omega_{Y/X}$ is an invertible sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules; (4) for every $y\in Y$ there are affine opens $y\in V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $f(V)\subseteq U$, such that $A\to B$ is flat and $\omega_{B/A}$ is invertible as a $B$-module. The invertibility requirement is that the relative dualizing module be locally free of rank one, not merely that it be flat.

The final explicitly defines the relative dualizing module and retains the pointwise local quantifier and invertibility, not mere flatness.

phase3.reason: The dualizing-sheaf comparison reduces the four equivalences to flat quasi-finite Gorenstein duality; the alternate field-fiber proof identifies the dualizing module as Hom_k(B,k).

source.label: lemma-gorenstein-quasi-finite
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gorenstein-quasi-finite}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a quasi-finite morphism of Noetherian schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is Gorenstein,
\item $f$ is flat and the fibres of $f$ are Gorenstein,
\item $f$ is flat and $\omega_{Y/X}$ is invertible
(Remark \ref{remark-relative-dualizing-for-quasi-finite}),
\item for every $y \in Y$ there are affine opens
$y \in V = \Spec(B) \subset Y$, $U = \Spec(A) \subset X$
with $f(V) \subset U$ such that $A \to B$ is flat
and $\omega_{B/A}$ is an invertible $B$-module.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-localize-differentials}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\varphi : \mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings. For any object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$
there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\Omega_{\mathcal{O}_2/\mathcal{O}_1}|_U =
\Omega_{(\mathcal{O}_2|_U)/(\mathcal{O}_1|_U)}
$$
compatible with universal derivations.

\label{lemma-supported-on-closed}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes of finite type over
a scheme $S$. Let $s \in S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
finite type, quasi-coherent sheaf on $Z$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is
(universally) pure along $Z_s$ if and only if $i_*\mathcal{F}$
is (universally) pure along $X_s$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a monoidal category. Let $X$ be an object of
$\mathcal{C}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the functor $L : Y \mapsto X \otimes Y$ is an equivalence,
\item the functor $R : Y \mapsto Y \otimes X$ is an equivalence,
\item there exists an object $X'$ such that
$X \otimes X' \cong X' \otimes X \cong \mathbf{1}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $K, L$ be objects
of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. The construction of $R\SheafHom(K, L)$
commutes with restrictions to opens, i.e.,
for every open $U$ we have
$R\SheafHom(K|_U, L|_U) = R\SheafHom(K, L)|_U$.

Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $L_1 \to L_2 \to \ldots \to L_n$
be a sequence of composable homomorphisms of
differential graded $A$-modules.
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
L_1 \ar[r] &
L_2 \ar[r] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
L_n \\
M_1 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
M_2 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
M_n \ar[u]
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that each $M_i \to M_{i + 1}$
is an admissible monomorphism and each $M_i \to L_i$
is a homotopy equivalence.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sequence-maps-split}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $L_1 \to L_2 \to \ldots \to L_n$
be a sequence of composable homomorphisms of
differential graded $A$-modules.
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
L_1 \ar[r] &
L_2 \ar[r] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
L_n \\
M_1 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
M_2 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
M_n \ar[u]
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that each $M_i \to M_{i + 1}$
is an admissible monomorphism and each $M_i \to L_i$
is a homotopy equivalence.

\label{lemma-proetale-induced}
Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-proetale-site}.
Let $T \in \Ob(\Sch_\proetale)$.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be an arbitrary pro-\'etale covering of $T$.
There exists a covering $\{U_j \to T\}_{j \in J}$ of $T$ in the site
$\Sch_\proetale$ which refines $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-P}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $P$ be a local property of rings.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is locally $P$.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the property
$P(\mathcal{O}_X(U))$ holds.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ satisfies $P$.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is locally $P$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is locally $P$ then every open subscheme
is locally $P$.

\label{lemma-etale-exact-pullback}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be an \'etale morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_Y = \mathcal{O}_X$, and
$f^*\mathcal{G} = f_{small}^{-1}\mathcal{G}$ for any sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules $\mathcal{G}$. In particular,
$f^* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
is exact.

\label{lemma-reduced-normalization}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Assume $X$ is reduced and any quasi-compact open $U \subset X$

$$
where $\mathcal{O}' \subset \mathcal{K}_X$ is the integral

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$.

surjective.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ses-cech-h1}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$. If there exists a cofinal system
of coverings $\mathcal{U}$ of $U$ such that
$\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$,
then the map $\mathcal{G}(U) \to \mathcal{H}(U)$ is
surjective.

\label{lemma-kill-cohomology-class-on-covering}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subspace.
Let $n > 0$ and let $\xi \in H^n(U, \mathcal{F})$.
Then there exists an open covering
$U = \bigcup_{i\in I} U_i$ such that $\xi|_{U_i} = 0$ for
all $i \in I$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-continuous-almost-cocontinuous}
Let $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ be sites.
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor.
Assume that $u$ is continuous and almost cocontinuous.
Then $u^s = u^p : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
commutes with pushouts and coequalizers (and more generally
finite connected colimits).

\label{lemma-push-pull-composition-modules}
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of ringed spaces.
The functors $(g \circ f)_*$ and $g_* \circ f_*$ are equal.
There is a canonical isomorphism of functors
$(g \circ f)^* \cong f^* \circ g^*$.

\label{lemma-ui-completion-direct-sum-into-product}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $A$ be a set.
Assume $R$ is Noetherian and complete with respect to $I$. There is a
canonical map
$$
\left(\bigoplus\nolimits_{\alpha \in A} R\right)^\wedge
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{\alpha \in A} R
$$
from the $I$-adic completion of the direct sum into the product
which is universally injective.

\label{lemma-check-torsion}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is torsion free if and only if
$\mathcal{F}_x$ is a torsion free $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module for all $x \in X$.

phase2.proposed_correction: Add the pinned definition of size from injectives.tex: for every object M in a Grothendieck abelian category, |M| is the cardinality of the set of subobjects of M. Preserve all original quantified conclusions, then independently re-review the amended standalone content.

phase3.reason: The cardinality bounds for subobjects and quotients follow immediately from their defining size function and its monotonicity under subquotients.

$\mathcal{A}$, then $|M'|, |M''| \leq |M|$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X' \to X$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
If $f : Y \to X$ is an envelope, then the base change $f' : Y' \to X'$
of $f$ is an envelope too.

conclusions: A locally separated algebraic space is decent.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

formulation.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. If $f:X\to Y$ is flat and quasi-finite, then the complex $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ has cohomology only in degree zero, so there exists a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\omega_{X/Y}=H^0(f^!\mathcal O_Y)$ with $f^!\mathcal O_Y\simeq\omega_{X/Y}[0]$. The sheaf $\omega_{X/Y}$ is flat over $Y$ via the morphism $f$.

phase3.reason: Flat-shriek vanishing and coherent cohomology of the shriek object give the announced coherent relative dualizing property.

\label{lemma-check-flat-stalks}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Let $\{p_i\}_{i \in I}$ be a conservative family of points of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is flat if and only if $\mathcal{F}_{p_i}$ is
a flat $\mathcal{O}_{p_i}$-module for all $i \in I$.

Let $f : X \to X'$ be a morphism of $D^b(\mathcal{A})$. Let $b \in \mathbf{Z}$
such that $H^i(X) = 0$ for $i > b$ and $H^i(X') = 0$ for $i \geq b$.

source.label: lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an elementary \'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
and an open subscheme
$$
V \subset X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})
$$
which contains the unique point of
$X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$ mapping to $x$
such that the pullback of $\mathcal{F}$ to $V$ is flat over
$\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$.

phase2.hold_reason: The quasi-affine iff is labeled single_implication and retains a raw Section reference. Its added editorial preface also wrongly claims relative Spec factorization uses f_*O_Y for f:X→Y (rather than f_*O_X).

phase3.reason: For a representable morphism, quasi-affineness is defined by quasi-affine scheme maps after affine scheme base changes; the criterion follows directly from the scheme definition.

source.label: lemma-quasi-affine-representable
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then
$f$ is quasi-affine (in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all affine schemes $Z$
and morphisms $Z \to Y$ the scheme $X \times_Y Z$ is quasi-affine.

\label{lemma-finiteness-curves}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $X$ be a separated
scheme of finite type type over $k$ of dimension $\leq 1$.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules
on $X$ which is torsion. Then $H^q_c(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a
finite $\Lambda$-module.

For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free sheaf of rank $r$ on $Y$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\alpha$ be a $k$-cycle on $Y$.
Then
$$
f^*(c_j(\mathcal{E}) \cap \alpha) = c_j(f^*\mathcal{E}) \cap f^*\alpha
$$
