source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-pullback-cap-cj}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free sheaf of rank $r$ on $Y$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\alpha$ be a $k$-cycle on $Y$.
Then
$$
f^*(c_j(\mathcal{E}) \cap \alpha) = c_j(f^*\mathcal{E}) \cap f^*\alpha
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-representable-diagonal-groupoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category fibred in groupoids.
Assume $\mathcal{C}$ has products of pairs of objects and fibre products.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The diagonal $\mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{S} \times \mathcal{S}$
is representable.
\item For every $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$, any $G : \mathcal{C}/U \to \mathcal{S}$
is representable.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-principal-fitting-ideal}
Let $R$ be a local ring. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Let $k \geq 0$.
Assume that $\text{Fit}_k(M) = (f)$ for some $f \in R$.
Let $M'$ be the quotient of $M$ by $\{x \in M \mid fx = 0\}$. Then
$M'$ can be generated by $k$ elements.

\label{lemma-closure-image-product-map}

\label{lemma-cone-koszul-abstract}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\varphi : E \to R$ be an $R$-module map.
Let $f \in R$. Set $E' = E \oplus R$ and define $\varphi' : E' \to R$
by $\varphi$ on $E$ and multiplication by $f$ on $R$.

cone of the map of complexes
$$
f :
K_\bullet(\varphi)
\longrightarrow
K_\bullet(\varphi).
$$

Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

Given a commutative square of ring maps $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$ with maps $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$, functoriality of the simplicial polynomial resolutions induces a canonical morphism $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\to L_{B'/A'}$ in $D(B')$. If the square is Tor-independent, meaning $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'$, this is the canonical base-change comparison.

Let $A\to B$ and $A'\to B'$ be a commutative square of ring maps. If the natural map from the derived tensor product is a quasi-isomorphism
$B \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' = B'$, then the functoriality map
induces an isomorphism
$$
L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} B' \longrightarrow L_{B'/A'}
$$

The hypothesis requires its comparison B⊗_A^L A'→B' to be a quasi-isomorphism; the source concludes the functorial base-change map L_{B/A}⊗_B^L B'→L_{B'/A'} is an isomorphism. The proposal reconstructs the square and Tor-independence condition without requiring A→A' itself flat.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

\label{lemma-decent-specialization}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x, x' \in |X|$ and assume $x' \leadsto x$, i.e., $x$ is a
specialization of $x'$. Then for every \'etale morphism
$\varphi : U \to X$ from a scheme $U$ and any $u \in U$ with
$\varphi(u) = x$, exists a point $u'\in U$, $u' \leadsto u$ with
$\varphi(u') = x'$.

Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Define its *algebraic upper-shriek functor* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ by choosing a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and putting
\[
\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n].
\]
For surjective $\varphi$, one may use $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$ with its natural $A$-action. Different polynomial presentations give isomorphic functors, but the isomorphisms are *not canonical*. Here $D^\pm$ means bounded below/above cohomology, $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}$ means coherent cohomology, and a *perfect* ring map is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension (equivalently $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex after a suitable finite polynomial presentation).

Let $R \to R'$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a perfect ring map
(More on Algebra, Definition
the perfect-map condition stated above)
such that $R'$ and $A$ are tor independent over $R$.
Let $\varphi' : R' \to A' = A \otimes_R R'$ be the map induced by $\varphi$.
Then we have a functorial isomorphism
$$
\varphi^!(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' =
(\varphi')^!(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} R')
$$
for $K$ in $D(R)$.

Tor-independence means Tor_i^R(A,R')=0 for i>0, and A'=A⊗_R R'.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bc}
Let $R \to R'$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a perfect ring map
(More on Algebra, Definition
\ref{more-algebra-definition-pseudo-coherent-perfect})
such that $R'$ and $A$ are tor independent over $R$.
Let $\varphi' : R' \to A' = A \otimes_R R'$ be the map induced by $\varphi$.
Then we have a functorial isomorphism
$$
\varphi^!(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' =
(\varphi')^!(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} R')
$$
for $K$ in $D(R)$.

Let $k$ be a field.
Let $A$ be a finite central simple $k$-algebra.
Let $k'/k$ be a finite field extension.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $k'$ splits $A$, and
\item there exists a finite central simple algebra $B$ similar to $A$
such that $k' \subset B$ and $[B : k] = [k' : k]^2$.
\end{enumerate}
Here, a field extension $k'/k$ splits $A$ if $A\otimes_k k'$ is a matrix algebra over $k'$, and two finite central simple $k$-algebras $A,B$ are similar if $\operatorname{Mat}_n(A)\cong\operatorname{Mat}_m(B)$ as $k$-algebras for some positive integers $n,m$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The pinned source definition at brauer.tex L622–628 says k'/k splits A if A⊗_k k' is a matrix algebra over k'; similarity at L383–388 is matrix-stabilized k-algebra isomorphism. The theorem L634–644 says for finite extension k'/k that splitting is EQUIVALENT to some finite central simple B similar to A containing k' with [B:k]=[k':k]^2. The proposed explicit definitions preserve all quantifiers and the two-way implication.

phase3.reason: The two splitting criteria are proved by centralizers inside End_k(B), a Brauer inverse construction, and a dimension comparison.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ideal-depth-function}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal.
Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module. Let $\mathfrak p \in V(I)$
be a prime ideal. Assume
$e = \text{depth}_{IA_\mathfrak p}(M_\mathfrak p) < \infty$.
Then there exists a nonempty open $U \subset V(\mathfrak p)$
such that $\text{depth}_{IA_\mathfrak q}(M_\mathfrak q) \geq e$
for all $\mathfrak q \in U$.

\label{lemma-silly-silly}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $x \in R$, $I \subset R$ an ideal, and
$\mathfrak p_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$ be prime ideals.
Suppose that $x + I \not \subset \mathfrak p_i$ for
$i = 1, \ldots, r$. Then there exists a $y \in I$
such that $x + y \not \in \mathfrak p_i$ for all $i$.

\label{lemma-cohomology-products}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $I$ be a set.
For $i \in I$ let  $\mathcal{F}_i$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $U \subset X$ be open. The canonical map
$$
H^p(U, \prod\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \in I} H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for $p = 0$ and injective for $p = 1$.

formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $u : M \to N$ be a surjective map of $A$-modules.
If $M$ is projective as an $A$-module, then there exists an ideal
$I \subset A$ such that for any ring map $\varphi : A \to B$
the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u \otimes 1 : M \otimes_A B \to N \otimes_A B$ is an
isomorphism, and
\item $\varphi(I) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $k$ be a field and let $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to Z$ be surjective and flat.
Then any morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(k') \to Z$ where $k'$ is a field is
surjective and flat.

\label{lemma-flat-cover-by-field}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $k$ be a field and let $\Spec(k) \to Z$ be surjective and flat.
Then any morphism $\Spec(k') \to Z$ where $k'$ is a field is
surjective and flat.

The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\operatorname{Spec}(k) \ar[rr] \ar[rd] & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
Assume that the image point $s \in S$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to S$ is
a closed point and that $\kappa(s) \subset k$ is algebraic.
Then the image $x$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ is a closed point of $|X|$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-solution-modulo}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian geometrically regular $k$-algebra.
Let $\mathfrak q \subset \Lambda$ be a prime ideal.
Let $n \geq 1$ be an integer and let
$E \subset \Lambda_\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_\mathfrak q$
be a finite subset.
Then we can find $m \geq 0$ and
$\varphi : k[y_1, \ldots, y_m] \to \Lambda$ with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item setting $\mathfrak p = \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ we have
$\mathfrak q\Lambda_\mathfrak q = \mathfrak p \Lambda_\mathfrak q$
and $k[y_1, \ldots, y_m]_\mathfrak p \to \Lambda_\mathfrak q$ is flat,
\item there is a factorization by homomorphisms of local Artinian rings
$$
k[y_1, \ldots, y_m]_\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^n k[y_1, \ldots, y_m]_\mathfrak p
\to D \to
\Lambda_\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_\mathfrak q
$$
where the first arrow is essentially smooth and the second is flat,
\item $E$ is contained in $D$ modulo $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_\mathfrak q$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-characterize-henselian-pair}
\begin{reference}
\cite[Chapter XI]{Henselian} and \cite[Proposition 1]{Gabber-henselian}
\end{reference}
Let $(A, I)$ be a pair. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(A, I)$ is a henselian pair,
\item given an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ and an $A$-algebra map
$\sigma : A' \to A/I$, there exists an $A$-algebra map $A' \to A$
lifting $\sigma$,
\item for any finite $A$-algebra $B$ the map $B \to B/IB$ induces
a bijection on idempotents,
\item for any integral $A$-algebra $B$ the map $B \to B/IB$ induces
a bijection on idempotents, and
\item (Gabber) $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$ and
every monic polynomial $f(T) \in A[T]$ of the form
$$
f(T) = T^n(T - 1) + a_n T^n + \ldots + a_1 T + a_0
$$
with $a_n, \ldots, a_0 \in I$ and $n \ge 1$ has a root $\alpha \in 1 + I$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in part (5) the root is unique.

hypotheses: $f:R\to S$ is universally injective/pure, and $M$ is an $R$-module.
formulation.statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. For each one of the following properties, $M$ has the property over $R$ if and only if $M\otimes_RS$ has it over $S$: (a) finitely generated; (b) finitely presented; (c) flat; (d) faithfully flat; (e) finite projective (finitely generated projective). The same pure ring map $f$ is used in each assertion.

The theorem L1356–1372 says EACH of finite generation, finite presentation, flat, faithfully flat and FINITE PROJECTIVE descends from M⊗_R S to M and ascends conversely. The proposal restores the standing purity premise for every independent equivalence.

For any scheme $S$, an *Azumaya algebra* $\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of associative unital $\mathcal O_S$-algebras étale locally isomorphic to a matrix algebra $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal O_S^d)$. Its Brauer class is its equivalence class under tensoring with endomorphism algebras of vector bundles, with addition induced by tensor product. An *invertible sheaf* is a locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of rank one; a *finite locally free sheaf of positive rank* is a vector bundle of finite positive rank, and $\mathcal E nd(\mathcal F)=\mathcal S heafHom_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)$ is its **algebra** of endomorphisms, not merely the underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module.

**Statement (source hypotheses preserved):**
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be finite locally
free sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules of positive rank. If there
exists an isomorphism
$\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_S}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}) \cong
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_S}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{G})$ of
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebras, then there exists an invertible sheaf
$\mathcal{L}$ on $S$ such that
$\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{G}$
and such that this isomorphism induces the given isomorphism of
endomorphism algebras.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-end-unique-up-to-invertible}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be finite locally
free sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules of positive rank. If there
exists an isomorphism
$\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_S}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}) \cong
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_S}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{G})$ of
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebras, then there exists an invertible sheaf
$\mathcal{L}$ on $S$ such that
$\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{G}$
and such that this isomorphism induces the given isomorphism of
endomorphism algebras.

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a surjective morphism
of curves over $k$. If $X$ is smooth over $k$ and
$Y$ is normal, then $Y$ is smooth over $k$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A surjective map from a smooth curve to a normal curve over k forces target smoothness. Both the surjectivity and normality hypotheses are retained.

phase3.reason: The proof chooses an arbitrary target point and lifts it by surjectivity, then invokes smooth descent along a flat morphism and the earlier lemma establishing flatness over a normal curve.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a surjective morphism
of curves over $k$. If $X$ is smooth over $k$ and
$Y$ is normal, then $Y$ is smooth over $k$.

\label{lemma-cartesian-cocartesian}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
w\ar[r]^f\ar[d]_g
& y\ar[d]^h\\
x\ar[r]^k
& z
}
$$
be a commutative diagram.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If the diagram is cartesian and $k$ is an epimorphism, 
then the diagram is cocartesian and $f$ is an epimorphism.
\item If the diagram is cocartesian and $g$ is a monomorphism, 
then the diagram is cartesian and $h$ is a monomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-have-functor-other-way
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-have-functor-other-way}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$, and $v : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$
be functors. Assume that $u$ is cocontinuous
and that $v$ is a right adjoint to $u$.
Let $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$ be
the morphism of topoi associated to $u$, see
Lemma \ref{lemma-cocontinuous-morphism-topoi}.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for a sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$ the sheaf
$g_*\mathcal{F}$ is equal to the presheaf $v^p\mathcal{F}$, in other words,
$(g_*\mathcal{F})(V) = \mathcal{F}(v(V))$, and
\item for a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $\mathcal{D}$ we have
$g^{-1}\mathcal{G} = (v_p\mathcal{G})^\#$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-when-gerbe}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{C}$
and $q : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{C}$ be stacks in groupoids.
Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
over $\mathcal{C}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item For some (equivalently any) factorization $F = F' \circ a$ where
$a : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}'$ is an equivalence of categories over
$\mathcal{C}$ and $F'$ is fibred in groupoids, the map
$F' : \mathcal{X}' \to \mathcal{Y}$ is a gerbe (with the topology
on $\mathcal{Y}$ inherited from $\mathcal{C}$).
\item The following two conditions are satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $y \in \Ob(\mathcal{Y})$ lying over
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ there exists a covering
$\{U_i \to U\}$ in $\mathcal{C}$ and objects $x_i$ of $\mathcal{X}$
over $U_i$ such that $F(x_i) \cong y|_{U_i}$ in $\mathcal{Y}_{U_i}$, and
\item for $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$,
$x, x' \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_U)$, and $b : F(x) \to F(x')$ in
$\mathcal{Y}_U$ there exists
a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ in $\mathcal{C}$ and morphisms
$a_i : x|_{U_i} \to x'|_{U_i}$ in $\mathcal{X}_{U_i}$ with
$F(a_i) = b|_{U_i}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$ and set $y = f(x)$.
Assume $f$ and $g$ locally of finite type.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$$
\begin{matrix}
\text{relative dimension of }g \circ f\text{ at }x \\
\leq \\
\text{relative dimension of }f\text{ at }x \\
+ \\
\text{relative dimension of }g\text{ at }y
\end{matrix}
$$
\item equality holds in (1) if for some morphism $\Spec(k) \to Z$
from the spectrum of a field in the class of $g(f(x)) = g(y)$
the morphism $X_k \to Y_k$ is flat at $x$, for example if $f$ is flat at $x$,
\item
$$
\begin{matrix}
\text{transcendence degree of }x/g(f(x)) \\
= \\
\text{transcendence degree of }x/f(x) \\
+ \\
\text{transcendence degree of }f(x)/g(f(x))
\end{matrix}
$$
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category.
Let $x\oplus y$ be a biproduct in $\mathcal{C}$, with canonical inclusions $i:x\to x\oplus y$, $j:y\to x\oplus y$ and projections $p:x\oplus y\to x$, $q:x\oplus y\to y$, satisfying $pi=1_x$, $qj=1_y$, $pj=qi=0$, and $ip+jq=1_{x\oplus y}$. Then $i : x \to x \oplus y$
is a kernel of $q : x \oplus y \rightarrow y$. Dually, $p$ is
a cokernel for $j$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The pinned biproduct has canonical i,j,p,q obeying pi=qj=1, pj=qi=0, ip+jq=1. With those identities the injection i is the universal kernel of q and projection p is the cokernel of j. The expanded setup is source equivalent.

phase3.reason: For qf=0 the proof uses ip+jq=1 to obtain f=i(pf), and pi=1 supplies uniqueness. The cokernel assertion is the dual universal-property argument.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-additive-cat-biproduct-kernel}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category.
Let $x \oplus y$ with morphisms $i, j, p, q$ as in
Lemma \ref{lemma-preadditive-direct-sum}
be a direct sum in $\mathcal{C}$. Then $i : x \to x \oplus y$
is a kernel of $q : x \oplus y \rightarrow y$. Dually, $p$ is
a cokernel for $j$.

Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f_* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is left exact. In fact it commutes with all limits.
\item The functor
$f^* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$

\item Pullback $f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$
on abelian sheaves is exact.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f_* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is left exact. In fact it commutes with all limits.
\item The functor
$f^* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
is right exact. In fact it commutes with all colimits.
\item Pullback $f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$
on abelian sheaves is exact.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-godement-resolution}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. For every sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ there is a resolution
$$
0 \to
\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to \ldots
$$
functorial in $\mathcal{F}$ such that each term
$f_*f^* \ldots f_*f^*\mathcal{F}$ is a flasque
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module and such that for all $x \in X$ the
map
$$
\mathcal{F}_x[0] \to \Big(
(f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to
(f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to
(f_*f^*f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to \ldots
\Big)
$$
is a homotopy equivalence in the category of complexes
of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules.

\label{lemma-etale-neighbourhoods-not-quite-filtered}
Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $s$ be a point of $S$.
The category of \'etale neighborhoods has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}

$s$ in $S$. Then there exists a third \'etale neighborhood
$(U, u)$ and morphisms
$(U, u) \to (U_i, u_i)$, $i = 1, 2$.
\item Let $h_1, h_2: (U, u) \to (U', u')$ be two
morphisms between \'etale neighborhoods of $s$.

fields. Then there exist an \'etale neighborhood $(U'', u'')$ and a morphism
$h : (U'', u'') \to (U, u)$
which equalizes $h_1$ and $h_2$, i.e., such that
$h_1 \circ h = h_2 \circ h$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which
are locally of finite type over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Y$ is separated over $S$ and $Z \subset X$ is a closed subset
proper over $S$, then $f(Z)$ is a closed subset of $Y$ proper over $S$.
\item If $f$ is universally closed and $Z \subset X$ is a
closed subset proper over $S$, then $f(Z)$ is a closed subset
of $Y$ proper over $S$.
\item If $f$ is proper and $Z \subset Y$ is a closed subset
proper over $S$, then $f^{-1}(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X$ proper over $S$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sheaf-subset-stalks}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on the topological space $X$.
For every open $U \subset X$ the map
$$
\mathcal{F}(U)
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{x \in U} \mathcal{F}_x
$$
is injective.

formulation.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. An $R$-module $Q$ is injective if and only if in every
commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathfrak{a} \ar[d] \ar[r] &  Q \\
R \ar@{-->}[ru]
}
$$
for $\mathfrak{a} \subset R$ an ideal, the dotted arrow exists.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-projective-space-bundle-formula}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally
free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of constant rank $r$. Consider the morphism
$p : P = \mathbf{P}(\mathcal{E}) \to X$.
Then the map
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1} H^*_{dR}(X/S)
\longrightarrow
H^*_{dR}(P/S)
$$
given by the rule
$$
(a_0, \ldots, a_{r - 1}) \longmapsto
\sum\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1} c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_P(1))^i \cup p^*(a_i)
$$
is an isomorphism.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

Let $R$ be a local ring with residue field $\kappa$.
Let $u \in R^*$ be a unit.
Let $M$ be a module of finite length over $R$.
Denote $u_M : M \to M$ the map multiplication by $u$.
Then
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(u_M) :
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M)
\longrightarrow
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M)
$$
is multiplication by $\overline{u}^l$ where $l = \text{length}_R(M)$
and $\overline{u} \in \kappa^*$ is the image of $u$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-check-universally-closed-Noetherian}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes.
Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian. Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is universally closed,
\item for every $n$ the morphism
$\mathbf{A}^n \times X \to \mathbf{A}^n \times S$ is closed,
\item for any diagram (\ref{equation-valuative}) there exists some
dotted arrow,
\item for all diagrams (\ref{equation-valuative}) with $A$ a discrete
valuation ring there exists some dotted arrow.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
Let $A$ be Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a proper morphism. Let
$\mathcal{I} = I\mathcal{O}_X$.
Then the functor $\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_X)\longrightarrow\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal{I}),\quad \mathcal{G}\longmapsto (\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{G})_{n\geq 1}$ is fully faithful.

\label{lemma-fully-faithful}
Let $A$ be Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a proper morphism. Let
$\mathcal{I} = I\mathcal{O}_X$.
Then the functor (\ref{equation-completion-functor}) is fully faithful.

Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If there exists an open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ and
strictly perfect complexes $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$ on $U_i$
such that $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$ represents $E|_{U_i}$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$, then $E$ is perfect.
\item If $E$ is perfect, then any complex representing $E$ is perfect.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings}
Let $K$ be a field. Let $A_1, \ldots, A_r \subset K$ be Noetherian
semi-local rings of dimension $1$ with fraction field $K$. If
$A_i \otimes A_j \to K$ is surjective for all $i \not = j$, then
there exists a Noetherian semi-local domain $A \subset K$
of dimension $1$ contained in $A_1, \ldots, A_r$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to A_i$ induces an open immersion $j_i : \Spec(A_i) \to \Spec(A)$,
\item $\Spec(A)$ is the union of the opens $j_i(\Spec(A_i))$,
\item each closed point of $\Spec(A)$ lies in exactly one of these
opens.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-support-quotient}
Let $R$ be a ring and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ is finite then the support
of $M/IM$ is $\text{Supp}(M) \cap V(I)$.
\item If $N \subset M$, then $\text{Supp}(N) \subset
\text{Supp}(M)$.
\item If $Q$ is a quotient module of $M$ then $\text{Supp}(Q) \subset
\text{Supp}(M)$.
\item If $0 \to N \to M \to Q \to 0$ is a short exact sequence
then $\text{Supp}(M) = \text{Supp}(Q) \cup \text{Supp}(N)$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-projection-formula}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})$ and $K \in D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$.
If $K$ is perfect, then
$$
Rf_*E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}} K =
Rf_*(E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}} Lf^*K)
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$.

conclusions: Canonical module support is maximal-dimensional components and satisfies S2.
hypotheses: Normalized Noetherian local A, d=dim A, ω_A=H^{-d} dualizing.
formulation.statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring, with a *normalized* dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$: this is a dualizing complex satisfying $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\kappa[0]$. For an $A$-module $M$ put $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,\omega_A^\bullet)=H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\omega_A^\bullet))$. Let $d=\dim A$ and define the *dualizing module* (canonical module of $A$) by $\omega_A=H^{-d}(\omega_A^\bullet)$, a finite $A$-module. Then (1) $\operatorname{Supp}_A(\omega_A)$ is exactly the union of irreducible components $V(\mathfrak p)$ with $\mathfrak p$ minimal and $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=d$; and (2) $\omega_A$ satisfies Serre condition $(S_2)$ as a module: for every $\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(\omega_A)_{\mathfrak p}\ge\min\{2,\dim\operatorname{Supp}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(\omega_A)_{\mathfrak p}\}$. This is a module statement even if $A$ is not Cohen–Macaulay.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The canonical module H^(−dim A)(ω) is supported on exactly the maximal-dimensional irreducible components and satisfies module Serre S2. Both conclusions and normalization assumptions survive.

phase3.reason: Localizing normalized dualizing complexes determines top-dimensional support; induction on dimension via regular-element quotient and finite-length torsion establishes Serre's S2 depth estimate.

source.label: lemma-depth-dualizing-module

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-image-open-technical}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Assume $f$ is surjective and $f(E) \not = Y$ for all proper
closed subsets $E \subset X$. Then for $U \subset X$ open the subset
$f(U)$ is contained in the closure of $Y \setminus f(X \setminus U)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universal-property-localization-module}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S \subset R$ a multiplicative subset. Let $M$, $N$
be $R$-modules. Assume all the elements of $S$ act as automorphisms on $N$.
Then the canonical map
$$
\Hom_R(S^{-1}M, N) \longrightarrow \Hom_R(M, N)
$$
induced by the localization map, is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-ses-gr}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $A$ be a filtered object and $X \subset A$. Then for each $p$
the sequence
$$

$$
is exact (with induced filtration on $X$ and quotient filtration on $A/X$).
\item Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then for each $p$ the sequences
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coim(f)) \to 0
$$
and
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Im(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
are exact.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-quasi-compact-permanence
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-compact-permanence}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.
If $g \circ f$ is quasi-compact and $g$ is quasi-separated
then $f$ is quasi-compact.

\label{lemma-sheaves-modules-space}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space, see
Sheaves, Section \ref{sheaves-section-ringed-spaces}.
The category of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on $X$
has enough injectives. In fact it has functorial injective embeddings.

The following conditions are equivalent: (1) for every prime $\mathfrak q'\subset S'$ containing $\mathfrak m'S'$, the localization $M'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is flat over $R'$; (2) $\varphi(I)=0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-scheme-over-limit}
Let $I$ be a directed set.
Let $(S_i, f_{ii'})$ be an inverse system of schemes over $I$.
Assume all the morphisms $f_{ii'} : S_i \to S_{i'}$ are affine,
Let $S = \lim_i S_i$. Let $0 \in I$.
Suppose that $T$ is a scheme over $S_0$.
Then
$$
T \times_{S_0} S = \lim_{i \geq 0} T \times_{S_0} S_i
$$

source.label: lemma-split-morphism-splitting
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-split-morphism-splitting}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category,
$x$ and $y$ be objects of $\mathcal{A}$,
and $j : y \to x$ and $q : x \to y$ be morphisms
satisfying $q \circ j = \text{id} _ y$.
If $j \circ q$ has at least one of a kernel or cokernel,
then both (co)kernels exist and
\begin{align*}
x
& \simeq \Ker (j \circ q) \oplus y \\
& \simeq \Coker (j \circ q) \oplus y
\end{align*}
with the structure of either direct product including $j , q$,
and the canonical (co)kernel morphism,
and the remaining map uniquely determined.

\label{lemma-generalization-versality}
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred
in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$ is
representable by algebraic spaces,
\item $\mathcal{X}$ has (RS*),
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is limit preserving.
\end{enumerate}
Let $x$ be an object of $\mathcal{X}$ over a scheme $U$ of finite type over
$S$. Let $u \leadsto u_0$ be a specialization of finite type points of $U$
such that $x$ is versal at $u_0$. Then $x$ is versal at $u$.

\label{lemma-points-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $X = U/R$ be a presentation of $X$, see
Spaces, Definition \ref{spaces-definition-presentation}.
Then the image of $|R| \to |U| \times |U|$ is an equivalence relation
and $|X|$ is the quotient of $|U|$ by this equivalence relation.

source.label: lemma-property-irreducible
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-property-irreducible}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Z_0 \subset X$ be an irreducible closed
subset with generic point $\xi$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of coherent
sheaves on $X$ with support contained in $Z_0$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any short exact sequence of coherent sheaves if two
out of three of them have property $\mathcal{P}$ then so does the
third.
\item For every integral closed subscheme $Z \subset Z_0 \subset X$,
$Z \not = Z_0$ and every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_Z$ we have
$\mathcal{P}$ for $(Z \to X)_*\mathcal{I}$.
\item There exists some coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{G}) = Z_0$,
\item $\mathcal{G}_\xi$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_\xi$,
\item $\dim_{\kappa(\xi)} \mathcal{G}_\xi = 1$, and
\item property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for every coherent sheaf
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ whose support is contained in $Z_0$.

formulation.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. A complex in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is *supported on* a closed subset $T$ if every cohomology sheaf is zero on $Y\setminus T$. If $V\subseteq Y$ is open, $U=f^{-1}(V)$, and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $j':U\hookrightarrow X$, the *restriction comparison* is the natural map $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_{f|_U}(j^*K)$. Then (1) for every closed $T\subseteq Y$, any $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$ has $a_f(Q)$ supported on $f^{-1}(T)$; and (2) for every open $V\subseteq Y$ and every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the natural restriction map $\rho_K:a_f(K)|_{f^{-1}(V)}\to a_{f|_{f^{-1}(V)}}(K|_V)$ is an isomorphism, understood locally on the open $V$ when it is not quasi-compact.

\label{lemma-proper-flat-noetherian-relative}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a perfect proper morphism of Noetherian schemes.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint for
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}. Then
\begin{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tensor-with-finitely-presented}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring and let $M$
and $Q$ be $\Lambda$-modules. If $Q$ is a finitely presented
$\Lambda$-module, then we have
$\underline{M \otimes_\Lambda Q}(U) = \underline{M}(U) \otimes_\Lambda Q$
for all $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.

\label{lemma-characterize-left-exact}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
Suppose all finite limits exist in $\mathcal{A}$,
see Lemma \ref{lemma-finite-limits-exist}.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is left exact,
\item $F$ commutes with finite products and equalizers, and
\item $F$ transforms a final object of $\mathcal{A}$
into a final object of $\mathcal{B}$, and commutes with fibre products.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-remove-embedded-points}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
The set of coherent subsheaves
$$
\{
\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{F}
\mid
\text{Supp}(\mathcal{K})\text{ is nowhere dense in }\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})
\}
$$
has a maximal element $\mathcal{K}$.
Setting $\mathcal{F}' = \mathcal{F}/\mathcal{K}$ we have the
following
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}') = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$,
\item $\mathcal{F}'$ has no embedded associated points, and
\item there exists a dense open $U \subset X$ such that
$U \cap \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ is dense in $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$
and $\mathcal{F}'|_U \cong \mathcal{F}|_U$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjection-space-of-sections}
Let $Z \to U$ be a finite morphism of schemes.
Let $W$ be an algebraic space and let $W \to Z$ be a
surjective \'etale morphism. Then there exists a surjective
\'etale morphism $U' \to U$ and a section
$$
\sigma : Z_{U'} \to W_{U'}
$$
of the morphism $W_{U'} \to Z_{U'}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-locally-free-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable and finite locally free,
\item $f$ is finite locally free,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is finite locally free, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each morphism $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is finite locally free.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-blowup-map-pd1
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowup-map-pd1}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$
be a homorphism of perfect $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of tor dimension $\leq 1$.
Let $U \subset X$ be a scheme theoretically dense open
such that $\mathcal{F}|_U = 0$ and $\mathcal{G}|_U = 0$.
Then there is a $U$-admissible blowup $b : X' \to X$ such that
the kernel, image, and cokernel of $b^*\varphi$ are
perfect $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules of tor dimension $\leq 1$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-acyclic-is-zero}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $K^\bullet, I^\bullet \in K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$.
Assume $K^\bullet$ is filtered acyclic and
$I^\bullet$ bounded below and consisting of filtered injective objects.
Any morphism $K^\bullet \to I^\bullet$ is homotopic to zero:
$\Hom_{K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))}(K^\bullet, I^\bullet) = 0$.

\label{lemma-properties-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. The category $\QCoh(S_\etale, \mathcal{O})$
of quasi-coherent modules on $S_\etale$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item The kernel and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
\item Given a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
if two out of three are quasi-coherent so is the third.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$
is of finite presentation.
then the internal hom
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is quasi-coherent.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-extensions-of-algebras}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $B$ be an $A$-algebra. Let $N$ be a $B$-module.
The set of isomorphism classes of extensions of $A$-algebras
$$
0 \to N \to B' \to B \to 0
$$
where $N$ is an ideal of square zero is canonically bijective to
$\Ext^1_B(\NL_{B/A}, N)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor}
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$
over $k$. Let $D$ be an effective Cartier divisor on $X$.
Then $D$ is finite over $\Spec(k)$ of degree
$\deg(D) = \dim_k \Gamma(D, \mathcal{O}_D)$. For a locally free sheaf
$\mathcal{E}$ of rank $n$ we have
$$
\deg(\mathcal{E}(D)) = n\deg(D) + \deg(\mathcal{E})
$$
where $\mathcal{E}(D) = \mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{O}_X(D)$.

\item For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}$ the graded $A$-module
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq k} H^0(X, \mathcal{F}(d))
$$

source.label: lemma-coherent-on-proj-general
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coherent-on-proj-general}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian graded ring. Set $X = \text{Proj}(A)$. Then $X$
is a Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists an $r \geq 0$ and
$d_1, \ldots, d_r \in \mathbf{Z}$ and a surjection
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, r} \mathcal{O}_X(d_j)
\longrightarrow \mathcal{F}.
$$
\item For any $p$ the cohomology group $H^p(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a finite
$A_0$-module.
\item If $p > 0$, then $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}(d)) = 0$ for all $d$ large enough.
\item For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}$ the graded $A$-module
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq k} H^0(X, \mathcal{F}(d))
$$
is a finite $A$-module.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-2-fibre-product-gives-stack-in-setoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{T}$ be stacks in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$
and let $\mathcal{R}$ be a stack in setoids over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $f : \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{S}$ and $g : \mathcal{R} \to \mathcal{S}$
be $1$-morphisms. If $f$ is faithful, then the $2$-fibre product
$$
\mathcal{T} \times_{f, \mathcal{S}, g} \mathcal{R}
$$
is a stack in setoids over $\mathcal{C}$.

\label{lemma-finiteness-compactly-supported}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field.
Let $X$ be a finite type separated scheme over $k$.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $K$ be an object of
$D^+_{tors, c}(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ or of $D_c(X_\etale, \Lambda)$
in case $\Lambda$ is torsion. Then
$H^i_c(X, K)$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module for all
$i \in \mathbf{Z}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$
be an \'etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$.
Then the quotient $U/R$ is an algebraic space,
and $U \to U/R$ is \'etale and surjective, in other words
$(U, R, U \to U/R)$ is a presentation of $U/R$.

conclusions: CM at x iff relative upper-shriek structure complex locally has only one nonzero cohomology sheaf.
hypotheses: f flat separated finite-type between S-schemes and point x.
formulation.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, and $x\in X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) the fibre-local ring $\mathcal O_{X_{f(x)},x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay; (2) there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is quasi-isomorphic to a *single* coherent cohomology sheaf placed in one cohomological degree (the degree may depend on $U$). In particular this is a neighbourhood statement about the relative dualizing complex, not just its single stalk.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L6066 assumes the Noetherian-base FTS_S situation and a FLAT morphism f with x∈X. It equates CM at x (CM local ring of fibre at x) with f^!O_Y having ONLY ONE nonzero cohomology SHEAF IN SOME OPEN NEIGHBOURHOOD of x. The proposal retains flatness and the neighbourhood rather than merely stalkwise criterion.

phase3.reason: One direction uses CM-shriek; for the reverse, generically CM fibers fix the degree, flatness of the sole dualizing cohomology sheaf identifies the fiber dualizing complex, hence CM.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $0 \to K \to A^{\oplus m} \to M \to 0$
be a sequence of $A$-modules. Consider the $A$-algebra
$C = \text{Sym}^*_A(M)$ with its presentation
$\alpha : A[y_1, \ldots, y_m] \to C$
coming from the surjection $A^{\oplus m} \to M$. Then
$$
\NL(\alpha) =
(K \otimes_A C \to \bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, m} C \text{d}y_j)
$$
(see Algebra, Section \ref{algebra-section-netherlander})
in particular $\Omega_{C/A} = M \otimes_A C$.

\label{lemma-glue-sheaves}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $X = \bigcup_{i\in I} U_i$ be an open covering.
Given any glueing data $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ij})$
for sheaves of sets with respect to the covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
there exists a sheaf of sets $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$
together with isomorphisms
$$
\varphi_i : \mathcal{F}|_{U_i} \to \mathcal{F}_i
$$
such that the diagrams
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}|_{U_i \cap U_j} \ar[r]_{\varphi_i} \ar[d]_{\text{id}} &
\mathcal{F}_i|_{U_i \cap U_j} \ar[d]^{\varphi_{ij}} \\
\mathcal{F}|_{U_i \cap U_j} \ar[r]^{\varphi_j} &
\mathcal{F}_j|_{U_i \cap U_j}
}
$$
are commutative.

Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme having no embedded points.
Let $X^0$ be the set of generic points of irreducible components of $X$.
Then we have
$$
\mathcal{K}_X =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta} =
\prod\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta}
$$
where $j_\eta : \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta}) \to X$ is the canonical map
of Schemes, Section \ref{schemes-section-points}. Moreover
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{K}_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-algebras,
\item for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the sheaf
$$
\mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{F}) =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{F}_\eta =
\prod\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{F}_\eta
$$
of meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent, and

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-K}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme having no embedded points.
Let $X^0$ be the set of generic points of irreducible components of $X$.
Then we have
$$
\mathcal{K}_X =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta} =
\prod\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta}
$$
where $j_\eta : \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta}) \to X$ is the canonical map
of Schemes, Section \ref{schemes-section-points}. Moreover
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{K}_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-algebras,
\item for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the sheaf
$$
\mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{F}) =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{F}_\eta =
\prod\nolimits_{\eta \in X^0} j_{\eta, *}\mathcal{F}_\eta
$$
of meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent, and
\item the ring of rational functions of $X$ is the ring of meromorphic
functions on $X$, in a formula: $R(X) = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{K}_X)$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Here $i:Z\to Y$ denotes the first immersion, and the conormal maps are induced by the defining ideals. For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. For an immersion $i:Z\to X$, choose an open $V\subset X$ where it is closed, with ideal $\mathcal I$; the conormal algebra $\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ has degree $n$ piece corresponding to $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ on $Z$, and $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal C_{Z/X,1}$. Its canonical map from $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})$ is induced by multiplication of ideals. Let $Z \to Y \to X$ be immersions of schemes. Assume that
$Z \to Y$ is $H_1$-regular. Then the canonical sequence of
Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-transitivity-conormal}
$$
0 \to i^*\mathcal{C}_{Y/X} \to
\mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to
\mathcal{C}_{Z/Y} \to 0
$$
is exact and locally split.

\label{lemma-transitivity-conormal-quasi-regular}
Let $Z \to Y \to X$ be immersions of schemes. Assume that
$Z \to Y$ is $H_1$-regular. Then the canonical sequence of
Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-transitivity-conormal}
$$
0 \to i^*\mathcal{C}_{Y/X} \to
\mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to
\mathcal{C}_{Z/Y} \to 0
$$
is exact and locally split.

\label{lemma-pullback-sieve-section}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $S$ be a sieve on $U$.
If $f : V \to U$ is in $S$, then
$S \times_U V = h_V$ is maximal.

sequences $\{\alpha_r : E_r(K) \to E_r(L)\}_{r \geq 0}$ compatible
with the bigradings.

formulation.statement:
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme of a Noetherian scheme. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z$ has no embedded points,
\item every irreducible component of $Z$ has codimension $1$ in $X$,
\item every local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$, $x \in Z$ is
a UFD or $X$ is regular.
\end{enumerate}
Then $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $X = U \cup V$ be
the union of two open subspaces of $X$.
For objects $E$, $F$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have a
Mayer-Vietoris sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
& \ldots \ar[r] & \Ext^{-1}(E_{U \cap V}, F_{U \cap V}) \ar[lld] \\
\Hom(E, F) \ar[r] &
\Hom(E_U, F_U) \oplus
\Hom(E_V, F_V) \ar[r] &
\Hom(E_{U \cap V}, F_{U \cap V})
}
$$
where the subscripts denote restrictions to the relevant opens
and the $\Hom$'s and $\Ext$'s are taken in the relevant
derived categories.

\label{lemma-global-pullback}
Let
$(f, f^\sharp) :
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})
\to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is free then $f^*\mathcal{F}$ is free.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is finite free then $f^*\mathcal{F}$ is finite free.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is generated by global sections
then $f^*\mathcal{F}$ is generated by global sections.
\item Given $r \geq 0$ if $\mathcal{F}$ is generated by $r$ global
sections, then $f^*\mathcal{F}$ is generated by $r$ global sections.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is generated by finitely many global sections
then $f^*\mathcal{F}$ is generated by finitely many global sections.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ has a global presentation then
$f^*\mathcal{F}$ has a global presentation.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ has a finite global presentation
then $f^*\mathcal{F}$ has a finite global presentation.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-finite-base-change}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$. Let $(S', s') \to (S, s)$ be a morphism of pointed schemes.
If $S' \to S$ is quasi-finite at $s'$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is pure along $X_s$,
then $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ is pure along $X_{s'}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-collate-constructible}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $E \subset X$ be a subset.
Let $X = V_1 \cup \ldots \cup V_m$ be a finite covering by
retrocompact opens.
Then $E$ is constructible in $X$ if and only if $E \cap V_j$
is constructible in $V_j$ for each $j = 1, \ldots, m$.

formulation.statement:
An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme with ideal locally generated by one nonzerodivisor. A relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ is such a divisor $D\subset X$ with $D\to S$ flat; this does not assume $X\to S$ flat. Sums are defined by products of ideal sheaves. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D \subset X$ be a relative effective Cartier divisor.
If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, then there exists
an open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that $D \subset U$ and
such that $f|_U : U \to S$ is flat.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-relative-Cartier-divisor}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D \subset X$ be a relative effective Cartier divisor.
If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, then there exists
an open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that $D \subset U$ and
such that $f|_U : U \to S$ is flat.

\label{lemma-local-cohomology-derived-completion}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module.
Then
$$
H^i(R\Gamma_\mathfrak m(M)^\wedge) = \lim H^i_\mathfrak m(M/I^nM)
$$
for all $i$ where $R\Gamma_\mathfrak m(M)^\wedge$ denotes
the derived $I$-adic completion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-commutes-with-countable-sums}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category with countable direct sums.
Let $K \in \mathcal{D}$ be an object such that for every
countable set of objects $E_n \in \mathcal{D}$ the canonical map
$$
\bigoplus \Hom_\mathcal{D}(K, E_n)
\longrightarrow
\Hom_\mathcal{D}(K, \bigoplus E_n)
$$
is a bijection. Then, given any system $L_n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ over
$\mathbf{N}$ whose derived colimit $L = \text{hocolim} L_n$
exists we have that
$$
\colim \Hom_\mathcal{D}(K, L_n) \longrightarrow \Hom_\mathcal{D}(K, L)
$$
is a bijection.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For complexes $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ of modules, $\mathrm{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}B^\bullet)$ denotes the ordinary total tensor-product complex with the standard signed differential; $K(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ is the homotopy category of complexes. A quasi-isomorphism is a morphism of complexes inducing an isomorphism on all cohomology objects.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex.
Then the functor
$$
K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}))
\longrightarrow
K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})), \quad
\mathcal{F}^\bullet
\longmapsto
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{K}^\bullet)
$$
transforms quasi-isomorphisms into quasi-isomorphisms.

\label{lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules}
Let
$(f, f^\sharp) :
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})
\to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed sites.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-modules.
There is a canonical bijection
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}}(f^*\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})
=
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{G}, f_*\mathcal{F}).
$$
In other words: the functor $f^*$ is the left adjoint to
$f_*$.

formulation.statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above, Let
$$
\xymatrix{
(U_3, T_3, \delta_3) \ar[d] \ar[r] & (U_2, T_2, \delta_2) \ar[d] \\
(U_1, T_1, \delta_1) \ar[r] & (U, T, \delta)
}
$$
be a fibre square in the category of divided power thickenings of
$X$ relative to $(S, \mathcal{I}, \gamma)$. If $T_2 \to T$ is
flat and $U_2 = T_2 \times_T U$, then $T_3 = T_1 \times_T T_2$ (as schemes).

\label{lemma-divided-power-thickening-base-change-flat}

$$
\xymatrix{
(U_3, T_3, \delta_3) \ar[d] \ar[r] & (U_2, T_2, \delta_2) \ar[d] \\
(U_1, T_1, \delta_1) \ar[r] & (U, T, \delta)
}
$$
be a fibre square in the category of divided power thickenings of
$X$ relative to $(S, \mathcal{I}, \gamma)$. If $T_2 \to T$ is
flat and $U_2 = T_2 \times_T U$, then $T_3 = T_1 \times_T T_2$ (as schemes).

\label{lemma-birational-varieties}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be varieties over a field $k$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ and $Y$ are birational varieties,
\item the function fields $k(X)$ and $k(Y)$ are isomorphic,
\item there exist nonempty opens of $X$ and $Y$ which are isomorphic
as varieties,
\item there exists an open $U \subset X$ and a birational morphism
$U \to Y$ of varieties.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-local-isomorphism
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-isomorphism}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ be a homomorphism
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $x \in X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{F}_x = 0$ then there exists an open neighbourhood
$U \subset X$ of $x$ such that $\mathcal{F}|_U = 0$.
\item If $\varphi_x : \mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{F}_x$ is injective,
then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$ such that
$\varphi|_U$ is injective.
\item If $\varphi_x : \mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{F}_x$ is surjective,
then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$ such that
$\varphi|_U$ is surjective.
\item If $\varphi_x : \mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{F}_x$ is bijective,
then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$ such that
$\varphi|_U$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

For a Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$, the punctured spectrum is $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. The Picard group $\operatorname{Pic}(U)$ classifies invertible $\mathcal O_U$-modules. For a Noetherian scheme $X$ and a sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I$, let $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ denote compatible formal coherent systems on the infinitesimal thickenings defined by $\mathcal I^n$. Completion of a coherent sheaf is its system of reductions to these thickenings. A colimit over opens containing a closed locus is taken via restrictions to smaller opens.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
and let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$. Let $Y = Z(s)$
be the zero scheme of $s$ and denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
the corresponding sheaf of ideals.
Let $\mathcal{V}$ be the set of open subschemes of $X$ containing $Y$
ordered by reverse inclusion.
Assume that for all $x \in X \setminus Y$ we have
$$
\text{depth}(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + \dim(\overline{\{x\}}) > 2
$$
Then the completion functor
$$
\colim_\mathcal{V}
\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_V)
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})
$$
is an equivalence on the full subcategories of finite locally free objects.

source.label: proposition-lefschetz-equivalence
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-lefschetz-equivalence}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
and let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$. Let $Y = Z(s)$
be the zero scheme of $s$ and denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
the corresponding sheaf of ideals.
Let $\mathcal{V}$ be the set of open subschemes of $X$ containing $Y$
ordered by reverse inclusion.
Assume that for all $x \in X \setminus Y$ we have
$$
\text{depth}(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + \dim(\overline{\{x\}}) > 2
$$
Then the completion functor
$$
\colim_\mathcal{V}
\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_V)
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})
$$
is an equivalence on the full subcategories of finite locally free objects.

of schemes with cartesian squares. Assume that

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-algebraize-formal-closed-subscheme}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Write $S = \Spec(A)$ and $S_n = \Spec(A/I^n)$.
Let $X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type.
For $n \geq 1$ we set $X_n = X \times_S S_n$.
Suppose given a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Z_1 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_2 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_3 \ar[r] \ar[d] & \ldots \\
X_1 \ar[r]^{i_1} & X_2 \ar[r]^{i_2} & X_3 \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
of schemes with cartesian squares. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z_1 \to X_1$ is a closed immersion, and
\item $Z_1 \to S_1$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a closed immersion of schemes $Z \to X$ such that
$Z_n = Z \times_S S_n$. Moreover, $Z$ is proper over $S$.

For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent}
\begin{slogan}
Cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves is the same no matter which
topology you use.
\end{slogan}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^q(S, \mathcal{F}) = H^q((\Sch/S)_\tau, \mathcal{F}^a).
$$
\item There are canonical isomorphisms
$$
H^q(S, \mathcal{F}) =
H^q(S_{Zar}, \mathcal{F}^a) =
H^q(S_\etale, \mathcal{F}^a).
$$
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-variant-separate-points-tangent-vectors}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field.
Let $X$ be a proper $k$-scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Suppose that for every closed subscheme $Z \subset X$
of dimension $0$ and degree $2$ over $k$ the map
$$
H^0(X, \mathcal{L}) \longrightarrow H^0(Z, \mathcal{L}|_Z)
$$
is surjective. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-normalization-finite}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a quasi-compact
morphism of locally algebraic schemes over $k$. Let $X'$
be the normalization of $X$ in $Y$. If $Y$ is reduced, then
$X' \to X$ is finite.
