hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme
equidimensional of dimension $1$ whose singularities are at-worst-nodal.
If $Y \subset X$ is a reduced closed subscheme
equidimensional of dimension $1$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the singularities of $Y$ are at-worst-nodal, and
\item if $Z \subset X$ is the scheme theoretic closure of
$X \setminus Y$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the scheme theoretic intersection $Y \cap Z$ is
the disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$,
\item each point of $Y \cap Z$ is a node of $X$, and
\item $Y \to \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is smooth at every point of $Y \cap Z$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: A reduced equidimensional one-dimensional closed subscheme Y⊂X of an at-worst-nodal X is itself nodal, and Y∩closure(X\Y) is a disjoint union of finite separable points, nodes in X, smooth along Y. All nested enumerated claims survive.

phase3.reason: A reduced pure-one-dimensional closed subscheme is a union of components. Away from nodes it agrees locally with X; at a node either both branches remain, retaining the node, or one remains, becoming smooth. In the latter case the complementary intersection has completed ideal (u,v), giving a separable reduced point, and the surviving branch is regular with separable residue.

\label{lemma-standard-open-containing-maximal-point}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime of $R$.
Let $W \subset \Spec(R)$ be a quasi-compact open
not containing the point $\mathfrak p$. Then there
exists an $f \in R$, $f \not \in \mathfrak p$ such
that $D(f) \cap W = \emptyset$.

For any morphism $f:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, write $\mu_f(K,L):Rf_*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbf L}Rf_*L\to Rf_*(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}L)$ for the canonical relative cup product. Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ and
$g : (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) \to (Z, \mathcal{O}_Z)$
be morphisms of ringed spaces. The relative cup product of
Remark \ref{remark-cup-product} is compatible with compositions
in the sense that the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
R(g \circ f)_*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Z}^\mathbf{L} R(g \circ f)_*L
\ar@{=}[rr] \ar[d] & &
Rg_*Rf_*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Z}^\mathbf{L} Rg_*Rf_*L \ar[d] \\
R(g \circ f)_*(K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} L) \ar@{=}[r] &
Rg_*Rf_*(K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} L) &
Rg_*(Rf_*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L}  Rf_*L) \ar[l]
}
$$
is commutative in $D(\mathcal{O}_Z)$ for all $K, L$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

source.label: lemma-torsion-sections
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-torsion-sections}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme with generic point $\eta$. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $U \subset X$ be nonempty
open and $s \in \mathcal{F}(U)$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item for some $x \in U$ the image of $s$ in $\mathcal{F}_x$ is torsion,
\item for all $x \in U$ the image of $s$ in $\mathcal{F}_x$ is torsion,
\item the image of $s$ in $\mathcal{F}_\eta$ is zero,
\item the image of $s$ in $j_*\mathcal{F}_\eta$ is zero, where $j : \eta \to X$
is the inclusion morphism.
\end{enumerate}

For a base scheme $S$ in a chosen big fppf site $\mathrm{Sch}_{fppf}$, write $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$ for the functor represented by a scheme $U/S$. A natural transformation $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable** if for every object $U/S$ and every $\xi\in G(U)$, the base change $h_U\times_G F$ is isomorphic to $h_{V_\xi}$ for some scheme $V_\xi/S$. This definition does not assume the presheaves are sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-schemes-gives-representable-transformation}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$ and let
$X$, $Y$ be objects of $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Then
$$
h_f : h_X \longrightarrow h_Y
$$
is a representable transformation of functors.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Let $X^0 \subset |X|$, resp.\ $Y^0 \subset |Y|$ denote the set of
codimension $0$ points of $X$, resp.\ $Y$. Let $y \in Y^0$. The following are
equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f^{-1}(\{y\}) \subset X^0$,

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a subsheaf of the final object of the \'etale

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-i-star-exact}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subset.
Denote $i : Z \to X$ the inclusion map. The functor
$$
i_* : \textit{Ab}(Z) \longrightarrow \textit{Ab}(X)
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image exactly those
abelian sheaves whose support is contained in $Z$. The functor $i^{-1}$
is a left inverse to $i_*$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-charpoly-module-ideal}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module.
Let $\varphi : M \to M$ be an endomorphism such
that $\varphi(M) \subset IM$.
Then there exists a monic polynomial
$P = t^n + a_1 t^{n - 1} + \ldots + a_n \in R[T]$
such that $a_j \in I^j$ and $P(\varphi) = 0$ as an endomorphism of $M$.

formulation.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. If $f:X\to Y$ is étale, then there is a natural isomorphism $f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*=Lf^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$. The identification concerns the compactification-based upper-shriek functor, not the generally different unrestricted right adjoint to $Rf_*$ for an arbitrary nonproper étale morphism.

Let $E \subset X$ be a subset.

Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be categories, and let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $v:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be functors with a specified adjunction $u\dashv v$, meaning natural bijections $\Mor_{\mathcal D}(u(X),Y)\cong\Mor_{\mathcal C}(X,v(Y))$.

$\Leftrightarrow$ $\eta : \text{id} \to v \circ u$ is an isomorphism,
\item $v$ is fully faithful $\Leftrightarrow$
$u \circ v \cong \text{id}$ $\Leftrightarrow$
$\epsilon : u \circ v \to \text{id}$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces $W=X\times_YZ$, with projections $p:W\to X$ and $q:W\to Z$, let $x\in|X|$ and $z\in|Z|$ have common image $y\in|Y|$. Define $F_{x,z}=\{w\in|W|:p(w)=x,\ q(w)=z\}$. For a field representative $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$, the fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ carries its ordinary Zariski topology, and the set $F_{x,z}$ is the fibre of the corresponding map of point spaces.

Let $X$ be an algebraic space locally of finite type over a field $k$.
Consider the conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|X|$ is a finite set,
\item $|X|$ is a discrete space,
\item $\dim(|X|) = 0$,
\item $\dim(X) = 0$,
\item $X \to \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is locally quasi-finite,

source.label: lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field}
Let $X$ be an algebraic space locally of finite type over a field $k$.
Consider the conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|X|$ is a finite set,
\item $|X|$ is a discrete space,
\item $\dim(|X|) = 0$,
\item $\dim(X) = 0$,
\item $X \to \Spec(k)$ is locally quasi-finite,
\end{enumerate}
Then (2), (3), (4), and (5) are equivalent.
If $X$ is decent, then (1) implies the others.

source.label: lemma-sitting-in-degrees
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sitting-in-degrees}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring with
normalized dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$. Let $M$ be a finite
$A$-module and let $d = \dim(\text{Supp}(M))$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $\Ext^i_A(M, \omega_A^\bullet)$ is nonzero, then
$i \in \{-d, \ldots, 0\}$,
\item the dimension of the support of $\Ext^i_A(M, \omega_A^\bullet)$
is at most $-i$,
\item $\text{depth}(M)$ is the smallest integer $\delta \geq 0$ such that
$\Ext^{-\delta}_A(M, \omega_A^\bullet) \not = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-dimension-formula-general}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Assume $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ locally
of finite type. Let $x \in |X|$ with image $y \in |Y|$.
Then we have
\begin{align*}
& \text{the dimension of the local ring of }X\text{ at }x \leq \\
& \text{the dimension of the local ring of }Y\text{ at }y + E - \\
& \text{ the transcendence degree of }x/y
\end{align*}
Here $E$ is the maximum of the transcendence degrees of $\xi/f(\xi)$
where $\xi \in |X|$ runs over the points specializing to $x$ at
which the local ring of $X$ has dimension $0$.

Let $\mathcal{I}$ and $\mathcal{J}$ be a categories and denote
$p : \mathcal{I} \times \mathcal{J} \to \mathcal{J}$ the projection.
If $\mathcal{I}$ is connected, then for a diagram
$M : \mathcal{J} \to \mathcal{C}$ the colimit $\colim_\mathcal{J} M$ exists
if and only if $\colim_{\mathcal{I} \times \mathcal{J}} M \circ p$ exists and
if so these colimits are equal.

The text matches, but logical_form=source_setup_existential misclassifies the proposition and should be corrected before authority.","original_source_statement_tex":"\label{lemma-total-complex-tensor-product}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$, $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras over $R$.
Denote $A^\bullet$, $B^\bullet$ the underlying cochain complexes.
As cochain complexes of $R$-modules we have

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-total-complex-tensor-product}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$, $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras over $R$.
Denote $A^\bullet$, $B^\bullet$ the underlying cochain complexes.
As cochain complexes of $R$-modules we have
$$
(A \otimes_R B)^\bullet = \text{Tot}(A^\bullet \otimes_R B^\bullet).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper flat morphism of finite presentation.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is the spectrum of a valuation ring,
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is trivial on the generic fibre $X_\eta$ of $f$,
\item the closed fibre $X_0$ of $f$ is integral,
\item $H^0(X_\eta, \mathcal{O}_{X_\eta})$ is equal to the function field of $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{L}$ is trivial.

formulation.statement:
An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme with ideal locally generated by one nonzerodivisor. A relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ is such a divisor $D\subset X$ with $D\to S$ flat; this does not assume $X\to S$ flat. Sums are defined by products of ideal sheaves. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. The conormal algebra
of $i$ has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $U \subset X$ be any open such that $i(Z)$ is
a closed subset of $U$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_U$
be the sheaf of ideals corresponding to the closed subscheme
$i(Z) \subset U$. Then
$$
\mathcal{C}_{Z/X, *} =
i^*\left(\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} \mathcal{I}^n\right) =
i^{-1}\left(
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} \mathcal{I}^n/\mathcal{I}^{n + 1}
\right)
$$
\item
For any affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset X$
such that $Z \cap U = \Spec(R/I)$ there is a
canonical isomorphism
$\Gamma(Z \cap U, \mathcal{C}_{Z/X, *}) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-conormal-sheaf}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. The conormal algebra
of $i$ has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $U \subset X$ be any open such that $i(Z)$ is
a closed subset of $U$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_U$
be the sheaf of ideals corresponding to the closed subscheme
$i(Z) \subset U$. Then
$$
\mathcal{C}_{Z/X, *} =
i^*\left(\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} \mathcal{I}^n\right) =
i^{-1}\left(
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} \mathcal{I}^n/\mathcal{I}^{n + 1}
\right)
$$
\item
For any affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset X$
such that $Z \cap U = \Spec(R/I)$ there is a
canonical isomorphism
$\Gamma(Z \cap U, \mathcal{C}_{Z/X, *}) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic
$k$-scheme of dimension $1$. Let $Y \to X$ be an \'etale morphism.
Let $y \in Y$ be a point with image $x \in X$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is a closed point of $X$ and a node, and
\item $y$ is a closed point of $Y$ and a node.
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: After geometric field extension, the closed node point residue fields become algebraically closed and the étale local map induces an isomorphism of completed local rings; the completed node model is therefore preserved in both directions.

\label{lemma-cover-by-union-affines}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
There exists a surjective \'etale morphism $U \to X$ where
$U$ is a disjoint union of affine schemes.
We may in addition assume each of these affines
maps into an affine open of $S$.

An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme with ideal locally generated by one nonzerodivisor. A relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ is such a divisor $D\subset X$ with $D\to S$ flat; this does not assume $X\to S$ flat. Sums are defined by products of ideal sheaves. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $D_1, D_2 \subset X$
are relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ then so
is $D_1 + D_2$ (Definition \ref{definition-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors}).

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $D_1, D_2 \subset X$
are relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ then so
is $D_1 + D_2$ (Definition \ref{definition-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors}).

\label{lemma-image-essentially-constant}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $M : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{C}$
be a diagram with filtered (resp.\ cofiltered) index category $\mathcal{I}$.
Let $F : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor.
If $M$ is essentially constant as an ind-object (resp.\ pro-object),
then so is $F \circ M : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{D}$.

For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locality-cohomology}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site, $\mathcal{F}$ an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$,
$U$ an object of $\mathcal{C}$, $p > 0$ an integer and $\xi \in
H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$. Then there exists a covering
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ of $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\xi |_{U_i} = 0$ for all $i \in I$.

\label{lemma-diagonal-formal-algebraic-space}
Let $S$ be a scheme. If $X$ is a formal algebraic space over
$S$, then the diagonal morphism $\Delta : X \to X \times_S X$
is representable, a monomorphism, locally quasi-finite,
locally of finite type, and separated.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $X$ is reduced. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the scheme theoretic image $Z$ of $f$ is the reduced induced algebraic
space structure on $\overline{|f|(|X|)}$, and
\item for any \'etale morphism $V \to Y$ the scheme theoretic image of
$X \times_Y V \to V$ is equal to $Z \times_Y V$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: If X is reduced, the scheme-theoretic image of f:X→Y is the reduced induced structure on closure of its topological image, and its formation commutes with any étale base change V→Y. Both conclusions and reducedness premise match.

phase3.reason: For reduced X, its topological image closure with reduced induced structure is the smallest closed subspace receiving f; étale localizations preserve reducedness and the open étale chart allows the closure to pull back, proving both assertions.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-localization}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S \subset R$ be a multiplicative subset.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The localization $S^{-1}R$ is a flat $R$-algebra.
\item If $M$ is an $S^{-1}R$-module, then $M$ is a flat $R$-module
if and only if $M$ is a flat $S^{-1}R$-module.
\item Suppose $M$ is an $R$-module. Then
$M$ is a flat $R$-module if and only if $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a flat
$R_{\mathfrak p}$-module for all primes $\mathfrak p$ of $R$.
\item Suppose $M$ is an $R$-module. Then $M$ is a flat $R$-module if
and only if $M_{\mathfrak m}$ is a flat
$R_{\mathfrak m}$-module for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $R$.
\item Suppose $R \to A$ is a ring map, $M$ is an $A$-module,
and $g_1, \ldots, g_m \in A$ are elements generating the unit
ideal of $A$. Then $M$ is flat over $R$ if and only if each localization
$M_{g_i}$ is flat over $R$.
\item Suppose $R \to A$ is a ring map, and $M$ is an $A$-module.
Then $M$ is a flat $R$-module if and only if the localization
$M_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module
(with $\mathfrak p$ the prime of $R$ lying under $\mathfrak q$)
for all primes $\mathfrak q$ of $A$.
\item Suppose $R \to A$ is a ring map, and $M$ is an $A$-module.
Then $M$ is a flat $R$-module if and only if the localization
$M_{\mathfrak m}$ is a flat $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module
(with $\mathfrak p = R \cap \mathfrak m$)
for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $A$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
If $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ and $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ are
representable by algebraic spaces and \'etale so is
$\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$.

Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.
The category of \'etale neighborhoods is cofiltered. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(U_i, \overline{u}_i)_{i = 1, 2}$ be two \'etale neighborhoods of
$\overline{s}$ in $S$. Then there exists a third \'etale neighborhood
$(U, \overline{u})$ and morphisms
$(U, \overline{u}) \to (U_i, \overline{u}_i)$, $i = 1, 2$.
\item Let $h_1, h_2: (U, \overline{u}) \to (U', \overline{u}')$ be two
morphisms between \'etale neighborhoods of $\overline{s}$. Then there exist an
\'etale neighborhood $(U'', \overline{u}'')$ and a morphism
$h : (U'', \overline{u}'') \to (U, \overline{u})$
which equalizes $h_1$ and $h_2$, i.e., such that
$h_1 \circ h = h_2 \circ h$.
\end{enumerate}
Cofiltered means any pair of lifted étale neighbourhoods has a common *refinement*, and any two parallel morphisms are made equal after a further refinement. The fibre-product/étale diagonal construction uses the chosen geometric lifts.
hypotheses:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of a scheme $S$ is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. An **étale neighbourhood** of $\bar s$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to S$ étale and a chosen $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $\bar s$; a morphism of such neighbourhoods is an $S$-morphism preserving the lifts. Their category is **cofiltered**, so a presheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** has stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}=\operatorname*{colim}_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)$ over the opposite (filtered) category. Write $\mathcal F^\#$ for the associated sheaf. This is a *geometric* stalk, not merely a Zariski local-ring stalk.

These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of a scheme $S$ is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. An **étale neighbourhood** of $\bar s$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to S$ étale and a chosen $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $\bar s$; a morphism of such neighbourhoods is an $S$-morphism preserving the lifts. Their category is **cofiltered**, so a presheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** has stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}=\operatorname*{colim}_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)$ over the opposite (filtered) category. Write $\mathcal F^\#$ for the associated sheaf. This is a *geometric* stalk, not merely a Zariski local-ring stalk.

Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.
The category of \'etale neighborhoods is cofiltered. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(U_i, \overline{u}_i)_{i = 1, 2}$ be two \'etale neighborhoods of
$\overline{s}$ in $S$. Then there exists a third \'etale neighborhood
$(U, \overline{u})$ and morphisms
$(U, \overline{u}) \to (U_i, \overline{u}_i)$, $i = 1, 2$.
\item Let $h_1, h_2: (U, \overline{u}) \to (U', \overline{u}')$ be two
morphisms between \'etale neighborhoods of $\overline{s}$. Then there exist an
\'etale neighborhood $(U'', \overline{u}'')$ and a morphism
$h : (U'', \overline{u}'') \to (U, \overline{u})$
which equalizes $h_1$ and $h_2$, i.e., such that
$h_1 \circ h = h_2 \circ h$.
\end{enumerate}

**Precise scope:** Cofiltered means any pair of lifted étale neighbourhoods has a common *refinement*, and any two parallel morphisms are made equal after a further refinement. The fibre-product/étale diagonal construction uses the chosen geometric lifts.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-topology-I-adic}
Let $I$ be an ideal of a Noetherian ring $A$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme
over $\Spec(A)$. Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
If $\text{cd}(A, I) = 1$, then for all $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the limit topology on
$\lim H^p(X, \mathcal{F}_n)$ is $I$-adic.

conclusions: $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.
hypotheses: For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the standing Cohen–Macaulay curve hypotheses imply $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional. Let $\omega_X$ be its coherent dualizing module, equal to $H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. A regular global section of an invertible sheaf is one whose multiplication map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is injective; an ample invertible sheaf is very ample if its global sections define a closed immersion into projective space.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $\omega_X$ be its coherent dualizing module, equal to $H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. A regular global section of an invertible sheaf is one whose multiplication map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is injective; an ample invertible sheaf is very ample if its global sections define a closed immersion into projective space.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular global section,
\item $H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$, and
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is ample.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.

phase3.reason: The complete proof builds the Cartier zero-scheme of a regular section, propagates H^1 vanishing, proves multiplication maps surjective for n>=3 using trivializations on the zero-scheme, and concludes the section ring is generated in degrees at most 3; the sixth Veronese then yields very ampleness. One minor nonemptiness detail is omitted.

\label{lemma-conormal-effective-Cartier-divisor}
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $D \subset S$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
Then the conormal sheaf is $\mathcal{C}_{D/S} = \mathcal{I}_D|_D =
\mathcal{O}_S(-D)|_D$ and the normal sheaf is
$\mathcal{N}_{D/S} = \mathcal{O}_S(D)|_D$.

of Topologies, Lemma \ref{topologies-lemma-at-the-bottom} or

formulation.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$. Then $f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s')[Z]
+
\text{div}(f)
$$
as Weil divisors.

\label{lemma-divisor-meromorphic-well-defined}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$. Then $f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s')[Z]
+
\text{div}(f)
$$
as Weil divisors.

\label{lemma-finite-residue-extension-closed}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $\mathfrak m \subset R$ be a maximal ideal.
Let $\mathfrak q \subset S$ be a prime ideal
lying over $\mathfrak m$ such that $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak m)$
is an algebraic field extension.
Then $\mathfrak q$ is a maximal ideal of $S$.

S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_i.
f_0:X_0\to Y_0 is a morphism of schemes over S_0.
S_0, X_0, Y_0 are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
For every i\ge 0, f_i:X_i\to Y_i is obtained from f_0 by base change along S_i\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is the corresponding base change of f_0 along S\to S_0.

formulation.statement: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). Fix \(0\in I\) and a morphism of \(S_0\)-schemes \(f_0:X_0\to Y_0\) with \(S_0,X_0,Y_0\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each \(i\ge 0\), let \(f_i:X_i\to Y_i\) be the base change of \(f_0\) to \(S_i\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be its base change to \(S\). If \(f\) is affine, then there exists \(i\ge 0\) such that \(f_i\) is affine.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra. Let

is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $S$ be a $k$-algebra over $k$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $S$ is a domain and finite dimensional over $k$,
then $S$ is a field.
\item If $S$ is integral over $k$ and a domain,

$S$ is a maximal ideal (see

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-factor-through-nicer}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let $E$ be a compact
object of $D(A, \text{d})$. Let $P$ be a differential graded $A$-module
which has a finite filtration
$$
0 = F_{-1}P \subset F_0P \subset F_1P \subset \ldots \subset F_nP = P
$$
by differential graded submodules such that
$$
F_{i + 1}P/F_iP \cong \bigoplus\nolimits_{j \in J_i} A[k_{i, j}]
$$
as differential graded $A$-modules for some sets $J_i$ and integers $k_{i, j}$.
Let $E \to P$ be a morphism of $D(A, \text{d})$.
Then there exists a differential graded submodule $P' \subset P$ such that
$F_{i + 1}P \cap P'/(F_iP \cap P')$ is equal to
$\bigoplus_{j \in J'_i} A[k_{i, j}]$ for some finite subsets
$J'_i \subset J_i$ and such that $E \to P$ factors through $P'$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a surjective integral morphism $Y \to X$ where $Y$
is a scheme,
\item given a surjective \'etale morphism $U \to X$ we may choose
$Y \to X$ such that for every $y \in Y$ there is an open neighbourhood
$V \subset Y$ such that $V \to X$ factors through $U$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-shriek-over-CM}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$ with image $y \in Y$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is Cohen-Macaulay, and
\item $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))}(\kappa(\xi)) \leq r$
for any generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component
of $X$ containing $x$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
$$
H^i(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x \not = 0
\Rightarrow - r \leq i
$$
and the stalk $H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x$ is $(S_2)$ as an
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module.

\label{lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-reduced}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X \to \Spec(k)$ be locally of finite type.
Assume $X$ has finitely many irreducible components.
Then there exists a finite purely inseparable extension $k'/k$
such that $(X_{k'})_{red}$ is geometrically reduced over $k'$.

\label{lemma-good-map}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with enough negative objects.
Let $X \in D^b(\mathcal{A})$. Let $b \in \mathbf{Z}$ with
$H^i(X) = 0$ for $i > b$. Then
there exists a map $N[-b] \to X$ such that the induced map
$N \to H^b(X)$ is surjective and $\Hom(H^b(X), N) = 0$.

\label{lemma-m-regular-multiply}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \geq 0$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $\mathbf{P}^n_k$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is $m$-regular, then the multiplication map
$$
H^0(\mathbf{P}^n_k, \mathcal{F}(m)) \otimes_k
H^0(\mathbf{P}^n_k, \mathcal{O}(1))
\longrightarrow
H^0(\mathbf{P}^n_k, \mathcal{F}(m + 1))
$$
is surjective.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$
between schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Then the rule that to $Y' \to Y$ assigns
$(f')^* : \mathrm{CH}_k(Y') \to \mathrm{CH}_{k + r}(X')$ where $X' = X \times_Y Y'$
is a bivariant class of degree $-r$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-pullback-bivariant}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$
between schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Then the rule that to $Y' \to Y$ assigns
$(f')^* : \CH_k(Y') \to \CH_{k + r}(X')$ where $X' = X \times_Y Y'$
is a bivariant class of degree $-r$.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). A short exact sequence of complexes is degreewise exact. Termwise flatness of **the quotient complex** $\mathcal K_3^\bullet$ is an additional essential hypothesis and is not automatically implied by the K-flat condition.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$0 \to \mathcal{K}_1^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_2^\bullet \to
\mathcal{K}_3^\bullet \to 0$ be a short exact sequence of complexes
such that the terms of $\mathcal{K}_3^\bullet$ are flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
If two out of three of $\mathcal{K}_i^\bullet$ are K-flat, so is the third.

source.label: lemma-standard-open
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-open}
Let $S$ be a graded ring. Let $f \in S$ homogeneous of positive degree.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $g\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree
and $D_{+}(g) \subset D_{+}(f)$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is invertible in $S_g$, and
$f^{\deg(g)}/g^{\deg(f)}$ is invertible in $S_{(g)}$,
\item $g^e = af$ for some $e \geq 1$ and $a \in S$ homogeneous,
\item there is a canonical $S$-algebra map $S_f \to S_g$,
\item there is a canonical $S_0$-algebra map $S_{(f)} \to S_{(g)}$
compatible with the map $S_f \to S_g$,
\item the map $S_{(f)} \to S_{(g)}$ induces an isomorphism
$$
(S_{(f)})_{g^{\deg(f)}/f^{\deg(g)}} \cong S_{(g)},
$$
\item these maps induce a commutative diagram of
topological spaces
$$
\xymatrix{
D_{+}(g) \ar[d] &
\{\mathbf{Z}\text{-graded primes of }S_g\} \ar[l] \ar[r] \ar[d] &
\Spec(S_{(g)}) \ar[d] \\
D_{+}(f) &
\{\mathbf{Z}\text{-graded primes of }S_f\} \ar[l] \ar[r] &
\Spec(S_{(f)})
}
$$
where the horizontal maps are homeomorphisms and the vertical maps
are open immersions,
\item there are compatible canonical $S_f$ and $S_{(f)}$-module
maps $M_f \to M_g$ and $M_{(f)} \to M_{(g)}$ for any graded $S$-module $M$,
and
\item the map $M_{(f)} \to M_{(g)}$ induces an isomorphism
$$
(M_{(f)})_{g^{\deg(f)}/f^{\deg(g)}} \cong M_{(g)}.
$$
\end{enumerate}
\item Any open covering of $D_{+}(f)$ can be refined to a finite
open covering of the form $D_{+}(f) = \bigcup_{i = 1}^n D_{+}(g_i)$.
\item Let $g_1, \ldots, g_n \in S$ be homogeneous of positive degree.
Then $D_{+}(f) \subset \bigcup D_{+}(g_i)$
if and only if
$g_1^{\deg(f)}/f^{\deg(g_1)}, \ldots, g_n^{\deg(f)}/f^{\deg(g_n)}$
generate the unit ideal in $S_{(f)}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chaotic-flat-quasi-coherent}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category viewed as a site with the chaotic
topology, see Sites, Example \ref{sites-example-indiscrete}.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$.
Assume for all $U \to V$ in $\mathcal{C}$ the restriction map
$\mathcal{O}(V) \to \mathcal{O}(U)$ is a flat ring map.
Then the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules is
a weak Serre subcategory of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-jordan-holder}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $A$ be an object
of $\mathcal{A}$ satisfying the equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{lemma-finite-length}. Given two filtrations
$$
0 \subset A_1 \subset A_2 \subset \ldots \subset A_n = A
\quad\text{and}\quad
0 \subset B_1 \subset B_2 \subset \ldots \subset B_m = A
$$
with $S_i = A_i/A_{i - 1}$ and $T_j = B_j/B_{j - 1}$ simple objects we have
$n = m$ and there exists a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$
such that $S_i \cong T_{\sigma(i)}$ for all $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$.

Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let
$\alpha : \mathcal{P}^\bullet \to \mathcal{Q}^\bullet$ be a

the induced map
$$
\text{Tot}(\text{id}_{\mathcal{F}^\bullet} \otimes \alpha) :
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{P}^\bullet)
\longrightarrow
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{Q}^\bullet)
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. \label{lemma-section-RHom-over-U}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $L, M$ be objects
of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. For every open $U$ we have
$$
H^0(U, R\SheafHom(L, M)) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_U)}(L|_U, M|_U)
$$
and in particular $H^0(X, R\SheafHom(L, M)) = \Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_X)}(L, M)$.

Let $M$ be a topological abelian group. Assume $M$ is linearly
topologized, complete, and has a countable fundamental system of
neighbourhoods of $0$. If $U_n \subset M$, $n \geq 1$
are open dense subsets, then $\bigcap_{n \geq 1} U_n$ is dense.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-a-version-of-brown}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the category of divided power rings. Let
$F : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a cardinal $\kappa$ such that for every
$f \in F(A, I, \gamma)$ there exists a morphism
$(A', I', \gamma') \to (A, I, \gamma)$ of $\mathcal{C}$ such that $f$
is the image of $f' \in F(A', I', \gamma')$ and $|A'| \leq \kappa$, and
\item $F$ commutes with limits.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is representable, i.e., there exists an object $(B, J, \delta)$
of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
$$
F(A, I, \gamma) = \Hom_\mathcal{C}((B, J, \delta), (A, I, \gamma))
$$
functorially in $(A, I, \gamma)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-on-subscheme-cut-out-by-Fit-0}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module.
Let $Z_0 \subset S$ be the closed subscheme cut out by
$\text{Fit}_0(\mathcal{F})$.
Let $Z \subset S$ be the scheme theoretic support of $\mathcal{F}$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z \subset Z_0 \subset S$ as closed subschemes,
\item $Z = Z_0 = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ as closed subsets,
\item there exists a finite type, quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{Z_0}$-module
$\mathcal{G}_0$ with
$$
(Z_0 \to X)_*\mathcal{G}_0 = \mathcal{F}.
$$
\end{enumerate}

Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}

is injective if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ is torsion free.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A $k$-linear *cohomological functor* $H:\mathcal T^{op}\to\mathrm{Vect}_k$ is contravariant and yields a long exact sequence under every shifted distinguished triangle. *Homological* means the analogous covariant long exact property. An object $C$ is *compact* if maps from $C$ commute with arbitrary small direct sums; a triangulated category is *compactly generated* if a set of compact objects detects zero objects.

\begin{reference}
In the projective case this is \cite[Theorem A.1]{BvdB}
\end{reference}
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$.
Let $F : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)^{opp} \to \text{Vect}_k$
be a $k$-linear cohomological functor such that
$$
\sum\nolimits_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \dim_k F(E[n]) < \infty
$$
for all $E \in D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then $F$ is isomorphic to a functor
of the form $E \mapsto \Hom_X(E, K)$ for some
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

**Scope and interpretation:** The representer K is bounded coherent even when X is singular, but is not claimed perfect. The hypothesis is total finite dimension of F(E[n]) over all shifts for **each** perfect E.

phase3.reason: Compact generation and representability reduce the functor to Hom(-,K), while the earlier characterization makes K bounded coherent.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $s \in S$. Then we have
$$
\mathcal{O}_{S, s}^h =
\colim_{(U, u)} \mathcal{O}(U)
$$
where the colimit is over the filtered category which is opposite to the
category of elementary \'etale neighbourhoods $(U, u)$ of $(S, s)$.

that $X_y = Z_{1, y} \cup \ldots \cup Z_{n, y}$ for all $y \in V$.

\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-complement-codim-1-closed-points}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be an open. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U$ is a retrocompact open of $X$,
\item $X \setminus U$ is discrete, and
\item for $x \in X \setminus U$ the local ring
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is Noetherian of dimension $\leq 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then (1) there exists an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{L}$
and a section $s$ such that $U = X_s$ and (2) the map
$\Pic(X) \to \Pic(U)$ is surjective.

\label{lemma-units-general-algebraically-closed}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field.
Let $X$ be a connected reduced scheme which is locally of finite type
over $k$ with finitely many irreducible components.
Then $\mathcal{O}^*(X)/k^*$ is a finitely generated abelian group.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spec-localization}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S \subset R$ be a multiplicative subset.
The map $R \to S^{-1}R$ induces via the functoriality of $\Spec$
a homeomorphism
$$
\Spec(S^{-1}R)
\longrightarrow
\{\mathfrak p \in \Spec(R) \mid S \cap \mathfrak p = \emptyset \}
$$
where the topology on the right hand side is that induced from the
Zariski topology on $\Spec(R)$. The inverse map is given
by $\mathfrak p \mapsto S^{-1}\mathfrak p = \mathfrak p(S^{-1}R)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-off-basis-module}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{B}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
on $\mathcal{B}$. Let $\mathcal{O}^{ext}$ be the sheaf
of rings on $X$ extending $\mathcal{O}$ and let
$\mathcal{F}^{ext}$ be the abelian sheaf on $X$ extending
$\mathcal{F}$, see Lemma \ref{lemma-extend-off-basis-structures}.
There exists a canonical map
$$
\mathcal{O}^{ext} \times \mathcal{F}^{ext}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{F}^{ext}
$$
which agrees with the given map over elements of $\mathcal{B}$
and which endows $\mathcal{F}^{ext}$ with the structure
of an $\mathcal{O}^{ext}$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
\begin{enumerate}
\item All limits and colimits exist in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.
\item Limits are the same as the corresponding limits of abelian presheaves
over $\mathcal{C}$ (i.e., commute with taking sections over objects of
$\mathcal{C}$).
\item Finite direct sums are the same as the corresponding finite direct sums
in the category of abelian pre-sheaves over $\mathcal{C}$.
\item A colimit is the sheafification of the corresponding colimit in
the category of abelian presheaves.
\item Filtered colimits are exact.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-flat-over-thickening}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O}' \to \mathcal{O}$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel $\mathcal{I}$ is
an ideal of square zero. Let $\mathcal{F}'$ be an $\mathcal{O}'$-module
and set $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}'/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F}'$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}'$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}'$-module, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module and
$\mathcal{I} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}'$
is injective.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-eventually-finite}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X = \lim X_i$ be a directed limit of schemes
over $S$ with affine transition morphisms. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
\item $X_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
\item the transition morphisms $X_{i'} \to X_i$ are finite,
\item $X_i \to S$ locally of finite type
\item $X \to S$ integral.
\end{enumerate}
Then $X_i \to S$ is finite for $i$ large enough.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-properties-diagonal}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $\Delta_{X/Y} : X \to X \times_Y X$ be the diagonal morphism.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_{X/Y}$ is representable,
\item $\Delta_{X/Y}$ is locally of finite type,
\item $\Delta_{X/Y}$ is a monomorphism,
\item $\Delta_{X/Y}$ is separated, and
\item $\Delta_{X/Y}$ is locally quasi-finite.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-sheaf-over-stack-is-stack}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $F : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{T}$
be a $1$-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{T}$ is a stack in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$,
\item for every $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ the functor
$\mathcal{S}_U \to \mathcal{T}_U$ of fibre categories is faithful,
\item for each $U$ and each $y \in \Ob(\mathcal{T}_U)$ the presheaf
$$
(h : V \to U)
\longmapsto
\{(x, f) \mid x \in \Ob(\mathcal{S}_V), f : F(x) \to f^*y\text{ over }V\}/\cong
$$
is a sheaf on $\mathcal{C}/U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{S}$ is a stack in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}$.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $f:x\to y$ and $g:y\to z$ 
be morphisms with $g\circ f=0$. Then, the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The sequence $x\overset{f}\to y\overset{g}\to z$ is exact.
\item For every $h:w\to y$ with $g\circ h=0$ there exist an object $v$, 
an epimorphism $k:v\to w$ and a morphism $l:v\to x$ with $h\circ k=f\circ l$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: With gf=0, exactness iff every h annihilated by g admits an epi cover k:v→w and lift l:v→x with hk=fl, retaining both universal and existential quantifiers.

phase3.reason: The proof constructs the fibre product of x and a test w over ker(g) and shows its projection epi in the exact case; conversely an epi lift onto ker(g) forces the image-to-kernel map epi and hence iso.

\label{lemma-additive-dual}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an additive monoidal category.
If $Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$ are left duals of $X_i$, $i = 1, 2$, then
$Y_1 \oplus Y_2$ is a left dual of $X_1 \oplus X_2$.

**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** An **ind-étale** map is a filtered colimit of étale algebras. A **pro-étale covering** of $T$ is a family of weakly étale maps whose images admit finite affine-open refinements covering every affine open of $T$. A **standard pro-étale covering** of affine $T$ is a finite jointly surjective family of affine weakly étale maps. The small pro-étale site $S_{\proetale}$ uses weakly étale $S$-schemes from a chosen big pro-étale universe; $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{\proetale}$ is its big slice site.

Let $S$ be an affine scheme. Let $S_{app}$ denote the full subcategory
of $S_\proetale$ consisting of affine objects $U$ such that
$\mathcal{O}(S) \to \mathcal{O}(U)$ is ind-\'etale. A covering of
$S_{app}$ will be a standard pro-\'etale covering, see
Definition \ref{definition-standard-proetale}.
Then restriction
$$
\mathcal{F} \longmapsto \mathcal{F}|_{S_{app}}
$$
defines an equivalence of topoi $\Sh(S_\proetale) \cong \Sh(S_{app})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-alternative}
Let $S$ be an affine scheme. Let $S_{app}$ denote the full subcategory
of $S_\proetale$ consisting of affine objects $U$ such that
$\mathcal{O}(S) \to \mathcal{O}(U)$ is ind-\'etale. A covering of
$S_{app}$ will be a standard pro-\'etale covering, see
Definition \ref{definition-standard-proetale}.
Then restriction
$$
\mathcal{F} \longmapsto \mathcal{F}|_{S_{app}}
$$
defines an equivalence of topoi $\Sh(S_\proetale) \cong \Sh(S_{app})$.

\label{lemma-recover-tail-graded-module-general}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian graded ring and let $d$ be the lcm of generators
of $A$ over $A_0$. Let $M$ be a finite graded $A$-module.
Set $X = \text{Proj}(A)$ and let $\widetilde{M}$ be

Let $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.

is a finite $A$-module,
\item $N = \bigoplus_{n \geq k} H^0(X, \widetilde{M}(n))$
is a finite $A$-module,
\item there is a canonical map $N \to N'$,
\item if $k$ is small enough there is a canonical map $M \to N'$,
\item the map $M_n \to N'_n$ is an isomorphism for $n \gg 0$,
\item $N_n \to N'_n$ is an isomorphism for $d | n$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$. Let $G$ be an algebraic
space over $S$, let $F$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, and let
$G \to F$ be a representable transformation of functors which is
surjective and \'etale. Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

phase2.semantic_review_note: An fppf sheaf F with a representable étale surjection from an algebraic space G is itself an algebraic space. The atlas G can be an algebraic space rather than necessarily a scheme, and the conclusion is preserved.

phase3.reason: The proof chooses a scheme étale-surjecting onto G and composes with the representable étale-surjective map G→F to apply the preceding quotient-space criterion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-locally-representable-by-space-gives-space}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$. Let $G$ be an algebraic
space over $S$, let $F$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, and let
$G \to F$ be a representable transformation of functors which is
surjective and \'etale. Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-reduced}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is reduced, see
Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-reduced}.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
such that each $\Gamma(U_i, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is reduced.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring
$\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is reduced.
\item For every open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is reduced.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-completion-flat}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. The sheaf
$\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge = \lim \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$
is a flat $\underline{\Lambda}$-algebra.
Moreover we have canonical identifications
$$
\underline{\Lambda}/I\underline{\Lambda} =
\underline{\Lambda}/\underline{I} =
\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge/I\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge =
\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge/\underline{I} \cdot \underline{\Lambda}^\wedge =
\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge/\underline{I}^\wedge =
\underline{\Lambda/I}
$$
where $\underline{I}^\wedge = \lim \underline{I/I^n}$.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
If $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$
is an algebraic field extension, then

\item $x$ is a closed point of its fibre, and
\item if in addition $s$ is a closed point of $S$, then
$x$ is a closed point of $X$.

formulation.statement:
**Source terminology (not an added hypothesis).** A constructible proétale $\Lambda$-module sheaf ($\Lambda$ Noetherian) is finite-type locally constant on a finite constructible locally closed stratification of each affine open. $D_{cons}(X,\Lambda)$ consists of derived $I$-complete $\Lambda$-complexes with mod-$I$ constructible cohomology and locally finite Tor dimension. In the derived sense, adic lisse means locally a finite complex of completed finite projective $\Lambda^\wedge$-modules, and adic constructible means finite locally closed strata with that property.

Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $K$ is adic constructible
(Definition \ref{definition-adic-constructible}).

\label{proposition-Noetherian-adic-constructible}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $K$ is adic constructible
(Definition \ref{definition-adic-constructible}).

\label{lemma-homotopy-colimit}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let
$\mathcal{M}_n$ be a system of differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-modules.
Then the derived colimit $\text{hocolim} \mathcal{M}_n$ in
$D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ is represented
by the differential graded module $\colim \mathcal{M}_n$.

formulation.statement:
Let C be a site and Λ a ring; D(C,Λ)=D(Mod(underline Λ)), the derived category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf underline Λ. For a derived Λ-module complex K∈D(Λ), underline K denotes its image in D(C,Λ) by the constant-sheaf derived inverse image. A **locally constant sheaf of finite-type modules** becomes constant with a finitely generated Λ-module on a covering of every site object; when Λ is Noetherian the finite-type condition is stable under the indicated constructions. Both input complexes are **bounded above** and have locally constant **finite-type cohomology sheaves**. No finite projective representative of either is assumed, and the conclusion is about cohomology sheaves of a derived tensor product, not necessarily locally constant complex terms.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $K, L \in D^-(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$. If the cohomology sheaves of
$K$ and $L$ are locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules of
finite type, then the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} L$
are locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules of finite type.

\label{lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $K, L \in D^-(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$. If the cohomology sheaves of
$K$ and $L$ are locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules of
finite type, then the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} L$
are locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules of finite type.

\label{lemma-map-into-dual}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. If
$M$ is a left differential graded $A$-module and $N$ is a
right differential graded $A$-module, then
\begin{align*}
\Hom_{\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}}(N, M^\vee)
& =
\Hom_{\text{Comp}(\mathbf{Z})}(N \otimes_A M, \mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z}) \\
& =
\text{DifferentialGradedBilinear}_A(N \times M, \mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z})
\end{align*}

\label{lemma-differential-objects-ses}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $0 \to (A, d) \to (B, d) \to (C, d) \to 0$ be a short exact sequence
of differential objects. Then we get an exact homology sequence
$$
\ldots \to H(C, d) \to H(A, d) \to H(B, d) \to H(C, d) \to \ldots
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $I$ be a preordered set and
let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system over $I$
consisting of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
(see Categories, Section \ref{categories-section-posets-limits}).
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I$ is directed,
\item $\mathcal{G}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation, and
\item $X$ has a cofinal system of open coverings
$\mathcal{U} : X = \bigcup_{j\in J} U_j$ with
$J$ finite and $U_j \cap U_{j'}$ quasi-compact
for all $j, j' \in J$.
\end{enumerate}
Then we have
$$
\colim_i \Hom_X(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F}_i)
=
\Hom_X(\mathcal{G}, \colim_i \mathcal{F}_i).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bourbaki-finite-type-general-base-at-point}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to S$ be locally of finite type.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$, then
$$
x \in \text{WeakAss}_X(\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f^*\mathcal{G})
\Leftrightarrow
s \in \text{WeakAss}_S(\mathcal{G})
\text{ and }
x \in \text{Ass}_{X_s}(\mathcal{F}_s).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibre-products-Zariski}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski
site containing $S$. The underlying categories of the sites
$\Sch_{Zar}$, $(\Sch/S)_{Zar}$,
$S_{Zar}$, $(\textit{Aff}/S)_{Zar}$, and $S_{affine, Zar}$ have fibre products.
In each case the obvious functor into the category $\Sch$ of
all schemes commutes with taking fibre products. The categories
$(\Sch/S)_{Zar}$, and $S_{Zar}$ both have a final object,
namely $S/S$.

Let $Z, Y \subset X$ be closed subspaces.

and

\xymatrix{
Z \cap Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z \ar[d] \\

}

source.label: lemma-scheme-theoretic-intersection
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-scheme-theoretic-intersection}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $Z, Y \subset X$ be closed subspaces.
Let $Z \cap Y$ be the scheme theoretic intersection of $Z$ and $Y$.
Then $Z \cap Y \to Z$ and $Z \cap Y \to Y$ are closed immersions
and
$$
\xymatrix{
Z \cap Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z \ar[d] \\
Y \ar[r] & X
}
$$
is a cartesian diagram of algebraic spaces over $S$, i.e.,
$Z \cap Y = Z \times_X Y$.

$D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{E}) \to D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})$.

is the integral closure of $A^h$, $A^{sh}$, resp.\ $A^\wedge$
in its total ring of fractions.

\label{lemma-extend-off-basis-structures}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $(\mathcal{C}, F)$ be
a type of algebraic structure.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf with values in $\mathcal{C}$
on $\mathcal{B}$.
There exists a unique sheaf $\mathcal{F}^{ext}$ with values in $\mathcal{C}$
on $X$ such that $\mathcal{F}^{ext}(U) = \mathcal{F}(U)$
for all $U \in \mathcal{B}$ compatibly with the restriction
mappings.

\label{lemma-spec-closed}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
The map $R \to R/I$ induces via the functoriality of
$\Spec$ a homeomorphism
$$
\Spec(R/I) \longrightarrow V(I) \subset \Spec(R).
$$
The inverse is given by $\mathfrak p \mapsto \mathfrak p / I$.

Let
$$
0 \to A^\bullet \to B^\bullet \to C^\bullet \to 0
$$
be a complex (!) of complexes.
Suppose that we are given splittings $B^n = A^n \oplus C^n$
compatible with the maps in the displayed sequence.
Let $s^n : C^n \to B^n$ and $\pi^n : B^n \to A^n$ be the
corresponding maps. Then the family of morphisms
$$
\pi^{n + 1} \circ d_B^n \circ s^n
:
C^n \to A^{n + 1}
$$
define a morphism of complexes $\delta : C^\bullet \to A[1]^\bullet$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For an additive category, the displayed complex of cochain complexes with degreewise biproduct decompositions B^n=A^n⊕C^n yields pi^(n+1)∘d_B^n∘s^n:C^n→A^(n+1), forming a cochain map C→A[1]. The candidate does not add abelianness.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ses-termwise-split-cochain}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an additive category.
Let
$$
0 \to A^\bullet \to B^\bullet \to C^\bullet \to 0
$$
be a complex (!) of complexes.
Suppose that we are given splittings $B^n = A^n \oplus C^n$
compatible with the maps in the displayed sequence.
Let $s^n : C^n \to B^n$ and $\pi^n : B^n \to A^n$ be the
corresponding maps. Then the family of morphisms
$$
\pi^{n + 1} \circ d_B^n \circ s^n
:
C^n \to A^{n + 1}
$$
define a morphism of complexes $\delta : C^\bullet \to A[1]^\bullet$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colimit-rings-flat}
Let $\{R_i, \varphi_{ii'}\}$ be a system of rings over the directed set $I$.
Let $R = \colim_i R_i$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ is an $R$-module such that $M$ is flat as an $R_i$-module
for all $i$, then $M$ is flat as an $R$-module.
\item For $i \in I$ let $M_i$ be a flat $R_i$-module and
for $i' \geq i$ let $f_{ii'} : M_i \to M_{i'}$ be a $\varphi_{ii'}$-linear
map such that $f_{i' i''} \circ f_{i i'} = f_{i i''}$. Then
$M = \colim_{i \in I} M_i$ is a flat $R$-module.
\end{enumerate}

whose horizontal arrows are elementary \'etale neighbourhoods

$\Gamma(X', g^*\mathcal{F})$ is a projective

\label{proposition-finite-presentation-flat-at-point}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a commutative diagram of pointed schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
(X, x) \ar[d] & (X', x') \ar[l]^g \ar[d] \\
(S, s) & (S', s') \ar[l]
}
$$
whose horizontal arrows are elementary \'etale neighbourhoods
such that $X'$, $S'$ are affine and such that
$\Gamma(X', g^*\mathcal{F})$ is a projective
$\Gamma(S', \mathcal{O}_{S'})$-module.

\label{lemma-frobenius}
Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Then the absolute frobenius $F_X : X \to X$
is a universal homeomorphism, is integral, and
induces purely inseparable residue field extensions.

Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes,
$\mathcal{F}$ an abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$, and $\overline{s}$ a
geometric point of $S$ lying over $s \in S$. Then
$$
\left(R^nf_* \mathcal{F}\right)_{\overline{s}} =
H_\etale^n( X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}),
p^{-1}\mathcal{F})
$$
where $p : X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}) \to X$
is the projection. For $K \in D^+(X_\etale)$ and $n \in \mathbf{Z}$
we have
$$
\left(R^nf_*K\right)_{\overline{s}} =
H_\etale^n(X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}), p^{-1}K)
$$
In fact, we have
$$
\left(Rf_*K\right)_{\overline{s}}
=
R\Gamma_\etale(X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}), p^{-1}K)
$$
in $D^+(\textit{Ab})$.

\label{theorem-higher-direct-images}
Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes,
$\mathcal{F}$ an abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$, and $\overline{s}$ a
geometric point of $S$ lying over $s \in S$. Then
$$

H_\etale^n( X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}),
p^{-1}\mathcal{F})
$$
where $p : X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}) \to X$
is the projection. For $K \in D^+(X_\etale)$ and $n \in \mathbf{Z}$
we have
$$
\left(R^nf_*K\right)_{\overline{s}} =
H_\etale^n(X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}), p^{-1}K)
$$
In fact, we have
$$
\left(Rf_*K\right)_{\overline{s}}
=
R\Gamma_\etale(X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S, \overline{s}}^{sh}), p^{-1}K)
$$
in $D^+(\textit{Ab})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-quasi-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an affine scheme.
A morphism $f : X \to S$ is quasi-affine if and only if it is quasi-compact.
In particular any morphism from an affine scheme to a quasi-separated
scheme is quasi-affine.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-finite-type-finite-presentation-local}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exist finitely many primes
$\mathfrak p_1, \ldots, \mathfrak p_m$ of $R$ such that
the map $R \to \prod R_{\mathfrak p_j}$ is injective,
\item $R \to S$ is of finite type,
\item $S$ flat over $R$, and
\item for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ the ring $S_{\mathfrak p}$
is of finite presentation over $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $S$ is of finite presentation over $R$.
