source.label: lemma-fully-faithful-general
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fully-faithful-general}
Let $I \subset \mathfrak a \subset A$ be ideals of a Noetherian ring $A$.
Let $U = \Spec(A) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$. Let $\mathcal{V}$ be
the set of open subschemes of $U$ containing $U \cap V(I)$
ordered by reverse inclusion. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $I$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item for any associated prime
$\mathfrak p \subset A$ with
$I \not \subset \mathfrak p$ and
$V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(I) \not \subset V(\mathfrak a)$
and $\mathfrak q \in V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(\mathfrak a)$ we have
$\dim((A/\mathfrak p)_\mathfrak q) > \text{cd}(A, I) + 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the completion functor
$$
\colim_\mathcal{V} \textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_V)
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(U, I\mathcal{O}_U),
\quad
\mathcal{F} \longmapsto \mathcal{F}^\wedge
$$
is fully faithful on the full subcategory of
finite locally free objects.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-approximate-complex}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal contained in
the Jacobson radical of $A$. Let
$$
S : L \xrightarrow{f} M \xrightarrow{g} N
\quad\text{and}\quad
S' : L \xrightarrow{f'} M \xrightarrow{g'} N
$$
be two complexes of finite $A$-modules as shown. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $c$ works in the Artin-Rees lemma for $f$ and $g$,
\item the complex $S$ is exact, and
\item $f' = f \bmod I^{c + 1}M$ and $g' = g \bmod I^{c + 1}N$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $c$ works in the Artin-Rees lemma for $g'$ and the
complex $S'$ is exact.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be continuous.
Assume furthermore the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the category $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and
$u(X)$ is a final object of $\mathcal{D}$ , and
\item the category $\mathcal{C}$ has fibre products and
$u$ commutes with them.
\end{enumerate}

\mathcal{C}$, in other words $u_s$ is exact.

The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Assume $R$ local and let $\mathfrak m \subset A$ be a maximal

$\varphi^!(\omega_R^\bullet)_\mathfrak m$ is a normalized
dualizing complex for $A_\mathfrak m$.

conclusions: The Picard group of every open in Spec R and every open in $\mathbf A_R^n$ is trivial; in particular this holds for opens of affine n-space over a field.
hypotheses: R is a UFD.
formulation.statement:
Let $R$ be a UFD. The Picard groups of the following are
trivial.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Spec(R)$ and any open subscheme of it.
\item $\mathbf{A}^n_R = \Spec(R[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$ and any open subscheme
of it.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the Picard group of any open subscheme of affine
$n$-space $\mathbf{A}^n_k$ over a field $k$ is trivial.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Trivial Picard groups are conclusions for all listed opens, including affine-space corollary.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For an integer $n$, the cycles $\ker(\mathcal K^n\to\mathcal K^{n+1})$ are $\mathcal O$-modules. The claim applies in each cohomological degree $n$; acyclicity and termwise flatness are **both** assumed, not consequences of K-flatness alone.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$
be a K-flat, acyclic complex with flat terms. Then
$\mathcal{F} = \Ker(\mathcal{K}^n \to \mathcal{K}^{n + 1})$
is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module.

phase3.reason: The proof computes Tor of cycles using a bounded-above flat resolution, uses acyclicity of tensor with the K-flat acyclic complex, and concludes Tor_1 vanishes.

\label{lemma-K-flat-flat-acyclic}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$
be a K-flat, acyclic complex with flat terms. Then
$\mathcal{F} = \Ker(\mathcal{K}^n \to \mathcal{K}^{n + 1})$
is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

\label{lemma-rational-tail-field-extension}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. Let $C \subset X$ be a rational tail
(Example \ref{example-rational-tail}).
For any field extension $K/k$ the base change $C_K \subset X_K$
is a finite disjoint union of rational tails.

hypotheses:
Let $u_1, u_2 : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be functors with right
adjoints $v_1, v_2 : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$. Let $\beta : u_2 \to u_1$
be a transformation of functors. Let $\beta^\vee : v_1 \to v_2$ be
the corresponding transformation of adjoint functors.
formulation.statement:
Let $u_1, u_2 : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be functors with right
adjoints $v_1, v_2 : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$. Let $\beta : u_2 \to u_1$
be a transformation of functors. Let $\beta^\vee : v_1 \to v_2$ be
the corresponding transformation of adjoint functors. Then
$$
\xymatrix{
u_2 \circ v_1 \ar[r]_\beta \ar[d]_{\beta^\vee} &
u_1 \circ v_1 \ar[d] \\
u_2 \circ v_2 \ar[r] & \text{id}
}
$$
is commutative where the unlabeled right and bottom arrows are the counits $\epsilon_1:u_1v_1\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ and $\epsilon_2:u_2v_2\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$; the top is $\beta v_1$ and the left is $u_2\beta^\vee$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The source naturality-of-mates lemma uses u1,u2:C→D, right adjoints v1,v2 and β:u2⇒u1 with mate β^∨:v1⇒v2. Its square involving u2v1, u1v1, u2v2, id_D commutes with top βv1, left u2β^∨, right/bottom counits. The final content adds only labels identifying these four transformations and retains their orientations.

phase3.reason: Characterizes adjoint mate uniquely on Hom sets and derives commutative counit square by specializing at the identity.

\label{lemma-brown}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a Grothendieck abelian category.
Let $H : D(\mathcal{A}) \to \textit{Ab}$ be a contravariant
cohomological functor which transforms direct sums into products.
Then $H$ is representable.

\label{lemma-nowhere-dense-local}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $X = \bigcup U_i$ be an open covering.
Let $T \subset X$ be a subset.
If $T \cap U_i$ is nowhere dense in $U_i$ for all $i$,
then $T$ is nowhere dense in $X$.

conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite \'etale morphism of schemes. Let $\Lambda$ be a
Noetherian ring. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a constructible sheaf of sets,
constructible sheaf of abelian groups, or constructible sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$, the same is true for
$f_*\mathcal{F}$ on $Y_\etale$.
All quantifiers and conditions from the pinned source are retained. The result is for constructible sheaves in the **small** étale category of a qcqs scheme.
hypotheses: On the small étale site $X_{\acute et}$ of a **qcqs scheme**, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* when its restriction to a finite constructible partition is **finite locally constant**; for modules over a **Noetherian** ring $\Lambda$, constructible means *finite type* locally constant on every stratum. For an étale object $j_U:U\to X$, $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$ is the representable sheaf, and $j_{U!}\underline M$ is **extension by zero** of the constant abelian or $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U$, left adjoint to $j_U^{-1}$. A *torsion abelian sheaf* has torsion stalks at every geometric point. A *filtered colimit* of sheaves is taken in the sheaf category (sheafification of the sectionwise colimit). A constructible sheaf is *finitely presented/compact for filtered colimits* if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\operatorname*{colim}_i\mathcal G_i)\cong\operatorname*{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ for every filtered system. *Essentially constant* for an ind-object means isomorphic in its ind-category to a constant ind-object. For a directed inverse system with affine transitions, its category-colimit means objects and morphisms descend from sufficiently large finite stages, **up to category equivalence**.

sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit}
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
of finite presentation. Let
$\mathcal{G} = \colim_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \mathcal{G}_\lambda$
be a filtered colimit of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Then the canonical map
$$
\colim_\lambda \SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_\lambda)
\longrightarrow
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})
$$
is an isomorphism.

source.label: lemma-image-contained-in
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-image-contained-in}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, F)$ be a type of algebraic structure.
Suppose that $A, B, C \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $f : A \to B$ and $g : C \to B$ be morphisms of
$\mathcal{C}$. If $F(g)$ is injective, and
$\Im(F(f)) \subset \Im(F(g))$, then
$f$ factors as $f = g \circ t$ for some morphism
$t : A \to C$.

For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). An $\mathcal O$-module is flat if tensoring with it is exact; the resolution claimed here is both **termwise flat** and **termwise surjective** (in addition to being a K-flat quasi-isomorphism).

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. For any complex
$\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ there exists a $K$-flat complex $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$
whose terms are flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules and a quasi-isomorphism
$\mathcal{K}^\bullet \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet$ which is termwise surjective.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-alternative-H0}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $f \in \mathfrak a \subset A$
be an element of an ideal of $A$. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $f$-adically complete,
\item $H^1_\mathfrak a(M)$ and $H^2_\mathfrak a(M)$ are
annihilated by a power of $f$.
\end{enumerate}
Then with $U = \Spec(A) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$ the map
$$
\Gamma(U, \widetilde{M})
\longrightarrow
\lim \Gamma(U, \widetilde{M/f^nM})
$$
is an isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-in-projective-space}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $Z \subset \mathbf{P}^n_R$ be a closed subscheme.
Let
$$
I_d = \Ker\left(
R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]_d
\longrightarrow
\Gamma(Z, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^n_R}(d)|_Z)\right)
$$
Then $I = \bigoplus I_d \subset R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$ is
a graded ideal and $Z = \text{Proj}(R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]/I)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-irreducible}
Let $R$ be a ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For a prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$ the closure
of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ in the Zariski topology is $V(\mathfrak p)$.
In a formula $\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}} = V(\mathfrak p)$.
\item The irreducible closed subsets of $\Spec(R)$ are
exactly the subsets $V(\mathfrak p)$, with $\mathfrak p \subset R$
a prime.
\item The irreducible components (see Topology,
Definition \ref{topology-definition-irreducible-components})
of $\Spec(R)$ are  exactly the subsets $V(\mathfrak p)$,
with $\mathfrak p \subset R$ a minimal prime.
\end{enumerate}

**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A ring map is **ind-étale** when its target is a filtered colimit of étale algebras over the source.

Let $A \to B$ be ind-\'etale. Then $A \to B$ is weakly \'etale
(that is, $A\to B$ is flat and the multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is flat).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flatten-module-pre}
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent module on $X$.
Let $U \subset S$ be a quasi-compact open. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to S$ is affine, of finite presentation, flat,
geometrically integral fibres,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a module of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{F}_U$ is of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at all generic points of
fibres lying over points of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $S' \to S$
and an open subscheme $V \subset X_{S'}$
such that (a) the strict transform $\mathcal{F}'$ of $\mathcal{F}$
restricts to a finitely locally free $\mathcal{O}_V$-module and
(b) $V \to S'$ is surjective.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-Noetherian}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is locally Noetherian.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Noetherian.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Noetherian.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is locally Noetherian.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is locally Noetherian then every open subscheme
is locally Noetherian.

Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $f : N \to N'$ be a
homomorphism of differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodules.
Then $f$ induces a morphism of functors
$$
1\otimes f :
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N
\longrightarrow
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N'
$$
If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $1 \otimes f$ is an isomorphism of
functors.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functoriality-bc}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $f : N \to N'$ be a
homomorphism of differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodules.
Then $f$ induces a morphism of functors
$$
1\otimes f :
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N
\longrightarrow
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N'
$$
If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $1 \otimes f$ is an isomorphism of
functors.

conclusions: The family is universally an effective epimorphism in schemes.
hypotheses: All affine base changes of the family are effective epimorphisms of schemes.
formulation.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes. Suppose that for every morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ an affine scheme, the base-changed family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism in the category of schemes: compatible maps from its members to any test scheme glue uniquely to a map from $Y$. Then the original family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes (with no affineness restriction on base change $Y\to X$).

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned L4031–4037 assumes for EVERY AFFINE base change Y→X that induced family is an EFFECTIVE EPIMORPHISM of SCHEMES. It concludes the original family is a UNIVERSAL effective epimorphism after ANY scheme base change. The draft restores this quantifier shift, not merely a covering condition on affine objects.

phase3.reason: The pinned proof descends arbitrary base changes by gluing effective-epimorphism maps on an affine open cover of Y; local uniqueness enforces overlap compatibility, with that routine step left to the reader.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-check-universal-effective-epimorphism-affine}
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes.
If for every morphism $Y \to X$ with $Y$ affine the family of base changes
$g_i : Y_i \to Y$ forms an effective epimorphism, then
the family of $f_i$ forms a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes.

For every i\ge 0, f_i:X_i\to Y_i is obtained from f_0 by base change along S_i\to S_0.

formulation.statement: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). Fix \(0\in I\) and a morphism of \(S_0\)-schemes \(f_0:X_0\to Y_0\) with \(S_0,X_0,Y_0\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each \(i\ge 0\), let \(f_i:X_i\to Y_i\) be the base change of \(f_0\) to \(S_i\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be its base change to \(S\). Suppose \(f_0\) is locally of finite presentation. If \(f\) is an isomorphism, then there exists \(i\ge 0\) such that \(f_i\) is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-numerical-polynomial-leading-term}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$. Let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let
$\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_r$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $d = \dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$.
Let $Z_i \subset X$ be the irreducible components
of $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ of dimension $d$. Let $\xi_i \in Z_i$
be the generic point and set
$m_i = \text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi_i}}(\mathcal{F}_{\xi_i})$.
Then
$$
\chi(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes
\mathcal{L}_r^{\otimes n_r}) -
\sum\nolimits_i
m_i\ \chi(Z_i, \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes
\mathcal{L}_r^{\otimes n_r}|_{Z_i})
$$
is a numerical polynomial in $n_1, \ldots, n_r$ of total degree $< d$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. If $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ is an object of
$\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$ then
$\bigoplus \Ker(\mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_n)$ is
a finite type, graded, quasi-coherent
$\bigoplus \mathcal{I}^n/\mathcal{I}^{n + 1}$-module.

If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. Let $C \subset X$ be a rational bridge
(with rational bridge as explicitly defined above).
For any field extension $K/k$ the base change $C_K \subset X_K$
is a finite disjoint union of rational bridges.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A rational bridge remains a finite disjoint union of rational bridges under any field extension K/k. The proposed conditions match the source and quantify over all extensions.

phase3.reason: Finite separability of the bridge's constant field decomposes k'⊗_k K into finitely many separable field factors; its degree-two attaching algebra decomposes compatibly. Cohomology base change preserves genus zero for each component and the attaching divisor remains degree two over its constant field.

\label{lemma-rational-bridge-field-extension}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. Let $C \subset X$ be a rational bridge
(Example \ref{example-rational-bridge}).
For any field extension $K/k$ the base change $C_K \subset X_K$
is a finite disjoint union of rational bridges.

\label{proposition-finite-set-of-points-of-codim-1-in-affine}
Let $X$ be a separated scheme such that every quasi-compact open
has a finite number of irreducible components. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_r \in X$
be points such that $\mathcal{O}_{X, x_i}$ is Noetherian
of dimension $\leq 1$. Then there exists an affine open subscheme
of $X$ containing all of $x_1, \ldots, x_r$.

\label{lemma-ext-2-zero}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Assume $\Ext^2_\mathcal{A}(B, A) = 0$
for any pair of objects $A$, $B$ of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then any object $K$ of $D^b(\mathcal{A})$ is isomorphic to the direct
sum of its cohomologies: $K \cong \bigoplus H^i(K)[-i]$.

hypotheses: $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a Koszul-regular finitely presented closed immersion of codimension $c$.
formulation.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume further that $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Then $\mathcal H^j_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})=0$ for $j<c$, and the local-cohomology Gysin morphism induces maps
$$\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\longrightarrow H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}).$$
These are compatible with the maps induced by the de Rham differential: for each $p,q$, $d\circ\gamma^{p,q}=\gamma^{p+1,q}\circ d$ (the target in the first composite has differential form degree $p+c+1$).

Both geometric conditions, the cohomology shift c, and compatibility survive.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-projective}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is locally projective, and
\item there exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
such that the $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$-module
$\mathcal{F}(U_i)$ is projective for every $i$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, if $X = \Spec(A)$ and $\mathcal{F} = \widetilde{M}$
then $\mathcal{F}$ is locally projective if and only if $M$ is a projective
$A$-module.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\operatorname{Spec}(k) \ar[rr] \ar[rd] & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
Assume that the image point $s \in S$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to S$ is
a closed point and that the field extension $k/\kappa(s)$ is finite.
Then $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ is a finite morphism. If $\kappa(s) = k$
then $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ is a closed immersion.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L3385–3403 assumes X decent, closed image s in S and FINITE k/κ(s); then Spec(k)→X is FINITE, and under the ADDITIONAL equality k=κ(s) it is a CLOSED IMMERSION. The proposal preserves this strengthening and does not assume the field equality by default.

phase3.reason: The image is closed; its reduced singleton closed subspace is a field by decency, and a finite field extension gives the finite map, with equality of residue fields giving a closed immersion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homomorphism-limit}
Let $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$, $(N_i, \nu_{ij})$ be
systems of $R$-modules over the same preordered set.
A morphism of systems $\Phi = (\phi_i)$ from $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$ to
$(N_i, \nu_{ij})$ induces a unique homomorphism
$$
\colim \phi_i : \colim M_i \longrightarrow \colim N_i
$$
such that
$$
\xymatrix{
M_i \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\phi_i} & \colim M_i \ar[d]^{\colim \phi_i} \\
N_i \ar[r] & \colim N_i
}
$$
commutes for all $i \in I$.

Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A $k$-linear *cohomological functor* $H:\mathcal T^{op}\to\mathrm{Vect}_k$ is contravariant and yields a long exact sequence under every shifted distinguished triangle. *Homological* means the analogous covariant long exact property. An object $C$ is *compact* if maps from $C$ commute with arbitrary small direct sums; a triangulated category is *compactly generated* if a set of compact objects detects zero objects.

Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$ which is regular.
Let $G : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \text{Vect}_k$
be a $k$-linear homological functor such that
$$
\sum\nolimits_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \dim_k G(E[n]) < \infty
$$
for all $E \in D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then $G$ is isomorphic to a functor
of the form $E \mapsto \Hom_X(K, E)$ for some $K \in D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

**Scope and interpretation:** Regularity of X identifies bounded coherent complexes with perfect objects; the covariant representer K is perfect.

phase3.reason: Duality on perfect complexes converts a covariant functor into a representable contravariant functor and back using perfect biduality.

\label{lemma-homological-representable}
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$ which is regular.
Let $G : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \text{Vect}_k$
be a $k$-linear homological functor such that
$$
\sum\nolimits_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \dim_k G(E[n]) < \infty
$$
for all $E \in D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then $G$ is isomorphic to a functor
of the form $E \mapsto \Hom_X(K, E)$ for some $K \in D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

\label{lemma-locally-normal}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is normal.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is normal.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is normal.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is normal.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is normal then every open subscheme
is normal.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $I \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ be an injective object.
Let $I^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of injectives in $\mathcal{A}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I^\bullet$ computes $RF$ relative to $\text{Qis}^{+}(\mathcal{A})$
for any exact functor $F : K^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \to \mathcal{D}$
into any triangulated category $\mathcal{D}$.
\item $I$ is right acyclic for any additive functor
$F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ into any abelian category $\mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-finite-locally-free-reduced}
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then the equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{lemma-finite-locally-free} are also equivalent to

the function
$$
\rho_\mathcal{F} : X \to \mathbf{Z}, \quad
x \longmapsto
\dim_{\kappa(x)} \mathcal{F}_x \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x)
$$
is locally constant in the Zariski topology on $X$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-hilb}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to B$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. If $f$ is of finite presentation and separated, then
$\Hilbfunctor_{X/B}$ is an algebraic space locally of finite
presentation over $B$.

formulation.statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Assume for each $j\in J$ the subfamily $\{g_i:U_i\to V_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ is an fpqc covering of $V_j$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. The underlying morphism of disjoint unions $\coprod_iU_i\to\coprod_jV_j$ is an fpqc covering, and the family-to-coproduct equivalence identifies the indicated pullback with pullback along that morphism.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{V_j \to S\}_{j \in J}$,
be families of morphisms with target $S$.
Let $\alpha : I \to J$, $\text{id} : S \to S$ and
$g_i : U_i \to V_{\alpha(i)}$ be a morphism of families
of maps with fixed target, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-morphism-coverings}.
Assume that for each $j \in J$ the family
$\{g_i : U_i \to V_j\}_{\alpha(i) = j}$ is an fpqc
covering of $V_j$. Then the pullback functor
$$
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{V}
\longrightarrow
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{U}
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback-family} is fully faithful.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclicity}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $f : L \to K$ be a morphism of
simplicial objects of $\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $i < n$ the morphism $L_i \to K_i$ is an isomorphism.
\item The morphism $L_n \to K_n$ is surjective after sheafification.
\item The canonical map $L \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n L$ is an isomorphism.
\item The canonical map $K \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n K$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H_i(f) : H_i(L) \to H_i(K)$ is an isomorphism.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{N}$ be an invertible sheaves on $X$.
Then
$$
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap \alpha  + c_1(\mathcal{N}) \cap \alpha =
c_1(\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{N}) \cap \alpha
$$
in $\mathrm{CH}_k(X)$ for every $\alpha \in Z_{k + 1}(X)$. Moreover,
$c_1(\mathcal{O}_X) \cap \alpha = 0$ for all $\alpha$.

\label{lemma-c1-cap-additive}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{N}$ be an invertible sheaves on $X$.
Then
$$
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap \alpha  + c_1(\mathcal{N}) \cap \alpha =
c_1(\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{N}) \cap \alpha
$$
in $\CH_k(X)$ for every $\alpha \in Z_{k + 1}(X)$. Moreover,
$c_1(\mathcal{O}_X) \cap \alpha = 0$ for all $\alpha$.

Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-tor-1-zero}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M \to M'$ be a map of $R$-modules with
$M$ of finite presentation
such that $\text{Tor}_1^R(M, N) \to \text{Tor}_1^R(M', N)$ is zero for all
$R$-modules $N$. Then $M \to M'$ factors through a free $R$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-trivial-cech}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ be an open covering.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$

Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$, define its support as $\{s\in S:\mathcal F_{\bar s}\ne0\}$ for any/every geometric point above $s$. For an étale $U\to S$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal F(U)$, the *support of $\sigma$* is $U\setminus W_\sigma$, where $W_\sigma$ is the largest **Zariski open** of $U$ on which $\sigma$ is zero. The support of an arbitrary abelian sheaf need **not** be closed, while support of an individual section is closed. A **subterminal sheaf** means a subsheaf of the terminal one-point sheaf on $S_{\acute etale}$; $h_W$ denotes the representable étale sheaf of an open subscheme $W\subseteq S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-isomorphism}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point with
image $s \in S$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, x} = \mathcal{O}_{S, s}$,
\item $S$ is reduced,
\item $X \to S$ is of finite type, and
\item $S$ has finitely many irreducible components,
\end{enumerate}
then there exists an open neighbourhood $U$
of $x$ such that $f|_U$ is an open immersion.

one morphism to $U$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $\mathcal{C}/U$.
The canonical maps $\mathcal{F} \to j_U^{-1}j_{U!}\mathcal{F}$
and $j_U^{-1}j_{U*}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$ are
isomorphisms.

A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

For a first-order thickening of ringed spaces with ideal $\mathcal I$, an extension of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal K$ on the thickened space means a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O_{X'}$-modules, with $\mathcal I$ annihilating the two end terms. It induces an $\mathcal O_X$-linear action map $c_{\mathcal F'}:\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$, defined by $c_{\mathcal F'}(a\otimes s)=a\tilde s$ for a local lift $\tilde s\in\mathcal F'$ of $s$. Isomorphisms of extensions fix their identified end terms.

Let $i : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (X', \mathcal{O}_{X'})$
be a first order thickening of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules and set
$\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map.
There exists an element
$$
o(\varphi) \in
\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{O}_X}(Li^*\mathcal{F}',
\mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}')
$$
whose vanishing is a necessary and sufficient condition for the
existence of a lift of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$.

formulation.statement:
For any ringed site (C,O), a **strictly perfect complex** E^bullet is a **bounded** complex whose every term is a direct summand of a finite free O-module (source Definition strictly-perfect at 11716–11724). For U∈C a strictly perfect complex on (C/U,O_U) uses the restricted ring; a finite locally projective module is not being assumed globally free. The two alternatives are **independent**: (1) the target complex F^bullet is acyclic; (2) E^j=0 for j<a and H^j(F^bullet)=0 for j≥a. Each yields a possibly different covering with nullhomotopy of α after restriction.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object
of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\alpha : \mathcal{E}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$
be a morphism of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect and $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$
acyclic. Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that each
$\alpha|_{U_i}$ is homotopic to zero.
\item Let $\alpha : \mathcal{E}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$
be a morphism of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect, $\mathcal{E}^i = 0$
for $i < a$, and $H^i(\mathcal{F}^\bullet) = 0$ for $i \geq a$.
Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that each
$\alpha|_{U_i}$ is homotopic to zero.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-local-homotopy}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object
of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\alpha : \mathcal{E}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$
be a morphism of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect and $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$
acyclic. Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that each
$\alpha|_{U_i}$ is homotopic to zero.
\item Let $\alpha : \mathcal{E}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$
be a morphism of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect, $\mathcal{E}^i = 0$
for $i < a$, and $H^i(\mathcal{F}^\bullet) = 0$ for $i \geq a$.
Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that each
$\alpha|_{U_i}$ is homotopic to zero.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-ses-ass}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
be a short exact sequence of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$.
Then
$\text{Ass}(\mathcal{F}_2) \subset
\text{Ass}(\mathcal{F}_1) \cup \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F}_3)$
and
$\text{Ass}(\mathcal{F}_1) \subset \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F}_2)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-effective-Cartier-makes-dimension-drop}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $D \subset S$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
Let $s \in D$.
If $\dim_s(S) < \infty$, then $\dim_s(D) < \dim_s(S)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compose-tensor}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{A}'$, $\mathcal{A}''$ be differential graded
$\mathcal{O}$-algebras. Let $\mathcal{N}$ and $\mathcal{N}'$ be a
differential graded $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}')$-bimodule
and $(\mathcal{A}', \mathcal{A}'')$-bimodule. Assume
that the canonical map
$$
\mathcal{N} \otimes_{\mathcal{A}'}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{N}'
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{N} \otimes_{\mathcal{A}'} \mathcal{N}'
$$
in $D(\mathcal{A}'', \text{d})$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
Then we have
$$
(\mathcal{M}
\otimes_\mathcal{A}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{N})
\otimes_{\mathcal{A}'}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{N}'
=
\mathcal{M}
\otimes_\mathcal{A}^\mathbf{L}
(\mathcal{N} \otimes_{\mathcal{A}'} \mathcal{N}')
$$
as functors $D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}) \to D(\mathcal{A}'', \text{d})$.

For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a Koszul regular closed immersion.
Then there exists a surjective smooth morphism $X' \to X$ such
that the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$ of $i$ is
a regular immersion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-koszul-regular-smooth-locally-regular}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a Koszul regular closed immersion.
Then there exists a surjective smooth morphism $X' \to X$ such
that the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$ of $i$ is
a regular immersion.

\label{lemma-compare-standard}
Let $R \to A$ be a ring map of finite presentation.
Let $a \in A$. Consider the following conditions on $a$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A_a$ is smooth over $R$,
\item $A_a$ is smooth over $R$ and $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ is stably free,
\item $A_a$ is smooth over $R$ and $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ is free,
\item $A_a$ is standard smooth over $R$,
\item $a$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$,
\item $a$ is elementary standard in $A$ over $R$.
\end{enumerate}
Then we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (4) $\Rightarrow$ (3) $\Rightarrow$ (2) $\Rightarrow$ (1),
\item[(b)] (6) $\Rightarrow$ (5),
\item[(c)] (6) $\Rightarrow$ (4),
\item[(d)] (5) $\Rightarrow$ (2),
\item[(e)] (2) $\Rightarrow$ the elements $a^e$, $e \geq e_0$ are
strictly standard in $A$ over $R$,
\item[(f)] (4) $\Rightarrow$ the elements $a^e$, $e \geq e_0$ are
elementary standard in $A$ over $R$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
The kth Fitting ideal is locally generated by the $(m-k)$-minors of a relation matrix for a presentation with m module generators; the conventions give the unit ideal for nonpositive minor size. The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module. Let $Z_k \subset S$ be the closed
subscheme cut out by $\text{Fit}_k(\mathcal{F})$, see
Section \ref{section-fitting-ideals}.
Let $S' \to S$ be the blowup of $S$ in $Z_k$ and let
$\mathcal{F}'$ be the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$.
Then $\mathcal{F}'$ can locally be generated by $\leq k$
sections.

sections.

\label{proposition-asymptotic-riemann-roch}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $d$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
$$
\dim_k \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) \sim c n^d + l.o.t.
$$
where $c = \deg_\mathcal{L}(X)/d!$ is a positive constant.

\label{lemma-blowup-complex}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ be perfect.
Let $U \subset X$ be a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme
such that $H^i(E|_U)$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r_i$
for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $b : X' \to X$ such that
$H^i(Lb^*E)$ is a perfect $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module
of tor dimension $\leq 1$ for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-assassin-in-neighbourhood}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\xi \in \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$ and set
$Z = \overline{\{\xi\}} \subset X$.
If $f$ is locally of finite type and $\mathcal{F}$ is a
finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module, then there exists a nonempty
open $V \subset Z$ such that for every $s \in f(V)$ the generic
points of $V_s$ are elements of $\text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-j-shriek-reflects-exactness}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. A complex of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
$\mathcal{G}_1 \to \mathcal{G}_2 \to \mathcal{G}_3$ is exact
if and only if
$j_{U!}\mathcal{G}_1 \to j_{U!}\mathcal{G}_2 \to j_{U!}\mathcal{G}_3$
is exact as a sequence of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.

\item Any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules is a quotient of

a flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be an irreducible, smooth, proper $k$-scheme of dimension $d$. Let $i:Z=\{x\}\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced closed subscheme defined by a $k$-rational point. The immersion has codimension $d$, so the Hodge Gysin map
$$\gamma^{0,0}:H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=k\longrightarrow H^d(X,\Omega^d_{X/k})$$
is defined. Its value $\gamma^{0,0}(1)$ is nonzero.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L5574–5583 assumes field k and irreducible SMOOTH PROPER X of dimension d, with Z a REDUCED CLOSED SUBSCHEME consisting of a k-RATIONAL point. It asserts the Hodge Gysin image of 1 in H^d(X,Ω^d_{X/k}) is NONZERO. The proposal retains properness, rationality, and top Hodge cohomology; there is no characteristic-zero hypothesis.

phase3.reason: Serre/Grothendieck duality identifies the dual of the top Hodge Gysin map with the class of a local Ext extension at the rational point. On a smooth local chart this class is the local cohomology Čech fraction 1/(f_1…f_d) for a regular parameter sequence, which is nonzero. Minor indexing/notation slips in the source do not affect the nonzero local class.

\label{lemma-class-of-a-point}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an irreducible smooth proper scheme over $k$
of dimension $d$. Let $Z \subset X$ be the reduced closed subscheme consisting
of a single $k$-rational point $x$. Then the image of
$1 \in k = H^0(Z, \mathcal{O}_Z) = H^0(Z, \Omega^0_{Z/k})$
by the map $H^0(Z, \Omega^0_{Z/k}) \to H^d(X, \Omega^d_{X/k})$
of Remark \ref{remark-how-to-use} is nonzero.

source.label: lemma-localization-abelian
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localization-abelian}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $S$ is a left multiplicative system, then
the category $S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ has cokernels and the functor
$Q : \mathcal{A} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ commutes with them.
\item If $S$ is a right multiplicative system, then
the category $S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ has kernels and the functor
$Q : \mathcal{A} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ commutes with them.
\item If $S$ is a multiplicative system, then the category
$S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ is abelian and the functor
$Q : \mathcal{A} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ is exact.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Assume $R$ is reduced and has finitely many
minimal primes. Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a normal ring,
\item $R$ is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions, and
\item $R$ is a finite product of normal domains.
\end{enumerate}
A normal domain means a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. A normal ring means a ring whose localization at every prime ideal is a normal domain.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. Assume $p$ is representable
by algebraic spaces and an open immersion. Then $p$ is limit preserving
on objects.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-over-space}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $U$, $U'$ be schemes over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $U \to U'$ is an \'etale morphism of schemes, and
if $U' \to X$ is an \'etale morphism from $U'$ to $X$, then the
composition $U \to X$ is an \'etale morphism from $U$ to $X$.
\item If $\varphi : U \to X$ and $\varphi' : U' \to X$ are
\'etale morphisms towards $X$, and if $\chi : U \to U'$ is a
morphism of schemes such that $\varphi = \varphi' \circ \chi$,
then $\chi$ is an \'etale morphism of schemes.
\item If $\chi : U \to U'$ is a surjective \'etale morphism
of schemes and $\varphi' : U' \to X$ is a morphism such that
$\varphi = \varphi' \circ \chi$ is \'etale, then $\varphi'$
is \'etale.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-characterize-integral-ideal}
Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $A = \sum I^nt^n \subset R[t]$ be the
subring of the polynomial ring
generated by $R \oplus It \subset R[t]$.
An element $s \in S$ is integral over $I$ if
and only if the element $st \in S[t]$
is integral over $A$.

Fields K over S have a given map Spec(K)→S, with X(K)=Mor_S(Spec K,X).

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the map $X(K) \to Y(K)$ is injective for every field $K$ over $S$
\item for every morphism $Y' \to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$
the induced map $|Y' \times_Y X| \to |Y'|$ is injective, and
\item the diagonal morphism $X \to X \times_Y X$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For any algebraic-space morphism f:X→Y over S, universal field-valued injectivity X(K)→Y(K), injectivity of underlying point maps after every algebraic-space base change, and surjectivity of its relative diagonal are equivalent. All three original alternatives are preserved.

phase3.reason: The field-valued-point injectivity criterion shows arbitrary base changes have injective underlying-point maps. Conversely any pair of K-valued lifts that agree in Y become equal over a common field extension and descend by the fpqc sheaf property. Surjectivity of the diagonal is equivalent to pointwise fibres having at most one point after all base changes.

$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of schemes. Let $W \subset X$, resp.\ $W' \subset X'$
be the open subscheme of points where $f$, resp.\ $f'$ is smooth.
Then $W' = (g')^{-1}(W)$ if
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, or
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $g$ is flat.
\end{enumerate}

The two alternative assumptions are retained.

phase3.reason: Geometric smoothness of fibres is stable under residue-field extension; base-change flatness and the smooth-at-a-point criterion identify and descend the smooth locus.

\label{lemma-intersection-in-projective-space}
Let $k$ be a field and $n \geq 0$. Let $X, Y \subset \mathbf{P}^n_k$
be nonempty closed subsets. If $\dim(X) = r$ and $\dim(Y) = s$ and
$r + s \geq n$, then $X \cap Y$ is nonempty and
$\dim(X \cap Y) \geq r + s - n$.

\item The support of $\sigma$ is closed in $U$.

the supports of $\sigma, \sigma' \in \mathcal{F}(U)$.
\item If $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is a map of
abelian sheaves on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$, then the support of $\varphi(\sigma)$
is contained in the support of $\sigma \in \mathcal{F}(U)$.
\item The support of $\mathcal{F}$ is the union of the images of the
supports of all local sections of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is surjective then the support
of $\mathcal{G}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is injective then the support
of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $U \in \Ob(S_\mathrm{\acute etale})$ and $\sigma \in \mathcal{F}(U)$.

\item The support of $\sigma$ is closed in $U$.

\label{lemma-support-section-closed}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $S_\etale$.
Let $U \in \Ob(S_\etale)$ and $\sigma \in \mathcal{F}(U)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The support of $\sigma$ is closed in $U$.
\item The support of $\sigma + \sigma'$ is contained in the union of
the supports of $\sigma, \sigma' \in \mathcal{F}(U)$.
\item If $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is a map of
abelian sheaves on $S_\etale$, then the support of $\varphi(\sigma)$
is contained in the support of $\sigma \in \mathcal{F}(U)$.
\item The support of $\mathcal{F}$ is the union of the images of the
supports of all local sections of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is surjective then the support
of $\mathcal{G}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is injective then the support
of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-perfect-on-locally-ringed}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $E$ be an object of
$D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Assume that all stalks $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
are local rings. Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is perfect,
\item there exists an open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
$E|_{U_i}$ can be represented by a finite complex of finite locally
free $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules, and
\item there exists an open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
$E|_{U_i}$ can be represented by a finite complex of finite
free $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-enough-acyclics}
\begin{slogan}
A functor on Abelian categories is extended to the (bounded below or above)
derived category by resolving with a complex that is acyclic for that functor.
\end{slogan}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be an additive functor of
abelian categories.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If every object of $\mathcal{A}$ injects into an object acyclic
for $RF$, then $RF$ is defined on all of $K^{+}(\mathcal{A})$
and we obtain an exact functor
$$
RF : D^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \longrightarrow D^{+}(\mathcal{B})
$$
see (\ref{equation-everywhere}). Moreover, any bounded below complex
$A^\bullet$ whose terms are acyclic for $RF$ computes $RF$.
\item If every object of $\mathcal{A}$ is quotient of
an object acyclic for $LF$, then $LF$ is defined on all of
$K^{-}(\mathcal{A})$ and we obtain an exact functor
$$
LF : D^{-}(\mathcal{A}) \longrightarrow D^{-}(\mathcal{B})
$$
see (\ref{equation-everywhere}). Moreover, any bounded above complex
$A^\bullet$ whose terms are acyclic for $LF$ computes $LF$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ is syntomic and induces a surjective map on spectra, or
\item $A \to B$ is a faithfully flat local complete intersection, or
\item $A \to B$ is faithfully flat of finite type with Gorenstein fibres.
\end{enumerate}
Then $K \in D(A)$ is a dualizing complex for $A$ if and only if
$K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B$ is a dualizing complex for $B$.
Syntomic means flat, finitely presented and locally complete intersection. The three alternatives all include faithful flatness and ensure that the relative shriek complex is invertible; ascension and descension are separate implications.

The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. formulation.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ is syntomic and induces a surjective map on spectra, or
\item $A \to B$ is a faithfully flat local complete intersection, or
\item $A \to B$ is faithfully flat of finite type with Gorenstein fibres.
\end{enumerate}
Then $K \in D(A)$ is a dualizing complex for $A$ if and only if
$K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B$ is a dualizing complex for $B$.

**Scope and interpretation:** Syntomic means flat, finitely presented and locally complete intersection. The three alternatives all include faithful flatness and ensure that the relative shriek complex is invertible; ascension and descension are separate implications.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Dualizing property descends and ascends under any one of: syntomic surjective-on-spectra, faithfully flat local complete intersection, or faithfully flat finite type with Gorenstein fibres. The iff and all three disjuncts remain.

phase3.reason: Under each stated faithfully flat hypothesis the relative shriek complex is invertible; tensoring with it preserves dualizing status, and the source invokes established ascent and descent criteria.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subscheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U$ is retrocompact in $X$,
\item $U$ is quasi-compact,
\item $U$ is a finite union of affine opens, and
\item there exists a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ such that $X \setminus U = V(\mathcal{I})$
(set theoretically).
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-base-change-tensor-with-flat}
Consider a cartesian diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_{g'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{S'}$-module
flat over $S$. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
For any $i \geq 0$ there is an identification
$$
\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S'}} g^*R^if_*\mathcal{F} =
R^if'_*\left((f')^*\mathcal{G}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}} (g')^*\mathcal{F}\right)
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-localization-functor}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with enough injectives.
Let $\mathcal{I}^f \subset \text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$
denote the strictly full additive subcategory whose objects are
the filtered injective objects. The canonical functor
$$
K^{+}(\mathcal{I}^f)
\longrightarrow
DF^{+}(\mathcal{A})
$$
is exact, fully faithful and essentially surjective, i.e., an
equivalence of triangulated categories. Furthermore the diagrams
$$
\xymatrix{
K^{+}(\mathcal{I}^f) \ar[d]_{\text{gr}^p} \ar[r] &
DF^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \ar[d]_{\text{gr}^p} \\
K^{+}(\mathcal{I}) \ar[r] &
D^{+}(\mathcal{A})
}
\quad
\xymatrix{
K^{+}(\mathcal{I}^f) \ar[d]^{\text{forget }F} \ar[r] &
DF^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \ar[d]^{\text{forget }F} \\
K^{+}(\mathcal{I}) \ar[r] &
D^{+}(\mathcal{A})
}
$$
are commutative, where $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{A}$ is the
strictly full additive subcategory whose objects are
the injective objects.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-application-H0}
Let $I \subset \mathfrak a$ be ideals of a Noetherian ring $A$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent module on
$U = \Spec(A) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $I$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item if $x \in \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F})$, $x \not \in V(I)$,
$\overline{\{x\}} \cap V(I) \not \subset V(\mathfrak a)$, and
$z \in V(\mathfrak a) \cap \overline{\{x\}}$, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{\overline{\{x\}}, z}) > \text{cd}(A, I) + 1$,
\item for $x \in U$ with $\overline{\{x\}} \cap V(I) \subset V(\mathfrak a)$
we have $\text{depth}(\mathcal{F}_x) \geq 2$,
\end{enumerate}
Then we obtain an isomorphism
$$
H^0(U, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
\lim H^0(U, \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F})
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-same-cohomology}
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a continuous and cocontinuous
functor of sites. Let $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be the corresponding morphism of topoi. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $M$ in $D(\mathcal{D})$ we have
$R\Gamma(U, g^{-1}M) = R\Gamma(u(U), M)$.
\item If $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$ is a sheaf of rings and
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C} = g^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$, then
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ we have
$R\Gamma(U, g^*M) = R\Gamma(u(U), M)$.
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: Two representatives of the rational map agree on a dense open of their intersection. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume $X$ is reduced and $Y$ is separated over $S$. Let

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $x \to y$ is surjective, then for every $z \to y$ the
projection $x \times_y z \to z$ is surjective.
\item If $x \to y$ is injective, then for every $x \to z$ the
morphism $z \to z \amalg_x y$ is injective.
\end{enumerate}

$$
\omega_X \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{Q} \to 0
$$
of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with $H^1(X, \mathcal{Q}) = 0$
(for example if $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{Q})) = 0$), then
either $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ or
$\mathcal{F} = \omega_X \oplus \mathcal{Q}$.

phase3.reason: The complete proof uses H^1(omega_X) dual to H^0(O_X)=k; when H^1(F) is nonzero, the induced cohomology map is an isomorphism, and the representing property of omega_X supplies a retraction, splitting the extension.

$$
\omega_X \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{Q} \to 0
$$
of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with $H^1(X, \mathcal{Q}) = 0$

$\mathcal{F} = \omega_X \oplus \mathcal{Q}$.

\label{lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective $\mathcal{O}$-module, i.e., an injective
object of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$. Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$

source.label: lemma-quotient-kolmogorov
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quotient-kolmogorov}
Suppose that $s, t : R \to U$ and $\pi : U \to X$ are continuous maps
of topological spaces such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\pi$ is open,
\item $U$ is sober,
\item $s, t$ have finite fibres,
\item generalizations lift along $s, t$,
\item $(t, s)(R) \subset U \times U$ is an equivalence relation on $U$ and
$X$ is the quotient of $U$ by this equivalence relation (as a set).
\end{enumerate}
Then $X$ is Kolmogorov.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), a complex E^bullet is **perfect** when after a covering of every site object it has a quasi-isomorphism from a **strictly perfect** complex (bounded, termwise direct summand of finite free O-modules); a derived object is perfect if represented by such a complex (source Definition perfect at 12734–12746). A perfect object is **not assumed globally bounded** unless the topos is quasi-compact. Its relation to pseudo-coherence and local finite Tor dimension is an equivalence only where stated, not an inherited hypothesis. **Locally** finite Tor dimension requires possibly different intervals after different local covers and does not assert globally finite Tor-amplitude.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is perfect, and
\item $E$ is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite tor dimension.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Perfectness is equivalent to pseudo-coherence and LOCALLY finite Tor dimension; the second condition does not force one globally uniform interval. Both directions encoded as equivalence.

phase3.reason: The proof derives local finite Tor dimension from a strictly perfect representative, and conversely applies the preceding finite-amplitude plus pseudo-coherence criterion.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd]_j \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume $X \to S$ smooth and $i$ and $j$ immersions.
If $i$ is a Koszul-regular (resp.\ $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular)
immersion, then so is $j$.

Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism
of ringed spaces. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finitely presented and $f$ is flat,

$$
f^*\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_Y}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})
\longrightarrow
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(f^*\mathcal{F}, f^*\mathcal{G})
$$
is an isomorphism.
