hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Y$ be a disjoint union of spectra of
zero dimensional local rings over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a monomorphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $f$ is representable, i.e., $X$ is a scheme.

\label{lemma-locally-Japanese}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is Japanese.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the domain $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Japanese.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
such that each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Japanese.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is Japanese.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is Japanese then every open subscheme
is Japanese.

formulation.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of Noetherian schemes: (1) if $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ are Deligne systems with constant restriction values $K,L$ on $U$, any morphism $\alpha:K\to L$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ extends to a **unique morphism of pro-objects** $(K_n)\to(L_n)$ that restricts to $\alpha$ (not necessarily a levelwise map with matching indices); (2) every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ occurs as the common restriction value of some Deligne system on $X$; and (3) such a pro-object is unique up to the unique pro-isomorphism inducing the identity on $K$. Thus $K\mapsto(K_n)$ defines the coherent pro-extension functor $Rj_!$.

The formulation explicitly avoids claiming a unique levelwise sequence map.

source.label: lemma-extension-by-zero
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extension-by-zero}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ be Deligne systems.
Let $K$ and $L$ be the values of the constant systems
$(K_n|_U)$ and $(L_n|_U)$. Given a morphism $\alpha : K \to L$
of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$
there is a unique morphism of pro-systems $(K_n) \to (L_n)$
of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\alpha$.
\item Given $K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$ there exists a
Deligne system $(K_n)$ such that $(K_n|_U)$ is constant
with value $K$.
\item The pro-object $(K_n)$ of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
of (2) is unique up to unique isomorphism (as a pro-object).
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-right-derived
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-right-derived}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras on
$(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Then any exact functor
$$
T : K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})) \longrightarrow \mathcal{D}
$$
of triangulated categories has a right derived extension
$RT : D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}) \to \mathcal{D}$
whose value on a graded injective and K-injective
differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-module $\mathcal{I}$
is $T(\mathcal{I})$.

source.label: lemma-locally-P-characterize
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-P-characterize}
Let $P$ be a local property of ring maps.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is locally of type $P$.
\item For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ we have $P(\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U))$.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is locally of type $P$.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that $P(\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i))$ holds, for all
$j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is locally of type $P$ then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally of type $P$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-coherent}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$
be coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $U \subset X$ be open and
let $\varphi : \mathcal{F}|_U \to \mathcal{G}|_U$ be an
$\mathcal{O}_U$-module map. Then there exists a coherent
submodule $\mathcal{F}' \subset \mathcal{F}$ agreeing with
$\mathcal{F}$ over $U$ such that $\varphi$ extends to
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}$.

\label{lemma-exact-category-stably-free}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $0 \to P' \to P \to P'' \to 0$ be a short
exact sequence of finite projective $R$-modules. If $2$ out of $3$
of these modules are stably free, then so is the third.

The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

Let $A \to B$ be a ring map such that $B = B \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B$.
Then $L_{B/A} = 0$ in $D(B)$.

Let $R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $N$ be an $S$-module.
Let $S \to S'$ be a ring map.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to S$ is of finite presentation and $N$ is of finite presentation
over $S$,
\item $N$ is flat over $R$,
\item $S \to S'$ is flat, and
\item the image of $\Spec(S') \to \Spec(S)$ contains
all primes $\mathfrak q$ such that $\mathfrak q$ is an associated prime
of $N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ where $\mathfrak p$ is the inverse

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-universally-flat}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $N$ be an $S$-module.
Let $S \to S'$ be a ring map.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to S$ is of finite presentation and $N$ is of finite presentation
over $S$,
\item $N$ is flat over $R$,
\item $S \to S'$ is flat, and
\item the image of $\Spec(S') \to \Spec(S)$ contains
all primes $\mathfrak q$ such that $\mathfrak q$ is an associated prime
of $N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ where $\mathfrak p$ is the inverse
image of $\mathfrak q$ in $R$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $N \to N \otimes_S S'$ is $R$-universally injective.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category which has finite limits.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $n$ the functor $\text{sk}_n : \text{Simp}(\mathcal{C})
\to \text{Simp}_n(\mathcal{C})$ has a right adjoint $\text{cosk}_n$.
\item For every $n' \geq n$ the functor
$\text{sk}_n : \text{Simp}_{n'}(\mathcal{C}) \to \text{Simp}_n(\mathcal{C})$
has a right adjoint, namely $\text{sk}_{n'}\text{cosk}_n$.
\item For every $m \geq n \geq 0$ and every $n$-truncated simplicial
object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$\text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_m \text{cosk}_n U = \text{cosk}_n U$.
\item If $U$ is a simplicial object of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_nU$
is an isomorphism for some $n \geq 0$, then the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_mU$
is an isomorphism for all $m \geq n$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cosk-up}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category which has finite limits.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $n$ the functor $\text{sk}_n : \text{Simp}(\mathcal{C})
\to \text{Simp}_n(\mathcal{C})$ has a right adjoint $\text{cosk}_n$.
\item For every $n' \geq n$ the functor
$\text{sk}_n : \text{Simp}_{n'}(\mathcal{C}) \to \text{Simp}_n(\mathcal{C})$
has a right adjoint, namely $\text{sk}_{n'}\text{cosk}_n$.
\item For every $m \geq n \geq 0$ and every $n$-truncated simplicial
object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$\text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_m \text{cosk}_n U = \text{cosk}_n U$.
\item If $U$ is a simplicial object of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_nU$
is an isomorphism for some $n \geq 0$, then the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_mU$
is an isomorphism for all $m \geq n$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$ be a map of sheaves of rings on $X$.

are differential operators of order $k$ and $k'$, then $D' \circ D$ is a
differential operator of order $k + k'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-kahler-different}
Consider a cartesian diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
Y' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r] & Y \ar[d]^f \\
X' \ar[r]^g & X
}
$$
with $f$ locally of finite type. Let $R \subset Y$, resp.\ $R' \subset Y'$
be the closed subscheme cut out by the K\"ahler different of $f$, resp.\ $f'$.
Then $Y' \to Y$ induces an isomorphism $R' \to R \times_Y Y'$.

formulation.statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *étale-local on the source* if $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ exactly when all composites $X_i\to X\to Y$ have it, for any étale covering $\{X_i\to X\}$. It is *étale-local on the target* if the corresponding equivalence holds after étale base change on $Y$. For any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and étale covering $\{a_i:X_i\to X\}$, $f$ is locally quasi-finite if and only if each $f\circ a_i$ is locally quasi-finite.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The pinned descent.tex 6963 assertion is that LOCALLY quasi-finite morphisms are étale-local on the SOURCE. The final formulation retains that exact local (not global quasi-finite) condition, both directions, and precomposition along any étale source-cover, with no target-covering assumption.

phase3.reason: The proof checks Zariski-locality and closure under precomposition with étale maps, and for affine surjective étale ascent uses finite-type descent plus finite fibres to conclude quasi-finiteness; this verifies the criterion's final condition.

If $p:X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, then $q:Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Separately, if $p$ is locally of finite type, then $q$ is locally of finite type.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-nilpotent-henselian}
Let $(A, I)$ be a pair with $I$ locally nilpotent. Then the functor
$B \mapsto B/IB$ induces an equivalence between the category of
\'etale algebras over $A$ and the category of \'etale algebras over $A/I$.
Moreover, the pair is henselian.

The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a characteristic-$p$ ring $A$ ($p$ prime), the Frobenius endomorphism is $F_A(a)=a^p$. Given a characteristic-$p$ ring map $A\to B$, its Frobenius square $(F_A,F_B)$ induces maps on the functorial simplicial standard resolution $P_\bullet$ and the cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$; these maps are generally semilinear over $B$ under $F_B$. A homotopy of simplicial maps means simplicial homotopy, and a chain homotopy on a complex induces the same map in its derived category.
formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a characteristic-$p$ ring $A$ ($p$ prime), the Frobenius endomorphism is $F_A(a)=a^p$. Given a characteristic-$p$ ring map $A\to B$, its Frobenius square $(F_A,F_B)$ induces maps on the functorial simplicial standard resolution $P_\bullet$ and the cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$; these maps are generally semilinear over $B$ under $F_B$. A homotopy of simplicial maps means simplicial homotopy, and a chain homotopy on a complex induces the same map in its derived category.

Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism
and assume that $p = 0$ in $A$. If $A$ and $B$ are perfect, then
$L_{B/A}$ is zero in $D(B)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L1818–1823 asserts that when p=0 in A and the characteristic-p rings A,B are BOTH PERFECT (Frobenius automorphisms), then L_{B/A}=0 in D(B). The proposal includes both perfectness hypotheses and the whole-complex vanishing conclusion, not merely Ω=0.

phase3.reason: The perfect Frobenius map acts both invertibly and trivially on the cotangent complex, forcing that complex to vanish.

\label{lemma-include}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Consider the functor
$i : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{PMod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
It is a left exact functor with right derived functors given by
$$
R^pi(\mathcal{F}) = \underline{H}^p(\mathcal{F}) :
U \longmapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})
$$
see discussion in Section \ref{section-locality}.

source.label: lemma-slice-smooth-once
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-slice-smooth-once}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point with image $s \in S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is smooth at $x$, and
\item the map
$$
\Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x)
\longrightarrow
\Omega_{\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)}
$$
has a nonzero kernel.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an affine open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
and an effective Cartier divisor $D \subset U$ containing $x$ such that
$D \to S$ is smooth.

The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is a G-scheme.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is a G-ring.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is a G-ring.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is a G-scheme.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is a G-scheme then every open subscheme is a
G-scheme.

source.label: lemma-locally-G-scheme
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-G-scheme}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is a G-scheme.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is a G-ring.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is a G-ring.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is a G-scheme.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is a G-scheme then every open subscheme is a
G-scheme.

formulation.statement:
An inverse system $(M_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition when, for every fixed $n$, the images of the transition maps $M_m\to M_n$ stabilize for all sufficiently large $m$. The graded ring $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ is the associated graded ring of the $I$-adic filtration. For a site $\mathcal C$ and ring $A$ with ideal $I$, an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules $\cdots\to\mathcal F_3\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_1$ is assumed to have $\mathcal F_n\cong\mathcal F_{n+1}/I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$. The graded module is built from **degree $p+1$** cohomology of the submodules $I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Assume
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
$$
satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module.
Then the inverse system $M_n = H^p(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image
for all $n \geq c$.}.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Assume
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
$$
satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module.
Then the inverse system $M_n = H^p(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition\footnote{In fact, there exists

for all $n \geq c$.}.

Let $f : X \to \Spec(R)$ be a morphism from an irreducible
scheme to the spectrum of a valuation ring. If $f$ is locally
of finite type and surjective, then the special fibre is

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-finite-complete-intersection}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $n \geq 1$ and
$h, f_1, \ldots, f_n \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Set $B = A[x_1, \ldots, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, \ldots, f_n)$.
Assume that $B$ is quasi-finite over $A$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B$ is flat over $A$ and $A \to B$ is a relative local complete
intersection,
\item the annihilator $J$ of $I = \Ker(B \otimes_A B \to B)$
is free of rank $1$ over $B$,
\item the Noether different of $B$ over $A$ is generated
by $\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$ in $B$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rank-tensor}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let
$\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The rank of $\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{G}$
is the product of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, then
the rank of $\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is the product of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-boundary-derivation-over-cup-product}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{O}' \to \mathcal{O}$ be a
surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}'$
has square zero. Then $M = H^1(X, \mathcal{I})$ is a
$R = H^0(X, \mathcal{O})$-module and the boundary map
$\partial : R \to M$ associated to the short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{O}' \to \mathcal{O} \to 0
$$
is a derivation (Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-derivation}).

A *spectral space* is quasi-compact and sober with a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersection. A sheaf of rings is *torsion* when its underlying additive-group stalks are torsion; an injective module sheaf is injective in the corresponding abelian category of module sheaves, not necessarily injective as a sheaf of sets.

$n + 1$ affine opens. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a torsion sheaf of rings on $X_\etale$

\label{lemma-limit-henselian}
Let $A = \lim A_n$ where $(A_n)$ is an inverse system of rings
whose transition maps are surjective and have locally nilpotent kernels.
Then $(A, I_n)$ is a henselian pair, where $I_n = \Ker(A \to A_n)$.

formulation.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, ideal $I$ and finitely generated $A$-module $M$, define $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ to be the maximal length of an $M$-regular sequence of elements of $I$ (and $\infty$ by convention if $IM=M$). A sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ is $M$-regular if each $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})M$ and the final quotient is nonzero. Assume $IM\ne M$, so $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ is finite. Then the following three integers are equal:
\[
\operatorname{depth}_I(M)
=\min\{i\ge0:\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(A/I,M)\ne0\}
=\min\{i\ge0:H_I^i(M)\ne0\},
\]
where $H_I^i(M)$ is the cohomology of the derived $I$-power-torsion functor (equivalently Čech local cohomology since $A$ is Noetherian). Moreover if $N$ is any finite module with $I^nN=0$ for some $n$, then $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(N,M)=0$ for every $i<\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Noetherian A, finite M and IM≠M give equality of depth, first nonzero Ext(A/I,M) and first nonzero I-local cohomology; moreover Ext(N,M) vanishes below depth for all finite I-power torsion N. The three equal quantities and added vanishing survive.

phase3.reason: Induction on depth using a regular element gives Ext vanishing/nonvanishing, extends it to finite torsion modules, and identifies the least nonzero local cohomology degree via filtered Ext.

source.label: lemma-depth
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-depth}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal, and
let $M$ be a finite $A$-module such that $IM \not = M$. Then
the following integers are equal:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{depth}_I(M)$,
\item the smallest integer $i$ such that $\Ext_A^i(A/I, M)$
is nonzero, and
\item the smallest integer $i$ such that $H^i_I(M)$ is nonzero.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we have $\Ext^i_A(N, M) = 0$ for $i < \text{depth}_I(M)$
for any finite $A$-module $N$ annihilated by a power of $I$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proj-quasi-compact}
Let $S$ be a graded ring.
The scheme $\text{Proj}(S)$ is quasi-compact if and only
if there exist finitely many homogeneous elements
$f_1, \ldots, f_n \in S_{+}$ such that
$S_{+} \subset \sqrt{(f_1, \ldots, f_n)}$. In this case
$\text{Proj}(S) = D_+(f_1) \cup \ldots \cup D_+(f_n)$.

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta : G \to G \times_H G$ is representable
by algebraic spaces, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Then $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

phase3.reason: The proof expresses every test fibre product as the base change of the representable diagonal and invokes the stability lemma.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a
Noetherian ring. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of sets, abelian
groups, or $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$. Let
$\mathcal{G} = \colim \mathcal{G}_i$ be a filtered colimit of sheaves of
sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules. Then
$$
\Mor(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) = \colim \Mor(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_i)
$$
in the category of sheaves of sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules on
$X_\etale$.
The property is *finitely presented with respect to **filtered colimits** in the appropriate sheaf category*; it is not compactness in the unbounded derived category.
hypotheses: On the small étale site $X_{\acute et}$ of a **qcqs scheme**, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* when its restriction to a finite constructible partition is **finite locally constant**; for modules over a **Noetherian** ring $\Lambda$, constructible means *finite type* locally constant on every stratum. For an étale object $j_U:U\to X$, $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$ is the representable sheaf, and $j_{U!}\underline M$ is **extension by zero** of the constant abelian or $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U$, left adjoint to $j_U^{-1}$. A *torsion abelian sheaf* has torsion stalks at every geometric point. A *filtered colimit* of sheaves is taken in the sheaf category (sheafification of the sectionwise colimit). A constructible sheaf is *finitely presented/compact for filtered colimits* if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\operatorname*{colim}_i\mathcal G_i)\cong\operatorname*{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ for every filtered system. *Essentially constant* for an ind-object means isomorphic in its ind-category to a constant ind-object. For a directed inverse system with affine transitions, its category-colimit means objects and morphisms descend from sufficiently large finite stages, **up to category equivalence**.

A constructible sheaf is *finitely presented/compact for filtered colimits* if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\operatorname*{colim}_i\mathcal G_i)\cong\operatorname*{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ for every filtered system. *Essentially constant* for an ind-object means isomorphic in its ind-category to a constant ind-object. For a directed inverse system with affine transitions, its category-colimit means objects and morphisms descend from sufficiently large finite stages, **up to category equivalence**.

**Standalone statement with the full source hypotheses:**
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a
Noetherian ring. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of sets, abelian
groups, or $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$. Let
$\mathcal{G} = \colim \mathcal{G}_i$ be a filtered colimit of sheaves of
sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules. Then
$$
\Mor(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) = \colim \Mor(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_i)
$$
in the category of sheaves of sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules on
$X_\etale$.

**Qualification and typing:** The property is *finitely presented with respect to **filtered colimits** in the appropriate sheaf category*; it is not compactness in the unbounded derived category.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-subcategory-right-resolution}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let
$\mathcal{I} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ be a subset containing $0$
such that every object of $\mathcal{A}$ is a subobject of an element of
$\mathcal{I}$. Let $a \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Given $K^\bullet$ with $K^n = 0$ for $n < a$
there exists a quasi-isomorphism $K^\bullet \to I^\bullet$
with $K^n \to I^n$ injective and $I^n \in \mathcal{I}$ for all $n$
and $I^n = 0$ for $n < a$,
\item Given $K^\bullet$ with $H^n(K^\bullet) = 0$
for $n < a$ there exists a quasi-isomorphism $K^\bullet \to I^\bullet$
with $I^n \in \mathcal{I}$ and $I^n = 0$ for $n < a$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-loc-cst-torsion}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a smooth proper morphism of schemes.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
finite type, locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules
on $X_\etale$ such that for every geometric point $\overline{x}$ of $X$
the stalk $\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}}$ is annihilated by an integer
$n > 0$ prime to the residue characteristic of $\overline{x}$.
Then $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type, locally constant sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $S_\etale$ for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.

Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $i : Z \subset X$ be an immersion.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion, and
\item $Z \to S$ is a flat morphism.
\end{enumerate}

$Z' = S' \times_S Z \to X' = S' \times_S X$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-regular-immersion}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $i : Z \subset X$ be an immersion.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion, and
\item $Z \to S$ is a flat morphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then for every morphism of schemes $g : S' \to S$ the base change
$Z' = S' \times_S Z \to X' = S' \times_S X$
is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $Z \to X$ be an immersion.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation,
\item $Z \to X$ is a relative quasi-regular immersion.
\end{enumerate}
Then $Z \to X$ is a regular immersion and
the same remains true after any base change.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-locally-free}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation and
for all $x \in X$ the stalk $\mathcal{F}_x$ is a free
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a locally free, finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type,
for every $x \in X$ the stalk $\mathcal{F}_x$ is a free
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module, and the function
$$
\rho_\mathcal{F} : X \to \mathbf{Z}, \quad
x \longmapsto
\dim_{\kappa(x)} \mathcal{F}_x \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x)
$$
is locally constant in the Zariski topology on $X$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement: Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. For every family $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ of objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_\lambda a_f(K_\lambda)\to a_f(\bigoplus_\lambda K_\lambda)$ is an isomorphism. Thus the right adjoint to the derived pushforward preserves arbitrary coproducts, not merely finite sums.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-flat}
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is proper, flat, and
of finite presentation.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint for
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}. Then $a$ commutes with direct sums.

\label{lemma-algebraic-space-over-affine-formal}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Y$ be an affine formal algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a map of sheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which is
representable by algebraic spaces. Then $X$ is a formal
algebraic space.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-exact}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $p$ be a point of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We have $(\mathcal{F}^\#)_p = \mathcal{F}_p$
for any presheaf of sets on $\mathcal{C}$.
\item The stalk functor
$\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$,
$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}_p$ is exact (see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-exact})
and commutes with arbitrary colimits.
\item The stalk functor
$\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$,
$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}_p$ is exact (see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-exact})
and commutes with arbitrary colimits.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

A simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ consists of $A$-algebras $P_n$ and simplicial face and degeneracy maps. An augmentation $P_\bullet\to B$ views $B$ as a constant simplicial algebra. A trivial Kan fibration on underlying simplicial sets has the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$. The $n$-skeleton $\operatorname{sk}_n(P_\bullet)$ retains degrees through $n$; the $n$-coskeleton $\operatorname{cosk}_n$ freely reconstructs compatible higher simplices by a right Kan extension. The condition $P_\bullet=\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nP_\bullet$ says it is $n$-coskeletal.

For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

A simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ consists of $A$-algebras $P_n$ and simplicial face and degeneracy maps. An augmentation $P_\bullet\to B$ views $B$ as a constant simplicial algebra. A trivial Kan fibration on underlying simplicial sets has the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$. The $n$-skeleton $\operatorname{sk}_n(P_\bullet)$ retains degrees through $n$; the $n$-coskeleton $\operatorname{cosk}_n$ freely reconstructs compatible higher simplices by a right Kan extension. The condition $P_\bullet=\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nP_\bullet$ says it is $n$-coskeletal.

\label{proposition-polynomial}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map.
There exists a simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ with an augmentation
$\epsilon : P_\bullet \to B$ such that each $P_n$ is a polynomial algebra
of finite type over $A$ and such that $\epsilon$ is a trivial
Kan fibration of simplicial sets.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-codim-1-part}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Assume there exist
\begin{enumerate}
\item a collection of integral effective Cartier divisors
$D_i \subset X$, $i \in I$
\item a closed subset $Z' \subset X$ all of whose irreducible components
have codimension $\geq 2$ in $X$
(Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-codimension})
\end{enumerate}
such that $Z \subset Z' \cup \bigcup_{i \in I} D_i$ set-theoretically.
Then there exist integers $a_i \geq 0$ with $a_i = 0$ for almost all $i \in I$
such that the effective Cartier divisor
$$
D = \sum a_i D_i
$$
is contained in $Z$ and such that the inclusion morphism $D \to Z$
is an isomorphism away from codimension $2$ in $X$
(in the sense that there exists an open $U \subset Z$ such that
$D \cap U \to Z \cap U$ is an isomorphism and such that every
irreducible component of $Z \setminus U$ has codimension $\geq 2$ in $X$).
When $Z$ is nowhere dense in $X$ existence of the $D_i$, $i \in I$ and $Z'$
is guaranteed if $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all $x \in Z$
or if $X$ is regular.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z$ is reduced and $|Z|$ is a singleton,
\item there exists a surjective flat morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to Z$
where $k$ is a field, and
\item there exists a locally of finite type, surjective, flat morphism
$\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to Z$ where $k$ is a field.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-derived-adjoint-tensor-hom}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ be differential graded $\mathcal{O}$-algebras.
Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a  differential graded
$(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$-bimodule. Then
$$
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{N}, -) :
D(\mathcal{B}, \text{d})
\longrightarrow
D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})
$$
is right adjoint to
$$
- \otimes_\mathcal{A}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{N} :
D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})
\longrightarrow
D(\mathcal{B}, \text{d})
$$

\label{lemma-weakly-ass-change-fields}
Let $K/k$ be a field extension. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $y \in X_K$ with image $x \in X$. If $y$ is a weakly
associated point of the pullback $\mathcal{F}_K$, then $x$
is a weakly associated point of $\mathcal{F}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-isomorphism}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of Hausdorff quasi-compact
topological spaces. If $Y$ is extremally disconnected, $f$ is surjective,
and $f(Z) \not = Y$ for every proper closed subset $Z$ of $X$, then
$f$ is a homeomorphism.

Let $X$ be a topological space. Suppose that
$Z \subset X$ is irreducible. Let $E \subset X$
be a finite union of locally closed subsets (e.g.\ $E$
is constructible). The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The intersection $E \cap Z$ contains an open
dense subset of $Z$.
\item The intersection $E \cap Z$ is dense in $Z$.
\end{enumerate}
If $Z$ has a generic point $\xi$, then this is
also equivalent to
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(3)] We have $\xi \in E$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For irreducible Z and a finite union of locally closed E, density of E∩Z is equivalent to containing a dense open; generic-point membership joins only if Z admits such a point.

phase3.reason: In an irreducible subspace, a finite union of locally closed sets is dense precisely when one contains a nonempty dense open; its generic point criterion follows.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
Let $K/k$ be an extension of fields. Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$
be the normalization of $X$ and let $Y^\nu \to X_K$ be the
normalization of the base change. Then the canonical morphism
$$
Y^\nu \longrightarrow X^\nu \times_{\Spec(k)} \Spec(K)
$$
is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is separable and a universal homeomorphism
in general.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tautological-same-sheaf}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$\mathcal{U} = \{\varphi_i : U_i \to U\}_{i\in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{\psi_j : V_j \to U\}_{j\in J}$ be two families of morphisms
with the same fixed target. Assume that the fibre products
$U_i \times_U U_{i'}$ and $V_j \times_U V_{j'}$ exist.
If $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ are
tautologically equivalent, then for any presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on
$\mathcal{C}$ the sheaf condition for $\mathcal{F}$ with respect to
$\mathcal{U}$ is equivalent to the sheaf condition for $\mathcal{F}$
with respect to $\mathcal{V}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chow-finite-type}
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type.
Then there exists an $n \geq 0$ and a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rd] & X' \ar[d] \ar[l]^\pi \ar[r] & \mathbf{P}^n_S \ar[dl] \\
& S &
}
$$
where $X' \to \mathbf{P}^n_S$ is an immersion, and
$\pi : X' \to X$ is proper and surjective.

\label{lemma-directed-category-system}
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a filtered index category.
There exist a directed set $I$
and a system $(x_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ over $I$ in $\mathcal{I}$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every category $\mathcal{C}$ and every diagram
$M : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{C}$ with values in $\mathcal{C}$,
denote $(M(x_i), M(\varphi_{ii'}))$
the corresponding system over $I$. If
$\colim_{i \in I} M(x_i)$ exists then so does
$\colim_\mathcal{I} M$ and the transformation
$$
\theta :
\colim_{i \in I} M(x_i)
\longrightarrow
\colim_\mathcal{I} M
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-functorial-colimit} is an isomorphism.
\item For every category $\mathcal{C}$ and every diagram
$M : \mathcal{I}^{opp} \to \mathcal{C}$ in $\mathcal{C}$, denote
$(M(x_i), M(\varphi_{ii'}))$ the corresponding inverse system
over $I$. If $\lim_{i \in I} M(x_i)$ exists then so does
$\lim_{\mathcal{I}^{opp}} M$ and the transformation
$$
\theta :
\lim_{\mathcal{I}^{opp}} M
\longrightarrow
\lim_{i \in I} M(x_i)
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-functorial-limit} is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-twist-with-general-divisor}
Let $k$ be a separably closed field. Let $X$ be a smooth projective
curve of genus $g$ over $k$. Let $K/k$ be a field extension and let
$\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $X_K$. Then there exists an
invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}_0$ on $X$ such that
$\dim_K H^0(X_K,
\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_K}} \mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K}) = 1$ and
$\dim_K H^1(X_K,
\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_K}} \mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K}) = 0$.

For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. \label{lemma-nowhere-dense-generic-fibre}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes. Assume
$Y$ irreducible with generic point $\eta$.
If $Z \subset X$ is a closed subset with $Z_\eta$ nowhere dense
in $X_\eta$, then there exists a nonempty open $V \subset Y$ such

Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian
ring and $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of

Under Noetherian Λ and ideal I, F≅completed constant sheaf M with M finite over Λ^wedge. Each of three conditions and the finite completed-module conclusion remain.

phase3.reason: Choose compatible abstract Λ/I^n-modules M_n representing the constant reductions and take their inverse limit M, finite over completed Λ by the finite mod-I condition. The isomorphism torsors between M_n and the reductions form a Mittag-Leffler system by the cited algebra lemma. Because X is weakly contractible, the eventual-image surjections have sections on X, yielding compatible trivializations and F≈completed constant M.

\label{lemma-weird}
Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian
ring and $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $X_\proetale$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F} = \lim \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$,
\item $\mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$ is a constant sheaf of
$\Lambda/I^n$-modules,
\item $\mathcal{F}/I\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{F} \cong \underline{M}^\wedge$ where $M$ is
a finite $\Lambda^\wedge$-module.

\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all $x \in D$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor.

\label{lemma-pullback-equivariant}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $G$ be a group scheme over $S$.
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a $G$-equivariant morphism between $S$-schemes
endowed with $G$-actions. The rule
$(\mathcal{F}, \alpha) \mapsto (f^*\mathcal{F}, (1_G \times f)^*\alpha)$
defines a functor from the category of $G$-equivariant quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules  to the category of
$G$-equivariant quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-X}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
If $X$ is flat at $x$ over $S$, then there exists an elementary
\'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$ and an open subscheme
$$
V \subset X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})
$$
which contains the unique point of
$X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$ mapping to $x$
such that $V \to \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$
is flat and of finite presentation.

Let $p : (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) \to (X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ and
$q : (Z, \mathcal{O}_Z) \to (X, \mathcal{O}_X)$

\Mor_{\text{LRS}/(X, \mathcal{O}_X)}((Z, \mathcal{O}_Z), (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y))

(f, f^\sharp) \longmapsto f
$$
is bijective. Here $\text{LRS}/(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is the category of
locally ringed spaces over $X$ and $\textit{Top}/X$ is the category
of topological spaces over $X$.

For a property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms preserved under arbitrary base change and fppf-local on the base, $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ precisely if all resulting scheme maps $V_\xi\to U$ have $\mathcal P$. \label{lemma-transformation-diagonal-properties}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}.
If for every $U, V \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and $a \in F(U)$,
$b \in F(V)$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h_U \times_{a, F, b} h_V$ is representable, say by the scheme $W$, and
\item the morphism $W \to U \times_S V$ corresponding to
$h_U \times_{a, F, b} h_V \to h_U \times h_V$ has property $\mathcal{P}$,
\end{enumerate}
then $\Delta : F \to F \times F$ is representable and has
property $\mathcal{P}$.

hypotheses:
Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.
Let $x \in X$.
formulation.statement:
Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.
Let $x \in X$. Then
$$
(f^*\mathcal{G})_x =
\mathcal{G}_{f(x)}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y, f(x)}}
\mathcal{O}_{X, x}
$$
as $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules where the tensor product on the right
uses $f^\sharp_x : \mathcal{O}_{Y, f(x)} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For (f,f♯) ringed-space morphism, sheaf G of O_Y-modules and x∈X, stalk (f*G)_x is G_{f(x)}⊗_(O_Y,f(x))O_X,x with O_X,x-module structure via f♯_x. The ring homomorphism, tensor direction and hypotheses match.

phase3.reason: The proof combines stalks of tensor sheaf modules and the inverse-image stalk identity to obtain the displayed base-change tensor formula.

Let $S = \Spec(K)$ with $K$ a field.
Let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.

formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $u : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and
$v : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ be additive functors with
$u$ right adjoint to $v$. Consider the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $v$ transforms injective maps into injective maps,
\item[(b)] $v$ is exact, and
\item[(c)] $u$ transforms injectives into injectives.
\end{enumerate}
Then (a) $\Leftrightarrow$ (b) $\Rightarrow$ (c). If $\mathcal{A}$
has enough injectives, then all three conditions are equivalent.

phase3.reason: The proof uses right exactness of the left adjoint, extension through monomorphisms under adjunction to preserve injectives, and enough injectives to obtain the converse.

conclusions: Each listed finite-presentation/differential/étale property of $A$ is equivalent to its validity after extension of scalars to $S$.
hypotheses: $R\to S$ is universally injective/pure, and $A$ is an $R$-algebra.
formulation.statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. Let $A$ be an $R$-algebra. Each of the following properties of the structure map $R\to A$ holds if and only if the corresponding property holds for $S\to A\otimes_RS$: (a) finite type; (b) finite presentation; (c) formally unramified; (d) unramified; (e) étale.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L1445–1463 in the SAME subsection assumes universally injective R→S and lists five independent R-algebra properties of A: finite type, finite presentation, formally unramified, unramified and ÉTALE. Each is equivalent to base-changed property over S; all are retained.

phase3.reason: The same descent argument applies to finite-type/presentation algebras, while differential modules and flatness give formal unramifiedness, étaleness and remaining clauses.

\label{lemma-constructible-shriek-rel-dim-1}
Let $Y$ be an affine scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on
$\mathbf{A}^1_Y$ which is torsion. Then $Rf_!\mathcal{F}$ has constructible
cohomology sheaves where $f : \mathbf{A}^1_Y \to Y$ is the structure morphism.

hypotheses:
Let $A \to B$ be ring map such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ identifies local rings,
\item the topological spaces $\Spec(B)$, $\Spec(A)$ are w-local,
\item $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$ is w-local, and
\item $\pi_0(\Spec(B)) \to \pi_0(\Spec(A))$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
formulation.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map $A\to B$ is a **local isomorphism** when near every prime of $B$ it induces an open immersion after inverting an element of $B$; it **identifies local rings** when $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism for every prime $q$ of $B$.

Let $A \to B$ be ring map such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ identifies local rings,
\item the topological spaces $\Spec(B)$, $\Spec(A)$ are w-local,
\item $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$ is w-local, and
\item $\pi_0(\Spec(B)) \to \pi_0(\Spec(A))$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $A \to B$ is an isomorphism

phase3.reason: A w-local map inducing bijection on π0 induces bijection of closed points, hence underlying points by unique specialization. Flat going-down and identical local rings then force equality after localization at every A-prime, whence A≈B.

\label{lemma-good-dga}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $(\mathcal{B}, \text{d})$ be a differential graded $\mathcal{O}$-algebra.
There exists a quasi-isomorphism of differential graded $\mathcal{O}$-algebras

$\mathcal{A}$ is graded flat and K-flat as a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
and such that the same is true after pullback by any morphism of
ringed topoi.

\label{lemma-spec-functorial}
\begin{slogan}
Functoriality of the spectrum
\end{slogan}
Suppose that $\varphi : R \to R'$ is a ring homomorphism.
The induced map
$$
\Spec(\varphi) : \Spec(R') \longrightarrow \Spec(R),
\quad
\mathfrak p' \longmapsto \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')
$$
is continuous for the Zariski topologies. In fact, for any
element $f \in R$ we have
$\Spec(\varphi)^{-1}(D(f)) = D(\varphi(f))$.

whose transition maps are faithfully flat.

taken as an element of $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, \infty\}$
is the supremum of the numbers of minimal primes of the $R_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a pre-triangulated category.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{D}$.
There exists a distinguished triangle $(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)$ which
is unique up to (nonunique) isomorphism of triangles.
More precisely, given a second such distinguished triangle
$(X, Y, Z', f, g', h')$ there exists an isomorphism
$$
(1, 1, c) : (X, Y, Z, f, g, h) \longrightarrow (X, Y, Z', f, g', h')
$$

hypotheses:
A *site* $\mathcal C$ is a small category endowed with covering families $\{U_i\to U\}$ satisfying the isomorphism, composition/refinement, and base-change axioms. A *presheaf* of sets (or abelian groups) is a contravariant functor. For a covering, a *matching family* consists of sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose restrictions to every fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ coincide (including $i=j$). A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

For a site $\mathcal C$ and a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$, the Čech cochain complex of an abelian presheaf $\mathcal G$ has $C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)}\mathcal G(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p})$ in degree $p\ge0$, with alternating restriction differential; **repeated indices are allowed**. Denote its cohomology $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. For an abelian *sheaf* $\mathcal F$ define $H^q(V,\mathcal F)=R^q\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ using injective resolutions on $\mathcal C$, and let $\underline H^q(\mathcal F)$ be the *presheaf* $V\mapsto H^q(V,\mathcal F)$; it need not itself be a sheaf.
formulation.statement:
A *site* $\mathcal C$ is a small category endowed with covering families $\{U_i\to U\}$ satisfying the isomorphism, composition/refinement, and base-change axioms. A *presheaf* of sets (or abelian groups) is a contravariant functor. For a covering, a *matching family* consists of sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose restrictions to every fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ coincide (including $i=j$). A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

For a site $\mathcal C$ and a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$, the Čech cochain complex of an abelian presheaf $\mathcal G$ has $C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)}\mathcal G(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p})$ in degree $p\ge0$, with alternating restriction differential; **repeated indices are allowed**. Denote its cohomology $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. For an abelian *sheaf* $\mathcal F$ define $H^q(V,\mathcal F)=R^q\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ using injective resolutions on $\mathcal C$, and let $\underline H^q(\mathcal F)$ be the *presheaf* $V\mapsto H^q(V,\mathcal F)$; it need not itself be a sheaf.

The forgetful functor $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})\to \textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})$
transforms injectives into injectives.

**Scope and interpretation:** The source is Ab(C), abelian sheaves on site C; the target is PAb(C), abelian presheaves. The preservation of injectives uses the **exact** left adjoint sheafification and does not confuse either with modules over a ringed site.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The forgetful functor Ab(C)→PAb(C) takes injective abelian sheaves to injective abelian presheaves. The source and target are not interchanged.

phase3.reason: The proof uses the exact left adjoint sheafification to the inclusion of abelian sheaves into presheaves; by adjunction, maps from any presheaf into the included injective extend, proving injectivity.

hypotheses:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme having no embedded points.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme having no embedded points.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular meromorphic section.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular-meromorphic-section-exists-noetherian}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme having no embedded points.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular meromorphic section.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $p$ be a point of $\mathcal{C}$ given by
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$. Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$
and let $x \in u(U)$. The functor

(\varphi : V \to U) \longmapsto \{y \in u(V) \mid u(\varphi)(y) = x\}

defines a point $q$ of the site $\mathcal{C}/U$ such that the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{

\Sh(\mathcal{C})
}
$$
commutes. In other words
$\mathcal{F}_p = (j_U^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q$ for any
sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glue-invertible-sheaves}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z_1, \ldots, Z_n \subset X$ be closed
subschemes. Let $\mathcal{L}_i$ be an invertible sheaf on $Z_i$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is reduced,
\item $X = \bigcup Z_i$ set theoretically, and
\item $Z_i \cap Z_j$ is a discrete topological space for $i \not = j$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}$ on $X$ whose restriction
to $Z_i$ is $\mathcal{L}_i$. Moreover, if we are given sections
$s_i \in \Gamma(Z_i, \mathcal{L}_i)$ which are nonvanishing at the
points of $Z_i \cap Z_j$, then we can choose $\mathcal{L}$ such
that there exists a $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$ with
$s|_{Z_i} = s_i$ for all $i$.

$$

\label{lemma-morphism-big-small-cartesian-diagram}
Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site. Consider a cartesian diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
T' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & T \ar[d]^f \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
in $\Sch_\proetale$. Then
$i_g^{-1} \circ f_{big, *} = f'_{small, *} \circ (i_{g'})^{-1}$
and $g_{big}^{-1} \circ f_{big, *} = f'_{big, *} \circ (g'_{big})^{-1}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an elementary \'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
and an open subscheme
$$
V \subset X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})
$$
which contains the unique point of
$X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$ mapping to $x$
such that the pullback of $\mathcal{F}$ to $V$ is an $\mathcal{O}_V$-module
of finite presentation and flat over $\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$.

formulation.statement:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is unramified, then the diagonal morphism
$\Delta : X \to X \times_S X$ is an open immersion.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite type
and $\Delta$ is an open immersion, then $f$ is unramified.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $\Delta$ is an open
immersion, then $f$ is G-unramified.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned morphisms.tex L7852 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism): If f UNRAMIFIED then its DIAGONAL is an OPEN IMMERSION. Conversely OPEN DIAGONAL plus LOCALLY FINITE TYPE implies UNRAMIFIED, and plus LOCALLY FINITE PRESENTATION implies G-UNRAMIFIED; all three guards remain distinct.

phase3.reason: For an unramified map the diagonal is an open immersion; conversely an open diagonal has zero conormal sheaf and therefore zero relative differentials.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal, and
let $M$ a finite $A$-module with $IM \not = M$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $x \in I$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, then
$\text{depth}_I(M/xM) = \text{depth}_I(M) - 1$.
\item Any $M$-regular sequence $x_1, \ldots, x_r$ in $I$ can be extended to an
$M$-regular sequence in $I$ of length $\text{depth}_I(M)$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: For a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, $D_c(X_{\acute et},\Lambda)$ consists of complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-support-proper-over-base-pushforward}
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
with support proper over $S$. Then $R^pf_*\mathcal{F}$
is a coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module for all $p \geq 0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-h0-cech}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $\check{H}^0(K, \mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{F}(X)$.

source.label: lemma-blowing-up-denominators
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowing-up-denominators}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s$ be a regular meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
Let $U \subset X$ be the maximal open subscheme such that
$s$ corresponds to a section of $\mathcal{L}$ over $U$.
The blowup $b : X' \to X$ in the ideal of denominators
of $s$ is $U$-admissible. There exists an effective Cartier divisor
$D \subset X'$ and an isomorphism
$$
b^*\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{O}_{X'}(D - E),
$$
where $E \subset X'$ is the exceptional divisor such that the
meromorphic section $b^*s$ corresponds, via the isomorphism,
to the meromorphic section $1_D \otimes (1_E)^{-1}$.

source.label: lemma-fully-faithful
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fully-faithful}
Let $I \subset \mathfrak a$ be ideals of a Noetherian ring $A$.
Let $U = \Spec(A) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $I$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item for any associated prime $\mathfrak p \subset A$ with
$\mathfrak p \not \in V(I)$ and
$V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(I) \not \subset V(\mathfrak a)$ and
$\mathfrak q \in V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(\mathfrak a)$ we have
$\dim((A/\mathfrak p)_\mathfrak q) > \text{cd}(A, I) + 1$,
\item for $\mathfrak p \subset A$ with $\mathfrak p \not \in V(I)$
and $V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(I) \subset V(\mathfrak a)$
we have $\text{depth}(A_\mathfrak p) \geq 2$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the completion functor
$$
\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_U)
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(U, I\mathcal{O}_U),
\quad
\mathcal{F} \longmapsto \mathcal{F}^\wedge
$$
is fully faithful on the full subcategory of
finite locally free objects.

\label{lemma-base-change-by-space-representable-by-space}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$
be categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$,
$g : \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be $1$-morphisms.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces, and
\item $\mathcal{Z}$ is representable by an algebraic space over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the $2$-fibre product
$\mathcal{Z} \times_{g, \mathcal{Y}, f} \mathcal{X}$
is representable by an algebraic space.

\label{lemma-extension-by-zero-triangle}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes. Let
$$
K \to L \to M \to K[1]
$$
be a distinguished triangle of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$.
Then there exists an inverse system of distinguished triangles
$$
K_n \to L_n \to M_n \to K_n[1]
$$
in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ such that $(K_n)$, $(L_n)$, $(M_n)$
are Deligne systems and such that the restriction of these
distinguished triangles to $U$ is isomorphic to the distinguished triangle
we started out with.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coim-im-map}
Let $f : x \to y$ be a morphism in a preadditive category
such that the kernel, cokernel, image and coimage all exist.
Then $f$ can be factored uniquely as
$x \to \Coim(f) \to \Im(f) \to y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-qc-colimits}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
has colimits and they agree with colimits in the categories
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, and
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\item Given $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ in $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
the tensor products $\mathcal{F} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{G}$
computed in $\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, or
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$ agree and the common value
is an object of $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\item Given $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ in $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
with $\mathcal{F}$ finite locally free (in fppf, or equivalently \'etale, or
equivalently Zariski topology) the internal homs
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
computed in $\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, or
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$ agree and the common value
is an object of $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-functor-finite-modules}
Let $A$ and $B$ be Noetherian rings. Let
$F : \text{Mod}^{fg}_A \to \text{Mod}^{fg}_B$ be a functor.
Then $F$ extends uniquely to a functor $F' : \text{Mod}_A \to \text{Mod}_B$
which commutes with filtered colimits. If $F$ is additive, then
$F'$ is additive and commutes with arbitrary direct sums.
If $F$ is exact, left exact, or right exact, so is $F'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometrically-reduced-open}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat proper morphism of finite presentation.
Then the set $\{y \in Y \mid X_y\text{ is geometrically reduced}\}$
is open in $Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glue-maps}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $X = \bigcup U_i$ be an open covering.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be sheaves of sets on $X$.
Given a collection
$$
\varphi_i :
\mathcal{F}|_{U_i}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{G}|_{U_i}
$$
of maps of sheaves such that for all $i, j \in I$ the maps
$\varphi_i, \varphi_j$ restrict to the same map
$\mathcal{F}|_{U_i \cap U_j} \to \mathcal{G}|_{U_i \cap U_j}$
then there exists a unique map of sheaves
$$
\varphi :
\mathcal{F}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{G}
$$
whose restriction to each $U_i$ agrees with $\varphi_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-power-works}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $1$.
Let $L = \prod A_\mathfrak p$ and $I = \bigcap \mathfrak p$
where the product and intersection are over
the minimal primes of $A$. Let $f \in L$ be an element
of the form $f = i + a$ where $a \in \mathfrak m_A$ and
$i \in IL$. Then some power of $f$ is in the image of $A \to L$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent Jacobson algebraic space over $S$.
