phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L5293–5297 requires X both DECENT and JACOBSON; then the subset X_ft-pts of finite type points is EXACTLY the closed points of |X|. The proposal keeps both directions, equality of sets, and does not conflate general Jacobson spaces with their underlying topology without decency.

\label{lemma-flatness-sheafification-refined}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Assume
that every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
such that $\mathcal{F}(U_i)$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}(U_i)$-module.
Then $\mathcal{F}^\#$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}^\#$-module.

\label{lemma-cech-complex-complex-computes}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{U} : X = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ be
an open covering. Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. If $H^i(U_{i_0 \ldots i_p}, \mathcal{F}^q) = 0$
for all $i > 0$ and all $p, i_0, \ldots, i_p, q$, then the map
$
\text{Tot}(\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}^\bullet))
\to
R\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)
$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-cech-complex-complex} is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces}
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a cofiltered index category.
Let $i \mapsto X_i$ be a diagram of spectral spaces such
that for $a : j \to i$ in $\mathcal{I}$ the corresponding map
$f_a : X_j \to X_i$ is spectral. Then
the inverse limit $X = \lim X_i$ is a spectral topological space
and the projection maps $p_i : X \to X_i$ are spectral.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pushforward-sheaf}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites.
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a continuous functor.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a sheaf on $\mathcal{D}$ then
$u^p\mathcal{F}$ is a sheaf as well.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pf-flat-module-open}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Assume $f$ locally finite presentation, $\mathcal{F}$ of
finite type, $X = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$, and
$\mathcal{F}$ flat over $Y$. Then $f$ is universally open.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gorenstein-base-change}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme over the field $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a finitely generated field extension.
Let $x \in X$ be a point, and let $x' \in X_{k'}$ be a point lying
over $x$. Then we have
$$
\mathcal{O}_{X, x}\text{ is Gorenstein}
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{O}_{X_{k'}, x'}\text{ is Gorenstein}
$$
If $X$ is locally of finite type over $k$, the same holds for any
field extension $k'/k$.

Standing assumptions and notation from Stacks Situation \ref{situation-setup}:
Here $S$ is a locally Noetherian, and universally catenary scheme.
Moreover, we assume $S$ is endowed with a dimension function
$\delta : S \longrightarrow \mathbf{Z}$.

Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be proper morphisms.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be proper morphisms.
Then $g_* \circ f_* = (g \circ f)_*$ as maps $Z_k(X) \to Z_k(Z)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned proper-cycle-pushforward composition lemma at 1923–1929 assumes X,Y,Z locally of finite type over (S,δ) and BOTH f:X→Y and g:Y→Z PROPER. It asserts equality g_*f_*=(g∘f)_* as homomorphisms on k-cycle groups Z_k(X)→Z_k(Z), not merely equivalence modulo rational equivalence. The added formula for pushforward of integral cycles agrees with the source conventions.

\label{lemma-compose-pushforward}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be proper morphisms.
Then $g_* \circ f_* = (g \circ f)_*$ as maps $Z_k(X) \to Z_k(Z)$.

\label{lemma-differentials-restrict-open}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ be open subschemes such
that $f(U) \subset V$. Then there is a unique isomorphism
$\Omega_{X/S}|_U = \Omega_{U/V}$ of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules such that
$\text{d}_{X/S}|_U = \text{d}_{U/V}$.

formulation.statement:
Let $\Sch_{smooth}$ be a big smooth site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_{smooth}$.
The functor
$$
u : (\Sch/T)_{smooth} \longrightarrow (\Sch/S)_{smooth},
\quad
V/T \longmapsto V/S
$$
is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint
$$
v : (\Sch/S)_{smooth} \longrightarrow (\Sch/T)_{smooth},
\quad
(U \to S) \longmapsto (U \times_S T \to T).
$$
They induce the same morphism of topoi
$$
f_{big} :
\Sh((\Sch/T)_{smooth})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_{smooth})
$$

source.label: lemma-morphism-big-smooth
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-big-smooth}
Let $\Sch_{smooth}$ be a big smooth site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_{smooth}$.
The functor
$$
u : (\Sch/T)_{smooth} \longrightarrow (\Sch/S)_{smooth},
\quad
V/T \longmapsto V/S
$$
is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint
$$
v : (\Sch/S)_{smooth} \longrightarrow (\Sch/T)_{smooth},
\quad
(U \to S) \longmapsto (U \times_S T \to T).
$$
They induce the same morphism of topoi
$$
f_{big} :
\Sh((\Sch/T)_{smooth})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_{smooth})
$$
We have $f_{big}^{-1}(\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
We have $f_{big, *}(\mathcal{F})(U/S) = \mathcal{F}(U \times_S T/T)$.
Also, $f_{big}^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_{big!}$ which commutes with
fibre products and equalizers.

\label{lemma-diagonal-morphism-finite-type}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$ with diagonal $\Delta : X \to X \times_Y X$. If $f$ is locally of
finite type then $\Delta$ is locally of finite presentation. If $f$ is
quasi-separated and locally of finite type, then $\Delta$ is of finite
presentation.

\label{lemma-when-tensor-is-equal}
Let $A$ be a finite central simple algebra over $k$, and let
$B$ be a simple subalgebra of $A$. If $B$ is a central
$k$-algebra, then $A = B \otimes_k C$ where $C$ is the (central simple)
centralizer of $B$ in $A$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.

is retrocompact in $X$, then inverse images of constructible
sets are constructible.

\label{lemma-no-embedded-points-endos}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
without embedded associated points. Set
$$
\mathcal{I}
=
\Ker(\mathcal{O}_X
\longrightarrow
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F})).
$$
This is a coherent sheaf of ideals which defines a closed
subscheme $Z \subset X$ without embedded points. Moreover
there exists a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $Z$
such that (a) $\mathcal{F} = (Z \to X)_*\mathcal{G}$,
(b) $\mathcal{G}$ has no associated embedded points, and
(c) $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{G}) = Z$ (as sets).

source.label: lemma-f-map-basis-below-modules
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-f-map-basis-below-modules}
Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$
be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $Y$.
Suppose given for every $V \in \mathcal{B}$ a
$\mathcal{O}_Y(V)$-module map
$$
\varphi_V :
\mathcal{G}(V)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{F}(f^{-1}V)
$$
(where $\mathcal{F}(f^{-1}V)$ has a module structure using
$f^\sharp_V : \mathcal{O}_Y(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(f^{-1}V)$)
compatible with restriction mappings.
Then there is a unique $f$-map (see discussion of $f$-maps in
Section \ref{section-ringed-spaces-functoriality-modules})
$\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$
recovering $\varphi_V$ for $V \in \mathcal{B}$.

formulation.statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$. Write $R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K)\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the *exact-support right adjoint* to $Ri_*:D(\mathcal O_Z)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$, characterized by $Ri_*R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal O_Z,K)$; affine locally for $X=\operatorname{Spec}A,Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ it corresponds to $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,-)$ with its natural $B$-module structure. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a pseudo-coherent closed immersion. Let $a_i:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ be the right adjoint to $Ri_*$. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^{+}(\mathcal O_X)$ there is a functorial isomorphism
\[
a_i(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K).
\]
The isomorphism is explicitly restricted to bounded-below quasi-coherent-derived inputs; it does not assert equality for arbitrary unbounded inputs.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-twisted-inverse-image-closed}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a pseudo-coherent closed immersion
(if $X$ is Noetherian, then any closed immersion is pseudo-coherent).
Let $a : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)$ be the
right adjoint to $Ri_*$. Then there is a functorial isomorphism
$$
a(K) = R\SheafHom(\mathcal{O}_Z, K)
$$
for $K \in D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-composition-relative-dimension-d}
Let $f : X \to Y$, $g : Y \to Z$ be locally of finite type.
If $f$ has relative dimension $\leq d$ and $g$ has relative dimension $\leq e$
then $g \circ f$ has relative dimension $\leq d + e$.
If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ has relative dimension $d$,
\item $g$ has relative dimension $e$, and
\item $f$ is flat,
\end{enumerate}
then $g \circ f$ has relative dimension $d + e$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then
$f$ is integral, resp.\ finite
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable}),
if and only if for all affine schemes $Z$
and morphisms $Z \to Y$ the scheme $X \times_Y Z$ is affine and
integral, resp.\ finite, over $Z$.

conclusions: At most countably many K-isomorphism classes of smooth proper Y with D_perf(Y)≃D_perf(X).
hypotheses: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and $X,Y$ **smooth proper** $K$-schemes. Here *derived equivalent* means that there exists a $K$-linear exact equivalence $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)\simeq D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, where $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is the triangulated category of perfect complexes (locally bounded complexes of finite-rank vector bundles). Two schemes count as one isomorphism class when isomorphic **over $K$**. The source preceding definition formally introduces derived equivalence for smooth projective schemes, but its proof and theorem use smooth proper schemes; this statement spells out the actual equivalence meant in the theorem.
formulation.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and $X,Y$ **smooth proper** $K$-schemes. Here *derived equivalent* means that there exists a $K$-linear exact equivalence $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)\simeq D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, where $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is the triangulated category of perfect complexes (locally bounded complexes of finite-rank vector bundles). Two schemes count as one isomorphism class when isomorphic **over $K$**. The source preceding definition formally introduces derived equivalence for smooth projective schemes, but its proof and theorem use smooth proper schemes; this statement spells out the actual equivalence meant in the theorem.

For each fixed smooth proper $K$-scheme $X$, the collection of $K$-isomorphism classes of smooth proper $K$-schemes $Y$ for which such a $K$-linear exact equivalence exists is **at most countable**. This is a claim about isomorphism classes, not the potentially uncountable set of individual derived equivalence functors or kernels.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a fixed smooth proper X over algebraically closed field K, at most countably many K-isomorphism classes of smooth proper Y have K-linear derived categories of perfect complexes equivalent to that of X. The draft preserves proper rather than projective hypotheses and counts isomorphism classes, not functors.

phase3.reason: Reduce to a countable family of Fourier–Mukai equivalence families; the relative isomorphism locus is covered by countably many finite-type schemes, and rigidity makes each family yield finitely many isomorphism types.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

\label{lemma-compact-objects-if-enough-qc}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Assume every object of
$\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by quasi-compact objects. Then every
compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$ is a direct summand in $D(\mathcal{O})$
of a finite complex whose terms are finite direct sums of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules of the form $j_!\mathcal{O}_U$
where $U$ is a quasi-compact object of $\mathcal{C}$.

Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible

then $X$ is affine.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Z$, $g : Y \to Z$ and $Z \to T$
be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over $S$. Consider the induced
morphism $i : X \times_Z Y \to X \times_T Y$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is representable (by schemes), locally of finite type,
locally quasi-finite, separated, and a monomorphism,
\item if $Z \to T$ is separated, then $i$ is a closed immersion, and
\item if $Z \to T$ is quasi-separated, then $i$ is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For the canonical map i:X×_Z Y→X×_T Y, the unconditional five representability/finiteness/separatedness/monomorphism properties remain, plus the two distinctly conditional improvements: Z→T separated implies i closed, and Z→T quasi-separated implies i quasi-compact. Both conditions remain inside the conclusions text.

phase3.reason: The natural map from the Z-fibre product to the T-fibre product is the base change of the relative diagonal Z→Z×_T Z, whose established representability and finiteness properties yield all assertions.

\label{lemma-fitting-ideal}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Choose a presentation
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j \in J} R \longrightarrow R^{\oplus n}
\longrightarrow M \longrightarrow 0.
$$
of $M$. Let $A = (a_{ij})_{i = 1, \ldots, n, j \in J}$ be the matrix
of the map $\bigoplus_{j \in J} R \to R^{\oplus n}$.
The ideal $\text{Fit}_k(M)$ generated by the
$(n - k) \times (n - k)$ minors of
$A$ is independent of the choice of the presentation.

\label{lemma-flat-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is flat.
\item For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is flat.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is flat.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is flat, for all
$j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is flat then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is flat.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-injectives}
Suppose $\mathcal{J}$ is a sheaf of abelian groups with the following
property: For all $X\in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, for any abelian subsheaf
$\mathcal{S} \subset \mathbf{Z}_X^\#$ and any morphism
$\varphi : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{J}$, there exists a morphism
$\mathbf{Z}_X^\# \to \mathcal{J}$ extending $\varphi$.
Then $\mathcal{J}$ is an injective sheaf of abelian groups.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For site morphism f:D→C given by u:C→D, if every D-object V is covered by objects in the essential image of u, then f_*:Sh(D)→Sh(C) reflects both injections and surjections. The source claims reflection, not preservation.

phase3.reason: Since the objects u(U_i) cover every D-object, any map whose f_* is injective is injective on all sections by the sheaf separatedness axiom. \label{lemma-cover-from-below}
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites given
by the functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
Assume that for every object $V$ of $\mathcal{D}$ there exist objects
$U_i$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and morphisms $u(U_i) \to V$ such that
$\{u(U_i) \to V\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal{D}$. In this case the functor
$f_* : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ reflects
injections and surjections.

\label{lemma-inverse-limit-complexes}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet)$
be an inverse system of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $m \in \mathbf{Z}$. Assume there exist a set $\mathcal{B}$
of open subsets of $X$ and an integer $n_0$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every open in $X$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item for every $U \in \mathcal{B}$
\begin{enumerate}
\item the systems of abelian groups
$\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 2}(U)$ and $\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 1}(U)$
have vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example these have the Mittag-Leffler
condition),
\item the system of abelian groups $H^{m - 1}(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U))$
has vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example it has the Mittag-Leffler condition), and
\item we have
$H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U)) = H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet(U))$
for all $n \geq n_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then the maps
$H^m(\mathcal{F}^\bullet) \to \lim H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet) \to
H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet)$
are isomorphisms of sheaves where
$\mathcal{F}^\bullet = \lim \mathcal{F}_n^\bullet$ is the termwise
inverse limit.

\label{lemma-closed-union-connected-components}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $T \subset \Spec(R)$ be a subset of the spectrum.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ is closed and is a union of connected components of
$\Spec(R)$,
\item $T$ is an intersection of open and closed subsets of
$\Spec(R)$, and
\item $T = V(I)$ where $I \subset R$ is an ideal generated by idempotents.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, the ideal in (3) if it exists is unique.

\label{lemma-zariski-induced}
Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-zariski-site}.
Let $T \in \Ob(\Sch_{Zar})$.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be an arbitrary Zariski covering of $T$.
There exists a covering $\{U_j \to T\}_{j \in J}$ of $T$ in the site
$\Sch_{Zar}$ which is tautologically equivalent (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-combinatorial-tautological})
to $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-directed-colimit-finite-presentation}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
There exist
\begin{enumerate}
\item a directed set $I$ (see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-directed-set}),
\item a system $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$
over $I$ in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ (see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-system-over-poset})
\item morphisms of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\varphi_i : \mathcal{F}_i \to \mathcal{F}$
\end{enumerate}
such that each $\mathcal{F}_i$ is of finite presentation
and such that the morphisms $\varphi_i$ induce an isomorphism
$$
\colim_i \mathcal{F}_i
=
\mathcal{F}.
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-j-shriek}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $j : U \to X$ be the inclusion of an open subset.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor $j_{p!}$ is a left adjoint to the
restriction functor $j_p$ (see Lemma \ref{lemma-j-pullback}).
\item The functor $j_!$ is a left adjoint to restriction,
in a formula
$$
\Mor_{\Sh(X)}(j_!\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})
=
\Mor_{\Sh(U)}(\mathcal{F}, j^{-1}\mathcal{G})
=
\Mor_{\Sh(U)}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}|_U)
$$
bifunctorially in $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on $U$.
The stalks of the sheaf $j_!\mathcal{F}$ are described
as follows
$$
j_{!}\mathcal{F}_x =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\emptyset & \text{if} & x \not \in U \\
\mathcal{F}_x & \text{if} & x \in U
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
\item On the category of presheaves of $U$ we have $j_pj_{p!} = \text{id}$.
\item On the category of sheaves of $U$ we have $j^{-1}j_! = \text{id}$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is unramified if and only if $f$ is locally of finite type
and $\Omega_{X/S} = 0$, and
\item $f$ is G-unramified if and only if $f$ is locally of finite presentation
and $\Omega_{X/S} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-descending-chain
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-chain}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module. Then the $A$-module
$H^i_\mathfrak m(M)$ satisfies the descending chain condition
for any $i$.
\item Let $U = \Spec(A) \setminus \{\mathfrak m\}$ be the
punctured spectrum of $A$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
Then the $A$-module $H^i(U, \mathcal{F})$
satisfies the descending chain condition for $i > 0$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-open-morphism-quotient-topology
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-open-morphism-quotient-topology}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be surjective, open, continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $T \subset Y$ be a subset. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f^{-1}(\overline{T}) = \overline{f^{-1}(T)}$,
\item $T \subset Y$ is closed if and only if $f^{-1}(T)$ is closed,
\item $T \subset Y$ is open if and only if $f^{-1}(T)$ is open, and
\item $T \subset Y$ is locally closed if and only if $f^{-1}(T)$
is locally closed.
\end{enumerate}
In particular we see that $f$ is submersive.

\sum (-1)^n[H^n(K^\bullet)] = \sum (-1)^{p + q} [E_r^{p, q}]

Serre subcategory of $\mathcal{A}$ containing the objects
$E_r^{p, q}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-biregular-ss-relation-in-K0}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a
filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume that the filtration on each $K^n$
is finite (see Definition \ref{definition-filtered}) and that for some
$r$ we have only a finite number of nonzero $E_r^{p, q}$. Then
only a finite number of $H^n(K^\bullet)$ are nonzero and we have
$$
\sum (-1)^n[H^n(K^\bullet)] = \sum (-1)^{p + q} [E_r^{p, q}]
$$
in $K_0(\mathcal{A}')$ where $\mathcal{A}'$ is the smallest weak
Serre subcategory of $\mathcal{A}$ containing the objects

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-monomorphism-isomorphism}
Let $A = \lim A_n$ be a limit of a system of rings
whose transition maps are surjective and with locally nilpotent
kernels. Let $S = \Spec(A)$. Let $T \to S$ be a monomorphism
which is locally of finite type. If $\Spec(A_n) \to S$
factors through $T$ for all $n$, then $T = S$.

$i : \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})$.

R^pi(\mathcal{F}) = \underline{H}^p(\mathcal{F}) :
U \longmapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})
$$
see discussion in Section \ref{section-locality}.

formulation.statement:
On a site C, an object U is **weakly contractible** if every epimorphism of sheaves of sets F→G induces a surjection on sections F(U)→G(U). This is stronger than topological weak contractibility of a space. For a ringed site (C,O), extension by zero j_{U!}O_U is the left adjoint to localization/restriction at U. Let B⊂Ob(C) consist of weakly contractible objects such that **every** site object admits a covering by members of B. The assertion is a seven-part conjunction, including exactness, truncation completeness, derived products and inverse-limit formulas. The tower/derived-limit results use **countable sequential** inverse systems, with R^1lim described by the difference map on products.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
such that every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ is weakly contractible and
every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item A complex $\mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3$
of $\mathcal{O}$-modules is exact, if and only if
$\mathcal{F}_1(U) \to \mathcal{F}_2(U) \to \mathcal{F}_3(U)$
is exact for all $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item Every object $K$ of $D(\mathcal{O})$ is a derived limit
of its canonical truncations: $K = R\lim \tau_{\geq -n} K$.
\item Given an inverse system
$\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1$
with surjective transition maps, the projection
$\lim \mathcal{F}_n \to \mathcal{F}_1$ is surjective.
\item Products are exact on $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.
\item Products on $D(\mathcal{O})$ can be computed by taking
products of any representative complexes.
\item If $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ is an inverse system of $\mathcal{O}$-modules,
then $R^p\lim \mathcal{F}_n = 0$ for all $p > 1$ and
$$
R^1\lim \mathcal{F}_n  =
\Coker(\prod \mathcal{F}_n \to \prod \mathcal{F}_n)
$$
where the map is $(x_n) \mapsto (x_n - f(x_{n + 1}))$.
\item If $(K_n)$ is an inverse system of objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$,
then there are short exact sequences
$$
0 \to R^1\lim H^{p - 1}(K_n) \to H^p(R\lim K_n) \to
\lim H^p(K_n) \to 0
$$
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-internal-hom-sheaf
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-internal-hom-sheaf}
\begin{slogan}
The category of sheaves on a site is cartesian closed
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ and
$\mathcal{H}$ be sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. There is a canonical bijection
$$
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}) =
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{F},\SheafHom(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}))
$$
which is functorial in all three entries.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is proper,
\item $f$ is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$, and

Then (a) $f_*\mathcal{O}_X = \mathcal{O}_S$ and this holds after

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-genus-in-nodal-family-of-curves}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is proper,
\item $f$ is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$, and
\item the geometric fibres of $f$ are connected.
\end{enumerate}
Then (a) $f_*\mathcal{O}_X = \mathcal{O}_S$ and this holds after
any base change, (b) $R^1f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module whose formation commutes with any base change,
and (c) $R^qf_*\mathcal{O}_X = 0$ for $q \geq 2$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-finite-pure}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a separated, finite type morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Assume that $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}_s)$ is finite for every $s \in S$.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is pure relative to $S$,
\item the scheme theoretic support of $\mathcal{F}$ is finite over $S$, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure relative to $S$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, given a quasi-finite separated morphism $X \to S$ we see
that $X$ is pure relative to $S$ if and only if $X \to S$ is finite.

\label{lemma-generated-by-separable}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $k$.

formulation.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N : D(A, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(B, \text{d})
$$ is a left adjoint to the functor
$$
R\Hom(N, -) : D(B, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(A, \text{d})
$$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a dg (A,B)-bimodule N the source's derived tensor functor D(A)→D(B) is left adjoint to RHom_B(N,-):D(B)→D(A). The proposed removal of named-lemma references does not alter N or the adjunction directions.

phase3.reason: The previously established dg tensor–Hom adjunction combined with existence/computation of both derived functors yields the derived adjunction under the cited general derived-adjoint-functor lemma. The functor directions and unit/counit are correct.

source.label: lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N : D(A, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(B, \text{d})
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-derived-bc} is a left adjoint to the functor
$$
R\Hom(N, -) : D(B, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(A, \text{d})
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-derived-restriction}.

source.label: lemma-base-change-quasi-finite
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-quasi-finite}
\begin{slogan}
(Locally) quasi-finite morphisms are stable under base change.
\end{slogan}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Denote $f' : X' \to S'$ the base change of $f$ by $g$
and denote $g' : X' \to X$ the projection.
Assume $X$ is locally of finite type over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $U \subset X$ (resp.\ $U' \subset X'$)
be the set of points where $f$ (resp.\ $f'$) is quasi-finite.
Then $U' = U \times_S S' = (g')^{-1}(U)$.
\item The base change of a locally quasi-finite morphism is
locally quasi-finite.
\item The base change of a quasi-finite morphism is
quasi-finite.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-when-surjective-local
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-when-surjective-local}
Let $A \to B$ be a local homomorphism of local rings.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B$ is finite as an $A$-module,
\item $\mathfrak m_B$ is a finitely generated ideal,
\item $A \to B$ induces an isomorphism on residue fields, and
\item $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2 \to \mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2$
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $A \to B$ is surjective.

{"approved_content_sha256":"42961171add1df2da857aab7d7d9be511ef1f6f9a3ef1f2371bb5637a2a49c17","candidate_id":"candidate.stacks.9abe4e0a111dc6edd0409917","decision":"source_equivalence_approved","final_content":{"conclusions":["Canonical equivalence of global RHom complexes."],"equivalence_sides":null,"hypotheses":["f qcqs; E,K quasi-coherent-derived; a_f right adjoint."],"logical_form":"single_implication","statement":"Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. formulation.statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. For any $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical morphism on global derived Hom complexes
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K),
\]
induced by $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(E,a_f(K))\to R\mathcal Hom_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ and derived global sections, is a quasi-isomorphism (hence an isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups). This is stronger than merely the degree-zero Hom-set adjunction but does *not* imply that the underlying sheaf-level map is an isomorphism before quasi-coherating.

The proposed quasi-isomorphism of global derived complexes is stronger than degree-zero adjunction but explicitly does not claim unsheafified sheaf-level equivalence.

phase2.semantic_review_note: With I both graded-injective and K-injective, a quasi-isomorphism b:M→M' and map M→I admit a dotted map M'→I commuting UP TO HOMOTOPY. The homotopy qualification distinguishes it from the strict acyclic-domain lifting lemma.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-second-property-dg-injective}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras on
$(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a
K-injective and graded injective
object of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$.
For every solid diagram in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{M} \ar[r]_a \ar[d]_b & \mathcal{I} \\
\mathcal{M}' \ar@{..>}[ru]
}
$$
where $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism a dotted arrow exists making the
diagram commute up to homotopy.

A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

Given a ring map $A\to B$ and a divided power ideal $(J,\delta)$ on $B$, a divided power $A$-derivation $d:B\to M$ into a $B$-module is additive, vanishes on $A$, satisfies $d(bb')=b\,d(b')+b'\,d(b)$, and $d(\delta_n(x))=\delta_{n-1}(x)d(x)$ for $x\in J$. The universal module representing such derivations is $\Omega_{B/A,\delta}$ with universal map $d_{B/A,\delta}$. The ordinary Kähler differential module $\Omega_{B/A}$ represents all $A$-derivations. For a divided power scheme $(T,\mathcal J,\delta)\to S$, the sheaf $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ represents divided power derivations and is the quotient of $\Omega_{T/S}$ by the divided-power derivative relations.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above,
For any affine object $(U, T, \delta)$ of $\text{Cris}(X/S)$
mapping into an affine open $V \subset S$ we have
$$
\Gamma((U, T, \delta), \Omega_{X/S}) =
\Omega_{\Gamma(T, \mathcal{O}_T)/\Gamma(V, \mathcal{O}_V), \delta}
$$
where the right hand side is
defined by the universal divided power derivation.

conclusions:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a smooth proper scheme over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let
$H : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \mathcal{A}$ be a homological
functor (Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-homological})
such that for all $K$ in $D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ the object
$H^i(K)$ is nonzero for only a finite number of $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Then there exists an integer $m \geq 1$ such that
$H^i(\mathcal{F}) = 0$ for any coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
$\mathcal{F}$ and $i \not \in [-m, m]$.
Similarly for cohomological functors.
For a (co)homological functor H, the symbols H^i(E) denote the standard shifted evaluations of H. The hypothesis is individual finite cohomological support **for every perfect K**; the conclusion is a uniform bound for all coherent sheaves, using smooth proper regularity.
hypotheses: A scheme $T$ has the *resolution property* if every finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf admits a surjection from a finite-rank locally free sheaf. For $S$-schemes $X,Y$, $\mathcal E\boxtimes\mathcal G=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal E\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal G$. A triangulated category has a *strong generator* if some object $G$ generates all objects by shifts, finite direct sums, direct summands and distinguished-triangle cones using at most a uniform finite number of cone steps.

A scheme $T$ has the *resolution property* if every finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf admits a surjection from a finite-rank locally free sheaf. For $S$-schemes $X,Y$, $\mathcal E\boxtimes\mathcal G=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal E\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal G$. A triangulated category has a *strong generator* if some object $G$ generates all objects by shifts, finite direct sums, direct summands and distinguished-triangle cones using at most a uniform finite number of cone steps.

\label{lemma-boundedness}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a smooth proper scheme over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let
$H : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \mathcal{A}$ be a homological
functor (Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-homological})
such that for all $K$ in $D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ the object
$H^i(K)$ is nonzero for only a finite number of $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Then there exists an integer $m \geq 1$ such that
$H^i(\mathcal{F}) = 0$ for any coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
$\mathcal{F}$ and $i \not \in [-m, m]$.
Similarly for cohomological functors.

\label{lemma-cover}
\begin{slogan}
Zariski-local properties of modules and algebras
\end{slogan}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $S$ be an $R$-algebra.
Suppose that $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ is a finite list of
elements of $R$ such that $\bigcup D(f_i) = \Spec(R)$,
in other words $(f_1, \ldots, f_n) = R$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If each $M_{f_i} = 0$ then $M = 0$.
\item If each $M_{f_i}$ is a finite $R_{f_i}$-module,
then $M$ is a finite $R$-module.
\item If each $M_{f_i}$ is a finitely presented $R_{f_i}$-module,
then $M$ is a finitely presented $R$-module.
\item Let $M \to N$ be a map of $R$-modules. If $M_{f_i} \to N_{f_i}$
is an isomorphism for each $i$ then $M \to N$ is an isomorphism.
\item Let $0 \to M'' \to M \to M' \to 0$ be a complex of $R$-modules.
If $0 \to M''_{f_i} \to M_{f_i} \to M'_{f_i} \to 0$ is exact for each $i$,
then $0 \to M'' \to M \to M' \to 0$ is exact.
\item If each $R_{f_i}$ is Noetherian, then $R$ is Noetherian.
\item If each $S_{f_i}$ is a finite type $R_{f_i}$-algebra, then
$S$ is a finite type $R$-algebra.
\item If each $S_{f_i}$ is of finite presentation over $R_{f_i}$, then
$S$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra.

Let $R$ be a domain. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The domain $R$ is a normal domain,
\item for every prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$ the local ring
$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain, and
\item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ the ring $R_{\mathfrak m}$
is a normal domain.
\end{enumerate}
A normal domain means a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. A normal ring means a ring whose localization at every prime ideal is a normal domain.

\label{lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section}
Let $X$ be a quasi-affine scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $E \subset W \subset X$ with $E$ finite
and $W$ open. Then there exists an $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$
such that $X_s$ is affine and $E \subset X_s \subset W$.

For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A $k$-linear *cohomological functor* $H:\mathcal T^{op}\to\mathrm{Vect}_k$ is contravariant and yields a long exact sequence under every shifted distinguished triangle. *Homological* means the analogous covariant long exact property. An object $C$ is *compact* if maps from $C$ commute with arbitrary small direct sums; a triangulated category is *compactly generated* if a set of compact objects detects zero objects.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-assassin-constructible}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of finite presentation.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
of finite presentation. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subscheme
such that $U \to Y$ is quasi-compact. Then the set
$$
E = \{y \in Y \mid \text{Ass}_{X_y}(\mathcal{F}_y) \subset U_y\}
$$
is locally constructible in $Y$.

Let $j : U \to X$ be a separated \'etale morphism of quasi-compact

A constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf is the $I$-adic inverse limit of its constructible reductions; lisse means reductions locally constant; adic lisse means locally completed constant finite-type reduction.

constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$, then $\mathcal{F}$
is adic lisse.

\label{lemma-connected-lisse}
Let $X$ be a connected scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let
$I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a lisse
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$, then $\mathcal{F}$
is adic lisse.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-weakly-etale}
Let $A \to B$ be a weakly \'etale ring map.
Then there exists a faithfully flat, ind-\'etale ring map
$B \to B'$ such that $A \to B'$ is ind-\'etale.

\label{lemma-largest-quasi-coherent-subsheaf}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{F}$ be a $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule.
There exists a unique quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule
$\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{G}$ with the following property:
For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{H}$ the map
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G}')
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G})
$$
is bijective. In particular $\mathcal{G}'$ is the largest quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule of $\mathcal{F}$ contained in $\mathcal{G}$.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Formation of the set
$$
T = \{x \in X \mid \mathcal{O}_{X_{f(x)}, x}
\text{ is a complete intersection over }\kappa(f(x))\}

commutes with arbitrary base change:

set $T'$ for the morphism $f'$ is equal to $T' = (g')^{-1}(T)$.

presentation then the same holds for the open set of points

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Formation of the set
$$
T = \{x \in X \mid \mathcal{O}_{X_{f(x)}, x}
\text{ is a complete intersection over }\kappa(f(x))\}
$$
commutes with arbitrary base change:
For any morphism $g : S' \to S$, consider
the base change $f' : X' \to S'$ of $f$ and the
projection $g' : X' \to X$. Then the corresponding
set $T'$ for the morphism $f'$ is equal to $T' = (g')^{-1}(T)$.
In particular, if $f$ is assumed flat, and locally of finite
presentation then the same holds for the open set of points
where $f$ is syntomic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-nil}
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal,
and let $\gamma$ be a divided power structure on $I$. Assume $p$ is nilpotent
in $A/I$. Then $I$ is locally nilpotent if and only if $p$ is nilpotent in $A$.

conclusions:
Let $G$ be a profinite topological group.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^i(G, M)$ is torsion for $i > 0$ and any $G$-module $M$, and
\item $H^i(G, M) = 0$ if $M$ is a $\mathbf{Q}$-vector space.
\end{enumerate}
The coefficients are **discrete continuous** G-modules. Only positive cohomological degrees are torsion/zero; invariants in degree zero can survive.
hypotheses: For a topological group $G$, a **discrete continuous $G$-module** is an abelian group with the discrete topology and continuous left $G$-action, equivalently every element has open stabilizer. Let $\operatorname{Mod}_G$ be their abelian category. For a ring $R$, $\operatorname{Mod}_{R,G}$ consists of $R$-modules with compatible continuous **$R$-linear** $G$-action. Group cohomology $H^i(G,M)$ is the right-derived functor of the **invariants** $M^G$ on these categories, not the continuous-cochain cohomology of arbitrary nondiscrete topological modules. If $M$ is finite projective as an $R$-module, $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ has **contragredient** action $(g\lambda)(m)=\lambda(g^{-1}m)$, and $M^\vee\otimes_RN$ the diagonal action. $\operatorname{Ext}^i(M,N)$ is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R,G}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-henselian-pair}
\begin{slogan}
Approximation for henselian pairs.
\end{slogan}
Let $(A, I)$ be a henselian pair with $A$ Noetherian.
Let $A^\wedge$ be the $I$-adic completion
of $A$. Assume at least one of the following
conditions holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to A^\wedge$ is a regular ring map,
\item $A$ is a Noetherian G-ring, or
\item $(A, I)$ is the henselization
(More on Algebra, Lemma \ref{more-algebra-lemma-henselization})
of a pair $(B, J)$ where $B$ is a Noetherian G-ring.
\end{enumerate}
Given $f_1, \ldots, f_m \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$
and $\hat{a}_1, \ldots, \hat{a}_n \in A^\wedge$ such that
$f_j(\hat{a}_1, \ldots, \hat{a}_n) = 0$
for $j = 1, \ldots, m$, for every $N \geq 1$ there exist
$a_1, \ldots, a_n \in A$ such that
$\hat{a}_i - a_i \in I^N$ and such that $f_j(a_1, \ldots, a_n) = 0$
for $j = 1, \ldots, m$.

Assume the open sets $X_s$, where $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$

form a basis for the topology on $X$.

\label{lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$, then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in
$[a, b]$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-P-universally-injective}
Let $R$ be a ring having property (P) of
Lemma \ref{lemma-auto-ass-implies-P}.
Let $u : N \to M$ be a homomorphism of projective $R$-modules.
Then $u$ is universally injective if and only if $u$ is injective.

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *stable curve* (in the situation $g\ge2$) has no rational tails or rational bridges, equivalently each genus-zero irreducible component meets the remainder of $X$ in at least three geometric points. Its dualizing sheaf $\omega_X$ is invertible. A contraction to a stable curve means a proper morphism $c:X\to X_{\mathrm{st}}$ obtained by successively contracting rational tails and bridges and whose target has no such components.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $c : X \to Y$ be a morphism of proper schemes over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_Y = c_*\mathcal{O}_X$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal{O}_X = 0$,
\item $X$ and $Y$ are reduced, Gorenstein, and have dimension $1$,
\item $\exists\ m \in \mathbf{Z}$ with
$H^1(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m}) = 0$ and $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$
generated by global sections.
\end{enumerate}
Then $c^*\omega_Y \cong \omega_X$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A proper c:X→Y with c_*O_X=O_Y and R¹c_*O_X=0 between reduced Gorenstein one-dimensional schemes satisfies c*ω_Y≅ω_X, provided some integer m makes ω_X^m globally generated with H¹=0. The source's existential integer and both vanish/generation hypotheses remain.

phase3.reason: Using Stein factorization and finite birationality off finitely many contracted fibres, the proof constructs the canonical duality trace morphism b:c^*omega_Y→omega_X, generically an isomorphism. A globally generated H^1-acyclic tensor power plus equality of Euler characteristics makes b^m an isomorphism on sections and hence on sheaves; b is therefore invertible. Preliminary reduction omits details.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-contract-gorenstein-canonical}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $c : X \to Y$ be a morphism of proper schemes over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_Y = c_*\mathcal{O}_X$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal{O}_X = 0$,
\item $X$ and $Y$ are reduced, Gorenstein, and have dimension $1$,
\item $\exists\ m \in \mathbf{Z}$ with
$H^1(X, \omega_X^{\otimes m}) = 0$ and $\omega_X^{\otimes m}$
generated by global sections.
\end{enumerate}
Then $c^*\omega_Y \cong \omega_X$.

On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$ of a scheme $X$, a *constant sheaf* $\underline E$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value a set $E$ (similarly an abelian group or $\Lambda$-module). A sheaf $\mathcal F$ is *locally constant* if there is an étale cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ on which it becomes isomorphic to a constant sheaf; it is *finite locally constant* for set-valued sheaves if its constant fibre sets are finite, and *finite type locally constant* for $\Lambda$-modules if its local fibre modules are finitely generated. For an étale map $U\to X$, its representable sheaf is $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$. In an abelian category a *weak Serre subcategory* is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions (without necessarily all subobjects).

**Statement (source hypotheses preserved):**
Let $X$ be a connected scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring and let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules.
Then there exists a $\Lambda$-module $M$ and an \'etale covering
$\{U_i \to X\}$ such that $\mathcal{F}|_{U_i} \cong \underline{M}|_{U_i}$.

**Typed interpretation:** The claim is interpreted using the preceding explicit definitions; retain exactly the original assumptions and conclusion on the small étale site (distinguishing finite from finite-type local fibres).

\label{lemma-connected-locally-constant}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Leray}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be
a bounded below complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
There is a spectral sequence
$$
E_2^{p, q} = H^p(Y, R^qf_*(\mathcal{F}^\bullet))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(X, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$.

Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. A *partial universe* is a sufficiently large set of schemes and morphisms used to choose a **small** big-$\tau$ site, closed under relevant finite limits and with every external $\tau$-cover of an object admitting a refinement internally; distinct choices give inclusions of corresponding sites. A small étale *topos* of $S$ is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$, the category of set-valued sheaves; it is not the category of all big-site sheaves.

\label{lemma-degree-tensor-product}
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$
over $k$, and let $\mathcal{E}$, $\mathcal{V}$ be locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of constant finite rank. Then
$$
\deg(\mathcal{E} \otimes \mathcal{V}) =
\text{rank}(\mathcal{E}) \deg(\mathcal{V}) +
\text{rank}(\mathcal{V}) \deg(\mathcal{E})
$$

formulation.statement:
A *site* $\mathcal C$ is a small category endowed with covering families $\{U_i\to U\}$ satisfying the isomorphism, composition/refinement, and base-change axioms. A *presheaf* of sets (or abelian groups) is a contravariant functor. For a covering, a *matching family* consists of sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose restrictions to every fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ coincide (including $i=j$). A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

The category of abelian sheaves on a site is an abelian category
which has enough injectives.

formulation.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. Being both **quasi-compact** (in the site sense) and **weakly contractible** is required for a site object U; neither property alone is the stated hypothesis.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$
be an object of $\mathcal{C}$ which is quasi-compact and
weakly contractible. Then
$j_!\mathcal{O}_U$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: If U is BOTH quasi-compact and weakly contractible, j_{U!}O_U is compact in the unbounded derived category. Distinction from merely compact topological space retained.

phase3.reason: The short proof combines vanishing of higher cohomology on weakly contractible objects with direct-sum commutation of sections over quasi-compact objects.

\label{lemma-quasi-compact-weakly-contractible-compact}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$

weakly contractible. Then
$j_!\mathcal{O}_U$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $R^h$, $R^{sh}$ are filtered colimits of \'etale $R$-algebras,
\item $R^h$ is henselian, $R^{sh}$ is strictly henselian,
\item $\mathfrak m R^h$ (resp.\ $\mathfrak m R^{sh}$) is the
maximal ideal of $R^h$ (resp.\ $R^{sh}$), and
\item $\kappa = R^h/\mathfrak m R^h$, and
$\kappa^{sep} = R^{sh}/\mathfrak m R^{sh}$ as extensions of $\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}
The maps R→R^h→R^sh are **flat and local**, both rings are *filtered colimits of étale R-algebras*, and the residue-field extensions are respectively κ and the **chosen κ^sep**. The strict construction depends on a separable-closure choice; 'canonical' means relative to that choice.

The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local ring and
$\kappa\subset\kappa^{sep}$ a separable algebraic closure.
There exist canonical flat local ring maps $R \to R^h \to R^{sh}$ where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R^h$, $R^{sh}$ are filtered colimits of \'etale $R$-algebras,
\item $R^h$ is henselian, $R^{sh}$ is strictly henselian,
\item $\mathfrak m R^h$ (resp.\ $\mathfrak m R^{sh}$) is the
maximal ideal of $R^h$ (resp.\ $R^{sh}$), and
\item $\kappa = R^h/\mathfrak m R^h$, and
$\kappa^{sep} = R^{sh}/\mathfrak m R^{sh}$ as extensions of $\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}

**Precise scope:** The maps R→R^h→R^sh are **flat and local**, both rings are *filtered colimits of étale R-algebras*, and the residue-field extensions are respectively κ and the **chosen κ^sep**. The strict construction depends on a separable-closure choice; 'canonical' means relative to that choice.

Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local ring and
$\kappa\subset\kappa^{sep}$ a separable algebraic closure.
There exist canonical flat local ring maps $R \to R^h \to R^{sh}$ where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R^h$, $R^{sh}$ are filtered colimits of \'etale $R$-algebras,
\item $R^h$ is henselian, $R^{sh}$ is strictly henselian,
\item $\mathfrak m R^h$ (resp.\ $\mathfrak m R^{sh}$) is the
maximal ideal of $R^h$ (resp.\ $R^{sh}$), and
\item $\kappa = R^h/\mathfrak m R^h$, and
$\kappa^{sep} = R^{sh}/\mathfrak m R^{sh}$ as extensions of $\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a
homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$H^i(L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}})$ is the sheaf associated to the
presheaf $U \mapsto H^i(L_{\mathcal{B}(U)/\mathcal{A}(U)})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-H1-regular}
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map.
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ be a sequence in $B$ such that $B/(f_1, \ldots, f_r)$
is $A$-flat. Let $A \to A'$ be a ring map. Then the canonical map
$$
H_1(K_\bullet(B, f_1, \ldots, f_r)) \otimes_A A'
\longrightarrow
H_1(K_\bullet(B', f'_1, \ldots, f'_r))
$$
is surjective. Here $B' = B \otimes_A A'$ and $f_i' \in B'$ is the image
of $f_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-finite-presentation-purity-open}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of finite presentation.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
of finite presentation flat over $S$. Then the set
$$
U = \{s \in S \mid \mathcal{F}\text{ is pure along }X_s\}
$$
is open in $S$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let
$$
p :
L = \underline{\Spec}(\text{Sym}^*(\mathcal{L}))
\longrightarrow
X
$$
be the associated vector bundle over $X$.
Then $p^* : \mathrm{CH}_k(X) \to \mathrm{CH}_{k + 1}(L)$ is an isomorphism for all $k$.

\label{lemma-linebundle}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let
$$
p :
L = \underline{\Spec}(\text{Sym}^*(\mathcal{L}))
\longrightarrow
X
$$
be the associated vector bundle over $X$.
Then $p^* : \CH_k(X) \to \CH_{k + 1}(L)$ is an isomorphism for all $k$.

\label{lemma-silly-normal}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $x, y \in R$ be nonzerodivisors.
Let $R[x/y] \subset R_{xy}$ be the $R$-subalgebra generated
by $x/y$, and similarly for the subalgebras $R[y/x]$ and $R[x/y, y/x]$.
If $R$ is integrally closed in $R_x$ or $R_y$, then the sequence
$$
0 \to R \xrightarrow{(-1, 1)} R[x/y] \oplus R[y/x] \xrightarrow{(1, 1)}
R[x/y, y/x] \to 0
$$
is a short exact sequence of $R$-modules.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is locally of finite type over $k$,
\item $\Omega_{X/k}$ is locally free,
\item $X$ is reduced, and
\item $k$ is perfect.
\end{enumerate}
Then the structure morphism $X \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth.

formulation.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring and $(A,\mathrm d),(B,\mathrm d)$ differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodule.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N$ defines a compact object of $D(B, \text{d})$, and
\item the map $H^k(A) \to \Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N[k])$ is an
isomorphism for all $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the functor $-\otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N$ is fully faithful.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The compactness hypothesis is on N as an object of D(B) and the comparison H^k(A)→Hom_D(B)(N,N[k]) must be an isomorphism for EVERY integer k. Exactly these assumptions imply derived tensor by N is fully faithful.

phase3.reason: By the tensor–RHom adjunction, full faithfulness reduces to the unit M→RHom(N,M⊗^L_A N). Compactness of N makes its cohomological test preserve sums; a property-(P) filtration reduces to the free shifts A[k], on which the assumed isomorphism H^k(A)→Hom(N,N[k]) establishes the unit.

hypotheses:
Standing assumptions and notation from Stacks Situation \ref{situation-setup}:
Here $S$ is a locally Noetherian, and universally catenary scheme.
Moreover, we assume $S$ is endowed with a dimension function
$\delta : S \longrightarrow \mathbf{Z}$.

Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism.
Assume $X$, $Y$ integral and $\dim_\delta(X) = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism.
Assume $X$, $Y$ integral and $\dim_\delta(X) = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
Then either $f(X)$ is contained in a proper closed subscheme
of $Y$, or $f$ is dominant and the extension of function fields
$R(X)/R(Y)$ is finite.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The pinned equal-dimension lemma at 1815–1824 applies to an arbitrary morphism f:X→Y of INTEGRAL schemes locally of finite type over (S,δ), with equal δ-dimensions. It has a DISJUNCTION: image inside a PROPER CLOSED subscheme of Y OR dominance with finite function field extension R(X)/R(Y); the reviewed formulation preserves both possibilities and finite, not necessarily isomorphic, fields.

phase3.reason: Separates the nondominant case, uses generic points in the dominant case, and derives finite function-field degree from transcendence-degree zero.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-equal-dimension}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism.
Assume $X$, $Y$ integral and $\dim_\delta(X) = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
Then either $f(X)$ is contained in a proper closed subscheme
of $Y$, or $f$ is dominant and the extension of function fields
$R(X)/R(Y)$ is finite.

\label{lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm}
Let $\pi : X \to Y$ be a finite locally free morphism of degree $d \geq 1$.
Then there exists a canonical norm of degree $d$ whose formation commutes
with arbitrary base change.

conclusions: The diagonal multiplication-kernel annihilator is generated by the image of det(gij).
hypotheses: Two Koszul-regular sequences f_i in P and g_j in P⊗_A B; B=P/(f) is A-flat; g generate the kernel of P⊗_A B→B; matrix gij expresses f⊗1.
formulation.statement: Let $A\to P$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in P$ be a *Koszul-regular sequence* (its Koszul complex is exact in positive degrees). Assume $B=P/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ is flat over $A$. Suppose $g_1,\ldots,g_n\in P\otimes_AB$ form a Koszul-regular sequence and generate the kernel of the natural multiplication map $P\otimes_AB\to B$. Choose elements $g_{ij}\in P\otimes_AB$ such that $f_i\otimes1=\sum_{j=1}^n g_{ij}g_j$. Let $\bar\delta\in B\otimes_AB$ be the image of $\det(g_{ij})$ under the map $P\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_AB$. Then the annihilator ideal $J=\operatorname{Ann}_{B\otimes_AB}(\ker(B\otimes_AB\xrightarrow\mu B))$ is the principal ideal $(\bar\delta)$ of $B\otimes_AB$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For A→P, a Koszul-regular sequence f_i cutting out B flat over A, and a second Koszul-regular sequence g_j generating the multiplication kernel in P⊗_A B with f_i⊗1=Σ g_{ij}g_j, the annihilator of the diagonal ideal in B⊗_A B is generated by det(g_{ij}). Both regularity hypotheses and the exact ring containing the annihilator remain.

phase3.reason: The Koszul resolutions of B and the diagonal have a morphism induced by the matrix (g_ij); flatness allows comparison of Tor and the determinant identifies the top-degree annihilator.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-permanence-quasi-finite}
Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Let $x \in X$. If $X \to S$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then
$X \to Y$ is quasi-finite at $x$.
If $X$ is locally quasi-finite over $S$, then $X \to Y$
is locally quasi-finite.

The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.
formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

Let $A \to B$ be a surjective ring map whose kernel $I$ is Koszul.
Then $L_{B/A}$ is quasi-isomorphic to $I/I^2[1]$.

The reconstructed text preserves this local notion rather than unnecessarily requiring a single global regular sequence.

\label{lemma-functor-on-fp-modules}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a category having filtered
colimits. Let $F : \text{Mod}^{fp}_A \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor. Then $F$
extends uniquely to a functor $F' : \text{Mod}_A \to \mathcal{B}$
which commutes with filtered colimits.
