source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-mapping-property-glue}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $X = \bigcup_{i\in I} U_i$ be an open covering.
The functor which associates to a sheaf of
sets $\mathcal{F}$ the following collection of
glueing data
$$
(\mathcal{F}|_{U_i},
(\mathcal{F}|_{U_i})|_{U_i \cap U_j}
\to
(\mathcal{F}|_{U_j})|_{U_i \cap U_j}
)
$$
with respect to the covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
defines an equivalence of categories between
$\Sh(X)$ and the category of glueing
data. A similar statement holds for
abelian sheaves, resp.\ sheaves of algebraic structures,
resp.\ sheaves of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-etale}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of affine schemes.
Let $Z' \to Z$ be an \'etale morphism with $Z'$ affine.
Then there exists an \'etale morphism $X' \to X$ with $X'$
affine such that $Z' \cong Z \times_X X'$ as schemes over $Z$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-add-simplices}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Let $U \subset V$ be simplicial sets, with $U_n, V_n$
finite nonempty for all $n$.
Assume that $U$ and $V$ have finitely many nondegenerate simplices.
Then the morphism
$$
\Hom(V, K)_0
\longrightarrow
\Hom(U, K)_0
$$
of $\text{SR}(\mathcal{C}, X)$ is a covering.

source.label: lemma-zariski
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-zariski}
Let $T$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $T' \to T$ is an isomorphism then $\{T' \to T\}$
is a Zariski covering of $T$.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is a Zariski covering and for each
$i$ we have a Zariski covering $\{T_{ij} \to T_i\}_{j\in J_i}$, then
$\{T_{ij} \to T\}_{i \in I, j\in J_i}$ is a Zariski covering.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is a Zariski covering
and $T' \to T$ is a morphism of schemes then
$\{T' \times_T T_i \to T'\}_{i\in I}$ is a Zariski covering.
\end{enumerate}

Let $f : X \to S$ be a dominant morphism of schemes.
Let $g : S' \to S$ be an open morphism of schemes, and let $f' : X' \to S'$
be the base change of $f$ by $g$. Then $f'$ is dominant.

\label{lemma-depth-pushforward}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $s \not \in f(X)$, then $s$ is not weakly associated
to $f_*\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $s \not \in f(X)$ and $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$ is Noetherian,
then $s$ is not associated to $f_*\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $s \not \in f(X)$, $(f_*\mathcal{F})_s$ is a finite
$\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$-module, and $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$
is Noetherian, then $\text{depth}((f_*\mathcal{F})_s) \geq 2$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ and $a \in \mathfrak m_s$
is a nonzerodivisor, then $a$ is a nonzerodivisor on $(f_*\mathcal{F})_s$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ and $a, b \in \mathfrak m_s$
is a regular sequence, then $a$ is a nonzerodivisor on $(f_*\mathcal{F})_s$
and $b$ is a nonzerodivisor on $(f_*\mathcal{F})_s/a(f_*\mathcal{F})_s$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ and $(f_*\mathcal{F})_s$
is a finite $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$-module, then
$\text{depth}((f_*\mathcal{F})_s) \geq
\min(2, \text{depth}(\mathcal{O}_{S, s}))$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible sheaf on $X$.
Let
$$
E \subset W \subset X
$$
with $E$ finite and $W$ open in $X$. Then there exists an $n > 0$
and a section $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ such that
$X_s$ is affine and $E \subset X_s \subset W$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characteristic-polynomial-prime}
Let $R \to A$ be a ring homomorphism.
Assume $A \cong R^{\oplus n}$ as an $R$-module.
Let $f \in A$. The multiplication map $m_f: A
\to A$ is $R$-linear and hence
has a characteristic polynomial
$P(T) = T^n + r_{n-1}T^{n-1} + \ldots + r_0 \in R[T]$.
For any prime
$\mathfrak{p} \in \Spec(R)$, $f$ acts nilpotently on $A
\otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak{p})$ if and only if $\mathfrak p \in
V(r_0, \ldots, r_{n-1})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proetale-cohomology-independent-partial-universe}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $S_\proetale \subset S_\proetale'$ be
two small pro-\'etale sites of $S$ as constructed in
Definition \ref{definition-big-small-proetale}. Then the inclusion functor
satisfies the assumptions of 
Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-bigger-site}.
Hence there exist morphisms of topoi
$$
\xymatrix{
\Sh(S_\proetale) \ar[r]^g &
\Sh(S_\proetale') \ar[r]^f &
\Sh(S_\proetale)
}
$$
whose composition is isomorphic to the identity and with $f_* = g^{-1}$.
Moreover,
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $\mathcal{F}' \in \textit{Ab}(S_\proetale')$ we have
$H^p(S_\proetale', \mathcal{F}') = H^p(S_\proetale, g^{-1}\mathcal{F}')$,
\item for $\mathcal{F} \in \textit{Ab}(S_\proetale)$ we have
$$
H^p(S_\proetale, \mathcal{F}) =
H^p(S_\proetale', g_*\mathcal{F}) =
H^p(S_\proetale', f^{-1}\mathcal{F}).
$$
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-very-ample-vanish-at-point}
Let $k$ be an infinite field. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a very ample invertible sheaf on $X$.
Let $n \geq 0$ and $x, x_1, \ldots, x_n \in X$ be points with
$x$ a $k$-rational point, i.e., $\kappa(x) = k$, and
$x \not = x_i$ for $i = 1, \ldots, n$.
Then there exists an $s \in H^0(X, \mathcal{L})$ which vanishes at
$x$ but not at $x_i$.

$f' : X' \to S$ and a closed immersion $X \to X'$ of schemes over $S$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a differential graded category over $R$ satisfying the following axioms. Axiom (A) requires a zero object and binary differential graded direct sums. Axiom (B) requires dg shift functors $[n]$, with $[0]=\mathrm{id}$ and $[n+m]=[n]\circ[m]$, and composition-compatible identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(x,y[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(x,y)[n]$ of dg modules. Axiom (C) requires, for every closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$, an admissible short exact sequence $y\to c(f)\to x[1]$ in $\operatorname{Comp}(\mathcal A)$ whose connecting morphism $x[1]\to y[1]$ agrees with $f[1]$. let $\alpha : x \to y$ and $\beta : y \to z$
define an admissible short exact sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
x \ar[r] &
y\ar[r] &
z
}
$$
in $\text{Comp}(\mathcal{A})$. Let $(x, y, z, \alpha, \beta, \delta)$
be the associated triangle in $K(\mathcal{A})$. Then, the triangles
$$
(z[-1], x, y, \delta[-1], \alpha, \beta)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(z[-1], x, c(\delta[-1]), \delta[-1], i, p)
$$
are isomorphic.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For arbitrary dg right A-module M and integer k, maps A[k]→M correspond to closed elements of M^{-k}, while homotopy classes correspond to H^{-k}(M). Both Hom categories and the negative shift degrees agree with the pinned source.

phase3.reason: A dg-map A[k]→M is uniquely determined by the closed image of the free generator in degree −k. Chain homotopies identify two such maps exactly when their images differ by a coboundary, giving the indicated H^{-k}(M).

source.label: lemma-hom-from-shift-free
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-hom-from-shift-free}
Let $(A, d)$ be a differential graded algebra. Then we have
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}}(A[k], M) =
\Ker(\text{d} : M^{-k} \to M^{-k + 1})
$$
and
$$
\Hom_{K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})}(A[k], M) = H^{-k}(M)
$$
for any differential graded $A$-module $M$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-countable-fg-tensor}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module which is countable.
Then $M$ is a finite $R$-module if and only if
$M \otimes_R R^\mathbf{N} \to M^\mathbf{N}$ is surjective.

hypotheses: Cartesian qcqs square, g flat or f and g Tor independent, and right adjoints as defined.
formulation.statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{matrix}
\]
where $f$ and $g$ are *Tor-independent*, meaning the higher Tor sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ over $\mathcal O_Y$ vanish. Write $a=a_f$ and $a'=a_{f'}$ for the respective right adjoints of derived pushforward. The usual derived base-change map is $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$; under Tor-independence it is an isomorphism. Its adjoint mate is the isomorphism $\xi:Rg'_*a'\xrightarrow{\sim} a Rg_*$. The duality base-change map is the natural transformation $\alpha:L(g')^*a\to a' Lg^*$ obtained by composing unit $\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^*$, $\xi^{-1}$, and counit $L(g')^*Rg'_*\to\mathrm{id}$. Then the canonical adjoint-mate transformation $\xi:Rg'_*a'\to a\,Rg_*$, considered as a natural transformation from $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, is an isomorphism. This holds if $g$ is flat, and more generally whenever $f$ and $g$ are Tor-independent; the square need not be proper.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L739 has a CARTESIAN qcqs square X'→X over Y'→Y, with g FLAT OR f,g Tor-independent, and concludes the right-adjoint mate Rg'_* a'→a Rg_* is an isomorphism. The proposal restores all square labels, the Tor-independent alternative and correct mate orientation; no properness assumption is added.

phase3.reason: Derived flat/Tor-independent base change is an isomorphism; taking the mate under adjunction gives the claimed base-change isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-finite-type-injective-into-flat-mod-m}
Let $A \to B$ be a local ring homomorphism of local rings
which is essentially of finite type. Let $M$ be a flat $A$-module,
$N$ a finite $B$-module and $u : N \to M$ an $A$-module map such that
$\overline{u} : N/\mathfrak m_AN \to M/\mathfrak m_AM$ is injective.
Then $u$ is $A$-universally injective, $N$ is of finite presentation over
$B$, and $N$ is flat over $A$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A \to B \to C$ be a complex of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Assume $A, B, C$ have finite filtrations and that
$\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to \text{gr}(C)$ is exact.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$\text{gr}^p(A) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to \text{gr}^p(C)$ is exact,
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$F^p(A) \to F^p(B) \to F^p(C)$ is exact,
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$A/F^p(A) \to B/F^p(B) \to C/F^p(C)$ is exact,
\item the maps $A \to B$ and $B \to C$ are strict, and
\item $A \to B \to C$ is exact (as a sequence in $\mathcal{A}$).
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $A,B\subset K$ subrings with fraction field $K$; put $R=A\cap B$. The map $A\otimes B\to K$ means multiplication (tensor over $\mathbf Z$ when no base subscript is supplied). In this setup assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is a Noetherian semi-local domain of dimension $1$,
\item $B$ is a Noetherian semi-local domain of dimension $1$,
\item $A \otimes B \to K$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Spec(A) \to \Spec(R)$ and $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(R)$
are open immersions covering $\Spec(R)$ and $K = A \otimes_R B$.

\label{lemma-iff-countably-indexed}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of affine
formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces,
surjective, and flat. Then $X$ is countably indexed if and only
if $Y$ is countably indexed.

source.label: lemma-unramified-at-point
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unramified-at-point}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$.
Set $s = f(x)$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type (resp.\ locally of finite presentation).
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified) at $x$.
\item The fibre $X_s$ is unramified over $\kappa(s)$ at $x$.
\item The $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module $\Omega_{X/S, x}$ is zero.
\item The $\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}$-module $\Omega_{X_s/s, x}$ is zero.
\item The $\kappa(x)$-vector space
$$
\Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) =
\Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x)
$$
is zero.
\item We have $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal{O}_{X, x} = \mathfrak m_x$
and the field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite
separable.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

for $\mathcal{F}$ quasi-coherent on $X$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-duality-dim-1-CM}
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$ which is Cohen-Macaulay
and equidimensional of dimension $1$. The module $\omega_X$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-duality-dim-1} has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_X$ is a dualizing module on $X$
(Duality for Schemes, Section \ref{duality-section-dualizing-module}),
\item $\omega_X$ is a coherent Cohen-Macaulay module whose support is $X$,
\item there are functorial isomorphisms
$\Ext^i_X(K, \omega_X[1]) = \Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)$
compatible with shifts for $K \in D_\QCoh(X)$,
\item there are functorial isomorphisms
$\Ext^{1 + i}(\mathcal{F}, \omega_X) = \Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, \mathcal{F}), k)$
for $\mathcal{F}$ quasi-coherent on $X$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and
residue field $\kappa$. Let $M$ be a finite length $R$-module
which is annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. Let $l = \dim_\kappa(M)$.
Then the map
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M) \longrightarrow \wedge^l_\kappa(M),
\quad
[e_1, \ldots, e_l] \longmapsto e_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge e_l
$$
is an isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-det}
Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and
residue field $\kappa$. Let $M$ be a finite length $R$-module
which is annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. Let $l = \dim_\kappa(M)$.
Then the map
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M) \longrightarrow \wedge^l_\kappa(M),
\quad
[e_1, \ldots, e_l] \longmapsto e_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge e_l
$$
is an isomorphism.

formulation.statement:
For a quasi-coherent nonnegatively graded algebra $\mathcal A$ on S, $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_S(\mathcal A)$ is formed by gluing affine Proj constructions; its twists $\mathcal O_X(d)$ are locally the sheaves associated to the shifted graded module $\mathcal A(d)$, $\mathcal A(d)_n=\mathcal A_{n+d}$, and $\mathcal G(d)=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_X(d)$. Indices of twists are integers. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra. Let
$p : X = \underline{\text{Proj}}_S(\mathcal{A}) \to S$ be the relative
Proj of $\mathcal{A}$. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed subscheme. Denote
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{A}$ the kernel of the canonical map
$$
\mathcal{A}
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq 0} p_*\left((i_*\mathcal{O}_Z)(d)\right).
$$
If $p$ is quasi-compact, then there is an isomorphism
$Z = \underline{\text{Proj}}_S(\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{I})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-subscheme-proj}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra. Let
$p : X = \underline{\text{Proj}}_S(\mathcal{A}) \to S$ be the relative
Proj of $\mathcal{A}$. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed subscheme. Denote
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{A}$ the kernel of the canonical map
$$
\mathcal{A}
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq 0} p_*\left((i_*\mathcal{O}_Z)(d)\right).
$$
If $p$ is quasi-compact, then there is an isomorphism
$Z = \underline{\text{Proj}}_S(\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{I})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
Then $x$ is a closed point of its fibre
if and only if $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is
a finite field extension.

formulation.statement:
For a scheme $T$ locally of finite type over a field $k$, $Z_n(T)$ is the group of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of Krull dimension $n$, and $\mathrm{CH}_n(T)$ is $Z_n(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $n+1$. If $A\subset T$ has dimension at most $n$, write $[A]_n$ for its cycle of $n$-dimensional components weighted by lengths of the local rings at generic points.

Let $k$ be a field, and let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$. Define exterior product on cycles by $[W]\times[V]=[W\times_k V]_{\dim W+\dim V}$ for integral closed $W\subset X$, $V\subset Y$, extending bilinearly, where $[W\times_kV]$ uses generic-point multiplicities even if this product is reducible or nonreduced.

Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$. For integers $n,m$, the map defined on integral closed cycles by the exterior-product formula above
$\times : \mathrm{CH}_n(X) \otimes_{\mathbf{Z}} \mathrm{CH}_m(Y) \to \mathrm{CH}_{n + m}(X \times_k Y)$
is well defined.

\label{lemma-base-change-div}
Let $(A, \text{d}, \gamma)$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-divided-powers-dga}.

Definition \ref{definition-divided-powers-dga}.

\begin{reference}
\cite[Exposee IX, Proposition 2.14]{SGA4}
\end{reference}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of sets on $X_\etale$.
There exist an injective map of sheaves
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} f_{i, *}\underline{E_i}
$$
where $f_i : Y_i \to X$ is a finite and finitely presented morphism and
$E_i$ is a finite set.
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$.
There exist an injective map of abelian sheaves
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} f_{i, *}\underline{M_i}
$$
where $f_i : Y_i \to X$ is a finite and finitely presented morphism and
$M_i$ is a finite abelian group.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$.
There exist an injective map of sheaves of modules
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} f_{i, *}\underline{M_i}
$$
where $f_i : Y_i \to X$ is a finite and finitely presented morphism and
$M_i$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module.
\end{enumerate}
All quantifiers and conditions from the pinned source are retained. The stated conclusion uses the site and sheaf/module categories defined above.
hypotheses: On a **Noetherian scheme** $X$, the definition of a constructible étale sheaf simplifies to a finite partition of $X$ by *locally closed* subschemes on which it is finite locally constant (sets/abelian groups) or **finite type locally constant** over a Noetherian coefficient ring $\Lambda$. A **Serre** subcategory of an abelian category is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions; a *Noetherian object* has ascending chain condition on subobjects. The *support* of an abelian or module sheaf is the set of ordinary points where its geometric stalk is nonzero. A subset is *closed under specialization* if $x\in E$ and $x\leadsto y$ imply $y\in E$. A *finite finitely presented morphism* has a finite algebra structure with finite-presentation constraint; a finite morphism alone need not be finitely presented over a non-Noetherian base.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant-general}
\begin{reference}
\cite[Exposee IX, Proposition 2.14]{SGA4}
\end{reference}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of sets on $X_\etale$.
There exist an injective map of sheaves
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} f_{i, *}\underline{E_i}
$$
where $f_i : Y_i \to X$ is a finite and finitely presented morphism and
$E_i$ is a finite set.
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$.
There exist an injective map of abelian sheaves
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} f_{i, *}\underline{M_i}
$$
where $f_i : Y_i \to X$ is a finite and finitely presented morphism and
$M_i$ is a finite abelian group.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$.
There exist an injective map of sheaves of modules
$$
\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} f_{i, *}\underline{M_i}
$$
where $f_i : Y_i \to X$ is a finite and finitely presented morphism and
$M_i$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module.
\end{enumerate}

Let $A' \to B'$ be a ring map. Let $I \subset A'$ be an ideal.
Set $A = A'/I$ and $B = B'/IB'$. Let $f'_1, \ldots, f'_r \in B'$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A' \to B'$ is flat and of finite presentation (for example smooth),
\item $I$ is locally nilpotent,
\item the images $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in B$ form a quasi-regular sequence,
\item $B/(f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ is smooth over $A$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $B'/(f'_1, \ldots, f'_r)$ is smooth over $A'$.

source.label: lemma-equivalence
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-equivalence}
Let $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ be sites.
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u$ is cocontinuous,
\item $u$ is continuous,
\item given $a, b : U' \to U$ in $\mathcal{C}$ such that
$u(a) = u(b)$, then there exists a covering $\{f_i : U'_i \to U'\}$
in $\mathcal{C}$ such that $a \circ f_i = b \circ f_i$,
\item given $U', U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and
a morphism $c : u(U') \to u(U)$ in $\mathcal{D}$ there exists
a covering $\{f_i : U_i' \to U'\}$ in $\mathcal{C}$
and morphisms $c_i : U_i' \to U$ such that $u(c_i) = c \circ u(f_i)$, and
\item given $V \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ there exists a covering
of $V$ in $\mathcal{D}$ of the form $\{u(U_i) \to V\}_{i \in I}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the morphism of topoi
$$
g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \longrightarrow \Sh(\mathcal{D})
$$
associated to the cocontinuous functor $u$ by
Lemma \ref{lemma-cocontinuous-morphism-topoi}
is an equivalence.

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a subsheaf of the final
object of the \'etale topos of $S$ (see
Sites, Example \ref{sites-example-singleton-sheaf}).
Then there exists a unique open
$W \subset S$ such that $\mathcal{F} = h_W$.
A subterminal sheaf on the **small étale topos** is $h_W$ for a **unique Zariski open W⊂S**. The equality is in Sh(S_etale), not a statement about arbitrary subsheaves of the constant presheaf on the big site.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$, define its support as $\{s\in S:\mathcal F_{\bar s}\ne0\}$ for any/every geometric point above $s$. For an étale $U\to S$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal F(U)$, the *support of $\sigma$* is $U\setminus W_\sigma$, where $W_\sigma$ is the largest **Zariski open** of $U$ on which $\sigma$ is zero. The support of an arbitrary abelian sheaf need **not** be closed, while support of an individual section is closed. A **subterminal sheaf** means a subsheaf of the terminal one-point sheaf on $S_{\acute etale}$; $h_W$ denotes the representable étale sheaf of an open subscheme $W\subseteq S$.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$, define its support as $\{s\in S:\mathcal F_{\bar s}\ne0\}$ for any/every geometric point above $s$. For an étale $U\to S$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal F(U)$, the *support of $\sigma$* is $U\setminus W_\sigma$, where $W_\sigma$ is the largest **Zariski open** of $U$ on which $\sigma$ is zero. The support of an arbitrary abelian sheaf need **not** be closed, while support of an individual section is closed. A **subterminal sheaf** means a subsheaf of the terminal one-point sheaf on $S_{\acute etale}$; $h_W$ denotes the representable étale sheaf of an open subscheme $W\subseteq S$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a subsheaf of the final
object of the \'etale topos of $S$ (see
Sites, Example \ref{sites-example-singleton-sheaf}).
Then there exists a unique open
$W \subset S$ such that $\mathcal{F} = h_W$.

**Precise scope:** A subterminal sheaf on the **small étale topos** is $h_W$ for a **unique Zariski open W⊂S**. The equality is in Sh(S_etale), not a statement about arbitrary subsheaves of the constant presheaf on the big site.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Each subobject of the final sheaf in the small étale topos is h_W for a unique Zariski open W⊂S. The unique-open correspondence and subterminal restriction are retained.

phase3.reason: The complete proof constructs the representing Zariski open from images of étale objects carrying a local section of the subterminal sheaf, with existence and uniqueness following from gluing.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-vanshing-gives-ample}
\begin{reference}
\cite[III Proposition 2.6.1]{EGA}
\end{reference}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $f : X \to \Spec(R)$ be a proper morphism.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X$ (this is equivalent to many other
things, see
Properties, Proposition \ref{properties-proposition-characterize-ample} and
Morphisms, Lemma
\ref{morphisms-lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample}),
\item for every coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ there exists
an $n_0 \geq 0$ such that
$H^p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) = 0$ for all $n \geq n_0$
and $p > 0$, and
\item for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$, there exists an $n \geq 1$
such that $H^1(X, \mathcal{I} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-CM-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. If $f$ is Cohen-Macaulay (More on Morphisms, Definition

$$
f^!\mathcal{O}_Y = \omega_{X/Y}[d]

for some coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\omega_{X/Y}$ flat over $Y$
where $d$ is the locally constant
function on $X$ which gives the relative dimension of $X$ over $Y$.

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $X$ be a variety over $k$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X^{(p)}$ is reduced,
\item $X$ is geometrically reduced,
\item there is a nonempty open $U \subset X$ smooth over $k$.
\end{enumerate}
In this case $X^{(p)}$ is a variety over $k$ and $F_{X/k} : X \to X^{(p)}$
is a finite dominant morphism of degree $p^{\dim(X)}$.
Absolute Frobenius acts identically on points and by $a\mapsto a^p$ on functions. For $X/S$, $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$, and $F_{X/S}$ is the canonical map induced by absolute Frobenius.

hypotheses: For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a sheaf homomorphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheafified two-term complex $(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{\mathcal P/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P}\mathcal B)$ in degrees $-1,0$, where locally $\mathcal P\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ is a polynomial algebra presentation with kernel $\mathcal I$. The canonical comparison identifies this complex with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ in the derived category.

A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
E \ar[r]_a \ar[d]_f & F \ar[d]^g \\
H \ar[r]^b & G
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of sheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, so
$E = H \times_G F$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation, and
\item $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces, separated, and
locally quasi-finite
\end{enumerate}
then $b$ is representable (by schemes) as well as separated and
locally quasi-finite.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L677–697 assumes a cartesian square E=H×_G F of fppf sheaves, g representable/surjective/flat/lfp, and a representable/separated/locally quasi-finite. The proposed conclusion correctly upgrades b to representable by SCHEMES, separated and locally quasi-finite.

phase3.reason: The proof reduces to the case of a scheme base, uses étale/fppf descent of separated locally quasi-finite spaces, and transfers the properties.

formulation.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $X$ be an integral normal scheme with separably closed
function field.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A separated \'etale morphism $U \to X$ is a
disjoint union of open immersions.
\item All local rings of $X$ are strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Assume $X$ is
integral and $n = \dim_\delta(X)$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$ be a nonzero global section.
Then
$$
\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) = [Z(s)]_{n - 1}
$$
in $Z_{n - 1}(X)$ and
$$
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [X] = [Z(s)]_{n - 1}
$$
in $\mathrm{CH}_{n - 1}(X)$.

\label{lemma-compute-c1}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Assume $X$ is
integral and $n = \dim_\delta(X)$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$ be a nonzero global section.
Then
$$
\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) = [Z(s)]_{n - 1}
$$
in $Z_{n - 1}(X)$ and
$$
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [X] = [Z(s)]_{n - 1}
$$
in $\CH_{n - 1}(X)$.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume that $Y \to S$ is syntomic, $X \to S$ smooth, and
$i$ an immersion. Then $i$ is a regular immersion.

source.label: lemma-rainwater
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rainwater}
Let $f : X \to X$ be a surjective continuous selfmap of a Hausdorff
topological space. If $f$ is not $\text{id}_X$, then there exists a
proper closed subset $E \subset X$ such that $X = E \cup f(E)$.

A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$, an $A$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $J\subset B$ containing $IB$, the divided power envelope $D_{B,\gamma}(J)=(D,\bar J,\bar\gamma)$ is the universal divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra equipped with a ring map $B\to D$ carrying $J$ into $\bar J$: maps $D\to(C,K,\delta)$ of divided power $A$-algebras correspond naturally to $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ carrying $J$ into $K$. The canonical map $D\to B/J$ has kernel $\bar J$. For a divided power ring $(B,I,\gamma)$, $B\langle x_t\rangle$ denotes the divided power polynomial algebra, the free divided power $B$-algebra on elements $x_t$ of the divided power ideal $IB\langle x_t\rangle+B\langle x_t\rangle_+$, with $x_t^{[n]}=\gamma_n(x_t)$.

Given a ring map $A\to B$ and a divided power ideal $(J,\delta)$ on $B$, a divided power $A$-derivation $d:B\to M$ into a $B$-module is additive, vanishes on $A$, satisfies $d(bb')=b\,d(b')+b'\,d(b)$, and $d(\delta_n(x))=\delta_{n-1}(x)d(x)$ for $x\in J$. The universal module representing such derivations is $\Omega_{B/A,\delta}$ with universal map $d_{B/A,\delta}$. The ordinary Kähler differential module $\Omega_{B/A}$ represents all $A$-derivations. For a divided power scheme $(T,\mathcal J,\delta)\to S$, the sheaf $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ represents divided power derivations and is the quotient of $\Omega_{T/S}$ by the divided-power derivative relations.

Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring. Let $A \to B$ be a ring
map and let $IB \subset J \subset B$ be an ideal. Let
$D_{B, \gamma}(J) = (D, \bar J, \bar \gamma)$ be the divided power envelope.
Then we have
$$
\Omega_{D/A, \bar\gamma} = \Omega_{B/A} \otimes_B D

\label{lemma-Galois-action-quasi-compact-open}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Let $\overline{k}$ be a (possibly infinite) Galois extension of $k$.
Let $V \subset X_{\overline{k}}$ be a quasi-compact open.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a finite subextension $\overline{k}/k'/k$
and a quasi-compact open $V' \subset X_{k'}$ such that
$V = (V')_{\overline{k}}$,
\item there exists an open subgroup $H \subset \text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)$
such that $\sigma(V) = V$ for all $\sigma \in H$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{proposition-unique-base-field}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $a : X \to \Spec(k_1)$ and
$b : X \to \Spec(k_2)$ be morphisms from $X$ to spectra of fields.
Assume $a, b$ are locally of finite type, and
$X$ is reduced, and connected. Then we have
$k_1' = k_2'$, where $k_i' \subset \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is
the integral closure of $k_i$ in $\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$.

A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Let $\varphi : M \to M$ be an endomorphism and $n > 0$
such that $\varphi^n = 0$ and such that $\Ker(\varphi)/\Im(\varphi^{n - 1})$
has finite length as an $R$-module.

$$
e_R(M, \varphi^i, \varphi^{n - i}) = 0
$$
for $i = 0, \ldots, n$.

\label{lemma-powers-period-length-zero}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Let $\varphi : M \to M$ be an endomorphism and $n > 0$
such that $\varphi^n = 0$ and such that $\Ker(\varphi)/\Im(\varphi^{n - 1})$
has finite length as an $R$-module.
Then
$$
e_R(M, \varphi^i, \varphi^{n - i}) = 0
$$
for $i = 0, \ldots, n$.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites.
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $u$ is cocontinuous, and
\item[(b)] $u$ is continuous.
\end{enumerate}
Let $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be the associated morphism of topoi. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item sheafification in the formula $g^{-1} = (u^p\ )^\#$ is
unnecessary, in other words $g^{-1}(\mathcal{G})(U) = \mathcal{G}(u(U))$,
\item $g^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $g_{!} = (u_p\ )^\#$, and
\item $g^{-1}$ commutes with arbitrary limits and colimits.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For u:C→D both continuous and cocontinuous, the associated inverse image on sheaves is precomposition u^p without another sheafification, admits left adjoint g_!=(u_p−)^#, and preserves arbitrary limits and colimits. The two independent continuity assumptions and all three conclusions match.

phase3.reason: Continuity eliminates sheafification of u^pG, giving g^{-1}=u^s. Its left adjoint is sheafified u_p by the cited sheaf adjunction. Consequently g^{-1}, as both left and right adjoint, preserves all colimits and limits.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$
with residual space $Z_x \subset X$. Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian.
Then $x$ is a closed point of $|X|$ if and only if
the morphism $Z_x \to X$ is a closed immersion.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned L3233–3240 assumes X LOCALLY NOETHERIAN and residual space Z_x⊆X; it gives the exact equivalence: x is CLOSED in |X| iff Z_x→X is a CLOSED IMMERSION. The proposed iff retains both directions and locally Noetherian restriction.

phase3.reason: A closed immersion has closed image; conversely the reduced closed singleton subspace exists and is locally Noetherian, hence coincides with the residual space.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-residual-space-closed}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$
with residual space $Z_x \subset X$. Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian.
Then $x$ is a closed point of $|X|$ if and only if
the morphism $Z_x \to X$ is a closed immersion.

\label{lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$, $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be complexes
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect.
Then the internal hom $R\SheafHom(\mathcal{E}^\bullet, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$
is represented by the complex $\mathcal{H}^\bullet$ with terms
$$
\mathcal{H}^n =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n = p + q}
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{E}^{-q}, \mathcal{F}^p)
$$
and differential as described in Section \ref{section-hom-complexes}.

source.label: lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and $G : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$
be functors of abelian categories such that $F$ is a right adjoint to $G$.
Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{A}$ and let $M^\bullet$ be
a complex of $\mathcal{B}$. If $RF$ is defined at $K^\bullet$
and $LG$ is defined at $M^\bullet$, then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{B})}(M^\bullet, RF(K^\bullet)) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{A})}(LG(M^\bullet), K^\bullet)
$$
This isomorphism is functorial in both variables on the triangulated
subcategories of $D(\mathcal{A})$ and $D(\mathcal{B})$
where $RF$ and $LG$ are defined.

source.label: lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre-pre
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre-pre}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map of finite presentation. Let $N$ be a
finitely presented $S$-module. Let $\mathfrak q \subset S$ be a prime ideal
lying over $\mathfrak p \subset R$. Set
$\overline{S} = S \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$,
$\overline{\mathfrak q} = \mathfrak q \overline{S}$, and
$\overline{N} = N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Then
we can find a $g \in S$ with
$g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that
$\overline{g} \in \mathfrak r$ for all
$\mathfrak r \in \text{Ass}_{\overline{S}}(\overline{N})$
such that $\mathfrak r \not \subset \overline{\mathfrak q}$.

let $K$ be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from $X$
to $Y$ over $S$. Let $S_1 \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let
$X_1 = S_1 \times_S X$ and $Y_1 = S_1 \times_S Y$. Then the pullback
$K_1 = L(X_1 \times_{S_1} Y_1 \to X \times_S Y)^*K$ is
the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from $X_1$

For arbitrary S1→S, the pullback of both inverse kernels and the two **diagonal convolution identities** gives a relative equivalence on X1,Y1; flatness of S1→S is not assumed.

A *Fourier–Mukai kernel* is the complex $K$. $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ denotes complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ those locally equivalent to bounded complexes of finite-rank locally free sheaves. let $K$ be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from $X$
to $Y$ over $S$. Let $S_1 \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let
$X_1 = S_1 \times_S X$ and $Y_1 = S_1 \times_S Y$. Then the pullback
$K_1 = L(X_1 \times_{S_1} Y_1 \to X \times_S Y)^*K$ is

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For $U\in\mathcal C$, $\mathcal C/U$ is the slice site with induced ring sheaf $\mathcal O_U$; $\mathcal K^\bullet|_U$ denotes termwise restriction to the slice.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
If $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules, then
$\mathcal{K}^\bullet|_U$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules.

phase2.semantic_review_note: K-flatness of a complex of O-modules is preserved after restriction to the slice ringed site C/U. The site, sheaf O_U and restriction meaning are explicitly included.

phase3.reason: For an acyclic complex on C/U, the proof applies exact extension by zero, the extension-by-zero/tensor identity and reflection of exactness, proving the restricted tensor acyclic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restriction-K-flat}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
If $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules, then
$\mathcal{K}^\bullet|_U$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules.

source.label: lemma-property-irreducible-higher-rank-cohomological
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-property-irreducible-higher-rank-cohomological}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Z_0 \subset X$ be an irreducible
closed subset with generic point $\xi$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property
of coherent sheaves on $X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any short exact sequence of coherent sheaves
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to 0
$$
if $\mathcal{F}_i$, $i = 1, 2$ have property $\mathcal{P}$
then so does $\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $\mathcal{P}$ holds for $\mathcal{F}^{\oplus r}$ for
some $r \geq 1$, then it holds for $\mathcal{F}$.
\item For every integral closed subscheme $Z \subset Z_0 \subset X$,
$Z \not = Z_0$ and every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_Z$ we have
$\mathcal{P}$ for $(Z \to X)_*\mathcal{I}$.
\item There exists some coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{G}) = Z_0$,
\item $\mathcal{G}_\xi$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_\xi$, and
\item for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ such that
$\mathcal{J}_\xi = \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}$ there exists a quasi-coherent
subsheaf $\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{J}\mathcal{G}$ with
$\mathcal{G}'_\xi = \mathcal{G}_\xi$ and such that
$\mathcal{P}$ holds for $\mathcal{G}'$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for every coherent sheaf
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ whose support is contained in $Z_0$.

Let $F : \mathcal{C}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume $\mathcal{C}$ has products of pairs of objects and fibre products.
The following three assertions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the diagonal $\Delta : F \to F \times F$ is representable,
\item for every $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$,
and any $\xi \in F(U)$ the map $\xi : h_U \to F$ is representable,
\item for every pair $U, V$ in $\mathcal{C}$
and any $\xi \in F(U)$, $\xi' \in F(V)$ the fibre product
$h_U \times_{\xi, F, \xi'} h_V$ is representable.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ be an
inverse system of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a set
of opens of $X$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every open of $X$ has a covering whose members are elements of
$\mathcal{B}$,
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_n) = 0$ for $p > 0$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$,
\item the inverse system $\mathcal{F}_n(U)$ has vanishing $R^1\lim$
for $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $R\lim \mathcal{F}_n = \lim \mathcal{F}_n$ and we have
$H^p(U, \lim \mathcal{F}_n) = 0$ for $p > 0$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-product-representable-by-spaces}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}_i, \mathcal{Y}_i$ be categories fibred in groupoids over
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, $i = 1, 2$.
Let $f_i : \mathcal{X}_i \to \mathcal{Y}_i$, $i = 1, 2$
be $1$-morphisms representable by algebraic spaces.
Then
$$
f_1 \times f_2 :
\mathcal{X}_1 \times \mathcal{X}_2
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{Y}_1 \times \mathcal{Y}_2
$$
is a $1$-morphism representable by algebraic spaces.

conclusions: Derived local cohomology and derived completion are quasi-inverse between torsion and complete subcategories.
hypotheses: A arbitrary, I finitely generated, derived torsion and completion via augmented Čech.
formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Define the *derived $I$-adic completion* of $K\in D(A)$ by $K^\wedge=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r),K)$, with its natural unit $K\to K^\wedge$. Let $D_{\rm comp}(A,I)$ be the full subcategory of derived $I$-complete complexes, i.e. those for which this unit is an isomorphism (equivalently $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_{f_i},K)=0$ for all $i$). These definitions use the derived Čech model and do not assume $A$ Noetherian or identify derived completion automatically with the naive inverse limit for arbitrary $K$. Then the restrictions
\[
R\Gamma_Z:D_{\rm comp}(A,I)\longrightarrow D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(-)^\wedge:D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\longrightarrow D_{\rm comp}(A,I)
\]
are quasi-inverse exact equivalences of triangulated categories. More precisely $R\Gamma_Z(K^\wedge)\simeq R\Gamma_Z(K)$ and $(R\Gamma_ZK)^\wedge\simeq K^\wedge$ for any $K\in D(A)$. This is the derived torsion-completion equivalence, not classical equality of torsion and complete modules.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Derived local cohomology and derived I-completion restrict to mutually quasi-inverse functors between derived torsion and derived complete subcategories for finitely generated I. The draft correctly uses Čech tensor/Hom rather than naive completion and preserves arbitrary commutative A.

phase3.reason: The torsion–completion equivalence follows directly from the preceding complete-and-local adjunction statement; the original proof explicitly cites that exact lemma.

\label{lemma-check-injective-on-ass}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let
$\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.

at least one of the following happens
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}_x \to \mathcal{G}_x$ is injective, or
\item $x \not \in \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F})$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\varphi$ is injective.

\label{lemma-affine-representable-by-algebraic-spaces}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable by
algebraic spaces. Then $f$ is representable (by schemes) and affine.

\label{lemma-cohomology-of-hocolim}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category having countable
direct sums. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with exact
colimits over $\mathbf{N}$.
Let $H : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{A}$ be a homological functor
commuting with countable direct sums.
Then $H(\text{hocolim} K_n) = \colim H(K_n)$
for any system of objects of $\mathcal{D}$.

conclusions: The blowup of $X$ in $Z$ is the identity morphism of $X$.
hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
The blowup of $X$ in $Z$ is the identity morphism of $X$.

\label{lemma-generic-finite-presentation}
Let $R \subset S$ be an inclusion of domains.

such that $R_f \to S_{fg}$ is of finite presentation.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit}
Let $I$ be a directed set. Let $(S_i, f_{ii'})$ be an inverse system of
schemes over $I$.  If all the schemes $S_i$
are affine, then the limit $S = \lim_i S_i$ exists
in the category of schemes.
In fact $S$ is affine and $S = \Spec(\colim_i R_i)$
with $R_i = \Gamma(S_i, \mathcal{O})$.

source.label: lemma-map-identifies-koszul-and-cech-complexes
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-identifies-koszul-and-cech-complexes}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Assume $\varphi : \mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}'$ is a flat homomorphism
of sheaves of rings. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ be global sections
of $\mathcal{O}$ such that $\mathcal{O}/(f_1, \ldots, f_r) \cong
\mathcal{O}'/(f_1, \ldots, f_r)\mathcal{O}'$.
Then the map of extended alternating {\v C}ech complexes
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{O} \to
\prod_{i_0} \mathcal{O}_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod_{i_0 < i_1} \mathcal{O}_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to \ldots \to
\mathcal{O}_{f_1\ldots f_r} \ar[d] \\
\mathcal{O}' \to
\prod_{i_0} \mathcal{O}'_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod_{i_0 < i_1} \mathcal{O}'_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}} \to \ldots \to
\mathcal{O}'_{f_1\ldots f_r}
}
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-approximation-property}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$f_1, \ldots, f_m \in R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Suppose that $(a_1, \ldots, a_n) \in (R^\wedge)^n$ is a solution
in $R^\wedge$. If $R$ is a henselian G-ring, then for every integer
$N$ there exists a solution $(b_1, \ldots, b_n) \in R^n$ in $R$ such that
$a_i - b_i \in \mathfrak m^NR^\wedge$.

Then \(N\) is exact.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset S$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $b : S' \to S$ be the blowing up of $Z$ in $S$. Let
$g : X \to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $g' : X \times_S S' \to Y \times_S S'$ be the base change
of $g$. Let $\mathcal{F}'$ be the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$
relative to $b$. Then $g'_*\mathcal{F}'$ is the strict transform
of $g_*\mathcal{F}$.

source.label: lemma-strict-transform-affine
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-strict-transform-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset S$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $b : S' \to S$ be the blowing up of $Z$ in $S$. Let
$g : X \to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $g' : X \times_S S' \to Y \times_S S'$ be the base change
of $g$. Let $\mathcal{F}'$ be the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$
relative to $b$. Then $g'_*\mathcal{F}'$ is the strict transform
of $g_*\mathcal{F}$.

Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. formulation.statement:
A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

For a first-order thickening of ringed spaces with ideal $\mathcal I$, an extension of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal K$ on the thickened space means a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O_{X'}$-modules, with $\mathcal I$ annihilating the two end terms. It induces an $\mathcal O_X$-linear action map $c_{\mathcal F'}:\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$, defined by $c_{\mathcal F'}(a\otimes s)=a\tilde s$ for a local lift $\tilde s\in\mathcal F'$ of $s$. Isomorphisms of extensions fix their identified end terms.

Let $i : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (X', \mathcal{O}_{X'})$
be a first order thickening of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules.
Set $\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map.
The set of lifts of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ is, if nonempty, a principal
homogeneous space under
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}')$.

\label{lemma-inf-map-special}
Let $i : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (X', \mathcal{O}_{X'})$
be a first order thickening of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules.
Set $\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map.
The set of lifts of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ is, if nonempty, a principal
homogeneous space under
$\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}')$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-product-presheaves}
Let $X$ be a topological space. The category of presheaves of sets
on $X$ has products (see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-product}).
Moreover, the set of
sections of the product $\mathcal{F} \times \mathcal{G}$
over an open $U$ is the product of the sets of sections of
$\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ over $U$.

\label{lemma-prepare-delta-invariant}
Let $X$ be a reduced Nagata scheme of dimension $1$. Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$
be the normalization. Let $x \in X$ denote a closed point. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ is finite, surjective, and birational,
\item $\mathcal{O}_X \subset \nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu}$ and
$\nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu}/\mathcal{O}_X$ is a direct sum of
skyscraper sheaves with value $\mathcal{Q}_x$ at $x$ which is nonzero
if and only if $x$ is a singular point of $X$,
\item $A' = (\nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu})_x$ is the integral closure
of $A = \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ in its total ring of fractions,
\item $\mathcal{Q}_x = A'/A$ has finite length equal to the
$\delta$-invariant of $X$ at $x$,
\item $A'$ is a semi-local ring which is a finite product of
Dedekind domains,
\item $A^\wedge$ is a reduced Noetherian complete
local ring of dimension $1$,
\item $(A')^\wedge$ is the integral closure of $A^\wedge$
in its total ring of fractions,
\item $(A')^\wedge$ is a finite product of
complete discrete valuation rings, and
\item $A'/A \cong (A')^\wedge/A^\wedge$.
\end{enumerate}

Pinned-source scope: fix the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. A $2$-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_\mathcal Z\mathcal Y$ has objects over a test scheme $T$ given by triples $(x,y,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal X_T$, $y\in\mathcal Y_T$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}g(y)$ in $\mathcal Z_T$. A morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of categories fibred in groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if all such 2-base changes along maps from schemes are stacks associated with algebraic spaces. A surjective smooth atlas of an algebraic stack is a smooth representable 1-morphism $(\Sch/U)_{fppf}\to\mathcal X$ locally surjective on objects in the smooth topology.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $j : \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ be a $1$-morphism of
categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Assume $j$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
Then, if $\mathcal{Y}$ is a stack in groupoids
(resp.\ an algebraic stack), so is $\mathcal{X}$.

\label{lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic}
\begin{reference}
Removing the hypothesis that $j$ is a monomorphism was observed
in an email from Matthew Emerton dates June 15, 2016
\end{reference}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $j : \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ be a $1$-morphism of
categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Assume $j$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
Then, if $\mathcal{Y}$ is a stack in groupoids
(resp.\ an algebraic stack), so is $\mathcal{X}$.

hypotheses: For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$, its cotangent complex $L_{X/Y}$ is the cotangent complex of the morphism of small étale ringed topoi. If $X,Y$ are represented by schemes $X_0,Y_0$, the canonical exact étale-site pullback $\epsilon^*$ from the Zariski-derived category of quasi-coherent complexes on $X_0$ to the small étale site of $X$ transports $L_{X_0/Y_0}$ to $L_{X/Y}$. Étale restrictions are compatible with the construction.
formulation.statement:
For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$, its cotangent complex $L_{X/Y}$ is the cotangent complex of the morphism of small étale ringed topoi. If $X,Y$ are represented by schemes $X_0,Y_0$, the canonical exact étale-site pullback $\epsilon^*$ from the Zariski-derived category of quasi-coherent complexes on $X_0$ to the small étale site of $X$ transports $L_{X_0/Y_0}$ to $L_{X/Y}$. Étale restrictions are compatible with the construction.

Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\Lambda$.
Then
$$
L_{X/\Spec(\Lambda)} = L_{\mathcal{O}_X/\underline{\Lambda}}
$$
where $\underline{\Lambda}$ is the constant sheaf with value
$\Lambda$ on $X_\etale$.

source.label: lemma-vanishing-nr-affines-quasi-separated
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-vanishing-nr-affines-quasi-separated}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme.
Let $X = U_1 \cup \ldots \cup U_n$ be an open covering
with each $U_i$ quasi-compact and separated (for example affine).
Set
$$
d = \max\nolimits_{I \subset \{1, \ldots, n\}}
\left(|I| + t(\bigcap\nolimits_{i \in I} U_i) - 1\right)
$$
where $t(U)$ is the minimal number of affines needed to cover
the scheme $U$. Then $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p \geq d$ and all
quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathcal{F}$.

\label{lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups
which is termwise surjective and induces a quasi-isomorphism on
associated chain complexes. Then $f$ is a trivial Kan fibration of

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-works-flat-extension}
Let $A \to B$ be a flat map of Noetherian rings. Let $I \subset A$ be
an ideal. Let $f : M \to N$ be a homomorphism of finite $A$-modules.
Assume that $c$ works for $f$ in the Artin-Rees lemma. Then $c$ works for
$f \otimes 1 : M \otimes_A B \to N \otimes_A B$ in the Artin-Rees lemma
for the ideal $IB$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-local-structure}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Y \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes
smooth over $S$. For every $y \in Y$ there exist integers
$0 \leq m, n$ and a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[d] &
V \ar[l] \ar[d] \ar[r] &
\mathbf{A}^m_S
\ar[d]^{(a_1, \ldots, a_m) \mapsto (a_1, \ldots, a_m, 0 \ldots, 0)} \\
X &
U \ar[l] \ar[r]^-\pi &
\mathbf{A}^{m + n}_S
}
$$
where $U \subset X$ is open, $V = Y \cap U$,
$\pi$ is \'etale, $V = \pi^{-1}(\mathbf{A}^m_S)$, and $y \in V$.

\label{lemma-internal-hom-restriction}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ be sheaves of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.

commutes with restriction to $U$ for $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.

Let $X$ be a scheme.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is quasi-compact,
\item for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ we have $H^1(X, \mathcal{I}) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-affine-geometrically-connected}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $A$ be a $k$-algebra.
Then $X = \Spec(A)$ is geometrically connected over $k$
if and only if $A$ is geometrically connected over $k$ (see
Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-geometrically-connected}).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
\item there exists an \'etale morphism $f : Y \to X$ of
algebraic spaces over $S$ with $|f| : |Y| \to |X|$ surjective
such that $f^*\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent on $Y$,
\item there exists a scheme $U$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$\varphi : U \to X$ such that $\varphi^*\mathcal{F}$ is a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_U$-module, and
\item for every affine scheme $U$ and \'etale morphism $\varphi : U \to X$ the
restriction $\varphi^*\mathcal{F}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a
filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume that the filtration on each $K^n$
is finite (i.e. for each $n$ there exist indices $a_n,b_n$ such that $F^{a_n}K^n=K^n$ and $F^{b_n}K^n=0$). Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the spectral sequence associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$ is bounded,
\item the filtration on each $H^n(K^\bullet)$ is finite,
\item the spectral sequence associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$ converges
to $H^*(K^\bullet)$,
\item if $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ is a weak Serre subcategory
and for some $r$ we have $E_r^{p, q} \in \mathcal{C}$ for all
$p, q \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $H^n(K^\bullet)$ is in $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $u : N \to M$ be a continuous map of topologized
abelian groups. Assume that $M$ separated and that $N$ is complete, linearly
topologized, and has a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of $0$.
Then exactly one of the following holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u$ is open, or
\item for some open subgroup $N' \subset N$ the image
$u(N')$ is nowhere dense in $M$.
\end{enumerate}
