Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of locally ringed spaces.
Assume that pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined
for $f$ (see
Definition \ref{definition-pullback-meromorphic-sections}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.
There is a canonical pullback map
$f^* : \Gamma(Y, \mathcal{K}_Y(\mathcal{F})) \to
\Gamma(X, \mathcal{K}_X(f^*\mathcal{F}))$
for meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
A regular meromorphic section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}$ pulls back
to a regular meromorphic section $f^*s$ of $f^*\mathcal{L}$.

\label{lemma-meromorphic-sections-pullback}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of locally ringed spaces.
Assume that pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined
for $f$ (see
Definition \ref{definition-pullback-meromorphic-sections}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.
There is a canonical pullback map
$f^* : \Gamma(Y, \mathcal{K}_Y(\mathcal{F})) \to
\Gamma(X, \mathcal{K}_X(f^*\mathcal{F}))$
for meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
A regular meromorphic section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}$ pulls back
to a regular meromorphic section $f^*s$ of $f^*\mathcal{L}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-iso-global-hom}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated finite type morphism of
quasi-separated and quasi-compact schemes. Let $\Lambda$ be a torsion ring.
For every $K \in D(Y_\etale, \Lambda)$ and $L \in D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ the map
(\ref{equation-sheafy-trace}) induces an isomorphism
$$
R\Hom_X(L, Rf^!K) \longrightarrow R\Hom_Y(Rf_!L, K)
$$
of global derived homs.

\begin{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-map}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $\beta : P^\bullet \to L^\bullet$ and
$\alpha : E^\bullet \to L^\bullet$ be
maps of complexes. Let $n \in \mathbf{Z}$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P^\bullet$ is a bounded complex of projectives and
$P^i = 0$ for $i < n$,
\item $H^i(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for $i > n$ and surjective
for $i = n$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a map of complexes $\gamma : P^\bullet \to E^\bullet$
such that $\alpha \circ \gamma$ and $\beta$ are homotopic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a field extension.
Let $x \in X$ be a point, and let $x' \in X_{k'}$ be a point lying over $x$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically reduced at $x$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is geometrically reduced at $x'$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $X$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ if and only if
$X_{k'}$ is geometrically reduced over $k'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits}
Let $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$ be a system over the preordered set $I$.
Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Then
$$
\colim (M_i \otimes N) \cong (\colim M_i)\otimes N.
$$
Moreover, the isomorphism is induced by the homomorphisms
$\mu_i \otimes 1: M_i \otimes N \to M \otimes N$
where $M = \colim_i M_i$ with natural maps $\mu_i : M_i \to M$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclic}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
The full subcategory $\text{Ac}$ of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$
consisting of acyclic modules is a strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$.
The corresponding saturated multiplicative system
(see Derived Categories, Lemma \ref{derived-lemma-operations})
of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$ is the class $\text{Qis}$
of quasi-isomorphisms. In particular, the kernel of the localization
functor
$$
Q : K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to
\text{Qis}^{-1}K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$
is $\text{Ac}$. Moreover, the functor $H^0$ factors through $Q$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-structures}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $(\mathcal{C}, F)$ be a type of algebraic structure.
Denote $\Sh(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$ the category of
sheaves with values in $\mathcal{C}$ on $\mathcal{B}$.
There is an equivalence of categories
$$
\Sh(X, \mathcal{C})
\longrightarrow
\Sh(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})
$$
which assigns to a sheaf on $X$ its restriction to
the members of $\mathcal{B}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-differentials-de-rham-complex-order-1}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$
be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $X$. The differentials
$\text{d} : \Omega^i_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}  \to
\Omega^{i + 1}_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}$
are differential operators of order $1$.

For schemes $U,V$ locally of finite type over $X$, define intersection of Chow classes by $\alpha\cdot\beta:=\Delta^!(\alpha\times\beta)\in\mathrm{CH}_*(U\times_XV)$; for $X$ smooth of pure dimension $d$, $\mathrm{CH}_n(U)\cdot\mathrm{CH}_m(V)\subseteq\mathrm{CH}_{n+m-d}(U\times_XV)$. For $U=V=X$ this defines the intersection product on $\mathrm{CH}_*(X)$.

On a regular closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow T$, $i^!$ is the Gysin pullback of bivariant intersection theory.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-intersect-properly}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an integral scheme smooth over $k$.
Let $Y, Z \subset X$ be integral closed subschemes. Set
$d = \dim(Y) + \dim(Z) - \dim(X)$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim(Y \cap Z) \leq d$, and
\item $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{Z, \xi}$
are Cohen-Macaulay for every $\xi \in Y \cap Z$ with
$\delta(\xi) = d$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $[Y] \cdot [Z] = [Y \cap Z]_d$ in $\CH_d(X)$.

formulation.statement:
For any ringed site (C,O), a **strictly perfect complex** E^bullet is a **bounded** complex whose every term is a direct summand of a finite free O-module (source Definition strictly-perfect at 11716–11724). For U∈C a strictly perfect complex on (C/U,O_U) uses the restricted ring; a finite locally projective module is not being assumed globally free. In the source diagram α:E^bullet→F^bullet is the given map, f:G^bullet→F^bullet the vertical map and a dotted E^bullet→G^bullet is to be constructed **up to homotopy after a covering**. No global lift or strict commutativity is asserted.

conclusions:
Let $A\to B$ be finite type ring map and $\mathfrak p \subset A$ a prime
ideal. Then there exist an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ and a prime
$\mathfrak p' \subset A'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\kappa(\mathfrak p) = \kappa(\mathfrak p')$,
\item
$ B \otimes_A A' = B_1\times \ldots \times B_r \times C$,
\item
$ A'\to B_i$ is finite and there exists a unique prime $q_i\subset B_i$ lying
over $\mathfrak p'$, and
\item all irreducible components of the fibre
$\Spec(C \otimes_{A'} \kappa(\mathfrak p'))$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak p'$
have dimension at least 1.
\end{enumerate}
The étale extension A→A' includes a **chosen prime p' above p with identical residue field**, and the decomposition B⊗_A A'=∏B_i×C is global over A'. Each finite B_i has exactly one prime over p'; C has **no zero-dimensional irreducible component in the fibre** at p', though it can have positive-dimensional fibre components.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

\label{theorem-quasi-finite-etale-locally}
Let $A\to B$ be finite type ring map and $\mathfrak p \subset A$ a prime
ideal. Then there exist an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ and a prime
$\mathfrak p' \subset A'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\kappa(\mathfrak p) = \kappa(\mathfrak p')$,
\item
$ B \otimes_A A' = B_1\times \ldots \times B_r \times C$,
\item
$ A'\to B_i$ is finite and there exists a unique prime $q_i\subset B_i$ lying
over $\mathfrak p'$, and
\item all irreducible components of the fibre
$\Spec(C \otimes_{A'} \kappa(\mathfrak p'))$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak p'$
have dimension at least 1.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let
$0 \to K \to L \to M \to 0$ be an admissible short exact sequence
of differential graded $A$-modules. The triangle
\begin{equation}
K \to L \to M \xrightarrow{\delta} K[1]
\end{equation}
where $\delta$ is the connecting arrow represented by $\pi\circ\mathrm d_L\circ s:M\to K[1]$ for graded $A$-module splittings $s:M\to L$ and $\pi:L\to K$ with $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}s$ is, up to canonical
isomorphism in $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$, independent of the choices of such graded splittings.

phase3.reason: For two graded splittings of an admissible short exact sequence, their difference factors through the kernel; comparison of the off-diagonal differentials shows the resulting connecting maps differ by a chain homotopy, by the cited split-cochain calculation.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bound-quotients-free}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \geq 0$. Let $r \geq 1$. Let $P \in \mathbf{Q}[t]$.
There exists an integer $m$ depending on $n$, $r$, and $P$
with the following property: if
$$
0 \to \mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{O}^{\oplus r} \to \mathcal{F} \to 0
$$
is a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves on $\mathbf{P}^n_k$
and $\mathcal{F}$ has Hilbert polynomial $P$, then
$\mathcal{K}$ is $m$-regular.

\label{lemma-normalization-and-henselization}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$
be the normalization morphism. Then for any point $x \in X$
the base change
$$
X^\nu \times_X \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^h) \to \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^h),
\quad\text{resp.}\quad
X^\nu \times_X \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^{sh}) \to \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^{sh})
$$
is the normalization of $\Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^h)$,
resp.\ $\Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^{sh})$.

A complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules is K-flat when $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ (sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')$, $f^*$ is the ordinary module pullback $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O')\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The source names the result `derived-base-change` but the claim is the **existence and computation of derived pullback** (not a cartesian base-change isomorphism).

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. There exists an exact functor
$$
Lf^* : D(\mathcal{O}') \longrightarrow D(\mathcal{O})
$$
of triangulated categories so that
$Lf^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet = f^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ for any
K-flat complex $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ with flat terms and
in particular for any bounded above complex of flat $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.

phase3.reason: The proof applies the existence criterion for left-derived functors to K-flat flat-term resolutions and checks that pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms between these using exact inverse image and K-flat tensor invariance.

$$

\label{lemma-immersion-group-schemes-closed-over-field}
Let $i : G' \to G$ be an immersion of group schemes over a field $k$.
Then $i$ is a closed immersion, i.e., $i(G')$ is a closed subgroup scheme
of $G$.

formulation.statement:
A complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of modules is K-injective if $\mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet[n])=0$ for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ and every integer $n$; such complexes compute unbounded right derived functors. A flat morphism of ringed topoi is assumed because its module pullback functor is exact, making the right adjoint $f_*$ preserve K-injectivity in this case. This flatness is candidate-local, not a chapter hypothesis.

(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a flat morphism
of ringed topoi. If $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$ is a K-injective
complex of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules, then
$f_*\mathcal{I}^\bullet$ is K-injective
as a complex of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-modules.

\label{lemma-norm-invertible}
Let $\pi : X \to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes. If there exists
a norm of degree $d$ for $\pi$, then there exists a homomorphism of
abelian groups
$$
\text{Norm}_\pi : \Pic(X) \to \Pic(Y)
$$
such that $\text{Norm}_\pi(\pi^*\mathcal{N}) \cong \mathcal{N}^{\otimes d}$
for all invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules $\mathcal{N}$.

\label{lemma-fibre-product-filtered}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : B \to A$ and $g : C \to A$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a fibre product
$$
\xymatrix{
B \times_A C \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & B \ar[d]^f \\
C \ar[r]^g & A
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.

\label{lemma-change-base-scheme}
Suppose given a big site $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $g : S \to S'$ be morphism of $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $j : (\Sch/S)_{fppf} \to (\Sch/S')_{fppf}$ be
the corresponding localization functor.
Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for a scheme $T'$ over $S'$ we have
$j_!F(T'/S') =
\coprod\nolimits_{\varphi : T' \to S} F(T' \xrightarrow{\varphi} S),$
\item if $F$ is representable by a scheme
$X \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$,
then $j_!F$ is representable by $j(X)$ which is
$X$ viewed as a scheme over $S'$, and
\item if $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$, then $j_!F$ is an algebraic
space over $S'$, and if $F = U/R$ is a presentation, then
$j_!F = j(U)/j(R)$ is a presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Let $F'$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S')_{fppf}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(4)] for a scheme $T$ over $S$ we have $j^{-1}F'(T/S) = F'(T/S')$,
\item[(5)] if $F'$ is representable by a scheme
$X' \in \Ob((\Sch/S')_{fppf})$, then
$j^{-1}F'$ is representable, namely by $X'_S = S \times_{S'} X'$, and
\item[(6)] if $F'$ is an algebraic space, then
$j^{-1}F'$ is an algebraic space, and if $F' = U'/R'$ is a presentation,
then $j^{-1}F' = U'_S/R'_S$ is a presentation.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-two-points}
Let $X$ be a spectral space. Let $x, y \in X$. Then either there exists
a third point specializing to both $x$ and $y$, or there exist disjoint
open neighbourhoods containing $x$ and $y$.

\label{lemma-unramified-quasi-finite}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
If $f$ is unramified at $x$ then $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$.
In particular, an unramified morphism is locally quasi-finite.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-slice-smooth-once-separable-residue-field-extension}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point with image $s \in S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is smooth at $x$,
\item the residue field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$
is separable, and
\item $x$ is not a generic point of $X_s$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an affine open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
and an effective Cartier divisor $D \subset U$ containing $x$ such that
$D \to S$ is smooth.

formulation.statement:
Let $(A, I)$ be a Zariski pair. Let $A \to B$ be a finite ring map.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B/IB = B_1 \times B_2$ is a product of $A/I$-algebras
\item $A/I \to B_1/IB_1$ is surjective,
\item $b \in B$ maps to $(1, 0)$ in the product.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a monic $f \in A[x]$ with $f(b) = 0$ and
$f \bmod I = (x - 1)x^d$ for some $d \geq 1$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a Zariski pair (A,I) and finite A→B with B/IB=B1×B2, A/I→B1/IB1 surjective and b mapping to (1,0), there is a monic f annihilating b with reduction (x−1)x^d. All three conditions and asymmetric exponent form remain.

phase3.reason: An étale lifted idempotent splits the integral algebra; localization and faithful-flat descent yield the polynomial relation with coefficients in I.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unramified-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
unramified (resp.\ G-unramified), for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified) then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).

factorization
$$

of $f|_U$ such that $j$ is a closed immersion and $D \to V$
is smooth of relative dimension $r$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-immersion-into-affine}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$. Let $V \subset S$ be
an affine open neighbourhood of $s$. If $f$ is locally of
finite type and
$$
r =
\dim_{\kappa(x)} \Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) =
\dim_{\kappa(x)} \Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) =
\dim_{\kappa(x)} T_{X/S, x}
$$
then there exist
\begin{enumerate}
\item an affine open $U \subset X$ with $x \in U$ and $f(U) \subset V$ and a
factorization
$$
U \xrightarrow{j} \mathbf{A}^{r + 1}_V \to V
$$
of $f|_U$ such that $j$ is an immersion, or
\item an affine open $U \subset X$ with $x \in U$ and $f(U) \subset V$ and a
factorization
$$
U \xrightarrow{j} D \to V
$$
of $f|_U$ such that $j$ is a closed immersion and $D \to V$
is smooth of relative dimension $r$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $R$ be a ring and let $T \subset \Spec(R)$
be constructible. Then there exists a ring map $R \to S$ of
finite presentation such that $T$ is the image of
$\Spec(S)$ in $\Spec(R)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-separated-presheaf-into-sheaf}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
A presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is separated (see
Definition \ref{definition-separated}) if and only if
the canonical map $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}^\#$ is injective.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-admissible-ses}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $0 \to K \to L \to M \to 0$ be an admissible short exact sequence
of differential graded $A$-modules. Let $s : M \to L$ and $\pi : L \to K$
be splittings such that $\Ker(\pi) = \Im(s)$.
Then we obtain a morphism
$$
\delta = \pi \circ \text{d}_L \circ s : M \to K[1]
$$
of $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ which induces the boundary maps
in the long exact sequence of cohomology (\ref{equation-les}).

\label{lemma-m-regular-globally-generated}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \geq 0$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $\mathbf{P}^n_k$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is $m$-regular, then $\mathcal{F}(m)$ is
globally generated.

For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let
$\mathcal{J}, \mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{O}_Y$
be quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism which is an isomorphism
over $V = Y \setminus V(\mathcal{K})$.
Set $\mathcal{I} = f^{-1}\mathcal{J} \mathcal{O}_X$.
Let $(\mathcal{G}_n)$ be an object of $\textit{Coh}(Y, \mathcal{J})$,
let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module, and let
$\beta : (f^*\mathcal{G}_n)  \to \mathcal{F}^\wedge$ be an isomorphism in
$\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$. Then there exists a map
$$
\alpha :
(\mathcal{G}_n)
\longrightarrow
(f_*\mathcal{F})^\wedge
$$
in $\textit{Coh}(Y, \mathcal{J})$ whose kernel and cokernel
are annihilated by a power of $\mathcal{K}$.

source.label: lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull}
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let
$\mathcal{J}, \mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{O}_Y$
be quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism which is an isomorphism
over $V = Y \setminus V(\mathcal{K})$.
Set $\mathcal{I} = f^{-1}\mathcal{J} \mathcal{O}_X$.
Let $(\mathcal{G}_n)$ be an object of $\textit{Coh}(Y, \mathcal{J})$,
let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module, and let
$\beta : (f^*\mathcal{G}_n)  \to \mathcal{F}^\wedge$ be an isomorphism in
$\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$. Then there exists a map
$$
\alpha :
(\mathcal{G}_n)
\longrightarrow
(f_*\mathcal{F})^\wedge
$$
in $\textit{Coh}(Y, \mathcal{J})$ whose kernel and cokernel
are annihilated by a power of $\mathcal{K}$.

formulation.statement:
Let $A' \to A$ be a surjection of rings with nilpotent kernel.
Let $A' \to P'$ be a flat ring map.
Set $P = P' \otimes_{A'} A$.
Let $M$ be an $A$-flat $P$-module.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there is an $A'$-flat $P'$-module $M'$ with
$M' \otimes_{P'} P = M$, and
\item there is an object $K' \in D^-(P')$ with
$K' \otimes_{P'}^\mathbf{L} P = M$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For nilpotent A'↠A, flat A'→P', and A-flat P-module M, the existence of an A'-flat module lift is equivalent to existence of a bounded-above derived P'-lift K' with derived reduction M. Both directions and flatness survive.

phase3.reason: The derived-flat lifting criterion is proved by comparison of derived tensors and nilpotent Nakayama, followed by Tor vanishing and the flatness criterion.

source.label: lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived}
Let $A' \to A$ be a surjection of rings with nilpotent kernel.
Let $A' \to P'$ be a flat ring map.
Set $P = P' \otimes_{A'} A$.
Let $M$ be an $A$-flat $P$-module.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there is an $A'$-flat $P'$-module $M'$ with
$M' \otimes_{P'} P = M$, and
\item there is an object $K' \in D^-(P')$ with
$K' \otimes_{P'}^\mathbf{L} P = M$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is locally of finite type.
\item For all affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is of finite type.
\item There exist an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is locally of finite type.
\item There exist an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
of finite type, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is locally of finite type then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally of finite type.

\label{lemma-product-henselian-pairs}
Let $J$ be a set and let $\{ (A_j, I_j)\}_{j \in J}$ be a collection
of pairs. Then $(\prod_{j \in J} A_j, \prod_{j\in J} I_j)$ is Henselian
if and only if so is each $(A_j, I_j)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-CM-dimension}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes
which is locally of finite type and Cohen-Macaulay.
For every point $x$ in $X$ with image $y$ in $Y$,
$$
\dim_x(X) = \dim_y(Y) + \dim_x(X_y),
$$
where $X_y$ denotes the fiber over $y$.

conclusions: The original module is finite type.
hypotheses: Open, surjective, flat morphism of locally ringed spaces; pullback of the module is finite type.
formulation.statement: Let $f:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a morphism of locally ringed spaces and let $\mathcal F$ be any $\mathcal O_Y$-module. Suppose the underlying continuous map $f$ is open and surjective, $f$ is flat (every induced map $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat), and $f^*\mathcal F$ is locally finitely generated. Then $\mathcal F$ is locally finitely generated on $Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-projective-Noetherian-pic-effective-Cartier}
\begin{slogan}
On a projective scheme, every line bundle has a regular meromorphic section.
\end{slogan}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme which has an ample invertible sheaf.
Then every invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module is isomorphic to
$$
\mathcal{O}_X(D - D') =
\mathcal{O}_X(D) \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{O}_X(D')^{\otimes -1}
$$
for some effective Cartier divisors $D, D'$ in $X$. Moreover, given a
finite subset $E \subset X$ we may choose $D, D'$ such that
$E \cap D = \emptyset$ and $E \cap D' = \emptyset$. If
$X$ is quasi-affine, then we may choose $D' = \emptyset$.

phase3.reason: Both directions are covered using stalkwise tensor exactness and exact skyscraper sheaves to test stalk flatness.

source.label: lemma-flat-stalks-flat
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-stalks-flat}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
An $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ is flat
if and only if the stalk $\mathcal{F}_x$ is a flat
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module for all $x \in X$.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.

Let $x \in X$ with $s = f(x)$.

dimension $0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-morphism-topoi}
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
be a morphism of topoi. Let $q : \Sh(pt) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be a point. Then $p = f \circ q$ is a point of the topos
$\Sh(\mathcal{C})$ and we have
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.

source.label: lemma-image-irreducible
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-image-irreducible}
Let $K/k$ be an extension of fields.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
For every irreducible component $\overline{T} \subset X_K$
the image of $\overline{T}$ in $X$ is an irreducible component in $X$.
This defines a canonical map
$$
\text{IrredComp}(X_K)
\longrightarrow
\text{IrredComp}(X)
$$
which is surjective.

\label{lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
For any complex $\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
there exists a commutative diagram of complexes of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{K}_1^\bullet \ar[d] \ar[r] &
\mathcal{K}_2^\bullet \ar[d] \ar[r] & \ldots \\
\tau_{\leq 1}\mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[r] &
\tau_{\leq 2}\mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
with the following properties: (1) the vertical arrows are quasi-isomorphisms
and termwise surjective,
(2) each $\mathcal{K}_n^\bullet$ is a bounded above complex whose terms
are direct sums of $\mathcal{O}$-modules of the form $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$, and
(3) the maps $\mathcal{K}_n^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_{n + 1}^\bullet$ are
termwise split injections whose cokernels are direct sums of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules of the form $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$. Moreover, the map
$\colim \mathcal{K}_n^\bullet \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
For any complex $\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
there exists a commutative diagram of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{K}_1^\bullet \ar[d] \ar[r] &
\mathcal{K}_2^\bullet \ar[d] \ar[r] & \ldots \\
\tau_{\leq 1}\mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[r] &
\tau_{\leq 2}\mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
with the following properties: (1) the vertical arrows are quasi-isomorphisms
and termwise surjective,
(2) each $\mathcal{K}_n^\bullet$ is a bounded above complex whose terms
are direct sums of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of the form
$j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$, and
(3) the maps $\mathcal{K}_n^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_{n + 1}^\bullet$ are
termwise split injections whose cokernels are direct sums of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of the form $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$. Moreover, the map
$\colim \mathcal{K}_n^\bullet \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let
$\eta \in X$ be a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$
whose stalk $\mathcal{F}_{\overline{\eta}}$ is zero.
Then $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$ is a filtered colimit of
constructible abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained
in a closed subscheme not containing $\eta$.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathcal{F}$ a sheaf
of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$ whose stalk
$\mathcal{F}_{\overline{\eta}}$ is zero. Then
$\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$
is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained in a closed subscheme
not containing $\eta$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: On the small étale site $X_{\acute et}$ of a **qcqs scheme**, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* when its restriction to a finite constructible partition is **finite locally constant**; for modules over a **Noetherian** ring $\Lambda$, constructible means *finite type* locally constant on every stratum. For an étale object $j_U:U\to X$, $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$ is the representable sheaf, and $j_{U!}\underline M$ is **extension by zero** of the constant abelian or $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U$, left adjoint to $j_U^{-1}$. A *torsion abelian sheaf* has torsion stalks at every geometric point. A *filtered colimit* of sheaves is taken in the sheaf category (sheafification of the sectionwise colimit). A constructible sheaf is *finitely presented/compact for filtered colimits* if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\operatorname*{colim}_i\mathcal G_i)\cong\operatorname*{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ for every filtered system. *Essentially constant* for an ind-object means isomorphic in its ind-category to a constant ind-object. For a directed inverse system with affine transitions, its category-colimit means objects and morphisms descend from sufficiently large finite stages, **up to category equivalence**.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let
$\eta \in X$ be a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$.

\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$

Then $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$ is a filtered colimit of
constructible abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained
in a closed subscheme not containing $\eta$.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathcal{F}$ a sheaf
of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$ whose stalk
$\mathcal{F}_{\overline{\eta}}$ is zero. Then
$\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$
is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained in a closed subscheme
not containing $\eta$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A $k$-linear *cohomological functor* $H:\mathcal T^{op}\to\mathrm{Vect}_k$ is contravariant and yields a long exact sequence under every shifted distinguished triangle. *Homological* means the analogous covariant long exact property. An object $C$ is *compact* if maps from $C$ commute with arbitrary small direct sums; a triangulated category is *compactly generated* if a set of compact objects detects zero objects.

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category. Let
$\mathcal{D}' \subset \mathcal{D}$ be a full triangulated subcategory. Let
$X \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$. The category of arrows $E \to X$ with
$E \in \Ob(\mathcal{D}')$ is filtered.

**Scope and interpretation:** The objects are arrows E→X with E in the full triangulated subcategory, and arrows are commutative triangles over X; filtered means nonempty, common successors, and eventual equalizers of any parallel pair.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For any triangulated D and full triangulated D′, the overcategory of E→X with E in D′ is filtered. The proposal does not impose compactness despite the lemma's label and retains arbitrary X.

phase3.reason: The undercategory is nonempty, filtered under finite direct sums and equalizes parallel arrows by the mapping-cone triangle and TR3.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-union-artinian}
Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $E$ be an injective hull of $\kappa$ over $R$.
Let $E_n$ be an injective hull of $\kappa$ over $R/\mathfrak m^n$.
Then $E = \bigcup E_n$ and $E_n = E[\mathfrak m^n]$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map of finite presentation.
Let $N$ be a finitely presented $S$-module
which is flat as an $R$-module. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak p \subset R$.
Then
$$
\mathfrak q \in \text{WeakAss}_S(M \otimes_R N)
\Leftrightarrow
\Big(
\mathfrak p \in \text{WeakAss}_R(M)
\text{ and }
\overline{\mathfrak q} \in \text{Ass}_{\overline{S}}(\overline{N})
\Big)
$$
Here $\overline{S} = S \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$,
$\overline{\mathfrak q} = \mathfrak q \overline{S}$, and
$\overline{N} = N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

\label{lemma-characterize-integral}
Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $s_1, \ldots, s_n$
be a finite set of elements of $S$.
In this case $s_i$ is integral over $R$ for all $i = 1, \ldots, n$
if and only if
there exists an $R$-subalgebra $S' \subset S$ finite over $R$
containing all of the $s_i$.

Then $\mathcal{J}$ is regular
(resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) if and only if
for every $x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J})$ there exists
an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$, $U = \Spec(A)$
such that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and such that $I$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Then $\mathcal{J}$ is regular
(resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) if and only if
for every $x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J})$ there exists
an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$, $U = \Spec(A)$
such that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and such that $I$
is generated by a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular,
quasi-regular) sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in A$.

A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

For a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth curves over $k$, the following are equivalent: the function-field extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable, the map of invertible differential sheaves $df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$ is generically nonzero, and $f$ is étale on a dense open subscheme of $X$. Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $X$ be a smooth proper
curve over $k$. Let $(\mathcal{L}, V)$ be a $\mathfrak g^r_d$ with $r \geq 1$.
Then one of the following two is true
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a $\mathfrak g^1_d$ whose corresponding morphism
$X \to \mathbf{P}^1_k$ (obtained from the two-dimensional subspace of sections as in the linear-series construction above)
is generically \'etale (equivalently its function field extension is finite separable), or
\item there exists a $\mathfrak g^r_{d'}$ on $X^{(p)}$ where
$d' \leq d/p$.
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: For pairs of independent sections either their ratio yields a generically étale pencil, or every ratio lies in k(X^(p)); the associated projective morphism then factors through relative Frobenius, and pullback of the descended line bundle gives d>=p·d'. The source appears to contain a P^1/P^r notation mismatch at line 2737, but its argument is discernible.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-zero-directed-limit}
Let $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$ be a directed system.
Let $M = \colim M_i$ with $\mu_i : M_i \to M$.
Then, $\mu_i(x_i) = 0$ for $x_i \in M_i$ if and only if
there exists $j \geq i$ such that $\mu_{ij}(x_i) = 0$.

For U in C and a surjection p:G→F of O_U-modules, the arrow E→F is given, while a lift E→G is required only after restricting to a covering of U.

$$

& \mathcal{G} \ar[u]_p
}

with $\mathcal{E}$ a direct summand of a finite free
$\mathcal{O}_U$-module and $p$ surjective, then there exists a
covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that a dotted arrow
making the diagram commute exists over each $U_i$.

\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_1) \to
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_2)
$$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-pullback-presheaves
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-presheaves}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map.
There exists a functor
$f_p : \textit{PSh}(Y) \to \textit{PSh}(X)$
which is left adjoint to $f_*$. For a presheaf
$\mathcal{G}$ it is determined by the rule
$$
f_p\mathcal{G}(U) = \colim_{f(U) \subset V} \mathcal{G}(V)
$$
where the colimit is over the collection of open neighbourhoods
$V$ of $f(U)$ in $Y$. The colimits are over
directed partially ordered sets.
(The restriction mappings of $f_p\mathcal{G}$ are explained in the proof.)

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-over-U-trivial}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $K$
be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a set of opens of $X$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every open of $X$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item $H^p(U, H^q(K)) = 0$ for all $p > 0$, $q \in \mathbf{Z}$, and
$U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^q(U, K) = H^0(U, H^q(K))$ for $q \in \mathbf{Z}$
and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

formulation.statement:
Fix a ring $R$, integers $m\geq0$ and $n\geq1$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n]=\mathbf A^{m+n}_S$, and let $i:Z=\mathbf A^m_S\hookrightarrow X$ be defined by $(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$. Let $b:L=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(X)\to X$ be the blow-up, $P=Z\times_S\mathbf P^{n-1}_S$, and $p:P\to Z$ the projection. Identify the exceptional divisor $E\subset L$ with $P$ via its zero-section embedding into the natural line bundle $L\to P$.

If $\mathcal E$ is any locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module and $0\leq j\leq n-1$, the canonical map
$$\mathcal E\longrightarrow Rb_*\bigl(b^*\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_L(jE)\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L2782–2793 is in that fixed affine blowup situation and assumes any locally FREE sheaf E on X, with twist iE satisfying 0≤i≤n−1. It asserts E→Rb_*(b^*E⊗O_L(iE)) is an isomorphism in D(O_X); the proposal preserves the upper bound and SIGN of exceptional divisor twist (positive iE).

phase3.reason: The projection formula reduces the claim to O_X; codimension at least two gives unchanged global functions on the blow-up twists, and the description pi_*O_L(iE)=⊕_{k>=-i}O_P(k), with 0<=i<=n−1, together with projective-space cohomology eliminates all positive higher cohomology. The n=1 blow-up is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-blowup-twist-same-cohomology}
Let $E = 0(P)$ be the exceptional divisor of the blowing up $b$.
For any locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{E}$ and
$0 \leq i \leq n - 1$ the map
$$
\mathcal{E}
\longrightarrow
Rb_*(b^*\mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_L} \mathcal{O}_L(iE))
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-abelian-opposite}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category.
The additions on sets of morphisms make
$\mathcal{A}^{opp}$ into a preadditive category.
Furthermore, $\mathcal{A}$ is additive if and only if $\mathcal{A}^{opp}$
is additive, and
$\mathcal{A}$ is abelian if and only if $\mathcal{A}^{opp}$ is abelian.

formulation.statement:
For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for the unbounded derived category of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology on $T$, and let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$. Its unit and counit are $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_fRf_*$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes $X'=X\times_Y Y'\xrightarrow{g'}X$ above $g:Y'\to Y$ and with vertical maps $f':X'\to Y'$ and $f:X\to Y$. Assume the pair $(f,g)$ is Tor-independent, so that the standard derived base-change map $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*L(g')^*$ is an isomorphism. Let $a_f,a_{f'}$ be the respective right adjoints. The *duality base-change transformation* is $\alpha:L(g')^*a_f\to a_{f'}Lg^*$, constructed by adjunction from $\beta$ using its mate $Rg'_*a_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_fRg_*$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the square
\[
\begin{matrix}
L(g')^*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))&\xrightarrow{L(g')^*(\mu_{f,K})}&L(g')^*a_f(K)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\alpha_K\\
L(f')^*Lg^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_{f'}(\mathcal O_{Y'})&\xrightarrow{\mu_{f',Lg^*K}}&a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\end{matrix}
\]
commutes, where the left vertical map uses derived-pullback associativity and $\alpha_{\mathcal O_Y}:L(g')^*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_{f'}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. All tensors in each row are over the relevant source scheme.

The final statement reconstructs their domains, codomains and orientation without incorrectly asserting any μ itself is an isomorphism.

are tor independent. Let $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$. The diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
L(g')^*(Lf^*K \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} a(\mathcal{O}_Y))
\ar[r] \ar[d] & L(g')^*a(K) \ar[d] \\
L(f')^*Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X'}}^\mathbf{L} a'(\mathcal{O}_{Y'})
\ar[r] & a'(Lg^*K)
}
$$
commutes where the horizontal arrows are the maps
(\ref{equation-compare-with-pullback}) for $K$ and $Lg^*K$
and the vertical maps are constructed using
Cohomology, Remark \ref{cohomology-remark-base-change} and

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-regular}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is regular.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Noetherian and regular.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Noetherian and regular.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is regular.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is regular then every open subscheme is regular.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is quasi-compact,

\end{enumerate}
Then $X$ is affine.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ses-split}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$
be a short exact sequence.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Given a morphism $s : C \to B$ right inverse to
$B \to C$, there exists a unique $\pi : B \to A$
such that $(s, \pi)$ splits the short exact sequence
as in Definition \ref{definition-ses-split}.
\item Given a morphism $\pi : B \to A$ left inverse to
$A \to B$, there exists a unique $s : C \to B$
such that $(s, \pi)$ splits the short exact sequence
as in Definition \ref{definition-ses-split}.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functoriality-differentials}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{O}_2 \ar[r]_\varphi & \mathcal{O}_2' \\
\mathcal{O}_1 \ar[r] \ar[u] & \mathcal{O}'_1 \ar[u]
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. The map
$\mathcal{O}_2 \to \mathcal{O}'_2$ composed with the map
$\text{d} : \mathcal{O}'_2 \to \Omega_{\mathcal{O}'_2/\mathcal{O}'_1}$
is a $\mathcal{O}_1$-derivation. Hence we obtain a canonical map of
$\mathcal{O}_2$-modules
$\Omega_{\mathcal{O}_2/\mathcal{O}_1} \to
\Omega_{\mathcal{O}'_2/\mathcal{O}'_1}$.
It is uniquely characterized by the property that
$\text{d}(f)$ maps to $\text{d}(\varphi(f))$
for any local section $f$ of $\mathcal{O}_2$.
In this way $\Omega_{-/-}$ becomes a functor on the category
of arrows of sheaves of rings.

formulation.statement:
For a topological space $Z$, $\pi_0(Z)$ is its space of connected components. A spectral space is **w-local** when its closed-point subset $Z_0$ is closed and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a continuous map between w-local spaces is **w-local** if it is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. This is terminology, not an additional ambient hypothesis.

Let $X$ be a spectral space, $T$ a profinite topological space, and $Y=X\times_{\pi_0(X)}T$ the fiber product in topological spaces for a continuous map $T\to\pi_0(X)$ and the canonical map $X\to\pi_0(X)$. Then $Y$ is spectral and $T$ identifies with $\pi_0(Y)$. If, in addition, $X$ is w-local, then $Y$ is w-local, $Y\to X$ is a w-local map, and the closed points of $Y$ are exactly the inverse image of the closed points of $X$.

Only when X is also W-LOCAL do Y and Y→X become w-local, with closed-point preimage equality; that additional assumption is kept.

phase3.reason: The fibre product is a closed subspace of the spectral product X×T because π0(X) is profinite Hausdorff; its fibres over T are connected copies of components of X. This identifies π0(Y) with T. For w-local X, closed points pull back bijectively from X_0; their specialization structure verifies w-locality and the w-local projection.

\label{lemma-silly}

set of closed points of $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-triangle-functor-kernel}
Let $F : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}'$ be an exact functor of
pre-triangulated categories. Let $\mathcal{D}''$ be the full subcategory
of $\mathcal{D}$ with objects
$$
\Ob(\mathcal{D}'') =
\{X \in \Ob(\mathcal{D}) \mid F(X) = 0\}
$$
Then $\mathcal{D}''$ is a strictly full saturated pre-triangulated
subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$. If $\mathcal{D}$ is a triangulated category,
then $\mathcal{D}''$ is a triangulated subcategory.

formulation.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. Let $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ be two finite open coverings of the same finite-type $S$-scheme $T$ by $S$-separated open subschemes. If a dualizing complex normalized relative to $(D_S,\mathcal U)$ exists, then one normalized relative to $(D_S,\mathcal V)$ exists, and their underlying complexes are canonically isomorphic compatibly with the local identifications on a common refinement. No separatedness assumption on all of $T$ is required.

\label{lemma-good-dualizing-independence-covering}
In Situation \ref{situation-dualizing} let $X$ be a scheme of finite type
over $S$ and let $\mathcal{U}$, $\mathcal{V}$ be two finite open coverings
of $X$ by schemes separated over $S$.
If there exists a dualizing complex normalized
relative to $\omega_S^\bullet$ and $\mathcal{U}$, then
there exists a dualizing complex normalized relative to
$\omega_S^\bullet$ and $\mathcal{V}$ and these complexes are
canonically isomorphic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-image-nowhere-dense}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $T \subset X$ be a subset.
If $f$ is a homeomorphism of $X$ onto a closed subset of $Y$
and $T$ is nowhere dense in $X$, then also $f(T)$ is nowhere dense in $Y$.

formulation.statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and let $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. For each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the sheafification functor $D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_U)$ sends a complex $D$ of $A$-modules to the associated quasi-coherent complex $\widetilde D$. A dualizing complex over the Noetherian ring $A$ means a bounded coherent complex $D$ of finite injective dimension for which $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$ is an isomorphism. Then the following are equivalent: (1) for *every* affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ there exists a dualizing $A$-complex $D_U$ with $K|_U\simeq\widetilde{D_U}$; (2) there exists *some* affine open cover $\{U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i\}$ of $X$ and dualizing $A_i$-complexes $D_i$ with $K|_{U_i}\simeq\widetilde{D_i}$. Hence being dualizing is an affine-local condition independent of a chosen affine cover.

Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $K$ be an object of
$D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. The following are equivalent

the functor $\widetilde{} : D(A) \to D(\mathcal{O}_U)$.
\item There is an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$, $U_i = \Spec(A_i)$
such that for each $i$ there exists a dualizing complex $\omega_i^\bullet$ for
$A_i$ such that $K|_{U_i}$ is isomorphic to the image of $\omega_i^\bullet$ by
the functor $\widetilde{} : D(A_i) \to D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-relative-weak-assassin-assassin-finite-type}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then $\text{WeakAss}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F}) = \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-into-reduction}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$, $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subspace.
Assume $Y$ is reduced.
A morphism $f : Y \to X$ factors through $Z$ if and only if
$f(|Y|) \subset |Z|$.

\label{lemma-lift-smooth-henselian}
Let $R$ be a ring and $S$ a smooth $R$-algebra. Assume that $A$
is an $R$-algebra and $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair. Then any $R$-algebra
map $S \to A/I$ can be lifted to an $R$-algebra map $S \to A$.

formulation.statement:
For any algebraic space X, the structure sheaf O_X and its quasi-coherent module category refer to the locally ringed small étale site defined earlier in this chapter.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
The category $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item The kernel and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
\item Given a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
if two out of three are quasi-coherent so is the third.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$
is of finite presentation (see
Section \ref{section-properties-modules}),
then the internal hom
$\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is quasi-coherent.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-properties-quasi-coherent
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-properties-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
The category $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item The kernel and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
\item Given a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
if two out of three are quasi-coherent so is the third.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$
is of finite presentation (see
Section \ref{section-properties-modules}),
then the internal hom
$\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is quasi-coherent.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-torsion}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. The torsion sections of $\mathcal{F}$ form
a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule
$\mathcal{F}_{tors} \subset \mathcal{F}$.
The quotient module $\mathcal{F}/\mathcal{F}_{tors}$ is torsion free.

formulation.statement:
For an $\mathcal O_X$-module F, $F^*=\mathcal Hom(F,\mathcal O_X)$ and reflexive means the evaluation map $F\to F^{**}$ is an isomorphism. The rank-one reflexive group law is $[F][G]=[(F\otimes G)^{**}]$. Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a rank 1 coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$. Let
$$
U = \{x \in X \mid s : \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{F}_x
\text{ is an isomorphism}\}
$$ Put $\mathcal F^{[1]}=\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F^{[n+1]}=(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F^{[n]})^{**}$; powers of s map into these sheaves. 
If $s$ is nonzero, then every irreducible component of $X \setminus U$
has codimension $1$ in $X$.

\label{lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $Z_i \subset X$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$ be closed subsets.
If $Z_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$ are proper over $S$, then the same is
true for $Z_1 \cup \ldots \cup Z_n$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-preadditive-zero}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category.
Let $x$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is an initial object,
\item $x$ is a final object, and
\item $\text{id}_x = 0$ in $\Mor_\mathcal{A}(x, x)$.
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore, if such an object $0$ exists, then a morphism
$\alpha : y \to z$ factors through $0$ if and only if $\alpha = 0$.

\label{lemma-check-K-flat-stalks}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$
be a complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Then $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$
is K-flat if and only if for all $x \in X$ the complex
$\mathcal{K}_x^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules is K-flat
(More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-K-flat}).

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $Z \to X$ be a relative $H_1$-regular immersion.
Assume $X \to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists an open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that
$Z \subset U$ and such that $U \to S$ is flat, and
\item $Z \to X$ is a regular immersion and the same remains
true after any base change.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-differential-d1}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $(K, F, d)$ be a filtered
differential object of $\mathcal{A}$. The spectral sequence
$(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ associated to $(K, F, d)$ has
$$
d_1^p :
E_1^p = H(\text{gr}^pK)
\longrightarrow
H(\text{gr}^{p + 1}K) = E_1^{p + 1}
$$
equal to the boundary map in homology associated to the short
exact sequence of differential objects
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^{p + 1}K \to F^pK/F^{p + 2}K \to \text{gr}^pK \to 0.
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-scheme-theoretic-intersection}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z, Y \subset X$ be closed subschemes.
Let $Z \cap Y$ be the scheme theoretic intersection of $Z$ and $Y$.
Then $Z \cap Y \to Z$ and $Z \cap Y \to Y$ are closed immersions
and
$$
\xymatrix{
Z \cap Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z \ar[d] \\
Y \ar[r] & X
}
$$
is a cartesian diagram of schemes, i.e., $Z \cap Y = Z \times_X Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sieves-set}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The collection of sieves on $U$ is a set.
\item Inclusion defines a partial ordering on this set.
\item Unions and intersections of sieves are sieves.
\item
\label{item-sieve-generated}
Given a family of morphisms $\{U_i \to U\}_{i\in I}$
of $\mathcal{C}$ with target $U$
there exists a unique smallest sieve $S$ on $U$ such that
each $U_i \to U$ belongs to $S(U_i)$.
\item The sieve $S = h_U$ is the maximal sieve.
\item The empty subpresheaf is the minimal sieve.
\end{enumerate}

\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-object}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a
filtered complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. There exists a canonical
spectral sequence $(E_r, \text{d}_r)_{r \geq 1}$ of bigraded
$\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$-modules with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r, -r + 1)$ and
$$
E_1^{p, q} = H^{p + q}(X, \text{gr}^p\mathcal{F}^\bullet)
$$
If for every $n$ we have
$$
H^n(X, F^p\mathcal{F}^\bullet) = 0\text{ for }p \gg 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
H^n(X, F^p\mathcal{F}^\bullet) = H^n(X, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)\text{ for }p \ll 0
$$
then the spectral sequence is bounded and converges to
$H^*(X, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ass-weakly-ass}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
If $\mathfrak m_x$ is a finitely generated ideal of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
then
$$
x \in \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F}) \Leftrightarrow
x \in \text{WeakAss}(\mathcal{F}).
$$
In particular, if $X$ is locally Noetherian, then

\label{lemma-perfect-pullback}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$. If $E$ is perfect in
$D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$, then $Lf^*E$ is perfect in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

Let $f : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D_1$, $D_2$ be effective Cartier divisors on $S$.
If the pullbacks of $D_1$ and $D_2$ are defined then the
pullback of $D = D_1 + D_2$ is defined and
$f^*D = f^*D_1 + f^*D_2$.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$.
Then
$$
g_{geom}(X/k) = \sum\nolimits_{C \subset X} g_{geom}(C/k)
$$
where the sum is over irreducible components $C \subset X$ of dimension $1$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bound-geometric-genus}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$.
Then
$$
g_{geom}(X/k) = \sum\nolimits_{C \subset X} g_{geom}(C/k)
$$
where the sum is over irreducible components $C \subset X$ of dimension $1$.

A field extension K/k is separably generated if some transcendence basis B makes K/k(B) separable algebraic. It is separable in the source sense if every finitely generated intermediate extension over k is separably generated. Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension.
There exists a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
K \ar[r] & K' \\
k \ar[u] \ar[r] & k' \ar[u]
}
$$
where $k'/k$, $K'/K$ are finite purely inseparable field
extensions such that $K'/k'$ is a separably generated field extension.

source.label: lemma-affine-representable
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then
$f$ is affine (in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all affine schemes $Z$
and morphisms $Z \to Y$ the scheme $X \times_Y Z$ is affine.

scheme the inverse image of $E$ in $U$ is a locally constructible
subset of $U$.

\label{lemma-equation-codim-1-in-projective-space}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian UFD. Let $Z \subset \mathbf{P}^n_R$ be a
closed subscheme
which has no embedded points such that every irreducible component
of $Z$ has codimension $1$ in $\mathbf{P}^n_R$.
Then the ideal $I(Z) \subset R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$ corresponding
to $Z$ is principal.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-ff}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{S}_1$, $\mathcal{S}_2$ be stacks over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $F : \mathcal{S}_1 \to \mathcal{S}_2$ be a $1$-morphism.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is fully faithful,
\item for every $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and for every
$x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{S}_{1, U})$ the map
$$
F :
\mathit{Mor}_{\mathcal{S}_1}(x, y)
\longrightarrow
\mathit{Mor}_{\mathcal{S}_2}(F(x), F(y))
$$
is an isomorphism of sheaves on $\mathcal{C}/U$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-limited-base-change}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is proper.
\item For any morphism $S' \to S$ which is locally of finite type
the base change $X_{S'} \to S'$ is closed.
\item For every $n \geq 0$ the morphism
$\mathbf{A}^n \times X \to \mathbf{A}^n \times S$ is closed.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism with $Y'$ Noetherian, form $X'=X\times_YY'$ with $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, and assume $X$ and $Y'$ are Tor-independent over $Y$. Then the canonical right-adjoint base-change transformation
\[
L(g')^*a_f(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\]
is an isomorphism for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, where the map is the mate of the usual Tor-independent derived pushforward base change. Tor-independence cannot be omitted merely because the morphisms are perfect.

It concludes the base-change mate L(g')^*a_f(K)→a_{f'}(Lg^*K) is an isomorphism on ALL D_QCoh(Y). The proposed condition retains Tor-independence explicitly despite f being perfect.

In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

An **étale equivalence relation** on a scheme $U/S$ is a subfunctor represented by $R$ with an equivalence-relation map $(s,t):R\to U\times_S U$ whose projections $s,t:R\to U$ are étale. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-group-scheme-over-field-translate-open}
If $(G, m)$ is a group scheme over a field $k$. Let $U \subset G$
open and $T \to G$ a morphism of schemes. Then the image of the
composition $T \times_k U \to G \times_k G \to G$ is open.

The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is Cohen-Macaulay.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay then every open subscheme
is Cohen-Macaulay.

source.label: lemma-locally-Cohen-Macaulay
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-Cohen-Macaulay}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is Cohen-Macaulay.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay then every open subscheme
is Cohen-Macaulay.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restrict-direct-image-open}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Given an open subspace $V \subset Y$, set $U = f^{-1}(V)$ and denote
$g : U \to V$ the induced morphism. Then
$(Rf_*E)|_V = Rg_*(E|_U)$ for $E$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

formulation.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{N}$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $s$, resp.\ $t$ be a nonzero meromorphic section
of $\mathcal{L}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{N}$. Then $st$ is a nonzero
meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{N}$, and
$$
\text{div}_{\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{N}}(st)
=
\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) + \text{div}_\mathcal{N}(t)
$$
in $\text{Div}(X)$. In particular, the Weil divisor class of
$\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{N}$ is the sum
of the Weil divisor classes of $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{N}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-c1-additive}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{N}$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $s$, resp.\ $t$ be a nonzero meromorphic section
of $\mathcal{L}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{N}$. Then $st$ is a nonzero
meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{N}$, and
$$
\text{div}_{\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{N}}(st)
=
\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) + \text{div}_\mathcal{N}(t)
$$
in $\text{Div}(X)$. In particular, the Weil divisor class of
$\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{N}$ is the sum
of the Weil divisor classes of $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{N}$.

conclusions: the structure morphism $X \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth.

formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is locally of finite type over $k$,
\item $\Omega_{X/k}$ is locally free, and
\item $k$ has characteristic zero.
\end{enumerate}
Then the structure morphism $X \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-affine}
Let $T$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be an \'etale covering of $T$.
Then there exists an \'etale covering
$\{U_j \to T\}_{j = 1, \ldots, m}$ which is a refinement
of $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ such that each $U_j$ is an affine
scheme. Moreover, we may choose each $U_j$ to be open affine
in one of the $T_i$.

\label{lemma-preadditive-direct-sum}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category.
Let $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$.
If the product $x \times y$ exists, then so does
the coproduct $x \amalg y$.
If the coproduct $x \amalg y$ exists, then so does
the product $x \times y$. In this case
also $x \amalg y \cong x \times y$.

\label{lemma-group-scheme-field-countable-affine}
Let $G$ be a group scheme over a field.

conclusions: Going down for R\to S is equivalent to lifting generalizations along f.
Going up for R\to S is equivalent to lifting specializations along f.
hypotheses: R\to S is a commutative unital ring map and f:Spec(S)\to Spec(R) is its induced continuous map.
formulation.statement: For a map of spaces f, generalizations lift if for every point x over y and every generalization y-prime of y there is a generalization x-prime of x over y-prime; specializations lift if the analogous statement holds with specialization in both places. In spectra, a specialization corresponds to inclusion of prime ideals. For a unital map of commutative rings $u:R\to S$, going down means: for every chain $\mathfrak p\subset\mathfrak p^\prime$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$, there exists $\mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p$. Going up means: for every such chain and $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, there exists $\mathfrak q^\prime\supset\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$. Let \(R\to S\) be a ring map and \(f:\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)\) its induced continuous map. The ring map satisfies going down if and only if generalizations lift along \(f\); it satisfies going up if and only if specializations lift along \(f\).

phase2.semantic_review_note: Two separate equivalences match direction of prime containment; going down corresponds to lifting generalizations, not specializations.

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
If $F$ is a presheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_F : F \to F \times F$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every scheme $T$ any map $T \to F$ is representable by algebraic
spaces, and
\item for every algebraic space $X$ any map $X \to F$ is representable
by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is a Deligne-Mumford stack and is a stack in setoids,

\item $\mathcal{X}$ is representable by an algebraic space.
\end{enumerate}
