source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-valuation-ring-through-flat-morphism}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $\Spec(A) \to Y$ be a morphism where $A$ is a
valuation ring. If the closed point of $\Spec(A)$ maps to a
point of $|Y|$ in the image of $|X| \to |Y|$, then there exists
a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(A') \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d] \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
where $A \to A'$ is an extension of valuation rings
(More on Algebra, Definition
\ref{more-algebra-definition-extension-valuation-rings}).

Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\psi : \mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r} \to \mathcal{F}$ is a surjection,
then $\Ker(\psi)$ is of finite type.
\item If $\theta : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ is surjective with
$\mathcal{G}$ of finite type, then $\Ker(\theta)$ is of finite type.
\end{enumerate}

be objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Let $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$
be a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules representing $M$. Let
$\mathcal{L}^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
representing $L$. Then
$$
H^0(\Gamma(U, \SheafHom^\bullet(\mathcal{L}^\bullet, \mathcal{I}^\bullet))) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_U)}(L|_U, M|_U)
$$
for all $U \subset X$ open.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For unbounded derived L,M over a ringed space, with M represented by K-injective I• and L by any complex L•, the H^0 of global sections over U of the internal Hom complex equals Hom_{D(O_U)}(L|U,M|U). The final retains the K-injective requirement, arbitrary open U and derived Hom target.

phase3.reason: Identifies degree-zero cohomology of internal Hom sections with derived Hom on an open via K-injective restriction.

formulation.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be sheaves.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective.
Then $a : F \to G$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned bootstrap.tex L378–392 defines flatness, surjectivity and locally finite presentation via every algebraic-space base change. Original L590–597 requires both F,G to be fppf sheaves and a to have all these properties, then concludes surjectivity as a map of sheaves (fppf-local lifting), not global-section surjectivity; the proposal retains that exact distinction.

phase3.reason: An étale scheme cover of the algebraic-space fibre product produces an fppf cover with local lifts, proving epimorphism of sheaves.

\label{lemma-surjective-flat-locally-finite-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be sheaves.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective.
Then $a : F \to G$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

\label{lemma-colimit}
Let $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$ be a system of $R$-modules over the preordered set $I$.
The colimit of the system $(M_i, \mu_{ij})$ is the quotient $R$-module
$(\bigoplus_{i\in I} M_i) /Q$ where $Q$ is the
$R$-submodule generated by all elements
$$
\iota_i(x_i) - \iota_j(\mu_{ij}(x_i))
$$
where $\iota_i : M_i \to \bigoplus_{i\in I} M_i$
is the natural inclusion. We denote the colimit
$M = \colim_i M_i$. We denote
$\pi : \bigoplus_{i\in I} M_i \to M$ the
projection map and
$\phi_i = \pi \circ \iota_i : M_i \to M$.

\label{lemma-injective-map-simplicial-abelian}
\begin{slogan}
The Dold-Kan normalization functor reflects
injectivity, surjectivity, and isomorphy.
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : U \to V$ be a morphism of
simplicial objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
If the induced morphisms $N(f)_i : N(U)_i \to N(V)_i$
are injective for all $i$, then $f_i$ is
injective for all $i$. Same holds with ``injective'' replaced
with ``surjective'', or ``isomorphism''.

\label{lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Set $R = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Let $\mathcal{F}_M$ be the quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules associated to $M$.
If $g : (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) \to (X, \mathcal{O}_X)$
is a morphism of ringed spaces, then
$g^*\mathcal{F}_M$ is the sheaf associated
to the $\Gamma(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$-module
$\Gamma(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) \otimes_R M$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular-local}
Let $R \to \Lambda$ be a ring map with $\Lambda$ Noetherian.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to \Lambda$ is regular,
\item $R_\mathfrak p \to \Lambda_\mathfrak q$ is regular for all
$\mathfrak q \subset \Lambda$ lying over $\mathfrak p \subset R$, and
\item $R_\mathfrak m \to \Lambda_{\mathfrak m'}$ is regular for
all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m' \subset \Lambda$
lying over $\mathfrak m$ in $R$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: $\mathcal{Y}$ is an algebraic stack.
hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.
formulation.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$
be a $1$-morphism of stacks in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is representable by an algebraic space, and
\item $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation,
\end{enumerate}
then $\mathcal{Y}$ is an algebraic stack.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The bootstrap theorem assumes X represented by an algebraic space and F:X→Y representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation. It concludes Y is an algebraic stack. The proposal retains all four map conditions and the distinction between represented source and algebraic target.

phase3.reason: After obtaining a representable diagonal, construct an atlas of the lci Hilbert stack and combine limit preservation, formal smoothness and surjectivity to prove its composite map to Y is smooth surjective.

It is different from the **ringed-site module pullback** $f^*$, which additionally tensors by the target structure sheaf. Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the induced **morphism of small étale topoi** $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute etale})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute etale})$ has inverse image $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$); it sends **sheaves of sets** on $Y_{\acute etale}$ to sheaves on $X_{\acute etale}$, and also induces inverse image of abelian sheaves. It is different from the **ringed-site module pullback** $f^*$, which additionally tensors by the target structure sheaf. For an étale $V\to Y$, let $h_V$ be its representable sheaf and $X\times_Y V$ the fibre product, an object of $X_{\acute etale}$. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale\}$ let $\pi_S:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau\to S_\tau$ be the canonical morphism of the **big** to the **small** site; its inverse image $\pi_S^{-1}$ takes small-site sheaves to big-site sheaves. For $f:T\to S$, $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on the *small* $\tau$-site $T_\tau$, and $\Gamma(T_\tau,-)$ denotes global sections over its final object $T$. An **fpqc cover** means a flat jointly surjective family with the finite affine-source cover condition over each affine open.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
Let $s, t \in \mathcal{F}(S)$. Then there exists an open $W \subset S$
characterized by the following property: A morphism $f : T \to S$
factors through $W$ if and only if $s|_T = t|_T$ (restriction is
pullback by $f_{small}$).

**Precise scope:** Both s,t are **global sections on small S_etale**. Their equality locus is a **unique maximal Zariski open W⊂S**. For an *arbitrary scheme morphism* f:T→S (not assumed étale), the equality is tested after applying the inverse-image functor f_small^{-1}.

\label{lemma-where-sections-are-equal}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on $S_\etale$.
Let $s, t \in \mathcal{F}(S)$. Then there exists an open $W \subset S$
characterized by the following property: A morphism $f : T \to S$
factors through $W$ if and only if $s|_T = t|_T$ (restriction is
pullback by $f_{small}$).

\label{proposition-quotient-by-finitely-generated-torsion-modules}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Let $K$ denote its field of fractions.
Let $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}$ denote the category of finitely generated $A$-modules
and $\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ its Serre subcategory of finitely generated torsion
modules. Then $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}/\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ is canonically equivalent
to the category of finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces.

\label{lemma-torsion-change-rings}
Let $A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism and let $I \subset A$
be a finitely generated ideal. Set $J = IB$. Let $Z = V(I)$ and $Y = V(J)$.
Then
$$
R\Gamma_Z(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B = R\Gamma_Y(K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B)
$$
functorially in $K \in D(A)$.

is a relative dualizing complex for $R \to B$.

source.label: lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit}
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Assume that the underlying topological space
of $X$ has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a basis of quasi-compact open subsets, and
\item the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Then for any directed system $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$
of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and for any quasi-compact open
$U \subset X$ the canonical map
$$
\colim_i H^q(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
H^q(U, \colim_i \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $q \geq 0$.

source.label: lemma-morphisms-right-localization
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphisms-right-localization}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category and let $S$ be a right multiplicative
system of morphisms of $\mathcal{C}$. Given any finite collection
$g_i : X \to Y_i$ of morphisms of $S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$
(indexed by $i$),
we can find an element $s : X' \to X$ of $S$ and a family
of morphisms $f_i : X' \to Y_i$ of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
$g_i$ is the equivalence class of the pair
$(f_i : X' \to Y_i, s : X' \to X)$.

conclusions: $A^p(X \to Y) = A^{p - d}(X \to Z)$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of schemes locally

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-invertible-module}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be
an open and let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
If $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all $x \in X \setminus U$,
then there exists an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{L}'$
with $\mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{L}'|_U$.

Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
For any complex $\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ there exists a $K$-flat complex
$\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ whose terms are flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal{K}^\bullet \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet$
which is termwise surjective.

Locally quasi-finite and quasi-finite properties follow the étale source-target local definitions in §27 and the quasi-compactness condition, respectively.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally quasi-finite,
\item for every morphism $\Spec(k) \to Y$ where $k$ is a field
the space $|X_k|$ is discrete. Here $X_k = \Spec(k) \times_Y X$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For an algebraic-space morphism f locally of finite type, local quasi-finiteness is equivalent to discreteness of the underlying topological space of every geometric fibre X_k over field-valued Y-points. The exact every-field quantifier and iff are preserved.

phase3.reason: If f is locally quasi-finite, scheme étale charts show every field fibre is discrete. Conversely, a failure of local quasi-finiteness gives a specialization in a field fibre of an étale scheme chart, and the transcendence-degree argument shows the two specialized points remain distinct in the algebraic-space fibre, contradicting its discreteness.

\label{lemma-supported-on-support-pre}
Let $X$ be an affine scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a nonzero quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. If
$\text{Supp}(\mathcal{E}) \subset \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$,
then there exists a nonzero map $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{E}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $D \subset X$ be a closed subscheme
corresponding to the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If for every $x \in D$ the ideal
$\mathcal{I}_x \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
can be generated by one element, then $D$ is locally principal.
\item If for every $x \in D$ the ideal
$\mathcal{I}_x \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
can be generated by a single nonzerodivisor, then $D$ is an
effective Cartier divisor.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-hypercovering-F}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Consider the simplicial object $F(K)$ of $\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$,
endowed with its augmentation to the constant simplicial presheaf $h_X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism of presheaves $F(K)_0 \to h_X$ becomes
a surjection after sheafification.
\item The morphism
$$
(d^1_0, d^1_1) :
F(K)_1
\longrightarrow
F(K)_0 \times_{h_X} F(K)_0
$$
becomes a surjection after sheafification.
\item For every $n \geq 1$ the morphism
$$
F(K)_{n + 1} \longrightarrow (\text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n F(K))_{n + 1}
$$
turns into a surjection after sheafification.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Assume there exist a function $p(-) : \mathbf{Z} \to \mathbf{Z}$
and a set $\mathcal{B}$ of opens of $X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every open in $X$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$, and
\item $H^p(U, H^{m - p}(E)) = 0$ for $p > p(m)$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map $E \to R\lim \tau_{\geq -n} E$ of
Derived Categories, Remark
\ref{derived-remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations}
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

formulation.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering. Here fpqc covering means each $g_i$ is flat and, for each affine open $U\subset Y$, there are finitely many affine opens $V_j\subset Y_{i_j}$ with $\bigcup_j g_{i_j}(V_j)=U$. Write $f_i:Y_i\times_Y X\to Y_i$ for the base changes. $f$ is universally closed if and only if every $f_i$ is universally closed.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-big-etale}
Let $\Sch_\etale$ be a big \'etale site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_\etale$.
The functor
$$
u :
(\Sch/T)_\etale
\longrightarrow
(\Sch/S)_\etale,
\quad
V/T \longmapsto V/S
$$
is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint
$$
v :
(\Sch/S)_\etale
\longrightarrow
(\Sch/T)_\etale,
\quad
(U \to S) \longmapsto (U \times_S T \to T).
$$
They induce the same morphism of topoi
$$
f_{big} :
\Sh((\Sch/T)_\etale)
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_\etale)
$$
We have $f_{big}^{-1}(\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
We have $f_{big, *}(\mathcal{F})(U/S) = \mathcal{F}(U \times_S T/T)$.
Also, $f_{big}^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_{big!}$ which commutes with
fibre products and equalizers.

\label{lemma-chow-limit}
Let $K/k$ be an algebraic field extension. Let $X$ be a finite type
scheme over $k$. Then $\CH_i(X_K) = \colim \CH_i(X_{k'})$ where the
colimit is over the subextensions $K/k'/k$ with $k'/k$ finite.

dimension $d$, then $\text{cd}(A, I) < d$.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $C$ be a proper curve over $k$.
Set $\kappa = H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C)$. Then
$$
[\kappa : k]_s \dim_\kappa H^1(C, \mathcal{O}_C) \geq g_{geom}(C/k)
$$

phase3.reason: The constant field kappa is finite over k; separable embeddings kappa→kbar index the geometric components. Flat cohomology base change gives each component the same h^1 dimension over kappa, while normalization can only lower h^1 and sums the geometric genera. Summation yields the separable-degree bound.

\label{lemma-bound-geometric-genus-curve}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $C$ be a proper curve over $k$.
Set $\kappa = H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C)$. Then
$$
[\kappa : k]_s \dim_\kappa H^1(C, \mathcal{O}_C) \geq g_{geom}(C/k)
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-application-H0-pre}
Let $I \subset \mathfrak a$ be ideals of a Noetherian ring $A$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent module on
$U = \Spec(A) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $I$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item if $x \in \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F})$, $x \not \in V(I)$,
$\overline{\{x\}} \cap V(I) \not \subset V(\mathfrak a)$,
and $z \in \overline{\{x\}} \cap V(\mathfrak a)$, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{\overline{\{x\}}, z}) > \text{cd}(A, I) + 1$,
\item one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the restriction of $\mathcal{F}$ to $U \setminus V(I)$ is $(S_1)$
\item the dimension of $V(\mathfrak a)$ is at most $2$\footnote{In
the sense that the difference of the maximal and minimal values
on $V(\mathfrak a)$ of a dimension function on $\Spec(A)$ is at most $2$.}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then we obtain an isomorphism
$$
\colim H^0(V, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
\lim H^0(U, \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F})
$$
where the colimit is over opens $V \subset U$ containing $U \cap V(I)$.

is smooth over $k'$ for all $i$.

\label{lemma-finite-over-finite-module}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Assume $f$ is a finite morphism.
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type
if and only if $f_*\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module of finite
type.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item The support of $\mathcal{F}$ is closed.
\item For a geometric point $\overline{x}$ lying over $x \in |X|$ we have
$$
x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}} \not = 0
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}}
\kappa(\overline{x}) \not = 0.
$$
\item For any morphism of algebraic spaces $f : Y \to X$ the pullback
$f^*\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type as well and we have
$\text{Supp}(f^*\mathcal{F}) = f^{-1}(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-support-finite-type
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-support-finite-type}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item The support of $\mathcal{F}$ is closed.
\item For a geometric point $\overline{x}$ lying over $x \in |X|$ we have
$$
x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}} \not = 0
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}}
\kappa(\overline{x}) \not = 0.
$$
\item For any morphism of algebraic spaces $f : Y \to X$ the pullback
$f^*\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type as well and we have
$\text{Supp}(f^*\mathcal{F}) = f^{-1}(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves-modules}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper smooth morphism of schemes with
geometrically connected fibres of dimension $1$. Let $\Lambda$
be a Noetherian ring. Let $M$ be a finite $\Lambda$-module
annihilated by an integer $n > 0$. Then $R^qf_*\underline{M}$
is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $S$.

formulation.statement:
Let C be a site and Λ a ring; D(C,Λ)=D(Mod(underline Λ)), the derived category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf underline Λ. For a derived Λ-module complex K∈D(Λ), underline K denotes its image in D(C,Λ) by the constant-sheaf derived inverse image. A **locally constant sheaf of finite-type modules** becomes constant with a finitely generated Λ-module on a covering of every site object; when Λ is Noetherian the finite-type condition is stable under the indicated constructions. Here I⊂Λ is an ideal of the **Noetherian** coefficient ring and K∈D^−(C,Λ) is **bounded above**. The hypothesis is local constancy of the cohomology sheaves after derived reduction **mod I**; the conclusion is for all powers **mod I^n**, not a claim of uniform boundedness in n.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $K \in D^-(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$. If the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I}$ are locally constant
sheaves of $\Lambda/I$-modules of finite type, then the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$
are locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda/I^n$-modules of finite type for all
$n \geq 1$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For Noetherian Λ, ideal I, bounded-above K, locally constant finite-type cohomology after derived mod I implies same after derived mod I^n for each n≥1. No mistaken uniform bound or reduction over Λ rather than quotient rings.

phase3.reason: The proof uses the weak Serre stability of locally constant finite-type sheaves, derived tensor triangles for powers of the ideal, and induction via the tensor stability lemma.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-constant-bounded}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $K \in D^-(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$. If the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I}$ are locally constant
sheaves of $\Lambda/I$-modules of finite type, then the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$
are locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda/I^n$-modules of finite type for all
$n \geq 1$.

source.label: lemma-finite-fibre-connected-components
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-fibre-connected-components}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of nonempty topological spaces. Assume
that
(a) $Y$ is connected,
(b) $f$ is open and closed, and
(c) there is a point $y\in Y$ such that the fiber $f^{-1}(y)$ is a finite set.
Then $X$ has at most $|f^{-1}(y)|$ connected components. Hence any connected 
component $T$ of $X$ is open and closed, and $f(T)$ is a nonempty open and 
closed subset of $Y$, which is therefore equal to $Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometrically-normal}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically normal,
\item $X_{k'}$ is a normal scheme for every field extension $k'/k$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is a normal scheme for every finitely generated field
extension $k'/k$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is a normal scheme for every finite purely inseparable
field extension $k'/k$,
\item for every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is geometrically normal (see
Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-geometrically-normal}), and
\item $X_{k^{perf}}$ is a normal scheme.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-completion-henselization-dualizing}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I \subset A$ be an ideal.
Let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing complex.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_A^\bullet \otimes_A A^h$ is a dualizing complex on the
henselization $(A^h, I^h)$ of the pair $(A, I)$,
\item $\omega_A^\bullet \otimes_A A^\wedge$ is a dualizing complex on
the $I$-adic completion $A^\wedge$, and
\item if $A$ is local, then $\omega_A^\bullet \otimes_A A^h$,
resp.\ $\omega_A^\bullet \otimes_A A^{sh}$ is a dualzing complex
on the henselization, resp.\ strict henselization of $A$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be a quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals corresponding to a closed subscheme $Z \subset X$.
Then there is some $n \geq 0$ such that $\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F} = 0$
if and only if $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \subset Z$ (set theoretically).

conclusions: A reduced, locally Noetherian singleton algebraic space $Z$ is regular.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-construct-quasi-inverse}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a fully faithful functor.
Suppose for every $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{B})$ we are given an
object $j(X)$ of $\mathcal{A}$ and an isomorphism $i_X : X \to F(j(X))$.
Then there is a unique functor $j : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$
such that $j$ extends the rule on objects, and the isomorphisms
$i_X$ define an isomorphism of functors
$\text{id}_\mathcal{B} \to F \circ j$. Moreover, $j$ and $F$
are quasi-inverse equivalences of categories.

A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Consider the map
(\ref{equation-c1}) $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the local rings of $X$ are UFDs, and
\item $X$ is normal and $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
In this case $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$ is an isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-internal-hom-locally-kernel-direct-sum}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is finitely presented then the sheaf
$\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$ is
locally a kernel of a map between finite direct sums
of copies of $\mathcal{G}$.
In particular, if $\mathcal{G}$ is coherent then
$\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is coherent too.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-normalization-and-smooth}
Let $X \to Y$ be a smooth morphism of schemes. Assume every quasi-compact
open of $Y$ has finitely many irreducible components. Then the same
is true for $X$ and there is a unique isomorphism $X^\nu = X \times_Y Y^\nu$
over $X$ where $X^\nu$, $Y^\nu$ are the normalizations of $X$, $Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-michael-artin}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $D \subset X$ be a relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$.
If $f$ is flat at all points of $X \setminus D$, then $f$ is flat.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Let $g : V \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces.
Let $Z \subset Y$ be the scheme theoretic image of $g$ and let $Z' \subset X$
be the scheme theoretic image of the base change $V \times_Y X \to X$.
Then $Z' = f^{-1}Z$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-application-directed-colimit}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $U \subset X$ be a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal{F}|_U$
is of finite presentation. Then there exists a map of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ with
(a) $\mathcal{G}$ of finite presentation,
(b) $\varphi$ is surjective, and
(c) $\varphi|_U$ is an isomorphism.

conclusions: Then $f$ is a homeomorphism.
formulation.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ and $Y$ are spectral,
\item $f$ is spectral and bijective, and
\item generalizations (resp.\ specializations) lift along $f$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is a homeomorphism.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Spectral bijective f between spectral spaces with lifting of generalizations or respectively specializations is a homeomorphism; all premises remain.

phase3.reason: A bijective spectral map becomes a constructible-topology homeomorphism; lifting of specialization or generalization upgrades it to an ordinary homeomorphism.

$\mathcal{E}_{k'}/X_{k'}/k'$.

source.label: lemma-fibre-product-tangent-spaces
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibre-product-tangent-spaces}
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$
and $q : \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be $1$-morphisms of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Assume $\mathcal{X}$,
$\mathcal{Y}$, $\mathcal{Z}$ satisfy (RS).
Let $k$ be a field of finite type over $S$ and let $w_0$ be an object of
$\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{X} \times_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z}$ over $k$.
Denote $x_0, y_0, z_0$ the objects of $\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$
you get from $w_0$. Then there is a $6$-term exact sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
0 \ar[r] &
\text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{W}, k, w_0}) \ar[r] &
\text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{X}, k, x_0}) \oplus
\text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{Z}, k, z_0}) \ar[r] &
\text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{Y}, k, y_0}) \ar[lld] \\
 &
T\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{W}, k, w_0} \ar[r] &
T\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{X}, k, x_0} \oplus
T\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{Z}, k, z_0} \ar[r] &
T\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{Y}, k, y_0}
}
$$
of $k$-vector spaces.

For a base scheme $S$, let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ denote **all schemes over $S$** (using the source's size conventions). An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

Given a covering $\{T_i\to T\}$, an *effective descent datum* for quasi-coherent sheaves is a family of quasi-coherent $\mathcal F_i$ on $T_i$ with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:\mathrm{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $T_i\times_TT_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triples, and an isomorphism of this datum with the pullbacks of a single quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$. For a ring map $A\to B$, its *Amitsur cochain complex* $(B/A)_\bullet$ has degree $q$ term $B^{\otimes_A(q+1)}$ and alternating coface differential inserting $1$ in every position.

For a base scheme $S$, let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ denote **all schemes over $S$** (using the source's size conventions). An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

Given a covering $\{T_i\to T\}$, an *effective descent datum* for quasi-coherent sheaves is a family of quasi-coherent $\mathcal F_i$ on $T_i$ with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:\mathrm{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $T_i\times_TT_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triples, and an isomorphism of this datum with the pullbacks of a single quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$. For a ring map $A\to B$, its *Amitsur cochain complex* $(B/A)_\bullet$ has degree $q$ term $B^{\otimes_A(q+1)}$ and alternating coface differential inserting $1$ in every position.

If $A \to B$ is faithfully flat and $M$ is an $A$-module, then the
complex $(B/A)_\bullet \otimes_A M$ is exact in positive degrees, and
$H^0((B/A)_\bullet \otimes_A M) = M$.

**Scope and interpretation:** Tensor the entire Amitsur complex with M over A. Its H^0 is the original A-module M via m↦1⊗m; positive-degree exactness does not require M to be flat.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For all A-modules M under faithfully flat A→B, the Amitsur complex tensored with M has H⁰=M and no higher cohomology; no extra flatness of M is assumed.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-yoneda}
\begin{reference}
Appeared in some form in \cite{Yoneda-homology}. Used by Grothendieck in a
generalized form in \cite{Gr-II}.
\end{reference}
Let $U, V \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Given any morphism of functors $s : h_U \to h_V$
there is a unique morphism $\phi : U \to V$
such that $h(\phi) = s$. In other words the
functor $h$ is fully faithful. More generally,
given any contravariant functor $F$ and any object
$U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have a natural bijection
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(h_U, F) \longrightarrow F(U),
\quad
s \longmapsto s_U(\text{id}_U).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-fibred-setoids-property}
Let $S$ be an object of $\Sch_{fppf}$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}.
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of
categories fibred in setoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $F$, resp.\ $G$ be the presheaf which to $T$ associates
the set of isomorphism classes of objects of
$\mathcal{X}_T$, resp.\ $\mathcal{Y}_T$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be the map of presheaves corresponding to $f$.
Then $a$ has $\mathcal{P}$ if and only if $f$ has $\mathcal{P}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-section-support-in-locally-closed}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a locally closed subscheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$. Given
$U, U' \subset X$ open containing $Z$ as a closed subscheme,
there is a canonical bijection
$$
\{s \in \mathcal{F}(U) \mid \text{Supp}(s) \subset Z\} =
\{s \in \mathcal{F}(U') \mid \text{Supp}(s) \subset Z\}
$$
which is given by restriction if $U' \subset U$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood}
\begin{slogan}
A proper morphism is finite in a neighbourhood of a finite fiber.
\end{slogan}
(For a more general version see
More on Morphisms,
Lemma \ref{more-morphisms-lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood}.)
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $s \in S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is locally Noetherian,
\item $f$ is proper, and
\item $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $V \subset S$ of $s$
such that $f|_{f^{-1}(V)} : f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

\label{lemma-i-upper-shriek}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.
There is a functor\footnote{This is likely nonstandard notation.}
$i^! : \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)$
which is a right adjoint to $i_*$. (Compare
Modules, Lemma \ref{modules-lemma-i-star-right-adjoint}.)

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
We have the following implications:
$i$ is regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

\label{lemma-regular-quasi-regular-immersion}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
We have the following implications:
$i$ is regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_S$-module
of finite presentation. Let $S = Z_{-1} \supset Z_0 \supset Z_1 \supset \ldots$
be the closed subschemes cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$.
Set $S_r = Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r$.
Then $S' = \coprod_{r \geq 0} S_r$ represents the functor
$$
F_{flat} : \Sch/S \longrightarrow \textit{Sets},\quad\quad
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ flat over }T\\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
Moreover, $\mathcal{F}|_{S_r}$ is locally free of rank $r$ and the
morphisms $S_r \to S$ and $S' \to S$ are of finite presentation.
For $T\to S$, $\mathcal F_T$ denotes the pullback to $T$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-presentation-module}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_S$-module
of finite presentation. Let $S = Z_{-1} \supset Z_0 \supset Z_1 \supset \ldots$
be as in Lemma \ref{lemma-locally-free-rank-r-pullback}.
Set $S_r = Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r$.
Then $S' = \coprod_{r \geq 0} S_r$ represents the functor
$$
F_{flat} : \Sch/S \longrightarrow \textit{Sets},\quad\quad
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ flat over }T\\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
Moreover, $\mathcal{F}|_{S_r}$ is locally free of rank $r$ and the
morphisms $S_r \to S$ and $S' \to S$ are of finite presentation.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-enough-finite-type-points}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
For any locally closed subset $T \subset |X|$ we have
$$
T \not = \emptyset
\Rightarrow
T \cap X_{\text{ft-pts}} \not = \emptyset.
$$
In particular, for any closed subset $T \subset |X|$ we
see that $T \cap X_{\text{ft-pts}}$ is dense in $T$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-closure-localize}
Integral closure commutes with localization: If $A \to B$ is a ring
map, and $S \subset A$ is a multiplicative subset, then the integral
closure of $S^{-1}A$ in $S^{-1}B$ is $S^{-1}B'$, where $B' \subset B$
is the integral closure of $A$ in $B$.

The source only assumes i:Z→X is a closed immersion; finite presentation iff its defining quasi-coherent ideal is of finite type.
phase2.proposed_correction: Keep only 'i is a closed immersion' and the ideal-definition in hypotheses; represent finite presentation ⇔ finite-type ideal as two equivalence sides and independently re-review.

phase3.reason: Both finite presentation of a closed immersion and finite generation of its defining ideal are checked after a surjective étale scheme presentation U→X. Their equivalence is the standard scheme closed-immersion finite-presentation theorem.

source.label: lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation}
A closed immersion $i : Z \to X$ is of finite presentation if and only if
the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} = \Ker(\mathcal{O}_X \to i_*\mathcal{O}_Z)$
is of finite type (as an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module).

source.label: lemma-make-spectral-space
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-make-spectral-space}
Let $W$ be a subset of a spectral space $X$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $W$ is an intersection of constructible sets and
closed under generalizations,
\item $W$ is quasi-compact and closed under generalizations,
\item there exists a quasi-compact subset $E \subset X$ such that
$W$ is the set of points specializing to $E$,
\item $W$ is an intersection of quasi-compact open subsets,
\item
\label{item-intersection-quasi-compact-open}
there exists a nonempty set $I$ and quasi-compact opens
$U_i \subset X$, $i \in I$
such that $W = \bigcap U_i$ and for all $i, j \in I$ there exists a
$k \in I$ with $U_k \subset U_i \cap U_j$.
\end{enumerate}
In this case we have (a) $W$ is a spectral space, (b) $W = \lim U_i$
as topological spaces, and (c) for any open $U$ containing $W$
there exists an $i$ with $U_i \subset U$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-set-of-subobjects}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with a generator $U$ and
$X$ an object of $\mathcal{A}$. If $\kappa$ is the cardinality of
$\Mor(U, X)$ then
\begin{enumerate}
\item There does not exist a strictly increasing
(or strictly decreasing) chain of subobjects
of $X$ indexed by a cardinal bigger than $\kappa$.
\item If $\alpha$ is an ordinal of cofinality $> \kappa$
then any increasing (or decreasing) sequence of subobjects
of $X$ indexed by $\alpha$ is eventually constant.
\item The cardinality of the set of subobjects of $X$
is $\leq 2^\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $D \subset X$ be an effective
Cartier divisor. Assume that there exist integral effective Cartier
divisors $D_i \subset X$ such that $D \subset \bigcup D_i$
set theoretically. Then $D = \sum a_i D_i$ for some $a_i \geq 0$.
The existence of the $D_i$ is guaranteed if $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is a UFD for all $x \in D$ or if $X$ is regular.

Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
Let $G:\mathrm{Mod}_{B'}\to\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ send $L'$ to $(L'\otimes_{B'}B,L'\otimes_{B'}A',\mathrm{can})$, with $\mathrm{can}$ the canonical identification after tensoring both components with $A$.
The functor $F:(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{\varphi,M}M'$ is right adjoint to $G$. Moreover $G\circ F$ is canonically isomorphic to the identity on $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$: for every compatible triple, $N'\otimes_{B'}B\cong N$ and $N'\otimes_{B'}A'\cong M'$, compatibly with $\varphi$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-module-over-fibre-product}
In Situation \ref{situation-module-over-fibre-product}
the functor (\ref{equation-functor}) has a right adjoint, namely
the functor
$$
F : (N, M', \varphi) \longmapsto N \times_{\varphi, M} M'
$$
where $M = M'/IM'$. Moreover, the composition of $F$ with
(\ref{equation-functor}) is the identity functor on
$\text{Mod}_B \times_{\text{Mod}_A} \text{Mod}_{A'}$. In other words,
setting $N' = N \times_{\varphi, M} M'$ we have
$N' \otimes_{B'} B = N$ and $N' \otimes_{B'} A' = M'$.

For a morphism $f:T\to U$, a degree-$p$ bivariant class $c\in A^p(T\to U)$ consists of homomorphisms $\mathrm{CH}_n(U')\to\mathrm{CH}_{n-p}(T\times_UU')$ for all $U'\to U$ of locally finite type, compatible with proper pushforwards, flat pullbacks of fixed relative dimension, and Gysin maps for zero schemes of invertible-sheaf sections. \label{lemma-projection-formula}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes smooth
over $k$. Then the Gysin map exists for $f$ and
$f_*(\alpha \cdot f^!\beta) = f_*\alpha \cdot \beta$.

of abelian groups on $X$. There exists a unique structure of an
abelian group on $\mathcal{F}_x$ such that for every
$U \subset X$ open, $x\in U$ the map $\mathcal{F}(U) \to \mathcal{F}_x$
is a group homomorphism. Moreover,
$$
\mathcal{F}_x
=
\colim_{x\in U} \mathcal{F}(U)
$$
holds in the category of abelian groups.

Let $R$ be a ring. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ has property (P) of

For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$
and $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}'$ be homomorphisms of sheaves of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$$
L_{\mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{B}'/\mathcal{A}}
\longrightarrow
L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} \oplus L_{\mathcal{B}'/\mathcal{A}}
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{B}')$.

\label{lemma-finite-type-eventually-proper}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X = \lim X_i$ be a directed limit of
schemes over $S$ with affine transition morphisms. Let $Y \to X$
be a morphism of schemes over $S$.
If $Y \to X$ is proper, $X_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and
$Y$ locally of finite type over $S$, then $Y \to X_i$ is proper
for $i$ large enough.

Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map, and let $R \to R'$
be faithfully flat. Set $A' = R' \otimes_R A$. If all descent data

source.label: lemma-explain-why-pure-direct-sum-finite-modules
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-explain-why-pure-direct-sum-finite-modules}
Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $N$ be an $S$-module.
Assume $N$ is isomorphic as an $R$-module to a direct
sum of finite $R$-modules. Then for any $R$-module $M$ and
for any prime $\mathfrak q \subset S$ which is an associated prime of
$N \otimes_R M$ we have $\mathfrak q + \mathfrak m S \not = S$.

source.label: lemma-wedge-product-ses
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-wedge-product-ses}
Let $X$ be an integral regular scheme of dimension $2$.
Let $i : D \to X$ be the immersion of an effective Cartier divisor.
Let $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}' \to i_*\mathcal{G} \to 0$
be an exact sequence of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}'$ are locally free of rank $r$ on a nonempty
open of $X$,
\item $D$ is an integral scheme,
\item $\mathcal{G}$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_D$-module
of rank $s$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{L} = (\wedge^r\mathcal{F})^{**}$ and
$\mathcal{L}' = (\wedge^r \mathcal{F}')^{**}$
are invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and
$\mathcal{L}' \cong \mathcal{L}(k D)$ for some
$k \in \{0, \ldots, \min(s, r)\}$.

source.label: lemma-map-from-set-lifts
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-from-set-lifts}
Suppose that $T = \colim_{\alpha < \beta} T_\alpha$
is a colimit of sets indexed by ordinals less than a given ordinal $\beta$.
Suppose that $\varphi : S \to T$ is a map of sets.
Then $\varphi$ lifts to a map into $T_\alpha$ for some $\alpha < \beta$
provided that $\beta$ is not a limit of ordinals indexed by $S$,
in other words, if $\beta$ is an ordinal with $\text{cf}(\beta) > |S|$.

Let $U$ be a simplicial set.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The rule
$$
U'_m = \bigcup\nolimits_{\varphi : [m] \to [i], \ i\leq n} \Im(U(\varphi))

$U'_i = U_i$ for $i \leq n$.

all $m > n$.

source.label: lemma-simplicial-set-n-skel-sub
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-simplicial-set-n-skel-sub}
Let $U$ be a simplicial set.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The rule
$$
U'_m = \bigcup\nolimits_{\varphi : [m] \to [i], \ i\leq n} \Im(U(\varphi))
$$
defines a sub simplicial set $U' \subset U$ with
$U'_i = U_i$ for $i \leq n$.
Moreover, all $m$-simplices of $U'$ are degenerate for
all $m > n$.

\label{lemma-RHom-into-K-injective}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $L$ and $M$
be objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$
be a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules representing $M$. Let
$\mathcal{L}^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
representing $L$.
Then
$$
H^0(\Gamma(U, \SheafHom^\bullet(\mathcal{L}^\bullet, \mathcal{I}^\bullet))) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_U)}(L|_U, M|_U)
$$
for all $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Similarly,
$H^0(\Gamma(\mathcal{C},
\SheafHom^\bullet(\mathcal{L}^\bullet, \mathcal{I}^\bullet))) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(L, M)$.

\label{lemma-bourbaki}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$ which is flat over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$.
Then we have
$$
\text{Ass}_X(\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f^*\mathcal{G})
\supset
\bigcup\nolimits_{s \in \text{Ass}_S(\mathcal{G})}
\text{Ass}_{X_s}(\mathcal{F}_s)
$$
and equality holds if $S$ is locally Noetherian (for the notation
$\mathcal{F}_s$ see above).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-presentation-flat-at-point-X}
Let $f : X \to S$ be locally of finite presentation.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
If $f$ is flat at $x$ over $S$, then there exists a commutative
diagram of pointed schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
(X, x) \ar[d] & (X', x') \ar[l]^g \ar[d] \\
(S, s) & (S', s') \ar[l]
}
$$
whose horizontal arrows are elementary \'etale neighbourhoods
such that $X'$, $S'$ are affine and such that
$\Gamma(X', \mathcal{O}_{X'})$ is a projective
$\Gamma(S', \mathcal{O}_{S'})$-module.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $I^\bullet$ be a complex. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I^\bullet$ is K-injective,
\item for every quasi-isomorphism $M^\bullet \to N^\bullet$ the map
$$
\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(N^\bullet, I^\bullet)
\to \Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(M^\bullet, I^\bullet)
$$
is bijective, and
\item for every complex $N^\bullet$ the map
$$
\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(N^\bullet, I^\bullet)
\to \Hom_{D(\mathcal{A})}(N^\bullet, I^\bullet)
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-K-injective}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $I^\bullet$ be a complex. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I^\bullet$ is K-injective,
\item for every quasi-isomorphism $M^\bullet \to N^\bullet$ the map
$$
\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(N^\bullet, I^\bullet)
\to \Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(M^\bullet, I^\bullet)
$$
is bijective, and
\item for every complex $N^\bullet$ the map
$$
\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(N^\bullet, I^\bullet)
\to \Hom_{D(\mathcal{A})}(N^\bullet, I^\bullet)
$$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-module-quotient-flat}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any presheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules is a quotient of
a direct sum $\bigoplus j_{U_i!}\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$.
\item Any presheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules is a quotient of
a flat presheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ is a site, $\mathcal{O}$ is a sheaf of rings,
then any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules is a quotient of
a direct sum $\bigoplus j_{U_i!}\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$.
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ is a site, $\mathcal{O}$ is a sheaf of rings,
then any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules is a quotient of
a flat sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-equivalent-f-good}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $f \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$. Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.

\begin{enumerate}
\item for all $n \geq 1$ the map
$f : \mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$ factors
through $\mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_n$ to give a
short exact sequence
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_n \to \mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to 0$,
\item for all $n \geq 1$ the map
$f^n : \mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$
factors through $\mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_1$
to give a short exact sequence
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_{n + 1} \to \mathcal{F}_n \to 0$
\item there exists an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{G}$

\item there exists an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ which is

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a birational proper
morphism of schemes with $Y$ reduced. Let $U \subset X$ be the
maximal open over which $f$ is an isomorphism. Then $U$ contains
\begin{enumerate}
\item every point of codimension $0$ in $X$,
\item every $x \in X$ of codimension $1$ on $X$ such that
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a discrete valuation ring,
\item every $x \in X$ such that the fibre of $Y \to X$ over $x$ is
finite and such that $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is normal, and
\item every $x \in X$ such that $f$ is quasi-finite at some
$y \in Y$ lying over $x$ and $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is normal.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is representable by algebraic spaces, and
\item $\mathcal{Y}$ is an algebraic stack over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{X}$ is an algebraic stack over $S$.

\label{lemma-zero-over-image}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{spaces, \etale}$.
Let $\sigma \in \mathcal{F}(U)$ be a local section.
There exists an open subspace $W \subset U$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $W \subset U$ is the largest open subspace of $U$ such
that $\sigma|_W = 0$,
\item for every $\varphi : V \to U$ in $X_{spaces, \etale}$ we have
$$
\sigma|_V = 0 \Leftrightarrow \varphi(V) \subset W,
$$
\item for every geometric point $\overline{u}$ of $U$ we have
$$
(U, \overline{u}, \sigma) = 0\text{ in }\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}}
\Leftrightarrow
\overline{u} \in W
$$
where $\overline{x} = (U \to X) \circ \overline{u}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acc-coherent}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The ascending chain condition holds for quasi-coherent submodules
of $\mathcal{F}$. In other words, given any sequence
$$
\mathcal{F}_1 \subset \mathcal{F}_2 \subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{F}
$$
of quasi-coherent submodules, then
$\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1} = \ldots $ for some $n \geq 0$.

For algebraic spaces $X\to Z\to B$ over $S$, the restriction-of-scalars functor $\operatorname{Res}_{Z/B}(X)$ sends $T\to B$ to the set of $Z$-morphisms $T\times_BZ\to X$. It is an fppf sheaf over $B$; there is a canonical square with $\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,X)$ over $\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,Z)$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{Z/B}(X)$ over $B$, the latter mapping into $\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,Z)$ through the identity section of $Z$.

For a finite locally free morphism $Z\to U$ and an étale algebraic-space morphism $W\to Z$, the functor of sections $F(T)=\{\sigma:Z\times_UT\to W\times_UT\mid\sigma\text{ is a section over }Z\times_UT\}$ on $U$-schemes is an fppf sheaf. If $W\to Z$ is surjective, sections exist étale-locally on $U$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X' \to X \to Z \to B$ be morphisms of
algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X' \to X$ is \'etale, and
\item $Z \to B$ is finite locally free.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\text{Res}_{Z/B}(X') \to \text{Res}_{Z/B}(X)$ is representable
by algebraic spaces and \'etale. If $X' \to X$ is also surjective,
then $\text{Res}_{Z/B}(X') \to \text{Res}_{Z/B}(X)$ is surjective.

source.label: lemma-galois-action-irreducible-components
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-galois-action-irreducible-components}
Let $k$ be a field, with separable algebraic closure $\overline{k}$.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
There is an action
$$
\text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)^{opp} \times \text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}})
\longrightarrow
\text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}})
$$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item An element $\overline{T} \in \text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}})$
is fixed by the action if and only if there exists an irreducible
component $T \subset X$, which is geometrically irreducible over $k$,
such that $T_{\overline{k}} = \overline{T}$.
\item For any field extension $k'/k$ with separable
algebraic closure $\overline{k}'$ the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\text{Gal}(\overline{k}'/k') \times \text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}'})
\ar[r] \ar[d] &
\text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}'}) \ar[d] \\
\text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k) \times \text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}})
\ar[r] &
\text{IrredComp}(X_{\overline{k}})
}
$$
is commutative (where the right vertical arrow is a bijection
according to Lemma \ref{lemma-separably-closed-field-irreducible-components}).
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$ be a point. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|f|(|Y|)$ is contained in $\{x\} \subset |X|$,
\item $Y$ is reduced, and
\item $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism
$x : \operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ where $k$ is a field (for example if $X$ is decent).
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ factors through
the residual space $Z_x = \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ of $X$ at $x$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-factor-through-residual-space-decent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$ be a point. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|f|(|Y|)$ is contained in $\{x\} \subset |X|$,
\item $Y$ is reduced, and
\item $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism
$x : \Spec(k) \to X$ where $k$ is a field (for example if $X$ is decent).
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ factors through
the residual space $Z_x = \Spec(k)$ of $X$ at $x$.

\label{lemma-finite-separable-enough}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion
as in Definition \ref{definition-valuative-criterion},
\item $f$ satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion
as in Definition \ref{definition-valuative-criterion} modified by
requiring the extension $K'/K$ to be finite separable.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-shriek-base-change}
Let $f: Y \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $j: V \to X$ be an \'etale
morphism. Consider the fibre product
$$
\xymatrix{
V' = Y \times_X V \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_-{j'} & Y \ar[d]^f \\
V \ar[r]^j & X
}
$$
Then we have $j'_! f'^{-1} = f^{-1} j_!$ on abelian sheaves and on
sheaves of modules.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed-topos morphism $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$, the left derived pullback $Lf^*:D(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})\to D(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$ is defined by K-flat resolutions, and $Rf_*$ denotes the right derived direct image; no flatness of $f$ is assumed unless stated. Here $f^{-1}\mathcal O'$ acts on any $\mathcal O$-module via $f^{-1}\mathcal O'\to\mathcal O$, so the right-hand derived tensor product takes place over the sheaf of rings $f^{-1}\mathcal O'$. Derived inverse image $f^{-1}\mathcal G^\bullet$ is exact on sheaves of modules, but $f^*$ need not be.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. There is a canonical bifunctorial
isomorphism
$$
\mathcal{F}^\bullet
\otimes_\mathcal{O}^{\mathbf{L}}
Lf^*\mathcal{G}^\bullet
=
\mathcal{F}^\bullet 
\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal{O}'}^{\mathbf{L}}
f^{-1}\mathcal{G}^\bullet 
$$
for $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ and
$\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal{O}')$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The base-change-of-scalars derived tensor identity over f^{-1}O' is maintained, with F in D(O), G in D(O'), right-hand inverse-image complex and no unmentioned flatness.

phase3.reason: The proof reduces derived tensor base-change to the ordinary associativity-of-tensor identity after choosing flat resolutions.

\label{lemma-variant-derived-pullback}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. There is a canonical bifunctorial
isomorphism
$$
\mathcal{F}^\bullet
\otimes_\mathcal{O}^{\mathbf{L}}
Lf^*\mathcal{G}^\bullet
=
\mathcal{F}^\bullet 
\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal{O}'}^{\mathbf{L}}
f^{-1}\mathcal{G}^\bullet 
$$
for $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ and
$\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal{O}')$.

source.label: lemma-two-split-injections
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-two-split-injections}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Suppose that
$\alpha : K \to L$ and $\beta : L \to M$ are admissible monomorphisms
of differential graded $A$-modules. Then there exist distinguished triangles
$(K, L, Q_1, \alpha, p_1, d_1)$, $(K, M, Q_2, \beta \circ \alpha, p_2, d_2)$
and $(L, M, Q_3, \beta, p_3, d_3)$ for which TR4 holds.

source.label: lemma-relative-cycles-h-descent
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-cycles-h-descent}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$. Let $\{g_i : S_i \to S\}$
be a h covering (More on Flatness, Definition
\ref{flat-definition-h-covering}). Then $\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle
if and only if each base change $g_i^*\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle.

source.label: lemma-locally-free-module
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-free-module}
Let $X = \Spec(R)$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F} = \widetilde{M}$ for some $R$-module $M$.
The quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is a (finite) locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module of if and only if $M$ is a (finite)
locally free $R$-module.

in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ functorial in both $K$ and $L$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compactify-f-shriek-separated}
Let $Y$ be a scheme. Let $j : X \to \overline{X}$ be an open
immersion of schemes over $Y$ with $\overline{X}$ proper over $Y$.
Denote $f : X \to Y$ and $\overline{f} : \overline{X} \to Y$
the structure morphisms. For $\mathcal{F} \in \textit{Ab}(X_\etale)$
there is a canonical isomorphism (see proof)
$$
f_!\mathcal{F} \longrightarrow \overline{f}_!j_!\mathcal{F}
$$
As we have $\overline{f}_! = \overline{f}_*$ by
Lemma \ref{lemma-proper-f-shriek} we obtain
$\overline{f}_* \circ j_! = f_!$ as functors
$\textit{Ab}(X_\etale) \to \textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$.

\label{lemma-homotopy}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K, L$ be hypercoverings of $X$.
Let $a, b : K \to L$ be morphisms of hypercoverings.
There exists a morphism of hypercoverings
$c : K' \to K$ such that $a \circ c$ is homotopic
to $b \circ c$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-quotient}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $M$ be a differential graded $A$-module. There exists a homomorphism
$P \to M$ of differential graded $A$-modules with the following
properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P \to M$ is surjective,
\item $\Ker(\text{d}_P) \to \Ker(\text{d}_M)$ is surjective, and
\item $P$ sits in an admissible short exact sequence
$0 \to P' \to P \to P'' \to 0$ where $P'$, $P''$ are direct sums
of shifts of $A$.
\end{enumerate}
