source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-left-dual-module}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
$\mathcal{O}$-module. Let $\mathcal{G}, \eta, \epsilon$
be a left dual of $\mathcal{F}$ in the monoidal category of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules, see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-dual}. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$
there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that $\mathcal{F}|_{U_i}$
is a direct summand of a finite free $\mathcal{O}|_{U_i}$-module,
\item the map
$e : \SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{O}) \to \mathcal{G}$
sending a local section $\lambda$ to $(\lambda \otimes 1)(\eta)$
is an isomorphism,
\item we have $\epsilon(f, g) = e^{-1}(g)(f)$ for local sections
$f$ and $g$ of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-invert-s-cohomology}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical map
$$
H^p_*(X, \mathcal{L}, \mathcal{F})_{(s)}
\longrightarrow
H^p(X_s, \mathcal{F})
$$
which maps $\xi/s^n$ to $s^{-n}\xi$ is an isomorphism.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}
$$
be a fibre product diagram of schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Assume $f : X \to Y$ proper and $g : Y' \to Y$ flat of relative dimension $r$.
Then also $f'$ is proper and $g'$ is flat of relative dimension $r$.
For any $k$-cycle $\alpha$ on $X$ we have
$$
g^*f_*\alpha = f'_*(g')^*\alpha
$$
in $Z_{k + r}(Y')$.

source.label: lemma-dual-perfect-complex
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dual-perfect-complex}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $K$ be a perfect object of
$D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then $K^\vee = R\SheafHom(K, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is a
perfect object too and $(K^\vee)^\vee \cong K$. There are
functorial isomorphisms
$$
M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} K^\vee = R\SheafHom(K, M)
$$
and
$$
H^0(X, M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} K^\vee) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_X)}(K, M)
$$
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

formulation.statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

A connection on an $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-module $\mathcal F$ is an additive map $\nabla:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X/S}}\Omega_{X/S}$ obeying $\nabla(fs)=f\nabla(s)+s\otimes df$. It extends to the de Rham complex by $\nabla(s\otimes\omega)=\nabla(s)\wedge\omega+s\otimes d\omega$; it is integrable when the resulting composite $\nabla^2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\otimes\Omega^2_{X/S}$ is zero.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above,
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a crystal in $\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-modules
on $\text{Cris}(X/S)$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ comes equipped with a
canonical integrable connection.

formulation.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Property (P) means an exhaustive filtration $0=F_{-1}P\subset F_0P\subset F_1P\subset\cdots$ by dg $A$-submodules with graded-split inclusions and successive quotients isomorphic to direct sums of shifts $A[k]$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential graded
$(A, B)$-bimodule which has property (P) as a left differential graded
$A$-module. Then $M \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N$ is computed by
$M \otimes_A N$ for all differential graded $A$-modules $M$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The original requires property (P) on N as a LEFT dg A-module, corresponding to a right A^opp dg module, not on the right B structure. With this hypothesis the ordinary tensor M⊗_A N computes derived tensor for every RIGHT dg A-module M. The statement maintains that explicit left-sided condition and the property-(P) filtration is understood relative to that left action.

phase3.reason: Uses the signed passage to the opposite algebra to regard the left A-property-(P) module N as a K-flat right A^opp-module. Tensoring any quasi-isomorphism M→M' with N is then a quasi-isomorphism by the derived tensor functoriality lemma, so the ordinary tensor already computes the derived one.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compute-bc}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential graded
$(A, B)$-bimodule which has property (P) as a left differential graded
$A$-module. Then $M \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N$ is computed by
$M \otimes_A N$ for all differential graded $A$-modules $M$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-sheaf}
Given a morphism of schemes $f : X \to Y$, a quasi-coherent sheaf
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$, and a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_Y$. Assume $Y$ locally
Noetherian, $f$ proper, and $\mathcal{F}$ coherent.
Then
$$
\mathcal{M} =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} R^pf_*(\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F})
$$
is a graded $\mathcal{A} = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} \mathcal{I}^n$-module
which is quasi-coherent and of finite type.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-derived-limit-injective}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $(K_n)$ be an
inverse system in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Let $x \in X$ and $m \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Assume there exist an integer $n(x)$ and a fundamental system $\mathfrak{U}_x$
of open neighbourhoods of $x$ such that for $U \in \mathfrak{U}_x$
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R^1\lim H^{m - 1}(U, K_n) = 0$, and
\item $H^m(U, K_n) \to H^m(U, K_{n(x)})$ is injective
for $n \geq n(x)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map on stalks $H^m(R\lim K_n)_x \to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ is injective.

The sheaf-theoretic closed immersion correspondence and module functors are source-defined.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals cutting out $Z$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction map
$\mathcal{F} \to i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$ induces an isomorphism
$\mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \cong i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$.
\item The functor $i^*$ is a left inverse to $i_*$, i.e., for any
$\mathcal{O}_Z$-module $\mathcal{G}$ the adjunction map
$i^*i_*\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{G}$ is an isomorphism.
\item The functor
$$
i_* :
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For closed immersion i:Z→X cut out by quasi-coherent ideal I, (1) F/IF≅i_*i^*F for each O_X-module F, (2) i^*i_*G≅G for each O_Z-module G, (3) i_* is exact and fully faithful on QCoh with essential image annihilated by I. The three independent source assertions and exact sheaf categories remain.

phase3.reason: The closed immersion's quotient exact sequence O_X→i_*O_Z gives i_*i^*F=F/IF. The counit i^*i_*G→G is an isomorphism because the restricted structure sheaf map is surjective. Quasi-compact separated pushforward preserves quasi-coherence, and annihilation by I characterizes its fully faithful essential image.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-i-star-equivalence}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals cutting out $Z$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction map
$\mathcal{F} \to i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$ induces an isomorphism
$\mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \cong i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$.
\item The functor $i^*$ is a left inverse to $i_*$, i.e., for any
$\mathcal{O}_Z$-module $\mathcal{G}$ the adjunction map
$i^*i_*\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{G}$ is an isomorphism.
\item The functor
$$
i_* :
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

For a ringed site (C,O), a complex E^bullet is **perfect** when after a covering of every site object it has a quasi-isomorphism from a **strictly perfect** complex (bounded, termwise direct summand of finite free O-modules); a derived object is perfect if represented by such a complex (source Definition perfect at 12734–12746). A perfect object is **not assumed globally bounded** unless the topos is quasi-compact. Its relation to pseudo-coherence and local finite Tor dimension is an equivalence only where stated, not an inherited hypothesis. The integer shift is **(a−1)-pseudo-coherent** (not a-pseudo-coherent), paired with Tor-amplitude [a,b].

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $a \leq b$ be integers. If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$
and is $(a - 1)$-pseudo-coherent, then $E$ is perfect.

\label{lemma-perfect-precise}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $a \leq b$ be integers. If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$
and is $(a - 1)$-pseudo-coherent, then $E$ is perfect.

\label{lemma-lift-morphism-presentations}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of algebraic
stacks over $S$.
Let $V \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$.
Let $y : (\Sch/V)_{fppf} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be surjective and smooth.
Then there exists an object $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a $2$-commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{

(\Sch/V)_{fppf} \ar[d]^y \\
\mathcal{X} \ar[r]^f & \mathcal{Y}
}
$$
with $x$ surjective and smooth.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-delocalize-base}
Let $R \to A \to \Lambda$ be ring maps with $A$ of finite presentation
over $R$. Let $S \subset R$ be a multiplicative
set. Let $S^{-1}A \to B' \to S^{-1}\Lambda$ be a factorization with
$B'$ smooth over $S^{-1}R$. Then we can find a factorization
$A \to B \to \Lambda$ such that some $s \in S$ maps to an
elementary standard element (Definition \ref{definition-strictly-standard})
in $B$ over $R$.

Derived tensor products $\otimes^\mathbf L$ are computed by K-flat resolutions, with rings indicated by the respective source and target topoi. Bifunctoriality is in both derived arguments.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi.
There is a canonical bifunctorial isomorphism
$$
Lf^*(
\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_{\mathcal{O}'}^{\mathbf{L}} \mathcal{G}^\bullet
) =
Lf^*\mathcal{F}^\bullet 
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}}^{\mathbf{L}}
Lf^*\mathcal{G}^\bullet 
$$
for $\mathcal{F}^\bullet, \mathcal{G}^\bullet \in \Ob(D(\mathcal{O}'))$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$.
Assume $s, t : R \to U$ finite locally free.
Then
$$
U = \coprod\nolimits_{r \geq 1} U_r
$$
is a disjoint union of $R$-invariant opens such that the restriction $R_r$ of
$R$ to $U_r$ has the property that $s, t : R_r \to U_r$ are finite locally
free of rank $r$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-double-structure-gives-derivation}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\varphi : \mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings.
Consider a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{O}_2 \to 0
$$
Here $\mathcal{A}$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_1$-algebras,
$\pi : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{O}_2$ is a surjection
of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_1$-algebras, and
$\mathcal{F} = \Ker(\pi)$ is its kernel. Assume $\mathcal{F}$ an ideal
sheaf with square zero in $\mathcal{A}$. So $\mathcal{F}$
has a natural structure of an $\mathcal{O}_2$-module.
A section $s : \mathcal{O}_2 \to \mathcal{A}$ of $\pi$
is a $\mathcal{O}_1$-algebra map such that $\pi \circ s = \text{id}$.
Given any section $s : \mathcal{O}_2 \to \mathcal{F}$
of $\pi$ and any $\varphi$-derivation $D : \mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{F}$
the map
$$
s + D : \mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{A}
$$
is a section of $\pi$ and every section $s'$ is of the form $s + D$
for a unique $\varphi$-derivation $D$.

formulation.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering. Here fpqc covering means each $g_i$ is flat and, for each affine open $U\subset Y$, there are finitely many affine opens $V_j\subset Y_{i_j}$ with $\bigcup_j g_{i_j}(V_j)=U$. Write $f_i:Y_i\times_Y X\to Y_i$ for the base changes. Unramified here means locally of finite type with $\Omega_{X/Y}=0$; G-unramified means locally of finite presentation with $\Omega_{X/Y}=0$. $f$ is locally of finite type and has zero sheaf of relative differentials if and only if every $f_i$ is locally of finite type and has zero sheaf of relative differentials. $f$ is locally of finite presentation and has zero sheaf of relative differentials if and only if every $f_i$ is locally of finite presentation and has zero sheaf of relative differentials.

hypotheses: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $x \in X$ we have $\mathcal{S}_x \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is the set of nonzerodivisors, and hence $\mathcal{K}_{X, x}$
is the total quotient ring of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$.
\item For any affine open $U \subset X$ the ring
$\mathcal{K}_X(U)$ equals the total quotient ring of $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of
abelian sheaves on $X$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$.
Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Assume the set of opens $V \subset Y$ such that
$H^p(f^{-1}(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(f^{-1}(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$
is a basis for the topology on $Y$. Then
$R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i$.

\label{proposition-derived-category}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Assume $\mathcal{A}$ has enough injectives.
Denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{A}$ the strictly full
additive subcategory whose objects are the injective objects of
$\mathcal{A}$.
The functor
$$
K^{+}(\mathcal{I}) \longrightarrow D^{+}(\mathcal{A})
$$
is exact, fully faithful and essentially surjective, i.e.,
an equivalence of triangulated categories.

source.label: lemma-inverse-image-connected-component
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-image-connected-component}
Let $K/k$ be an extension of fields.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
For every connected component $T$ of $X$ the inverse image
$T_K \subset X_K$ is a union of connected components of $X_K$.

hypotheses: Let $K$ be a field with separable closure $K^{sep}$ and absolute Galois group $G_K$. For a maximal pro-$\ell$ subgroup $H\subseteq G_K$, its fixed field is $L=(K^{sep})^H$, so $\operatorname{Gal}(K^{sep}/L)=H$; $\ell$-*primary torsion étale sheaves* on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ are discrete continuous $G_K$-modules killed elementwise by some power of $\ell$. Their cohomology agrees with continuous Galois cohomology. The *Brauer group* $\operatorname{Br}(K)$ consists of Morita classes of finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebras. A field $K$ is **$C_r$** if, for every positive integer degree $d$ and number of variables $n>d^r$, every homogeneous degree-$d$ polynomial over $K$ in $n$ variables has a **nonzero common solution** (for one polynomial). A *variety over $k$* in this source means a **separated integral scheme of finite type** over $k$, and its function field is the local ring at the generic point.

phase2.semantic_review_note: If Br(K')=0 for every finite extension K'/K, the entire positive-degree Galois cohomology of (Ksep)^× vanishes and every torsion GK-module has vanishing H^q for q≥2. The strong finite-extension premise remains.

phase3.reason: The extensive proof uses Kummer and Artin–Schreier sequences, Sylow reductions, torsion/rational cohomology and higher-degree induction to derive Serre's cohomological criterion.

of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules.

formulation.statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Then $\mathcal F^a$ is quasi-coherent as a module on the big ringed $\tau$-site, for every indicated $\tau$. For $\tau$ equal to Zariski or étale, $\mathcal F^a$ is likewise quasi-coherent on the respective small ringed site.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-gives-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The sheaf $\mathcal{F}^a$ is a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}$-module on $(\Sch/S)_\tau$, as defined in
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-site-local}.
\item If $\tau = Zariski$ or $\tau = \etale$, then the sheaf
$\mathcal{F}^a$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-module on
$S_{Zar}$ or $S_\etale$ as defined in
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-site-local}.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$, $(B, F)$ be filtered objects.
Let $u : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
If $u$ is injective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $A$ is the induced filtration.
If $u$ is surjective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $B$ is the quotient filtration.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-induced-and-quotient-strict}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$, $(B, F)$ be filtered objects.
Let $u : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
If $u$ is injective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $A$ is the induced filtration.
If $u$ is surjective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $B$ is the quotient filtration.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dominant-pullback-rank}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a dominant morphism of integral schemes.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Then the rank of $\mathcal{G}$ on $Y$ is equal to the rank
of $f^*\mathcal{G}$ on $X$.

affine schemes \'etale over $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-describe-reflexive-hull}
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme with
generic point $\eta$. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $T : \mathcal{G}_\eta \to \mathcal{F}_\eta$
be a linear map. Then $T$ extends to a map
$\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}^{**}$ of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
if and only if
\begin{itemize}
\item[(*)] for every $x \in X$ with $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) = 1$
we have
$$
T\left(\Im(\mathcal{G}_x \to \mathcal{G}_\eta)\right) \subset
\Im(\mathcal{F}_x \to \mathcal{F}_\eta).
$$
\end{itemize}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-catenary-in-codimension}
Let $X$ be a topological space. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is catenary, and
\item for every pair of irreducible closed subsets $Y \subset Y'$ we have
$\text{codim}(Y, Y') < \infty$ and for every triple
$Y \subset Y' \subset Y''$ of irreducible closed subsets we have
$$
\text{codim}(Y, Y'') = \text{codim}(Y, Y') + \text{codim}(Y', Y'').
$$
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unramfied-over-affine}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a finite type morphism of affine schemes.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$. Let
$$
r =
\dim_{\kappa(x)} \Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) =
\dim_{\kappa(x)} \Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) =
\dim_{\kappa(x)} T_{X/S, x}
$$
Then there exists a factorization
$$
X \xrightarrow{\pi} \mathbf{A}^r_S \to S
$$
of $f$ such that $\pi$ is unramified at $x$.

\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-pure-along-fibre-is-universal}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at all points of $X_s$, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is pure along $X_s$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure along $X_s$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-nonempty-generic-fibre}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes. Assume
$Y$ irreducible with generic point $\eta$. If $X_\eta \not = \emptyset$
then there exists a nonempty open $V \subset Y$ such that
$X_V = V \times_Y X \to V$ is surjective.

At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $s \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be a
regular (i.e., nonzero) meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$. Then the sets
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ a prime divisor with generic point }\xi
\text{ and }s\text{ not in }\mathcal{L}_\xi\}
$$
and
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ is a prime divisor and }
\text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s) \not = 0\}
$$
are locally finite in $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \geq 0$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf
on $\mathbf{P}^n_k$ with Hilbert polynomial $P \in \mathbf{Q}[t]$.
Then
$$
P(d) = \dim_k H^0(\mathbf{P}^n_k, \mathcal{F}(d))
$$
for all $d \gg 0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-reduced-local-ring}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$ be a point. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the local ring of $X$ at $x$ is reduced
(Remark \ref{remark-list-properties-local-ring-local-etale-topology}),
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}$ is reduced for some geometric
point $\overline{x}$ lying over $x$, and
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}$ is reduced for any geometric
point $\overline{x}$ lying over $x$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-kill-cohomology-class-on-covering}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $n > 0$ and let $\xi \in H^n(U, \mathcal{F})$.
Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ of $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\xi|_{U_i} = 0$ for all $i \in I$.

hypotheses: Affine-line projection over an object of FTS_S.
formulation.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Let $Y\in\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ be the affine-line projection. Then there exists a natural isomorphism of functors
\[
p^!(-)\cong Lp^*(-)[1]:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1_Y}).
\]
The isomorphism is explicitly *noncanonical*; it follows after choosing a trivialization of the restriction of the relative canonical line bundle of $\mathbf P^1_Y$.

It asserts a NONCANONICAL functor isomorphism p^!≅Lp^*[1], not a preferred natural transformation with coherent choices; the final explicitly preserves that qualification and the +1 cohomological shift.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ass-functorial-equal}
Let $f : X \to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
If $X$ is locally Noetherian, then we have
$$
f(\text{Ass}_X(\mathcal{F})) =
\text{Ass}_S(f_*\mathcal{F}) =
\text{WeakAss}_S(f_*\mathcal{F}) =
f(\text{WeakAss}_X(\mathcal{F}))
$$

conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is quasi-separated,
\item $X$ is separated,
\item $X$ is Hausdorff,
\item every affine open is closed.
\end{enumerate}
In this case the connected components of $X$ are points and every
quasi-compact open of $X$ is affine. In particular, if $X$
is quasi-compact, then $X$ is affine.

\label{lemma-sequence-reflexive}
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{F}''$ be
an exact sequence of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
If $\mathcal{F}'$ is reflexive and $\mathcal{F}''$ is torsion free,
then $\mathcal{F}$ is reflexive.

source.label: lemma-base-change-universally
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-universally}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure along $X_s$, and
\item for every morphism of pointed schemes $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
the pullback $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ is pure along $X_{s'}$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure relative to $S$ if and
only if every base change $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is
pure relative to $S'$.

\label{lemma-cech-trivial}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian presheaf on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ be an open covering. If
$U_i = U$ for some $i \in I$, then the extended {\v C}ech complex
$$
\mathcal{F}(U) \to \check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
obtained by putting $\mathcal{F}(U)$ in degree $-1$ with differential given by
the canonical map of $\mathcal{F}(U)$ into
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$
is homotopy equivalent to $0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-big}
Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_{Zar}$.
The functor
$$
u : (\Sch/T)_{Zar} \longrightarrow (\Sch/S)_{Zar},
\quad
V/T \longmapsto V/S
$$
is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint
$$
v : (\Sch/S)_{Zar} \longrightarrow (\Sch/T)_{Zar},
\quad
(U \to S) \longmapsto (U \times_S T \to T).
$$
They induce the same morphism of topoi
$$
f_{big} :
\Sh((\Sch/T)_{Zar})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_{Zar})
$$
We have $f_{big}^{-1}(\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
We have $f_{big, *}(\mathcal{F})(U/S) = \mathcal{F}(U \times_S T/T)$.
Also, $f_{big}^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_{big!}$ which commutes with
fibre products and equalizers.

\label{lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume that $f$ is quasi-separated and quasi-compact.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the
higher direct images $R^pf_*\mathcal{F}$ are quasi-coherent on $S$.
\item If $S$ is quasi-compact, there exists an integer $n = n(X, S, f)$
such that $R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = 0$ for all $p \geq n$ and any
quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$.
\item In fact, if $S$ is quasi-compact we can find $n = n(X, S, f)$
such that for every
morphism of schemes $S' \to S$ we have $R^p(f')_*\mathcal{F}' = 0$
for $p \geq n$ and any quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}'$
on $X'$. Here $f' : X' = S' \times_S X \to S'$ is the base change of $f$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $X$ be a Noetherian topological space.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Noetherian X is quasi-compact, and every subset is retrocompact; the second item is not erroneously strengthened to all subsets being closed.

phase3.reason: A bad open cover constructs a strict descending chain of closed complements, contradicting Noetherianity; subspaces inherit it.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-factor-through-open-subspace}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$, $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $X' \subset X$ be an open subspace.
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $f$ factors through $X'$ if and only if $|f| : |Y| \to |X|$
factors through $|X'| \subset |X|$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chow-group-product}
Let $K$ be a field.
Let $C_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$ be smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible
curves over $K$. Let $P_i \in C_i(K)$ be a rational point and
let $Q_i \in C_i$ be a point such that $[\kappa(Q_i) : K] = 2$.
Then $[P_1 \times \ldots \times P_n]$ is nonzero in
$\CH_0(U_1 \times_K \ldots \times_K U_n)$ where $U_i = C_i \setminus \{Q_i\}$.

source.label: lemma-i-star-equivalence
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-i-star-equivalence}
Let $i : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. Assume $i$ is a closed immersion of topoi
and $i^\sharp : \mathcal{O}' \to i_*\mathcal{O}$ is surjective.
Denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}'$ the kernel of $i^\sharp$.
The functor
$$
i_* :
\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})
\longrightarrow
\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}')
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those
$\mathcal{O}'$-modules $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{G} = 0$.

source.label: lemma-adjoint-push-pull-presheaves-modules
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-adjoint-push-pull-presheaves-modules}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings on $Y$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a presheaf of $f_p\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Then
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PMod}(f_p\mathcal{O})}(f_p\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})
=
\Mor_{\textit{PMod}(\mathcal{O})}(\mathcal{G}, f_*\mathcal{F}).
$$
Here we use
Lemmas \ref{lemma-pullback-presheaf-module}
and \ref{lemma-pushforward-presheaf-module}, and we think of
$f_*\mathcal{F}$ as an $\mathcal{O}$-module via the map
$i_\mathcal{O} : \mathcal{O} \to f_*f_p\mathcal{O}$
(defined first in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback-presheaves}).

Let $X \to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes of relative dimension $1$.

degrees $d_1$, $d_2$ over $S$. Then $D_1 + D_2$ is finite locally free
of degree $d_1 + d_2$ over $S$.

\label{lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Denote $\Sh(\mathcal{B})$ the category of
sheaves on $\mathcal{B}$.
There is an equivalence of categories
$$
\Sh(X) \longrightarrow \Sh(\mathcal{B})
$$
which assigns to a sheaf on $X$ its restriction to

formulation.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. For a ring $R$, “every local ring of $R$ is strictly henselian” means this for $R_\mathfrak p$ at each prime. An integral normal scheme has a function field at its generic point; the function field is *separably closed* if it has no nontrivial separable finite extensions. For $f\in R$, $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$.

**Standalone theorem (source data preserved):**
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes where $X$ is an integral
normal scheme with separably closed function field. Then
$R^qf_*\underline{M} = 0$ for $q > 0$ and any abelian group $M$.

**Scope and typing:** All original assumptions and the precise sheaf/site categories have been retained; all source abbreviations use the definitions above.

\label{lemma-Rf-star-zero-normal-with-alg-closed-function-field}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes where $X$ is an integral
normal scheme with separably closed function field. Then
$R^qf_*\underline{M} = 0$ for $q > 0$ and any abelian group $M$.

\label{lemma-finite-type-quasi-compact-colimit}
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $I$ be a preordered set and
let $(\mathcal{F}_i, f_{ii'})$ be a system over $I$ consisting of sheaves
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules (see
Categories, Section \ref{categories-section-posets-limits}).
Let $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$ be the colimit. Assume
(a) $I$ is directed,
(b) $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module, and
(c) $X$ is quasi-compact. Then there exists an $i$ such that
$\mathcal{F}_i \to \mathcal{F}$ is surjective.
If the transition maps $f_{ii'}$ are injective
then we conclude that $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}_i$ for some $i \in I$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-under-smooth}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes locally
of finite type over $k$. Let $x \in X$ be a point and set $y = f(x)$.
If $X \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$
then $Y \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth at $y$. In particular, if $X$ is
smooth over $k$ and $f$ is flat and surjective, then $Y$ is smooth over $k$.

Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules such that
$f : K^\bullet \to K^\bullet$ is an isomorphism for some

$R\Gamma_I(K^\bullet) = 0$.

\label{lemma-UFD-one-equation-CM}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian UFD. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal
such that $R/I$ has no embedded primes and such that
every minimal prime over $I$ has height $1$.
Then $I = (f)$ for some $f \in R$.

The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A *partial universe* is a sufficiently large set of schemes and morphisms used to choose a **small** big-$\tau$ site, closed under relevant finite limits and with every external $\tau$-cover of an object admitting a refinement internally; distinct choices give inclusions of corresponding sites. A small étale *topos* of $S$ is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$, the category of set-valued sheaves; it is not the category of all big-site sheaves.

\label{lemma-approximate-given-relative-dimension}
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of finite presentation.
Let $d \geq 0$ be an integer.
If $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme such that
$\dim(Z_s) \leq d$ for all $s \in S$, then there exists a
closed subscheme $Z' \subset X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z \subset Z'$,
\item $Z' \to X$ is of finite presentation, and
\item $\dim(Z'_s) \leq d$ for all $s \in S$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-enough}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site and let $\{(p_i, u_i)\}_{i\in I}$ be a
family of points. The family is conservative if and only if for every
sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ and every $U\in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and every
pair of distinct sections $s, s' \in \mathcal{F}(U)$, $s \not = s'$ there
exists an $i$ and $x\in u_i(U)$ such that the triples
$(U, x, s)$ and $(U, x, s')$ define distinct elements of
$\mathcal{F}_{p_i}$.

\label{lemma-stalk-internal-hom}
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $K, M$ be objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $x \in X$. The canonical map
$$
R\SheafHom(K, M)_x \longrightarrow
R\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}}(K_x, M_x)
$$
is an isomorphism in the following cases
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K$ is perfect,
\item $K$ is pseudo-coherent and $M$ is (locally) bounded below.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-cech-vanish}
\begin{slogan}
If higher {\v C}ech cohomology of an abelian sheaf vanishes for all open covers,
then higher cohomology vanishes.
\end{slogan}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module such that
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0
$$
for all $p > 0$ and any open covering $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$
of an open of $X$. Then $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$
and any open $U \subset X$.

Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_\proetale$.
The functor $T_\proetale \to (\Sch/S)_\proetale$

The functor $i_f^{-1}$ also has a left adjoint $i_{f, !}$ which commutes
with fibre products and equalizers.

\label{lemma-put-in-T}
Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_\proetale$.
The functor $T_\proetale \to (\Sch/S)_\proetale$
is cocontinuous and induces a morphism of topoi
$$
i_f :
\Sh(T_\proetale)
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_\proetale)
$$
For a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$
we have the formula $(i_f^{-1}\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
The functor $i_f^{-1}$ also has a left adjoint $i_{f, !}$ which commutes
with fibre products and equalizers.

source.label: lemma-systems-with-proper-support
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-systems-with-proper-support}
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $f : X \to S$ be a finite type morphism.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be
a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. The following are Serre subcategories
of $\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$
\begin{enumerate}
\item the full subcategory of $\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$
consisting of those objects $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ such that
the support of $\mathcal{F}_1$ is proper over $S$,
\item the full subcategory of $\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$
consisting of those objects $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ such that
there exists a closed subscheme $Z \subset X$ proper over $S$
with $\mathcal{I}_Z \mathcal{F}_n = 0$ for all $n \geq 1$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.
formulation.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$
which is reduced, connected, and has dimension $1$. Let $g$ be the genus
of $X$ and let $g_{geom}$ be the sum of the geometric genera of the
irreducible components of $X$. For any prime $\ell$ different from
the characteristic of $k$ we have
$$
\dim_{\mathbf{F}_\ell} \operatorname{Pic}(X)[\ell]
\leq g + g_{geom}
$$
and equality holds if and only if all the singularities of $X$
are multicross.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For proper reduced connected one-dimensional X over algebraically closed k and each prime ℓ≠char k, the ℓ-torsion rank of Pic(X) is bounded by arithmetic plus geometric genus; equality iff every singularity is multicross. Both the bound and the exact equality characterization are retained.

phase3.reason: Factors normalization into gluing connected-component points, gluing same-component points and squishing tangent vectors. The first changes neither Picard torsion nor h^1, the second raises ell-torsion and h^1 by one, and the third raises h^1 but not prime-to-characteristic ell-torsion. Comparing with smooth normalization yields the bound; equality precisely excludes tangent-vector squishing, corresponding to multicross singularities. Final local-to-global gluing details are omitted.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-torsion-picard-reduced-proper}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$
which is reduced, connected, and has dimension $1$. Let $g$ be the genus
of $X$ and let $g_{geom}$ be the sum of the geometric genera of the
irreducible components of $X$. For any prime $\ell$ different from
the characteristic of $k$ we have
$$
\dim_{\mathbf{F}_\ell} \Pic(X)[\ell]
\leq g + g_{geom}
$$
and equality holds if and only if all the singularities of $X$
are multicross.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kunneth-general}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes over $k$ and
let $\mathcal{F}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module, resp.\ $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
Then we have a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^n(X \times_{\Spec(k)} Y, \text{pr}_1^*\mathcal{F}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X \times_{\Spec(k)} Y}} \text{pr}_2^*\mathcal{G}) =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{p + q = n}
H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) \otimes_k H^q(Y, \mathcal{G})
$$
provided $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

formulation.statement:
An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme with ideal locally generated by one nonzerodivisor. A relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ is such a divisor $D\subset X$ with $D\to S$ flat; this does not assume $X\to S$ flat. Sums are defined by products of ideal sheaves. Let $\varphi : X \to S$ be a flat morphism which is locally of finite
presentation. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $x \in Z$ with image $s \in S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$,
then there exists an open $U \subset X$ and a
relative effective Cartier divisor $D \subset U$ such that
$Z \cap U \subset D$ and $Z_s \cap U = D_s$.
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$,
the morphism $Z \to X$ is of finite presentation, and $Z \to S$ is flat at
$x$, then we can choose $U$ and $D$ such that $Z \cap U = D$.
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$
and $Z$ is a locally principal closed subscheme of $X$ in a neighbourhood
of $x$, then we can choose $U$ and $D$ such that $Z \cap U = D$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, if $Z \to S$ is locally of finite presentation and flat and
all fibres $Z_s \subset X_s$ are effective Cartier divisors, then
$Z$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor. Similarly, if $Z$
is a locally principal closed subscheme of $X$ such that all fibres
$Z_s \subset X_s$ are effective Cartier divisors, then
$Z$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor. The opens U in the three local assertions are neighbourhoods of x.

\label{lemma-fibre-Cartier}
Let $\varphi : X \to S$ be a flat morphism which is locally of finite
presentation. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $x \in Z$ with image $s \in S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$,
then there exists an open $U \subset X$ and a
relative effective Cartier divisor $D \subset U$ such that
$Z \cap U \subset D$ and $Z_s \cap U = D_s$.
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$,
the morphism $Z \to X$ is of finite presentation, and $Z \to S$ is flat at
$x$, then we can choose $U$ and $D$ such that $Z \cap U = D$.
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$
and $Z$ is a locally principal closed subscheme of $X$ in a neighbourhood
of $x$, then we can choose $U$ and $D$ such that $Z \cap U = D$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, if $Z \to S$ is locally of finite presentation and flat and
all fibres $Z_s \subset X_s$ are effective Cartier divisors, then
$Z$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor. Similarly, if $Z$
is a locally principal closed subscheme of $X$ such that all fibres
$Z_s \subset X_s$ are effective Cartier divisors, then

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-criterion-affine-morphism}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism with $X$ and $Y$ quasi-separated.
If $R^1f_*\mathcal{I} = 0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I}$ on $X$, then $f$ is affine.

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ and $U\in\mathcal C$, the localization $\mathcal C/U$ carries restricted ring $\mathcal O_U$ and the exact restriction functor $D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O_U)$. For any **unbounded** derived object $K$, $H^p(U,K)$ means the $p$th cohomology of the right derived section complex $R\Gamma(U,K)$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
For $K$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ we have
$H^p(U, K) = H^p(\mathcal{C}/U, K|_{\mathcal{C}/U})$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For arbitrary unbounded K∈D(O), derived section cohomology H^p(U,K) agrees with that over localized slice C/U after restricting K. Includes all integer p.

phase3.reason: The proof compares global sections of a K-injective resolution on U with the localized ringed site and uses restriction preserving K-injectives.

\label{lemma-unbounded-cohomology-of-open}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
For $K$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ we have
$H^p(U, K) = H^p(\mathcal{C}/U, K|_{\mathcal{C}/U})$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-relative-assassin}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Consider the base change diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r]_{g'} & X \ar[d] \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
and set $\mathcal{F}' = (g')^*\mathcal{F}$. Let $x' \in X'$ be a point
with images $x \in X$, $s' \in S'$ and $s \in S$.
Assume $f$ locally of finite type.
Then $x' \in \text{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal{F}')$ if and only if
$x \in \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$ and $x'$ corresponds to
a generic point of an irreducible component of
$\Spec(\kappa(s') \otimes_{\kappa(s)} \kappa(x))$.

formulation.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, smooth morphism of schemes. For $p\geq 0$ put $\Omega^p_{X/S}=\bigwedge^p_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$, and let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ be the relative de Rham complex. Each $Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and the derived direct image $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are perfect objects of $D(\mathcal O_S)$.

More precisely, for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, let $X'=X\times_S S'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S'$ be the induced maps. For each $p\geq0$ the canonical derived base-change map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^p_{X'/S'}$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{S'})$, and so is the analogous map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S'}.$$

The proposal correctly expands both derived base-change isomorphisms and retains the quantification over all g:S'→S.

phase3.reason: Smoothness makes Omega^p finite locally free and base-change compatible, and proper flat perfect direct-image theory gives perfect pushforwards with derived base change. A finite truncation filtration of the relative de Rham complex, using exact triangles and two-out-of-three for perfect objects and base change, extends this to the entire complex.

\label{lemma-proper-smooth-de-Rham}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper smooth morphism of schemes. Then
$Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$, $p \geq 0$ and $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are
perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_S)$ whose formation commutes
with arbitrary change of base.

it is tautologically equivalent to a covering in $\Sch_\etale$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-integral-closure-smooth-pullback}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a smooth morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-algebras. The integral closure
of $\mathcal{O}_Y$ in $f^*\mathcal{A}$ is equal to $f^*\mathcal{A}'$
where $\mathcal{A}' \subset \mathcal{A}$ is the integral closure of

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-module-support-proper-over-base}
Consider a cartesian diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_{g'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
S' \ar[r]^g & S
}
$$
with $f$ locally of finite type. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
finite type, quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
If the support of $\mathcal{F}$ is proper over $S$, then
the support of $(g')^*\mathcal{F}$ is proper over $S'$.

\label{lemma-silly}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\mathfrak p_1, \ldots, \mathfrak p_r$
be prime ideals of $R$ with $\mathfrak p_i \not \subset \mathfrak p_j$
if $i \not = j$. Let $k_i \subset \kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ be
subfields such that the extensions $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)/k_i$
are not algebraic. Let $J \subset R$ be an ideal not contained
in any of the $\mathfrak p_i$. Then there exists an element $x \in J$
such that the image of $x$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$
is transcendental over $k_i$ for $i = 1, \ldots, r$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-compact-immersion}
Let $h : Z \to X$ be an immersion. Assume either $h$ is quasi-compact
or $Z$ is reduced. Let $\overline{Z} \subset X$ be the scheme theoretic
image of $h$. Then the morphism $Z \to \overline{Z}$ is an open immersion
which identifies $Z$ with a scheme theoretically dense open
subscheme of $\overline{Z}$. Moreover, $Z$ is topologically
dense in $\overline{Z}$.

\item $R = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is semi-local, e.g., if $\dim_k R < \infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the pullback map $\Pic(X) \to \Pic(X_{k'})$ is injective.

formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$; set $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and let $f:X\to S$ be a separated finite-type morphism, and put $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$.
Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
Let $\textit{Coh}_{\mathrm{proper}/S}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote coherent sheaves whose supports are proper over $S$, and let $\textit{Coh}_{\mathrm{proper}/S}(X,\mathcal I)$ denote objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ for which $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ is proper over $S$.
Then The induced $I$-adic completion functor $\textit{Coh}_{\mathrm{proper}/S}(\mathcal O_X)\to\textit{Coh}_{\mathrm{proper}/S}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal F\mapsto(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)_{n\geq1}$, is an equivalence of categories.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For separated finite-type X over I-complete Noetherian A, Grothendieck existence identifies coherent sheaves with support proper over A with coherent I-adic formal systems whose first-level support is proper over A. Both support-restricted categories and completion equivalence survive; a duplicated 'The' is editorial only.

phase3.reason: A Noetherian maximal-counterexample argument and Chow's lemma reduce algebraization of coherent systems with proper support to the projective existence theorem; supports are shown to remain proper through pushforward and the Serre subcategory.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-grothendieck-existence}
\begin{reference}
\cite[III Theorem 5.1.5]{EGA}
\end{reference}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Let $X$ be a separated, finite type scheme over $A$. Then
the functor
(\ref{equation-completion-functor-proper-over-A})
$$
\textit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }A}(\mathcal{O}_X)
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }A}(X, \mathcal{I})
$$
is an equivalence.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $V$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$.
The canonical morphism of chain complexes
$N(V) \to s(V)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
In other words, the complementary degenerate subcomplex $D(V)$ in the functorial splitting $s(V)=N(V)\oplus D(V)$ is acyclic.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The pinned quasi-isomorphism N(V)→s(V) is equivalent to acyclicity of D(V), and the proposal explicitly recalls the functorial splitting s(V)=N(V)⊕D(V) from the previous lemma, avoiding a dangling source reference.

phase3.reason: The proof uses Eilenberg–Mac Lane objects as base cases and an induction on truncated low degrees, using short exact sequences and the five lemma on induced homology to show the normalized-to-Moore quasi-isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-isomorphism}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $V$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$.
The canonical morphism of chain complexes
$N(V) \to s(V)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
In other words, the complex $D(V)$ of Lemma
\ref{lemma-decompose-associated-complexes} is acyclic.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. If $X$ does not have a rational tail
(with rational tail as explicitly defined above),

On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of $X$ along $Z$. Then
$b$ induces an bijective map from the set of generic points
of irreducible components of $X'$ to the set of generic points of
irreducible components of $X$ which are not in $Z$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blow-up-and-irreducible-components}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of $X$ along $Z$. Then
$b$ induces an bijective map from the set of generic points
of irreducible components of $X'$ to the set of generic points of
irreducible components of $X$ which are not in $Z$.

formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Let
$(M_n)$ be an inverse system of $A$-modules such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M_n$ is a flat $A/I^n$-module,
\item $M_{n + 1} \to M_n$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $M = \lim M_n$ is a flat $A$-module and
$Q \otimes_A M = \lim Q \otimes_A M_n$ for every finite $A$-module $Q$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For Noetherian A, inverse system M_n flat over A/I^n with SURJECTIVE transitions yields flat M=lim M_n and Q⊗_A M≅lim(Q⊗_A M_n) for every finite Q. Both conclusions and surjectivity are preserved.

phase3.reason: Strict pro-vanishing of Tor and a Mittag–Leffler lemma commute tensor with inverse limits, giving the finite-module injectivity criterion for flatness.

On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. Let $b : S' \to S$ be the blowing up with center $Z$. Let $Z' \subset S'$ be
a closed subscheme. Let $S'' \to S'$ be the blowing up with center $Z'$.
Let $Y \subset S$ be a closed subscheme such that
$Y = Z \cup b(Z')$ set theoretically and the composition $S'' \to S$
is isomorphic to the blowing up of $S$ in $Y$.
In this situation, given any scheme $X$ over $S$ and
$\mathcal{F} \in \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$ with respect to the blowing

\label{lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset S$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $b : S' \to S$ be the blowing up with center $Z$. Let $Z' \subset S'$ be
a closed subscheme. Let $S'' \to S'$ be the blowing up with center $Z'$.
Let $Y \subset S$ be a closed subscheme such that
$Y = Z \cup b(Z')$ set theoretically and the composition $S'' \to S$
is isomorphic to the blowing up of $S$ in $Y$.
In this situation, given any scheme $X$ over $S$ and
$\mathcal{F} \in \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$ with respect to the blowing
up of $S$ in $Y$ is equal to the strict transform with respect to the
blowup $S'' \to S'$ in $Z'$ of the strict transform of $\mathcal{F}$
with respect to the blowup $S' \to S$ of $S$ in $Z$, and
\item the strict transform of $X$ with respect to the blowing
up of $S$ in $Y$ is equal to the strict transform with respect to the
blowup $S'' \to S'$ in $Z'$ of the strict transform of $X$
with respect to the blowup $S' \to S$ of $S$ in $Z$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: $f$ is \'etale and $X$ is irreducible.

Let $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C}$ be abelian categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and $G : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}$
be left exact functors. Assume $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ have
enough injectives. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F(I)$ is right acyclic for $G$ for each injective object $I$
of $\mathcal{A}$, and
\item the canonical map
$$
t : R(G \circ F) \longrightarrow RG \circ RF.
$$
is isomorphism of functors from $D^{+}(\mathcal{A})$ to $D^{+}(\mathcal{C})$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compose-derived-functors}
Let $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C}$ be abelian categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and $G : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}$
be left exact functors. Assume $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ have
enough injectives. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F(I)$ is right acyclic for $G$ for each injective object $I$
of $\mathcal{A}$, and
\item the canonical map
$$
t : R(G \circ F) \longrightarrow RG \circ RF.
$$
is isomorphism of functors from $D^{+}(\mathcal{A})$ to $D^{+}(\mathcal{C})$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-condition-star-sections}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal{B}$.
The map
$$
\mathcal{F}(U) \to \prod\nolimits_{x \in U} \mathcal{F}_x
$$
identifies $\mathcal{F}(U)$ with the elements $(s_x)_{x\in U}$
with the property
\begin{itemize}
\item[(*)] For any $x \in U$ there exists a $V \in \mathcal{B}$,
with $x \in V \subset U$ and a section $\sigma \in \mathcal{F}(V)$
such that for all $y \in V$ we have $s_y = (V, \sigma)$ in $\mathcal{F}_y$.
\end{itemize}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-torsion-change-rings}
Let $A \to B$ be a flat homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $T \subset \Spec(A)$ be a subset stable under specialization.
Let $T' \subset \Spec(B)$ be the inverse image of $T$.
Then the canonical map
$$
R\Gamma_T(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_{T'}(K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B)
$$
is an isomorphism for $K \in D^+(A)$. If $A$ and $B$ have finite
dimension, then this is true for $K \in D(A)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibre-product-Noetherian}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ and $Z \to Y$ be morphisms
of formal algebraic spaces over $S$. If $Z$ is locally
Noetherian and $f$ locally of finite type, then
$Z \times_Y X$ is locally Noetherian.

\label{lemma-diagram}
Suppose given a cartesian diagram of rings
$$
\xymatrix{
B \ar[r]_s & R \\
B'\ar[u] \ar[r] & R' \ar[u]_t
}

Let $W' \subset \Spec(R')$ be an open of

such that $t(f_i) = s(g_i)$ for some $g_i \in B$
and $B_{g_i} \cong R_{s(g_i)}$. Then $B' \to R'$
induces an open immersion of $W'$ into $\Spec(B')$.

\label{lemma-finite-presentation-permanence}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $Y \to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.
If $X$ is locally of finite presentation over $Z$, and
$Y$ is locally of finite type over $Z$, then $f$ is locally
of finite presentation.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion. Let $X' \to X$ be a flat
morphism. Then the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$
is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion.

\label{lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion. Let $X' \to X$ be a flat
morphism. Then the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$
is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometrically-connected-if-connected-and-point}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Assume $X$ is connected and has a point $x$ such that
$k$ is algebraically closed in $\kappa(x)$.
Then $X$ is geometrically connected.
In particular, if $X$ has a $k$-rational point and $X$ is connected,
then $X$ is geometrically connected.

phase2.proposed_correction: Set logical_form to equivalence and define universally injective representable f through all scheme-base-change tests, removing the raw source reference, then independently re-review.

phase3.reason: The universal-injectivity criterion for representable maps is equivalent to at-most-one lifting on every field-valued point. Base changes have K-valued points equal to fibre products of K-points, so injectivity for all fields is stable under all scheme tests and conversely detected by them.

source.label: lemma-universally-injective-representable
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universally-injective-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then $f$ is universally injective
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all fields $K$ the map $X(K) \to Y(K)$ is injective.

formulation.statement:
A first-order thickening of ringed topoi is a morphism $i:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O')$ whose direct-image functor identifies the underlying topoi and whose structure-sheaf map $\mathcal O'\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O$ is surjective with square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Under this identification $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O$-module. A general thickening requires only a locally nilpotent kernel.

For a first-order thickening of ringed topoi, an extension of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal K$ means a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules, where $\mathcal I$ annihilates the end terms. Such an extension induces the map $c_{\mathcal F'}:\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$ given by multiplication on local lifts.

Let $i : (\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}')$
be a first order thickening of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}'$-modules and set
$\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-linear map.
There exists an element
$$
o(\varphi) \in
\operatorname{Ext}^1_\mathcal{O}(Li^*\mathcal{F}', \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}')
$$
whose vanishing is a necessary and sufficient condition for the
existence of a lift of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}'$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spectral-closed-in-product-two-point-space}
Let $W$ be the topological space with two points, one closed,
the other not. A topological space is spectral if and only if
it is homeomorphic to a subspace of a product of
copies of $W$ which is closed in the constructible topology.

hypotheses: A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$, an $A$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $J\subset B$ containing $IB$, the divided power envelope $D_{B,\gamma}(J)=(D,\bar J,\bar\gamma)$ is the universal divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra equipped with a ring map $B\to D$ carrying $J$ into $\bar J$: maps $D\to(C,K,\delta)$ of divided power $A$-algebras correspond naturally to $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ carrying $J$ into $K$. The canonical map $D\to B/J$ has kernel $\bar J$. For a divided power ring $(B,I,\gamma)$, $B\langle x_t\rangle$ denotes the divided power polynomial algebra, the free divided power $B$-algebra on elements $x_t$ of the divided power ideal $IB\langle x_t\rangle+B\langle x_t\rangle_+$, with $x_t^{[n]}=\gamma_n(x_t)$.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ with $A$ a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-algebra, together with an $A$-algebra $C$ such that $IC=0$ and $p$ is nilpotent in $C$. An object of $\mathrm{CRIS}(C/A)$ is a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $(B,J_B,\delta)$ with $p$ nilpotent in $B$ and a compatible $A$-algebra map $C\to B/J_B$; morphisms preserve the divided powers and this map from $C$. The full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ consists of objects with $C\cong B/J_B$. The completed category $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ has analogously compatible objects complete for the $p$-adic topology, with divided powers extended to the completion; for sufficiently large $e$, reductions $B/p^eB$ lie in $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$.

For a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $D$ with distinguished ideal $\bar J$, write $D^\wedge=\varprojlim_eD/p^eD$ for its $p$-adic completion. For $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $J$, put $P_e=P/p^eP$, $J_e=(J+p^eP)/p^eP$, $D_e=D_{P_e,\gamma}(J_e)$ (for all sufficiently large $e$), and let $J^\wedge$ be the completed distinguished ideal. A divided power structure on $\bar J$ extends uniquely to $J^\wedge$ when $p$ is nilpotent in $D/\bar J$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lambda-trace}
Let $f : P\to P$ be an endomorphism of the finite projective
$\Lambda[G]$-module $P$. Then
$$
\text{Tr}_{\Lambda}(f; P) = \# G \cdot \text{Tr}_\Lambda^G(f; P).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-has-dualizing-module-CM}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. If there exists a finite $A$-module
$\omega_A$ such that $\omega_A[0]$ is a dualizing complex, then
$A$ is Cohen-Macaulay.
