For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

In the following localized setting, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, let $E$ be perfect in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $p\ge0$. Suppose that $E|_{X\setminus Z}$ is zero (for $P_p$), or a finite locally free sheaf of rank less than $p$ in degree $0$ (for $c_p$); also assume one of: $X$ is quasi-compact, its irreducible components are quasi-compact, $E$ has a locally bounded finite locally free representative, or $E$ is pulled back from a perfect object on a locally finite type $X'$ with quasi-compact irreducible components. The associated localized classes $P_p(Z\to X,E)$ and $c_p(Z\to X,E)$ lie in $A^p(Z\to X)$, characterized by $i_*\circ P_p(Z\to X,E)=P_p(E)$ and $i_*\circ c_p(Z\to X,E)=c_p(E)$. The localized character is $\operatorname{ch}(Z\to X,E)=\sum_{p\ge0}P_p(Z\to X,E)/p!$.

formulation.statement:
For an $\mathcal O_X$-module F, $F^*=\mathcal Hom(F,\mathcal O_X)$ and reflexive means the evaluation map $F\to F^{**}$ is an isomorphism. The rank-one reflexive group law is $[F][G]=[(F\otimes G)^{**}]$. Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a rank 1 coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$. Let
$$
U = \{x \in X \mid s : \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{F}_x
\text{ is an isomorphism}\}
$$ Put $\mathcal F^{[1]}=\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F^{[n+1]}=(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F^{[n]})^{**}$; powers of s map into these sheaves. 
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the inclusion morphism $j : U \to X$ is affine, and
\item for every $x \in X \setminus U$ there is an $n > 0$
such that $s^n \in \mathfrak m_x \mathcal{F}^{[n]}_x$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-generic-flatness-reduced}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is reduced,
\item $f$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open dense subscheme $U \subset S$ such that
$X_U \to U$ is flat and of finite presentation and such that
$\mathcal{F}|_{X_U}$ is flat over $U$ and of finite presentation
over $\mathcal{O}_{X_U}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibred-category-representable-goes-up}
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a fibred category.
Let $x \to y$ and $z \to y$ be morphisms of $\mathcal{S}$
with $x \to y$ strongly cartesian. If $p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$ exists,
then $x \times_y z$ exists, $p(x \times_y z) = p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$,
and $x \times_y z \to z$ is strongly cartesian.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.

\label{lemma-derived-tor-exact}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
The functors
$$
K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X))
\longrightarrow
K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)),
\quad
\mathcal{F}^\bullet \longmapsto
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{G}^\bullet \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{F}^\bullet)
$$
and
$$
K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X))
\longrightarrow
K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)),
\quad
\mathcal{F}^\bullet \longmapsto
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{G}^\bullet)
$$
are exact functors of triangulated categories.

In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

An open (respectively closed, locally closed) immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism which, after every base change by a scheme, is an open (respectively closed, locally closed) immersion of schemes.

\label{lemma-base-change-immersions}
Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.

immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.

\label{lemma-target-graded-projective}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $M \to P$ be a surjective homomorphism of differential graded
$A$-modules. If $P$ is projective as a graded $A$-module, then
$M \to P$ is an admissible epimorphism.

\label{lemma-coherent-filter}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
There exists a filtration
$$
0 = \mathcal{F}_0 \subset \mathcal{F}_1 \subset
\ldots \subset \mathcal{F}_m = \mathcal{F}
$$
by coherent subsheaves such that for each $j = 1, \ldots, m$
there exist an integral closed subscheme $Z_j \subset X$ and
a nonzero coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal{I}_j \subset \mathcal{O}_{Z_j}$
such that
$$
\mathcal{F}_j/\mathcal{F}_{j - 1}
\cong (Z_j \to X)_* \mathcal{I}_j
$$

\label{lemma-finite-directed-colimit-surjective-maps}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

of finite presentation and all transition maps
$\mathcal{F}_i \to \mathcal{F}_{i'}$ surjective.

\label{lemma-kahler-different}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $R \subset Y$ be the closed subscheme defined by
the K\"ahler different. Then $R \subset Y$ is exactly
the set of points where $f$ is not unramified.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible sheaf on $X$.
Assume we have morphisms of schemes
$$
\Spec(k) \leftarrow \Spec(A) \to W \subset X
$$
where $k$ is a field, $A$ is an integral $k$-algebra, $W$ is open in $X$.
Then there exists an $n > 0$ and a section
$s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ such that
$X_s$ is affine, $X_s \subset W$, and $\Spec(A) \to W$ factors through $X_s$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-compact-immersion}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $h : Z \to X$ be an immersion of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume either $Z \to X$ is quasi-compact or $Z$ is reduced.
Let $\overline{Z} \subset X$ be the scheme theoretic image of $h$.
Then the morphism $Z \to \overline{Z}$ is an open immersion
which identifies $Z$ with a scheme theoretically dense open
subspace of $\overline{Z}$. Moreover, $Z$ is topologically
dense in $\overline{Z}$.

conclusions: Then $\Omega_{X/S} = \Omega_{X/X^{(p)}}$.
hypotheses:

Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$.
formulation.statement:
Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $S$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$. Then $\Omega_{X/S} = \Omega_{X/X^{(p)}}$.
Absolute Frobenius acts identically on points and by $a\mapsto a^p$ on functions. For $X/S$, $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$, and $F_{X/S}$ is the canonical map induced by absolute Frobenius.

conclusions:
There is a canonical map $L_f \to \NL_f$ which
identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
$\tau_{\geq -1}L_f$.
hypotheses: For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a sheaf homomorphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheafified two-term complex $(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{\mathcal P/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P}\mathcal B)$ in degrees $-1,0$, where locally $\mathcal P\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ is a polynomial algebra presentation with kernel $\mathcal I$. The canonical comparison identifies this complex with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ in the derived category.

\label{lemma-Noetherian-base-change}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$. If $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$ is Noetherian then
$\mathcal{F}$ is pure along $X_s$ if and only if $\mathcal{F}$
is universally pure along $X_s$.

source.label: lemma-regular
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume all fibres of $f$ are locally Noetherian.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is regular,
\item $f$ is flat and its fibres are geometrically regular schemes,
\item for every pair of affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset Y$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_Y(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is regular,
\item there exists an open covering $Y = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$ is regular, and
\item there exists an affine open covering $Y = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring maps $\mathcal{O}_Y(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ are regular.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-directed-colimits-global-sections}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$\mathcal{I} \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$, $i \mapsto \mathcal{F}_i$
be a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets.
Consider the canonical map
$$
\Psi :
\colim_i \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \colim_i \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
We have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If all the transition maps are injective then $\Psi$ is injective.
\item If $\Sh(\mathcal{C})$ is quasi-compact, then $\Psi$ is injective.
\item If $\Sh(\mathcal{C})$ is quasi-compact and all the transition maps
are injective then $\Psi$ is an isomorphism.
\item Assume there exists a set $S \subset \Ob(\Sh(\mathcal{C}))$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every surjection $\mathcal{F} \to *$ there exists a
$\mathcal{K} \in S$ and a map $\mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{F}$
such that $\mathcal{K} \to *$ is surjective,
\item for $\mathcal{K} \in S$ the product
$\mathcal{K} \times \mathcal{K}$ is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Psi$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-constructible-derived}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $D_c(X_\etale, \Lambda)$, resp.\ $D_c(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$
be the full subcategory of
$D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$, resp.\ $D(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$
consisting of those complexes whose cohomology sheaves are
constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. Then
$$
\epsilon^{-1} :
D_c^+(X_\etale, \Lambda)
\longrightarrow
D_c^+(X_\proetale, \Lambda)
$$
is an equivalence of categories.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.
formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a family of schemes $U_i$ and
\'etale morphisms $\varphi_i : U_i \to X$ such that
$\coprod \varphi_i : \coprod U_i \to X$ is surjective,
and such that for each $i$ the fibre of
$|U_i| \to |X|$ over $x$ is finite, and
\item for every affine scheme $U$ and \'etale morphism $\varphi : U \to X$
the fibre of $|U| \to |X|$ over $x$ is finite.
\end{enumerate}

It says existence of some jointly surjective étale scheme-family with FINITE fibre over x for EACH member is equivalent to finiteness of x-fibres for EVERY affine étale U→X. The proposal preserves the existential versus universal quantifiers and both finiteness conditions; its descriptions of (α), (β), (γ) agree with the pinned Lemmas U/R/UR-finite-above-x (L317, L515).

phase3.reason: Pull the chosen étale cover back along an arbitrary affine étale U→X, extract finitely many quasi-compact neighbourhoods and use the quasi-finite fibre bound to prove finiteness over x.

\label{lemma-bijection-connected-components}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $k$.
Assume $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$.
Then the projection morphism
$$
p : X \times_k Y \longrightarrow Y
$$
induces a bijection between connected components.

conclusions:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal{F}$ a sheaf of sets on $X_\etale$.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is finite locally constant, and
\item $\mathcal{F} = h_U$ for some finite \'etale morphism $U \to X$.
\end{enumerate}
The claim is interpreted using the preceding explicit definitions; retain exactly the original assumptions and conclusion on the small étale site (distinguishing finite from finite-type local fibres).
hypotheses: On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$ of a scheme $X$, a *constant sheaf* $\underline E$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value a set $E$ (similarly an abelian group or $\Lambda$-module). A sheaf $\mathcal F$ is *locally constant* if there is an étale cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ on which it becomes isomorphic to a constant sheaf; it is *finite locally constant* for set-valued sheaves if its constant fibre sets are finite, and *finite type locally constant* for $\Lambda$-modules if its local fibre modules are finitely generated. For an étale map $U\to X$, its representable sheaf is $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$. In an abelian category a *weak Serre subcategory* is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions (without necessarily all subobjects).

\label{lemma-factor-through-K-flat}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $a : \mathcal{K}^\bullet \to \mathcal{L}^\bullet$ be a map of complexes
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. If $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ is K-flat, then
there exist a complex $\mathcal{N}^\bullet$ and maps of complexes
$b : \mathcal{K}^\bullet \to \mathcal{N}^\bullet$
and $c : \mathcal{N}^\bullet \to \mathcal{L}^\bullet$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{N}^\bullet$ is K-flat,
\item $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism,
\item $a$ is homotopic to $c \circ b$.
\end{enumerate}
If the terms of $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ are flat, then we may choose
$\mathcal{N}^\bullet$, $b$, and $c$
such that the same is true for $\mathcal{N}^\bullet$.

On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $U \subset X$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme.
Let $b : X' \to X$ be a $U$-admissible blowup.
Let $X'' \to X'$ be a $U$-admissible blowup.
Then the composition $X'' \to X$ is a $U$-admissible blowup.

\label{lemma-cohomology-homological}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. The functor 
$H^0 : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$
of Section \ref{section-modules} factors through a
functor
$$
H^0 : K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})
$$
which is homological in the sense of
Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-homological}.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that

\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme
is (quasi-)excellent.

source.label: lemma-locally-excellent
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-excellent}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme
is (quasi-)excellent.

\label{lemma-infinite-product-surjective}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $I$ be a set and for each $i \in I$
let $f_i : T_i \to S$ be a surjective affine morphism. Then the
product $T = \prod T_i$ in the category of schemes over $S$
(Lemma \ref{lemma-infinite-product})
maps surjectively to $S$.

formulation.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If $p$ is
representable by algebraic spaces, then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p$ is limit preserving on objects, and
\item $p$ is locally of finite presentation (meaning that all algebraic-space base changes have this property).
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a morphism representable by algebraic spaces, limit preservation on objects is equivalent to local finite presentation. The draft preserves representability as a prerequisite and retains the symmetric iff.

phase3.reason: Uses 2-Yoneda to turn finite-stage objects into points of representable fibres and applies the limit criterion for locally finite-presentation maps in each direction.

\label{lemma-finite-product-integral}
Let $R_i\to S_i$ be ring maps $i = 1, \ldots, n$.
Let $R$ and $S$ denote the product of the $R_i$ and $S_i$ respectively.
Then an element $s = (s_1, \ldots, s_n) \in S$ is integral over $R$
if and only if each $s_i$ is integral over $R_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ample-on-locally-closed}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $i : X' \to X$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume at least one of the following conditions holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is a quasi-compact immersion,
\item $X'$ is quasi-compact and $i$ is an immersion,
\item $i$ is quasi-compact and induces a homeomorphism
between $X'$ and $i(X')$,
\item $X'$ is quasi-compact and $i$ induces a homeomorphism
between $X'$ and $i(X')$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $i^*\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X'$.

formulation.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $U = \Spec(A)$ be an affine open
subscheme of $X$ and let $I \subset A$ be the ideal corresponding to
$\mathcal{I}|_U$. If $b : X' \to X$ is the blowup of $X$ in $\mathcal{I}$,
then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
b^{-1}(U) = \text{Proj}(\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq 0} I^d)
$$
of $b^{-1}(U)$ with the homogeneous spectrum of the Rees algebra
of $I$ in $A$. Moreover, $b^{-1}(U)$ has an affine open covering by
spectra of the affine blowup algebras $A[\frac{I}{a}]$.

source.label: lemma-blowing-up-affine
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowing-up-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $U = \Spec(A)$ be an affine open
subscheme of $X$ and let $I \subset A$ be the ideal corresponding to
$\mathcal{I}|_U$. If $b : X' \to X$ is the blowup of $X$ in $\mathcal{I}$,
then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
b^{-1}(U) = \text{Proj}(\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq 0} I^d)
$$
of $b^{-1}(U)$ with the homogeneous spectrum of the Rees algebra
of $I$ in $A$. Moreover, $b^{-1}(U)$ has an affine open covering by
spectra of the affine blowup algebras $A[\frac{I}{a}]$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibred-over-fibred}
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}$ be functors between
categories. If $\mathcal{A}$ is fibred over $\mathcal{B}$ and
$\mathcal{B}$ is fibred over $\mathcal{C}$, then $\mathcal{A}$
is fibred over $\mathcal{C}$.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids is algebraic if for every scheme $T$ and every object $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack. This notion is broader than being representable by algebraic spaces.
formulation.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids is algebraic if for every scheme $T$ and every object $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack. This notion is broader than being representable by algebraic spaces.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism
of stacks in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If $\mathcal{X}$ is an
algebraic stack and $\Delta : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Y} \times \mathcal{Y}$
is representable by algebraic spaces, then $F$ is algebraic.

phase2.semantic_review_note: If X is algebraic and Y has representable diagonal, the stack morphism F:X→Y is algebraic; the draft defines 'algebraic morphism' as algebraic stack base changes rather than stronger algebraic-space representability, matching the source.

phase3.reason: A smooth surjective atlas of the algebraic source is pulled back to each fibre of F; the target diagonal makes this atlas an algebraic space, giving algebraic-stack fibres.

source.label: lemma-map-from-algebraic
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-from-algebraic}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism
of stacks in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. If $\mathcal{X}$ is an
algebraic stack and $\Delta : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Y} \times \mathcal{Y}$
is representable by algebraic spaces, then $F$ is algebraic.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localize-given-products}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Assume $\mathcal{C}$ has products of pairs of objects.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the functor $j_U$ has a continuous right adjoint,
namely the functor $v(X) = X \times U / U$,
\item the functor $v$ defines a morphism of sites
$\mathcal{C}/U \to \mathcal{C}$ whose associated morphism of topoi equals
$j_U : \Sh(\mathcal{C}/U) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$, and
\item we have $j_{U*}\mathcal{F}(X) = \mathcal{F}(X \times U/U)$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-simplicial-abelian-n-skel-sub}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $U$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The rule
$$
U'_m = \sum\nolimits_{\varphi : [m] \to [i], \ i\leq n} \Im(U(\varphi))
$$
defines a sub simplicial object $U' \subset U$ with $U'_i = U_i$
for $i \leq n$.
Moreover, $N(U'_m) = 0$ for all $m > n$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exact-sequence-j-star}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $X = U \cup V$ be the union of two open subspaces.
For any object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have a distinguished
triangle
$$
E \to 
Rj_{U, *}E|_U \oplus Rj_{V, *}E|_V \to
Rj_{U \cap V, *}E|_{U \cap V} \to
E[1]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

hypotheses: For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibre-products-etale}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_\etale$ be a big \'etale
site containing $S$. The underlying categories of the sites
$\Sch_\etale$, $(\Sch/S)_\etale$, $S_\etale$, $(\textit{Aff}/S)_\etale$,
and $S_{affine, \etale}$ have fibre products.
In each case the obvious functor into the category $\Sch$ of
all schemes commutes with taking fibre products. The categories
$(\Sch/S)_\etale$, and $S_\etale$ both have a
final object, namely $S/S$.

conclusions: $\mathcal J$ is a finite type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf.
hypotheses: X is a scheme and $\mathcal J$ is an ideal sheaf that is regular, Koszul-regular, H1-regular, or quasi-regular.
formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Any regular, Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, or quasi-regular sheaf
of ideals on a scheme is a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Any one of four regularity types implies finite type quasi-coherent ideal on a scheme.

\label{lemma-map-fibre-products-smooth}
Let $\mathcal{H}_1 \to \mathcal{G}$, $\mathcal{H}_2 \to \mathcal{G}$, and
$\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ be maps of categories cofibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are deformation categories,
\item $T\mathcal{G} \to T\mathcal{F}$ is injective, and
\item $\text{Inf}(\mathcal{G}) \to \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F})$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{H}_1 \times_\mathcal{G} \mathcal{H}_2 \to
\mathcal{H}_1 \times_\mathcal{F} \mathcal{H}_2$ is smooth.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-polynomials-divide}
Let $K$ be a field. Let $n, m \in \mathbf{N}$ and
$a_0, \ldots, a_{n - 1}, b_0, \ldots, b_{m - 1} \in K$.
If the polynomial $x^n + a_{n - 1}x^{n - 1} + \ldots + a_0$
divides the polynomial $x^m + b_{m - 1} x^{m - 1} + \ldots + b_0$
in $K[x]$ then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $a_0, \ldots, a_{n - 1}$ are integral over any subring
$R_0$ of $K$ containing the elements $b_0, \ldots, b_{m - 1}$, and
\item each $a_i$ lies in $\sqrt{(b_0, \ldots, b_{m-1})R}$
for any subring $R \subset K$ containing the elements
$a_0, \ldots, a_{n - 1}, b_0, \ldots, b_{m - 1}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-matrix-right-inverse}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $n \geq m$. Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be an
$n \times m$ matrix with coefficients in $R$, written in block form
as
$$
A =
\left(
\begin{matrix}
A_1 \\
A_2
\end{matrix}
\right)
$$
where $A_1$ has size $m \times m$. Let $B$ be the adjugate (transpose of
cofactor) matrix to $A_1$. Then
$$
AB = 
\left(
\begin{matrix}
f 1_{m \times m} \\
C
\end{matrix}
\right)
$$
where $f = \det(A_1)$ and $c_{ij}$ is (up to sign) the determinant of the
$m \times m$ minor of $A$ corresponding to the rows
$1, \ldots, \hat j, \ldots, m, i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-irreducible}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is irreducible.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$
such that $I$ is not empty, $U_i$ is irreducible for all $i \in I$, and
$U_i \cap U_j \not = \emptyset$ for all $i, j \in I$.
\item The scheme $X$ is nonempty and every nonempty affine open
$U \subset X$ is irreducible.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relatively-compact-refinement}
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff and quasi-compact space.
Let $X = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ be an open covering.
Then there exists an open covering $X = \bigcup_{i \in I} V_i$
such that $\overline{V_i} \subset U_i$ for all $i$.

The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

subsets such that $S$ maps into $T$.

in $D(T^{-1}B)$.

\label{lemma-compute-colimit}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Assume colimits over $\mathbf{N}$
exist and are exact. Then countable direct sums exists and are exact.
Moreover, if $(A_n, f_n)$ is a system over $\mathbf{N}$, then there is
a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \bigoplus A_n \to \bigoplus A_n \to \colim A_n \to 0
$$
where the first map in degree $n$ is given by $1 - f_n$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-geometric-structure-unramified}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$.
Let $V = \Spec(A)$ be an affine open neighbourhood of $f(x)$ in $S$.
If $f$ is unramified at $x$, then there exist exists an affine open
$U \subset X$ with $x \in U$ and $f(U) \subset V$
such that we have a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d] & U \ar[l] \ar[rd] \ar[r]^-j &
\Spec(A[t]_{g'}/(g)) \ar[d] \ar[r] &
\Spec(A[t]) = \mathbf{A}^1_V \ar[ld] \\
Y & & V \ar[ll]
}
$$
where $j$ is an immersion, $g \in A[t]$ is a monic polynomial, and
$g'$ is the derivative of $g$ with respect to $t$. If $f$ is \'etale
at $x$, then we may choose the diagram such that $j$ is an open immersion.

\label{lemma-exists-hom-from-simplicial-set-finite}
Assume the category $\mathcal{C}$
has coproducts of any two objects and finite
limits. Let $U$ be a simplicial set, with $U_n$ finite nonempty
for all $n \geq 0$. Assume that all $n$-simplices
of $U$ are degenerate for all $n \gg 0$.
Let $V$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $\Hom(U, V)$ exists, moreover
we have the expected equalities
$$
\Hom(U, V)_n = \Hom(U \times \Delta[n], V)_0.
$$

source.label: lemma-hom-derived
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-hom-derived}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$.
Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ be differential graded
$\mathcal{A}$-modules. Let $\mathcal{N} \to \mathcal{I}$ be a
quasi-isomorphism with $\mathcal{I}$ a graded injective and
K-injective differential graded $\mathcal{A}$-module. Then
$$
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})}(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N}) =
\Hom_{K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}))}(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{I})
$$

If $g \circ f : X \to Z$ is locally of finite type, then $f : X \to Y$
is locally of finite type.

source.label: lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the derived completion $K^\wedge$ is equal to
$R\lim (K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}^n)$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ is a pseudo-coherent object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(2)] the cohomology sheaf $H^q(K^\wedge)$ is equal to
$\lim H^q(K)/\mathcal{I}^nH^q(K)$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module\footnote{For example
$H^q(K)$ for $K$ pseudo-coherent on our locally Noetherian $X$.}. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(3)] the derived completion $\mathcal{F}^\wedge$ is equal to
$\lim \mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F}$,
\item[(4)]
$\lim \mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}^n \mathcal{F} =
R\lim \mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}^n \mathcal{F}$,
\item[(5)] $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}^\wedge) = 0$ for $p \not = 0$ for all
affine opens $U \subset X$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). A sequence $\mathcal K_1^\bullet\to\mathcal K_2^\bullet\to\cdots$ is a sequential direct system of complexes, and its colimit is computed termwise in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{K}_1^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_2^\bullet \to \ldots$
be a system of K-flat complexes.
Then $\colim_i \mathcal{K}_i^\bullet$ is K-flat.

formulation.statement:
Let $j : Y \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume there exists an open $U \subset X$ with complement
$Z = X \setminus U$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U \to X$ is affine,
\item $j^{-1}(U) \to U$ is affine, and
\item $j(Y) \cap Z$ is closed.
\end{enumerate}
Then $j$ is affine. In particular, if $X$ is affine, so is $Y$.

phase3.reason: A locally closed immersion is affine near its image via a closed chart, over the chosen affine open U by hypothesis, and away from the closed intersection by empty inverse image; these cover the target.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rotate-cone}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $f : K \to L$ be a homomorphism of differential graded modules.
The triangle $(L, C(f), K[1], i, p, f[1])$ is
the triangle associated to the admissible short exact sequence
$$
0 \to L \to C(f) \to K[1] \to 0
$$
coming from the definition of the cone of $f$.

\label{lemma-refine-covering-basis}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_i U_i$ be an open covering of
$U \subset X$. There exists an open covering $U = \bigcup V_j$
which is a refinement of $\mathcal{U}$ such that each
$V_j$ is an element of the basis $\mathcal{B}$.

Let $A$ be a ring. Let $I$ be an ideal generated by an
$H_1$-regular sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ in $A$.

sequence in $A$.

source.label: lemma-integral-local
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable and integral (resp.\ finite),
\item $f$ is integral (resp.\ finite),
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is integral (resp. finite), and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is integral (resp.\ finite).
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-flat-ses}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings.
Let
$$
0 \to
\mathcal{F}_2 \to
\mathcal{F}_1 \to
\mathcal{F}_0 \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of presheaves of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{F}_2$ and $\mathcal{F}_0$ are flat so is
$\mathcal{F}_1$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}_1$ and $\mathcal{F}_0$ are flat so is
$\mathcal{F}_2$.
\end{enumerate}
If $\mathcal{C}$ is a site and $\mathcal{O}$ is a
sheaf of rings then the same result holds in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.

source.label: lemma-evaluate
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-evaluate}
Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be an artinian local ring.
Let $E$ be an injective hull of $\kappa$.
For any finite $R$-module $M$ the evaluation map
$$
M \longrightarrow \Hom_R(\Hom_R(M, E), E)
$$
is an isomorphism. In particular $R = \Hom_R(E, E)$.

\item The morphism $\varphi$ is injective

if and only if $\varphi$ is injective as a map of presheaves
(Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-presheaves-injective-surjective}),
if and only if $\varphi$ is injective as a map of sheaves
(Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-sheaves-injective-surjective}).
\item The cokernel $\Coker(\varphi)$ of $\varphi$ is the sheafification
of the cokernel of $\varphi$ as a morphism of presheaves.
\item The morphism $\varphi$ is surjective
(Homology, Definition \ref{homology-definition-injective-surjective})
if and only if $\varphi$ is surjective as a map of sheaves
(Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-sheaves-injective-surjective}).
\item A complex of abelian sheaves
$$
\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H}
$$
is exact at $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if for all
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and all $s \in \mathcal{G}(U)$
mapping to zero in $\mathcal{H}(U)$ there exists a covering
$\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ in $\mathcal{C}$ such that each

\label{lemma-euler-characteristic-extend-base-field}
Let $k'/k$ be an extension of fields. Let $X$ be a proper scheme
over $k$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$ be the pullback of $\mathcal{F}$ to $X_{k'}$.
Then $\chi(X, \mathcal{F}) = \chi(X', \mathcal{F}')$.

\label{lemma-bimodule-property-P-sequence}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $P$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule having property (P)
with corresponding filtration $F_\bullet$, then we obtain a
short exact sequence
$$
0 \to
\bigoplus\nolimits F_iP \to
\bigoplus\nolimits F_iP \to P \to 0
$$
of differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodules which is split as a sequence
of graded $(A, B)$-bimodules.

\label{lemma-reach-points-scheme-theoretic-image}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $Z$ be the scheme theoretic image of $f$.
Let $z \in |Z|$. There exists a valuation ring $A$ with
fraction field $K$ and a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[rr] \ar[d] & & X \ar[d] \ar[ld] \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] & Z \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
such that the closed point of $\Spec(A)$ maps to $z$.

\label{lemma-intersection-flat}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $I_1$, $I_2$ be ideals of $R$.
If $M/I_1M$ is flat over $R/I_1$ and $M/I_2M$ is flat over $R/I_2$,
then $M/(I_1 \cap I_2)M$ is flat over $R/(I_1 \cap I_2)$.

source.label: lemma-inertia-fibred-category
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inertia-fibred-category}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ and
$p' : \mathcal{S}' \to \mathcal{C}$ be fibred categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{S}'$ be a $1$-morphism of
fibred categories over $\mathcal{C}$. Consider the category
$\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{S}'}$ over $\mathcal{C}$ whose
\begin{enumerate}
\item objects are pairs $(x, \alpha)$ where $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{S})$
and $\alpha : x \to x$ is an automorphism with $F(\alpha) = \text{id}$,
\item morphisms $(x, \alpha) \to (y, \beta)$ are given by morphisms
$\phi : x \to y$ such that
$$
\xymatrix{
x\ar[r]_\phi\ar[d]_\alpha &
y\ar[d]^{\beta} \\
x\ar[r]^\phi &
y \\
}
$$
commutes, and
\item the functor $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{S}'} \to \mathcal{C}$
is given by $(x, \alpha) \mapsto p(x)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there is an equivalence
$$
\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{S}'} \longrightarrow
\mathcal{S}
\times_{\Delta, (\mathcal{S} \times_{\mathcal{S}'} \mathcal{S}), \Delta}
\mathcal{S}
$$
in the $(2, 1)$-category of categories over $\mathcal{C}$, and
\item $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{S}'}$ is a fibred category over
$\mathcal{C}$.
\end{enumerate}

For every family $(K_\lambda)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the canonical comparison $\bigoplus_\lambda a_f(K_\lambda)\to a_f(\bigoplus_\lambda K_\lambda)$ is an isomorphism. This does not require $f$ to be flat; perfectness and properness are the relevant assumptions.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a perfect proper morphism of Noetherian schemes.

\label{lemma-uniqueness-third-arrow}
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a pre-triangulated category. Let
$$
(a, b, c) : (X, Y, Z, f, g, h) \to (X', Y', Z', f', g', h')
$$
be a morphism of distinguished triangles. If one of the following
conditions holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Hom(Y, X') = 0$,
\item $\Hom(Z, Y') = 0$,
\item $\Hom(X, X') = \Hom(Z, X') = 0$,
\item $\Hom(Z, X') = \Hom(Z, Z') = 0$, or
\item $\Hom(X[1], Z') = \Hom(Z, X') = 0$
\end{enumerate}
then $b$ is the unique morphism from $Y \to Y'$ such that
$(a, b, c)$ is a morphism of triangles.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids is algebraic if for every scheme $T$ and every object $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack. This notion is broader than being representable by algebraic spaces.
formulation.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids is algebraic if for every scheme $T$ and every object $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack. This notion is broader than being representable by algebraic spaces.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism
of stacks in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
If $F$ is algebraic and
$\Delta : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Y} \times \mathcal{Y}$
is representable by algebraic spaces, then
$\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For algebraic F:X→Y and a representable diagonal of Y, the diagonal of X is representable by algebraic spaces. The draft preserves both premises and does not confuse the diagonals of X and Y.

phase3.reason: Express the isomorphism sheaf for two source objects over the target's algebraic-space isomorphism sheaf; its fibres identify with isomorphism sheaves in algebraic fibres of F.

\label{lemma-diagonals-and-algebraic-morphisms}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism

If $F$ is algebraic and
$\Delta : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Y} \times \mathcal{Y}$
is representable by algebraic spaces, then
$\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spell-out-theorem-formal-functions}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Assume $A$ is
Noetherian and complete with respect to $I$.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a proper morphism.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
Then
$$
H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) = \lim_n H^p(X, \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F})
$$
for all $p \geq 0$.

\label{lemma-geometrically-regular}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme over $k$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically regular,
\item $X_{k'}$ is a regular scheme for every finitely generated field
extension $k'/k$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is a regular scheme for every finite purely inseparable
field extension $k'/k$,
\item for every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is geometrically regular (see
Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-geometrically-regular}), and
\item there exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is geometrically regular over $k$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-generated-by-local-sections-stalk}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Given a set $I$, and
local sections $s_i$, $i \in I$ of $\mathcal{F}$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the subsheaf generated by the
$s_i$ and let $x\in X$.
Then $\mathcal{G}_x$ is the $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-submodule of
$\mathcal{F}_x$ generated by the elements $s_{i, x}$
for those $i$ such that $s_i$ is defined at $x$.

formulation.statement: Here $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denotes the full derived subcategory of complexes with coherent cohomology, and $D^{\pm},D^b$ denote bounded-below, bounded-above, and bounded derived subcategories. A *dualizing complex* over a Noetherian ring $A$ is a bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology, finite injective dimension, and a homothety quasi-isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $X$, a complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is the sheafification of such a ring-theoretic dualizing complex. If $K$ is such a dualizing complex on $X$, then $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and the contravariant functor $\mathbb D_K(E)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,K)$ takes $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ to itself and is an anti-equivalence, with the natural biduality map $E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb D_K\mathbb D_K(E)$ for every $E$ in this coherent-derived category. If $X$ is in addition quasi-compact, $\mathbb D_K$ exchanges $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^{+}$ and $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^{-}$ and restricts to an anti-equivalence of $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ with itself.

\label{lemma-dualizing-schemes}
Let $K$ be a dualizing complex on a locally Noetherian scheme $X$.
Then $K$ is an object of $D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
and $D = R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(-, K)$ induces an anti-equivalence
$$
D :
D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)
\longrightarrow
D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
which comes equipped with a canonical isomorphism
$\text{id} \to D \circ D$. If $X$ is quasi-compact, then
$D$ exchanges $D^+_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and
$D^-_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and induces an anti-equivalence
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

source.label: lemma-affine-space-over-field
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-space-over-field}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $d \geq 0$. Let $W \subset \mathbf{A}^d_k$
be nonempty open. Then there exists a closed point $w \in W$ such that
$k \subset \kappa(w)$ is finite separable.

hypotheses: For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.
formulation.statement:
For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $X$ be a proper curve over a field $k$ with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$.
Assume $X$ has genus $0$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module of degree $d > 0$. Then we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_k H^0(X, \mathcal{L}) = d + 1$ and $\dim_k H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$,
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is very ample and defines a closed immersion into
$\mathbf{P}^d_k$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For a genus-zero proper curve with H⁰(O_X)=k and invertible L of degree d>0, the source gives h⁰(L)=d+1, h¹(L)=0, very ampleness and an embedding in P^d. All four conclusions survive.

phase3.reason: Riemann–Roch yields sections and the cohomology count; a nonzero section defines an effective Cartier divisor whose cohomology sequence gives generation and H^1 vanishing. Surjectivity of all multiplication maps then identifies X with Proj of a degree-one generated section ring, giving the claimed closed immersion into P^d. Source omits only identification of that immersion with the displayed basis.

hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a full triangulated subcategory.
formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a full triangulated subcategory.
The kernel of the quotient functor
$Q : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}/\mathcal{B}$
is the strictly full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$ whose objects are
$$
\Ob(\Ker(Q)) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
Z \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})
\text{ such that there exists a }Z' \in \Ob(\mathcal{D}) \\
\text{ such that }Z \oplus Z'\text{ is isomorphic to an object of }\mathcal{B}
\end{matrix}
\right\}
$$
In other words it is the smallest strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$ containing $\mathcal{B}$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The kernel of triangulated quotient D→D/B is exactly the retract/summand closure of B and the smallest strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory containing B. Both descriptions are preserved.

phase3.reason: The kernel is triangulated and summand-closed by the prior kernel lemma, while the object characterization follows from the quotient localization criterion.

\label{lemma-tensor-dual}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a monoidal category. If $Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$
are left duals of $X_i$, $i = 1, 2$, then $Y_2 \otimes Y_1$ is
a left dual of $X_1 \otimes X_2$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-hull-goes-up}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa) \to (B, \mathfrak n, l)$
be a flat local homorphism of Noetherian rings such that
$\mathfrak n = \mathfrak m B$. If $E$ is the injective
hull of $\kappa$, then $E \otimes_A B$ is the injective
hull of $l$.

scheme over $k$. The multiplicity $m_{Z', Z_K}$ of an irreducible
component $Z' \subset Z_K$ is $1$ or a power of the characteristic of $k$.

formulation.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Fix a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with $V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$. Let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ with a *uniform* cohomological amplitude $[a,b]$, i.e. $H^i(K_n)=0$ for all $n$ when $i\notin[a,b]$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for $U\subseteq X$; (2) for every $p\in\mathbf Z$ there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F_p$ such that the inverse systems of coherent sheaves $(H^p(K_n))_n$ and $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_p)_n$ are isomorphic as pro-objects. This condition is independent of the choice of coherent $\mathcal F_p$ and only finitely many $p$ are nonzero due to $[a,b]$.

It equates being pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system with each cohomology pro-system H^p(K_n) pro-isomorphic to (I^nF_p)_n for some coherent F_p. The proposal preserves all quantifiers, fixed bound and characterisation of every degree p.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-extension-by-zero-algebra}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
Let $a \leq b$ be integers. Let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system of
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
such that $H^i(K_n) = 0$ for $i \not \in [a, b]$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system,
\item for every $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ there exists a coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ such that the pro-systems
$(H^p(K_n))$ and $(\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F})$ are pro-isomorphic.
\end{enumerate}

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of rank $n$.
Then
$$
\deg(\mathcal{E}) = \sum m_i \deg(\mathcal{E}|_{C_i})
$$
where $C_i \subset X$, $i = 1, \ldots, t$ are the irreducible components
of dimension $1$ with reduced induced scheme structure and $m_i$ is the
multiplicity of $C_i$ in $X$.

\label{lemma-union-essential-extensions}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $E = \colim E_i$
be a filtered colimit of $R$-modules. Suppose given a compatible
system of essential injections $M \to E_i$ of $R$-modules.
Then $M \to E$ is an essential injection.

\label{lemma-surjection}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the
topology on $X$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$.
There exists a set $I$ and for each $i \in I$ an element
$U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and a finite set $S_i$ such that there exists
a surjection $\coprod_{i \in I} j_{U_i!}\underline{S_i} \to \mathcal{F}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-finite-type-local-colimit-free}
Let $A \to B$ be a local ring map of local rings which is essentially of
finite type. Let $N$ be a finite $B$-module which is flat as an $A$-module.
If $A$ is henselian, then $N$ is a filtered colimit
$$
N = \colim_i F_i
$$
of free $A$-modules $F_i$ such that all transition maps
$u_i : F_i \to F_{i'}$ of the system induce injective maps
$\overline{u}_i : F_i/\mathfrak m_AF_i \to F_{i'}/\mathfrak m_AF_{i'}$.
Also, $N$ is a Mittag-Leffler $A$-module.

\label{lemma-decompose-associated-complexes}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $U$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$.
The canonical morphism of chain complexes
$N(U) \to s(U)$ is split. In fact,
$$
s(U) = N(U) \oplus D(U)
$$
for some complex $D(U)$. The construction $U \mapsto D(U)$
is functorial.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extension-finite-type}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
The image of a morphism of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of finite
type is of finite type.
Let
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
If $\mathcal{F}_1$ and $\mathcal{F}_3$ are of finite type,
so is $\mathcal{F}_2$.

A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ with $A$ a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-algebra, together with an $A$-algebra $C$ such that $IC=0$ and $p$ is nilpotent in $C$. An object of $\mathrm{CRIS}(C/A)$ is a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $(B,J_B,\delta)$ with $p$ nilpotent in $B$ and a compatible $A$-algebra map $C\to B/J_B$; morphisms preserve the divided powers and this map from $C$. The full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ consists of objects with $C\cong B/J_B$. The completed category $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ has analogously compatible objects complete for the $p$-adic topology, with divided powers extended to the completion; for sufficiently large $e$, reductions $B/p^eB$ lie in $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$.

For a divided power ideal $(I,\gamma)$, $I^{[n]}$ is the ideal generated by products $\prod_j\gamma_{e_j}(x_j)$ with $x_j\in I$ and $\sum e_j\ge n$, with $I^{[0]}=A$ and $I^{[1]}=I$. The ideal $I^{[2]}$ consists of terms of divided-power order at least two.

Given a ring map $A\to B$ and a divided power ideal $(J,\delta)$ on $B$, a divided power $A$-derivation $d:B\to M$ into a $B$-module is additive, vanishes on $A$, satisfies $d(bb')=b\,d(b')+b'\,d(b)$, and $d(\delta_n(x))=\delta_{n-1}(x)d(x)$ for $x\in J$. The universal module representing such derivations is $\Omega_{B/A,\delta}$ with universal map $d_{B/A,\delta}$. The ordinary Kähler differential module $\Omega_{B/A}$ represents all $A$-derivations. For a divided power scheme $(T,\mathcal J,\delta)\to S$, the sheaf $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ represents divided power derivations and is the quotient of $\Omega_{T/S}$ by the divided-power derivative relations.

Under the affine crystalline setup stated above,
Let $(B, J, \delta)$ be an object of $\text{CRIS}(C/A)$.
Let $(B(1), J(1), \delta(1))$ be the coproduct of $(B, J, \delta)$
with itself in $\text{CRIS}(C/A)$. Denote
$K = \Ker(B(1) \to B)$. Then $K \cap J(1) \subset J(1)$
is preserved by the divided power structure and
$$
\Omega_{B/A, \delta} = K/ \left(K^2 + (K \cap J(1))^{[2]}\right)
$$
canonically.

The proposal restores the affine setup and preserves this category-specific statement.

The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the full subcategory of $(\Sch/X)$ consisting
of $Y \to X$ such that the inverse image of $Z$ is an effective
Cartier divisor on $Y$. Then the blowing up $b : X' \to X$ of $Z$ in $X$
is a final object of $\mathcal{C}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universal-property-blowing-up}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the full subcategory of $(\Sch/X)$ consisting
of $Y \to X$ such that the inverse image of $Z$ is an effective
Cartier divisor on $Y$. Then the blowing up $b : X' \to X$ of $Z$ in $X$
is a final object of $\mathcal{C}$.

\label{lemma-separably-closed-field-irreducible-components}
Let $k'/k$ be an extension of fields.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$. Set $X' = X_{k'}$.
Assume $k$ separably algebraically closed.
Then the morphism $X' \to X$ induces a bijection of irreducible components.
