A finite-type point x∈|X| means that some locally-finite-type map Spec(k)→X represents x.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a morphism $\Spec(k) \to X$
which is locally of finite type and represents $x$.
\item There exists a scheme $U$, a closed point $u \in U$, and an \'etale
morphism $\varphi : U \to X$ such that $\varphi(u) = x$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: A point x of algebraic space X is represented by a locally finite type morphism Spec(k)→X iff it is the image of a closed point of some scheme étale over X. Both existential criteria and their equality are preserved.

phase3.reason: A closed point in an étale scheme presentation gives a locally finite-type map Spec κ(u)→X. Conversely a finite-type field-valued point lifts after an étale scheme presentation to a finite-type point of the fibre, whose image is a finite-type point of U; shrinking the étale neighbourhood makes that point closed.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S \subset R$ be a multiplicative subset.

\label{lemma-covering-surjective-after-sheafification}
\begin{slogan}
Coverings become surjective after sheafification.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. If
$\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ is a covering of the site
$\mathcal{C}$, then the morphism of presheaves of sets

\coprod\nolimits_{i \in I} h_{U_i} \to h_U
$$
becomes surjective after sheafification.

\label{lemma-coherent-proper-ample}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $X \to \Spec(R)$ be a proper morphism.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The graded ring
$A = \bigoplus_{d \geq 0} H^0(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})$
is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.
\item There exists an $r \geq 0$ and
$d_1, \ldots, d_r \in \mathbf{Z}$ and a surjection
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, r} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d_j}
\longrightarrow \mathcal{F}.
$$
\item For any $p$ the cohomology group $H^p(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a finite
$R$-module.
\item If $p > 0$, then
$H^p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) = 0$
for all $d$ large enough.
\item For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}$ the graded $A$-module
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq k}
H^0(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})
$$
is a finite $A$-module.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lichtenbaum}
Let $U$ be a variety. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
If $H^d(U, \mathcal{F})$ is nonzero, then $\dim(U) \geq d$ and if
equality holds, then $U$ is proper.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is unramified then for any $x \in X$ the field extension
$\kappa(x)/\kappa(f(x))$ is finite separable.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite type, and for every
$s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is unramified.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, and for every
$s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is G-unramified.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-unramified-etale-fibres
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unramified-etale-fibres}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is unramified then for any $x \in X$ the field extension
$\kappa(x)/\kappa(f(x))$ is finite separable.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite type, and for every
$s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is unramified.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, and for every
$s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is G-unramified.
\end{enumerate}

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$, $(B, \text{d})$, and
$(C, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Let $N'$ be a differential graded $(B, C)$-module.
Assume the canonical morphism $N_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N'\to(N\otimes_B N')_C$ is an isomorphism.
Then the composition
$$
\xymatrix{
D(A, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N} & &
D(B, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} N'} & &
D(C, \text{d})
}
$$
is isomorphic to $- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N''$ with
$N'' = N \otimes_B N'$ viewed as $(A, C)$-bimodule.

Its isomorphism locus is closed under coproducts and triangles and includes all free shifts A[k] by the assumed comparison, hence all of D(A).

\label{lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$, $(B, \text{d})$, and
$(C, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Let $N'$ be a differential graded $(B, C)$-module.
Assume (\ref{equation-plain-versus-derived}) is an isomorphism.
Then the composition
$$
\xymatrix{
D(A, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N} & &
D(B, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} N'} & &
D(C, \text{d})
}
$$
is isomorphic to $- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N''$ with
$N'' = N \otimes_B N'$ viewed as $(A, C)$-bimodule.

If $V\subseteq Y$ is open, $U=f^{-1}(V)$, and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $j':U\hookrightarrow X$, the *restriction comparison* is the natural map $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_{f|_U}(j^*K)$. Then (1) for every closed subset $T\subseteq Y$ and every $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$, $a_f(Q)$ is supported on $f^{-1}(T)$; and (2) for every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq Y$ and *every unbounded* $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the restriction comparison $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism. Both results hold without Noetherian assumptions on $Y$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-flat-relative}
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is proper, flat, and
of finite presentation.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint for
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every closed $T \subset Y$ if $Q \in D_\QCoh(Y)$ is supported on $T$,
then $a(Q)$ is supported on $f^{-1}(T)$,
\item for every quasi-compact open $V \subset Y$ and any
$K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ the map (\ref{equation-sheafy})
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\varphi$ is regular,
\item $S$ is Noetherian, and
\item $R$ is Noetherian and regular.
\end{enumerate}
Then $S$ is regular.

phase2.semantic_review_note: A regular morphism R→S between Noetherian rings sends regular R to regular S. The regularity of both morphism and R are separate hypotheses and are kept.

phase3.reason: Regularity is the full family of Serre Rk conditions, each of which ascends.

source.label: lemma-equality-of-morphisms
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-equality-of-morphisms}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$.
Let $f, g : X \to Y$ be morphisms of schemes over $S$.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subscheme such that
$f|_U = g|_U$. If the scheme theoretic closure of $U$
in $X$ is $X$ and $Y \to S$ is separated, then $f = g$.

source.label: lemma-coherent-Noetherian
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coherent-Noetherian}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is coherent,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a quasi-coherent, finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
\item for any affine open $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ we have
$\mathcal{F}|_U = \widetilde M$ with $M$ a finite $A$-module, and
\item there exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$,
$U_i = \Spec(A_i)$ such that each
$\mathcal{F}|_{U_i} = \widetilde M_i$ with $M_i$ a finite $A_i$-module.
\end{enumerate}
In particular $\mathcal{O}_X$ is coherent, any invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module is coherent, and more generally any
finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module is coherent.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-limit-finite-presentation}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Set $R = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
The $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}_M$ associated to $M$
is a directed colimit of finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.

source.label: lemma-localize-morphism
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localize-morphism}
Let $f : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a morphism of sites
corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
Let $V \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ and set $U = u(V)$.
Then the functor $u' : \mathcal{D}/V \to \mathcal{C}/U$,
$V'/V \mapsto u(V')/U$ determines a morphism of sites
$f' : \mathcal{C}/U \to \mathcal{D}/V$.
The morphism $f'$ fits into a commutative diagram of topoi
$$
\xymatrix{
\Sh(\mathcal{C}/U) \ar[r]_{j_U} \ar[d]_{f'} &
\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \ar[d]^f \\
\Sh(\mathcal{D}/V) \ar[r]^{j_V} &
\Sh(\mathcal{D}).
}
$$
Using the identifications
$\Sh(\mathcal{C}/U) = \Sh(\mathcal{C})/h_U^\#$ and
$\Sh(\mathcal{D}/V) = \Sh(\mathcal{D})/h_V^\#$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-essential-image-j-shriek}
the functor $(f')^{-1}$ is described by the rule
$$
(f')^{-1}(\mathcal{H} \xrightarrow{\varphi} h_V^\#)
=
(f^{-1}\mathcal{H} \xrightarrow{f^{-1}\varphi} h_U^\#).
$$
Finally, we have $f'_*j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1}f_*$.

source.label: lemma-composition-cocontinuous
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-composition-cocontinuous}
\begin{slogan}
Composition of site functors respects cocontinuity of site functors.
\end{slogan}
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$, and $v : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{E}$
be cocontinuous functors. Then $v \circ u$ is cocontinuous and we
have $h = g \circ f$
where $f : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$,
resp.\ $g : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{E})$,
resp.\ $h : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{E})$ is the
morphism of topoi associated to $u$, resp.\ $v$, resp.\ $v \circ u$.

For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. The canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\ge -n}E$ uses good truncations. For an inverse system of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules $(\mathcal F_n)$, the ordinary inverse limit is taken in the sheaf category. inverse system of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a subset. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are elements
of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_n) = 0$ for $p > 0$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$,
\item the inverse system $\mathcal{F}_n(U)$ has vanishing $R^1\lim$
for $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $R\lim \mathcal{F}_n = \lim \mathcal{F}_n$ and we have
$H^p(U, \lim \mathcal{F}_n) = 0$ for $p > 0$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

source.label: lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ be an
inverse system of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a subset. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are elements
of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_n) = 0$ for $p > 0$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$,
\item the inverse system $\mathcal{F}_n(U)$ has vanishing $R^1\lim$
for $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $R\lim \mathcal{F}_n = \lim \mathcal{F}_n$ and we have
$H^p(U, \lim \mathcal{F}_n) = 0$ for $p > 0$ and $U \in \mathcal{B}$.

hypotheses: $I$ is an ideal of a ring $A$, and $\mathcal C$ is a site.
$(\mathcal F_n)$ is an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules with $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F_{n+1}/I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$.
$p\ge0$, $N_n$ is the intersection of the specified images for all $m\ge n$, and the graded module $\bigoplus_n N_n$ satisfies ACC over $\bigoplus_n I^n/I^{n+1}$.
formulation.statement:
An inverse system $(M_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition when, for every fixed $n$, the images of the transition maps $M_m\to M_n$ stabilize for all sufficiently large $m$. The graded ring $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ is the associated graded ring of the $I$-adic filtration. For every $n$, set $N_n=\bigcap_{m\ge n}\mathrm{Im}(H^{p+1}(\mathcal C,I^n\mathcal F_{m+1})\to H^{p+1}(\mathcal C,I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}))$. The graded Noetherian/ACC hypothesis is on **$\bigoplus N_n$**, not on the larger direct sum of all degree-$p+1$ cohomology groups; the weaker image condition is essential.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of $A$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Given $n$ define
$$
N_n =
\bigcap\nolimits_{m \geq n}
\Im\left(
H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{m + 1}) \to
H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
\right)
$$
If $\bigoplus N_n$ satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module, then the inverse system
$M_n = H^p(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the Mittag-Leffler
condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image
for all $n \geq c$.}.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-property-filtered-injective}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $u : A \to B$ be a strict monomorphism
of $\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$
and $f : A \to I$ a morphism from $A$ into a filtered injective object
in $\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$.
Then there exists a morphism $g : B \to I$ such that $f = g \circ u$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale}\}$, and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules on the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. Assume (1) its restriction to the small $\tau$ ringed site $S_\tau$ is quasi-coherent; and (2) for every flat locally finitely presented morphism $g:U\to S$, the canonical comparison map from the small-site pullback $g_{\tau,\mathrm{small}}^*(\mathcal G|_{S_\tau})$ to $\mathcal G|_{U_\tau}$ is an isomorphism. Then for every such $U$ and every $p\geq0$ the natural comparison map from fppf cohomology of $\mathcal G$ over $U$ to cohomology of its restriction on the small site $U_\tau$ is an isomorphism:
$$H^p((\operatorname{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}},\mathcal G|_U)\cong H^p(U_\tau,\mathcal G|_{U_\tau}).$$

source.label: lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\tau \in \{Zar, \etale\}$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules on
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{G}|_{S_\tau}$ is quasi-coherent, and
\item for every flat, locally finitely presented morphism
$g : U \to S$ the canonical map
$g_{\tau, small}^*(\mathcal{G}|_{S_\tau}) \to \mathcal{G}|_{U_\tau}$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^p(U, \mathcal{G}) = H^p(U, \mathcal{G}|_{U_\tau})$
for every $U$ flat and locally of finite presentation over $S$.

source.label: lemma-etale-characterize
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is \'etale.
\item For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is \'etale.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is \'etale.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
\'etale, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is \'etale then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is \'etale.

A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Let $x \in R$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim(\text{Supp}(M)) \leq 1$, and
\item $\dim(\text{Supp}(M/xM)) \leq 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Write
$\text{Supp}(M) = \{\mathfrak m, \mathfrak q_1, \ldots, \mathfrak q_t\}$.
Then
$$
e_R(M, 0, x) =
\sum\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, t}
\text{ord}_{R/\mathfrak q_i}(x)
\text{length}_{R_{\mathfrak q_i}}(M_{\mathfrak q_i}).
$$

phase2.semantic_review_note: The original Noetherian-local multiplicity formula at 309–325 requires M finitely generated, support dimension ≤1, support of M/xM dimension ≤0 and the indicated maximal and one-dimensional support primes q_i. It expresses e_R(M,0,x) as the sum of orders of x on R/q_i weighted by local lengths M_{q_i}; all conditions and summation indices are retained.

phase3.reason: Reduces by finite-length terms and local supports to a one-dimensional lattice, then obtains the length formula from determinant valuation.

**Source notation/definitions, not inherited hypotheses:** With the compatible chosen sites, $\epsilon:X_{\proetale}\to X_{\etale}$ is the morphism of sites induced by the inclusion of étale objects.

Let $X$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$
we have $R\epsilon_*(\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{F}$.
\item For $K \in D^+(X_\etale)$ the map $K \to R\epsilon_*\epsilon^{-1}K$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned proetale.tex L3952 (lemma-relative-comparison): For abelian étale sheaf F, Rε_*ε^{-1}F=F; for K in BOUNDED-BELOW derived étale category D⁺, K→Rε_*ε^{-1}K is an isomorphism. Both sheaf-level and derived statements remain.

phase3.reason: Injective étale sheaves have no positive higher ε_* after ε^{-1}, using affine pro-étale vanishing and an affine étale cover. Resolve a bounded-below complex by injectives, apply Leray acyclicity and the full-faithfulness ε_* ε^{-1}=id to recover the complex, proving both parts.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth proper schemes over $k$.
If $F : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is a $k$-linear exact equivalence of triangulated categories then
there exists a Fourier-Mukai functor
$F' : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ whose
kernel is in $D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_{X \times Y})$
which is an equivalence and a sibling of $F$.
For smooth proper X,Y, an exact equivalence F has a Fourier–Mukai **sibling which is also an equivalence**, not necessarily an isomorphic functor.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian and $\mathcal D$ triangulated. Two exact functors $F,F':D^b(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D$ are *siblings* if (i) their restrictions to the heart $\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D^b(\mathcal A)$ are **naturally isomorphic**, and (ii) for every $K\in D^b(\mathcal A)$ the objects $F(K)$ and $F'(K)$ are isomorphic (with no claim these isomorphisms are natural in $K$). The category $\mathcal A$ has *enough negative objects* if for each $X\in\mathcal A$ there exists an epimorphism $N\twoheadrightarrow X$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,N)=0$.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and $S$-schemes $X,Y$. For a complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$, its *Fourier–Mukai functor* is $\Phi_K:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$, $\Phi_K(M)=R\operatorname{pr}_{2*}(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X\times_SY}}K)$; $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2$ are projections. A *Fourier–Mukai kernel* is the complex $K$. $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ denotes complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ those locally equivalent to bounded complexes of finite-rank locally free sheaves. The factor interchange $\tau:Y\times_SX\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_SY$ sends a kernel to one on the reversed product. For perfect $K$, $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$.

\label{lemma-exists-hom-0-from-simplicial-set-finite}
Assume the category $\mathcal{C}$
has coproducts of any two objects and finite
limits. Let $U$ be a simplicial set, with $U_n$ finite nonempty
for all $n \geq 0$. Assume that all $n$-simplices
of $U$ are degenerate for all $n \gg 0$.
Let $V$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then the functor
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathcal{C}^{opp} & \longrightarrow & \textit{Sets} \\
X
& \longmapsto &
\Mor_{\text{Simp}(\mathcal{C})}(X \times U, V)
\end{eqnarray*}
is representable.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $\overline{k}/k$ be a (possibly infinite)
Galois extension. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$. Let
$\overline{T} \subset X_{\overline{k}}$ have the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\overline{T}$ is a closed subset of $X_{\overline{k}}$,
\item for every $\sigma \in \text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)$
we have $\sigma(\overline{T}) = \overline{T}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a closed subset $T \subset X$ whose inverse image
in $X_{\overline{k}}$ is $\overline{T}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtration-subobject}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$ be a filtered object of $\mathcal{A}$.
Let $X \subset Y \subset A$ be subobjects of $A$.
On the object
$$
Y/X = \Ker(A/X \to A/Y)
$$
the quotient filtration coming from the induced filtration on $Y$ and the
induced filtration coming from the quotient filtration on $A/X$ agree.
Any of the morphisms $X \to Y$, $X \to A$, $Y \to A$, $Y \to A/X$,
$Y \to Y/X$, $Y/X \to A/X$ are strict (with induced/quotient filtrations).

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$, $Y$ be proper schemes over $k$. Assume
$X$ is regular. Let
$F, G : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
be $k$-linear exact functors such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F(\mathcal{F}) \cong G(\mathcal{F})$ for any coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})) = 0$,
\item $F$ is fully faithful.
\end{enumerate}
Then the essential image of $G$ is contained in the essential
image of $F$.
Only zero-dimensional-support coherent sheaves are compared objectwise, and F must be fully faithful. The conclusion is **containment of essential images**, not equality or natural isomorphism.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian and $\mathcal D$ triangulated. Two exact functors $F,F':D^b(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D$ are *siblings* if (i) their restrictions to the heart $\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D^b(\mathcal A)$ are **naturally isomorphic**, and (ii) for every $K\in D^b(\mathcal A)$ the objects $F(K)$ and $F'(K)$ are isomorphic (with no claim these isomorphisms are natural in $K$). The category $\mathcal A$ has *enough negative objects* if for each $X\in\mathcal A$ there exists an epimorphism $N\twoheadrightarrow X$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,N)=0$.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and $S$-schemes $X,Y$. For a complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$, its *Fourier–Mukai functor* is $\Phi_K:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$, $\Phi_K(M)=R\operatorname{pr}_{2*}(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X\times_SY}}K)$; $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2$ are projections. A *Fourier–Mukai kernel* is the complex $K$. $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ denotes complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ those locally equivalent to bounded complexes of finite-rank locally free sheaves. The factor interchange $\tau:Y\times_SX\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_SY$ sends a kernel to one on the reversed product. For perfect $K$, $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian and $\mathcal D$ triangulated. Two exact functors $F,F':D^b(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D$ are *siblings* if (i) their restrictions to the heart $\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D^b(\mathcal A)$ are **naturally isomorphic**, and (ii) for every $K\in D^b(\mathcal A)$ the objects $F(K)$ and $F'(K)$ are isomorphic (with no claim these isomorphisms are natural in $K$). The category $\mathcal A$ has *enough negative objects* if for each $X\in\mathcal A$ there exists an epimorphism $N\twoheadrightarrow X$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,N)=0$.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and $S$-schemes $X,Y$. For a complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$, its *Fourier–Mukai functor* is $\Phi_K:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$, $\Phi_K(M)=R\operatorname{pr}_{2*}(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X\times_SY}}K)$; $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2$ are projections. A *Fourier–Mukai kernel* is the complex $K$. $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ denotes complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ those locally equivalent to bounded complexes of finite-rank locally free sheaves. The factor interchange $\tau:Y\times_SX\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_SY$ sends a kernel to one on the reversed product. For perfect $K$, $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$, $Y$ be proper schemes over $k$. Assume
$X$ is regular. Let
$F, G : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
be $k$-linear exact functors such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F(\mathcal{F}) \cong G(\mathcal{F})$ for any coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})) = 0$,
\item $F$ is fully faithful.
\end{enumerate}
Then the essential image of $G$ is contained in the essential
image of $F$.

**Scope and interpretation:** Only zero-dimensional-support coherent sheaves are compared objectwise, and F must be fully faithful. The conclusion is **containment of essential images**, not equality or natural isomorphism.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For proper X,Y and regular X, if F,G agree objectwise on zero-dimensional-support coherent sheaves and F is fully faithful, then the essential image of G is contained in F's essential image. The result remains containment only.

phase3.reason: Adjoint orthogonality shows the right adjoint of G kills the right orthogonal of F's essential image, forcing G to factor through that image.

\label{lemma-two-functors-pre}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$, $Y$ be proper schemes over $k$. Assume

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-descend-pure}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$. Let $(S', s') \to (S, s)$ be a morphism of pointed schemes.
Assume $S' \to S$ is flat at $s'$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ is pure along $X_{s'}$,
then $\mathcal{F}$ is pure along $X_s$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ is universally pure along $X_{s'}$,
then $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure along $X_s$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-vanishing-ravi}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf
on $X$. Let $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ be an
open covering. Assume the restriction mappings
$\mathcal{F}(U) \to \mathcal{F}(U')$ are surjective
for $U'$ an arbitrary union of opens of the form $U_{i_0 \ldots i_p}$.
Then $\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$
vanishes for $p > 0$.

formulation.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. If $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, then for each $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a functorial isomorphism
\[
i^!(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,K),
\]
where $R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,-)$ denotes the *exact-support* derived right adjoint to $Ri_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$; its pushforward is $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(i_*\mathcal O_X,K)$, and on affines $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $B=A/I$ it is the sheafification of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,-)$ with its natural $B$-module structure.

The proposed statement uses the correct target X, bounded-below D_QCoh domain, and its i_* relation to internal Hom over Y rather than ordinary Hom_Y as an X-valued functor.

source.label: lemma-i-star-reflects-finite-type
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-i-star-reflects-finite-type}
Let $i : (Z, \mathcal{O}_Z) \to (X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Assume $i$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset of $X$ and
that $\mathcal{O}_X \to i_*\mathcal{O}_Z$ is surjective.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_Z$-module.
Then $i_*\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type if and only if
$\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type.

source.label: lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism}
Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Consider a commutative
diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
B \ar[rd] \\
A \ar[u] \ar[r] & A/I
}
$$
where $B$ is a smooth $A$-algebra. Then there exists an \'etale ring
map $A \to A'$ which induces an isomorphism $A/I \to A'/IA'$ and an
$A$-algebra map $B \to A'$ lifting the ring map $B \to A/I$.

Write $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O'\to\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{\mathcal B'}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal B})$. The square is strict if $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ is surjective (for square-zero kernels, equivalent to $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ being surjective).

Assume $(f, f')$ is a strict morphism of thickenings and

and an isomorphism

isomorphism classes of such pairs is principal homogeneous
under
$\Ext^1_\mathcal{O}(

Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$, define its support as $\{s\in S:\mathcal F_{\bar s}\ne0\}$ for any/every geometric point above $s$. For an étale $U\to S$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal F(U)$, the *support of $\sigma$* is $U\setminus W_\sigma$, where $W_\sigma$ is the largest **Zariski open** of $U$ on which $\sigma$ is zero. The support of an arbitrary abelian sheaf need **not** be closed, while support of an individual section is closed. A **subterminal sheaf** means a subsheaf of the terminal one-point sheaf on $S_{\acute etale}$; $h_W$ denotes the representable étale sheaf of an open subscheme $W\subseteq S$.

formulation.statement: Let $f:U\to V$ be an étale morphism of schemes, $u\in U$, $v=f(u)$. The local ring $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ is regular if and only if $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ is regular (a regular local ring is Noetherian and its maximal ideal has a minimal generating set of cardinality equal to its Krull dimension).

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L5259 states an IF AND ONLY IF between regularity of O_{U,u} and O_{V,v} under an étale f and v=f(u). The proposed regular-local-ring definition and both directions of the equivalence preserve the exact claim without adding smooth-relative-dimension assumptions.

phase3.reason: The pinned proof reduces regularity equivalence of étale local rings to the cited More on Algebra regular-étale-extension lemma for A_p→B_q; both implications are covered by that cited result.

source.label: lemma-regular-local-ring-local
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-regular-local-ring-local}
Let $f : U \to V$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
Let $u \in U$ and $v = f(u)$. Then
$\mathcal{O}_{U, u}$ is a regular local ring if and only if
$\mathcal{O}_{V, v}$ is a regular local ring.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Noetherian-geometrically-reduced-at-point}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$.
Let $x \in X$.
Assume $X$ locally Noetherian and geometrically reduced at $x$.
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
which is geometrically reduced over $k$.

conclusions: $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal I(U')$ is surjective.
hypotheses: $X$ is a ringed space, $U'\subseteq U\subseteq X$ are open, and $\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module.
formulation.statement:
\begin{slogan}
Injectives are flasque.
\end{slogan}
Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $U' \subset U \subset X$ be open subspaces.
For any injective $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{I}$ the
restriction mapping
$\mathcal{I}(U) \to \mathcal{I}(U')$ is surjective.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Injective O_X-modules are flasque on any ringed space: for all nested opens U'⊂U, restriction I(U)→I(U') is surjective. The final formulation retains injectivity, arbitrary opens and the universal surjectivity rather than incorrectly asserting that all sheaves are flasque.

phase3.reason: Represents open sections via extension-by-zero sheaves and applies injectivity to the canonical monomorphism between extensions.

Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of $S$ is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Its small étale stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ is the filtered colimit of sections $\mathcal F(U)$ over lifted étale neighbourhoods $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar s$. The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{S_{\acute etale}}$ assigns $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ to an étale $S$-scheme $U$. For $s\in S$, $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is the **ordinary Zariski local ring**, $\mathcal O_{S,s}^{h}$ its henselization, and $\mathcal O_{S,s}^{sh}$ its strict henselization with chosen residue-field separable closure.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-cohomology-vanishes}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules such that
$f : K^\bullet \to K^\bullet$ is an isomorphism for some
$f \in I$, i.e., $K^\bullet$ is a complex of $A_f$-modules. Then
$R\Gamma_Z(K^\bullet) = 0$.

formulation.statement:
For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $q\ge0$, write $\underline H^q(\mathcal F)$ for the abelian presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(V,\mathcal F)$ with natural restriction maps. For a covering $\mathcal U$, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ is Čech cohomology of this presheaf.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$. For any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there
is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(U, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-spectral-sequence}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$. For any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there
is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(U, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

\label{lemma-stalk-flat}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $p$ be a point of $\mathcal{C}$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module, then
$\mathcal{F}_p$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_p$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-glueing-increasing-union}
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $E$ be a well ordered set and let
$$
X = \bigcup\nolimits_{\alpha \in E} W_\alpha
$$
be an open covering with $W_\alpha \subset W_{\alpha + 1}$
and $W_\alpha = \bigcup_{\beta < \alpha} W_\beta$ if $\alpha$ is not
a successor. Let $K_\alpha$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_{W_\alpha})$
with $\Ext^i(K_\alpha, K_\alpha) = 0$ for $i < 0$.
Assume given isomorphisms
$\rho_\beta^\alpha :  K_\alpha|_{W_\beta} \to K_\beta$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{W_\beta})$ for all $\beta < \alpha$ with
$\rho_\gamma^\alpha = \rho_\gamma^\beta \circ \rho^\alpha_\beta|_{W_\gamma}$
for $\gamma < \beta < \alpha$.
Then there exists an object
$K$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and isomorphisms
$K|_{W_\alpha} \to K_\alpha$ for $\alpha \in E$
compatible with the isomorphisms $\rho_\beta^\alpha$.

formulation.statement:
A morphism of schemes $S'\to S$ is a *universal homeomorphism* when every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces, equivalently it is **integral, universally injective, and surjective**. The *small étale site* $S_{\acute et}$ consists of schemes étale over $S$ with jointly surjective étale covers, and its topos is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute et})$. For an étale $X\to S$, the pullback $X'=X\times_SS'$ is étale over $S'$. An equivalence of sites means a functor inducing an equivalence of categories **and** identifying covering families; it gives equivalence of sheaf categories and of abelian-sheaf cohomology.

**Statement (with original hypotheses):**
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two schemes over a base scheme $S$. Let
$S' \to S$ be a universal homeomorphism.
Denote $X'$ (resp.\ $Y'$) the base change to $S'$.
If $X$ is \'etale over $S$, then the map
$$
\Mor_S(Y, X) \longrightarrow \Mor_{S'}(Y', X')
$$
is bijective.

**Scope of conclusion:** The scheme $Y\to S$ is arbitrary; only **$X\to S$ is assumed étale**. The canonical bijection on Hom sets is induced by base change along $S'\to S$, so no descent data are choices in the conclusion.

phase3.reason: The proof reduces to base schemes étale over S, supplies a canonical descent datum over a universal homeomorphism using its thickened diagonal, and uses full faithfulness of étale descent.

\label{lemma-zariski-affine}
Let $T$ be an affine scheme. Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be a
Zariski covering of $T$. Then there exists a Zariski covering
$\{U_j \to T\}_{j = 1, \ldots, m}$ which is a refinement
of $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ such that each $U_j$ is a standard
open of $T$, see
Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-standard-covering}.
Moreover, we may choose each $U_j$ to be an open of one of the $T_i$.

In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

Let $F$, $G$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $G \to F$ be a representable morphism.
Let $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$, and $q : U \to F$
surjective and \'etale. Set $V = G \times_F U$.
Finally, let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms
of schemes as in Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}.
Then $G \to F$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ if and only if
$V \to U$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-representable-morphisms-spaces-property}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$, $G$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $G \to F$ be a representable morphism.
Let $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$, and $q : U \to F$
surjective and \'etale. Set $V = G \times_F U$.
Finally, let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms
of schemes as in Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}.
Then $G \to F$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ if and only if
$V \to U$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $A$ be an object
of $\mathcal{A}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is Artinian and Noetherian, and
\item there exists a filtration
$0 \subset A_1 \subset A_2 \subset \ldots \subset A_n = A$
by subobjects such that $A_i/A_{i - 1}$ is simple for $i = 1, \ldots, n$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-depth-flat-CM}
Let $R \to S$ be a flat local ring homomorphism of Noetherian local
rings. Denote $\mathfrak m \subset R$ the maximal ideal.
Let $I \subset S$ be an ideal.
If $S/\mathfrak mS$ is Cohen-Macaulay, then
$$
\text{depth}_I(S) \geq \dim(S/\mathfrak mS) - \dim(S/\mathfrak mS + I)
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-cohomology-big-small}
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. For $K$ in $D(S_\proetale)$
we have
$$
H^n_\proetale(S, \pi_S^{-1}K) = H^n(S_\proetale, K)
$$
and
$$
H^n_\proetale(T, \pi_S^{-1}K) = H^n(T_\proetale, f_{small}^{-1}K).
$$
For $M$ in $D((\Sch/S)_\proetale)$ we have
$$
H^n_\proetale(T, M) = H^n(T_\proetale, i_f^{-1}M).
$$

\label{lemma-cech-h0}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian presheaf on $X$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is an abelian sheaf and
\item for every open covering $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$
the natural map
$$
\mathcal{F}(U) \to \check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
is bijective.
\end{enumerate}

Let C be a site and Λ a ring; D(C,Λ)=D(Mod(underline Λ)), the derived category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf underline Λ. For a derived Λ-module complex K∈D(Λ), underline K denotes its image in D(C,Λ) by the constant-sheaf derived inverse image. A **locally constant sheaf of finite-type modules** becomes constant with a finitely generated Λ-module on a covering of every site object; when Λ is Noetherian the finite-type condition is stable under the indicated constructions. Perfectness is assumed **only for K**; L is any derived Λ-module. The local representatives α_i are **maps in D(Λ)** whose constant images equal the restricted sheaf-derived map.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with final object $X$.
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. Let $K, L$ be objects of
$D(\Lambda)$ with $K$ perfect. Let $\varphi : \underline{K} \to \underline{L}$
be map in $D(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$. There exists a covering $\{U_i \to X\}$
such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is equal to $\underline{\alpha_i}$
for some map $\alpha_i : K \to L$ in $D(\Lambda)$.

\label{lemma-locally-constant-map}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with final object $X$.
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. Let $K, L$ be objects of
$D(\Lambda)$ with $K$ perfect. Let $\varphi : \underline{K} \to \underline{L}$
be map in $D(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$. There exists a covering $\{U_i \to X\}$
such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is equal to $\underline{\alpha_i}$
for some map $\alpha_i : K \to L$ in $D(\Lambda)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bijective-map}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
If $f$ is bijective, $X$ is quasi-compact, and $Y$ is Hausdorff,
then $f$ is a homeomorphism.

\item if $X$ is a variety, then $X^\nu$ is a variety and

source.label: lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic scheme over $k$.
Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ be the normalization morphism, see
Morphisms, Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-normalization}.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\nu$ is finite, dominant, and $X^\nu$ is a disjoint
union of normal irreducible locally algebraic schemes over $k$,
\item $\nu$ factors as $X^\nu \to X_{red} \to X$ and the first
morphism is the normalization morphism of $X_{red}$,
\item if $X$ is a reduced algebraic scheme, then $\nu$ is
birational,
\item if $X$ is a variety, then $X^\nu$ is a variety and
$\nu$ is a finite birational morphism of varieties.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $n \geq 0$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type.
The set
$$
W_n = \{x \in |X|
\text{ such that the relative dimension of }f\text{ at } x \leq n\}
$$
is open in $|X|$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ an open covering. Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such descent datum is effective and the canonical functor
$$\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Desc}_{\{U_i\to S\}}(\operatorname{QCoh}),\quad\mathcal F\longmapsto(\mathcal F|_{U_i},\mathrm{can})$$
is fully faithful (indeed an equivalence of categories).

The proposal accurately defines compatible overlap cocycles and effectiveness, and retains BOTH essential surjectivity (every datum glues) and full faithfulness; these together give categorical equivalence.

phase3.reason: Effectiveness and full faithfulness of Zariski quasi-coherent descent follow from ordinary sheaf gluing and locality of quasi-coherence.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-zariski-descent-effective}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $S = \bigcup U_i$ be an open covering.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for the family $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is
effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.

\label{lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}'$ be a morphism of
sheaves of rings on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Let $x \in X$. We have
$$
\mathcal{F}_x \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_x} \mathcal{O}'_x
=
(\mathcal{F} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{O}')_x
$$
as $\mathcal{O}'_x$-modules.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cartesian-over-cartesian}
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and $G : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}$
be composable functors between categories. Let $x \to y$ be a morphism of
$\mathcal{A}$. If $x \to y$ is strongly $\mathcal{B}$-cartesian
and $F(x) \to F(y)$ is strongly $\mathcal{C}$-cartesian, then
$x \to y$ is strongly $\mathcal{C}$-cartesian.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-countable-fp-tensor}
Let $R$ be a countable ring. Let $M$ be a countable $R$-module. Then $M$
is finitely presented if and only if the canonical map
$M \otimes_R R^\mathbf{N} \to M^\mathbf{N}$ is an isomorphism.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. Let $C \subset X$ be a rational tail
(with rational tail as explicitly defined above). Then $\deg(\omega_X|_C) < 0$.

\label{lemma-rational-tail-negative}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. Let $C \subset X$ be a rational tail
(Example \ref{example-rational-tail}). Then $\deg(\omega_X|_C) < 0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-over-ideal-is-submodule}
Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
The set of elements of $S$ which are integral
over $I$ form a $R$-submodule of $S$.
Furthermore, if $s \in S$ is integral over
$R$, and $s'$ is integral over $I$, then
$ss'$ is integral over $I$.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$, let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and let $i:D=Z(s)\hookrightarrow X$ be its zero-scheme immersion.
Then the rule that to $f : X' \to X$ assigns
$(i')^* : \mathrm{CH}_k(X') \to \mathrm{CH}_{k - 1}(D')$ where $D' = D \times_X X'$
is a bivariant class of degree $1$.

Definition \ref{definition-gysin-homomorphism}.
Then the rule that to $f : X' \to X$ assigns
$(i')^* : \CH_k(X') \to \CH_{k - 1}(D')$ where $D' = D \times_X X'$
is a bivariant class of degree $1$.

conclusions: $b' \circ b$ is homotopic to $0$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For étale U→X from a scheme into an algebraic space, the support of pulled-back quasi-coherent F on U is exactly the inverse image of Supp(F). The scheme-vs-space support distinction and base-change direction are preserved.

phase3.reason: On an étale scheme chart U→X, quasi-coherent geometric stalks are obtained by faithfully flat strict henselization of local rings at ordinary points. Faithful flatness detects whether a stalk vanishes, proving equality of the support inverse image.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-support-covering}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $U$ be a scheme and let $\varphi : U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism.
Then
$$
\text{Supp}(\varphi^*\mathcal{F}) = |\varphi|^{-1}(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))
$$
where the left hand side is the support of $\varphi^*\mathcal{F}$ as a
quasi-coherent module on the scheme $U$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. For $U \subset X$ open the
functor $R\Gamma(U, -)$ commutes with $R\lim$. Moreover, there are
short exact sequences
$$
0 \to
R^1\lim H^{m - 1}(U, K_n) \to H^m(U, R\lim K_n) \to
\lim H^m(U, K_n) \to 0
$$
for any inverse system $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and any $m \in \mathbf{Z}$.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
The following quantities are equal:

\label{lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let
$\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_r$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
The map
$$
(n_1, \ldots, n_r) \longmapsto
\chi(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes
\mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes
\mathcal{L}_r^{\otimes n_r})
$$
is a numerical polynomial in $n_1, \ldots, n_r$ of total degree at
most the dimension of the support of $\mathcal{F}$.

formulation.statement:
A complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules is K-flat when $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ (sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). $f^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}'$-modules whose
terms are flat $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.

\label{lemma-pullback-K-flat}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}') \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. Let $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex
of $\mathcal{O}$-modules whose terms are flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Then
$f^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}'$-modules whose
terms are flat $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.

Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume every quasi-compact open of $X$ has
finitely many irreducible components. Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$
be the normalization of $X$. Let $x \in X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The number of branches of $X$ at $x$ is the number of
inverse images of $x$ in $X^\nu$.
\item The number of geometric branches of $X$ at $x$ is
$\sum_{\nu(x^\nu) = x} [\kappa(x^\nu) : \kappa(x)]_s$.
\end{enumerate}
Branch number is the number of minimal primes of the henselization of the local ring; geometric branch number uses its strict henselization (infinity if not finite). Geometrically unibranch means one geometric branch.

formulation.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $Z \to X$ be a relative quasi-regular immersion.
If $x \in Z$ and $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is Noetherian, then $f$ is flat at $x$.

\label{lemma-quasi-regular-immersion-flat-at-x}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $Z \to X$ be a relative quasi-regular immersion.
If $x \in Z$ and $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is Noetherian, then $f$ is flat at $x$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let
$g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$ be the morphism of topoi
associated to a continuous and cocontinuous functor
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u$ has a left adjoint $w$, then $g_!$ agrees with $g_!^{\Sh}$
on underlying sheaves of sets and $g_!$ is exact.
\item If in addition $w$ is cocontinuous, then $g_! = h^{-1}$ and
$g^{-1} = h_*$ where
$h : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ is the morphism of topoi
associated to $w$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: For continuous cocontinuous u:C→D with left adjoint w, g_! agrees with its underlying-set counterpart and is exact; if w also cocontinuous, g_!=h^{-1} and g^{-1}=h_* for the topos morphism h from w. Both tiers and orientations remain.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-have-left-adjoint}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let
$g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$ be the morphism of topoi
associated to a continuous and cocontinuous functor
$u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u$ has a left adjoint $w$, then $g_!$ agrees with $g_!^{\Sh}$
on underlying sheaves of sets and $g_!$ is exact.
\item If in addition $w$ is cocontinuous, then $g_! = h^{-1}$ and
$g^{-1} = h_*$ where
$h : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ is the morphism of topoi
associated to $w$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-integral-morphism}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $j : V \to Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Let $\pi : Z \to V$ be an integral morphism.
Then there exists an integral morphism $\nu : Y' \to Y$ such that
$Z$ is $V$-isomorphic to the inverse image of $V$ in $Y'$.

formulation.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I_i \subset R$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$,
and $J \subset R$ be ideals. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $J \not\subset I_i$ for $i = 1, \ldots, r$, and
\item all but two of $I_i$ are prime ideals.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an $x \in J$, $x\not\in I_i$ for all $i$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The prime-avoidance lemma assumes J⊄I_i for every i and that at most two of the I_i are not prime; it concludes one x∈J avoids all I_i. The proposal retains both nontrivial hypotheses, the finite family, and the simultaneous avoidance conclusion, omitting only the schematic slogan.

phase3.reason: Prime avoidance is proved through two-ideal base cases and a multi-ideal induction replacing x by x+y.

\label{lemma-dimension-specializations-lift}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of topological spaces.
Suppose that $Y$ is a sober topological space, and $f$ is surjective.
If either specializations or generalizations lift along $f$, then
$\dim(X) \geq \dim(Y)$.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category,
$x$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$,
and $f : x \to x$ be idempotent.
Write $g = \text{id} _ x - f$
so that $f\circ g=g\circ f=0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ has kernel $i : \Ker (f) \to x$
and $p$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$,
then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Ker (f)}$
and $p$ is the cokernel of $f$.
\item If $f$ has cokernel $p : x \to \Coker (f)$
and $i$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$,
then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Coker (f)}$
and $i$ is the kernel of $f$.
\item If $g$ has kernel $j : \Ker (g) \to x$
and $q$ is the unique morphism such that $f = j \circ q$,
then $q \circ j = \text{id} _ {\Ker (g)}$
and $q$ is the cokernel of $g$.
\item If $g$ has cokernel $q : x \to \Coker (g)$
and $j$ is the unique morphism such that $f = j \circ q$,
then $q \circ j = \text{id} _ {\Coker (g)}$
and $j$ is the kernel of $g$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-idempotent-kernel-cokernel}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category,
$x$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$,
and $f : x \to x$ be idempotent.
Write $g = \text{id} _ x - f$
and recall by Remark \ref{remark-idempotent-symmetry}
that $f \circ g = g \circ f = 0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ has kernel $i : \Ker (f) \to x$
and $p$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$,
then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Ker (f)}$
and $p$ is the cokernel of $f$.
\item If $f$ has cokernel $p : x \to \Coker (f)$
and $i$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$,
then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Coker (f)}$
and $i$ is the kernel of $f$.
\item If $g$ has kernel $j : \Ker (g) \to x$
and $q$ is the unique morphism such that $f = j \circ q$,
then $q \circ j = \text{id} _ {\Ker (g)}$
and $q$ is the cokernel of $g$.
\item If $g$ has cokernel $q : x \to \Coker (g)$
and $j$ is the unique morphism such that $f = j \circ q$,
then $q \circ j = \text{id} _ {\Coker (g)}$
and $j$ is the kernel of $g$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is reduced,
\item for every $x \in |X|$ the local ring of $X$ at $x$ is
reduced (Remark \ref{remark-list-properties-local-ring-local-etale-topology}).
\end{enumerate}
In this case $\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is a reduced ring and
if $f \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ has $X = V(f)$, then $f = 0$.

\label{lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with enough injectives.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any exact functor $F : K^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \to \mathcal{D}$
into a triangulated category $\mathcal{D}$ the right derived
functor
$$
RF : D^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \longrightarrow \mathcal{D}
$$
is everywhere defined.
\item For any additive functor $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ into an
abelian category $\mathcal{B}$ the right derived functor
$$
RF : D^{+}(\mathcal{A}) \longrightarrow D^{+}(\mathcal{B})
$$
is everywhere defined.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-pushforward-commutes-with-derived-completion}
\begin{reference}
Generalization of \cite[Lemma 6.5.9 (2)]{BS}. Compare with
\cite[Theorem 6.5]{HL-P} in the setting of quasi-coherent modules
and morphisms of (derived) algebraic stacks.
\end{reference}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}') \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$
be a finite type sheaf of ideals. Let $\mathcal{I}' \subset \mathcal{O}'$
be the ideal generated by $f^\sharp(f^{-1}\mathcal{I})$.
Then $Rf_*$ commutes with derived completion, i.e.,
$Rf_*(K^\wedge) = (Rf_*K)^\wedge$.

For a unital map of commutative rings $u:R\to S$, going down means: for every chain $\mathfrak p\subset\mathfrak p^\prime$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$, there exists $\mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p$. Then $\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$ is open.
More generally this holds for any ring map $R \to S$ of
finite presentation which satisfies going down.

source.label: lemma-fundamental-class-almost-lci
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fundamental-class-almost-lci}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $r \geq 0$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is Cohen-Macaulay (Properties, Definition
\ref{properties-definition-Cohen-Macaulay}),
\item $f$ factors as $X \to P \to Y$ where the first morphism is
an immersion and the second is smooth and proper,
\item if $x \in X$ and $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) \leq 1$,
then $f$ is Koszul at $x$ (More on Morphisms, Definition
\ref{more-morphisms-definition-lci}), and
\item if $\xi$ is a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$, then
we have
$\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))} \kappa(\xi) = r$.
\end{enumerate}
Then with $\omega_{X/Y} = H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)$ there is a map
$$
\wedge^r\Omega_{X/Y} \longrightarrow \omega_{X/Y}
$$
which is an isomorphism on the locus where $f$ is smooth.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-separate-disjoint-locally-closed-by-blowing-up}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $U \subset X$ be a quasi-compact open.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Z_1, Z_2 \subset X$ are closed subschemes of finite
presentation such that $Z_1 \cap Z_2 \cap U = \emptyset$, then
there exists a $U$-admissible blowing up $X' \to X$
such that the strict transforms of $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ are disjoint.
\item If $T_1, T_2 \subset U$ are disjoint constructible closed subsets, then
there is a $U$-admissible blowing up $X' \to X$ such that the closures of
$T_1$ and $T_2$ are disjoint.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{slogan}
The henselization of a Noetherian pair is a Noetherian pair
with the same completion
\end{slogan}
Let $(A, I)$ be a pair with $A$ Noetherian.  Let $(A^h, I^h)$ be as in 
Lemma \ref{lemma-henselization}. Then the map of $I$-adic completions
$$
A^\wedge \to (A^h)^\wedge
$$
is an isomorphism. Moreover, $A^h$ is Noetherian, the maps
$A \to A^h \to A^\wedge$ are flat, and $A^h \to A^\wedge$ is
faithfully flat.

Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$.
If $X$ is reduced and $\dim(X) \leq 1$, then there exists
an open immersion $j : X \to \overline{X}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\overline{X}$ is H-projective over $k$, i.e., $\overline{X}$
is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf{P}^d_k$ for some $d$,
\item $j(X) \subset \overline{X}$ is dense and scheme
theoretically dense,
\item $\overline{X} \setminus X = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$
for some closed points $x_i \in \overline{X}$,
\item the local rings $\mathcal{O}_{\overline{X}, x_i}$
are discrete valuation rings for $i = 1, \ldots, n$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-equivalent}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ be categories over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.

stack.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-module-characterize}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$.
\item For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the $\mathcal{O}_S(V)$-module $\mathcal{F}(U)$ is flat.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the modules $\mathcal{F}|_{U_i}$ is
flat over $V_j$, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that $\mathcal{F}(U_i)$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j)$-module, for all
$j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is flat over $V$.

\label{proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. The homotopy category
$K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$ of differential graded $A$-modules with its
natural translation functors and distinguished triangles is a triangulated
category.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Any locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module of rank $1$ is invertible.
If all stalks $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ are local rings, then
the converse holds as well (but in general this is not the case).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-factorization-monic}
Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal. Let $f \in A[x]$ be a
monic polynomial. Let $\overline{f} = \overline{g} \overline{h}$ be a
factorization of $f$ in $A/I[x]$ such that $\overline{g}$ and $\overline{h}$
are monic and generate the unit ideal in $A/I[x]$. Then there exists an
\'etale ring map $A \to A'$ which induces an isomorphism $A/I \to A'/IA'$
and a factorization $f = g' h'$ in $A'[x]$ with $g'$, $h'$ monic
lifting the given factorization over $A/I$.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

\label{lemma-decent-no-specializations-map-to-same-point}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Let $U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism from a scheme to $X$.
If $u, u' \in |U|$ map to the same point of $|X|$, and
$u' \leadsto u$, then $u = u'$.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$, $\mathcal{F}$ be finite locally free sheaves
on $X$ of ranks $r$, $r - 1$ which fit into a short
exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{O}_X \to \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{F} \to 0
$$
Then we have
$$
c_r(\mathcal{E}) = 0, \quad
c_j(\mathcal{E}) = c_j(\mathcal{F}), \quad j = 0, \ldots, r - 1
$$
in $A^*(X)$.

\label{lemma-get-rid-of-trivial-subbundle}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$, $\mathcal{F}$ be finite locally free sheaves
on $X$ of ranks $r$, $r - 1$ which fit into a short
exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{O}_X \to \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{F} \to 0
$$
Then we have
$$
c_r(\mathcal{E}) = 0, \quad
c_j(\mathcal{E}) = c_j(\mathcal{F}), \quad j = 0, \ldots, r - 1
$$
in $A^*(X)$.

\label{lemma-presheaf-mor-map-fibred-categories}
Let $F : \mathcal{S}_1 \to \mathcal{S}_2$ be a $1$-morphism of fibred
categories over the category $\mathcal{C}$. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
and $x, y\in \Ob((\mathcal{S}_1)_U)$. Then $F$ defines a canonical
morphism of presheaves
$$
\mathit{Mor}_{\mathcal{S}_1}(x, y)
\longrightarrow
\mathit{Mor}_{\mathcal{S}_2}(F(x), F(y))
$$
on $\mathcal{C}/U$.

\label{lemma-apply-Mittag-Leffler}
Let
$$
(A_i) \to (B_i) \to (C_i) \to (D_i)
$$
be an exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups. If the
system $(A_i)$ is ML, then the sequence
$$
\lim_i B_i \to \lim_i C_i \to \lim_i D_i
$$
is exact.
