source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ is smooth.
Then the module of differentials $\Omega_{X/S}$ of $X$ over $S$
is finite locally free and
$$
\text{rank}_x(\Omega_{X/S}) = \dim_x(X_{f(x)})
$$
for every $x \in X$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Suppose $X$ is a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$ be a closed point. Then $x$ can be represented by a
closed immersion $i : \operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ from the spectrum of a field.

phase3.reason: On an affine étale chart, fibres over the closed point consist of closed points; the field mono pulls back to finitely many field charts mapping as closed immersions, descending closedness to X.

Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A scheme morphism is **étale** if it is flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified, equivalently smooth of relative dimension zero. A map $A\to B$ is **standard étale** if $B\simeq(A[t]/(f))_g$, with $f\in A[t]$ monic, $g\in A[t]$ and $f'(t)$ invertible in $B$. A map $A\to B$ is étale **at** $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ if $A\to B_h$ is étale for some $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. An étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has étale maps and jointly surjective images.
formulation.statement:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A scheme morphism is **étale** if it is flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified, equivalently smooth of relative dimension zero. A map $A\to B$ is **standard étale** if $B\simeq(A[t]/(f))_g$, with $f\in A[t]$ monic, $g\in A[t]$ and $f'(t)$ invertible in $B$. A map $A\to B$ is étale **at** $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ if $A\to B_h$ is étale for some $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. An étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has étale maps and jointly surjective images.

A ring map $A \to B$ is \'etale at a prime $\mathfrak q$ if and only if there
exists $g \in B$, $g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that $B_g$ is standard
\'etale over $A$.

**Precise scope:** The element g avoids q and **localizes B**, not A; B_g is standard étale as defined. The two local conditions are equivalent for arbitrary ring maps and primes of B.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The chapter defines standard étale as (A[t]/(f))_g for monic f with f′ invertible. The theorem correctly equates étaleness at q with a localization B_g, g∉q, of that form.

phase3.reason: The source directly cites the Algebra proposition that an étale morphism of rings is locally standard étale at a prime, matching localization in B at g∉q rather than localization in A.

\label{theorem-standard-etale}
A ring map $A \to B$ is \'etale at a prime $\mathfrak q$ if and only if there
exists $g \in B$, $g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that $B_g$ is standard
\'etale over $A$.

formulation.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $T \subset X$ be finite set of points. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ has finitely many irreducible components $Z_1, \ldots, Z_t$, and
\item $Z_i \cap T$ is contained in an affine open of the reduced
induced subscheme corresponding to $Z_i$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an affine open subscheme of $X$ containing $T$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian and universally catenary scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ such that $X$ is decent
and such that the structure morphism $X \to S$ is locally of
finite type. Then $X$ is catenary.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universally-catenary-scheme}
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian and universally catenary scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ such that $X$ is decent
and such that the structure morphism $X \to S$ is locally of
finite type. Then $X$ is catenary.

Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $S = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a graded polynomial algebra over $R$,
i.e., $\deg(x_i) > 0$ but not necessarily equal to $1$.
Let $M$ be a graded $S$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a local ring,
\item $M$ is a finite $S$-module, and
\item $M$ is flat over $R$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $M$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module.

source.label: lemma-flat-graded-finite-type-finite-presentation-module
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-graded-finite-type-finite-presentation-module}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $S = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a graded polynomial algebra over $R$,
i.e., $\deg(x_i) > 0$ but not necessarily equal to $1$.
Let $M$ be a graded $S$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a local ring,
\item $M$ is a finite $S$-module, and
\item $M$ is flat over $R$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $M$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module.

\label{lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Then we have
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}}(M, A^\vee[k]) =
\Ker(\text{d} : (M^\vee)^k \to (M^\vee)^{k + 1})

and
$$
\Hom_{K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})}(M, A^\vee[k]) = H^k(M^\vee)
$$
as functors in the differential graded $A$-module $M$.

source.label: lemma-left-dual-module
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-left-dual-module}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $\mathcal{G}, \eta, \epsilon$
be a left dual of $\mathcal{F}$ in the monoidal category of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-dual}. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is locally a direct summand of a finite free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
\item the map
$e : \SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{O}_X) \to \mathcal{G}$
sending a local section $\lambda$ to $(\lambda \otimes 1)(\eta)$
is an isomorphism,
\item we have $\epsilon(f, g) = e^{-1}(g)(f)$ for local sections
$f$ and $g$ of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: The original sheaf is finite locally free.
hypotheses: Every fpqc pullback is finite locally free.
formulation.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering. If every pullback $f_i^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally free (locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_i}^{\oplus n}$ for some finite $n$), then $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free on $X$. Here no conclusion about arbitrary-rank locally free modules is asserted.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L2004–2010 says finite locally free property for a QUASI-COHERENT sheaf F DESCENDS through an FPQC cover of scheme X. The proposal preserves 'finite' in finite locally free, not an unsupported claim about locally free of unbounded rank.

phase3.reason: A finite locally free sheaf is finite presented and flat, both of which descend by earlier lemmas.

source.label: lemma-finite-locally-free-descends
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-locally-free-descends}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be an fpqc covering such that
each $f_i^*\mathcal{F}$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_{X_i}$-module.
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-points-in-affine}
Let $f : T \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $X^0$, resp.\ $T^0$
denote the sets of generic points of irreducible components.
Let $t_1, \ldots, t_m \in T$ be a finite set of points
with images $x_j = f(t_j)$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ is affine,
\item $X$ is quasi-separated,
\item $X^0$ is finite
\item $f(T^0) \subset X^0$ and $f : T^0 \to X^0$ is injective, and
\item $\mathcal{O}_{X, x_j} = \mathcal{O}_{T, t_j}$,
\end{enumerate}
then there exists an affine open of $X$ containing $x_1, \ldots, x_r$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-weak-bourbaki}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map which is essentially of finite type.
Let $N$ be a localization of a finite $S$-module flat over $R$.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Then
$$
\text{WeakAss}_S(M \otimes_R N)
=
\bigcup\nolimits_{\mathfrak p \in \text{WeakAss}_R(M)}
\text{Ass}_{S \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)}(N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p))
$$

\label{lemma-product-graded-injective}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.

on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Let $T$ be a set and for

graded $\mathcal{A}$-module.

source.label: lemma-subsheaf-of-constant-sheaf
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-subsheaf-of-constant-sheaf}
\begin{reference}
\cite[Page 168]{Tohoku}.
\end{reference}
Let $X$ be a topological space such that the intersection of any
two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. Let
$\mathcal{F} \subset \underline{\mathbf{Z}}$
be a subsheaf generated by finitely many sections over quasi-compact opens.
Then there exists a finite filtration
$$
(0) = \mathcal{F}_0 \subset \mathcal{F}_1 \subset \ldots \subset
\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}
$$
by abelian subsheaves such that for each $0 < i \leq n$
there exists a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to j'_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}}_V \to j_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}}_U \to
\mathcal{F}_i/\mathcal{F}_{i - 1} \to 0
$$
with $j : U \to X$ and $j' : V \to X$ the inclusion of quasi-compact opens
into $X$.

hypotheses: $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a finitely presented closed immersion with locally free conormal of rank $c$, and $\gamma^p$ is its canonical Gysin map.
formulation.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.

For all $p\geq0$, the canonical global Gysin maps $\gamma^p$ commute with exterior differentiation: the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\Omega^p_{Z/S}&\xrightarrow{\gamma^p}&\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})\\
\downarrow d&&\downarrow d\\
\Omega^{p+1}_{Z/S}&\xrightarrow{\gamma^{p+1}}&\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c+1}_{X/S})\end{array}$$
commutes.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L5290–5294 imports precisely the setting of the GLOBAL Gysin lemma: finitely presented closed immersion with locally free conormal rank c. It asserts commutation of global γ^p with de Rham DIFFERENTIAL; the proposed square preserves both p↦p+1 and shifted target form degree p+c.

phase3.reason: The canonical global construction is local on X, where its defining fractions are the local Gysin maps; their differential compatibility was proved in the preceding lemma, so the global maps form a chain map.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $n \geq m$. Let $A$ be an
$n \times m$ matrix with coefficients in $R$. Let $J \subset R$
be the ideal generated by the $m \times m$ minors of $A$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $f \in J$ there exists a $m \times n$ matrix $B$
such that $BA = f 1_{m \times m}$.
\item If $f \in R$ and $BA = f 1_{m \times m}$ for some $m \times n$ matrix
$B$, then $f^m \in J$.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ss-converges-trivial}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a
filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every $n$ there exist $p_0(n)$ such that
$H^n(F^pK^\bullet) = 0$ for $p \geq p_0(n)$,
\item for every $n$ there exist $p_1(n)$ such that
$H^n(F^pK^\bullet) \to H^n(K^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism
for $p \leq p_1(n)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the spectral sequence associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$ is bounded,
\item the filtration on each $H^n(K^\bullet)$ is finite,
\item the spectral sequence associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$ converges
to $H^*(K^\bullet)$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
and denote $\mathcal{F}^a$ the associated quasi-coherent sheaf
on the small \'etale site of $X$

\item $H^q_Z(X, \mathcal{F})$ agrees with $H^q_Z(X_\etale, \mathcal{F}^a)$,
\item if the complement of $Z$ is retrocompact in $X$, then
$i_*\mathcal{H}^q_Z(\mathcal{F}^a)$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules equal to $(i_*\mathcal{H}^q_Z(\mathcal{F}))^a$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, including unbounded $K$, the canonical projection-comparison morphism
\[
Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_f(K)
\]
is an isomorphism. This requires perfect properness, but not flatness.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes of finite presentation.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$ and $(\mathcal{F}_s)_x$ is a flat
$\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}$-module, then $\mathcal{F}$
is finite free in a neighbourhood of $x$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-periodic-determinant-sign}
Let $R$ be a local ring with residue field $\kappa$.
Let $(M, \varphi, \varphi)$ be a $(2, 1)$-periodic complex over $R$.
Assume that $M$ has finite length and that $(M, \varphi, \varphi)$ is
exact. Then $\text{length}_R(M) = 2 \text{length}_R(\Im(\varphi))$
and
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M, \varphi, \varphi)
=
(-1)^{\text{length}_R(\Im(\varphi))}
=
(-1)^{\frac{1}{2}\text{length}_R(M)}
$$

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian and universally catenary scheme.
Let $\delta : S \to \mathbf{Z}$ be a dimension function.
Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$ such that
the structure morphism $X \to S$ is locally of
finite type. Let $\delta_X : |X| \to \mathbf{Z}$ be the map
sending $x$ to $\delta(f(x))$ plus the transcendence degree
of $x/f(x)$. Then $\delta_X$ is a dimension function on $|X|$.

source.label: lemma-scheme-with-dimension-function
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-scheme-with-dimension-function}
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian and universally catenary scheme.
Let $\delta : S \to \mathbf{Z}$ be a dimension function.
Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$ such that
the structure morphism $X \to S$ is locally of
finite type. Let $\delta_X : |X| \to \mathbf{Z}$ be the map
sending $x$ to $\delta(f(x))$ plus the transcendence degree
of $x/f(x)$. Then $\delta_X$ is a dimension function on $|X|$.

formulation.statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X\to X'$ be an $S$-morphism. Assume the structure map $X\to S$ is surjective and flat. Then pullback $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ is faithful, even without requiring $f$ itself to be surjective or flat.

The proposal correctly does not require f to be flat or surjective, distinguishes f from X→S, and does not strengthen faithful to fully faithful.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-source-faithfully-flat}
Let $f : X \to X'$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Assume $X \to S$ is surjective and flat. Then the pullback functor
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback} is a faithful functor
from the category of descent data relative to $X'/S$ to the
category of descent data relative to $X/S$.

\label{lemma-lift-once}
Let $R \to \Lambda$ be a ring map. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I^2 = 0$, and
\item $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/I$-algebras.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\varphi : A \to \Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra map with $A$ of finite
presentation over $R$. Then there exists a factorization
$$
A \to B/J \to \Lambda
$$
where $B$ is a smooth $R$-algebra and $J \subset IB$ is a finitely generated
ideal.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

If $X$ has a $\mathfrak g^r_d$, then $X$ has a $\mathfrak g^s_d$ for
all $0 \leq s \leq r$.

formulation.statement:
A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring. Let $M$ be an $A$-module.
Let $B = A \oplus M$ as an $A$-algebra where $M$ is an ideal of square zero
and set $J = I \oplus M$. Set
$$
\delta_n(x + z) = \gamma_n(x) + \gamma_{n - 1}(x)z
$$
for $x \in I$ and $z \in M$.
Then $\delta$ is a divided power structure and
$A \to B$ is a homomorphism of divided power rings from
$(A, I, \gamma)$ to $(B, J, \delta)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: The square-zero extension B=A⊕M with J=I⊕M carries the divided power δ_n(x+z)=γ_n(x)+γ_{n−1}(x)z, and the inclusion A→B is a divided-power map. Both the formula and compatibility conclusion are unchanged.

\label{lemma-divided-power-first-order-thickening}
Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring. Let $M$ be an $A$-module.
Let $B = A \oplus M$ as an $A$-algebra where $M$ is an ideal of square zero
and set $J = I \oplus M$. Set
$$
\delta_n(x + z) = \gamma_n(x) + \gamma_{n - 1}(x)z
$$
for $x \in I$ and $z \in M$.
Then $\delta$ is a divided power structure and
$A \to B$ is a homomorphism of divided power rings from
$(A, I, \gamma)$ to $(B, J, \delta)$.

\label{lemma-ML-general-better}
Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $X$ be a topological space. Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of $A$-modules on $X$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Given $n$ define
$$
N_n =
\bigcap\nolimits_{m \geq n}
\Im\left(
H^{p + 1}(X, I^n\mathcal{F}_{m + 1}) \to H^{p + 1}(X, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
\right)
$$
If $\bigoplus N_n$ satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module, then the inverse system
$M_n = H^p(X, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the Mittag-Leffler
condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image
for all $n \geq c$.}.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-differentials}
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$.
Then there is a canonical identification
$f^{-1}\Omega_{\mathcal{O}_2/\mathcal{O}_1} =
\Omega_{f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_2/f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_1}$
compatible with universal derivations.

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.
formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is smooth,
\item $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$,
\item $k(X)/k(Y)$ is purely inseparable.
\end{enumerate}
Then $Y$ is smooth, $H^0(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) = k$, and the genus of $Y$
is equal to the genus of $X$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Given X smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=k and k(X)/k(Y) purely inseparable, the target Y is smooth, has H⁰(O_Y)=k and the same genus. All three conclusions and all source premises are retained.

phase3.reason: Identifies Y with the n-fold Frobenius base change of X, preserving smoothness and constant-field/cohomology/genus by the previously established base-change theorem.

\label{lemma-purely-inseparable-smooth-genus}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is smooth,
\item $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$,
\item $k(X)/k(Y)$ is purely inseparable.
\end{enumerate}
Then $Y$ is smooth, $H^0(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) = k$, and the genus of $Y$
is equal to the genus of $X$.

\label{lemma-point-finite-type-monomorphism}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is a finite type point,
\item there exists an algebraic space $Z$ whose underlying topological space
$|Z|$ is a singleton, and a morphism $f : Z \to X$ which is locally of finite
type such that $\{x\} = |f|(|Z|)$, and
\item there exists an algebraic space $Z$ and a morphism $f : Z \to X$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item there is a surjective \'etale morphism
$z : \Spec(k) \to Z$ where $k$ is a field,
\item $f$ is locally of finite type,
\item $f$ is a monomorphism, and
\item $x = f(z)$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-acyclic-general
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclic-general}
Let $H : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{A}$ be a homological functor from a
triangulated category $\mathcal{D}$ to an abelian category $\mathcal{A}$, see
Definition \ref{definition-homological}.
The subcategory $\Ker(H)$ of $\mathcal{D}$ is a strictly full
saturated triangulated subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$ whose corresponding
saturated multiplicative system (see
Lemma \ref{lemma-operations})
is the set
$$
S = \{f \in \text{Arrows}(\mathcal{D}) \mid
H^i(f)\text{ is an isomorphism for all }i \in \mathbf{Z}\}.
$$
The functor $H$ factors through the quotient functor
$Q : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}/\Ker(H)$.

formulation.statement:
All rings are commutative with identity and all ring maps preserve identity. For $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$, write $\widetilde M$ for the associated sheaf of a graded module, $M(n)_j=M_{n+j}$, $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{A(n)}$, and $\mathcal F(n)=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(n)$. Choose finitely many positive-degree homogeneous generators $f_i$ of $A$ over $A_0$, and put $d=\operatorname{lcm}_i\deg(f_i)$ (empty lcm $1$). Let $\operatorname{Gr}^{fg}(A)$ consist of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-graded $A$-modules with degree-zero maps. Let $\mathcal I$ be the Serre subcategory of modules with $M_{nd}=0$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$; equivalently every homogeneous element $x$ satisfies $(A_+x)_{nd}=0$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This is the source-specific notion of irrelevant module, not the degree-one torsion category. Let $A$ be a Noetherian graded ring. Set $X = \text{Proj}(A)$. The functor
$M \mapsto \widetilde M$ induces an equivalence
$$
\operatorname{Gr}^{fg}(A)/\mathcal I
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
whose quasi-inverse is given by
$\mathcal{F} \longmapsto \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}(n))$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-coherent-modules-on-proj-general}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian graded ring. Set $X = \text{Proj}(A)$. The functor
$M \mapsto \widetilde M$ induces an equivalence
$$
\text{Mod}^{fg}_A/\text{Mod}^{fg}_{A, irrelevant}
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
whose quasi-inverse is given by
$\mathcal{F} \longmapsto \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}(n))$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-construct-profinite}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $X = \Spec(A)$. Let $T$ be a profinite space and
let $T \to \pi_0(X)$ be a continuous map. There exists an
ind-Zariski ring map $A \to B$ such that with $Y = \Spec(B)$ the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & \pi_0(Y) \ar[d] \\
X \ar[r] & \pi_0(X)
}
$$
is cartesian in the category of topological spaces and such that
$\pi_0(Y) = T$ as spaces over $\pi_0(X)$.

conclusions: The $\mathcal I$-adic completion functor $\textit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\longrightarrow\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I),\quad\mathcal E\longmapsto(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$ is exact.
hypotheses: Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
formulation.statement:
Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
The $\mathcal I$-adic completion functor $\textit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\longrightarrow\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I),\quad\mathcal E\longmapsto(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$ is exact.

source.label: lemma-cohomology-of-neighbourhoods-of-closed
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-of-neighbourhoods-of-closed}
Let $X$ be a spectral space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $X$.
Let $E \subset X$ be a quasi-compact subset. Let $W \subset X$ be the set of
points of $X$ which specialize to a point of $E$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(W, \mathcal{F}|_W) = \colim H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$
where the colimit is over quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of $E$,
\item $H^p(W \setminus E, \mathcal{F}|_{W \setminus E}) =
\colim H^p(U \setminus E, \mathcal{F}|_{U \setminus E})$
if $E$ is a constructible subset.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-colim-hocolim}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $L_n^\bullet$
be a system of complexes of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume
colimits over $\mathbf{N}$ exist and are exact in $\mathcal{A}$.
Then the termwise
colimit $L^\bullet = \colim L_n^\bullet$ is a homotopy colimit of the
system in $D(\mathcal{A})$.

be a fibred category. Let $\text{Cov}(\mathcal{S})$
be the set of families $\{x_i \to x\}_{i \in I}$ of morphisms in $\mathcal{S}$
with fixed target such that (a) each $x_i \to x$ is strongly cartesian,
and (b) $\{p(x_i) \to p(x)\}_{i \in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $(\mathcal{S}, \text{Cov}(\mathcal{S}))$ is a site.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-integral-no-inclusion}
Suppose $R \to S$ is integral.
Let $\mathfrak q, \mathfrak q' \in \Spec(S)$
be distinct primes
having the same image in $\Spec(R)$.
Then neither $\mathfrak q \subset \mathfrak q'$
nor $\mathfrak q' \subset \mathfrak q$.

\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-local}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism which is locally of finite presentation.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type.
If $x \in X$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$, then
$\mathcal{F}_x$ is an $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module of finite presentation.

\label{lemma-smooth-induced}
Let $\Sch_{smooth}$ be a big smooth site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-smooth-site}.
Let $T \in \Ob(\Sch_{smooth})$.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be an arbitrary smooth covering of $T$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a covering $\{U_j \to T\}_{j \in J}$ of $T$ in the site
$\Sch_{smooth}$ which refines $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ is a standard smooth covering, then
it is tautologically equivalent to a covering of $\Sch_{smooth}$.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ is a Zariski covering, then
it is tautologically equivalent to a covering of $\Sch_{smooth}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-pi0-profinite}
Let $X$ be a topological space. If $X$ is quasi-compact
and every connected component of $X$ is the intersection
of the open and closed subsets containing it, then $\pi_0(X)$
is a profinite space.

formulation.statement: Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. There exists an integer $N$ depending only on $f$ such that for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and integer $c$, if $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\le c$, then $H^i(a_f(K))=0$ for every $i\le c-N$. In particular $a_f$ carries $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ into $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$.

Final preserves the direction and uniformity of this shift, and does NOT confuse bounded-below with bounded-above.

\label{lemma-twisted-inverse-image-bounded-below}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes. Let $a : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}.
Then $a$ maps $D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ into $D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
In fact, there exists an integer $N$ such that
$H^i(K) = 0$ for $i \leq c$ implies $H^i(a(K)) = 0$ for $i \leq c - N$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be locally of finite type. Let $y \in Y$ be a point
such that $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is Noetherian of dimension $\leq 1$.
Assume in addition one of the following conditions is satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component
of $X$ the field extension $\kappa(\eta)/\kappa(f(\eta))$
is finite (or algebraic),
\item for every generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component
of $X$ such that $f(\eta) \leadsto y$ the field extension
$\kappa(\eta)/\kappa(f(\eta))$ is finite (or algebraic),
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at every generic point of an
irreducible component of $X$,
\item $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $f$
is quasi-finite at a dense set of points of $X$,
\item add more here.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is quasi-finite at every point of $X$ lying over $y$.

phase3.reason: Polynomial presentations identify flat algebra lifts with flat module lifts; completion and local syntomic lifting give the required comparison.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-equivalence}
Let $A' \to A$ be a surjective map of Noetherian rings with nilpotent kernel.
Let $A \to B$ be a finite type flat ring map.
Let $\mathfrak b \subset B$ be an ideal such that
$\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$ is syntomic on the complement of $V(\mathfrak b)$.
Then $B$ has a flat lift to $A'$ if and only if the $\mathfrak b$-adic
completion $B^\wedge$ has a flat lift to $A'$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be continuous map of topological spaces.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is separated,
\item $\Delta(X) \subset X \times_Y X$ is a closed subset,
\item given distinct points $x, x' \in X$ mapping to the same point of
$Y$, there exist disjoint open neighbourhoods of $x$ and $x'$.
\end{enumerate}

phase3.reason: All three implications are demonstrated: separatedness gives a closed relative diagonal, its closed complement yields disjoint neighbourhoods of equal-fibre points, and those neighbourhoods imply the diagonal is a closed map.

For a ringed site (C,O), RSheafHom(L,M) is the internal derived Hom in D(O), contravariant in the first variable and covariant in the second. It may be represented by SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet,I^bullet) for any representative L^bullet of L and a **K-injective** representative I^bullet of M; equivalently it is right adjoint to −⊗^L_O L (source lines 8839–8869). Derived tensor uses K-flat replacements; the notation F|_U denotes exact restriction to the slice site C/U.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Given $K, L, M$
in $D(\mathcal{O})$ there is a canonical morphism
$$
K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} R\SheafHom(M, L)
\longrightarrow
R\SheafHom(M, K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} L)
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O})$ functorial in $K, L, M$.

Let $A$ be a ring. Set $X = \Spec(A)$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a locally closed
subscheme which is of the form $D(f) \cap V(I)$ for some $f \in A$ and
ideal $I \subset A$. Then

$\Spec(S^{-1}A)$ maps by a homeomorphism to the set of points of $X$
specializing to $Z$,
\item the $A$-algebra $A_Z^\sim = S^{-1}A$ depends only on
the underlying locally closed subset $Z \subset X$,
\item $Z$ is a closed subscheme of $\Spec(A_Z^\sim)$,
\end{enumerate}

locally closed subscheme of the same form which maps into $Z$,

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localization}
Let $A$ be a ring. Set $X = \Spec(A)$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a locally closed
subscheme which is of the form $D(f) \cap V(I)$ for some $f \in A$ and
ideal $I \subset A$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a multiplicative subset $S \subset A$ such that
$\Spec(S^{-1}A)$ maps by a homeomorphism to the set of points of $X$
specializing to $Z$,
\item the $A$-algebra $A_Z^\sim = S^{-1}A$ depends only on
the underlying locally closed subset $Z \subset X$,
\item $Z$ is a closed subscheme of $\Spec(A_Z^\sim)$,
\end{enumerate}
If $A \to A'$ is a ring map and $Z' \subset X' = \Spec(A')$ is a
locally closed subscheme of the same form which maps into $Z$,
then there is a unique $A$-algebra map
$A_Z^\sim \to (A')_{Z'}^\sim$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-presentation-stalk-free}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be
a finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $x \in X$ such that
$\mathcal{F}_x \cong \mathcal{O}_{X, x}^{\oplus r}$. Then there exists
an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that
$\mathcal{F}|_U \cong \mathcal{O}_U^{\oplus r}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme all of whose local rings are Noetherian of dimension
$\leq 1$. Let $U \subset X$ be a retrocompact open. Denote
$j : U \to X$ the inclusion morphism. Then $R^pj_*\mathcal{F} = 0$, $p > 0$
for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module $\mathcal{F}$.

\label{lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-of-partial-section}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated morphism of schemes.
Let $V \subset Y$ be a retrocompact open. Let $s : V \to X$
be a morphism such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_V$.
Let $Y'$ be the scheme theoretic image of $s$.
Then $Y' \to Y$ is an isomorphism over $V$.

Let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of abelian groups. Let
$$
\ldots \to A_2^\bullet \to A_1^\bullet \to A_0^\bullet \to M^\bullet \to 0
$$
be an exact complex of complexes of abelian groups such that for all
$p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the complexes
$$
\ldots \to \Ker(d_{A_2^\bullet}^p) \to \Ker(d_{A_1^\bullet}^p)
\to \Ker(d_{A_0^\bullet}^p) \to \Ker(d_{M^\bullet}^p) \to 0
$$
are exact as well. Set $A^{p, q} = A_{-p}^q$ to obtain a double
complex. Then $\text{Tot}(A^{\bullet, \bullet}) \to M^\bullet$
induced by $A_0^\bullet \to M^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis}
Let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of abelian groups. Let
$$
\ldots \to A_2^\bullet \to A_1^\bullet \to A_0^\bullet \to M^\bullet \to 0
$$
be an exact complex of complexes of abelian groups such that for all
$p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the complexes
$$
\ldots \to \Ker(d_{A_2^\bullet}^p) \to \Ker(d_{A_1^\bullet}^p)
\to \Ker(d_{A_0^\bullet}^p) \to \Ker(d_{M^\bullet}^p) \to 0
$$
are exact as well. Set $A^{p, q} = A_{-p}^q$ to obtain a double
complex. Then $\text{Tot}(A^{\bullet, \bullet}) \to M^\bullet$
induced by $A_0^\bullet \to M^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.

\label{lemma-closed-immersion-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is a closed immersion (resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion),
\item for every scheme $Z$ and any morphism $Z \to Y$ the morphism
$Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a closed immersion (resp.\ open immersion,
resp.\ immersion),
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and any morphism
$Z \to Y$ the morphism $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion),
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion), and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is a closed immersion
(resp.\ open immersion, resp.\ immersion).
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a characteristic-$p$ ring $A$ ($p$ prime), the Frobenius endomorphism is $F_A(a)=a^p$. Given a characteristic-$p$ ring map $A\to B$, its Frobenius square $(F_A,F_B)$ induces maps on the functorial simplicial standard resolution $P_\bullet$ and the cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$; these maps are generally semilinear over $B$ under $F_B$. A homotopy of simplicial maps means simplicial homotopy, and a chain homotopy on a complex induces the same map in its derived category.

Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism
and assume that $p = 0$ in $A$. The map $L_{B/A} \to L_{B/A}$
induced by the natural Frobenius square of ring maps induced by the
Frobenius maps $F_A$ and $F_B$ is homotopic to zero.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L1800–1806 assumes prime p, characteristic p for A (hence also B), and Frobenius maps F_A and F_B inducing the functorial endomorphism on cotangent complexes. The result says that induced map is HOMOTOPIC TO ZERO, not necessarily literally the zero map in each resolution degree. The reconstruction restores the prior functoriality context, preserves semilinearity and the homotopy-level conclusion.

phase3.reason: The homotopy comparison of two Frobenius actions and the zero derivative of pth powers prove Frobenius acts trivially on cotangent complexes.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-after-blowing-up}
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $U \subset S$ be a quasi-compact open.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to S$ is of finite type and quasi-separated, and
\item $X_U \to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $S' \to S$ such that
the strict transform of $X$ is flat and of finite presentation
over $S'$.

\label{lemma-pushforward-perfect}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $j : U \to X$ be an
open subspace. Let $E$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$
whose cohomology
sheaves are supported on a closed subset $T \subset U$ with $j(T)$
closed in $X$. Then $Rj_*E$ is a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

phase3.reason: Inducts on length of a local strictly perfect representative, splits its top finite-free cohomology and shortens the complex.

source.label: lemma-perfect-max-open-coh-loc-free
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-perfect-max-open-coh-loc-free}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $E$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be perfect. Assume that all stalks $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ are local rings.
Then the set
$$
U =
\{x \in X \mid
H^i(E)_x\text{ is a finite free }
\mathcal{O}_{X, x}\text{-module for all }i\in \mathbf{Z}\}
$$
is open in $X$ and is the maximal open set $U \subset X$ such that
$H^i(E)|_U$ is finite locally free for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.

source.label: lemma-injective-trivial-cech-variant
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-trivial-cech-variant}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with equalizers and fibre products.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $\mathcal{G}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal{C}$.
Then
$$
\check{H}^p(K, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
H^0(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{I}) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$

Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be an exact functor.
Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory

source.label: lemma-quotient-by-kernel-exact-functor
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quotient-by-kernel-exact-functor}
Let $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be an exact functor.
Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory
contained in the kernel of $F$.
Then $\mathcal{C} = \Ker(F)$ if and only if the induced functor
$\overline{F} : \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{B}$
(Lemma \ref{lemma-serre-subcategory-is-kernel}) is faithful.

Let $I$ be a differential graded $A$-module with property (I).

$$
\Hom_{K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})}(N, I) = 0
$$
for all acyclic differential graded $A$-modules $N$.

phase3.reason: Uses the complete descending property-(I) filtration and its distinguished triangle to reduce homotopy maps from acyclic N to maps into the finite quotients. phase3.reason: Every clopen subset of the continuous image has clopen preimage in the connected domain, so the image has no nontrivial clopen partition.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-image-connected-space}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
If $E \subset X$ is a connected subset, then $f(E) \subset Y$
is connected as well.

formulation.statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base, and let $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fpqc},\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic}\}$. Say that *morphisms of type $\mathcal P$ satisfy descent for $\tau$-coverings* if, for every $\tau$-covering $\{U_i\to S\}$, every scheme descent datum $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ with each $X_i\to U_i$ having $\mathcal P$ is effective, i.e. isomorphic to the canonical pullback descent datum of some $S$-scheme.

Suppose (1) $\mathcal P$ is preserved by arbitrary base change; (2) $\mathcal P$ is preserved by finite disjoint unions of morphisms, so that if $Y_j\to V_j$ have $\mathcal P$ for $1\leq j\leq m$, then $\coprod_jY_j\to\coprod_jV_j$ has $\mathcal P$; and (3) for each surjective map of affine schemes $X\to S$ of the corresponding class—flat for fpqc, flat and of finite presentation for fppf, étale for étale, smooth for smooth, and syntomic for syntomic—every descent datum $(V,\varphi)$ for $X/S$ with $V\to X$ having $\mathcal P$ is effective. Then morphisms of type $\mathcal P$ satisfy descent for all $\tau$-coverings. This asserts effectivity of the descent datum; the definition does not separately assert that its descended morphism has $\mathcal P$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L9027 provides a reduction lemma for EFFECTIVITY of descent data of morphisms with property P. The proposal retains arbitrary-base-change stability, FINITE disjoint-union stability, and effectivity for single surjective affine tau-type covers, then concludes effectivity for all tau-coverings. The preceding source definition of 'morphisms of type P satisfy descent' indeed means effectiveness, not an extra requirement that the eventual descended morphism have P.

phase3.reason: The detailed proof reduces a τ-cover to a finite standard affine refinement on each affine base, applies the affine descent hypothesis after disjoint union, then descends local realizations on affine opens and glues using full faithfulness. Some routine cocycle verification is omitted but the main construction is explicit.

source.label: lemma-descending-types-morphisms
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-types-morphisms}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base.
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, \etale, smooth, syntomic\}$.
Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is stable under any base change
(see Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-preserved-by-base-change}),
\item if $Y_j \to V_j$, $j = 1, \ldots, m$ have $\mathcal{P}$,
then so does $\coprod Y_j \to \coprod V_j$, and
\item for any surjective morphism of affines
$X \to S$ which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
any descent datum $(V, \varphi)$ relative
to $X$ over $S$ such that $\mathcal{P}$ holds for
$V \to X$ is effective.
\end{enumerate}
Then morphisms of type $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy descent for $\tau$-coverings.

formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $K,L\in D(A)$. Suppose all cohomology modules of $K$ are finitely generated and $L$ has finite injective dimension (i.e. it is represented by a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules). Write $\widetilde K,\widetilde L$ for the associated quasi-coherent complexes on $X$. Then the canonical morphism
\[
\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)}\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\widetilde K,\widetilde L)
\]
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. There is no perfectness or finite-Tor-dimension assumption on $K$ beyond the stated coherent cohomology.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L148 assumes A Noetherian, K∈D_Coh(A) and L of FINITE INJECTIVE DIMENSION. It identifies derived internal Hom of sheafifications with sheafified RHom_A(K,L). The proposal retains unbounded coherent K, finite injective L, and the canonical comparison direction; it does not wrongly require K to be perfect.

phase3.reason: Reduction to an injective module plus localization of Ext and finite-generation of cohomology identifies affine RHom with sheaf RHom.

source.label: lemma-affine-duality
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-duality}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $X = \Spec(A)$. Let $K, L$ be objects
of $D(A)$. If $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$ and $L$ has finite injective
dimension, then
$$
R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\widetilde{K}, \widetilde{L})
=
\widetilde{R\Hom_A(K, L)}
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $n \geq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally
free $\mathcal{O}_S$-module of constant rank $n + 1$.
Consider the structure morphism
$$
\pi : \mathbf{P}(\mathcal{E}) \longrightarrow S.
$$
We have
$$
R^q\pi_*(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{E})}(d)) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\text{Sym}^d(\mathcal{E}) & \text{if} & q = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & q \not = 0, n \\
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_S}(
\text{Sym}^{- n - 1 - d}(\mathcal{E})
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S}
\wedge^{n + 1}\mathcal{E},
\mathcal{O}_S)
& \text{if} & q = n
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
These identifications are compatible with base change and
isomorphism between locally free sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-projective-bundle}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $n \geq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally
free $\mathcal{O}_S$-module of constant rank $n + 1$.
Consider the structure morphism
$$
\pi : \mathbf{P}(\mathcal{E}) \longrightarrow S.
$$
We have
$$
R^q\pi_*(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{E})}(d)) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\text{Sym}^d(\mathcal{E}) & \text{if} & q = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & q \not = 0, n \\
\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_S}(
\text{Sym}^{- n - 1 - d}(\mathcal{E})
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S}
\wedge^{n + 1}\mathcal{E},
\mathcal{O}_S)
& \text{if} & q = n
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
These identifications are compatible with base change and
isomorphism between locally free sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-ML}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is Noetherian and $I$-adically complete,
\item $M$ is flat over $R$, and
\item $M/IM$ is a projective $R/I$-module.
\end{enumerate}
Then the $I$-adic completion $M^\wedge$ is a flat Mittag-Leffler
$R$-module.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory.
Suppose that the functor $v : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}$
has a left adjoint $u : \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$
such that $vu \cong \text{id}$. Then
$$
D(\mathcal{A})/D_\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A}) = D(\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B})
$$
and similarly for the bounded versions.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quotient-by-serre-easy}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory.
Suppose that the functor $v : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}$
has a left adjoint $u : \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$
such that $vu \cong \text{id}$. Then
$$
D(\mathcal{A})/D_\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{A}) = D(\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B})
$$
and similarly for the bounded versions.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a differential graded category over $R$ satisfying the following axioms. Axiom (A) requires a zero object and binary differential graded direct sums. Axiom (B) requires dg shift functors $[n]$, with $[0]=\mathrm{id}$ and $[n+m]=[n]\circ[m]$, and composition-compatible identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(x,y[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(x,y)[n]$ of dg modules. Axiom (C) requires, for every closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$, an admissible short exact sequence $y\to c(f)\to x[1]$ in $\operatorname{Comp}(\mathcal A)$ whose connecting morphism $x[1]\to y[1]$ agrees with $f[1]$. the homotopy category $K(\mathcal{A})$
with its natural translation functors and distinguished triangles
is a pre-triangulated category.

\label{lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper curve over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{L}$ has a nonzero section, then
$\deg(\mathcal{L}) \geq 0$.
\item If $\mathcal{L}$ has a nonzero section $s$ which vanishes
at a point, then $\deg(\mathcal{L}) > 0$.
\item If $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{L}^{-1}$ have nonzero sections, then
$\mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{O}_X$.
\item If $\deg(\mathcal{L}) \leq 0$ and $\mathcal{L}$ has a nonzero
section, then $\mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{O}_X$.
\item If $\mathcal{N} \to \mathcal{L}$ is a nonzero map of invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, then $\deg(\mathcal{L}) \geq \deg(\mathcal{N})$
and if equality holds then it is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

Let $k'/k$ be an extension of fields. Let $n \geq 0$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $\mathbf{P}^n_k$.

$m$-regular.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $B$ be a finitely generated graded $A$-algebra.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a proper morphism.
Set $\mathcal{B} = f^*\widetilde B$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
graded $\mathcal{B}$-module of finite type.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $p \geq 0$ the graded $B$-module $H^p(X, \mathcal{F})$
is a finite $B$-module.
\item If $\mathcal{L}$ is an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
then there exists an integer $d_0$ such that
$H^p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) = 0$

source.label: lemma-graded-finiteness
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-graded-finiteness}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $B$ be a finitely generated graded $A$-algebra.
Let $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ be a proper morphism.
Set $\mathcal{B} = f^*\widetilde B$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
graded $\mathcal{B}$-module of finite type.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $p \geq 0$ the graded $B$-module $H^p(X, \mathcal{F})$
is a finite $B$-module.
\item If $\mathcal{L}$ is an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module,
then there exists an integer $d_0$ such that
$H^p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}) = 0$
for all $p > 0$ and $d \geq d_0$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-hom}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. The construction above
defines a functor
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, -) :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$
by an application of Lemma \ref{lemma-functorial}.

source.label: lemma-pushforward-module
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pushforward-module}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $X$. Let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
The pushforward $f_*\mathcal{F}$, as defined in
Lemma \ref{lemma-pushforward-presheaf-module}
is a sheaf of $f_*\mathcal{O}$-modules.

\label{lemma-baire-category-locally-compact}
Let $X$ be a locally quasi-compact Hausdorff space.
Let $U_n \subset X$, $n \geq 1$ be dense open subsets. Then
$\bigcap_{n \geq 1} U_n$ is dense in $X$.

\label{lemma-when-injective-covering}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n \in R$.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Then $M \to \bigoplus M_{f_i}$ is injective if and only if
$$
M \longrightarrow \bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} M, \quad
m \longmapsto (f_1m, \ldots, f_nm)

formulation.statement:
For $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ on a ringed site, the derived tensor product $\mathcal F\otimes^\mathbf L_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ is computed by a K-flat resolution (sites-cohomology.tex:3299–3311), and $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O}_p(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=H^{-p}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}^\mathbf L\mathcal G)$ (definition at 3328–3339).

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module, and
\item $\text{Tor}_1^\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) = 0$
for every $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

Standing assumptions and notation from Stacks Situation \ref{situation-Cohen-Macaulay-curve}:
Here $k$ is a field, $X$ is a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$.

\omega_X \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{Q} \to 0

$\mathcal{Q}' \to \mathcal{Q}$ is injective.

Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a proper $k$-scheme of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, and $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ its dualizing module for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.  Given an exact sequence
$$
\omega_X \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{Q} \to 0
$$
of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{Q})) = 0$
and $\dim_k H^0(X, \mathcal{Q}) \geq 2$ and such that there is no nonzero
submodule $\mathcal{Q}' \subset \mathcal{F}$ such that
$\mathcal{Q}' \to \mathcal{Q}$ is injective.
Then the submodule of $\mathcal{F}$ generated by global
sections surjects onto $\mathcal{Q}$.

\label{lemma-globally-generated}
In Situation \ref{situation-Cohen-Macaulay-curve}. Given an exact sequence
$$
\omega_X \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{Q} \to 0
$$
of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{Q})) = 0$
and $\dim_k H^0(X, \mathcal{Q}) \geq 2$ and such that there is no nonzero
submodule $\mathcal{Q}' \subset \mathcal{F}$ such that
$\mathcal{Q}' \to \mathcal{Q}$ is injective.
Then the submodule of $\mathcal{F}$ generated by global
sections surjects onto $\mathcal{Q}$.

\label{lemma-equation-codim-1-in-projective-space}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $Z \subset \mathbf{P}^n_k$ be a closed subscheme
which has no embedded points such that every irreducible component
of $Z$ has dimension $n - 1$. Then the ideal $I(Z) \subset k[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$
corresponding to $Z$ is principal.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-connectedness-ample-divisor}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$
be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let
$s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $s$ is a regular section
(Divisors, Definition \ref{divisors-definition-regular-section}),
\item for every closed point $x \in X$ we have
$\text{depth}(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) \geq 2$, and
\item $X$ is connected.
\end{enumerate}
Then the zero scheme $Z(s)$ of $s$ is connected.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cover-smooth-by-special}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes. Then there exists an
\'etale covering $\{U_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ such that $U_i \to S$
factors as $U_i \to V_i \to S$ where $V_i \to S$ is \'etale and
$U_i \to V_i$ is a smooth morphism of affine schemes, which
has a section, and has geometrically connected fibres.

formulation.statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. If $f:X\to X$ is any morphism over $S$, then $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor. The isomorphism uses the descent datum to identify changes of the chosen presentation map $X\to S$.

\label{lemma-pullback-selfmap}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $f : X \to X$ be a selfmap of $X$ over $S$.
In this case pullback by $f$ is isomorphic to the
identity functor on the category of descent data
relative to $X \to S$.

Let $f : X \to S$ be flat, locally of finite presentation, separated,
locally quasi-finite with universally bounded fibres. Then there exist
closed subsets
$$
\emptyset = Z_{-1} \subset Z_0 \subset Z_1 \subset Z_2 \subset
\ldots \subset Z_n = S
$$
such that with $S_r = Z_r \setminus Z_{r - 1}$ the stratification
$S = \coprod_{r = 0, \ldots, n} S_r$ is characterized by the following
universal property: Given $g : T \to S$ the projection
$X \times_S T \to T$ is finite locally
free of degree $r$ if and only if $g(T) \subset S_r$ (set theoretically).

\label{lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded}
Let $f : X \to S$ be flat, locally of finite presentation, separated,
locally quasi-finite with universally bounded fibres. Then there exist
closed subsets
$$
\emptyset = Z_{-1} \subset Z_0 \subset Z_1 \subset Z_2 \subset
\ldots \subset Z_n = S
$$
such that with $S_r = Z_r \setminus Z_{r - 1}$ the stratification
$S = \coprod_{r = 0, \ldots, n} S_r$ is characterized by the following
universal property: Given $g : T \to S$ the projection
$X \times_S T \to T$ is finite locally
free of degree $r$ if and only if $g(T) \subset S_r$ (set theoretically).

conclusions:
Then there exists a separated morphism of finite presentation
$f' : X' \to S$ and a closed immersion $X \to X'$ of schemes over $S$.
formulation.statement:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is of finite type and separated, and
\item $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a separated morphism of finite presentation
$f' : X' \to S$ and a closed immersion $X \to X'$ of schemes over $S$.

\label{lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic $k$-scheme.
Then there exists a finite purely inseparable extension $k'/k$
such that the normalization $Y$ of $X_{k'}$ is geometrically normal over $k'$.

Notation: for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$, $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of inverse systems $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules satisfying $\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_n=0$ and $\mathcal E_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E_{n+1}\cong\mathcal E_n$ via the transition maps; morphisms are compatible maps of systems. For any coherent $\mathcal E$, put $\mathcal E^\wedge=(\mathcal E/\mathcal I^n\mathcal E)_{n\geq1}$.
If $X = \Spec(A)$ is the spectrum of a Noetherian ring and
$\mathcal{I}$ is the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals associated to the ideal
$I \subset A$, then $\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$ is equivalent to the
category of finite $A^\wedge$-modules where $A^\wedge$ is the completion
of $A$ with respect to $I$.

category of finite $A^\wedge$-modules where $A^\wedge$ is the completion
of $A$ with respect to $I$.

\label{lemma-etale-stratified-finite}
Let $U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes (for example an \'etale morphism of Noetherian schemes). Then there
exists a partition $X = \coprod_i X_i$ by constructible locally closed
subschemes such that $X_i \times_X U \to X_i$ is finite \'etale for all $i$.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

Let $(R', \mathfrak m') \to (R, \mathfrak m)$ be a local ring
homomorphism which induces an isomorphism on residue fields $\kappa$.
Then for every finite length $R$-module the restriction $M_{R'}$
is a finite length $R'$-module and there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\det\nolimits_{R, \kappa}(M)
\longrightarrow
\det\nolimits_{R', \kappa}(M_{R'})
$$
This isomorphism is functorial in $M$ and compatible with the
isomorphisms $\gamma_{K \to L \to M}$ defined by concatenating admissible sequences in short exact sequences
defined for $\det_{R, \kappa}$ and $\det_{R', \kappa}$.

\label{lemma-determinant-quotient-ring}
Let $(R', \mathfrak m') \to (R, \mathfrak m)$ be a local ring
homomorphism which induces an isomorphism on residue fields $\kappa$.
Then for every finite length $R$-module the restriction $M_{R'}$
is a finite length $R'$-module and there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\det\nolimits_{R, \kappa}(M)
\longrightarrow
\det\nolimits_{R', \kappa}(M_{R'})
$$
This isomorphism is functorial in $M$ and compatible with the
isomorphisms $\gamma_{K \to L \to M}$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-det-exact-sequences}
defined for $\det_{R, \kappa}$ and $\det_{R', \kappa}$.
