source.label: lemma-acyclics
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-acyclics}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. The full subcategory $\text{Ac}$
of the homotopy category $K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}))$
consisting of acyclic modules is a strictly full saturated
triangulated subcategory of $K(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}))$.

\item the images of $h_1, \ldots, h_r$ in

source.label: lemma-slice-given-elements
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-slice-given-elements}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$ be a point with image $s \in S$.
Let $h_1, \ldots, h_r \in \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item $f$ is flat at $x$, and
\item the images of $h_1, \ldots, h_r$ in
$\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x} = \mathcal{O}_{X, x}/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
form a regular sequence.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an affine open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
such that $h_1, \ldots, h_r$ come from
$h_1, \ldots, h_r \in \Gamma(U, \mathcal{O}_U)$ and such
that $Z = V(h_1, \ldots, h_r) \to U$ is a regular immersion with
$x \in Z$ and $Z \to S$ flat and locally of finite presentation.
Moreover, the base change $Z_{S'} \to U_{S'}$ is a regular immersion
for any scheme $S'$ over $S$.

source.label: lemma-local-cohomology-change-rings
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-cohomology-change-rings}
If $A \to B$ is a homomorphism of Noetherian rings and $I \subset A$
is an ideal, then in $D(B)$ we have
$$
R\Gamma_I(A) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B =
R\Gamma_Z(A) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B =
R\Gamma_Y(B) = R\Gamma_{IB}(B)
$$
where $Y = V(IB) \subset \Spec(B)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-skyscraper-functor-exact}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$p : \Sh(pt) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a point of
the topos associated to $\mathcal{C}$.
The functor $p_* : \textit{Sets} \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
has the following properties: It commutes with arbitrary limits,
it is left exact, it is faithful, it transforms surjections into surjections,
it commutes with coequalizers, it reflects injections, it reflects
surjections, and it reflects isomorphisms.

\label{theorem-colimit}
Let $X = \lim_{i \in I} X_i$ be a limit of a directed system of schemes
with affine transition morphisms $f_{i'i} : X_{i'} \to X_i$. We assume
that $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated for all $i \in I$.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{i'i})$ be a system of abelian sheaves
on $(X_i, f_{i'i})$. Denote $f_i : X \to X_i$ the projection and set
$\mathcal{F} = \colim f_i^{-1}\mathcal{F}_i$. Then
$$
\colim_{i\in I} H_\etale^p(X_i, \mathcal{F}_i) = H_\etale^p(X, \mathcal{F}).
$$
for all $p \geq 0$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-f-map-basis-below-structures}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces.
Let $(\mathcal{C}, F)$ be a type of algebraic structures.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf with values in $\mathcal{C}$ on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf with values in $\mathcal{C}$ on $Y$.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis for the topology on $Y$.
Suppose given for every $V \in \mathcal{B}$ a morphism
$$
\varphi_V :
\mathcal{G}(V)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{F}(f^{-1}V)
$$
of $\mathcal{C}$ compatible with restriction mappings.
Then there is a unique $f$-map (see Definition \ref{definition-f-map}
and discussion of $f$-maps in
Section \ref{section-presheaves-structures-functorial})
$\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$
recovering $\varphi_V$ for $V \in \mathcal{B}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coherent-projective}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
For every coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbf{P}^n_R$
we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists an $r \geq 0$ and
$d_1, \ldots, d_r \in \mathbf{Z}$ and a surjection
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, r}
\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^n_R}(d_j)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{F}.
$$
\item We have $H^i(\mathbf{P}^n_R, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ unless
$0 \leq i \leq n$.
\item For any $i$ the cohomology group $H^i(\mathbf{P}^n_R, \mathcal{F})$
is a finite $R$-module.
\item If $i > 0$, then
$H^i(\mathbf{P}^n_R, \mathcal{F}(d)) = 0$ for all $d$ large enough.
\item For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}$ the graded $R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$-module
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{d \geq k} H^0(\mathbf{P}^n_R, \mathcal{F}(d))
$$
is a finite $R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$-module.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $|X|$ is a singleton then $X$ is a scheme.
\item If $|X|$ is a singleton and $X$ is reduced, then
$X \cong \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ for some field $k$.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L3313–3324 says for a DECENT algebraic space X, (1) if |X| is singleton X is a SCHEME, and (2) if |X| is singleton AND X REDUCED then X≅Spec(k) for some field k. Both independent conditional clauses are preserved; the second is not inferred without reducedness.

phase3.reason: A singleton decent space has finite étale groupoid charts; after passing to a zero-dimensional henselian affine chart, the finite étale equivalence relation has a scheme quotient.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-equal}
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a cofiltered category. Let $i \mapsto X_i$ be a diagram
of spectral spaces such that for $a : j \to i$ in $\mathcal{I}$
the corresponding map $f_a : X_j \to X_i$ is spectral. Let $X = \lim X_i$
with projections $p_i : X \to X_i$. Let $i \in \Ob(\mathcal{I})$ and let
$E, F \subset X_i$ be subsets with $E$ closed in the constructible topology
and $F$ open in the constructible topology.
Then $p_i^{-1}(E) \subset p_i^{-1}(F)$ if and only if there is a morphism
$a : j \to i$ in $\mathcal{I}$ such that $f_a^{-1}(E) \subset f_a^{-1}(F)$.

\label{lemma-finite-type-nagata}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
If $Y$ is Nagata and $f$ locally of finite type then $X$ is Nagata.

formulation.statement:
For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of ringed spaces.
Then there is a canonical distinguished triangle
$$
Lf^* L_{Y/Z} \to L_{X/Z} \to L_{X/Y} \to Lf^*L_{Y/Z}[1]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Original L3546–3554 applies to composable ringed-space morphisms f:X→Y and g:Y→Z and gives the CANONICAL triangle Lf^*L_{Y/Z}→L_{X/Z}→L_{X/Y}→Lf^*L_{Y/Z}[1] in D(O_X). The proposal retains derived pullback Lf^* rather than underived f^-1, and the target category and arrow sequence.

phase3.reason: The natural cotangent triangle for composable morphisms is identified with the transitivity triangle for the underlying sheaves of rings.

$$

formulation.statement:
For an ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ of finite type on a ringed topos, $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal O,\mathcal I)$ denotes the full subcategory of derived $\mathcal I$-complete complexes, and derived completion is the left adjoint to its inclusion where defined. $Rf_*$ denotes derived pushforward and $Lf^*$ derived pullback. The exact source hypotheses relate the two ideal sheaves by $f^\sharp$.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}') \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$
and $\mathcal{I}' \subset \mathcal{O}'$ 
be finite type sheaves of ideals such that $f^\sharp$ sends
$f^{-1}\mathcal{I}$ into $\mathcal{I}'$.
Then $Rf_*$ sends $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O}', \mathcal{I}')$
into $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O}, \mathcal{I})$ and has a left adjoint
$Lf_{comp}^*$ which is $Lf^*$ followed by derived completion.

\label{lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}') \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$
and $\mathcal{I}' \subset \mathcal{O}'$ 
be finite type sheaves of ideals such that $f^\sharp$ sends
$f^{-1}\mathcal{I}$ into $\mathcal{I}'$.
Then $Rf_*$ sends $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O}', \mathcal{I}')$
into $D_{comp}(\mathcal{O}, \mathcal{I})$ and has a left adjoint
$Lf_{comp}^*$ which is $Lf^*$ followed by derived completion.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-strongly-cartesian-fibre-product}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $x \to y$ and $z \to y$ be morphisms of $\mathcal{S}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x \to y$ is strongly cartesian,
\item $p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$ exists, and
\item there exists a strongly cartesian morphism $a : w \to z$ in
$\mathcal{S}$ with $p(w) = p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$ and
$p(a) = \text{pr}_2 : p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z) \to p(z)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the fibre product $x \times_y z$ exists and is isomorphic to $w$.

hypotheses: Let $S\to S'$ be a morphism of schemes in a fixed big fppf site. Conversely, Construction B regards a stack $\mathcal X'$ over $S'$ equipped with a map $\mathcal X'\to(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ over $S'$ as a stack over $S$. These are mutually inverse 2-functors.

Let $S \to S'$ be a morphism of this site.

formulation.statement:
A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring.
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. Let $J \subset B$ be an ideal
with $IB \subset J$. There exists a homomorphism of
divided power rings
$$
(A, I, \gamma) \longrightarrow (D, \bar J, \bar \gamma)
$$
such that
$$
\Hom_{(A, I, \gamma)}((D, \bar J, \bar \gamma), (C, K, \delta)) =
\Hom_{(A, I)}((B, J), (C, K))
$$
functorially in the divided power algebra $(C, K, \delta)$ over
$(A, I, \gamma)$. Here the LHS is morphisms of divided
power rings over $(A, I, \gamma)$ and the RHS is morphisms of
(ring, ideal) pairs over $(A, I)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-covering-Cech}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] fppf, \linebreak[0]
\etale, \linebreak[0] smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic\}$
and $\mathcal{C} = (\Sch/S)_\tau$, or
\item[(b)] let $\tau = \etale$ and $\mathcal{C} = S_\etale$, or
\item[(c)] let $\tau = Zariski$ and $\mathcal{C} = S_{Zar}$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be affine.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$ be a standard affine
$\tau$-covering in $\mathcal{C}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{V} = \{\coprod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} U_i \to U\}$ is a
$\tau$-covering of $U$,
\item $\mathcal{U}$ is a refinement of $\mathcal{V}$, and
\item the induced map on {\v C}ech complexes
(Cohomology on Sites,
Equation (\ref{sites-cohomology-equation-map-cech-complexes}))
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
is an isomorphism of complexes.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-hom-from-finitely-presented}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $R$-module.
Let $N$ be an $R$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $f \in R$ we have
$\Hom_R(M, N)_f = \Hom_{R_f}(M_f, N_f) = \Hom_R(M_f, N_f)$,
\item for a multiplicative subset $S$ of $R$ we have
$$
S^{-1}\Hom_R(M, N) = \Hom_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M, S^{-1}N) =
\Hom_R(S^{-1}M, S^{-1}N).
$$
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
A dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$ over a Noetherian ring is a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$. On a local ring $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ it is *normalized* if $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\kappa[0]$. Its canonical module is $H^{-\dim A}(\omega_A^\bullet)$. A local ring is *Cohen–Macaulay* if its depth equals Krull dimension; a finite module is Cohen–Macaulay if depth equals dimension of its support.

Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring
with normalized dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$
and dualizing module $\omega_A = H^{-\dim(A)}(\omega_A^\bullet)$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is Cohen-Macaulay,
\item $\omega_A^\bullet$ is concentrated in a single degree, and
\item $\omega_A^\bullet = \omega_A[\dim(A)]$.
\end{enumerate}
In this case $\omega_A$ is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module.

A maximal Cohen–Macaulay module has depth equal to dim A.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-apply-CM}
Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring
with normalized dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$
and dualizing module $\omega_A = H^{-\dim(A)}(\omega_A^\bullet)$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is Cohen-Macaulay,
\item $\omega_A^\bullet$ is concentrated in a single degree, and
\item $\omega_A^\bullet = \omega_A[\dim(A)]$.
\end{enumerate}
In this case $\omega_A$ is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module.

and only if each cohomology sheaf $H^p(K)$ is derived complete.

if and only if $K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I}$
is bounded above.
\item An object $K \in D_{comp}(\mathcal{C}, \Lambda)$ is bounded
if $K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I}$ has finite
tor dimension.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-free}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an elementary \'etale neighbourhood $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
and a commutative diagram of pointed schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
(X, x) \ar[d] & (X', x') \ar[l]^g \ar[d] \\
(S, s) & (\Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}), s') \ar[l]
}
$$
such that $X' \to X \times_S \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{S', s'})$
is \'etale, $\kappa(x) = \kappa(x')$, the scheme $X'$ is
affine of finite presentation over $\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$,
the sheaf $g^*\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation over $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$,
and such that $\Gamma(X', g^*\mathcal{F})$ is a free
$\mathcal{O}_{S', s'}$-module.

\label{lemma-completed-direct-sum-ML}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal. Let $A$ be a set.
Assume $R$ is Noetherian and complete with respect to $I$. The completion
$(\bigoplus\nolimits_{\alpha \in A} R)^\wedge$
is flat and Mittag-Leffler.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-completion-internal-hom}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ be
coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Set
$\mathcal{H} = \SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})$.
Then
$$
\lim H^0(X, \mathcal{H}/\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{H}) =
\Mor_{\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})}
(\mathcal{G}^\wedge, \mathcal{F}^\wedge).
$$

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-local}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is proper,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is proper,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is proper,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is proper, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: Every regular local ring is Gorenstein.

A regular local ring is Gorenstein.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pushforward-coherent-on-open}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $j : U \to X$ be the inclusion of an open.
Let $T \subset X$ be a closed subset contained in $U$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a coherent $\mathcal{O}_U$-module
with $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \subset T$, then
$j_*\mathcal{F}$ is a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

\label{lemma-locally-projective-pullback}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.

is locally projective on $X$.

\label{lemma-enough-finite-type-points}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
For any locally closed subset $T \subset S$ we have
$$
T \not = \emptyset
\Rightarrow
T \cap S_{\text{ft-pts}} \not = \emptyset.
$$
In particular, for any closed subset $T \subset S$ we
see that $T \cap S_{\text{ft-pts}}$ is dense in $T$.

\label{lemma-scheme-theoretic-union}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X, Y \subset S$ be closed subschemes.
Let $X \cup Y$ be the scheme theoretic union of $X$ and $Y$.
Let $X \cap Y$ be the scheme theoretic intersection of $X$ and $Y$.
Then $X \to X \cup Y$ and $Y \to X \cup Y$ are closed immersions, there is a
short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathcal{O}_{X \cup Y} \to \mathcal{O}_X \times \mathcal{O}_Y
\to \mathcal{O}_{X \cap Y} \to 0
$$
of $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules, and the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \cap Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d] \\
Y \ar[r] & X \cup Y
}
$$
is cocartesian in the category of schemes, i.e.,
$X \cup Y = X \amalg_{X \cap Y} Y$.

\label{lemma-lift-fs}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field $k$.
Let $B$ be a Noetherian complete local $k$-algebra. Assume $k \to B$
is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology.
Then there exists a Noetherian complete local ring $C$
and a local homomorphism $A \to C$ which is formally smooth
in the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology such that $C \otimes_A k \cong B$.

formulation.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $f \in R(X)^*$.
Then the collections
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z\text{ a prime divisor with generic point }\xi
\text{ and }f\text{ not in }\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}\}
$$
and
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ a prime divisor and }\text{ord}_Z(f) \not = 0\}
$$
are locally finite in $X$.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Two different prime-divisor collections locally finite; nonnegative order not equated with regularity.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-divisor-locally-finite}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $f \in R(X)^*$.
Then the collections
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z\text{ a prime divisor with generic point }\xi
\text{ and }f\text{ not in }\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}\}
$$
and
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ a prime divisor and }\text{ord}_Z(f) \not = 0\}
$$
are locally finite in $X$.

\label{lemma-closed-proper-over-base}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subset. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the morphism $Z \to S$ is proper if $Z$ is endowed with the reduced
induced closed subscheme structure
(Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-reduced-induced-scheme}),
\item for some closed subscheme structure on $Z$ the morphism $Z \to S$
is proper,
\item for any closed subscheme structure on $Z$ the morphism
$Z \to S$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-smooth-quotient-smooth-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then the morphism $\mathcal{S}_U \to [U/R]$ is smooth and surjective.

formulation.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Let $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$. If $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x$ is nonzero, then
\[
i\ge-\dim_x(X_y).
\]
This is a lower bound for degrees of the upper-shriek structure complex; without extra hypotheses there is no asserted universal upper bound.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L5674 assumes f in FTS_S and x∈X with y=f(x), asserting H^i(f^!O_Y)_x≠0 implies i≥−dim_x(X_y), the dimension of the FIBRE GERM rather than of its local ring. The final includes the right degree inequality and definition of fibre germ, without adding an upper bound.

phase3.reason: Reduce to affine relative dualizing complexes and apply the algebraic vanishing theorem to the shriek complex.

\label{lemma-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$ with image $y \in Y$. Then
$$
H^i(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x \not = 0
\Rightarrow - \dim_x(X_y) \leq i.
$$

\label{lemma-pick-irreducible-components}
Let $X$ be a topological space and suppose $X = \bigcup_{i = 1, \ldots, n} X_i$
where each $X_i$ is an irreducible closed subset of $X$ and no $X_i$
is contained in the union of the other members.  Then each $X_i$ is an
irreducible component of $X$ and each irreducible component of $X$
is one of the $X_i$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-derived-products}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ be a sheaf of differential graded algebras
on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $D(\mathcal{A}, \text{d})$ has both direct sums and products,
\item direct sums are obtained by taking direct sums of differential graded
$\mathcal{A}$-modules,
\item products are obtained by taking products of
K-injective differential graded modules.
\end{enumerate}

The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

For finite-length $R$-module $M$ and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:M\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=\psi\varphi=0$ and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, call $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex. With $I_\varphi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, $I_\psi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, put $K_\varphi=\ker\varphi=I_\psi$, $K_\psi=\ker\psi=I_\varphi$. Let $\gamma_\varphi:\det K_\varphi\otimes\det I_\varphi\to\det M$, $\gamma_\psi:\det K_\psi\otimes\det I_\psi\to\det M$ be the determinant isomorphisms and $\sigma$ swap the tensor factors. Define $\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)\in\kappa^\times$ as the unique scalar such that $\gamma_\psi\circ\sigma\circ\gamma_\varphi^{-1}$ acts on $\det M$ by $(-1)^{\ell(I_\varphi)\ell(I_\psi)}\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)$.

Define the determinant symbol $d_M(a,b)=\det_\kappa(M/abM,a,b)\in\kappa^\times$. hypotheses: Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel $I$; let $A\to B$ be an $A$-algebra, $N$ a $B$-module, and $c:I\to N$ an $A$-linear map. A solution of the lifting problem is a commutative diagram of ring homomorphisms with exact rows $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ and $0\to N\to B'\to B\to0$ in which $N\subset B'$ is square-zero, $B'$ is an $A'$-algebra and the induced map $I\to N$ equals $c$. Isomorphisms of solutions commute with the maps from $A'$ and to $B$ and are the identity on the identified $N$.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.
formulation.statement:
Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel $I$; let $A\to B$ be an $A$-algebra, $N$ a $B$-module, and $c:I\to N$ an $A$-linear map. A solution of the lifting problem is a commutative diagram of ring homomorphisms with exact rows $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ and $0\to N\to B'\to B\to0$ in which $N\subset B'$ is square-zero, $B'$ is an $A'$-algebra and the induced map $I\to N$ equals $c$. Isomorphisms of solutions commute with the maps from $A'$ and to $B$ and are the identity on the identified $N$.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.

Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a flat finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the fibres $A \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are Gorenstein
for all primes $\mathfrak p \subset R$, and
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ is an invertible object of $D(A)$, see
More on Algebra, Lemma \ref{more-algebra-lemma-invertible-derived}.
\end{enumerate}
A Noetherian ring is Gorenstein when all its localizations at primes are Gorenstein local rings (finite self-injective dimension). Derived-invertible means locally a shift of a line bundle, and the condition concerns all residue-field fibres.

formulation.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a flat finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the fibres $A \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are Gorenstein
for all primes $\mathfrak p \subset R$, and
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ is an invertible object of $D(A)$, see
More on Algebra, Lemma \ref{more-algebra-lemma-invertible-derived}.
\end{enumerate}

**Scope and interpretation:** A Noetherian ring is Gorenstein when all its localizations at primes are Gorenstein local rings (finite self-injective dimension). Derived-invertible means locally a shift of a line bundle, and the condition concerns all residue-field fibres.

phase2.semantic_review_note: For flat finite-type Noetherian R→A, all residue-field fibres are Gorenstein if and only if the relative dualizing complex is derived tensor-invertible. The categorical invertibility and all-fibres quantifier are intact.

phase3.reason: Invertible relative dualizing complexes specialize to Gorenstein dualizing complexes on fibres; conversely the Gorenstein fibre condition makes their derived fibres rank-one shifts, yielding local invertibility.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $S$.
If $f : Y \to X$ and $g : Z \to Y$ are envelopes, then
$f \circ g$ is an envelope.

\label{lemma-torsion-submodule-sum-injective-hulls}
Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local ring.
Let $E$ be the injective hull of $\kappa$.
Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak m$-power torsion $R$-module
with $n = \dim_\kappa(M[\mathfrak m]) < \infty$.
Then $M$ is isomorphic to a submodule of $E^{\oplus n}$.

formulation.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Let $A\to B$ be flat with $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}B/IB$. If $K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$ and $L\in D(A)$, then the canonical map
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(K\otimes_AB,L\otimes_AB)
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism of underlying derived complexes of abelian groups (equivalently of $A$-modules by restriction on the right). In particular, for $A$-modules $M,N$ with $M$ $I$-power torsion, $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}_B^i(M\otimes_AB,N\otimes_AB)$ for every $i\ge0$. Flatness allows ordinary tensor rather than derived tensor on modules.

phase3.reason: Reduce both derived Hom sides to local-cohomology objects and invoke torsion flat base change and the comparison lemma to obtain the quasi-isomorphism.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-neighbourhood-extensions}
Let $A \to B$ be a flat ring map and let $I \subset A$ be a
finitely generated ideal such that $A/I \to B/IB$ is an isomorphism.
For $K \in D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A)$ and $L \in D(A)$
the map
$$
R\Hom_A(K, L) \longrightarrow R\Hom_B(K \otimes_A B, L \otimes_A B)
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. In particular, if $M$, $N$ are $A$-modules and
$M$ is $I$-power torsion, then the canonical map
$$
\Ext^i_A(M, N)
\longrightarrow
\Ext^i_B(M \otimes_A B, N \otimes_A B)
$$
is an isomorphism for all $i$.

\label{lemma-is-limit-dimension}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Assume there exist an integer $d \geq 0$ and a basis $\mathcal{B}$ for the
topology of $X$ such that
$$
H^p(U, H^q(E)) = 0 \text{ for }
U \in \mathcal{B},\ p > d, \text{ and }q < 0
$$
Then the map $E \to R\lim \tau_{\geq -n} E$ of
Derived Categories, Remark
\ref{derived-remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations}
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-alternative-colim-H0}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $f \in \mathfrak a \subset A$
be an element of an ideal of $A$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent
module on $U = \Spec(A) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $f$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item if $x \in \text{Ass}(\mathcal{F})$, $x \not \in V(f)$,
$\overline{\{x\}} \cap V(f) \not \subset V(\mathfrak a)$,
and $z \in \overline{\{x\}} \cap V(\mathfrak a)$, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{\overline{\{x\}}, z}) > 2$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map
$$
\colim_V \Gamma(V, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
\lim \Gamma(U, \mathcal{F}/f^n\mathcal{F})
$$
is an isomorphism where the colimit is over opens $V \subset U$
containing $U \cap V(f)$.

\label{lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I}, \mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals. Let $b : X' \to X$
be the blowing up of $X$ in $\mathcal{I}$. Let $b' : X'' \to X'$ be the
blowing up of $X'$ in $b^{-1}\mathcal{J} \mathcal{O}_{X'}$. Then $X'' \to X$
is canonically isomorphic to the blowing up of $X$ in $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{J}$.

conclusions: Gorenstein at x iff f^!O_Y derived-invertible around x; locus open.
hypotheses: f flat in FTS_S, x∈X.
formulation.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and $x\in X$. Then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ iff there exists an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is **derived-invertible**, i.e. locally isomorphic to a shift of a line bundle. In particular the pointwise Gorenstein locus is open. This relative criterion uses the upper-shriek *complex*, not just its zeroth cohomology.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L6504 requires FLAT f in FTS_S. It equates f Gorenstein AT x with derived invertibility of f^!O_Y on AN OPEN NEIGHBOURHOOD of x, and concludes the Gorenstein locus is open. The final retains the flatness and local derived-invertibility rather than merely stalkwise rank one.

phase3.reason: The six equivalences relate Gorenstein fibers, invertibility of the fiber dualizing complex and one-dimensional stalk cohomology via the cited pseudo-coherent lifting lemma.

source.label: lemma-affine-flat-Noetherian-gorenstein
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-flat-Noetherian-gorenstein}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism
of $\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$. If $f$ is flat, then
the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$,
\item $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ is isomorphic to an invertible object
in a neighbourhood of $x$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the set of points where $f$ is Gorenstein is
open in $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-colimit}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X = \lim_{i \in I} X_i$ be a limit of a
directed system of schemes over $S$ with affine transition morphisms
$f_{i'i} : X_{i'} \to X_i$. We assume the structure morphisms
$g_i : X_i \to S$ and $g : X \to S$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{i'i})$ be a system of abelian sheaves
on $(X_i, f_{i'i})$. Denote $f_i : X \to X_i$ the projection and set
$\mathcal{F} = \colim f_i^{-1}\mathcal{F}_i$. Then
$$
\colim_{i\in I} R^p g_{i, *} \mathcal{F}_i = R^p g_* \mathcal{F}
$$
for all $p \geq 0$.

Let $k$ be an infinite field. Let $X$ be an algebraic $k$-scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $V \to \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$ be a linear map of $k$-vector spaces
whose image generates $\mathcal{L}$. Then there exists a subspace
$W \subset V$ with $\dim_k(W) \leq \dim(X) + 1$ which generates $\mathcal{L}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closure-of-product}
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $k$, and let
$A \subset X$, $B \subset Y$ be subsets.
Set
$$
AB =
\{z \in X \times_k Y \mid \text{pr}_X(z) \in A, \ \text{pr}_Y(z) \in B\}
\subset X \times_k Y
$$
Then set theoretically we have
$$
\overline{A} \times_k \overline{B} = \overline{AB}
$$

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Assume that $\mathcal{C}$ has
a final object $X$ and fibred products.
Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor such that
\begin{enumerate}

\item for every pair of morphisms $U \to W$ and $V \to W$ with

$u(U \times_W V) \to u(U) \times_{u(W)} u(V)$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}

and consequently the stalk functor $\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$,

Both structural premises and both conclusions match.

phase3.reason: The singleton value at a final object makes neighbourhoods nonempty; the functor's fibre-product preservation supplies common refinements, and preservation of their equalizers supplies equalization of parallel neighbourhood arrows. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-neighbourhoods-directed}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Assume that $\mathcal{C}$ has
a final object $X$ and fibred products.
Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u(X)$ is a singleton set, and
\item for every pair of morphisms $U \to W$ and $V \to W$ with
the same target the map
$u(U \times_W V) \to u(U) \times_{u(W)} u(V)$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
Then the the category of neighbourhoods of $p$ is cofiltered
and consequently the stalk functor $\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$,
$\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}_p$ commutes with finite limits.

\label{lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $y \in Y$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ locally Noetherian,
\item $f$ is proper, and
\item $\dim(X_y) = d$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for any coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ we have
$(R^pf_*\mathcal{F})_y = 0$ for all $p > d$.

\label{lemma-zariski-after-blowup}
Let $\varphi : X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type with
$S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $U \subset S$ be a
quasi-compact open such that $\varphi^{-1}U \to U$ is an isomorphism.
Then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $S' \to S$ such that
the strict transform $X'$ of $X$ is isomorphic to an open subscheme
of $S'$.

formulation.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subscheme, and denote
$i : Y = X \setminus U \to X$ as a reduced closed subscheme of $X$.
Let $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Suppose $\alpha, \beta \in Z_k(X)$.
If $\alpha|_U \sim_{rat} \beta|_U$ then there exist a cycle
$\gamma \in Z_k(Y)$ such that
$$
\alpha \sim_{rat} \beta + i_*\gamma.
$$
In other words, the sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\CH_k(Y) \ar[r]^{i_*} & \CH_k(X) \ar[r]^{j^*} & \CH_k(U) \ar[r] & 0
}
$$
is an exact complex of abelian groups.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restrict-to-open}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subscheme, and denote
$i : Y = X \setminus U \to X$ as a reduced closed subscheme of $X$.
Let $k \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Suppose $\alpha, \beta \in Z_k(X)$.
If $\alpha|_U \sim_{rat} \beta|_U$ then there exist a cycle
$\gamma \in Z_k(Y)$ such that
$$
\alpha \sim_{rat} \beta + i_*\gamma.
$$
In other words, the sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\CH_k(Y) \ar[r]^{i_*} & \CH_k(X) \ar[r]^{j^*} & \CH_k(U) \ar[r] & 0
}
$$
is an exact complex of abelian groups.

The source's chosen big fppf site and base-scheme conventions remain in force, and terms such as algebraic space refer to fppf sheaves with representable diagonal and an étale surjective scheme atlas.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $U$ be a scheme. Let $\varphi : U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism such that
the projections $R = U \times_X U \to U$ are quasi-compact; for example if
$\varphi$ is quasi-compact. Then the fibres of
$$
|U| \to |X|
\quad\text{and}\quad
|R| \to |X|

\label{lemma-finite-fibres-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $U$ be a scheme. Let $\varphi : U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism such that
the projections $R = U \times_X U \to U$ are quasi-compact; for example if
$\varphi$ is quasi-compact. Then the fibres of
$$
|U| \to |X|
\quad\text{and}\quad
|R| \to |X|
$$
are finite.

conclusions: Fully faithful descent, effective descent, and universal injectivity are equivalent.

\label{lemma-algebra-relations}
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$.
Let $F'$ and $F_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$
be finite separable $F$-algebras. Let $A$ be a finite $F$-algebra.
Let $\sigma, \sigma' : A \to F'$ and $\sigma_i : A \to F_i$
be $F$-algebra maps. Assume $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ surjective.
If there is a relation
$$
\text{Tr}_{F'/F} \circ \sigma - \text{Tr}_{F'/F} \circ \sigma' =
n(\sum m_i \text{Tr}_{F_i/F} \circ \sigma_i)
$$
where $n > 1$ and $m_i$ are integers, then $\sigma = \sigma'$.

formulation.statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

Under the global crystalline setup above, let $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ or $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules on $\mathcal C$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is locally quasi-coherent and a crystal in
$\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: The pinned module criterion says crystalline quasi-coherence is equivalent to the conjunction of local quasi-coherence and crystal descent isomorphisms. The proposal specifies the relevant site C and the crystalline module definition without weakening the iff.

phase3.reason: Shows local presentations imply quasi-coherence and crystal pullback, then constructs site-local presentations from affine quasi-coherent modules using the crystal property.

For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$, its cotangent complex $L_{X/Y}$ is defined using the map of their Zariski ringed spaces. On affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, one has a canonical quasi-isomorphism $\widetilde{L_{B/A}}\to L_{X/Y}|_U$, compatible with smaller affine opens; $\widetilde{-}$ denotes the quasi-coherent complex associated to a complex of modules.

For a ring map $A\to B$, the ring cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is the normalized complex of the simplicial module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$ for the standard augmented simplicial polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, in nonpositive degrees. Its affine scheme counterpart is $\widetilde{L_{B/A}}$. For a scheme $X$ over a ring $\Lambda$, $\underline\Lambda$ denotes the constant sheaf of rings on the Zariski site of $X$; on the small étale site of an algebraic space it denotes the corresponding constant sheaf.

Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. Let $X$ be a scheme over $\Lambda$.
Then
$$
L_{X/\Spec(\Lambda)} = L_{\mathcal{O}_X/\underline{\Lambda}}
$$
where $\underline{\Lambda}$ is the constant sheaf with value
$\Lambda$ on $X$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection}
Let $R \to A$ be a syntomic ring map. Then there exists a smooth $R$-algebra
map $A \to C$ with a retraction such that $C$ is a global relative complete
intersection over $R$, i.e.,
$$
C \cong R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)
$$
flat over $R$ and all fibres of dimension $n - c$.

source.label: lemma-normalize-noetherian-dim-1
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-normalize-noetherian-dim-1}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme of dimension $1$.
Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ be the normalization. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\nu$ is integral, surjective, and induces a bijection
on irreducible components,
\item there is a factorization $X^\nu \to X_{red} \to X$
and the morphism $X^\nu \to X_{red}$ is the normalization
of $X_{red}$,
\item $X^\nu \to X_{red}$ is birational,
\item for every closed point $x \in X$ the stalk
$(\nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu})_x$ is the integral closure
of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ in the total ring of fractions
of $(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})_{red} = \mathcal{O}_{X_{red}, x}$,
\item the fibres of $\nu$ are finite and the residue
field extensions are finite,
\item $X^\nu$ is a disjoint union of integral normal locally Noetherian
schemes and each affine open is the spectrum of a finite
product of Dedekind domains.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-covering-of-a-closed}
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff and locally quasi-compact space.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a quasi-compact (hence closed) subset.
Suppose given an integer $p \geq 0$, a set $I$, for every $i \in I$
an open $U_i \subset X$, and for every $(p + 1)$-tuple
$i_0, \ldots, i_p$ of $I$ an open
$W_{i_0 \ldots i_p} \subset U_{i_0} \cap \ldots \cap U_{i_p}$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z \subset \bigcup U_i$, and
\item for every $i_0, \ldots, i_p$ we have
$W_{i_0 \ldots i_p} \cap Z = U_{i_0} \cap \ldots \cap U_{i_p} \cap Z$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exist opens $V_i$ of $X$ such that
we have $Z \subset \bigcup V_i$,
for all $i$ we have $\overline{V_i} \subset U_i$, and
we have $V_{i_0} \cap \ldots \cap V_{i_p} \subset W_{i_0 \ldots i_p}$
for all $(p + 1)$-tuples $i_0, \ldots, i_p$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-blowup-complex-integral}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ be perfect.
Then there exists a nonempty open $U \subset X$
such that $H^i(E|_U)$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r_i$
for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ and there exists a $U$-admissible blowup
$b : X' \to X$ such that $H^i(Lb^*E)$ is a perfect
$\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module of tor dimension $\leq 1$ for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.

Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring.
Let $B \to B'$ be a homomorphism of $A$-algebras.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B/IB \to B'/IB'$ is flat, and
\item $\text{Tor}_1^B(B', B/IB) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for any ideal $IB \subset J \subset B$ the canonical map
$$
D_B(J) \otimes_B B' \longrightarrow D_{B'}(JB')
$$
is an isomorphism.

\label{lemma-projection-formula-Rf-lower-shriek}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated finite type morphism of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated schemes. Let $\Lambda$ be a torsion ring. Let
$E \in D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ and $K \in D(Y_\etale, \Lambda)$. Then
$$
Rf_!E \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} K =
Rf_!(E \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} f^{-1}K)
$$
in $D(Y_\etale, \Lambda)$.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $D \subset S$ be a closed subscheme.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The subscheme $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $S$.
\item For every $x \in D$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood
$\Spec(A) = U \subset S$ of $x$ such that
$U \cap D = \Spec(A/(f))$ with $f \in A$ a nonzerodivisor.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-flat-morphism-from-CM-scheme}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of locally Noetherian schemes.
If $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay, then $f$ is Cohen-Macaulay and
$\mathcal{O}_{Y, f(x)}$ is Cohen-Macaulay for all $x \in X$.

\label{lemma-category-summands-finite-free}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Set $R = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$. The category of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules which are summands of finite free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules is equivalent to the category of
finite projective $R$-modules.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is of locally of finite type.
\item The scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and
\item The scheme $S$ is quasi-separated.
\end{enumerate}
Then $X = \lim X_i$ where the $X_i \to S$ are of
finite presentation, the $X_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
and the transition morphisms $X_{i'} \to X_i$ are closed immersions
(which implies that $X \to X_i$ are closed immersions for all $i$).

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-is-limit-finite-presentation}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is of locally of finite type.
\item The scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and
\item The scheme $S$ is quasi-separated.
\end{enumerate}
Then $X = \lim X_i$ where the $X_i \to S$ are of
finite presentation, the $X_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
and the transition morphisms $X_{i'} \to X_i$ are closed immersions
(which implies that $X \to X_i$ are closed immersions for all $i$).

A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). formulation.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
If $X$ is smooth and $k(Y) \subset k(X)$ is inseparable of degree $p$,
then there is a unique isomorphism $Y = X^{(p)}$ such that
$f$ is $F_{X/k}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a
nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over $k$.
If $X$ is smooth and $k(Y) \subset k(X)$ is inseparable of degree $p$,
then there is a unique isomorphism $Y = X^{(p)}$ such that
$f$ is $F_{X/k}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjective-representable}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then
$f$ is surjective (in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if $|f| : |X| \to |Y|$ is surjective.

\label{lemma-scheme-theoretically-dense}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subspace.

\begin{enumerate}
\item for every \'etale morphism $\varphi : V \to X$ (of algebraic spaces)

\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$\varphi : V \to X$ such that the scheme theoretic closure of
$\varphi^{-1}(U)$ in $V$ is equal to $V$,
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-module-support-proper-over-base}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally
of finite type. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the support of $\mathcal{F}$ is proper over $S$,
\item the scheme theoretic support of $\mathcal{F}$
(Morphisms, Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-scheme-theoretic-support})
is proper over $S$, and
\item there exists a closed subscheme $Z \subset X$ and
a finite type, quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Z$-module
$\mathcal{G}$ such that (a) $Z \to S$ is proper, and (b)
$(Z \to X)_*\mathcal{G} = \mathcal{F}$.
\end{enumerate}

formulation.statement:
In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, an **algebraic space** is a sheaf with a representable diagonal and a surjective étale atlas $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$. A map of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** if all Yoneda test fibres $h_T\times_G F$ are schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$
such that there exists $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and a map
$U \to F$ which is representable, surjective, and \'etale.
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

phase2.semantic_review_note: If F is an fppf sheaf and admits a representable surjective étale morphism U→F from a scheme U, then F is an algebraic space; all three properties of the atlas are preserved.

phase3.reason: The proof forms an étale equivalence relation U×_F U, invokes the quotient presentation theorem, and identifies its quotient with F using sheaf-surjectivity.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-locally-representable-gives-space}
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$
such that there exists $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and a map
$U \to F$ which is representable, surjective, and \'etale.
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

conclusions: If both maps satisfy going down, then the composite $R\to T$ satisfies going down.
Independently, if both maps satisfy going up, then the composite satisfies going up.
hypotheses: $R\to S\to T$ are unital maps of commutative rings.
formulation.statement:
For a unital map of commutative rings $u:R\to S$, going down means: for every chain $\mathfrak p\subset\mathfrak p^\prime$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$, there exists $\mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p$. Going up means: for every such chain and $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, there exists $\mathfrak q^\prime\supset\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$. Suppose $R \to S$ and $S \to T$ are ring maps satisfying
going down. Then so does $R \to T$. Similarly for going up.

conclusions: The composite satisfies going down.
hypotheses: Both maps satisfy going down.

conclusions: The composite satisfies going up.
hypotheses: Both maps satisfy going up.

phase2.semantic_review_note: Two separately guarded composition laws: going-down maps compose, and independently going-up maps compose. Neither property assumed in the other branch.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-first-order-henselization}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $B$ be a finite type $k$-algebra.
Let $J \subset B$ be an ideal such that
$\Spec(B) \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth on the complement of $V(J)$.
Let $N$ be a finite $B$-module.
Then there is a canonical bijection
$$
\text{Exal}_k(B, N) \to \text{Exal}_k(B^h, N^h)
$$
Here $(B^h, J^h)$ is the henselization of $(B, J)$
and $N^h = N \otimes_B B^h$.

\label{lemma-functor-fp-modules}
Let $A$ and $B$ be rings. Let
$F : \text{Mod}^{fp}_A \to \text{Mod}^{fp}_B$ be a functor.
Then $F$ extends uniquely to a functor
$F' : \text{Mod}_A \to \text{Mod}_B$
which commutes with filtered colimits.

\begin{enumerate}

is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjective-continuous-irreducible-components}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a surjective, continuous map of topological spaces.
If $X$ has a finite number, say $n$, of irreducible components, then
$Y$ has $\leq n$ irreducible components.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-largest-quasi-coherent-subsheaf}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{F}$
be a $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule. There exists a unique quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule $\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{G}$
with the following property: For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
$\mathcal{H}$ the map
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G}')
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G})
$$
is bijective. In particular $\mathcal{G}'$ is the largest quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule of $\mathcal{F}$ contained in $\mathcal{G}$.

\label{lemma-lift-idempotents-noncommutative}
Let $A$ be a possibly noncommutative algebra.
Let $e \in A$ be an element such that $x = e^2 - e$ is nilpotent.
Then there exists an idempotent of the form
$e' = e + x(\sum a_{i, j}e^ix^j) \in A$
with $a_{i, j} \in \mathbf{Z}$.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-smooth-affine}
Let $T$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be a smooth covering of $T$.
Then there exists a smooth covering
$\{U_j \to T\}_{j = 1, \ldots, m}$ which is a refinement
of $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ such that each $U_j$ is an affine
scheme, and such that each morphism $U_j \to T$ is standard
smooth, see Morphisms, Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-smooth}.
Moreover, we may choose each $U_j$ to be open affine in one of the $T_i$.

formulation.statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a directed system of ring maps $(A_i\to B_i)$, let $A=\varinjlim A_i$ and $B=\varinjlim B_i$. When comparing $L_{B_i/A_i}$ over the different rings $B_i$, use the transition maps to view their filtered colimit as a complex over $B$. Filtered colimits of modules are exact and commute with polynomial algebra formation and Kähler differentials.

Let $A_i \to B_i$ be a system of ring maps over a directed index
set $I$. Then, with the filtered colimit taken using the functorial transition maps and viewed as a complex of $\varinjlim B_i$-modules, $\varinjlim_i L_{B_i/A_i}\simeq L_{\varinjlim_i B_i/\varinjlim_i A_i}$.

The source lemma L156–160 asserts filtered colimits of these complexes agree with the cotangent complex of filtered-colimit ring maps. The proposal explicitly states use of transition maps and comparison over colim B_i, preserving directedness and the asserted quasi-isomorphism.

phase3.reason: The colimit comparison follows from compatibility of free/forgetful adjoints with filtered colimits and from the cited commutation of Kähler differentials.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a Grothendieck abelian category.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $D(\mathcal{A})$ has both direct sums and products,
\item direct sums are obtained by taking termwise direct sums of
any complexes,
\item products are obtained by taking termwise products of
K-injective complexes.
\end{enumerate}

phase2.semantic_review_note: D(A) for Grothendieck A has direct sums and products. Direct sums use degreewise sums of arbitrary complexes, but products use degreewise products of K-injective complexes. The important K-injective restriction is retained.

phase3.reason: Termwise direct sums satisfy the derived universal property by testing against K-injective targets; products arise as termwise products of K-injective representatives using the cited derived product lemma.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chern-classes-E-tensor-L}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free sheaf of
rank $r$ on $X$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
sheaf on $X$. Then we have
\begin{equation}
\label{equation-twist}
c_i({\mathcal E} \otimes {\mathcal L})
=
\sum\nolimits_{j = 0}^i
\binom{r - i + j}{j} c_{i - j}({\mathcal E}) c_1({\mathcal L})^j
\end{equation}
in $A^*(X)$.

conclusions: $\Hom_R(S, E)$ is an injective $S$-module.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-ringed-intrinsic-morphism}
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{C}') \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
be a morphism of topoi. If $\mathcal{O}$ is a sheaf of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$, then
$$
f^{-1}(\mathcal{O}^*) = (f^{-1}\mathcal{O})^*.
$$
In particular, if $\mathcal{O}$ turns $\mathcal{C}$ into a locally
ringed site, then setting $f^\sharp = \text{id}$
the morphism of ringed topoi
$$
(f, f^\sharp) :
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), f^{-1}\mathcal{O})
\to
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})
$$
is a morphism of locally ringed topoi.

formulation.statement:
For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper curve over $k$ with
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. If $X$ has a $\mathfrak g^r_d$, then
$r \leq d$. If equality holds, then $H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = 0$, i.e.,
the genus of $X$ (defined as $\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$) is $0$.

phase3.reason: Uses an effective Cartier divisor from a section to obtain r≤d, then propagates equality to tensor powers and applies Serre vanishing to force genus zero.

If $\text{cd}(A, I) = 1$, then there exist $c \geq 1$ and maps
$\varphi_j : I^c \to A$ such that $\sum f_j \varphi_j : I^c \to I$
is the inclusion map.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-lichtenbaum}
Let $X$ be a nonempty separated scheme of finite type over a field $k$.
Let $d = \dim(X)$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^d(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$,
\item $H^d(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$ on $X$, and
\item no irreducible component $X' \subset X$ of dimension $d$
is proper over $k$.
\end{enumerate}

source.label: lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit}
Let $I$ be a directed set. Let $(S_i, f_{ii'})$ be an
inverse system of schemes over $I$. If all the morphisms
$f_{ii'} : S_i \to S_{i'}$ are affine, then the limit $S = \lim_i S_i$ exists
in the category of schemes. Moreover,
\begin{enumerate}
\item each of the morphisms $f_i : S \to S_i$ is affine,
\item for an element $0 \in I$ and any open subscheme $U_0 \subset S_0$
we have
$$
f_0^{-1}(U_0) = \lim_{i \geq 0} f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)
$$
in the category of schemes.
\end{enumerate}

object of $X_\proetale$, then

f_{small}^{-1}\mathcal{F}(W) = \colim_{W \to V} \mathcal{F}(V)

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-small-pullback-weakly-contractible}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf
of sets on $Y_\proetale$. If $W$ is an affine weakly contractible
object of $X_\proetale$, then
$$
f_{small}^{-1}\mathcal{F}(W) = \colim_{W \to V} \mathcal{F}(V)
$$
where the colimit is over morphisms $W \to V$ over $Y$
with $V \in Y_\proetale$.
