source.label: lemma-topology-presheaves-sheaves
source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-topology-presheaves-sheaves}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $\{ \mathcal{F}_i \}_{i\in I}$ be a
collection of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal{C}$. For each
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ denote
$J(U)$ the set of sieves $S$ on $U$ with the following property:
For every morphism $V \to U$, the maps
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(h_V, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(S \times_U V, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
are bijective for all $i \in I$. Then $J$ defines a
topology on $\mathcal{C}$. This topology is the finest
topology in which all of the $\mathcal{F}_i$ are sheaves.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proj-sheaves}
Let $S$ be a graded ring. Let $M$ be a graded $S$-module.
Let $\widetilde M$ be the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(S)}$-modules
associated to $M$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $f \in S$ homogeneous of positive degree we have
$$
\Gamma(D_{+}(f), \mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(S)}) = S_{(f)}.
$$
\item For every $f\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree
we have $\Gamma(D_{+}(f), \widetilde M) = M_{(f)}$
as an $S_{(f)}$-module.
\item Whenever $D_{+}(g) \subset D_{+}(f)$ the restriction mappings
on $\mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(S)}$ and $\widetilde M$
are the maps
$S_{(f)} \to S_{(g)}$ and $M_{(f)} \to M_{(g)}$ from Lemma
\ref{lemma-standard-open}.
\item Let $\mathfrak p$ be a homogeneous prime of $S$ not containing
$S_{+}$, and let $x \in \text{Proj}(S)$
be the corresponding point. We have
$\mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(S), x} = S_{(\mathfrak p)}$.
\item Let $\mathfrak p$ be a homogeneous prime of $S$ not containing
$S_{+}$, and let $x \in \text{Proj}(S)$
be the corresponding point. We have $(\widetilde M)_x = M_{(\mathfrak p)}$
as an $S_{(\mathfrak p)}$-module.
\item
\label{item-map}
There is a canonical ring map
$
S_0 \longrightarrow \Gamma(\text{Proj}(S), \widetilde S)
$
and a canonical $S_0$-module map
$
M_0 \longrightarrow \Gamma(\text{Proj}(S), \widetilde M)
$
compatible with the descriptions of sections over standard opens
and stalks above.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, all these identifications are functorial in the graded
$S$-module $M$. In particular, the functor $M \mapsto \widetilde M$
is an exact functor from the category of graded $S$-modules
to the category of $\mathcal{O}_{\text{Proj}(S)}$-modules.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$ be a point. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|f|(|Y|)$ is contained in $\{x\} \subset |X|$,
\item $Y$ is reduced, and
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ factors through the residual space $Z_x$ of $X$ at $x$.

phase3.reason: On an affine étale chart over locally Noetherian X, the finite point set above x admits no nontrivial specialization; reduce the morphism to these points and descend factoring via an étale cover.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

Let $X$ be a proper curve over a field $k$ with $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$.
If $X$ has genus $0$, then every invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
$\mathcal{L}$ of degree $0$ is trivial.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-criterion-representable-map-stack-in-groupoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ be categories fibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism.
Make a choice of pullbacks for $\mathcal{Y}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item each functor $F_U : \mathcal{X}_U \longrightarrow \mathcal{Y}_U$
between fibre categories is faithful, and
\item for each $U$ and each $y \in \mathcal{Y}_U$ the presheaf
$$
(f : V \to U)
\longmapsto
\{(x, \phi) \mid x \in \mathcal{X}_V, \phi : f^*y \to F(x)\}/\cong
$$
is a representable presheaf on $\mathcal{C}/U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is representable.

\label{lemma-Noetherian-h-ph}
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. A family of morphisms
$\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ with target $X$ is an h covering
if and only if it is a ph covering.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-flat-up-down}
Let $X \to T \to S$ be morphisms of schemes with $T \to S$ \'etale.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $x \in X$ be a point. Then
$$
\mathcal{F}\text{ flat over }S\text{ at }x
\Leftrightarrow
\mathcal{F}\text{ flat over }T\text{ at }x
$$
In particular $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ if and only if $\mathcal{F}$
is flat over $T$.

Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

Over algebraically closed k the degree-two quotient is split or dual numbers.

source.original_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-epimorphism-modules}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}'$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of rings.
Let $\mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2$ be $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.
Then
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2) =
\Hom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2).
$$
In other words, the restriction functor
$\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}') \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$ is fully faithful.
